articles.title: Google transforme son moteur de recherche en assistant personnel, avec vos données comme carburant
articles.text:
Google étend les connexions entre son Mode IA et vos applications pour enrichir ses réponses avec vos dépenses, vos documents et vos conversations Gemini. Une nouvelle étape vers un moteur de recherche qui connaît vos projets, à condition de lui en ouvrir l’accès.
Pour préparer un voyage, on cherche une destination sur Google, on compare les prix, puis on ouvre sa boîte mail pour retrouver une réservation. Avec son Mode IA, Google veut réunir ces étapes dans la même conversation. Le moteur connaît déjà le Web. Il voudrait maintenant avoir assez de contexte sur vous pour vous aider à organiser la suite, sans vous demander de tout raconter à chaque recherche. Et pour cela, Google va se servir dans l’ensemble de vos données personnelles.
Vos fichiers et vos conversations rejoignent la recherche
Google ajoute ainsi Wallet aux connexions de son Intelligence personnalisée. Drive et l’application Gemini doivent suivre dans les prochaines semaines. Ces services rejoignent Gmail, Agenda et Photos parmi les sources susceptibles d’alimenter les réponses du Mode IA.
Le moteur de recherche avait déjà intégré l’analyse des dépenses de Wallet dans Gemini. Cette fois, ces informations arrivent directement dans le moteur de recherche, pour aider à comprendre son budget ou à repérer des économies. L’accès aux données financières reste limité à la lecture.
Drive apporterait le contenu des documents, tableaux et PDF. Quant au lien avec Gemini, il permettrait de reprendre dans la recherche une idée explorée avec le chatbot, et vice-versa. Google prévoit aussi que le contexte des recherches récentes accompagne davantage les réponses, y compris dans un nouveau fil.
L'idée derrière ces modifications est de vous faire gagner du temps. Plus besoin de réexpliquer le contexte dans une nouvelle conversation. Comme dans un chatbot traditionnel, le mode IA de Google va retenir les informations clés pour vous apporter une réponse rapide, précise et pertinente.
Un assistant personnel auquel il faut donner les clés
Si donner accès à vos informations de paiement ou vos fichiers vous dérange, Google a pensé à vous. Ces connexions demandent une activation volontaire et peuvent être coupées à la demande. Google prévoit une icône sous les réponses personnalisées pour montrer le contexte utilisé. L’utilisateur pourra également corriger une information dans la conversation. Le service peut toujours se tromper sur vos goûts ou vos intentions.
Cette personnalisation a aussi un coût. L’aide de Google précise que des résumés, extraits et déductions issus des contenus consultés peuvent servir à entraîner ses modèles. Dans certains cas, un extrait peut correspondre à l’intégralité d’un message ou d’un document court. Attention donc aux informations que vous partagez.
Pour les utilisateurs français, il faudra encore patienter. La France ne figure pas dans la liste actuelle des pays compatibles avec les connexions de contenus à la recherche. Google réserve par ailleurs l’accès à Drive aux États-Unis, en anglais.
Le moteur de recherche se rapproche ainsi de l’assistant personnel que Google construit autour de Gemini. Pour lui demander conseil, il suffira toujours de quelques mots. Pour qu’il vous connaisse, il faudra décider jusqu’où le laisser entrer.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, Ruby2Shell, and a Whole Lot of Shell Trouble
articles.text:
A stolen key. A trusted message. A routine update. None of these looks like the start of a major security problem. That's partly why they work. Attackers don't always need to break down a door. Sometimes they just use one that's already open.
This week's stories show how quickly a small opening can turn into a much bigger mess. One breach helps attackers reach another target. Tools people rely on become ways to get inside. Even features built for safety can end up helping the wrong person. And some of the latest research shows just how little effort certain attacks need.
The strange part is how normal it all looks until something goes wrong. A few attacks are clever. Others are almost embarrassingly simple. Both can do real damage. Here's what caught our attention this week.
⚡ Threat of the Week
Threat Actor Exploits VMware vCenter Flaw as a 0-Day — The suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group known as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) has been attributed to the zero-day exploitation of a critical security flaw in VMware vCenter Server in early September 2026. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of authentication bypass in the VMware Directory Service that could be exploited to gain unauthorized access to the system. In October, Google described a campaign by Armory Castle to exploit organizations through BeyondTrust's Remote Support tool, using a zero-day to breach the edge appliance and steal secrets useful for network reconnaissance and downstream compromises within organizations. The latest findings show that BeyondTrust was merely an entry point to a deeper and more complex campaign that involved the deployment of backdoors on Linux machines.
Is Your Workforce Secured from AI Threats?
Attackers now weaponize AI to launch personalized phishing attacks faster than employees can react. Fight AI with AI, using realistic simulations to train employees to spot and stop threats. Stop phishing before it becomes a breach.
Book a Demo ➝
🔔 Top News
- Cursor Links Malicious Claude Extension Release to Fireworks AI Incident — Cursor has traced the origins of a security incident involving a malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension in its marketplace to a breach at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks. "An attacker obtained an access key we had issued to Fireworks," Cursor said. "The key was exposed by Fireworks, and the attacker used it to copy data from a read-only storage bucket we used to share data with them." The Cursor incident is another indication of how the rapid adoption of AI-powered development tools and increasingly interconnected software ecosystems has worsened software supply chain risks.
- Cold Relic Exploits Cloud Breaches to Target Organizations — The Russian cyberespionage group known as Cold Relic is turning cloud breaches into a springboard for targeting a victim organization's wider network of trusted relationships. In the first intrusion observed late last year, the attackers gained control of a cloud administrator account and harvested internal communications, employee details, and other organizational records. Cold Relic later used that information to impersonate an employee of the first organization to conduct a social engineering attack on an individual at a second organization. The campaigns "demonstrate the convergence of human-centric social engineering and cloud identity abuse," Google said. "By obtaining access to strategic personnel rosters and operational documents, Russian intelligence services turn legitimate business communications into attack vectors against trusted partners."
- Malicious Web Pages Can Hijack Meta Muse — New research from the NebuSec research team has demonstrated that an attacker-controlled web page can be exploited to gain unauthorized access to user data associated with Meta Muse and compromise the underlying virtual machine (VM) in which it operates. "An attacker could retrieve conversation history and stored memories without triggering Muse's network approval prompts," NebuSec said. "The attack also allowed us to alter stored memories and conversation history, creating risks beyond unauthorized data access. By exploiting a vulnerability in the shared Linux kernel, we escaped the agent's runtime container and obtained root privileges in the underlying user VM." Meta has since addressed the issue.
- New FastUnlock Windows Narrator LockScreen Bypass Detailed — Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri (aka Chaotic Eclipse) published FastUnlock, a new unpatched Windows 11 zero-day that abuses the Narrator screen reader to get past the lock screen and execute code as the lock screen account "WsiAccount." The attack requires physical access and at least one account linked to an online Microsoft account.
- GL.iNet GoodCloud Exploited to Serve Reverse Shells, Backdoors — Hackers have exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud cloud management platform to install malware, backdoors, and remote access tools on customers' routers and KVM devices."An unauthorized party exploited the vulnerability to access and install malicious software on some GL.iNet routers and KVM devices," GL.iNet said. "The attack path has been blocked. We fixed the cloud vulnerability and blocked the access used in this incident. Devices can no longer be newly infected through this attack path. The cloud-side fix alone does not remove malware from devices that were already infected." GL.iNet has not disclosed how the attackers exploited its cloud platform, how many customers were affected, or whether information was stolen as a result of these compromises. RemoteToHome said it examined 183 routers and found suspicious activity on 152, including 24 with root-level reverse shells, 47 with an older persistent backdoor, and 81 showing evidence that attacker-supplied commands had executed. It has also identified a potential command injection vulnerability in the GoodCloud client, although GL.iNet has not confirmed if this is the same vulnerability that was used in the attacks.
️‍🔥 Trending CVEs
Bugs drop weekly, and the gap between a patch and an exploit is shrinking fast. These are the heavy hitters for the week: high-severity, widely used, or already being poked at in the wild.
Check the list, patch what you have, and hit the ones marked urgent first — CVE-2026-14978, CVE-2026-45110, CVE-2026-49401, CVE-2026-59890 (Unicode Normalization Collision on macOS), CVE-2026-114938 aka Java4Shell (Java 17, 21, 25, and 27), CVE-2026-28400 (Docker Model Runner), CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425 aka NGINX2Root (NGINX and NGINX Plus), CVE-2026-120718 (F5 BIG-IP), CVE-2026-126822, CVE-2026-126336, CVE-2026-121812, CVE-2026-123637, CVE-2026-125272 (F5 BIG-IP APM), CVE-2026-120722, CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-116953 (F5 BIG-IP iRule), CVE-2026-125274 (F5 BIG-IP and BIG-IQ), CVE-2026-114819 (Oracle AI Database), CVE-2026-132825 aka Ruby2Shell (Ruby), CVE-2026-130963, CVE-2026-131031, CVE-2026-131060, CVE-2026-131008, CVE-2026-131054, CVE-2026-130975 (Google Chrome), CVE-2026-132165 (Drupal), CVE-2026-123890, CVE-2026-119618 (Broadcom VMware), CVE-2026-114202, CVE-2026-114204, CVE-2026-114205 (ASUS Control Center Express Agent), CVE-2026-126574 (ASUS Control Center), CVE-2026-112115 (ASUS Armoury Crate), CVE-2026-99312, CVE-2026-99362 (Linux kernel), CVE-2026-132798 (Temenos Application Framework Java), CVE-2026-134624 (N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud), CVE-2026-131914 (Idunno.AntiCsrf), CVE-2026-125396 aka Upload2Shell (Ghostscript), CVE-2026-129975 (GPGME), GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 (MONAI Label), CVE-2026-23871 (WhatsApp for Android and WhatsApp Business for Android), and CVE-2026-134814 (binary-parser).
🎥 Cybersecurity Webinars
- 6,000 Social Engineering Attacks Reveal Why MFA Still Fails to Stop Account Takeovers → AI-powered phishing and voice scams are evolving, while attackers exploit weaker authentication and recovery paths to bypass MFA. Join this webinar to uncover real attack techniques and learn how to prevent account takeovers.
- 8 Million Security Events Reveal Why Attackers Can Hide Behind Tools You Already Trust → Attackers abuse legitimate IT tools to evade detection, but only about 12 in a million uses are malicious. Join this webinar to learn how to distinguish real threats from normal activity without drowning in alerts.
- Your GitHub Actions Are SHA-Pinned. But Are They Actually Secure? → SHA pinning locks code to a commit, but doesn't verify its author or origin. Attackers can exploit this trust gap to sneak malicious code past security checks. Join this webinar to learn how impostor commits threaten CI/CD pipelines and how to defend against them.
📰 Around the Cyber World
- Google Cloud-owned VirusTotal has introduced new cipher-agnostic file-encryption verification across Windows and macOS sandboxes to check whether a suspicious file actually encrypts user documents upon execution. This has led to the detection of a .k404 extortion campaign that managed to go undetected by 75 static antivirus engines, while its companion binary ("K404T_Fidye.exe") only had 10 / 75 detections.
- The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has warned that threat actors can abuse an authenticated WhatsApp Web session to gain unauthorized access to a user's account, allowing them to read messages, send messages while impersonating the user, and misuse the identity of the account holder for fraud, phishing, social engineering, or other malicious activities. Users are advised to log out of sessions when not required and avoid signing in using public computers.
- A large-scale malvertising operation dubbed MoldyRoost that's leveraging advertising infrastructure to deliver iPhone exploit chain kits like Coruna, DarkSword, SilkPath (iOS 17.2.2 to 18.3), and GhostWave (iOS 18.7.3 to 26) with an aim to exfiltrate crypto wallet seed phrases, iCloud Keychain data, messages, and photos. "Just loading the landing page of a MoldyRoost ad on a vulnerable iPhone is enough to get infected," Confidant said. "The exploit runs while the landing page loads, with no decoy download or ClickFix-style command to paste. What MoldyRoost adds is expertise in distributing the exploit kits through malvertising." Only an iOS device running Safari is offered an exploit chain. Other devices are served a working decoy website, an empty frame, or a harmless landing page. More than 480 domains have been linked to the operation between May 12 and November 17, 2026. The activity has targeted over 47 countries, mainly Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, the U.S., South Korea, the U.K., and India.
- The average time from an infostealer infection to the threat actor logging in via the same credentials is only eight minutes in some cases, according to a report from Elastic Security Labs.
- Unknown threat actors have siphoned an estimated $133 million from Crédit Mutuel Arkéa by using the bank’s own account to wire the funds to other banks, from where it was potentially converted into cryptocurrency. "The attackers used Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account to make transactions to other banking institutions, which then potentially allowed them to convert this money into cryptocurrency via specialized platforms," the bank said, adding the attackers did not go through the accounts of customers at its federations or subsidiaries.
- Uber has confirmed that nearly 150,000 people had their personal information compromised after hackers broke into one of its AI suppliers. A filing with Oregon's Attorney General puts the number of victims at 149,346. The access data includes images of drivers' licenses and information extracted from them, including names, home addresses, dates of birth, and license numbers.
- Arion Kurtaj, a 21-year-old member of the LAPSUS$ group, pleaded guilty in a U.K. court to hacking Rockstar Games, Uber, BT, and Revolut, after being released from a secure hospital after he was deemed fit to stand trial. He was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay at a hospital due to the severity of his autism.
- Browser extensions associated with Lacuna Web PKI, Softplan Web Signer, Certisign WebSigner, Certisign CertiPlugin, and BRy Assinatura Digital have been found to be rife with critical vulnerabilities rated 9.6 on the CVSS scoring system. These digital signing extensions are used by millions of government agencies and legal, medical, and tax professionals. "All five make the same mistake, they let the website choose which DLL the vendor's native host loads," Bay Area Labs said. "Loading a DLL runs its code and the software built to verify signatures never checked the signature on the code it loaded and on Web PKI and CertiSign WebSigner, a malicious page or iframe, such as an ad, was enough, with no click. On Softplan Web Signer, opening a link was enough. On CertiPlugin and BRy, visiting the page was enough, and the page downloaded the payload automatically." The bug class has been codenamed Sign2Shell. The flaws could have allowed fraudsters to sign legal documents in victims' names and potentially breach major organizations. The issues have since been fixed.
- Anthropic has become the latest company to cut its coordinated vulnerability disclosure window from 90 to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues, as AI collapses bug discovery timelines. The new deadlines cover reports sent on or after January 1, 2027.
- Recovery from a ransomware attack takes a median time of 20 days, and nearly a third of victims require more than six weeks. "Only 32% were recovered within two weeks and 28% took longer than six weeks," Rubrik said. "The full case, measured until the customer was content to close it, had a median of 26 days and 45% of cases stayed open for more than 30 days."
- Fortra said it's tracking targeted, large-scale "mail bombing" attacks, followed immediately by IT support impersonation on Microsoft Teams. "In the attacks, individual users are being flooded with email, then contacted by the threat actor through Teams as the volume peaks," Fortra said. "In the calls, the threat actors are claiming to be representatives from Internal IT, providing the user both verbal and email instructions they claim will stop the flood, but in reality attempting to compromise the user account, system, or both."
- Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, has been sentenced to six years in prison in the U.S. for his role in conspiring to hack into at least a dozen companies' computer systems via smishing attacks and steal over $11.6 million in virtual currency from individual victims throughout the U.S. A member of the Scattered Spider group, Buchanan pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of aggravated identity theft in April 2026. He was arrested in Spain in June 2024 and extradited to the U.S. in April 2025.
- Igor Andreevich D'iu, a 25-year-old Russian national, has been indicted in the U.S. for allegedly acting as a spy of a foreign government to "conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company." Although the name of the company was not disclosed, it's understood to be Palantir Technologies. D'iu was arrested on October 30, 2026. "The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said United States Attorney Craig H. Missakian. He is said to have entered the U.S. illegally through Mexico in June 2026 and was instructed by co-conspirators on Telegram to "identify company employees, and photograph their laptop screens while they worked," as well as "include surveillance of company employees and their residences."
- At least $247 million of the stolen funds from the record-breaking Binance hack has now gone into coinjoins coordinated by Kruw to obscure the financial trail, Elliptic has revealed. "Almost all of these coinjoins were coordinated by Kruw, the most widely used coordinator for Wasabi Wallet users," the company said. "A coordinator organizes each coinjoin round, bringing together the users taking part, but never takes custody of their funds." Last week, blockchain investigator ZachXBT accused Kruw of knowingly helping the Lazarus Group launder stolen cryptocurrency assets, calling the threat actor their "largest" user. Arkham Intelligence has also identified 2,173.76 BTC, roughly $154.45 million, flowing into CoinJoin from wallets connected to the $387 million Bitget hack of September 2025, also linked to North Korea. Kruw.io was also the subject of an advisory issued by the U.S. Secret Service in May 2025. "Numerous illicit actors use Kruw.io to launder funds including the Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking collective also known as АPТ38 and TraderTraitor which is subject to U.S. and international sanctions," the advisory said. "The Lazarus Group has previously used Kruw.io to mix approximately $14.3 million in cryptocurrency stolen by the North Korean regime. The Lazarus Group is currently laundering some proceeds of the $1.5 billion Bybit hack through the Kruw.io service."
Conclusion
The tricky part isn't always finding the problem. It's knowing how far it has already spread. A stolen login can lead to another company. A fixed bug can leave infected devices behind. And a tool that worked fine yesterday might be the reason someone gets in tomorrow. There isn't always a clean ending once the damage is done.
That's it for this week's recap. Some of these stories need a closer look. Others are useful reminders to check the things we tend to trust without thinking. Either way, there's plenty here worth keeping an eye on. See you next week, hopefully with fewer surprises.

articles.text:

Today’s best Bambu Lab 3D printer deals

articles.title: Hasta cuántas personas puedes añadir en un mismo grupo de WhatsApp
articles.text:
WhatsApp aumentó el límite de integrantes que puede tener un grupo: ahora admite hasta 1.500 personas en una misma conversación, frente al tope de 1.024 que regía hasta el momento. El cambio llega de forma gradual a cuentas de Android y iOS, por lo que todavía no está disponible para todos los usuarios de la aplicación.
La actualización implica sumar 476 lugares a cada grupo, un incremento cercano al 50% respecto del límite anterior. La medida apunta a organizaciones, asociaciones, comunidades educativas y equipos de trabajo que utilizan la aplicación para comunicarse con un número elevado de personas dentro de un mismo chat.
Cuál es el nuevo límite de participantes en los grupos de WhatsApp
El tope de 1.024 miembros por grupo se había incorporado en 2022 y, aunque permitía reunir a comunidades numerosas, comenzaba a quedarse corto para colectivos que coordinan actividades o comparten información a través de la plataforma.
Con la ampliación, cualquier grupo que ya hubiera alcanzado el máximo anterior podrá sumar hasta 476 integrantes adicionales. Esto evita que los administradores deban dividir a los participantes en varias conversaciones paralelas para mantener a todos comunicados.
El nuevo límite de participantes en WhatsApp es de 1.500 personas por grupo, un 50% más que el máximo de 1.024 vigente hasta ahora. El cambio se aplica de manera automática a los grupos existentes, sin necesidad de crear uno nuevo ni de modificar su configuración.
Según informó WABetaInfo, el aumento no requiere ninguna acción especial por parte de los usuarios. Cuando la función se habilita en una cuenta, los administradores pueden añadir más integrantes directamente al grupo existente, sin que esto afecte el historial de mensajes ni obligue a trasladar a los participantes a otra conversación.
La ampliación también alcanza a los grupos vinculados con las comunidades de WhatsApp, una función que permite organizar varios chats relacionados bajo un mismo espacio. En ese tipo de estructuras, asociaciones o entidades con distintos equipos podrán incorporar más personas a cada uno de sus grupos internos.
Cómo se está desplegando la actualización en Android y iOS
WhatsApp está distribuyendo esta novedad de forma progresiva en las versiones más recientes de su app, tanto para Android como para iOS. Por ese motivo, algunos usuarios ya pueden superar los 1.024 miembros al añadir participantes, mientras que otros todavía se encuentran con el límite anterior.
Este tipo de despliegue por etapas es habitual en la compañía: primero habilita una función en una parte de las cuentas y luego la va extendiendo al resto. WABetaInfo señaló que, por el momento, no existe una fecha oficial para que la capacidad de 1.500 miembros quede disponible de manera generalizada.
Quienes administran un grupo pueden verificar si la opción ya llegó a su cuenta al intentar sumar nuevos participantes. Si la aplicación sigue sin permitir superar los 1.024 miembros, será necesario esperar a que la actualización se active en ese dispositivo en particular.
Mantener la aplicación actualizada favorece la llegada de este tipo de novedades, aunque no garantiza que se habiliten de forma inmediata, ya que la disponibilidad depende del despliegue gradual que realiza la compañía.
Qué implica este cambio para quienes administran grupos grandes
Para los administradores, contar con un límite más alto reduce la necesidad de crear chats paralelos cuando una conversación llega a su capacidad máxima. También simplifica la incorporación de nuevos integrantes, que pueden sumarse sin perder el historial previo ni empezar una conversación desde cero.
El impacto puede notarse especialmente en grupos que funcionan como canales de coordinación diaria, como los de asociaciones vecinales, centros educativos o equipos de trabajo numerosos. Concentrar la comunicación en un único chat ordena la gestión, aunque manejar una conversación con cientos de personas sigue requiriendo moderación y reglas de uso claras.
El aumento de capacidad no convierte a los grupos en espacios públicos ni suma miembros de manera automática. Los administradores conservan el control total sobre quién ingresa a la conversación y sobre la configuración general del grupo.
Por ahora, WhatsApp no anunció una fecha concreta para completar el despliegue de esta función. Su llegada depende de cada cuenta y, una vez habilitada, permitirá que los grupos existentes sumen más integrantes sin alterar su historial ni su estructura previa.

articles.title: Anthropic lanzó Claude Ship, una IA que revisa, corrige y aprueba el código de los programadores
articles.text:
Anthropic lanzó en versión de prueba Claude Ship, un conjunto de herramientas de su IA Claude que revisa los cambios de código propuestos por un programador, corrige sus fallas y decide cuáles están listos para incorporarse, según las reglas que fije cada equipo.
Esos cambios se llaman pull requests: propuestas para sumar código nuevo a un proyecto, que normalmente otra persona revisa y aprueba antes de que se integren. Según Anthropic, el objetivo es que el código se publique “tan rápido como los equipos lo escriben”, ahora que muchos programadores trabajan con asistentes de IA.
Claude Ship reúne tres piezas. La primera, Code Review, analiza cada propuesta, publica sus hallazgos y ya estaba disponible para el público general. Las otras dos, PR Steward y Claude Approvals, están en beta, es decir, en fase de prueba.
Tres agentes para revisar, corregir y aprobar
PR Steward actúa cuando una propuesta falla las verificaciones automáticas, tiene conflictos con otras partes del código o recibe comentarios de revisión. Después de cada cambio, deja un comentario con lo que modificó y cómo deshacerlo. Anthropic precisa que está diseñado para no aprobar ni fusionar propuestas.
Los desarrolladores pueden escribir “@claude” con una instrucción para orientar su trabajo, o “@claude stop” para que se detenga.
La decisión final la toma Claude Approvals, que aplica una política de aprobación escrita por el equipo en un archivo del repositorio, el espacio donde se guarda el proyecto. Puede aprobar por sí solo los cambios rutinarios si la política lo permite, y exigir revisión humana en otros casos. La empresa lo compara con un archivo de asignación de responsables, pero más flexible.
Para la mayoría de los clientes, Anthropic recomienda activarlo primero en modo de observación, sin que su decisión tenga efecto, para ganar confianza antes de exigir su visto bueno.
Quién puede usarlo y cuánto cuesta
Claude Ship está disponible en los planes Team y Enterprise de Claude, para repositorios alojados en GitHub. Los administradores eligen en qué repositorios se activa, el nivel de revisión (rápido, estándar o profundo), cuándo se ejecutan las revisiones y el límite de gasto mensual.
El uso se cobra por “tokens”, las unidades de texto que procesa y factura un modelo de IA, por lo que activarlo puede aumentar los costos de una organización. Según Anthropic, el monto depende de la cantidad y el tamaño de las propuestas, del nivel de revisión y de la frecuencia con que se ejecuta. Claude Approvals no tiene cargo base, pero sus clasificadores sí se facturan.
La empresa ofrece a organizaciones Enterprise elegibles al menos USD 10.000 en créditos para usar dentro de los 30 días posteriores a reclamarlos. El plazo para reclamarlos vence el 15 de enero de 2027 y se aplican condiciones.
Quedan fuera las organizaciones con retención cero de datos, con la configuración para el reglamento de salud HIPAA de Estados Unidos o con claves de cifrado administradas por el cliente.
El comando /ship para programadores individuales
Quienes no administran un equipo pueden probar la herramienta con el nuevo comando “/ship” de Claude Code, el asistente de programación de Anthropic.
Según la documentación oficial, el comando puede registrar el trabajo, subir la rama, abrir la propuesta en GitHub, revisarla y trabajar sobre los comentarios y las verificaciones fallidas. La fusión final la hace el propio programador, según sus permisos y las reglas del repositorio.
La documentación advierte que “/ship” avanza sin pedir confirmación: tras presionar Enter, solo muestra un aviso de unos segundos antes de registrar y subir los cambios. También recomienda revisar que no haya archivos con claves o contraseñas, porque la herramienta solo las detecta por el nombre del archivo. Requiere Claude Code 2.1.330 o posterior, y no funciona de forma continua en Windows nativo.
Anthropic informó que, en el equipo de Claude Code, las propuestas fusionadas más que se duplicaron entre junio y septiembre, mientras que la proporción de cambios revertidos cayó más de 40%. La empresa aclara que la revisión de Claude es una capa de un proceso más amplio. Anthropic indicó que “/ship” se despliega desde este 23 de noviembre en Claude Code y en su aplicación de escritorio.

articles.title: “La superintelligence arrive” : pourquoi l'avertissement du chef de l'IA de Meta agace au plus haut point
articles.text:
Alexandr Wang, le patron de l’intelligence artificielle chez Meta, prévient que la superintelligence est en route et que l’humanité pourrait en perdre le contrôle. Un cri d’alarme qui ne passe pas.
Car depuis le mois de septembre, les alertes sur une IA qui pourrait échapper à tout contrôle se multiplient. Et visiblement, Alexandr Wang, recruté l’année dernière par Mark Zuckerberg pour diriger sa super équipe de chercheurs, est lui aussi inquiet. Dans un essai partagé sur X.com, anciennement Twitter, il tire la sonnette d’alarme.
« Un esprit extraterrestre que nous ne comprenons pas »
« La superintelligence arrive », écrit-il. Selon lui, une IA plus capable que les meilleurs humains dans tous les domaines n’a plus rien de lointain. Son argument : la preuve de l’hypothèse de Riemann, un problème de maths resté sans réponse depuis 1859.
Obtenue par le mathématicien Levent Alpöge avec l’aide de Claude, elle a été validée par les communautés Lean et Mathlib, qui vérifient ces démonstrations par ordinateur. Wang y voit une découverte réalisée « avec l'aide d’un esprit extraterrestre que nous ne comprenons pas ».
Car Wang estime que Riemann est le sommet de l’intelligence humaine. « De nombreux physiciens s’accorderaient à dire que la découverte de la bombe atomique est un simple exercice à côté de l’hypothèse de Riemann », affirme-t-il. « Les lacunes restantes ne sont plus l'intelligence ; ce sont le savoir-faire propre à chaque domaine, la plomberie et l’expérimentation », poursuit-il.
Wang assure que les modèles seront « clairement assez intelligents pour automatiser toute la recherche en IA » et pour être « surhumains » dans leur propre amélioration. « Il est difficile d’imaginer un monde où l’humanité peut garder le contrôle d’une auto-amélioration récursive sans aucune contrainte », assure-t-il, et il en va de même face à une superintelligence « 1 000 fois plus intelligente et capable que les humains ».
- Tâches complètes de bout en bout
- Contrôles d’accès très détaillés
- Travail autonome en arrière-plan
Des alertes mais peu d’actes
De quoi susciter de vives inquiétudes chez le jeune milliardaire, qui réclame des progrès urgents en matière de sécurité et d’alignement, c’est-à-dire de respect des valeurs humaines. Il s’en prend aussi à une « pensée paresseuse » de l’industrie, qui juge la superintelligence inévitable et n’y voit qu’un problème à résoudre : la rendre sûre. « Nous ne devrions pas accepter un transfert de la société à l’IA », prévient-il, puis appelle l’industrie à s’écarter de la « voie par défaut », sans dire comment.
Un message vu des millions de fois, mais qui passe mal aux yeux de certains, puisqu’il ne propose aucune solution. « Ne nous laissez pas sur notre faim », a lancé Alexis Ohanian, cofondateur de Reddit. La commentatrice conservatrice Megyn Kelly, elle, s’en est pris à ceux « qui ont CRÉÉ ces monstres d’IA et nous annoncent l’air de rien qu’on sera tous au chômage, puis probablement tués ».
D’autant que Wang n’est pas le premier à lancer un tel cri du cœur. Il y a quelques semaines, Dario Amodei, le patron d’Anthropic, a averti que l’IA pourrait « dépasser notre capacité à comprendre et à contrôler ces systèmes », et demandé l’intervention d’évaluateurs indépendants. Mais rien ne semble pouvoir enrayer la machine, chaque géant souhaitant surpasser l’autre.
Pour preuve, l’éditeur de Claude vient de signer la plus importante entrée en Bourse de l’Histoire. Wang, pour sa part, affirme que la sécurité reste une priorité chez Meta. Mais si l’on s’intéresse à certains agissements de l’agent Muse, force est de constater que le risque 0 n’existe pas.
La superintelligence désigne une IA qui dépasserait les meilleurs humains dans pratiquement tous les domaines cognitifs : raisonnement, créativité, planification, recherche scientifique ou stratégie. Ce n’est pas juste un modèle qui excelle sur des benchmarks, mais un système capable de généraliser, d’apprendre vite et de résoudre des problèmes inédits avec une avance stable. La différence clé est l’avantage cumulatif : une IA très performante peut rester cantonnée à des tâches ciblées, tandis qu’une superintelligence aurait un spectre de compétences large et transférable. Dans ce cadre, le risque ne vient pas uniquement de la puissance brute, mais de la difficulté à anticiper ses décisions et ses priorités à grande échelle.
Lean est un assistant de preuve : un logiciel qui vérifie formellement qu’une démonstration suit des règles logiques sans trous implicites. Mathlib est la grande bibliothèque collaborative de définitions et de théorèmes utilisée avec Lean, qui permet de réutiliser des briques mathématiques déjà formalisées. Quand une preuve est validée par ce type d’outil, la confiance ne repose plus seulement sur une lecture humaine, mais sur une vérification mécanique pas à pas. Cela ne garantit pas que l’idée vient de l’IA, ni que la formalisation reflète parfaitement l’intuition mathématique, mais ça réduit fortement le risque d’erreurs de logique. En pratique, ça transforme un résultat « plausible » en résultat « vérifié formellement », ce qui change son statut dans la communauté.
L’auto-amélioration récursive décrit un scénario où une IA contribue à améliorer les versions suivantes (algorithmes, données, outils, architecture), qui deviennent à leur tour meilleures pour s’améliorer elles-mêmes. Le point sensible est l’effet d’accélération : si chaque génération rend la suivante plus efficace, le rythme de progression peut dépasser la capacité humaine à auditer, tester et encadrer. Le risque de perte de contrôle vient alors du décalage entre la vitesse d’évolution du système et la vitesse des garde-fous (évaluations, sécurité, gouvernance, déploiement). Ce n’est pas automatique : il faut des boucles de feedback réelles, des accès aux outils et une capacité d’ingénierie, mais le concept sert à expliquer pourquoi certains craignent une dynamique difficile à freiner.

articles.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
articles.text:
A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1.
"Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption()," according to a description of the flaw in the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
"Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled."
According to an advisory released by the project maintainer on November 11, 2026, the problem arose from the fact that some user-controlled string options were inserted directly into the generated JavaScript code without adequate validation.
The parser options include -
- length
- lengthInBytes
- key
- tag
- offset, and
- the alias passed to namely()
"Parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition is not affected," Keichi Takahashi, who maintains the library, said. "These options are now validated as identifier paths (e.g. foo, $parent.len). Expressions such as 'len - 1' are rejected; use a function instead."
CVE-2026-134814 can also be viewed as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-1245 (CVSS score: 6.5), another code injection vulnerability that was fixed back in January 2026 and resulted from insufficient validation of field names and encoding parameters.
"[The flaw] allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject and execute arbitrary JavaScript within the host Node.js process upon parser compilation," Upwind Security said in an X post. Users are advised to update to the latest version of the library for optimal protection.

Team Group Industrial Enhances S845 Embedded Storage Solutions
Team Group today announced the launch of two storage solutions featuring the Team Group INDUSTRIAL S845-25W 2.5" SSD and the Team Group INDUSTRIAL S845-M80W M.2 SATA SSD. As Edge AI continues to advance, embedded systems across smart healthcare, industrial automation, and defense surveillance increasingly require responsive performance, adaptability to demanding environments, and data security technologies. The S845 Series integrates reliability, durability, and data security with wide-temperature operation from -40°C to 85°C. Designed to accommodate diverse interface and space requirements, the series delivers flexible storage options for industrial environments.
Building on the embedded storage solutions introduced with the S745 Series, the S845 Series features industrial-grade 112-layer BiCS 3D NAND flash memory with up to 3,000 P/E cycles. By combining SLC Caching technology with Global Wear Leveling, the series not only enhances the stability of sustained sequential writes under heavy data workloads, but also effectively distributes and manages data processing efficiency. In addition, Advanced Garbage Collection eliminates invalid data during idle time, delivering reliable stability for industrial applications that require long-term operation.Seamlessly balancing performance and stability, the S845 Series complies with TCG Opal standards, utilizing hardware-based encryption to safeguard sensitive applications against unauthorized access and data tampering. Designed for demanding operating environments, the S845 Series has been certified for military-grade shock and vibration resistance and supports a wide operating temperature range of -40°C to 85°C, ensuring robust storage adaptability under extreme conditions. To maximize system management efficiency, the S845 Series further incorporates Team Group's proprietary S.M.A.R.T. function, enabling real-time monitoring of SSD health status.
Driven by the rapid development of industrial automation, Edge AI, and smart devices, real-time data processing, system stability, and data security have become top priorities in embedded applications. Team Group continues to expand its embedded storage and edge computing solutions to support high-reliability and long-term operational needs. In response to global memory supply tightness, Team Group remains committed to stable supply and quality, partnering with customers to capture growth opportunities in edge computing.

articles.title: Cómo ver quién usa tu cuenta de Netflix, Disney+ o HBO Max y cerrar sus sesiones
articles.text:
Netflix, Disney+ y HBO Max permiten revisar desde la configuración qué aparatos tienen la sesión abierta en una cuenta y cerrar los que no se reconocen. Según sus páginas de ayuda, el proceso lleva pocos pasos y conviene completarlo con un cambio de contraseña.
La revisión sirve en tres casos: cuando alguien usa la cuenta sin permiso, cuando se olvidó cerrar sesión en un hotel o en la casa de un familiar, y cuando la plataforma avisa de que la cuenta se comparte fuera del hogar.
HBO Max, por ejemplo, indica en su centro de ayuda que la suscripción se puede compartir con las personas que viven en el mismo hogar. Quien quiera dar acceso a alguien de fuera puede contratar un miembro adicional.
La compañía propone dos medidas ante accesos no autorizados: revisar los dispositivos conectados y restablecer la contraseña.
Netflix: una página para ver y cerrar sesiones
En Netflix, el punto de partida es la página “Administrar acceso y dispositivos”, dentro de la cuenta. Allí aparece el tipo de aparato, el último perfil que se usó para ver contenido y la fecha y hora de la última reproducción.
Para cerrar una sesión concreta, se toca la flecha hacia abajo junto al dispositivo y se elige “Cerrar sesión”. Para desconectar todos, se pulsa “Cerrar sesión en todos los dispositivos”, en la parte inferior de la página, y se confirma.
Netflix advierte de que la lista tiene límites. Los equipos pueden tardar hasta 48 horas en aparecer, y no se muestran los que llevan más de 90 días sin actividad ni los que solo se usaron para juegos de Netflix o para el sitio Tudum. La app para Windows puede figurar como un navegador Edge.
Si la sospecha es de uso sin permiso, la empresa recomienda primero cambiar la contraseña, que debe ser exclusiva para Netflix y tener al menos 8 caracteres con mayúsculas, minúsculas, números y símbolos. Después hay que cerrar la sesión en los aparatos desconocidos. Al desconectar todos, habrá que volver a entrar con la clave nueva en los que se quieran conservar.
Disney+: cerrar todo exige un código por correo
En Disney+, según su centro de ayuda (artículo actualizado el 14 de abril de 2026), se entra en DisneyPlus.com desde el móvil o un navegador, se abre el perfil, luego “Account” (cuenta) y, en “Access & Security” (acceso y seguridad), “Manage Devices” (administrar dispositivos). Junto a cada equipo aparece la opción “Log Out” (cerrar sesión).
Cada dispositivo muestra su tipo, la ubicación general del último uso, la fecha y hora de la última actividad y el perfil que lo usó, si es de una persona de al menos 18 años.
Para desconectar todo, Disney remite a la cuenta MyDisney, en my.disney.com. Hay que elegir “Access & Security”, luego “Log out of everywhere” (cerrar sesión en todas partes), escribir el código de un solo uso enviado al correo de la cuenta y confirmar.
La compañía precisa que esa opción también cierra sesiones en otros servicios de The Walt Disney Family of Companies y que borra los videos descargados en los dispositivos. La sesión actual se cierra de inmediato; las demás pueden tardar hasta 4 horas. La misma opción aparece al cambiar la contraseña o el correo.
HBO Max: dispositivos y contraseña
HBO Max indica que, ante sospechas, el usuario debe revisar qué dispositivos usan su cuenta. Puede cerrar sesión en algunos o en todos, con la guía “Gestiona dispositivos de HBO Max” de su centro de ayuda.
Después, la empresa pide restablecer la contraseña: se inicia sesión en hbomax.com, se abre la página de la cuenta y se edita la contraseña desde allí. La FAQ consultada corresponde a España; en otros países los precios y las condiciones del miembro adicional pueden variar.

Pour ceux qui préfèrent un smartphone intelligent plutôt qu'un monstre de puissance brute, le Google Pixel 11 a de sérieux arguments. Derrière son format relativement compact et son écran Oled lumineux de 6,3 pouces se cache la puce Tensor G6, spécialement pensée pour les usages liés à l'intelligence artificielle. Gemini, assistance photographique, retouches intelligentes et autres outils maison viennent enrichir une expérience Android 17 fluide et intuitive. Sans oublier l'un des grands talents de Google : la photo, avec un trio polyvalent comprenant notamment un véritable téléobjectif x5.
Tout n'est pas parfait pour autant. Son autonomie reste en retrait face à une concurrence de plus en plus endurante, tandis que sa charge filaire à 30 W manque franchement de peps. Heureusement, la charge magnétique Qi2.2 à 25 W et les sept ans de suivi logiciel viennent redorer son blason. Proposé à 649 € en version 256 Go chez Amazon, Boulanger et Fnac/Darty, le Pixel 11 devient une option particulièrement intéressante pour ceux qui veulent un smartphone doué en photo, intelligent et conçu pour durer.

Marre de devoir plisser les yeux pour lire un message en plein soleil ? Le TCL P80 Ultra pourrait bien devenir votre meilleur allié. Son originalité tient à son grand écran de 6,83 pouces, qui associe pour la première fois les technologies Amoled et NxtPaper. Résultat : une dalle lumineuse, aux reflets particulièrement bien maîtrisés, avec des modes d'affichage dédiés à la lecture qui rappellent le confort des liseuses. Un vrai bonheur pour les amateurs d'ebooks et ceux qui passent leur journée les yeux rivés sur leur écran.
Le reste de la fiche technique ne manque pas d'intérêt : batterie de 5800 mAh offrant une excellente endurance, certification IP68 et triple module photo avec téléobjectif x3. Sa puce Dimensity 7400 Elite assure l'essentiel sans broncher, même si les amateurs de performances extrêmes préféreront regarder ailleurs. On regrettera également une recharge un peu lente, l'absence de charge sans-fil et quelques apps préinstallées superflues. Mais à 449 € chez Amazon, ce smartphone atypique a largement de quoi séduire ceux qui privilégient le confort visuel et l'autonomie à la course aux benchmarks.
Trois smartphones, trois philosophies, mais un même constat : le Black Friday 2026 offre de belles occasions de monter en gamme sans nécessairement y laisser sa chemise. Reste à choisir celui qui mérite une place dans votre poche… avant que les prix ne remontent.

articles.title: Garmin adds dog profiles to its Fenix and Forerunner series — fitness watch update lets fans earn badges for their 'imaginary' pets
articles.text:
Garmin brings dog profiles to its Forerunner and Fenix series — and runners are already earning badges for their 'imaginary' pets
Turns out you can teach an old dog new tricks
- Garmin has added badges and achievements for dogs
- The new feature lets you add a dog to an activity
- People are taking part even if they don’t own any pets
Got a furry friend that you like to take out for runs and walks? Well, now your dog can score achievements and hit personal milestones during your activities, with its own record of badges to keep track of its progress. All you need is a Garmin watch and time to 'paws' and add in its workouts.
The new feature can be found in the 24.20 system software update that’s compatible with many of the best Garmin watches. You can also find it on other watches like the Forerunner and Venu series in software version 19.23 , which is rolling out now.
As part of the update, Garmin says that it has added “dog profiles, badges, activities, and activity data.” All you’ve got to do is whip up a profile for your pooch sidekick, then add it to any activities you feel like doing. Your dog will then have its own track record of achievements as it stays fit and active.
To get started, open the Settings app on your Garmin watch and head to Privacy and Profile > Dog. Add a pup profile, then just pick the ‘include dog’ option every time you go to edit an activity.
And with that, your device will log your own metrics and note that your canine companion came along for the ride (even if it can’t yet monitor their stats in addition to your own).
Add a virtual pup
The funny part about this new feature is that it doesn’t actually require you to own a dog in the first place — you can just add a fictional friend and have it come along on your runs and walks as a virtual companion. It’s like your own little mascot whose progress you can track, despite it not actually existing. As one Reddit user put it, “My imaginary dog will be joining me in many of my activities.”
According to a post on Reddit, there is a wide range of badges for pooches (real or imaginary) to earn. That includes achievements for recording an activity on International Dog Day (August 26), running certain distances (including 5K, 10K, a half marathon and more), recording three or more activities with a dog in one day, and finishing an activity with several dogs at once.

But while it doesn’t sound so serious, adding a companion (even if they’re entirely virtual) could help encourage you to get out and active even when you’re feeling a little ruff. And the good news is that Garmin’s Fitness Age feature doesn’t appear to work in dog years — for the time being, at least.

articles.title: Black Friday : votre prochain PC gaming pourrait commencer avec le Ryzen 7 7800X3D à 283,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Avec une remise de 43 % proposée par Amazon à l’occasion du Black Friday, le processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D revient actuellement à 283,99 €. Un prix intéressant pour ce CPU qui optimise les performances en jeu grâce à sa technologie 3D V-Cache.
Flambée des prix des composants oblige, la période actuelle est assez peu propice à l’assemblage d’un nouveau PC gaming. Mais c’est sans compter sur les remises d’Amazon durant le Black Friday. Jusqu’au 30 novembre, le processeur Ryzen 7 7800X3D est proposé à 283,99 € chez le cybermarchand, contre un prix de référence de 496,99 €. Avec ses huit cœurs et ses seize threads, ce CPU est particulièrement adapté à une configuration gaming. Il est conçu pour être installé sur une carte mère AM5 et fonctionne avec de la mémoire DDR5.
Le processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D est à 283,99 € chez Amazon, avec une remise de 43 %.
Pourquoi choisir le Ryzen 7 7800X3D ?
- Pour son cache dédié aux performances en jeu : les 96 Mo de cache L3 peuvent accélérer les jeux gourmands en accès mémoire.
- Pour ses huit cœurs : cette configuration permet aussi de travailler et d’utiliser plusieurs applications au quotidien.
- Pour son efficacité énergétique : notre test a relevé un bon équilibre entre performances en jeu et consommation.
Un processeur au potentiel évident dans les jeux
Notre test du Ryzen 7 7800X3D met notamment en avant le bénéfice de la technologie 3D V-Cache dans les usages gaming. Cela en fait un processeur particulièrement adapté aux joueurs en quête d’une fréquence d’images élevée, à condition de l’associer à une carte graphique adaptée. Le test souligne également l’efficacité énergétique du processeur, ainsi que sa montée en température modérée au regard de ses performances. Il a reçu la note de 8 sur 10.
Un choix orienté gaming plutôt que création intensive
Même si le 7800X3D d’AMD est sorti il y a quelques années déjà, son intérêt dans une configuration gaming est toujours d’actualité. En revanche, si vous désirez réaliser du rendu 3D ou des encodages intensifs, des processeurs dotés de davantage de cœurs peuvent s’avérer plus pertinents.
✅ Les points forts
- Performances en jeu et apport du 3D V-Cache.
- Huit cœurs et seize threads.
- Bonne efficacité énergétique.
❌ Les limites
- Carte mère AM5 et mémoire DDR5 indispensables.
- Système de refroidissement non fourni.
Disponible pour 283,99 € durant le Black Friday d’Amazon, le Ryzen 7 7800X3D peut se faire une place de choix dans une config’ gaming.
Si vous disposez déjà d’une machine AM5 ou que vous êtes en train d’en construire une pour jouer, alors ce processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D peut la compléter de manière efficace.
Pour une utilisation davantage tournée vers la création 3D, il faudra plutôt opter pour un CPU avec davantage de cœurs. De même, pour les usages essentiellement bureautiques, cette puce est sans doute trop puissante, et donc, trop chère.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
articles.text:
Threat actors are exploiting a now-patched security flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to target managed service provider (MSP) servers.
The activity revolves around CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host.
"On November 12, 2026, we observed one managed service provider's (MSP) technician's workstation exploited to run a guest-pushed batch file, which then reported to a Telegram bot, downloaded an installer from masterdarky[.]com, and started a rogue ScreenConnect client pointing at the attacker's own relay, all in about 9 seconds," Huntress security researcher John Hammond said.
The batch script, "update_224ac089.bat," is designed to decode a Base64 Telegram bot token and chat ID, and register the new infection. Subsequently, it downloads an MSI installer that masquerades as a Windows update ("WindowsUpdate.msi") to launch a ScreenConnect client, enabling the attacker to gain remote access to the technician's machine.
The activity, observed between October 20 and November 16, 2026, is said to have sprayed servers blindly, with Huntress observing at least 688,000 guest "run file" requests for files named update.bat or update_<8 hex>.bat hitting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses. The guests have been found to make repeated requests that have blank session names or default-looking Windows hostnames.
In another instance, a guest machine at 91.224.92[.]167 pushed a seemingly harmless text file ("marker.txt") two seconds after a technician joined a session, effectively acting as a canary to alert the operator that the exploit works against the target before sending the actual payload.
What's more, a targeted attack aimed at an MSP server in October 2026 had the attacker joining as a guest across three real sessions the technician had created and asked the client to run a file designed to drop a batch script ("Sync.bat") into the technician's computer's Windows Startup folder.
It's worth noting that this activity is distinct from a recently disclosed attack wave in which unknown threat actors gained unauthorized access to partner ScreenConnect environments by leveraging an authentication flaw in a third-party extension to deploy a malware toolkit called SCKit, which then exploits the flaw to propagate the malware to a technician's workstation.
The attacks also coincide with another cluster in which thousands of unauthorized ScreenConnect guest sessions have originated from machines with cryptocurrency exchange-themed names like BITMEX-BOT, KUCOIN-SRV, and LAPTOP-BINANCE to trick technicians into connecting to them. No following malicious activity such as file transfers or command execution has been observed.
Specifically, the threat actors have been found to obtain access to publicly downloadable ScreenConnect Access installers to extract the relay address needed to register a guest client with the corresponding ScreenConnect server, and then create fake guest sessions and make those sessions appear online.
"Someone is registering unauthorized guest computers on MSPs' servers, where they sit in these session lists. They come from a scripted emulator that impersonates a Windows ScreenConnect client, and nearly all of them had connected from a single IONOS-hosted IP, 74.208.158[.]106," Huntress said.
"As of November 13, we've seen related activity across at least 118 self-hosted ScreenConnect servers belonging to 109 Huntress-protected organizations. In total, we found 2,408 unauthorized sessions enrolled since November 3, 2026."
Organizations are advised to ensure that technicians' ScreenConnect host clients are updated to 26.6.5 or later, hunt for signs of exposure, isolate affected workstations, and rotate all credentials reachable from that workstation. If immediate patching is not feasible, it's recommended to remove the TransferFiles permission from roles and session groups.
"An MSP technician's workstation typically holds RMM consoles, saved credentials, and access to every customer, making it an exceptionally attractive target," Huntress said. "When a technician joins a remote session, their ScreenConnect host client and the guest machine can exchange files. Normally, the technician decides what moves and what runs."
"A malicious guest exploiting CVE-2026-84869 can push a file to the technician's machine and get the technician's own client to run it. From the technician's view, no prompt appears. They only have to join the session, whether from an attacker-controlled machine or a real customer's support session that the attacker has slipped into as an extra guest."

articles.title: “La junta ha decidido no reincorporar a Jensen”: el drástico giro de Nvidia en menos de 7 días
articles.text:
Jensen Huang volvió a la dirección de Nvidia como presidente y consejero delegado, tras una decisión unánime del consejo de administración que lo restituyó con efecto inmediato. La resolución llega apenas días después de que la propia junta directiva hubiera descartado esa posibilidad, en un vaivén corporativo que sacudió a la compañía de semiconductores más relevante del sector de la IA.
El anuncio del regreso impulsó las acciones de Nvidia un 31,8% en las operaciones previas a la apertura de Wall Street.
El rechazo inicial de la junta directiva a reincorporar a Huang
Días antes del anuncio final, la junta directiva de Nvidia había descartado la posibilidad de restituir a Jensen Huang como director ejecutivo de la compañía. La decisión se tomó pese a que el propio fundador había manifestado su disposición a retomar el cargo tras su salida, ocurrida en medio de un presunto caso de espionaje.
Colette Kress, quien ejercía como consejera delegada interina, confirmó esa postura en una entrevista con CNBC. “Jensen renunció a su puesto en Nvidia. Y la junta aceptó su renuncia. La junta ha decidido no reincorporar a Jensen. Esa es nuestra declaración y lo que la junta ha decidido hacer”, afirmó.
Kress explicó entonces que la prioridad de la compañía apuntaba en otra dirección. “Queremos enfocarnos en estos momentos en hacer crecer nuestro negocio. Queremos crecer en términos de todo lo que debemos hacer con nuestros empleados, nuestros clientes, nuestros accionistas, y eso es donde nos vamos a enfocar de ahora en adelante”, señaló la ejecutiva.
En ese momento, la junta ya analizaba perfiles internos y externos para cubrir el puesto que había dejado vacante Huang al frente de la empresa.
La apertura de Huang a un eventual regreso como CEO
En sus primeras declaraciones públicas tras su dimisión, Huang se mostró dispuesto a volver a liderar la compañía que fundó hace 33 años, siempre que la decisión partiera del consejo. Según declaraciones recogidas por Financial Times, el ejecutivo de origen taiwanés afirmó que consideraría un honor retomar el cargo si así lo resolvía la junta.
“Si el consejo considera que mi regreso beneficia a los accionistas, a los empleados, a la empresa y a Estados Unidos, me sentiría honrado de atender esa petición y volver a ejercer como director ejecutivo”, declaró Huang al citado medio.
Durante el fin de semana posterior a esas palabras, ganó fuerza una campaña pública para promover su reincorporación al frente de Nvidia. La iniciativa sumó incluso el respaldo condicionado del presidente Donald Trump, quien el lunes se mostró abierto a esa posibilidad.
El anuncio final del consejo y el respaldo a Colette Kress
Pese a la resistencia inicial, la junta terminó por revertir su posición. Nvidia informó que la reincorporación de Huang se produjo tras varias conversaciones con el ejecutivo, en las que los directores evaluaron su continuidad al frente del grupo y descartaron que su regreso supusiera riesgos para la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos.
Harvey C. Jones, presidente del Consejo, respaldó la decisión con una declaración difundida por la compañía. “El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar NVIDIA y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes. Tenemos plena confianza en Jensen y esperamos colaborar con él en su regreso al frente de la compañía”, afirmó.
Jones también reconoció el papel de Kress durante la transición. “Agradecemos a Colette Kress su excelente labor como Directora Ejecutiva interina, además de seguir desempeñando sus funciones como Directora Financiera de NVIDIA”, señaló.
El origen del escándalo: la investigación por presunto espionaje
La salida de Huang y todo el proceso posterior tuvieron su origen en una investigación independiente abierta por la junta directiva de Nvidia, con el objetivo de determinar si el entonces director ejecutivo pudo haber sido blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera. La revisión quedó a cargo de un comité de directores independientes, con asesoramiento legal externo.
La pesquisa se inició después de que informaciones periodísticas vincularan a Huang con una empresaria china investigada por autoridades estadounidenses. En ese momento, la compañía sostuvo que no tenía razones para creer que la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos o sus propios secretos corporativos hubieran resultado comprometidos.
La investigación puso bajo escrutinio tanto la conducta del entonces director ejecutivo como los mecanismos de gobierno corporativo de una compañía considerada decisiva para el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial a nivel global.
Por qué el caso trascendió lo personal y llegó al plano político
La controversia que derivó en la salida de Huang adquirió una dimensión política por las sospechas sobre posibles transferencias de chips avanzados a compañías chinas. La empresaria vinculada al caso había trabajado para Megaspeed, una firma de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur que se encontraba bajo investigación por un eventual acceso de China a procesadores de Nvidia sujetos a controles de exportación de Estados Unidos.
Las acusaciones contra la empresaria no fueron verificadas de manera independiente por medios estadounidenses, y China negó cualquier implicación en una operación de espionaje vinculada al caso.
Aun así, legisladores estadounidenses solicitaron explicaciones sobre el caso y plantearon la necesidad de endurecer las restricciones sobre las ventas de chips de inteligencia artificial al gigante asiático.

S’il est bien un constructeur chez qui Android ne s’embarrasse pas de fioritures, c’est Google. Son Pixel 10a profite d’une interface épurée, sans surcouche tierce ni avalanche d’apps préinstallées. Et avec sept ans de mises à jour promis par la firme de Mountain View, il y a de quoi prendre ses habitudes sans avoir à en changer de sitôt.
Le terminal a par ailleurs le bon goût de conserver un format relativement compact, à l’heure où les smartphones prennent toujours plus de place dans nos poches. Son écran lumineux, son dos parfaitement plat et ses prestations photo font partie de ses principaux atouts. Sur ce dernier point, Google maîtrise toujours aussi bien son sujet : pas besoin de jongler avec les réglages pour immortaliser un repas de famille ou rapporter de jolis clichés de vacances.
Certes, sa charge manque encore de peps et les nouveautés par rapport au Pixel 9a se comptent presque sur les doigts d’une main. Mais à 429 € chez Boulanger, contre 549 € à son lancement, le Pixel 10a a de solides arguments à faire valoir auprès de ceux qui veulent avant tout un bon smartphone, sans avoir à se soucier de sa fiche technique.

C’est un peu toute la philosophie de Fairphone, dont la sixième génération pousse assez loin le curseur de la durabilité. Grâce à sa conception modulaire, il est possible de remplacer soi-même plusieurs de ses composants, dont l’écran et la batterie, sans être un as du bricolage.
Mais le terminal du constructeur néerlandais a un autre argument qui nous intéresse tout particulièrement ici : son interface Android, débarrassée de tout logiciel superflu. Fairphone a même poussé le concept un peu plus loin avec son mode Moments, accessible via un bouton physique, qui permet de retrouver une interface minimaliste, limitée aux apps de son choix. Pratique pour profiter de son smartphone sans être constamment sollicité par ce dernier.
Le tout s’accompagne d’un bel écran Oled 120 Hz, de performances enfin à la hauteur de son positionnement, d’un suivi logiciel jusqu’en 2033 et d’une garantie pouvant atteindre cinq ans après enregistrement. Un investissement qui prend tout son sens si vous êtes du genre à garder votre smartphone jusqu’à ce que celui-ci rende l’âme… et qui pourrait bien vous éviter d’en arriver là.

articles.title: Black Friday Australia laptop deals for 2026: score up to 52% off Lenovo, Apple, Dell, HP and more
articles.text:
Black Friday Australia laptop deals for 2026: score up to 52% off Lenovo, Apple, Dell, HP and more
I'm tracking the best Australian discounts and you can save a bundle on a new notebook for home, work or gaming
Black Friday falls on 27 November this year, and runs through to Cyber Monday on November 30, but Australian retailers are offering great early discounts on a huge range of laptops.
You can get a Windows machine with 16GB of RAM for under AU$900, and there are also deals on lightweight 2-in-1s through to high-end gaming laptops. Apple deals are also better than usual, with some great prices on refurbished MacBook Neos, or new models from Amazon.
As TechRadar Australia's resident laptop expert, I'm here to help. I've been keeping tabs on price changes across the entire year, so I can confidently tell you what's an actual good buy and filter out all the bad deals. I've been hunting Black Friday deals since the start of the month, as many device-makers started their sales early, and will be here till at least December 3.
If you’re still deciding what to buy, our guides to the best laptops in Australia and the best gaming laptops explain what to look for. It’s also worth checking our HP coupon codes and Lenovo coupon codes if you’re buying direct.
Top retailers for Black Friday laptop deals
- Lenovo: great deals on a wide range of everyday and gaming laptops
- Amazon: sparse but solid laptop deals
- JB Hi-Fi: big discounts on Apple laptops
- HP: take an extra 5% off with code FUTURE5
- Mwave: deals on major PC brands
- The Good Guys: great for MacBooks and Microsoft deals
- Apple: much loved laptops but few discounts when buying direct
After something else entirely? Check out our full coverage of Black Friday deals and get your Christmas shopping done before the rush.
Everyday laptop deals
The Aspire Lite is a budget Windows laptop with a 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 anti-glare screen and a weight of just 1.3kg. The Ryzen 3 and 8GB of RAM are fine for browsing and streaming, and the 256GB SSD is reasonable for the price.
The IdeaPad Slim 3x gives you a roomy 15.3-inch, 1920 x 1200 IPS display and 16GB of RAM at an affordable price. Its eight-core Snapdragon X is well suited to everyday multitasking, though it’s worth checking that any specialist apps or peripherals you rely on support Windows on Arm.
The Dell 15 is well equipped for the money, with a 10-core Intel Core i5-1334U and 16GB of RAM to handle everyday tasks and multitasking. Its 15.6-inch display pairs a 1920 x 1080 resolution with a 120Hz refresh rate for a smooth experience.
The HP OmniBook 3 is an affordable big-screen laptop with a 17.3-inch, 1920 x 1080 IPS display that’s a good fit for watching movies at home. The Intel Core 5 315 and 16GB of RAM can comfortably handle everyday multitasking, and the 512GB SSD gives you room for apps and media.
The OmniBook 5’s 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 OLED display covers the full DCI-P3 colour gamut, so it’s a good pick for editing photos as well as watching movies. At 1.33kg it’s easy to carry, and the Intel Core 5 320 and 16GB of RAM are well suited to everyday use.
MacBook deals
This Apple Certified Refurbished MacBook Neo is an affordable way into macOS and comes with a one-year Apple warranty. The A18 Pro and 8GB of memory suit everyday use, and the 13-inch, 2408 x 1506 display is sharp for a laptop in this price range. Buying refurbished gives a decent discount compared to buying it new for AU$1,049 from Apple.
The MacBook Neo hasn't seen much in the way of discounts yet (in fact, it has had a price rise), so this meagre 5% off is the best we have seen. Still, it's something at least, and it's well worth checking out our MacBook Neo review for the full scoop.
This Apple Certified Refurbished Neo has a 512GB SSD for keeping photos and apps on the laptop, plus Touch ID for signing in and approving purchases. The A18 Pro and 8GB of memory make it a good everyday Mac, and Apple includes a one-year warranty. Buying refurbished gives a decent discount compared to buying it new for AU$1,249 from Apple.
The MacBook Neo hasn't seen much in the way of discounts yet (in fact, it has had a price rise), so this meagre 4% off is not far off the best we have seen for the 512GB model with Touch ID. Still, it's something at least, and it's well worth checking out our MacBook Neo review for a deeper dive.
This is the cheapest option going if you want the M5 Air and with the 512GB SSD. Want to know more? Check out our MacBook Air M5 review.
Apple has raised prices, and we have seen very few discounts so far, making this minor drop worth considering. This is the upgraded Air with the 1TB SSD and M5 CPU with a 10-core GPU (rather than the base spec 8-core) that costs AU$2549 from Apple. Want to know more? Check out our MacBook Air M5 review.
The 16GB MacBook Pro currently has a small discount from Amazon compared to buying it for AU$3,199 from Apple. Read our Apple MacBook Pro M5 review for the full scoop.
Thin and light laptop deals
The Yoga Slim 7 weighs just 1.16kg, yet its 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 OLED display gives movies deep blacks and rich colours. The Core Ultra 5 226V and 16GB of RAM make it a capable everyday laptop for travel.
While we have seen it about AU$200 cheaper, the current discount on the Yoga Slim 7i Aura is not bad. It features the new Series 2 Intel Core Ultra 5 226V CPU, a compact 14-inch 1920 x 1200 OLED display, plus premium features like a facial recognition webcam and Wi-Fi 7. Want to know more? Check out our Lenovo Yoga Slim 7i Aura review.
This Snapdragon-powered laptop has an impressive spec for the price, with an X Elite X1E78100 CPU, 32GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD. It also has a very nice 2944 x 1840 OLED touchscreen display that outputs 100% of the sRGB gamut. We have seen this machine slightly cheaper, but it's still a good deal if its Windows on Arm compatibility suits the apps you use.
MSI packs a 13.3-inch, 2880 x 1800 OLED display into a laptop that weighs under a kilo. The 32GB of RAM and 1TB SSD give you room to tackle bigger projects on the go, such as editing a large photo library.
2-in-1 laptop deals
The 14-inch, 1920 x 1200 touchscreen folds back for tablet use, whether you’re reading or browsing. This HP-refurbished model has a Core i5 and 16GB of RAM that is a good fit for everyday multitasking.
The 14-inch OLED touchscreen folds back for tablet use, and the included pen is handy for handwritten notes or sketches. At 1.38kg it’s light enough to carry to class, and the Core Ultra 5 226V and 16GB of RAM give it the performance to be a capable everyday laptop.
This large-screen 2-in-1 from HP uses the Intel Series 2 Core Ultra 7 258V CPU, giving it a good mix of performance and battery life. The 16-inch laptop also has a 2880 x 1800 OLED touchscreen, 32GB of RAM, 1TB of storage, Wi-Fi 7, Thunderbolt 4 and a facial recognition webcam. We have seen it for slightly less, but this is still a pretty good price if you want a big premium 2-in-1.
Gaming laptop deals
The Victus is an entry-level gaming laptop with an RTX 4050 that’s well matched to its 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080 display. The 144Hz refresh rate suits competitive games. Use BFDEAL at checkout to get the full discount.
The Cyborg 15 is an affordable option for 1080p gaming, with an RTX 5050 and a 15.6-inch, 144Hz display that suits fast-paced multiplayer games. The 16GB of RAM is a sensible starting point, though a few large game installs can easily fill the 512GB SSD.
The Lenovo LOQ Essential 15 is an affordable way to get RTX 5060 graphics, with a 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080 display that refreshes at 144Hz for smooth play in fast-paced games. The main trade-off is the GPU’s 65W power limit, so expect lower frame rates in demanding games than you’d get from a higher-powered RTX 5060 laptop.
The Legion 5i gives its RTX 5060 up to 115W, a good match for playing demanding games at the 15.3-inch screen’s native 1920 x 1200 resolution. The 1TB SSD is a welcome inclusion at this price, especially if you keep several big games installed.
The Gaming A16 is a relatively affordable way to get an RTX 5070 and a 16-inch IPS screen in the same laptop. The 165Hz refresh rate suits competitive games, while the 1TB SSD gives you room for a mix of multiplayer favourites and larger single-player titles.
The Legion 5a’s 15.3-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display combines deep blacks with a 165Hz refresh rate, so it suits both atmospheric single-player games and fast shooters. The 32GB of RAM also gives you headroom for demanding tasks beyond gaming, such as video editing.
Intel’s 24-core i9-14900HX and 32GB of RAM make this Legion a good fit for heavier workloads beyond gaming, including video editing and 3D rendering. Its RTX 5070 drives a 15.1-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display with a 165Hz refresh rate.
The Raider pairs a 140W RTX 5070 Ti with 12GB of video memory with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 display that runs at 240Hz. That’s an appealing combination for high-detail gaming, though the 512GB SSD is small for a machine in this class.
The Pro model of one of our favourite Lenovo laptops has a reasonable discount on the RTX 5070 Ti variant. The pre-discount web price is beyond steep, but at this sale price it's decent enough value for a premium gaming machine with an OLED, 2560 x 1600, 165Hz display.
The Legion Pro 7i pairs a 175W RTX 5080 with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 OLED display, giving demanding games plenty of graphics power and the deep blacks that make dark scenes stand out. The 240Hz refresh rate also makes good use of the higher frame rates you can reach in competitive games.
The Infinity Y16 pairs a 175W RTX 5090 with a 16-inch, 2560 x 1600 display, making it a good pick for playing demanding games at high settings. The screen’s 300Hz refresh rate is particularly useful for competitive shooters, where the GPU can push much higher frame rates.
For those who want mighty gaming power, the Legion Pro 7i with an Intel Ultra 9 275HX processor and RTX 5090 GPU is one of the better options going, despite the painfully high cost compared to last year. There are very few comparable machines at this price, making it an excellent deal if you are willing to spend big. Read our review to learn more.
Affordable RTX 5060 gaming
If you’re after a gaming laptop for under AU$1,600, the Lenovo LOQ Essential 15 puts its money in the right places for 1080p play. The RTX 5060 pairs nicely with the 15.6-inch, 144Hz screen, especially if you spend more time in multiplayer matches than chasing ultra high settings.
There’s one spec worth knowing before you buy. Lenovo gives the GPU 65W in this model, so a bigger laptop with the same RTX 5060 can deliver higher frame rates.
- Lenovo LOQ Essential 15 | Core i5-13450HX / RTX 5060 / 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD: AU$1,597 at The Good Guys
A refurbished MacBook Neo straight from Apple
If you’ve been waiting for a more affordable way into macOS, Apple has the 13-inch MacBook Neo in Indigo for AU$899 refurbished. That saves AU$150 over buying the same model new from Apple, and you still get a one-year Apple warranty.
The A18 Pro chip and 8GB of memory suit everyday tasks, and the 13-inch screen has a sharp 2408 x 1506 resolution. This is the 256GB version, so it’s worth checking how much storage you use on your current laptop before purchasing.
- Apple Certified Refurbished MacBook Neo | A18 Pro / 8GB RAM / 256GB SSD: AU$899 at Apple
An affordable 15-inch laptop
If you want a bigger everyday laptop with more power than the usual 15-inch fare in this price range, the Lenovo Ideapad Slim 3x is a very appealing option for just AU$878. 
Under the hood you’re getting a Snapdragon X processor, 16GB of RAM and a 512GB SSD, so it’s well suited to heavier everyday workloads. You also get a roomy 15.3-inch, 1920 x 1200 IPS display and fast Wi-Fi 6E.
- Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x 15.3-inch | Snapdragon X / 16GB RAM / 512GB SSD: was AU$1,599 now AU$878 at JB Hi-Fi
Black Friday Australia 2026 laptop deals are here
Morning all, and welcome to our live coverage of Black Friday laptop deals in Australia.
Black Friday officially lands on November 27 this year, but the sales have already started to roll in from the big brands and retailers. Some of them are genuinely great prices on machines I have been watching for months.
Others are... less impressive....
And that's what this live blog is here for. I spent the year tracking laptop prices and promos so I have a clear idea of what a fair street price looks like, and what a real discount is versus an inflated RRP. 
To vet a deal, I check its recent price history and prices during previous sales to see whether it is actually a saving worth caring about.
Laptops are usually at their most competitive around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but the volume of configurations, coupon codes and, uh, creative pricing strategies from sellers can make it hard to know where to start.
But fear not, as I will highlight the offers that stand out for value, not just the biggest percentage claims, whether you are after an affordable machine for work or study, a creator laptop with a colour accurate screen or a gaming rig from budgets big to small.
Behind the scenes I will be living in the glow of spreadsheets across four displays, and I will keep updating this page right through the Black Friday weekend and into Cyber Monday.
So bookmark this page and check it regularly to see the latest price changes and new deals.
