articles.title: 60 Millions de consommateurs : le patron de Free va reprendre le magazine... qui compare ses forfaits !
articles.text:
L'État a validé l'offre de NJJ Médias, la holding de Xavier Niel, pour reprendre le mensuel édité par l'Institut national de la consommation. Une majorité des salariés seront conservés, mais pas tous, et l'indépendance éditoriale du titre reste en question.
Les forfaits de Free figurent depuis des années dans les comparatifs de 60 Millions de consommateurs. Le fondateur de l’opérateur est désormais en passe de devenir le propriétaire du mensuel. Lundi 23 novembre, le ministère de l’Économie a confirmé à l’AFP avoir retenu l’offre de NJJ Médias, la holding de Xavier Niel.
L’emploi a pesé dans le choix de Bercy
Le magazine a été mis en vente après la dissolution de son éditeur public, l’Institut national de la consommation (INC), placé en liquidation le 31 mars. La loi de finances pour 2026 avait prévu la cession éventuelle de son activité de presse à un acteur privé. Trois candidats se sont manifestés, dont NJJ Médias et Que Choisir Ensemble, l’ancienne UFC-Que Choisir, qui édite le magazine concurrent Que Choisir.
Bercy juge l’offre de NJJ Médias la plus favorable à l’emploi et met en avant le projet présenté pour assurer la pérennité du titre. La Commission des participations et des transferts (CPT) doit encore publier son avis sur la valeur des actifs concernés. La cession doit être autorisée par un arrêté du ministre chargé de la consommation.
Le plan de sauvegarde de l’emploi prévoit le départ de 20 salariés de l’INC. Les 29 personnes reprises travaillent notamment à la rédaction et dans les services techniques. Bien que la CFDT a signé l’accord collectif, le SNME-CFDT juge toutefois le dispositif déséquilibré et critique notamment les conditions d’indemnisation des salariés les plus anciens.
L’indépendance des comparatifs en question
À ces départs s’ajoute, selon le syndicat, la décision de l’État de licencier les 22 journalistes pigistes qui contribuent régulièrement au titre. Le SNME-CFDT craint que l’équipe ne puisse plus produire le mensuel, alimenter le site et préparer les hors-série dans les mêmes conditions.
Le syndicat souligne que l’INC a renoué avec les bénéfices en 2025. L’institut a dégagé 236 000 euros de bénéfice pour 11,9 millions d’euros de chiffre d’affaires, après une perte de 719 000 euros l’année précédente. Le magazine comptait alors plus de 71 000 abonnés et vendait environ 20 000 exemplaires en kiosque par numéro.
Dès septembre, des élus, des associations et des syndicats ont alerté sur le risque de conflit d’intérêts. Xavier Niel contrôle le groupe Iliad, maison mère de Free, dont les offres sont régulièrement évaluées par le mensuel. La sénatrice Michelle Gréaume a demandé au gouvernement de préciser les garanties dont disposerait la rédaction pour enquêter sur les entreprises dans lesquelles le repreneur a des intérêts. Les modalités de cette protection restent à préciser publiquement.
Si le prochain comparatif de forfaits mobiles ou de box Internet tourne au désavantage de Free, le mensuel pourra-t-il encore le dire aussi librement qu’avant ?

articles.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
articles.text:
N-able yesterday disclosed a critical flaw it found while investigating the breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, an email filtering service it runs for managed service providers.
The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw. It allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing on the platform's servers.
The company fixed the flaw and restored access to the dashboard and APIs late on Saturday, closing an outage that began last Monday. Email delivery and spam filtering kept working throughout, according to the company. It has not said whether the flaw was the attackers' way in.
The bug sat in a connection check that Mail Assure runs for LDAP synchronization when a relay is configured. Before the fixed build, nothing restricted that check's destination, so the server could be pointed at any internal host and port to see which ones answered.
"An authenticated API user can cause the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.," the vendor's security advisory says.
The advisory gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3, and lists builds earlier than 20261121.1943 as affected, with that same build as the fix. It does not claim code execution.
N-able informed customers of a service disruption last Monday and initially traced it to platform configuration and service dependencies, according to its incident timeline.
Last Wednesday, the company said the outage was, in fact, a security incident: an unauthorized party had accessed one of the Hosted Cloud servers. The dashboard and APIs were kept offline as a precaution while it investigated.
It responded by taking the affected server offline, rotating internal platform credentials, revoking customers' existing API tokens, invalidating OAuth tokens, and resetting local users' passwords.
The company says it has found no evidence that customer data was compromised, including tenants' mailboxes, and no sign of exploitation beyond that one server since the fix was implemented.
The investigation is still open, and the breach is unrelated to the N-central incident, according to the company. In that earlier incident, it took its hosted remote-monitoring platform offline on November 9 after a researcher published 33 unpatched flaws.
For hosted customers, the work now is reconnecting. Scripts and integrations that used the revoked API tokens or OAuth tokens will need new credentials. The exact steps differ by setup: each partner has been emailed guidance specific to its environment, and anyone who has not received it is asked to contact support.
The hosted platform itself is already patched, according to yesterday's incident update, so there is nothing for Hosted Cloud users to install.
SpamExperts Local Cloud runs on customer hardware, with software updates applied on a weekly schedule, according to the product's update documentation. The incident statements describe the Hosted Cloud only, so Local Cloud operators should confirm their servers are on build 20261121.1943.
What the account so far does not say is how the attackers first got in, or whether any of the credentials they may have reached were actually taken. An outside digital forensics and incident response team has been brought in, and the company says a formal root cause analysis is due within two weeks of yesterday's update. Separate restoration times for quarantine, logging, and mailbox synchronization, which were being brought back in phases, have not been given.

articles.title: ASRock Industrial Unveils Robotics-in-a-Box to Democratize Physical AI Development
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
ASRock Industrial Unveils Robotics-in-a-Box to Democratize Physical AI Development
ASRock Industrial, a global provider of industrial computing and edge AI solutions, today announced the launch of RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box. Designed to simplify robotic AI development and make hands-on experimentation more accessible to researchers, educators, and developers, RBK-100 is an integrated Physical AI development platform powered by the ASRock Industrial NUC BOX-358H featuring the Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H. RBK-100 integrates local AI computing, an RGB depth camera, a 6-DOF leader-and-follower robotic arm set, and pre-installed AiRoboStarter software in a ready-to-use development platform. By integrating edge AI computing, visual perception, robotic manipulation, and software workflows, RBK-100 reduces system integration complexity and enables users to focus on AI model experimentation, robotic skill development, and real-world Physical AI applications.Key Capabilities of RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box
- AI-Ready Edge Computing: Powered by the Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H in the NUC BOX-358H, RBK-100 delivers local AI computing capabilities for robotic development, AI model experimentation, and Physical AI workflows. The platform comes with 32 GB DDR5 memory in the standard configuration or 64 GB DDR5 memory in the Advanced configuration, along with a 512 GB PCIe Gen 4 SSD.
- Integrated Robotic Vision and Manipulation: An integrated RGB-D camera captures color and depth information for robotic perception and object interaction. Combined with a 6-DOF leader-and-follower robotic arm set, the platform enables developers to record demonstrations and explore AI-based pick-and-place, object handling, and learned robotic skills.
- Physical AI Development with AiRoboStarter: The standard configuration includes 32 GB DDR5 memory and pre-installed AiRoboStarter software, providing a streamlined environment for developing, training, and executing robotic skills. Its workflow spans demonstration recording, dataset review, model training, and robot skill execution, with support for model workflows including ACT, Pi0.5, and SmolVLA support planned for a future release.
- Optional Agentic AI Integration with AiRoboStarter Advanced: Available with the 64 GB configuration, AiRoboStarter Advanced extends the development environment with an integrated agentic AI workflow connecting voice interaction, AI reasoning, visual perception, and trained robotic skills. Capabilities include speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), large language models (LLMs), vision, object detection, web search, custom APIs, and robot skill integration. Supported models, features, and performance depend on the software release and validated configuration.
"Physical AI represents an important step forward in bringing intelligence into the physical world," said James Lee, Chairman of ASRock Industrial. "Building on our expertise in edge AI computing, we see tremendous potential in making Physical AI development more accessible and practical. Through Robotics-in-a-Box, developed in collaboration with Intel, we aim to simplify the development journey from AI experimentation to real-world robotic applications, empowering researchers, educators, and developers to explore new possibilities and accelerate innovation in Physical AI."
"Scaling Physical AI requires more than powerful AI. It requires an open technology foundation that makes complex robotic systems easier to develop and deploy," said John Healy, vice president and general manager of the Industrial and Robotics Division, Intel. "Powered by Intel Core Ultra processors, ASRock's Industrial Robotics-in-a-Box gives researchers and developers an integrated platform to accelerate experimentation and turn promising robotics concepts into practical, real-world applications."

articles.title: ChatGPT passe à GPT-6.2 : ce qui change dans vos conversations avec l'IA
articles.text:
Une semaine après avoir présenté GPT-6.2 Astra et Sol, OpenAI déploie une version de sa nouvelle génération de modèles pensée pour les conversations du quotidien. Au programme, une meilleure compréhension des consignes et des images, des recherches web plus pertinentes, mais aussi quelques compromis.
Jusqu'ici réservée à ChatGPT Work, Codex et à l'API d'OpenAI, la nouvelle génération de modèles investit désormais l'interface conversationnelle classique du chatbot. Depuis ce lundi 23 novembre, OpenAI a commencé à déployer une variante de GPT-6.2 Sol, simplement appelée GPT-6.2 dans le sélecteur de modèles de ChatGPT, qui a fait l'objet d'optimisations spécifiques pour mieux répondre aux usages du quotidien, qu'il s'agisse de retravailler un texte, d'analyser une photo ou de chercher des informations sur Internet.
ChatGPT comprend mieux vos demandes et affine ses recherches sur le web
Parmi les améliorations revendiquées par OpenAI figure la capacité de ChatGPT à respecter des consignes complexes. Sur une série de requêtes conçues pour mettre le modèle en difficulté, le taux de réussite est passé de 62,5 % avec GPT-6 à 78,1 % avec GPT-6.2. Les progrès sont encore plus marqués dans la compréhension des images, avec un score de 71,7 %, contre 47,4 % pour la génération précédente.
OpenAI a aussi travaillé sur la capacité de son chatbot à mener des recherches sur Internet et à tenir compte des préférences de ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices. Sur une version interne du benchmark BrowseComp, qui évalue la capacité des modèles à trouver des informations difficiles à dénicher sur le web, GPT-6.2 a surpassé son prédécesseur à tous les niveaux de raisonnement testés, avec un taux de réussite de 64,5 % contre 54,4 % au niveau le plus élevé.
Dans la pratique, si vous lui demandez de comparer des hôtels, par exemple, ChatGPT devrait mieux hiérarchiser les résultats en fonction de vos priorités, qu'il s'agisse du prix, de l'emplacement ou des prestations proposées. L'IA devrait aussi mieux identifier les situations dans lesquelles il serait utile de vous proposer un suivi, comme vous prévenir lorsque le prix d'un produit baisse.
Une IA plus fiable, mais aussi moins souple
Dans le rapport d'évaluation qui accompagne le lancement de GPT-6.2, OpenAI fait état d'une baisse importante des hallucinations lorsque le modèle est confronté à des requêtes pour lesquelles des internautes avaient déjà signalé des erreurs factuelles. Les résultats sont en revanche beaucoup moins tranchés sur les autres questions factuelles et dans des domaines sensibles comme la médecine, le droit ou la finance, où les taux d'erreur restent comparables à ceux de GPT-6 Sol.
Plus paradoxal, si GPT-6.2 respecte mieux les consignes de réécriture d'un texte ou de modification du code informatique, il a aussi davantage tendance à privilégier les règles de comportement qu'OpenAI lui impose par défaut, y compris lorsque les internautes lui demandent de s'en écarter de façon légitime. Sur les tests destinés à mesurer cette capacité, le taux de réussite a chuté de 60,6 % à 48,6 %. Invité à défendre un point de vue sur un sujet controversé, le nouveau modèle est ainsi plus enclin à exposer aussi les arguments de la partie adverse, même lorsque l'exercice ne le demande pas.
OpenAI a par ailleurs renforcé les protections destinées aux mineurs, en intégrant ces exigences de sécurité à l'entraînement du modèle. Sur les conversations difficiles portant sur la dépendance affective à l'IA et les troubles du comportement alimentaire, le taux de conformité aux règles de protection des moins de 18 ans est respectivement passé de 77,1 % à 94,3 % et de 77,2 % à 92,9 %. Les évaluations de sécurité générales révèlent toutefois une légère hausse des refus opposés à des requêtes légitimes.
Le déploiement de GPT-6.2 a débuté à l'échelle mondiale pour les abonnements Plus, Pro, Business et Enterprise, sous réserve des paramètres définis par les administrateurs dans le cas de cette dernière offre. La mise à jour concerne le mode Instant ainsi que les niveaux de raisonnement Medium, High et Extra High, selon la formule souscrite. Le modèle GPT-6 Pro, propulsé par GPT-6 Astra, demeure inchangé, tandis que les générations précédentes de GPT (5.6 et 6) restent accessibles depuis le sélecteur de modèles. Les offres Free et Go ne sont pour l'heure pas concernées par ce déploiement, qui ne change rien non plus aux modèles déjà disponibles dans ChatGPT Work et Codex.
- Assistant IA extrêmement polyvalent
- Fonctionnalités gratuites nombreuses
- Automatisation de tâches complexes

articles.title: Nvidia se une a empresa de implantes cerebrales para hacer portátil el sistema que permite hablar
articles.text:
La empresa de neurotecnología Paradromics anunció una colaboración con Nvidia para achicar el equipo externo que necesita su implante cerebral. Ese equipo traduce en voz las señales de una paciente con enfermedad de neurona motora y hoy ocupa un carro con electrónica. Su director dice que en un año cabrá en una caja.
Matt Angle, fundador y director ejecutivo de Paradromics, dijo a Wired el 23 de noviembre que la paciente, una mujer de Michigan, podrá llevar esa caja sobre su silla de ruedas dentro de un año. A más largo plazo, según Angle, la electrónica será tan pequeña que cabrá en un teléfono.
El implante no se ve desde afuera. Pero decodificar lo que la mujer intenta decir exige mucha capacidad de cálculo, así que debe estar cerca del carro, conectado a un enchufe. Reducir ese equipo le permitiría moverse con el sistema, según Wired.
Qué aporta Nvidia al implante
Paradromics usará Jetson, un módulo de cómputo de bajo consumo de Nvidia, para que la decodificación del habla ocurra en un dispositivo pequeño y cercano al usuario. También usará Holoscan, el software de Nvidia que procesa datos de sensores, para que las respuestas lleguen con poco retraso.
Según MassDevice, ambas empresas se proponen que la voz se genere con un retraso menor a 10 milisegundos cuando el sistema traduzca directo del cerebro al habla, y menor a 100 milisegundos cuando primero convierta la señal en texto. Otro objetivo es que los modelos se reajusten solos cuando cambien las señales cerebrales.
David Niewolny, director de desarrollo de negocios de salud de Nvidia, explicó a Wired por correo electrónico que incluso pequeños retrasos hacen que la comunicación se sienta poco natural. Dijo además que Nvidia no tendrá acceso a los datos cerebrales a través de estas alianzas, y que trabaja también con Synchron, otra empresa de implantes.
Con modelos de Nvidia funcionando en el propio aparato, la voz podría hacerse más expresiva y no dependería de una conexión a internet, según Vikash Gilja, director científico de Paradromics, citado por Wired.
Un implante todavía en fase experimental
El dispositivo, llamado Connexus, tiene 421 microelectrodos que registran la actividad de neuronas individuales, según la Universidad de Michigan. Un transmisor en el pecho envía los datos por vía inalámbrica a un receptor externo. En noviembre de 2025, la agencia de medicamentos de Estados Unidos (la FDA) autorizó a Paradromics a probarlo en personas.
Los cirujanos de la Universidad de Michigan lo implantaron por primera vez el 17 de junio de 2026. La participante será seguida durante seis años. El estudio, de factibilidad temprana, evalúa sobre todo la seguridad a largo plazo, y el dispositivo solo puede usarse en investigación.
El 14 de septiembre, Paradromics informó que la mujer, de unos 60 años, eligió sus propias palabras, respondió preguntas abiertas y habló por teléfono con sus nietos. Esos resultados provienen de la propia empresa y de una sola participante. Un medio especializado, Medical Daily, señaló que aún no se publicaron en una revista científica con revisión de expertos.
Según MassDevice, el trabajo comenzará con el traslado de los decodificadores de habla de Paradromics a Holoscan, seguido de pruebas de consumo de energía y de su despliegue en centros de investigación asociados. En 2027, la colaboración se ampliará al control de movimiento, con modelos que combinan visión y acción.

articles.title: ‘It’s time to start running’: Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey says AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated defenses
articles.text:
‘It’s time to start running’: Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey says AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated defenses
Palmer Luckey says AI attackers are outrunning legacy defenses
- Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey claims AI-built exploits are outpacing legacy defenses
- Luckey predicted AI will favor defenders in the long run, but only if they move much faster now
- US officials say the recent outage wave came from botched updates and rushed patches, not cyberattacks
Palmer Luckey has a blunt message for anyone still running yesterday's infrastructure: "It's time to start running."
Speaking with Andrew Ross Sorkin at the recent The New York Times DealBook Summit, the Anduril co-founder and Oculus founder warned that AI tools are letting attackers build exploits faster than older systems can be defended.
The setting gave Luckey's warning extra weight, as that same morning, Vice President JD Vance pulled out of his own DealBook appearance shortly before he was due on stage, staying in Washington for meetings about a run of outages that had hit Microsoft, the FAA, JPMorgan Chase, Zelle and the National Security Agency.
An interesting argument at a time when the call was coming from inside the building
Luckey argued that the consequences of advanced AI are already visible, describing what is happening as "the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools" being used to create exploits. When Sorkin asked how worried people should be, he said it "depends on how well prepared you are," then added, without elaborating, that the audience would "find out what's going on soon enough."
The core of his case is a speed mismatch: On one side are attackers he called "very fast-moving," quick to put new technology to work. On the other are "old, outdated systems" that cannot adopt new technology as quickly as it is developed. People who say everything can be hacked, he said, "are right, for now." He also said US adversaries are exploiting that gap for strategic and financial reasons and singled out North Korea, though Luckey offered no specific incidents.
Luckey was not fatalistic about where this ends, however: In the long run, Luckey said, the advantages will "accrue to the side that is most effectively using AI for defense." The danger is the stretch between now and then, and he said, "people are going to have to pick up the pace."
What Luckey did not say, at least in the remarks reported, is that the outages themselves were attacks. That distinction matters here because nearly every official account also says they were not.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation-state," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNBC. Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio, speaking in Manila, said the country was "not under systemic attack" and that the incidents were not linked, the Associated Press reported.
Microsoft traced its two-day Outlook and Teams collapse to a cascading failure across its servers rather than an intrusion. The FAA's nationwide ground stop was reportedly caused by two newly installed HPE Juniper routers flooding its aging communications network with connection requests. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said there was "zero evidence of anything AI-related," while HPE said the router had behaved as its installer configured it, according to Implicator.
JPMorgan Chase blamed a software bug in on-premises hardware and said there was no evidence it was cyber-related, even as a ransomware group called n0n added the bank and Visa to its leak site, a claim JPMorgan has denied. Apple put its outage down to an internal update.
All roads lead to AI? Not quite
The NSA is where the story turns back toward AI. The agency's classified NSANet network recently went down, and while its own statement cited scheduled maintenance, Clayton said on Fox Business the failure followed a patch for major vulnerabilities disclosed last month, with patched systems failing to come back up as expected.
Those vulnerabilities have a name: PHP2Shell is a pair of critical flaws in the PHP runtime, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, rated 9.2 out of 10 and disclosed on October 21. Calif found one of them with help from an OpenAI model, and Wiz independently found both using frontier models from Google and OpenAI.
Wiz argued the episode shows how AI can "change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities," and says the bugs reach back to PHP 5.4. PHP powers an estimated 70% of websites, and in October 2026 sites as large as Wikipedia and the Internet Archive briefly went dark to patch.
This is where Luckey's speed argument and the official accounts converge: Attackers did not wait for even a moment. Amazon says it saw a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt four days before public disclosure, and Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince reported thousands of attempts in the 10 hours before the patch, climbing to hundreds of thousands within two hours. Within nine days, researchers had documented Chinese attackers chaining PHP2Shell with a Linux privilege escalation flaw to gain root on 25 servers, some tied to the US government.
Faced with that, defenders did what Luckey prescribes: they ran. Wall Street executives and the NSA told members of Congress that the outages came from rushed attempts to fix AI-identified vulnerabilities, The Washington Sun reported, citing three anonymous sources.
One congressional official said patches were being pushed through all at once, "more than the system was designed for." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CNBC that new technology is being layered onto very old systems, and warned that more such disruptions are coming.
Read that way, the outages are not evidence against Luckey's thesis; They are what the gap he described looks like from the defender's side: AI surfaces a decade-old flaw, attackers move within days, and organizations sitting on legacy stacks break their own systems trying to keep up.
The patch-rush explanation should not be stretched over the whole cluster, however: Microsoft's root cause was a latent bug introduced in a July 2026 update, well before PHP2Shell was disclosed. The FAA's trouble began with router work during a copper-to-fiber upgrade, and its administrator explicitly ruled out an AI link. Even the NSA and the DNI did not describe the agency's outage the same way.
Lawmakers have noticed the mixed messaging. Senator Mark Warner, the Intelligence Committee's top Democrat, said the White House had offered no clear explanation and that "people are freaking out," The National News Desk reported. Republican Representative Nick LaLota said he worried the week's events went beyond coincidence. Shoppers cleared Costco shelves of water and batteries, and most of its pricier generators sold out online.
None of this makes Luckey wrong about the threat. AI-driven offense is well documented. In September 2026, Gambit researchers described a likely Chinese, financially motivated operation in which autonomous AI agents stole more than 600,000 payment records, compromising 27 organizations to varying degrees in under a week, with roughly $7,000 in spend over four weeks. CrowdStrike and Censys have tracked ARTEX, an AI agent layer for reconnaissance, being used against South Korean banks, with more than 1,400 exposed consoles found online.
Via TechCrunch
Anduril: Not exactly a neutral party
Luckey is not a neutral commentator: Anduril sells AI-driven defense systems built around its Lattice software, has partnered with Booz Allen to run cyber capabilities on its Menace hardware, and recently landed a Navy deal worth up to $2.9 billion days after Luckey joined a Pentagon weapons initiative. "The side most effectively using AI for defense" is, among other things, a fair description of Anduril's sales pitch, and it echoes his earlier line that there is "no moral high ground in using inferior technology."
That does not make the argument wrong, but it does expose its gap. AI for defense is exactly what found PHP2Shell, and finding bugs faster only helps if organizations can ship fixes without breaking things. On this month's evidence, the bottleneck is less about detection than about legacy stacks, thin testing, and rollouts that cannot absorb emergency change at AI speed. Running requires legs that many institutions do not yet have.
Luckey may well be right that the public will find out what is going on soon enough. If the past week is a preview, though, the next big failure may look less like a hack and more like a fix.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf ("Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll") following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule HTTP module.
Idunno.AntiCsrf is a third-party ASP.NET IHttpModule designed to provide double-submit cookie Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection for ASP.NET WebForms applications. The open-source project is currently defunct and has not been updated since December 2008.
At its core, the problem stems from the fact that the module deserializes untrusted CSRF form token data using an unkeyed .NET System.Web.UI.ObjectStateFormatter instance without cryptographic MAC or signature verification when handling incoming HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms (System.Web.UI.Page) endpoints.
This behavior, in turn, can allow a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary remote code execution (RCE). Google's Mandiant division has given the vulnerability a "High" exploitability assessment, adding that exploitation hinges only on a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token.
LDB, Genwei Jiang, Dhanesh Kizhakkinan, Brian Bahtiarian, and Lucas Kossack of Google Cloud and Mandiant Incident Response have been credited with discovering the flaw earlier this month.
"A remote attacker can supply any non-empty value in the configured CSRF cookie alongside a Base64-encoded .NET ObjectStateFormatter gadget chain in the configured CSRF form field to execute arbitrary code in the context of the IIS worker process (w3wp.exe), resulting in complete compromise of the web application server," Google-owned Mandiant said in an alert issued last week.
"Active exploitation in the wild has been observed."
Google's threat intelligence team did not disclose any further details related to the activity. When reached for comment, Google told The Hacker News that it does not have anything to share at this time.
In the absence of an official patch, organizations still using the library are advised to discontinue its use and replace it with an actively supported anti-CSRF alternative such as follows -
- System.Web.Helpers.AntiForgery
- ASP.NET WebForms Page.ViewStateUserKey combined with MAC-verified/encrypted ViewState on postback forms
- ASP.NET Core Anti-Request Forgery (IAntiforgery)
"Audit all ASP.NET Web.config files and bin/ directories for references to Idunno.AntiCsrf or AntiCsrfModule, and review IIS logs for anomalous POST requests to .aspx endpoints returning HTTP 302 or HTTP 500 with elevated cs-bytes (where logged)," Google said.
"Environments with evidence of exploitation should rotate all secrets stored in Web.config and applicationHost.config (including <machineKey> keys, encryption keys, and database credentials) and inspect webroots for unauthorized files."

This may result in blocky artifacts, jagged edges, and a general loss of fine details, particularly when viewed on a larger screen. Simply increasing sharpness can make compression artifacts more noticeable rather than restore useful details.
Instead of simply applying a sharpening filter, Aiarty Video Enhancer uses AI processing to sharpen edges, enhance visible details, and reduce distracting pixelation. This helps give footage that has lost clarity a cleaner, more defined look, making fine textures and visual elements easier to distinguish.AI Video Denoising: Remove Noise While Preserving Details
Nighttime recordings, indoor videos, and footage shot at high ISO settings often contain visible grain or colored noise. These imperfections can become more noticeable when editing clips or watching them on a larger display.
The superVideo vHQ model in Aiarty Video Enhancer is designed specifically for noisy and low-light footage. It helps reduce visible noise while preserving important image details, making grainy recordings cleaner without unnecessarily smoothing out textures.Adjust Colors and Convert SDR to HDR for More Vivid Video
Older recordings and footage captured under challenging lighting conditions may look dull, washed out, or lack contrast. Color and lighting adjustments can help improve their overall appearance, making details and colors more visible.
Aiarty Video Enhancer provides controls for adjusting exposure, contrast, saturation, and other color settings, giving users more flexibility to fine-tune the overall look of their footage. It also supports SDR-to-HDR conversion with 10-bit output, allowing users to convert SDR videos into HDR output for compatible displays.AI Frame Interpolation: Create Smoother Motion
Gameplay recordings captured at 30 FPS can look less fluid when played on high-refresh-rate monitors. The same applies to action footage and other videos with fast-moving subjects. Frame interpolation can help by generating additional frames between the original ones.
Aiarty Video Enhancer supports AI frame interpolation with output options of 60, 90, and 120 FPS, allowing users to increase the frame rate of existing clips for smoother playback or video projects. AI models analyze motion between frames to generate intermediate images, helping create more fluid transitions between movements.
Harnessing Desktop Compute with Local AI Video Enhancement
When tackling heavy video enhancement tasks—such as upscaling a 25-minute standard-definition archive to crisp 4K—cloud-based solutions quickly run into bottlenecks. Subscription fees pile up, file size limits constrain workflows, and privacy concerns arise when uploading personal or proprietary footage to external servers.
Running optimization models locally on your own GPU, Aiarty changes the equation entirely:
- GPU Acceleration & Optimized AI Models: Aiarty supports NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Apple Silicon GPUs, as well as CPU processing. Its optimized AI models are designed to improve inference efficiency while maintaining visual quality. A dedicated Turbo Mode can further speed up processing with a subtle trade-off in output quality.
- Local Processing & Privacy: Video files are processed directly on your computer without uploading them to cloud servers or relying on cloud processing credits. This gives users more control over personal recordings and other video files.
- Batch Processing: Multiple video files can be added to the enhancement workflow and processed in batches, making it easier to work through collections of recordings without handling each clip individually.
Final Thoughts
We have reached a point where desktop hardware capacity is no longer the primary bottleneck in video restoration- having software optimized to saturate those hardware pipelines is what makes the difference. From polishing screen captures and enhancing digital camera footage to restoring legacy video archives, deep-learning models are making local video processing more practical than ever.

Black Friday 2026 : La batterie externe Anker PowerBank 25K 165W à 74,99 € (-25%)
Actuellement notée 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, la batterie externe Anker PowerBank 25K 165W assure une charge rapide et pratique grâce à ses câbles intégrés ainsi que son écran informatif. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 74,99 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 25 % et 25,00 € d'économie.
L'Anker PowerBank 25K 165W vise les utilisateurs en déplacement qui cherchent une réserve d'énergie importante et une charge rapide pour leurs appareils mobiles. Ce modèle haut de gamme associe une puissance de charge élevée à une ergonomie travaillée. Lors de son passage dans notre labo, cette batterie externe a convaincu nos testeurs par son équipement complet.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'Anker PowerBank 25K 165W descend à 74,99 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit environ 25 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 99,99 €. Cela représente une économie de 25,00 €.
Câbles intégrés et écran de contrôle : un équipement bien pensé
L'Anker PowerBank 25K 165W facilite les déplacements en intégrant directement ses propres câbles de charge, ce qui évite d'avoir à transporter des fils supplémentaires dans son sac. Notre modèle dispose également d'un écran LCD informatif très pratique, qui affiche en temps réel les données de fonctionnement pour surveiller la distribution du courant. Comme nous l'avons souligné dans notre test complet, la marque a aussi porté une attention particulière au risque de surchauffe lors des transferts d'énergie importants, ce qui sécurise les sessions de recharge prolongées pour vos différents appareils.
Anker PowerBank 25K 165W
Points forts
- Câbles intégrés très bien pensés.
- Écran informatif pratique.
- Attention portée au risque de surchauffe.
Points faibles
- 165 W annoncés, mais cumulés.
- Capacité réelle inférieure aux 25 000 mAh revendiqués.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).

Points forts

articles.title: Pour son VPN, Firefox rajoute un split tunneling par site
articles.text:
Le VPN gratuit de Firefox peut désormais être activé ou coupé pour des sites précis. Mozilla ajoute donc une forme de split tunneling à son navigateur.
Mozilla vient de publier Firefox 161 sur ses serveurs et le lancement officiel est prévu aujourd'hui. L'équipe s’est focalisée sur les améliorations du VPN intégré en apportant davantage de flexibilité.
Un VPN limité aux sites que vous choisissez
Le split tunneling, ou « tunnel fractionné », consiste à trier le trafic qui passe ou non par le VPN activé sur le système. D’ordinaire, cela permet de couper le VPN sur certaines applications. Certaines recevront donc votre vraie adresse IP tandis que d’autres verront celles du serveur géré par le fournisseur.
Firefox 161 applique ce principe site par site. Selon Mozilla, le VPN ne tourne qu’aux endroits où l’on veut plus de confidentialité ou une autre localisation. Il sera par exemple possible de l’activer en consultant sa messagerie ou pour éviter le ciblage géolocalisé sur les réseaux communautaires ou sites marchands.
- Gratuit et open source
- Protection renforcée contre le pistage
- Nombreuses extensions et personnalisations
Avec des mises à jour désormais passées à un rythme bi-mensuel pour le navigateur, les travaux s’accélèrent sur le VPN. Nous rapportions en mars, lors de son arrivée avec Firefox 149, qu'il s'agissait techniquement d'un proxy, c’est-à-dire un intermédiaire qui relaie les requêtes web. Il ne protège alors que le navigateur, avec un relais unique, un serveur choisi automatiquement et 50 Go par mois. Deux mois plus tard , avec Firefox 151, il devenait possible de choisir le pays de connexion. Ce nouveau réglage apporte donc encore davantage de flexibilité et devrait par ailleurs permettre de mieux gérer le quota de 50 Go mensuels.
Firefox 161 apporte d’autres nouveautés. Un raccourci permet de copier l’adresse de l’onglet actif. Il est possible de le configurer dans les paramètres, sous « Personnaliser les raccourcis clavier ». Une section de thèmes classiques arrive aussi, avec le thème Proton des anciennes versions, un thème OLED et des teintes unies. L’historique importé depuis Chrome garde désormais la fréquence de visite des pages. Les sites habituels remontent donc dans les suggestions de la barre d’adresse. Enfin, Mozilla corrige des onglets qui ne se restauraient pas après un redémarrage, lorsque la session renvoyait vers un groupe d’onglets supprimé.

articles.title: Cómo reconocer las trampas de diseño que empujan a comprar y a suscribirse antes del Black Friday
articles.text:
La Comisión Europea propuso el 11 de noviembre una ley que prohibiría los llamados patrones oscuros: diseños de sitios y aplicaciones que presionan o confunden para que el usuario compre o se suscriba. Como todavía es solo un proyecto, antes del Black Friday la defensa depende de reconocer esas trampas.
El texto, llamado Ley de Equidad Digital, es una propuesta que debe negociar el Parlamento Europeo con el Consejo de la Unión Europea antes de convertirse en norma, según el análisis publicado el 16 de noviembre por el estudio jurídico Addleshaw Goddard. Rige, por ahora, únicamente como borrador.
Su lista de prácticas prohibidas sirve igual como inventario de lo que conviene mirar con desconfianza, vengan de donde vengan las ofertas. La propia Comisión, en su documento de preguntas y respuestas, ofrece ejemplos concretos de cada una.
Tres señales de presión para detectar en la pantalla
La primera es la falsa escasez. La Comisión cita avisos como “Solo queda 1” o “¡5 personas más están interesadas!” cuando no son ciertos. Si el aviso no cita una fuente verificable, conviene abrir otra pestaña y comparar el precio y la disponibilidad en otra tienda antes de decidir.
La segunda es la culpa como herramienta. El documento menciona mensajes del tipo “Nos da pena que te vayas” y botones para rechazar una promoción con frases como “No me gustan las buenas ofertas”. Ninguno cambia el precio ni las condiciones: solo buscan que el usuario desista de cancelar o de darse de baja.
La tercera son las casillas ya marcadas. Según la Comisión, las opciones que el usuario debe rechazar, como un seguro o un producto extra añadido automáticamente al carrito, figuran entre las prácticas que la propuesta vetaría en todos los casos. Antes de pagar, revisar el resumen línea por línea evita cobros inesperados.
Un cuarto punto es el precio. La Comisión señala que la ley exigiría mostrar, en las filas virtuales de venta de entradas, el precio actual en tiempo real y el más alto posible. Hasta entonces, quien compra tickets debe confirmar el total final antes de ingresar los datos de pago.
Pruebas gratuitas y renovaciones: cómo no quedar atrapado
El problema que la Comisión describe es conocido: darse de alta es fácil y cancelar es difícil. Algunas pruebas gratuitas pasan a ser de pago sin que el cliente lo acepte, otras se renuevan sin aviso y, a veces, no hay manera de hablar con una persona.
La propuesta obligaría a las empresas a ofrecer una opción de cancelación sencilla y a avisar antes de que termine la prueba o se renueve la suscripción. También exigiría una confirmación activa del usuario para pasar a un contrato pago y garantizaría atención humana cuando otros medios no resuelvan el problema.
Mientras tanto, la guía de aplicación de la Comisión Federal de Comercio de Estados Unidos (FTC) sobre suscripciones plantea un criterio práctico: la cancelación debería ser al menos tan fácil como el alta y estar disponible por el mismo medio, por ejemplo la misma web o aplicación.
Esa agencia también considera inaceptable que se cuelgue el teléfono a quien llama para cancelar o se le dé información falsa sobre cómo hacerlo.
Una regla específica de la FTC que exigía un “clic para cancelar” fue anulada por un tribunal de apelaciones de Estados Unidos en julio de 2025, según el sitio de consumo Checkbook. El criterio general de la agencia sigue vigente como política de aplicación, según el documento oficial de 2021.
Pasos concretos antes de aceptar y para dar de baja
Los sitios de consumo coinciden en lo básico. Antes de dar los datos de la tarjeta, conviene anotar el precio completo, la fecha en que termina la prueba y dónde se cancela. Una captura de pantalla de la oferta y el correo de confirmación sirven como prueba si hay un reclamo posterior.
Para evitar sorpresas, se puede poner un recordatorio en el calendario unos días antes del vencimiento de la prueba. Al cancelar, se recomienda guardar la confirmación. Checkbook sugiere pagar las suscripciones con tarjeta de crédito, porque permite disputar un cobro indebido con el banco, algo que suele ser más difícil con una tarjeta de débito.
La Comisión Europea mantiene en su sitio la propuesta, los anexos y el análisis de impacto de la Ley de Equidad Digital. La propuesta debe ahora pasar por el Parlamento Europeo y el Consejo antes de poder aplicarse en la Unión Europea.

articles.title: Timekettle’s LiveTalk AI earbuds are the closest thing to a Babel Fish
articles.text:
Timekettle LiveTalk Black Friday deal: save 20% on the closest thing yet to a real-life Babel Fish
AI-powered summaries help you review important conversations
In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Douglas Adams' Babel Fish promised us real-time translation right in our ears. And while TimeKettle's LiveTalk AI translation earbuds aren't quite that quick, they're as close as we've come yet to rapid-fire speech-to-text and speech-to-audio translation.
With Black Friday on the way, TimeKettle's LiveTalk AI Translation earbuds are now $103.20(was $129) at TimeKettle. The offer also includes a free Earbuds Cleaning Pen (worth $9.99) and one year of Extended Care (worth $13).
I'd recommend these buds to international travelers, business professionals, and students who regularly communicate in different languages and want hands-free translation assistance. Chatting in another language can be difficult, especially when you're travelling, attending international meetings, or speaking with clients overseas. The Timekettle LiveTalk AI translation earbuds are designed to help bridge that gap, offering real-time translations for face-to-face conversations, video calls, and presentations.
Timekettle LiveTalk AI earbuds support 54 languages, 108 accents, 25 offline pairs, four translation modes, dual-device connectivity, AI summaries, 200 monthly translation minutes, and four-hour translation battery life per charge.
Why we recommend it
In his four-star review, our expert Alastair said: "The translation quality is excellent and a huge improvement on using Google Translate." Speech-to-text is pretty fast, although speech-to-audio is slower, with a delay of around seven seconds.
He concluded: "When you factor in the different translation approaches and the range of translation options, these small, easy-to-use earphones perform surprisingly well for situations such as watching live presentations, some multimedia content and quick conversations."
Voice Call and Multi-Media modes support translated phone calls, video meetings, and other audio content. You can connect the earbuds to a phone and computer, making them useful for Zoom or Microsoft Teams meetings without installing TimeKettle software on the second device.
Each earbud weighs just 6.9g and uses an open-ear design to leave the ear canal uncovered. Battery life is rated at up to four hours of continuous translation per charge.
Price context & historical value
The Timekettle LiveTalk AI translation earbuds have been reduced from $129 to $103.20 for Black Friday, saving you $25.80. This isn't the cheapest we've seen it - the earbuds have been as low as $97 in the past. The deal also includes a free Earbuds Cleaning Pen (worth $9.99) and one year of Extended Care (worth $13), bringing the total advertised value of the freebies to $22.99.
The Timekettle LiveTalk includes 200 free translation minutes each month, with additional plans costing $5.99 to $9.99 per month. An unlimited translation plan is also available for $14.99 per month.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Timekettle LiveTalk AI translation earbuds if...
You frequently travel internationally or attend multilingual meetings and want translation support for in-person conversations, calls, and presentations.
❌ Skip the Timekettle LiveTalk AI translation earbuds if...
You only occasionally need to translate a phrase while traveling, in which case a free smartphone translation app may be sufficient.
Also consider
The same product is also on sale at Amazon for a slightly higher price, but it comes with a free pair of Polypal P1 AI Translation Earbuds, worth $64.99, which support 43 languages and offer seven translation modes.
These Interpreter Earbuds support real-time translation across more than 50 languages, including two-way conversations, phone calls, and video meetings. They offer Bluetooth connectivity and compatibility with iOS and Android devices for business use.
The deal also includes two free gifts: a protective case worth $29.99 and one year of Extended Care worth $45, with a total value of $74.99.
If you buy this from Amazon, it's priced at $359 with a free pair of Polypal P1 AI Translation Earbuds, worth $64.99.

articles.title: Hackers Exploited GL.iNet Cloud Flaw to Install Malware on Routers and KVM Devices
articles.text:
Hackers exploited a vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service to install malware on some customer routers and KVM devices, the maker of travel routers and remote-access KVM hardware said in a security notice updated today.
The company identified and fixed the flaw on Friday and blocked the access the attacker used, so devices can no longer be infected through this route. The cloud-side fix does not remove malware from devices that were already infected, so owners still need to check their hardware and install the security firmware listed today.
A KVM is a small device used to control a computer remotely as if sitting in front of it. The company is still investigating whether computers attached to infected KVMs were affected.
It has not said how many devices were infected, when the attacks began, or how its cloud service was breached. It is emailing customers it identifies as affected, but owners do not need to wait for a message to act.
A model missing from the firmware table below is not necessarily unaffected, the notice says, and owners should not install firmware meant for another model.
RemoteToHome Consulting, a security consultancy that examined the incident on routers it manages, says in its incident investigation that it verified a root-level reverse shell on one of its GL-AXT1800 routers.
The shell started on Friday evening and connected to 170.39.226[.]219, and two more owners reported the same shell on the same model and firmware, 4.8.3, with GoodCloud switched on.
On GL-MT6000 routers, the same shell command ran but the connection never completed. On other routers the firm manages, a one-off command searched for files linked to a KVM implant and reported the result to the same address.
The shell leaves no files behind, and its traces vanish when the device restarts, per the firm's reverse-shell analysis. The process marker the vendor published was absent on the router with the verified shell.
After the researchers filed an abuse report late last week, the hosting provider told them it had suspended the server behind the address and preserved its data.
The shell arrived through the GoodCloud client software on the router itself, according to the firm's technical analysis. A handler in that client takes two values from a cloud message and runs them as root through the shell without checking them. The vendor has not confirmed that finding.
The unchecked code has been in the firmware since at least December 5, 2024, when it appeared in a GL-MT3000 release. It runs whether or not AstroWarp, the SD-WAN feature it belongs to, is in use, and its presence since 2024 does not mean attacks began then.
The researchers reported a second, separate weakness in the cloud client to the vendor yesterday and are withholding details until it is fixed.
One KVM owner described an infected GL-RM1 in an owner's report. Starting on Thursday, the device downloaded a script and two programs from 66.245.219[.]252, looked up the copycat domain gl-inet[.]top, and scanned the local network.
It also kept connecting to 65.20.71[.]131, which the owner suspects was a command channel. The owner did not keep the downloaded files, and the method by which the device was infected has not been confirmed.
The vendor advises checking the computer attached to an infected KVM for unfamiliar programs, accounts, startup items, and unusual network activity.
The investigation also found an unrelated, older backdoor on 49 of the routers the firm manages, installed in batches between September 2025 and May 2026 by a route that is not known. Nothing so far links it to last week's attacks.
How to Check a Device
GL.iNet's check looks for one marker: a running process whose details contain the exact text crond -i /tmp/.log. A line showing only the grep command itself is not a match.
- Router, web panel: sign in to LuCI under System → Advanced Settings, open Status → Processes, and search for tmp/.log.
- Router, SSH: run ps | grep tmp.
- KVM: open the device's own terminal under Toolbox → Terminal → Access, then run ps -a | grep tmp on the RMQ1 or ps -aux | grep tmp on other models. Run it on the KVM, not on the attached computer.
Check before rebooting or upgrading where compromise is suspected, the researchers advise, because the shell's traces disappear at restart. The marker can also miss infected devices: it was absent on the router with the verified shell.
Before running netstat on a suspect device, check that /bin/netstat is still a link to busybox. The command itself may have been swapped, a forum warning and the researchers' indicator list say, and running a compromised copy starts the malware.
The notice also points to an unofficial community check script, with the warning that the vendor has not reviewed it and that it can run with administrative privileges. Fuller indicators are in the researchers' detailed findings.
What the Update Does and Does Not Remove
GL.iNet listed stable security firmware for its router and KVM lines in the security notice it updated today, which now says the update "removes the malware identified in this incident without requiring a factory reset," with settings kept. That replaces earlier guidance, which offered a factory reset for infected devices ahead of the firmware's release.
| Model(s) | Minimum fixed version | 
|---|---|
| GL-MG1300, GL-MT3000, GL-MT6000 | 4.11.1 | 
| GL-E5800 | 4.10.3 | 
| GL-BE3600, GL-BE9300 | 4.10.2 | 
| GL-BE14000 | 4.9.3 | 
| GL-BE6500, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000 | 4.9.1 | 
| GL-BE10000 | 4.8.7 | 
| GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-SFT1200, GL-X3000, GL-XE3000 | 4.8.4 | 
| GL-MT2500 / GL-MT2500A, GL-X2000 | 4.7.14 | 
| RM1, RM1V2, RM10, RM10RC, RM1PE, RM4PE (KVM) | 1.10.3 | 
| RMQ1 (KVM) | 1.8.7 | 
In spot checks today, The Hacker News found the GL-MT3000 and GL-RM1 builds available at the vendor's router downloads and KVM downloads pages.
The update is not shown to cover everything a root-level attacker may have left behind. In RemoteToHome's KVM firmware analysis, upgrading an RM1 to the earlier 1.10.2 security build with settings kept carried the device's password file, SSH keys and user directory across, and that directory holds scripts that run at every boot. Whether a planted script survives the upgrade has not been tested.
For a device with signs of compromise, the researchers' advice is a firmware reinstall without keeping settings, and treating every stored secret as exposed: VPN keys, Wi-Fi and admin passwords, cloud credentials and SSH keys. The vendor's notice and that advice differ on this point.
Until a device is updated, the option the researchers describe is switching GoodCloud off, after first securing another way to reach the device. Switching it off stops the cloud client from running but does not clean a device that was already infected.
The attacker's identity, the number of affected devices, and how the cloud service itself was breached remain unknown, and The Hacker News found no CVE identifier for the flaw as of publication.

articles.title: Valve Opens Nominations for 10th Anniversary Steam Awards With 3 New Categories
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Valve Opens Nominations for 10th Anniversary Steam Awards With 3 New Categories
Valve has officially opened nominations for the 10th Anniversary Steam Awards, marking the special occasion with a new Hall of Fame awards category, which allows players to nominate a prior Game of the Year award winner as the best game of the last decade. That list includes Grand Theft Auto V, The Witcher III, PUBG: Battlegrounds, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Red Dead Redemption, Resident Evil Village, Elden Ring, Baldur's Gate III, Black Myth Wukong, and Hollow Knight: Silksong. 
The other categories are the standard fair of Game of the Year, VR Game of the Year, Labor of Love, Best Handheld Game, Better with Friends, Outstanding Visual Style, Best Soundtrack, Best Game You Suck At, Outstanding Story-Rich, and the Sit Back and Relax award. However, there are also a few newcomer categories that bring the total category count to 14: The "This Is My Job Now" award for real-world job simulators, the "Defies Description" award for games that mix genres and gameplay mechanics to the extent that they no longer conform to one specific genre, and the "Just Five More Minutes" award for games that suck players into a hole of "just one more level."Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards is open until November 30, and players can nominate any game they've played that fits the bill and was released in 2026, or they can choose from a list of popular and recommended games. Official voting for the Steam Awards starts on December 17.

articles.title: LEGO Harry Potter 76419 : le château de Poudlard de plus de 2 600 pièces perd 62 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 - Le LEGO Harry Potter Le château et le domaine de Poudlard (76419) est à 107,99 € (-36 %)
Plus de 2 600 pièces, Grande salle, tour d'astronomie, Saule cogneur et Ford Anglia : le château de Poudlard LEGO 76419 passe à 107,99 € chez Amazon.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, le set LEGO Harry Potter Le château et le domaine de Poudlard (76419) affiche 107,99 € contre 169,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 36 %. Il est noté 4,8/5 sur près de 3 900 avis, et plus de 900 exemplaires ont été achetés le mois dernier.
Le château de Poudlard et son domaine
Ce set destiné aux adultes et aux fans de l'univers Harry Potter compte plus de 2 600 pièces. Il reproduit la Tour principale, la Tour d'astronomie, la Grande salle, le hangar à bateaux, les cours, les serres, ainsi que les chemins et les ponts qui les relient.
Le paysage rocheux accueille le lac noir, et la maquette cache plusieurs lieux emblématiques des films : la chambre des secrets, la salle de la clé ailée, la salle de potions et la salle de l'échiquier.
Durmstrang, Beauxbâtons et le Saule cogneur
Le set comprend aussi le vaisseau de Durmstrang, le carrosse de Beauxbâtons, le Saule cogneur et la célèbre Ford Anglia. Une statue dorée de l'architecte de Poudlard et une plaque au nom du château complètent la présentation.
Une fois assemblée, la maquette mesure plus de 21 cm de haut et 35 cm de large, de quoi trôner sur une étagère. Elle peut aussi faire une belle idée de cadeau pour Noël.

articles.title: Free traduit désormais vos appels en direct dans 10 langues, et c'est gratuit avec l'un de ses forfaits mobiles
articles.text:
Free lance ce mardi Traduction Live, un service de traduction des appels en direct dans 10 langues, intégré à son réseau mobile. L'option, présentée comme une première en France, est incluse gratuitement dans les forfaits Free Max et Free Pro Max.
Un nouveau service arrive sur les forfaits Free Max. L'opérateur de Xavier Niel a lancé, ce mardi 24 novembre, l'option Traduction Live, qui comme son nom l'indique traduit les appels en direct, le tout sans application, dans dix langues dont l'anglais, l'espagnol, le japonais et le mandarin. L'outil, développé en interne, repose sur l'intelligence artificielle et s'active en pleine conversation par simple commande vocale. L'opérateur assure que les données sont traitées en France, et il y ajoute même deux options, avec le clonage de la voix et le résumé de l'appel par SMS.
Free peut désormais traduire vos appels en direct… avec votre propre voix
Que vous souhaitiez honorer un rendez-vous avec une personne dont vous ne partagez pas la langue ou que vous ayez besoin de bloquer une réservation à l'étranger, Free précise que le service Traduction Live couvre dix langues, à savoir l'anglais, l'allemand, l'italien, le français, l'espagnol, le mandarin, le portugais brésilien, le russe, le coréen et le japonais. « Chacun parle sa langue et tout le monde se comprend », résume Nicolas Thomas, le directeur général de Free. Votre interlocuteur peut être chez n'importe quel opérateur et décrocher sur un fixe ou un mobile. Vous pouvez appeler de France comme de l'étranger, où la 4G ou la 5G passe alors par les opérateurs partenaires de Free.
Il n'y a pas besoin d'application supplémentaire, car c'est le réseau de Free qui traduit, et non votre téléphone. Il suffit juste d'activer l'option dans l'Espace Abonné ou l'application bientôt fusionnée Free, rubrique « Mes options ». Les clients Free Pro, eux, l'activent une première fois dans leur Espace Client, puis l'allument et l'éteignent par SMS. Pendant un appel, que vous l'ayez passé ou reçu, on tape ## puis on dit « Ok Free, traduis en… », et il ne reste plus qu'à parler normalement. « C'est ultra simple à utiliser », promet Nicolas Thomas. Si vous n'avez pas besoin d'application, vous devez tout de même avoir un téléphone portable compatible VoLTE, VoNR ou appels Wi-Fi, qui sont les technologies qui font passer la voix par la 4G, la 5G ou le Wi-Fi.
Et Free a décidé de pousser le concept un cran plus loin encore, avec le clonage vocal. Plutôt qu'une voix de synthèse un brin robotique, la traduction peut reprendre la voix de celui qui parle. On peut aussi obtenir un résumé de la conversation envoyé par SMS une fois l'appel terminé, pour garder les détails d'une réservation, d'un rendez-vous ou d'un échange professionnel. Ces deux options s'activent depuis l'Espace Abonné ou l'application Free. Votre correspondant est prévenu en début d'appel et peut refuser le résumé en tapant « 0 ».
Une traduction des appels hébergée en France, mais pas infaillible
On imagine que confier ses appels à une IA, ça peut rebuter. Free insiste donc sur le fait que le service, construit par ses équipes à partir de plusieurs technologies d'intelligence artificielle, est traité sur des serveurs situés en France, qu'il exploite lui-même, probablement ceux de sa filiale cloud Scaleway. Les conversations ne sont ni enregistrées ni utilisées pour entraîner des modèles d'IA, et les transcriptions qui servent au résumé sont effacées dès son envoi. Un message vocal prévient même l'interlocuteur qu'il est traduit, et il peut s'y opposer.
Alors quelles sont les limites de l'outil ? Déjà, il ne fonctionne qu'entre deux personnes, jamais vers les numéros d'urgence (112, 15, 17, 18). Free reconnaît que la machine peut commettre des erreurs, des oublis ou des contresens, et que sa traduction n'a pas valeur à être certifiée ou professionnelle. Mieux vaut donc ne pas s'y fier seul pour une consultation médicale, une démarche administrative ou un dossier juridique. Concernant le prix, rien ne bouge pour les abonnés au forfait Free Max, lancé le 31 mars, qu'ils soient déjà clients ou fraîchement arrivés au sein de l'opérateur. « Comme d'habitude c'est inclus sans surcoût pour tous nos abonnés Free Max et Free Pro Max ! », se réjouit le directeur général de Free.
Et la concurrence dans tout ça ? À notre connaissance, aucun autre opérateur français ne traduit encore les appels. Orange, qui vient de lancer une application ouverte à plusieurs IA, a présenté il y a quelques jours un assistant intégré à son réseau, capable de prendre des notes, sans annoncer de date de lancement. Bouygues Telecom, lui, a commencé en juin à tester la traduction des sous-titres à la télé. À l'étranger, T-Mobile et Deutsche Telekom disposent déjà présenté des services similaires, avec une cinquantaine de langues. Nicolas Thomas le dit, Free « révolutionne la voix sur mobile ». Disons qu'il a surtout pris de vitesse ses rivaux français.

articles.title: Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
articles.text:
Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
She used eye tracking and gyroscopes for thumbstick control.
EEG machines are used to detect and record brain activity, so one enterprising tech enthusiast decided to use them to play GTA VI. Creator Perri Karyal showed her feat on X, where she streamed her gameplay while wearing a wireless electroencephalogram (EEG) designed for research.
Perri could be seen jumping a fence with Jason on a motorbike, before proceeding toward a parked fighter to steal and fly it. Her brain activity is overlaid on the screen while she’s playing, and viewers could also see the creator intensely focused on the game.
She trained the software to recognize specific brain signals and mapped them to an action on her Xbox controller. For example, imagining pushing a cube forward would correspond to a button press, getting angry lets her interact with cars and other vehicles, while picturing a hopping cricket would also make her character jump. The joysticks, on the other hand, are controlled via eye tracking and through gyroscopes on the head unit.
While Perri makes it look effortless, using the EEG device for gaming is way harder than what many people think. “People don’t realize how challenging it is!” Karyal replied to a comment. One viewer also mentioned the huge mass of brainwaves that appeared on the screen when she took off on the jet, to which she responded, “I was so stressed out. DO YOU KNOW HOW MANY TIMES I TRIED TO DO THIS.” Even though using wireless EEG for gaming does not have any apparent side effects, the creator said that she gets headaches after hours of gaming because of how much the headset squeezes her head.
This isn’t the first time that we’ve seen people playing games using just their mind. Neuralink has recently shown off one of its patients shooting at NPCs and even “threading the needle” with a speedboat using a brain-computer interface (BCI) chip. The big difference between Perri’s creation and Neuralink’s BCI, though, is that the latter requires invasive neurosurgery.
It may be surprising to think how a tech creator could beat Neuralink at its own game, but the latter has already applied the technology to multiple trial patients. We’ve seen them playing complicated games like World of Warcraft and Counter-Strike 2, while others used it for productivity and creativity, like editing a YouTube video.
These technologies are still in the development and trial phases or are being experimented on by enterprising creators and tech tubers. However, it also gives hope to individuals with limited mobility, as it gives them hope that they could regain some form of mobility and independence in the future.
