articles.title: Tamara expands debt financing facilities by $400 million with two global banks
articles.text:
Tamara expands debt financing facilities by $400 million with two global banks
- Saudi fintech Tamara has secured $400 million in asset-backed financing (ABF) facilities from Japan's MUFG Bank and Standard Chartered, comprising a SAR 749 million ($200 million) facility from MUFG and a $200 million expansion of its existing US dollar-denominated facility with Standard Chartered.
- The MUFG agreement marks the first Saudi riyal-denominated securitisation facility extended by an international bank to a fintech company in the region, according to Tamara. The financing incorporates Shariah-compliant structures.
- Co-founded and led by CEO Abdulmajeed Alsukhan, Tamara provides digital financial services to more than 26 million customers and 160,000 merchants across Saudi Arabia and the GCC.
- The financing will strengthen Tamara's funding capacity, support the expansion and diversification of its financial products, and create opportunities for further collaboration with Standard Chartered in cash management and debt capital markets.
Press release:
Tamara, a leading fintech platform in Saudi Arabia and the GCC, serving more than 26 million customers and over 160,000 merchants, has expanded its asset-backed financing (ABF) facilities with MUFG and Standard Chartered, totalling an initial value of $400 million. The agreements comprise a SAR 749 million facility with MUFG, equivalent to approximately $200 million, and a $200 million expansion of Tamara’s core USD-denominated facility with Standard Chartered. Together, the partnerships strengthen Tamara’s ABF funding platform and support the continued expansion and diversification of its product portfolio.
The agreement with MUFG Bank, Ltd., part of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), Japan’s largest financial group, marks the first time an international bank has extended SAR-denominated securitisation funding to a fintech in the region. The transaction demonstrates Tamara’s ability to attract global capital through locally denominated financing. It draws on MUFG’s global expertise, local market execution and Shariah-compliant financing capabilities, while reflecting continued international interest in the Saudi fintech market.
Standard Chartered’s $200 million commitment reinforces its support for the Middle East’s digital economy and Tamara’s growing contribution to the region’s financial ecosystem. The partnership creates opportunities to explore broader collaboration across cash management, debt capital markets and future strategic initiatives. It also strengthens the relationship by combining Tamara’s regional presence in digital payments with Standard Chartered’s international network and financing capabilities.
Abdulmajeed Alsukhan, co-founder and CEO of Tamara, said, "The commitment from MUFG and Standard Chartered reflects the strength of Tamara’s business model and growing international trust in the region’s financial services market. Together, these partnerships reinforce our funding capabilities and support our ambition to bring more innovative, flexible financial solutions to consumers across the Kingdom and the wider region.”
The agreements underscore Tamara’s role in connecting international institutional capital with Saudi Arabia’s evolving financial ecosystem as the company continues to expand its product portfolio. The partnerships also bolster its long-term funding strategy and support the Kingdom’s Financial Sector Development Program in line with Saudi Vision 2030, including its goals of increasing access to finance, strengthening non-bank financial institutions and developing alternative funding mechanisms.

articles.title: Tesla change en douce une règle clé de son pilote automatique : les grands excès de vitesse sont terminés
articles.text:
Voilà peut-être la roulette la plus piégeuse de toute l’industrie automobile. Vous la connaissez possiblement, celle qui se trouve sur la branche droite du volant des Tesla. Une fois la conduite autonome activée, il suffit de la manipuler pour augmenter ou réduire la vitesse de consigne. Les effets sont immédiats, et rappelés par le petit cercle bleu englobant l’inscription « Max » indiquant l’allure à ne pas excéder.
Comme tout système, l’ensemble détecte la vitesse maximale autorisée, mais laisse le choix au conducteur de fixer sa propre allure. Si la chose est là encore commune aux autres véhicules, cela pose réellement problème lorsque la voiture est équipée du FSD autorisant une autonomie quasi complète. L’ordinateur de bord a en effet une plus grande emprise sur les commandes, et nombre de propriétaires pourraient donc le pousser à la faute.
Du FSD au TAS : une mise à jour en apparence purement cosmétique
C’est d’autant plus vrai que le FSD peut dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la limite de vitesse détectée si on le souhaite ! Le véhicule peut ainsi en théorie filer à 135 km/h sur une nationale limitée à 90 km/h. Rejeter la responsabilité d’un excès de vitesse sur le constructeur est alors très tentant pour éviter la sanction. Sauf que l’esquive est désormais impossible avec la dernière version du système.
Ce n’est pourtant pas ce que suggère la mise à jour 2026.39.100, qui renomme au passage le FSD (Full Self Driving) en TAS (Tesla Assisted Driving). Le petit texte d’information concernant cette mise à jour précise que « cette modification concerne uniquement le nom de certaines fonctionnalités et certains textes dans votre véhicule, sans en altérer le fonctionnement ». Hormis les réglages d’ordre sémantique, rien ne bouge, vraiment ?
Une marge d’excès de vitesse sabrée à 10 % en toute discrétion
Certains utilisateurs ont tout de même signalé une nette réduction de la vitesse pouvant être excédée par le véhicule. On passerait d’un dépassement de 50 % à seulement 10 %. Pour reprendre l’exemple précédent, le FSD ne pourrait faire rouler la voiture qu’à 99 km/h sur une route limitée à 90 km/h. Et à chaque redémarrage, la marge de dépassement de la vitesse maximale serait réinitialisée à 0 %.
Pourquoi de telles modifications, au-delà d’évidentes raisons de sécurité ? Le but est surtout de répondre aux demandes souhaitées par plusieurs pays de l’Union Européenne, dont l’Allemagne, qui voulait un dépassement de la vitesse autorisée allant à 10 % au maximum. Le pays soutiendra donc le système lors du prochain vote d’approbation à l’échelle de l’Union Européenne. De quoi inciter la France à faire de même ?

articles.title: Contrata como empleada de hogar durante 4 meses a la mujer de un amigo y consigue que tenga derecho a paro en Vigo
articles.text:
Un juez de Santiago de Compostela ha anulado la multa de 7.501 euros que la Inspección de Trabajo impuso a un empresario de Vigo por contratar durante cuatro meses como empleada del hogar a la mujer de un amigo, una oficinista de más de 52 años que, gracias a esas cotizaciones, acabó cobrando el subsidio por desempleo. Tal y como ha contado La Voz de Galicia, la sentencia, dictada el 22 de septiembre de 2026, concluye que aquel contrato fue real.
Un contrato justo después de la negativa. La mujer había pedido en Vigo el subsidio para mayores de 52 años, pero se lo denegaron a mediados de noviembre de 2022. Y apenas dos semanas más tarde, el 1 de diciembre, el amigo de la familia la contrató a tiempo parcial como su empleada del hogar, en una relación laboral que terminó a finales de marzo de 2023. Poco después, ya en el paro, volvió a solicitar el subsidio, y esta vez se lo concedieron al acreditar esos cuatro meses cotizados.
Lo que vio la Inspección. Para los inspectores, aquello olía a fraude de ley. Y es que el empresario nunca había necesitado una empleada del hogar ni contrató a otra después de prescindir de esta, que además era la esposa de un amigo con el que había coincidido en el trabajo. En febrero de 2024 lo acusaron de actuar en connivencia con ella para que cobrase un subsidio al que, siempre según la Inspección, no habría tenido derecho sin ese acuerdo, algo que la ley de sanciones laborales califica de infracción muy grave. Le impusieron 7.501 euros de multa y le ordenaron devolver lo que ella había cobrado del subsidio.
Primero ganó la trabajadora. Pero la historia ya había pasado por los juzgados de Vigo. Cuando el Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal (SEPE) le reclamó el dinero a la mujer, ella lo llevó a juicio, y en 2025 el juez de la plaza número 4 de lo Social de Vigo le dio la razón y confirmó su derecho a las prestaciones que la Administración le había reconocido en su momento.
El razonamiento de Santiago. El juez de la plaza número 4 de lo Social de Santiago de Compostela parte de ahí: si en Vigo se descartó el fraude por parte de la trabajadora, tampoco puede haberlo por parte del empresario. Vamos, que no ve que ambos estuviesen compinchados. Y para dar el contrato por real se apoya en que el marido de ella había comentado a varios testigos que su esposa estaba buscando trabajo.
Según la sentencia, el hombre no tuvo empleada del hogar hasta que se divorció, y durante esos meses le fue transfiriendo el salario, porque el contrato era real y no un artificio para conseguir el subsidio.

articles.title: Cómo estar cerca de los hijos si hay una separación: consejo de tecnología para evitar discusiones
articles.text:
Las discusiones entre parejas separadas por temas relacionados con sus hijos son habituales y la tecnología ofrece una solución para evitar ese tipo de situaciones, que afectan la tranquilidad y vida del menor. A través de aplicaciones de crianza compartida es posible coordinar visitas, pagos de pensión y comunicación.
Estos espacios ponen orden al caos normal de ser padres sin convivir, dándole prioridad al bienestar del niño o niña, e incluso sirve como documentación durante procesos judicales.
Qué aplicaciónes de crianza compartida son ideales para padres separados
- Kinnai
Es una aplicación desarrollada en Chile y permite hacer seguimiento del régimen de visitas y del pago de la pensión alimenticia.
Su módulo de mensajería impide modificar o borrar los textos enviados. “Lo que se escribe ahí no se puede modificar ni tampoco borrar, lo que permite mantener un registro”, explicó Gonzalo Ibarra, su creador, a Las Últimas Noticias.
La app también ofrece la modalidad “Un Hogar”, pensada para parejas que viven juntas. Según Bruna Arlegui,cofundadora, esta función “ayuda a ordenar las distintas tareas de la casa y quién se hace cargo de ellas”.
- OurFamilyWizard
OurFamilyWizard cuenta con respaldo de profesionales del derecho de familia y tribunales de los 50 estados de Estados Unidos. Su mensajería no permite retirar ni editar textos y suma la función ToneMeter, que advierte sobre lenguaje potencialmente conflictivo antes de enviar un mensaje.
Incluye calendario compartido para programar tiempo de crianza, registro de gastos con gestión de reembolsos y un banco de información con datos médicos y horarios escolares. No ofrece versión gratuita y requiere que ambos padres acepten usarla y pagarla.
- TalkingParents
Esta plataforma construye un registro permanente de comunicación mediante mensajes, llamadas grabadas, calendario y almacenamiento de documentos. Su función Accountable Calling permite hacer videollamadas o llamadas grabadas sin compartir el número de teléfono personal.
Ofrece un plan gratuito con funciones esenciales, lo que la vuelve más accesible que otras plataformas legadas. Su enfoque, sin embargo, resulta reactivo: documenta el conflicto en lugar de prevenirlo y carece de filtros de inteligencia artificial o herramientas de seguridad emocional.
- BestInterest
Adopta un enfoque distinto al priorizar la prevención de conflictos sobre la documentación. Utiliza inteligencia artificial para filtrar mensajes de entrada hostiles, manipulativos o fuera de tema antes de que el usuario los vea.
También revisa los mensajes salientes y sugiere una redacción más neutral cuando detecta lenguaje que podría escalar el conflicto. Funciona incluso si la expareja no se une a la plataforma, ya que permite redactar y enviar mensajes manteniendo privado el número personal.
Sus registros quedan timestampados, son inalterables y exportables para mediación o procesos judiciales. Cuenta con versión gratuita que incluye mensajería ilimitada y acompañamiento de inteligencia artificial, aunque ofrece menos herramientas financieras integradas que otros competidores.
- 2Houses
La app se concentra en la gestión de gastos compartidos y los horarios de parentalidad. Su sistema permite registrar gastos relacionados con los hijos, rastrear quién debe qué monto y gestionar solicitudes de reembolso dentro de la propia aplicación.
Suma un calendario interactivo para horarios complejos, un banco de información con datos esenciales de los hijos y un diario donde los padres comparten noticias y fotos. Resulta una opción más asequible que otras plataformas legadas, aunque sus funciones de seguridad emocional son limitadas y su enfoque judicial es menor que el de OurFamilyWizard o TalkingParents.
- Custody X Change
Se diferencia del resto por centrarse en la construcción de planes de parentalidad y horarios de custodia con valor legal, antes que en la mensajería diaria. Su creador de horarios permite definir noches de estancia, días festivos y ocasiones especiales, mientras que sus plantillas generan planes de parentalidad estructurados y exportables.
La plataforma también produce informes que comparan el tiempo de crianza planificado con el real y entrega documentos listos para presentar ante abogados, mediadores o tribunales.
No incorpora filtros de mensajes con inteligencia artificial ni funciones de acompañamiento emocional, por lo que resulta más útil para padres que necesitan formalizar un acuerdo de custodia que para quienes buscan mejorar la comunicación cotidiana.

articles.title: Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox "puro" para iPhone
articles.text:
Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorrência no âmbito digital.
Entre várias outras medidas, a DMA determina que os usuários tenham a opção de escolher o navegador padrão de seus dispositivos. Isso também deu abertura para que outros motores de navegação pudessem ser usados no iOS.
Então, problema resolvido, certo? De acordo com a Mozilla, não. A organização explica que as condições determinadas pela Apple para que um navegador para iPhone conte com um motor diferente do WebKit são tão complexas que, até hoje, nenhum desenvolvedor conseguiu encontrar um caminho viável para isso.
Em um comunicado recente, a Mozilla conta o principal problema relacionado às condições da Apple:
Para usar o Gecko [no iOS], não podemos simplesmente atualizar o Firefox que as pessoas já usam e adoram. Teríamos que criar um aplicativo completamente separado, um segundo Firefox.
Depois, teríamos que pedir a todos os usuários do Firefox que baixassem a nova versão, transferissem seus favoritos, senhas e histórico e fizessem a transição manualmente, passo a passo, de modo confuso.
Onde, exatamente, está o problema? O Firefox é um software de distribuição global. Para se adequar à DMA, a Apple passou a permitir o uso de mecanismos alternativos ao seu, mas com a condição de que eles sejam distribuídos exclusivamente na região autorizada, e não em escala global.
A Mozilla teria então que ter um Firefox para iOS válido globalmente (a versão atual, com WebKit) e outro, com o Gecko, específico para a União Europeia. Pelo menos até o momento, é inviável para a Mozilla trabalhar com essa dualidade.
Na prática, isso significa que os usuários teriam que baixar um novo app e transferir manualmente seus dados para ele. A organização também considera esse aspecto inviável.
Por conta disso, a solução vislumbrada pela Mozilla é a de pressionar a Apple: “continuaremos lutando por condições realmente justas, não por uma brecha que prejudique os navegadores independentes”.

articles.title: En Vietnam hay una cueva tan disparatadamente grande que tiene sus propias selvas, sus propios ríos y hasta sus propias nubes
articles.text:
En las selvas del centro de Vietnam, cerca de la frontera con Laos, la vegetación es tan espesa que puede ocultar accidentes geográficos de dimensiones extraordinarias. Tanto es así que un hombre que conocía perfectamente aquel territorio encontró por casualidad algo que, durante casi dos décadas, fue incapaz de volver a localizar.
Una tormenta en mitad de la selva. En diciembre de 1990, Hồ Khanh, un vietnamita que se ganaba la vida buscando madera de agar, una materia prima muy apreciada en la elaboración de perfumes e incienso, fue sorprendido por una fuerte tormenta. Mientras buscaba refugio, encontró una abertura entre las rocas de la que salían corrientes de aire frío y niebla.
Desde el interior también llegaba el estruendo de lo que parecía ser un río subterráneo. Khanh decidió no adentrarse en la cavidad y continuó su camino cuando mejoraron las condiciones meteorológicas. No tenía ni idea de lo que acababa de descubrir.
El hombre que perdió una cueva gigantesca. Años después, Khanh contó su experiencia a unos espeleólogos británicos que exploraban el parque nacional de Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng. El relato llamó la atención de Howard Limbert, que comprendió que aquellas corrientes de aire podían delatar la existencia de una enorme cavidad subterránea.
Sin embargo, la espesura de la selva y la complicada orografía del terreno frustraron los intentos de localizarla. Finalmente, en 2008, Khanh regresó por su cuenta y encontró la entrada. En 2009 condujo hasta ella a una expedición científica.
15 pirámides bajo tierra. Lo que encontraron fue Sơn Đoòng, considerada la mayor cueva del mundo por el volumen de su pasaje principal. Según el estudio publicado en 2016 en el Boletín Geológico y Minero, la cavidad cuenta con 8.950 metros de longitud.
Su volumen estimado alcanza los 38,5 millones de metros cúbicos, una cifra que permite establecer una comparación extraordinaria: teniendo en cuenta que la Gran Pirámide de Guiza tiene un volumen aproximado de 2,6 millones de metros cúbicos, el espacio interior de la cueva equivale al de casi 15 pirámides de Keops. De hecho, algunos de sus tramos presentan dimensiones suficientes para albergar rascacielos de 40 plantas.
Todo comenzó con una grieta. Los investigadores sitúan el origen de la cueva entre hace dos y cinco millones de años. El agua aprovechó las fracturas existentes en el macizo de piedra caliza y comenzó a disolver progresivamente la roca. La combinación de un importante caudal fluvial y las características geológicas del terreno permitió que la cavidad alcanzara unas dimensiones excepcionales.
El proceso, además, continúa activo: los investigadores estiman que el caudal máximo anual del río subterráneo puede alcanzar entre 400 y 450 metros cúbicos por segundo.
Dos selvas dentro de otra selva. En determinados puntos, el techo de Sơn Đoòng se derrumbó y permitió que la luz solar penetrara hasta el fondo de la cavidad. Con el tiempo, se desarrollaron dos grandes espacios de vegetación tropical en su interior, con árboles de hasta 30 metros de altura. Los exploradores han documentado la presencia de monos, serpientes, murciélagos y numerosas especies de aves.
Las particulares condiciones de humedad y temperatura permiten incluso la formación de nubes dentro de la propia cueva. Uno de estos lugares fue bautizado por los expedicionarios como "Cuidado con los dinosaurios", por su parecido con los paisajes de la novela El mundo perdido, de Arthur Conan Doyle.
La Gran Muralla de Vietnam. La primera expedición de 2009 tuvo que detenerse ante una gigantesca barrera de calcita que impedía continuar la exploración. Los espeleólogos regresaron en 2010 y emplearon dos días en superar una ascensión de 90 metros mediante técnicas de escalada.
Al otro lado encontraron un pasaje de aproximadamente 400 metros que conducía a una segunda salida en mitad de la selva. Durante las exploraciones también documentaron estalagmitas de más de 75 metros de altura y fósiles de corales de unos 300 millones de años de antigüedad.
El desafío de mantenerla intacta. El descubrimiento despertó rápidamente el interés de la industria turística. En 2014 llegó a plantearse la construcción de un teleférico de unos diez kilómetros, una propuesta que generó una fuerte controversia por su posible impacto ambiental. National Geographic apostó por una alternativa menos invasiva y desarrolló en 2015 una experiencia virtual para recorrer la cavidad.
Lo más fascinante, sin embargo, es que los propios investigadores consideran posible que existan cuevas todavía mayores en aquel remoto macizo vietnamita. Al fin y al cabo, hicieron falta millones de años para formar Sơn Đoòng, una tormenta para descubrirla y otros 18 años para encontrarla de nuevo.

articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, ce smartphone Apple noté 5/5 perd 67,62 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le smartphone Apple iPhone 18 Pro 256 Go "5 étoiles" à 1 384,98 €
Actuellement noté 5 étoiles par notre rédaction, l'Apple iPhone 18 Pro se distingue par son écran très lumineux, sa puissance élevée et son autonomie de longue durée. Pour le Black Friday 2026, son prix tombe à 1 384,98 € chez Cdiscount, soit une baisse d'environ 5 % et 67,62 € d'économie.
L'Apple iPhone 18 Pro conserve le format monobloc traditionnel de la marque en intégrant une puce plus rapide pour assurer une puissance élevée au quotidien. Conçu pour répondre aux usages les plus exigeants sans concession technique, ce smartphone haut de gamme s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à un équipement photo complet et une autonomie solide.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'iPhone 18 Pro descend à 1 384,98 € chez Cdiscount, soit environ 5 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (1 452,60 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 67,62 €.
Un affichage OLED lumineux et une puce A20 Pro sans compromis

articles.title: Miren launches flexible application deployment platform built for the agentic era
articles.text:
Miren launches flexible application deployment platform built for the agentic era
Miren Inc., an agentic infrastructure company, launched its platform today to make it easier for developers to deploy applications anywhere they need, without requiring them to become a solutions expert or set up and configure the application.
Artificial intelligence coding agents have changed the playing field for developers by making it easier than ever to build applications, but getting that software into deployment has remained a challenge. Configuration of resources, storage and the actual end maintenance of infrastructure that keeps everything running can be a burden that requires constant attention.
“[Our platform] transforms a computer anywhere you want into a place for your application to live,” Chief Executive Evan Phoenix told SiliconANGLE in an interview.
Miren gives developers a way to turn virtually any computer, from a virtual machine or bare-metal server to a local system, into a platform for running applications. Developers write their code locally, or have an AI coding agent generate it, and then hand it over to Miren, which handles building, running and much of the configuration necessary to deploy it. Once deployed, the application is accessible through a URL, without the developer having to set up and manage the underlying infrastructure individually.
The idea is to take much of the heavy lifting off the developer so they can do what they do best: designing, coding and strategizing.
“I was always interested in this, like the application development is sort of like the final boss of someone’s great idea, right? They’re working on this great idea, and they’re like, ‘Oh, now I need to share it with somebody,'” Phoenix explained.
The deployment is easy. A developer logs into their virtual machine or bare-metal server and installs Miren server, which then acts like a technician on the other end, watching over maintenance and deployment. The developer can then code locally, sandbox and do all of their work on a laptop or local machine, and when they’re ready, deploy to production with a command.
Critically, all of a developer’s data and application resources exist and run on their chosen infrastructure, virtual machines and servers. Phoenix stressed that this provides customers the flexibility to run wherever they choose and however they like. One customer in particular wanted to run software inside a German sovereign cloud environment, something that could be difficult with traditional platform-as-a-service providers that restrict users to their infrastructure. Miren lets the customer choose an appropriate environment while keeping the same development and deployment workflow.
“We’ve really attempted to have people be able to control where it runs, but still have the ease and the flexibility of it just running on the internet at the same time,” Phoenix said.
Miren Cloud for coordination and discovery
Miren also provides a third service that complements the developer client and the server: Miren Cloud, which is optional for a standalone deployment. However, it becomes particularly useful when multiple developers need to work with the same infrastructure.
Miren Cloud provides the organizational layer, coordinating cluster discovery and authentication. A developer can log in, discover available clusters and present signed credentials to access them without manually managing addresses and certificates. It acts as a coordination layer for infrastructure, pointing to where applications are hosted and helping with domain name registration, credentials and other authentication and attestation needs.
“Miren is addressing one of the biggest challenges in modern application development: giving developers the flexibility to run applications anywhere without adding another layer of operational complexity,” said Paul Nashawaty, practice lead and principal analyst, application development at ECI Research. “As enterprises expand across hyperscalers, sovereign clouds and private infrastructure, managing distributed clusters becomes increasingly difficult.”
Nashawaty cited ECI internal research, noting that 61% of developers cite tool fragmentation as the biggest barrier, making more unified approaches to application delivery and operations a top need.
Bridging the gap between code and infrastructure
Alongside the platform, Miren is also introducing Workbench, an AI-powered infrastructure operator built into Miren Cloud that can help developers manage and troubleshoot their applications. Unlike coding agents that primarily work with application code, Workbench has access to deployed clusters and specialized knowledge of Miren’s infrastructure. Developers can ask it to investigate performance problems, examine logs and analyze traffic without having to manually navigate the underlying systems.
“Think of it as a teammate, a sysadmin teammate,” Phoenix said.
Phoenix added that many customers were already bridging the gap between development and deployment using their own AI coding agents, allowing agents to generate application code, deploy it and then check results. With Workbench, they can extend this into the operational environment where the application runs in production, where the agentic operator can investigate problems and help navigate issues specific to the end infrastructure and relate them back to the coding agent.
Miren is also introducing paid support packages, giving customers a direct line to the company’s team, which has primarily provided community support until now. Phoenix said the company is expanding Miren Cloud with services that improve the reliability of customer-operated infrastructure, including automatic database backups.
Phoenix also sees an opportunity to turn customer support into a continuously improving layer of automation. Rather than having engineers repeatedly diagnose the same problems for different customers, Miren wants to feed the knowledge gained from individual support interactions back into its AI operators.
In theory, that would allow the platform to recognize and resolve familiar problems before other customers encounter them, shortening the cycle between discovering an issue and making its solution available across the platform. This follows a broader industry trend in which companies have begun building self-diagnosing, learning AI agents that improve themselves.

articles.title: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
articles.text:
A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.
The lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the company’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.
“Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”
Park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.
When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma said, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”
Faith in the Process
Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the company would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”
Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.
Park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.
Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.
The lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It says the company’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.
In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching plan, which she completed in late 2023.
Changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.
Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.
In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.
On her new team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.
The incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly said Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.
A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had said. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.
During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly said she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”
The manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.
“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit said.
Park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.
Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.
In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”
Park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.
Park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time she returned to work. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.
“It’s really scary for me,” she said about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”
This piece was updated to clarify when Park said Figma implemented the recommendations from her medical professionals.

articles.title: The RTX 5090’s 16-pin connector just got a free pin-by-pin watchdog — RTX Lens taps Asus Astral, WireView Pro II, and MSI PSU sensors to alert your phone or shut down your PC
articles.text:
The RTX 5090’s 16-pin connector just got a free pin-by-pin watchdog — RTX Lens taps Asus Astral, WireView Pro II, and MSI PSU sensors to alert your phone or shut down your PC
With the right hardware, it compares current at both cable ends and alerts your phone.
A developer known as Codeh4ck released a free, open-source Windows app, RTX Lens, to help assuage melting power connector fears for owners of powerful RTX 5080 and 5090 GPUs. The app can read per-pin current information on Asus Astral cards, the WireView Pro II GPU monitoring device from Thermal Grizzly, and MSI MPG Ai1300TS/Ai1600TS PSUs, enabling an optional shutdown for persistent warnings. It works by reading current at the GPU, PSU, or both ends of the cable, and can even notify you by phone to provide extra protection for your investment.
The project’s README says that the app allows reading of “GPU power, pin currents, and temperatures at a glance.” The per-pin monitoring is the important part here, as the 12V-2x6 connection carries current on six 12V pins with a rating of about 9A, with Asus’s warning at 9.2A, and exceeding the per-pin limit has led to melted connectors. An RTX 5090 is rated at 575W of board power, which is close to the connector’s 600W rating. This led to the app’s construction, the developer says, due to “double paranoia about the 12VHPWR connector melting, since I own 2 5090s.”
For supported Asus ROG Astral RTX 5080 and 5090 GPUs, the app uses the open-source LibreHardwareMonitor library. The WireView Pro II already measures inline at the GPU connector, but the app can read and edit the device’s settings, mirroring the official app’s settings.
The MSI PSUs measure at the PSU side of each connector and reveal per-pin currents for both 12V-2x6 ports, as well as PSU temperature and fan status, although a USB data connection is needed for both the PSUs and the WireView. The project clarifies that “With an Astral or WireView Pro II, you can compare both ends of the cable.” All of the listed hardware has been tested on real devices, the developer says.
| Where RTX Lens gets its readings, per the developer’s README |  |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Device | Cable end | Per-pin data | Also reads | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Asus ROG Astral RTX 5080, 5090 | GPU | Current | Connector power, current totals | 
| Thermal Grizzly WireView Pro II | Inline at GPU | Current, voltage, power | Cable rating, temps, faults | 
| MSI MPG Ai1300TS, Ai1600TS | PSU (both ports) | Current | PSU temp, fan | 
| Other GeForce RTX cards | None | None | Clocks, temps, usage, VRAM, fans | 
The app allows users to set up warning profiles per device with thresholds and reminders, and optionally a shutdown when a warning persists. This would be used in cases of sustained overcurrent or uneven pin loads on Astral, or WireView device faults. The app’s service initiates a Windows shutdown after a set time, from one second to almost 24 hours. The app can also make performance recordings that are exportable as interactive HTML.
Additionally, it can configure MSI Afterburner Safeguard+ for the MSI PSUs with per-connector alarms and timeouts, emergency low-power profiles, or even a script for delayed shutdowns or optional methods of notification, like email. More customization is available, in this case, as the app can set the PSUs’ fan curves with up to six temperature points.
Phone apps for Android, using a sideloaded APK from GitHub, and the iPhone, through a TestFlight beta or sideloaded with iLoader, are available. The sideloaded iPhone app only shows warnings while it’s open and connected, though. Pairing happens by QR code on the same network, and remote access from outside the network requires a reachable address. The PC also must stay awake, with the service running, for local or remote connections to work. An alternative way to monitor is a read-only iCUE widget for the Corsair Xeneon Edge touchscreen, if you’re so inclined.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The ongoing melting connector problem has led to solutions in the past, including a vibe-coded safeguard that now limits the GPU if a pin current exceeds 9.5A for more than 15 seconds, then shuts down the system if it stays that high. That tool, 12VHPWR Guard, is limited to Asus cards; RTX Lens adds wider device support and more options. Some hardware already works to help here, as MSI’s Ai1600TS cut GPU power after about three minutes in our testing, and Cooler Master’s GPU Shield can scale down an RTX 5090 to 450W, but these are not an option, or the best option, for everyone.
RTX Lens updates have been fast, with five shipped releases in the last week or so, and the maintainer appears motivated to keep development going. The developer says the project is in a “beta-ish phase,” and that “Google Play Store and App Store releases are coming soon, pending approval from Google and Apple.”
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
articles.text:
Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
Mitte September hat der Bitkom neue Zahlen veröffentlicht. 57 Prozent der Unternehmen in Deutschland setzen inzwischen KI ein, ein Jahr zuvor waren es 36 Prozent. Mich haben zwei andere Zahlen aus derselben Befragung mehr beschäftigt. 66 Prozent aller befragten Unternehmen schätzen die KI-Kompetenz ihrer Beschäftigten als gering ein. Und nur elf Prozent schulen alle Beschäftigten im Umgang mit KI.
Die Lizenzen sind also schnell gekauft. Was danach kommen soll, ist in vielen Organisationen offen. Wie führt man ein Unternehmen dahin, KI sinnvoll zu verankern, wenn niemand weiß, wie das Ziel genau aussieht?
Der Plan ist auch eine Absicherung
Die naheliegende Antwort ist ein Masterplan. Drei Jahre, klare Meilensteine, ein Budget, das hält. Im ersten Schritt ist das nachvollziehbar. Aufsichtsrat und Banken wollen wissen, wofür Geld ausgegeben wird, und Mitarbeitende wollen wissen, woran sie sind. Ein Plan schützt außerdem den, der ihn geschrieben hat. Geht etwas schief, hat man sich zumindest an den Plan gehalten.
Bei KI ändert sich die Grundlage jeder Planung allerdings in Monaten. Modelle werden leistungsfähiger, Preise und Nutzungsbedingungen verschieben sich, neue Werkzeuge sind da, bevor die alten eingeführt sind. Viele etablierte Geschäftsmodelle stehen unter Druck und neue Geschäftsmodelle implodieren genauso schnell, wie sie entstanden sind. Und manchmal ist ein Werkzeug über Nacht weg, wie beim Ausfall von Fable 5. Ein Dreijahresplan ist veraltet, bevor er alle Gremien durchlaufen hat. Wer auf ihn wartet, verliert die Zeit, in der andere lernen.
Was ist die Alternative? Auf Sicht führen. Kurze Schritte. Schnelle Rückmeldungen. Korrekturen ohne Gesichtsverlust. Das ist in meinen Augen kein Kontrollverlust, sondern Realismus. Auf Sicht zu steuern heißt aber nicht, ohne Regeln zu fahren.
Vier Spielregeln für alle
Dass Verbote genau die unkontrollierte Nutzung erzeugen, die sie verhindern sollen, sehe ich weiterhin so. Was Mitarbeitende brauchen, sind verständliche Spielregeln. Bei uns sind es vier. Erstens ist die Nutzung von KI ausdrücklich erwünscht, und zwar über gesicherte interne Plattformen. Zweitens gilt der Datenschutz auch für KI: Vertrauliche und personenbezogene Daten, auch die unserer Kunden, gehören nicht unreflektiert in externe Werkzeuge. Drittens setzen wir KI verantwortungsvoll ein. Im Personalbereich fließt KI nicht in die Beurteilung ein. Wir nutzen sie erst im Nachgang, um mögliche Verzerrungen in unseren Bewertungen zu erkennen. Und viertens zeichnet, wer ein KI-Ergebnis nutzt, mit dem eigenen Namen dafür.
Der erste Punkt wird oft unterschätzt. Solange niemand laut sagt, dass KI erwünscht ist, nutzen viele sie heimlich oder gar nicht. Beides kostet. Der vierte Punkt beantwortet die Frage, die bei jedem KI-Ergebnis mitschwingt: Wer steht dafür gerade? Bei uns der Mensch, der es weitergibt.
Dazu kommt eine klare Aufgabenteilung. Ein zentrales Plattform-Team stellt die Infrastruktur bereit und prüft Datenschutz, Kosten und die Anforderungen des EU-AI-Acts. Welche Anwendungsfälle sich lohnen, finden die Fachbereiche und Projektteams selbst heraus, denn nur sie können beurteilen, ob ein Ergebnis fachlich taugt. Salopp gesagt: zentrale Plattform, dezentrale Ideen.
Lernen braucht feste Orte
Zurück zu den Bitkom-Zahlen. Eine Schulung ist schnell gebucht. Ob danach jemand KI im Alltag nutzt, entscheidet sich woanders: im Austausch mit Kolleg:innen, beim Ausprobieren, beim Nachlesen. Bei uns heißt das ganz praktisch: Im KI-Webfrühstück zeigen sich Kolleg:innen regelmäßig eine halbe Stunde lang remote, was funktioniert, mit Demos und Fragen. Im Code Retreat, unserem KI-Hackathon, arbeiten Teams einen halben Tag vor Ort an konkreten Aufgaben und zeigen am Ende ihre Ergebnisse. In einer internen Blogreihe lässt sich nachlesen, was andere gelernt haben. In unserer AI Community of Practice auf Slack kommen jeden Tag ganz praktische Tipps, Ideen und Fragen auf den Tisch, die sehr schnell beantwortet werden. Niedrigschwellig, intensiv, dokumentiert. Die Formate verlangen unterschiedlich viel Zeit, weil Menschen unterschiedlich lernen.
Mindestens so wichtig ist der Einstieg, und das nicht nur für Berufseinsteiger:innen in der Softwareentwicklung. Wer anfängt, braucht Aufgaben mit geringem Risiko und die Erlaubnis, dass etwas schiefgeht. Scheitern ist auf dem Weg vom Spieltrieb zur handwerklichen Professionalität ein notwendiger Zwischenschritt. Wer Fehler bestraft, bekommt Menschen, die KI verstecken. Das Risiko, die Aufgaben an die Entwicklung der Skills zu koppeln, ist auch hier eine unternehmerische Selbstverständlichkeit.
Befähigung schlägt Lizenz
Wenn jemand mich fragen würde, was die eine Sache ist, die ich für morgen mitgeben soll, dann diese: Investieren Sie in Befähigung. Den Vorsprung hat am Ende die Organisation, die am schnellsten gemeinsam lernt, nicht die mit der teuersten Lizenz.
Das Lernen bezieht sich dabei auf alle Beteiligten im Unternehmen, von den (Top-)Führungskräften bis zu den Mitarbeitenden und von der reinen Skillvermittlung bis hin zur Akzeptanz, dass es auf viele Fragen aktuell noch keine Antwort gibt. Nur eines ist ganz klar: dass die KI gekommen ist, um zu bleiben.
Handlungsfähig bleibt nicht, wer den perfekten Plan hat, sondern wer Rahmen schafft, in denen Menschen eigenverantwortlich lernen und entscheiden können. Die nächste Bitkom-Umfrage wird wieder zählen, wie viele Unternehmen KI einsetzen. Mich würde eine andere Zahl mehr interessieren: wie viele ihren Leuten das Lernen ermöglichen.

Des fonctionnalités additionnelles utiles au quotidien
Moonlock intègre également plusieurs outils pensés pour renforcer votre cybersécurité au sens large sur votre Mac. Le premier est un Coach sécurité.
Particulièrement utile si vous êtes peu expérimenté en informatique, votre Coach Sécurité vous prodigue de bons conseils. Cela vous évite de pratiquer des comportements à risque et vous aide à adopter de bons réflexes en ligne.
Autre fonctionnalité incluse, l’Inspecteur réseau veille à ce qu’aucune connexion ne soit établie en direction de certains pays. Votre Inspecteur réseau bloque le transfert d’information vers ces destinations depuis une application, dont votre navigateur Web. Cela réduit le risque de subir une arnaque.
Un outil dédié à la Protection du système analyse en temps réel le paramétrage de votre Mac. Il vous invite à l’adapter en cas d’alerte ciblée, ou encore de mise à jour disponible à l’installation. Cela a le mérite d’être aussi clair qu’intuitif.
Enfin, MacPaw pense également à votre confidentialité en ligne. Moonlock intègre ainsi un réseau virtuel privé parmi ses fonctionnalités. Votre VPN comprend une centaine de serveurs répartis dans une cinquantaine de pays.
C’est suffisant pour aller à l’essentiel, à savoir masquer votre véritable adresse IP et emplacement géographique. Les protocoles utilisés, IKEv2 comme OpenVPN, sont toujours aussi fiables en termes de sécurité.
En somme, vous pouvez retrouver un avis indépendant sur la suite de cybersécurité dédiée à votre Mac. Un test complet et une présentation approfondie des fonctionnalités disponibles, vous permettront de vous faire votre propre avis sur cette solution.
Une réduction de - 30 % est à saisir pour le Black Friday

articles.title: Google va supprimer l’application Nest : voici ce que vous devez absolument faire avant janvier 2027
articles.text:
Google a annoncé la fermeture de l’application Nest pour le 25 janvier 2027. Les clients Nest passeront ainsi sur l’application Google Home. Cette transition sera en bonne partie automatique, mais ceux qui disposent d’un compte Nest doivent tout de même effectuer quelques manœuvres pour pouvoir continuer à profiter de tous les services. Voici ce qu’il faut savoir.
Google va mettre un terme à l’application Nest
C’est officiel, l’application Nest fermera ses portes le 25 janvier 2027. À partir de cette date, l’application ne sera plus disponible sur Android et iOS, sur les téléviseurs ou encore sur le web. Tous les appareils de la marque passeront dans l’application Google Home. L’objectif de Google est bien entendu d’unifier ses services domotiques au sein d’une même application. L’entreprise américaine précise par ailleurs que cette manœuvre permettra de mieux intégrer les nouvelles fonctionnalités de Gemini et d’offrir une meilleure sécurité (l’application Nest a été créée il y a plus de 15 ans). Notons également que Google Assistant cessera de fonctionner sur les appareils Nest pour laisser sa place à Gemini dès le 2 août 2027.
Deux points sont à retenir particulièrement. Le premier : la fermeture de l’application Nest ne signifie absolument pas que les appareils de la marque cesseront de fonctionner. Ceux-ci resteront totalement opérationnels. En revanche, les personnes qui n’auront pas effectué la migration de leur compte vers l’application Google Home ne recevront plus de notifications et ne pourront plus contrôler leurs appareils à distance. Le second point à retenir : Google commencera à supprimer les données des comptes qui n’ont pas été migrés vers l’application Google Home, à partir du 25 janvier 2027. Mais, concrètement, quelles sont les mesures à prendre ?
Que faire si vous disposez d’un compte Nest ?
Tout d’abord, les personnes qui disposent d’un appareil Nest doivent migrer leur compte Nest vers l’application Google Home, avant le 25 janvier 2027. Pour ce faire, il suffit de se rendre dans les paramètres de l’application Nest où un bouton « Migrer vers un compte Google » devrait être disponible.
Ensuite, Google précise que les clips vidéo qui ont été enregistrés manuellement ne seront pas transférés automatiquement. Il faut donc se rendre sur home.nest.com et cliquer sur le bouton « Tout télécharger », avant le 25 janvier 2027. En revanche, l’entreprise américaine précise que « vos appareils Nest, y compris les caméras et l’historique vidéo, seront automatiquement transférés de l’application Nest vers l’application Google Home ».
Enfin, une question se pose : est-ce que tout cela aura un impact tarifaire pour les clients des appareils Nest ? Selon Google, la réponse est non. Ceux qui disposent d’un abonnement Nest Aware (première génération) passeront automatiquement à la formule Google Home Premium Advanced à partir du 25 janvier 2027, sans surcoût ou modification de tarif.

articles.title: GTA VI devient le plus gros lancement de l'histoire PlayStation : 39 millions de joueurs en quatre jours
articles.text:
Après des années d’attente et deux reports, Grand Theft Auto VI est enfin sorti le jeudi 19 novembre, et le jeu de Rockstar Games accumule déjà les records.
Dans un billet publié ce lundi 23 novembre sur le PlayStation.Blog, Tim Turi, Content Communications Manager chez Sony Interactive Entertainment, parle du « plus gros lancement de l’histoire pour PlayStation ». Autrement dit, aucun jeu n’a fait mieux sur les consoles de la marque en trois décennies et cinq générations, avec plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques sur PS5.
683 millions d’heures en quatre jours
Tous les chiffres couvrent la période du 19 au 22 novembre 2026. Sur ces quatre jours, les joueurs PS5 ont cumulé 683 millions d’heures de jeu, soit 17,4 heures en moyenne par joueur, un peu plus de quatre heures par jour. GTA VI a aussi battu le record de joueurs connectés en même temps sur PlayStation, devant tous les précédents détenteurs, qu’ils soient multijoueur, free-to-play ou solo. Sony ne donne en revanche pas le chiffre de ce pic.
Le jeu a également fait sortir des consoles de leur carton. Sony a enregistré le plus grand nombre de PS5 connectées pour la première fois en une seule journée depuis la sortie de la console, en dehors des fêtes de fin d’année. Surtout, GTA VI a été le premier jeu lancé sur 70 % des PS5 neuves mises en service depuis le 19 novembre. Manière de confirmer qu’il est un moteur de vente de consoles pour Sony.
Pas de chiffres de ventes
Pour autant, Sony ne communique aucune vente en unités, seulement des joueurs et des heures, ce qui empêche toute comparaison avec le lancement de GTA V en 2013.
Il ne faut d’ailleurs pas mélangé le nombre de joueurs avec le nombre de jeux vendus. Plusieurs joueurs peuvent profiter du même exemplaire avec une seule console.

articles.title: Russia will launch a routine ISS supply mission tomorrow—apparently, it’s a big secret
articles.text:
It was the most simple of questions. On Monday afternoon, during a NASA news conference about the International Space Station, Space News reporter Jeff Foust asked about an upcoming launch of a Russian spacecraft.
“It’s my understanding there’s another cargo mission going to the ISS this week, a Russian Progress,” Foust said. “Can you confirm that, and give the date and time that will launch?”
This Progress MS-36 cargo launch, mind you, is presently scheduled for fewer than 16 hours from now, at 10:13 UTC (05:13 am ET) on Tuesday. It is going to a space station co-operated by the US space agency. But no, NASA would not provide this basic information about the upcoming Progress launch.
“Regarding the Progress launch, I would ask you to please reach out to Roscosmos directly for any questions tied to that vehicle,” said the senior NASA official on the call, Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager for NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program.
Effectively, this is a “Go f- yourself” response from NASA. Roscosmos typically does not reply to Western media outlets, and everyone knows this.
So why is a bog-standard Progress launch suddenly a state secret? It seems to be a recent policy change, because, historically, NASA has televised every one of these cargo flights from Russia’s main spaceport in Baikonur, Kazakhstan. But there is no information about the upcoming launch on NASA’s television schedule for upcoming “live” events.
As recently as September, NASA provided live television coverage of Progress launches from Baikonur. It even issued a media advisory promising to update its broadcast schedule once Roscosmos provided launch details. Two months later, NASA officials apparently are unwilling to confirm that another Progress launch is taking place.
Who made this decision?
The question is whether this decision was made by NASA or was a request from Roscosmos, and, ultimately, whether any of this matters. We can make some educated guesses.
It is probably safe to surmise that the decision here was originally made by state-sponsored Russian space corporation Roscosmos. The company has not been advertising the preparation of the Progress spacecraft as it customarily does, some local sources say. Russian space reporter Anatoly Zak confirms that Roscosmos has “dramatically curtailed” its coverage of all launch campaigns in recent months. There is no mention of the launch on Roscosmos’ Telegram channel.

articles.title: GTA 6's First Post-Launch Patch Fixes Crashes, Stuck Weather, and Autosaves
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
GTA 6's First Post-Launch Patch Fixes Crashes, Stuck Weather, and Autosaves
Rockstar has released the first post-launch patch for GTA 6. It is quite a small one, weighing 603.8 MB on the PS5 and 1.6 GB on the Xbox Series X|S. The patch started rolling out on November 23, just four days after the game's record-breaking launch. The patch notes have been posted on Rockstar's support site, and they mention some key bug fixes along with other general improvements. The patch shows up as version 01.002.002 on PlayStation and 1.0.2.2 on Xbox.
The update claims to fix several crashes, autosaves that weren't working correctly, as well as a bug that caused weather to stay stuck for long stretches. That last one was making the rounds on X and Reddit recently, as many players were surprised at the lack of rain in the game. Turns out, it was a weather bug that has now been fixed by Rockstar. Other fixes include phone calls that failed to trigger, which often stranded players, unable to progress the story. Rockstar has also sorted out a bug that kept players from losing their Wanted level, and a couple of other fixes related to the gym and fences. Curiously, Rockstar's notes don't mention the infamous red barn money glitch northeast of Hamlet, with players reporting that it still works after the update. Rockstar doesn't list any performance changes for this patch, so all consoles are still stuck at 30 FPS for the foreseeable future.
Source:

articles.title: The Best CPUs - Late 2026 Update
articles.text:
If you're building a new PC or considering a platform upgrade, choosing the right CPU in late 2026 presents an unusual dilemma. There are plenty of good processors covering a wide range of prices, and some holiday deals, particularly on Intel CPUs, are outstanding. But with DDR5 memory prices through the roof and new processors from both Intel and AMD on the horizon, this might not be the best time to invest in an entirely new platform.
In fact, if you can afford to wait, that's exactly what we'd recommend. Intel's next-generation Nova Lake processors are expected in early 2027, potentially within the first quarter, with AMD's Zen 6 series likely following a little later. Faster CPUs are just around the corner, and their arrival should put downward pressure on pricing for existing hardware.
Of course, not everyone can wait. If you need a new PC today, there are some excellent deals worth considering, including a few that challenge our usual advice about avoiding dead-end platforms.
Intel's Core Ultra 5 250K Plus and Core Ultra 7 270K Plus are particularly attractive right now, with some frankly insane discounts. Amazon has been among those offering the most aggressive deals, though it's hard to say how long those will last. Availability and pricing vary considerably by region, however. In Australia, for example, the 250K Plus is still around $300 AUD, though that's considerably less than the Ryzen 7 9700X, which costs $385 AUD even after Amazon's discount.
As we've noted repeatedly, we normally wouldn't recommend investing in Intel's LGA1851 platform, given its limited upgrade path. But at current prices, you're effectively getting the motherboard for free compared to competing AMD configurations. The other major consideration is memory pricing. DDR5 has become painfully expensive, making older DDR4 platforms attractive again, especially for anyone who already owns a decent memory kit.
The AI bubble also looks like it might be losing some air, it's impossible to predict what will happen, but NAND flash prices have been dropping lately, falling by around 20% in recent weeks.
With all that in mind, we've updated our CPU recommendations to reflect current pricing and the unusual state of the market. We'll start with the best affordable DDR4 options, move on to DDR5, and then look at the processors offering the most performance for your money.
Best Entry-Level Platform Upgrade (DDR4)
Ryzen 7 5700X or Core i5-14400F
Let's start with the cheapest worthwhile hardware options available right now. The premise for this category is simple: you need a new PC or a complete platform upgrade, but don't want to pay current DDR5 prices, perhaps because you already own a decent DDR4 kit.
As it stands, a basic 16GB DDR5 memory kit costs roughly twice as much as DDR4, at around $260 versus $130. For budget builders who can get away with 16GB of memory, DDR4 is considerably more attractive, even if it means investing in older platforms such as AM4 or LGA1700.
So what are the options? As usual, availability and pricing will depend on your region, especially since many of these processors are quite old now.
Starting with AMD, the cheapest AM4 processor worth considering is the Ryzen 5 5600 or 5600X, whichever is cheaper or more readily available. The Ryzen 5 5500 has been a popular choice at $90. While its name suggests it's simply a slightly downclocked 5600, it's actually a much worse processor, featuring an entirely different design with just half the L3 cache. As a result, it performs more like a Ryzen 5 3600 than a 5600, making it difficult to justify the $45 saving over the 5600X.
Beyond the 5600 models, there's the Ryzen 7 5700X, currently on sale for $160, just $25 more than the 5600. Frankly, it's well worth coughing up the extra cash if you can. The 5700X packs two additional cores and is generally a little faster for gaming, while offering a much more substantial improvement in productivity performance. We should also point out that there's a Ryzen 7 5700 (non-X), which you should avoid like the plague. Essentially, it's an 8-core version of the Ryzen 5 5500, meaning it features a cut-down 16MB L3 cache rather than the 32MB found in the 5700X and 5800X.
Turning to Intel, your DDR4 options are limited to the LGA1700 platform, which supports 12th-, 13th-, and 14th-generation Core processors. Again, availability and pricing will vary considerably.
In the US, the Core i3-14100F costs around $105, but it's only a quad-core processor, so we'd avoid it. That leaves the Core i5-14400F at $155 as Intel's best budget DDR4 option. It packs six P-cores, four E-cores, and 20MB of L3 cache. The 14400F is slightly faster than the Ryzen 5 5600 for gaming while offering superior productivity performance, largely thanks to those additional E-cores. It currently costs about 15% more, but the extra performance helps offset the price increase.
Beyond that, you're looking at spending over $200 on something like the Core i5-14600KF at $230 or the Core i7-12700KF at $285, which is well beyond entry-level territory.
So which DDR4-compatible CPU should you buy for under $200? Your main options are the Ryzen 5 5600 at $135, the Core i5-14400F at $155, and the Ryzen 7 5700X at $160.
We think the 5700X is a better buy than the 5600 at those prices, so it really comes down to the 5700X versus the 14400F. There's no wrong choice here. They're quite similar in performance, especially for gaming, so the decision will largely depend on pricing and availability in your region.
Best Gaming Platform Upgrade (DDR4)
Intel Core i5-14600KF
What if you want to build the fastest gaming PC you can while still using DDR4 memory, either because you don't want to pay today's DDR5 prices or because you already own a good DDR4 kit?
Right now, the most viable options include the Intel Core i5-14600KF at $230, the Core i7-12700KF at $285, and the Ryzen 7 5800X3D at $320. In a normal market, the 14600KF at $230 wouldn't be particularly appealing. You'd be better off investing in AMD's AM5 platform or buying something even cheaper and slightly faster, such as the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus.
Sadly, we're not in a normal market, and those alternatives all require DDR5 memory. For anyone specifically looking for a DDR4 solution, the 14600KF is therefore extremely attractive and easily our top recommendation.
Overall gaming performance is very similar to the 5800X3D, but at almost a 30% discount, the Core i5 represents considerably better value. The 14600KF also outperforms the 12700KF, offering better single-core and multi-core performance, so there's little reason to spend another $55 on the older Core i7.
If you're after the best-performing processor that still supports DDR4 memory without breaking the bank, the 14600KF is the one to get. Obviously, the fastest LGA1700 processor is the Core i9-14900K, but even the KF variant starts at $430, and it's absolutely not worth paying almost twice as much as the Core i5-14600KF.
The 13th- and 14th-generation Core i7 and Core i9 processors have also been plagued by stability issues. While Intel has introduced fixes intended to address those problems, we can't say for certain that every affected processor is in the clear.
On that note, we strongly recommend avoiding second-hand 13th- or 14th-gen Core i7 and i9 processors. Many have suffered degradation that can lead to stability problems or poor performance, and there's no reliable way to know what you're getting.
Best Entry-Level Platform Upgrade (DDR5)
AMD Ryzen 5 7500F
Sadly, budget CPU options remain pretty miserable, especially if you want to move to AMD's or Intel's latest platform. On Intel's side, the Core Ultra 5 225F is its cheapest current-generation offering, and at $160, it's pretty horrible. Despite packing six P-cores and four E-cores, it only delivers multi-core performance comparable to the Ryzen 5 7500F while being considerably slower for gaming.
Several factors hurt the 225F's performance. One is its 4.9GHz boost clock, but the bigger issue is the measly 20MB L3 cache, the smallest cache capacity of any Core Ultra 200 series processor. That's a significant problem given that these CPUs aren't particularly impressive for gaming to begin with. Even if the 225F were considerably more competitive, you'd still have the problem of buying into a dead platform.
The LGA1851 socket won't support any future CPU architectures, making it effectively a dead end. Intel's upcoming Nova Lake-S desktop processors will use the new LGA1954 socket, which is incompatible with LGA1851.
So if you're building a new PC or performing a complete platform upgrade with DDR5 memory, it's difficult to justify investing in a platform with no future CPU upgrade path. That really leaves AMD's AM5 platform as the only viable option for budget builders right now.
This is why we continue to recommend the Ryzen 5 7500F for budget gamers, though the older Core i5 processors are potentially better investments for productivity workloads. For gaming, however, the 7500F is only slightly slower than those older Core i5 models, making it an excellent value choice, particularly given AM5's much stronger upgrade path.
The main downside is availability, as the 7500F isn't officially sold in every region. In the US, it's not generally available through local retailers, but you can order it from AliExpress for around $120. Alternatively, the Ryzen 5 7600X costs $185 at most retailers, although AMD's store on Amazon currently has it for just $165, making it a reasonable alternative to the imported 7500F.
Best CPU for ~$200
Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus
If we ignore future platform upgrades and simply focus on getting the most CPU performance for your money, there's one standout option that's become irresistibly cheap. Whether you're gaming, working, or doing just about anything else, the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus is the CPU to get right now.
Retailers such as Newegg have the 250K Plus for around $170, but Amazon is currently offering it for just $140 to eligible Amazon Visa cardholders, thanks to a $60 discount on its $200 list price. At that price, it's an absolute steal.
The 250K Plus packs six P-cores clocked up to 5.3GHz with a shared 30MB L3 cache, along with 12 E-cores. It also features a 43% increase in die-to-die frequency, jumping from 2.1GHz to 3GHz. This improvement addresses many of the latency issues found in the original Arrow Lake processors, leading to substantially better gaming performance.
AMD is currently floundering at this price point. While the Ryzen 7 9700X might deliver similar gaming performance, the 250K Plus is up to 50% faster in core-heavy productivity workloads.
To get comparable gaming and productivity performance from AMD, you'd need to spend at least $300 on the Ryzen 9 7900X, though that processor can be a bit sketchy for gaming at times. Ideally, you'd want the Ryzen 9 9900X, but that processor costs around $330, making it more than twice as expensive as the 250K Plus at Amazon's promotional price.
That means you can currently buy the 250K Plus along with a quality Z890 motherboard for roughly the same price as the Ryzen 9 9900X alone, making Intel's dead-platform issue a complete non-issue from a financial perspective. So while we normally wouldn't recommend investing in Intel's dead-end LGA1851 socket, especially with Nova Lake and its new socket expected in early 2027, the 250K Plus is cheap enough that the deal makes sense.
Frankly, at these prices, it's much better value than anything AMD has on offer right now.
Best Value Productivity CPU
Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus
If you have more than $200 to spend, the good news is that you don't actually need to spend much more than that on a CPU right now. In fact, Amazon is currently selling Intel's Core Ultra 7 270K Plus for just $221, which is complete madness.
The 270K Plus is a one-stop shop for just about any workload. Whether you're gaming or tackling demanding productivity tasks, if you want a CPU that handles everything with a high degree of efficiency, this is the one to get.
This model packs eight P-cores clocked at up to 5.5GHz, along with 16 E-cores that can reach 4.7GHz. There's also 36MB of L3 cache, and Intel has specified a maximum turbo power rating of 250 watts.
In multi-threaded, core-heavy productivity workloads, it performs within 2 – 5% of the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X, a processor that often retails for twice the price. That makes the 270K Plus, by far, one of the most cost-effective ways to get high-end workstation-class performance on a mainstream desktop.
Not only that, but unlike the original Core Ultra 7 265K, the Plus version addresses internal latency issues, greatly improving gaming performance to the point where it's no longer embarrassing.
Of course, AMD's X3D processors still hold the crown for pure gaming performance, but we think the 270K Plus is now close enough that the price savings make it more attractive for most people, especially if you're looking for strong performance across a variety of workloads.
The fact that you're getting productivity performance approaching that of the 9950X, along with very capable gaming performance, at a fraction of the price makes concerns about future platform support largely irrelevant. As with the 250K Plus, you're effectively getting the motherboard for free.
The cheapest Ryzen 9 9950X we could find at the time of writing was $490. Meanwhile, shoppers can get the 270K Plus at Amazon for just $221, along with a really nice $200 Z890 motherboard, for less than the price of the Ryzen 9 alone.
Once again, the motherboard is effectively free, and at that point, the lack of a future upgrade path becomes much less of a concern. For anyone who needs serious productivity performance without spending a fortune, it's an incredibly compelling deal.
Best Gaming CPU
AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D or Ryzen 7 7700X3D
There's no debating which company makes the fastest gaming CPUs. AMD continues to dominate with its X3D processors, and the Ryzen 7 9850X3D remains the fastest gaming CPU money can buy.
What's changed in the last few months is pricing, and right now the 9850X3D is a much more attractive option. Amazon has discounted the 9850X3D to just $399, matching the price of the 9800X3D. Given that the 9850X3D is ~5% faster on average, there's really no reason to buy the 9800X3D at the same price.
Of course, that 4-5% improvement isn't exactly exciting, and as we found in our original review, the additional performance comes at the cost of substantially higher power consumption. Still, both processors are relatively efficient compared to Intel's previous flagships, and at identical prices, we'd take the extra performance.
The 9850X3D is also around 15% faster than the Ryzen 7 7800X3D in our CPU-limited gaming benchmarks, and a massive 40% faster than Intel's Core Ultra 9 285K. AMD's lead is particularly impressive in titles such as Baldur's Gate 3, Cyberpunk 2077, and Assetto Corsa Competizione, where the additional L3 cache makes a significant difference.
But do you really need to spend $400 on a gaming CPU? Absolutely not.
The older Ryzen 7 7800X3D remains an option at around $339. It's roughly 15% slower than the 9850X3D, but costs 15% less, making it a reasonable alternative. There's also the newer Ryzen 7 7700X3D, which launched in July at $329 and is currently available for $299. This is essentially a slightly downclocked 7800X3D, and in our 13-game benchmark we found it was just 7% slower on average, while trailing the 9800X3D by 15%.
At these prices, the 7700X3D is arguably the best-value X3D processor for gamers. It delivers excellent gaming performance, and you're saving $100 compared to the 9850X3D. All of these processors use AMD's AM5 platform, so you're also getting a much better upgrade path than Intel's current LGA1851 offerings.
One important consideration is that all these CPUs require DDR5 memory, which has become painfully expensive. The good news is that AMD's X3D processors aren't particularly sensitive to memory speed. In our testing, the 9850X3D lost very little performance when switching from DDR5-6000 CL30 to slower DDR5-4800 CL40 memory, making cheaper DDR5 kits a viable option.
For most gamers, our Core Ultra 7 270K Plus recommendation will be more than sufficient, especially considering its outstanding productivity performance and current pricing. But if gaming is your priority, AMD's X3D processors remain the top choice.

articles.title: Samsung 990 Pro 4TB SSD drops by $400 to $700 at Amazon
articles.text:
Samsung's 990 Pro is one of the fastest PCIe 4.0 SSDs you can buy, and now all capacities up to 4TB are discounted for Black Friday
A stellar SSD for professionals, creators, and gamers
The Samsung 990 Pro SSD has long been one of our favorite SSDs for creators, PC builders, and gamers. Currently, the 4TB version is down to $700 (was $1100) at Amazon for Black Friday, with price drops on the 1TB and 2TB versions, too.
Unless you need the workstation-level speeds of the 9100 Pro (also discounted for Black Friday), the 990 Pro is the internal SSD to opt for.
The PCIe 4.0 M.2 2280 drive hits read/write speeds of up to 7450/6900 MB/s respectively, alongside 2,400TB of rated endurance, AES 256-bit hardware encryption, and a five-year warranty.
A PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD in the M.2 2280 size with 4TB of storage and rated sequential speeds of up to 7,450MB/s reads and 6,900MB/s writes. It's single-sided, so it fits slim laptops and the PS5, and it's rated for 2,400 TB written with a five-year warranty. 1TB and 2TB capacities are also discounted.
Why we recommend it
We gave the 990 Pro a Best in Class award in our review, calling it a stellar SSD for both professionals and gamers. If your PC supports PCIe 5.0, faster drives like the 9100 Pro may be the better pick on speed, but the 990 Pro remains near the top of what PCIe 4.0 can deliver. For most users, it's the one we recommend.
Price Context & Historical Value
SSD prices have climbed sharply this year, and the 4TB 990 Pro was $799.90 at Amazon in late October, so $699.99 is the best price we've seen in months. It's still well above what this drive sold for last year, though. If you can wait for storage prices to settle, it may get cheaper, but we wouldn't count on it soon.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Samsung 990 Pro 4TB if...
you need 4TB of fast storage now, you want a drive that fits a PS5 or slim laptop, or you value Samsung's reliability and long warranty.
❌ Skip the Samsung 990 Pro 4TB if...
you have a PCIe 5.0 slot and want the fastest drive possible, you only need 1TB or 2TB, or you'd rather wait to see if storage prices fall.
