articles.title: Demandan a SpaceX en Estados Unidos por imágenes explicitas falsas de menores creadas con Grok
articles.text:
Los fiscales generales de Virginia, Jay Jones, y de Oregon, Dan Rayfield, demandaron a SpaceX, la empresa de Elon Musk que opera la red social X y la inteligencia artificial Grok. Los acusan de no impedir que Grok creara imágenes explicitas falsas de adultos y niños, y de presentar sus productos como seguros.
Son las primeras demandas de un estado contra la compañía por este asunto, según la agencia Reuters. Cada fiscal presentó su propia denuncia, “separada pero similar”, según el comunicado de Virginia.
Las denuncias invocan las leyes de protección al consumidor de cada estado: la Ley de Protección al Consumidor de Virginia y la Ley de Prácticas Comerciales Desleales de Oregon, informó CNBC. Según esa cadena, los tribunales aún no habían aceptado los escritos a primera hora del lunes 23 de noviembre.
Qué piden los fiscales
Ambos estados reclaman órdenes judiciales que obliguen a la empresa a poner salvaguardas más estrictas, multas, la devolución de las ganancias obtenidas y el pago de costos legales, según CNBC. Virginia suma el reintegro de dinero a los consumidores afectados.
Wired agregó que los fiscales señalan como antecedente el acuerdo de Meta con 51 estados y territorios de Estados Unidos este verano, por presuntas fallas en la protección de menores. Esa conciliación, sin admisión de culpa, mostró que los fiscales pueden exigir cambios amplios en un producto.
Los dos estados contrataron al estudio Platkin LLP, dirigido por el exfiscal general de Nueva Jersey Matthew Platkin, para llevar los casos, según Wired.
Cuáles fueron las promesas de SpaceX
Según el comunicado de Virginia, con una sola fotografía Grok podía fabricar una imagen o un video realista de una persona desnuda o en una situación sexual, sin su consentimiento. La demanda sostiene que la empresa ignoró las medidas de seguridad habituales de la industria para diferenciarse de sus rivales.
Rayfield sostuvo que la falta de controles “se consideraba una característica, no un error”, y que la compañía la promocionó como “modo picante”. Jones afirmó que la empresa “engañó al público” con garantías falsas sobre la seguridad de los datos y las imágenes de los usuarios.
Virginia cita un estudio del Centro para Contrarrestar el Odio Digital. Entre el 29 de diciembre de 2025 y el 8 de enero de 2026, Grok habría creado y publicado en X unos 3 millones de imágenes sexualizadas, unas 23.000 de ellas con aspecto de menores. Cerca del 30% de las imágenes de menores identificadas seguía visible una semana después.
Wired, que leyó las denuncias, informó que investigadores de Virginia probaron Grok antes de demandar y hallaron que sus filtros eran “inconsistentes e ineficaces”. Según el relato de la revista, el chatbot explicó qué palabras activaban los filtros y ayudó a redactar instrucciones para evitarlos. En ningún momento preguntó si la persona de la foto había dado su consentimiento.
Los estados también sostienen que miles de reportes enviados al centro estadounidense para niños desaparecidos y explotados llegaron sin datos clave, lo que impidió actuar en el 90% de los casos, según Wired.
La respuesta de SpaceX y otros frentes legales
SpaceX no respondió de inmediato a los pedidos de comentarios. En octubre, ante el Concejo Municipal de Nueva York, una responsable de políticas de IA de la compañía, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, dijo que existían “salvaguardas” y “controles estrictos”, según CNBC. Los fiscales afirman que esa declaración contradice lo que sus pruebas mostraron.
La demanda no sorprendió a la empresa: en una presentación de valores de octubre, SpaceX informó que Virginia evaluaba demandarla, según The Next Web. Reuters añadió que SpaceX enfrenta más de una docena de demandas de personas que dicen haber sido víctimas de imágenes sexuales generadas con Grok. En un caso contra un usuario, sus abogados describieron a Grok como una herramienta neutral sujeta al control del usuario.
Virginia y Oregon piden ahora que los tribunales acepten las demandas; hasta el momento de la publicación, ninguno lo había hecho.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 24, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 24, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, November 24, 2026.
From Google Cloud cutting jobs in India to Keralam’s new initiative, 'Avalkkoppam' (With Her), to tackle domestic and cyber violence against women, here are the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
Google Cloud confirms 30 role cuts in India, rejects claims of wider layoffs
Google Cloud has confirmed that around 30 roles in India were eliminated last week due to work reprioritisation. It, however, rejected online claims that much of its local workforce had been affected.
“These rumors are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organizational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritization of work,” the company said in response to a user on X.
Latest News
Keralam to roll out 'Avalkkoppam' initiative against domestic, cyber violence targeting women
Keralam will roll out a new initiative, 'Avalkkoppam' (With Her) to tackle domestic and cyber violence against women as part of a 16-day statewide campaign beginning November 25.
The initiative is part of the Women and Child Development Department's 'Orange the World' campaign, aimed at ending violence and gender discrimination against women and girls.
This year's campaign will focus on ensuring that survivors of violence can seek assistance without fear and on strengthening legal action against perpetrators.
Funding news
CortexSpark Ventures launches Rs 1,000 Cr deeptech fund
CortexSpark Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on deeptech and artificial intelligence segment, has launched a Rs 1,000 crore fund with an additional greenshoe option of Rs 400 crore.
CortexSpark Ventures, founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, will focus on startup investments across spacetech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech & Bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials.
Cosine Robots raises Rs 22.36 Cr to build made-in-India robot actuators
Bengaluru-based Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore in a round led by deeptech fund Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors. Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas, the startup makes integrated servo actuators that combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics and proprietary control software. Its joint-level controller runs a 25 kHz loop, or 25,000 updates per second.
The company offers cycloidal and planetary actuators for industrial arms, cobots, quadrupeds and humanoids. The money will fund a new R&D and production facility covering machining, assembly, calibration and endurance testing, and expand the engineering team. Cosine aims to offer robot makers a cost-competitive alternative to established suppliers.
Other news
IIIT-Delhi to host eighth symposium on computational gastronomy
IIIT-Delhi's Complex Systems Laboratory will host GastroSym2026, the eighth edition of its symposium on computational gastronomy. The symposium brings together chefs, scientists, historians, entrepreneurs and policymakers. The field of computational gastronomy turns culinary knowledge into structured data that can be modelled and analysed.
Speakers include chef Manjit Singh Gill, Prof. Ganesh Bagler, anthropologist Prof. Kurush F. Dalal, and Amura Health's Saravanan Balakrishnan. Sessions cover food safety, sensory science, fragrance, personalised nutrition, the gut microbiome and ageing. TasteTron will demonstrate a cooking-machine prototype; Foodoscope Technologies and Bettrlabs will also present. The event also features research posters and startup showcases.
Cashfree launches wallet that lets Indian users authorise AI agents to pay
Payments platform Cashfree has launched Cashfree Wallet, which it calls India's first wallet that lets users authorise personal AI agents to make payments for them. Users link the wallet to their agent with a mobile OTP, add money via UPI, card or net banking, and set budgets and spending rules.
Agents pay only from the wallet balance; so they never see card, UPI or bank details. For now, Cashfree Wallet supports bill payments; travel, food, grocery and ecommerce are under testing. Developers can integrate through Cashfree's Agentpay MCP server; more than 100 agent and bot builders have already done so, said the company. Payment data is stored in India.

articles.title: Nigeria plans 500,000-job pipeline in data protection
articles.text:
Nigeria’s data protection regulator wants more mid-career professionals to step into the country’s growing privacy workforce, betting that local talent can fill a global shortage of certified experts.
Speaking at a capacity-building session for media professionals in Abuja on Friday, November 20, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji outlined the agency’s push to expand the country’s data privacy ecosystem and position Nigeria as an exporter of compliance talent.
Section 32 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires businesses to employ Data Protection Officers (DPOs), but without enough certified professionals, local companies risk non-compliance, data breaches, and lost foreign investment.
To prevent a talent crunch and preserve local experts, the NDPC said it is using a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to create 500,000 jobs. According to Olatunji, compliance with the Act has already triggered a sharp rise in certified professionals across the country, though supply still lags behind market demand.
While he did not specify the exact number of DPOs the market requires, the regulator’s 500,000-job target highlights how wide the talent deficit remains.
“When we started, we had less than 1,000 data protection officers in all of this country,” he said. “At the commission, we have over 90% of our staff that are certified. And in Nigeria, we have over 10,000 certified data protection officers.”
Exporting talent
Olatunji noted that the ecosystem has already created more than 27,000 jobs in under three years, driven largely by Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) licenced to conduct audits and enforce compliance on behalf of the government.
Beyond local businesses, the regulator said it is pitching Nigeria as a talent hub for international markets grappling with privacy skill shortages.
“We want data privacy within the ecosystem, or if you need the service of a DPO, you look towards Africa, and of course, Nigeria,” Olatunji said, pointing to talent gaps abroad. “Even in the UK, 94.7% of breaches are due to lack of qualified personnel in data privacy and protection. So everywhere, all over the world, they are looking for data privacy and protection experts.”
Several former NDPC staffers have already transitioned into international roles across the United States and the United Kingdom, including executive leadership positions at global financial institutions, he added. To sustain the talent pipeline, the commission said it has begun taking data privacy training directly into Nigerian tertiary institutions to introduce students to the field as a viable career path.
For working professionals, Olatunji framed data protection not as a complete career pivot, but as a flexible, high-demand add-on. Because organisations are legally required to appoint DPOs, certified individuals can consult for multiple firms simultaneously.
“The good thing about this is you can be a DPO and do some other stuff. And you can be a DPO for four, five, three, ten organisations. You can be a freelance DPO. Nobody ties you down to any particular spot,” he said.

articles.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
articles.text:
“It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want.
But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age.
Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history, smart devices, and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price.
Surveillance pricing versus dynamic pricing
Surveillance pricing, according to the nonprofit Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), is an algorithmic pricing practice that charges individuals or groups of individuals different prices “for the same goods or services.”
“The goal of surveillance pricing is to infer the highest price that the customer is willing to pay, based on consumers’ personal data and other market data,” EPIC explains.
Instacart previously practiced surveillance pricing, also called personalized pricing. In 2025, Consumer Reports found that, “based on how much Instacart says the typical household of four spends on groceries, the average price variations observed could translate into a cost swing of about $1,200 per year.” Instacart has since removed its surveillance pricing tools.
Dynamic pricing, or surge pricing, differs from surveillance pricing in that, instead of relying on consumer data, it uses changing market trends, like supply and demand, inventory levels, and competitor pricing, to set prices.
While dynamic pricing may charge you more for an Uber ride when it’s very busy, surveillance pricing can feel less reasonable.
For instance, Target’s app was previously accused of using location data to charge users $100 more for a TV if they bought it while standing inside a Target store. At the time, Target said that it would match lower prices presented by customers, but many customers wouldn’t think to look for pricing discrepancies. In another instance from 2012, Orbitz was found to more prominently feature expensive hotels to people using macOS. Companies often dispute whether their practices truly qualify as surveillance pricing. But these examples all reflect companies using data about their customers to influence the prices they show them.

articles.title: MacBook modder turns Apple’s Force Touch trackpad into a speaker using haptic engine — MacBook ‘talks’ using only vibrations from the motor, can play speech, tones, and even music
articles.text:
MacBook modder turns Apple’s Force Touch trackpad into a speaker using haptic engine — MacBook ‘talks’ using only vibrations from the motor, can play speech, tones, and even music
There's a remote chance this could be useful one day, if all your other audio output options failed simultaneously.
The MacBook's Force Touch trackpad is considered one of the crown jewels among Apple's laptop technologies. Now Cody Collier, AKA os6 on GitHub, has devised another way to make use of Apple's trackpad design, albeit an unusual and probably not very useful one. The trackpad's haptic engine can be used to make it work as a speaker using Collier's No Speaker software. Want to see and hear it for yourself before installing? There's a demo video below mixing speech, tones, and music playback through a MacBook trackpad.
As indicated in the intro, Apple's Force Touch trackpad has many fans, largely because of its smooth and solid glass surface with consistent and accurate tactile feedback driven by haptics, making it a step up from traditional clattering 'diving board' mechanical alternatives. The haptics that make it feel so responsive can also produce sounds, Collier found, after its haptic vibration frequencies were manipulated into the human hearing range.
"There's no speaker in a MacBook trackpad, just a small haptic motor that taps the glass so you feel a click," Collier explains on the GitHub project page. "No Speaker drives that motor up to 4,000 times a second, fast enough to make sound you can hear, and turns it into a voice. It talks, sings, raps, and becomes an instrument under your finger."
In the video, Collier shows the trackpad being used to play a melody, and as a simple drum machine with kick, snare, and high hats programmed on a 16-step grid. If for some reason you can't play the demo video for yourself, suffice to say No Speaker audio quality is pretty terrible. The nearest approximation to the trackpad's output quality might be the legendary but ancient Speak & Spell with a severely damaged speaker.
The GitHub page contains links to the Mac software and command-line examples to test on your trackpad. Passing parameters to the installed nospeaker command lets you send text strings for it to speak, adjust the No Speaker voice, play test tones, and switch between various UI modes.
To have some no speaker fun with this project, you can run it yourself and fiddle with the input parameters and settings. It has been tested on a MacBook Pro (Mac17,10) with M5 Max and macOS 27.2.1. The author notes the Force Touch trackpad first appeared in MacBooks starting in 2015, so it may work on anything from then onwards. macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon, or macOS 13 or later on Intel, are also essentials. The app is smart enough to alert a user that there is no Force Touch trackpad present if they attempt to run it on such a machine.
The MacBook Force Touch trackpad isn't the first device or component that has been coaxed into audio playback duties contrary to its designed purpose. Tech tinkerers have previously played music on floppy drive motors and used hard drive actuators as speakers. Another example of out-of-scope hacking on a modern MacBook was the use of the hidden ‘LidAngleSensor’ API to make opening and closing the lid sound like a creaky door being adjusted.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.text:
Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
Artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia Corp. today announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as chief executive, president and board director effective immediately after resigning almost two weeks ago.
The company’s rockstar leather-jacket-wearing CEO faced turmoil earlier this month after it was revealed that he had been embroiled in a scandal involving multiple extramarital affairs, including with an Nvidia executive and a suspected Chinese spy. The board did not address the affairs, customarily a firing offense at most companies, in its statement.
News of his affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., broke on Nov. 10, reported by The Information. She was reportedly instrumental in helping China earn over $7.5 billion in chip sales through Nvidia, which is currently sanctioned by the United States from shipping to the country under trade restrictions.
Huang resigned amid reports that Nvidia’s board was in talks with plans to replace him. Today’s announcement marks a major about-face by the company.
In today’s announcement, the board said it voted unanimously to reinstate him to his vacated roles after a series of discussions and that it was “satisfied with his candor and ability to lead.” The board added that it received input from “senior levels of United States government” on its decision, and is “confident” that Huang poses no national security risk.
Huang thanked Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who stood in as interim CEO, for taking up the helm in his absence before taking back control of the company.
“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”
Nvidia shares surged more than 31% today. The stock had fallen almost 33% after Huang admitted to the affair with Alice Huang earlier in November.
“Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is a stunning new development, but not an altogether surprising one,” eMarketer Inc. analyst Jacob Bourne told SiliconANGLE. “After more than three decades at the helm, Huang has become so central to Nvidia’s identity and the broader AI trade that his departure fueled uncertainty during an already volatile period for the industry.”
Bourne added that Huang’s return may assuage investor upset and restore confidence in the company, reflected in the current stock upsurge, but the upheaval echoes the brief ouster of OpenAI Group PBC CEO Sam Altman in 2023. Between Nvidia and OpenAI, removing and then welcoming back CEOs amid disagreement and now scandal raises pertinent questions about corporate governance and how the outsized influence of individual leaders in the AI industry will affect the future.
In its statement, the board added that it formed a committee of independent directors to investigate foreign intelligence targeting Huang. The same committee has retained independent counsel to assist it and intends to reach a conclusion despite his reinstatement.
Huang announced his full support for the investigation and said he would cooperate fully.
The board also announced the formation of a National Security and Export Control Committee, composed of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The company added that it will make certain the committee oversees national security matters and trade controls and is currently searching to fill a new chief compliance officer role.

articles.title: GTA 6 pousse le réalisme des voitures électriques très loin, mais oublie un détail essentiel
articles.text:
Ce n’est clairement pas la première fois qu’un jeu vidéo convoque des véhicules électriques. C’est par contre bien la première fois que la manœuvre se fait avec un tel réalisme. GTA 6 pousse ainsi la précision et les détails à un niveau rarement atteint dans l’industrie vidéoludique. Déjà, contrairement à l’opus précédent, les voitures n’ont pas une autonomie illimitée. Il faudra donc filer à une station-service ou à une borne de recharge pour se ravitailler.
Et le plus étonnant, c’est que la couverture des stations de recharge rapide est très inégale sur la carte. Les zones les plus défavorisées n’ont quasiment pas de bornes et cela se ressent d’ailleurs sur le trafic, où les voitures électriques se font rares et les vieux modèles plus courants. Plus on se dirige vers le nord, plus la proportion de véhicules à batterie augmente avec leurs bornes de recharge.
Des copies de Tesla et de Porsche dans les rues de Vice City
D’ailleurs, Rockstar n’ayant toujours pas le droit de mettre en scène des modèles réels, faute de licence, ce sont une nouvelle fois des copies imparfaites qui arpentent les rues de Vice City. Imparfaites, mais parfaitement reconnaissables ! On remarquera en ce sens des imitations assez habiles de la Tesla Model S et de la Porsche Taycan. On pourrait même voir sur certains véhicules un revival maladroit de la Fisker Karma !
Rigolo, même si le plus drôle dans l’histoire est ailleurs : des voitures thermiques se permettent de squatter les bornes de recharge ! GTA 6 a ainsi retranscrit le fléau gangrenant le monde réel vers le monde virtuel. C’est franchement bien fait. Et il faut garder à l’esprit que GTA 6 n’est pas un jeu uniquement orienté vers la bagnole. Il s’agit d’un monde ouvert XXL où tout ou presque est possible, ce qui rend la performance d’autant plus impressionnante.
Une autonomie et une vitesse de recharge un peu trop généreuses
Alors bien entendu, gérer autant de choses implique quelques couacs. Mineurs, certes, mais bien réels. L’autonomie des véhicules à batterie est par exemple incroyablement élevée. Elle est même similaire aux voitures à essence. Certains joueurs se sont penchés sur le sujet et en effet, une copie de Tesla Model 3 a tenu plus de 20 minutes avec un plein, contre 18 minutes pour un modèle thermique équivalent.
Côté recharge, le branchement à domicile manque à l’appel, mais les voitures électriques sont en revanche aussi efficaces en charge rapide que leurs homologues à essence. Tant mieux, dirons-nous, même si le réalisme en prend un petit coup. Et avec 120 bornes de recharge contre 57 stations-service sur la carte, ça donnerait presque envie aux réfractaires d’accomplir leurs missions en électrique…
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Electrek

articles.title: UN human rights watchdog finds Bill C-22 violates human rights
articles.text:
The United Nations’ Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights has said that several elements of the federal government’s lawful access bill (Bill C-22) could violate human rights.
In an assessment of the bill, which was reported on by the Canadian Civil Liberties Association (CCLA), the human rights body noted several issues with the proposal, which include:
- The government’s ability to secretly impose surveillance-by-design mechanisms onto service providers without robust judicial authorization
- The government’s ability to obligate digital service providers to keep metadata indiscriminately on everyone, including in situations where it cannot be linked to a specific investigation or security threat.
- The government’s ability to impose surveillance-by-design obligations that break safeguards like end-to-end encryption
- The government’s need to include individual notice requirements and other safeguards into search provisions
- being able to prevent the federal government from using the surveillance powers to facilitate investigations of any activity that is not criminal here by law enforcement in other countries.
“Bill C-22’s excessive in its breadth of application and its inconsistency with global standards could threaten Canada’s ongoing attempts to integrate digitally with partners in the European Union,” writes the Canadian Civil Liberties Association.
The Canadian Civil Liberties Association also says the assessment raises questions about the government’s assertions that Bill C-22 aligns Canada with its Five Eyes intelligence partners.
Bill C-22 is currently being reviewed by the Senate Standing Committee on National Security, Defence, and Veteran Affairs (SECD).
Now, this isn’t the only organization concerned about the bill. Tech giant Apple warned about the bill’s privacy concerns and said it “will never” add the backdoors. Alongside that, Google, Meta, and Signal all expressed concerns about the bill, with Signal threatening to exit the Canadian market if it passes. Recently, Apple, Meta, and Google made a final lobbying push to rewrite Bill C-22 before it officially goes into law.
Image credit: Shutterstock

articles.title: Hace casi 30 años encontramos vida dentro del sarcófago de Chernóbil. Hoy es la clave para degradar pesticidas y agentes nerviosos
articles.text:
En 1997, cuando los investigadores analizaron el interior del sarcófago de la central nuclear de Chernóbil, encontraron creciendo en las paredes de la Unidad 4 un auténtico ecosistema biológico. En total identificaron 37 especies de hongos pertenecientes a 19 géneros distintos, con especímenes como Cladosporium sphaerospermum y Penicillium hirsutum. Y lógicamente, ver vida en una zona donde no debería existir es algo llamativo a cualquier nivel.
El secreto. Para entender cómo podía prosperar la vida en ese reactor radioactivo, los investigadores tomaron muestras y vieron que un pigmento oscuro que le servía de escudo era la clave de todo esto. Y no era ni más ni menos que la melanina.
Ahora, casi tres décadas después, aquel hallazgo ha servido de inspiración para crear materiales capaces de neutralizar algunas de las sustancias más peligrosas creadas por el ser humano, desde pesticidas agrícolas hasta agentes nerviosos como el gas sarín que se puede usar en una guerra química.
El pigmento que sobrevive a la radiación. Los hongos hallados en Chernóbil producen un tipo específico de melanina llamada alomelanina. Pero a diferencia de la eumelanina humana, la alomelanina carece de nitrógeno y posee una estructura química intrínsecamente microporosa que le permite actuar como una esponja molecular.
A partir de aquí, en 2021, un equipo de investigadores vio que se podía fabricar esta alomelanina en los laboratorios con una superficie interna extraordinaria que alcanzaba los 860 metros por gramo. Aplicada como recubrimiento sobre tejidos, esta "esponja" lograba bloquear el paso de sustancias que simulaban ser gases nerviosos. El problema era que atrapar el tóxico es solo la mitad del trabajo, puesto que el material seguía a reteniendo a una sustancia potencialmente mortal.
A destruir. El nuevo avance que se ha conseguido logra resolver este gran problema, puesto que han convertido este filtro en un catalizador activo. Para lograrlo, solo tuvieron que combinar la alomelanina sintética con clústeres de zirconio, que es un metal que degrada los agentes químicos.
El resultado es una melanina que cuenta con microporos para atrapar las moléculas tóxicas para el ser humano, y también tiene unos nodos de zirconio que rompen los enlaces químicos del compuesto mediante hidrólisis, transformándolo en subproductos menos peligrosos.
Muy importante. Aunque la protección frente a las armas químicas es la aplicación más evidente que se le puede ver al integrarlo en mascarillas o uniformes, el impacto más cotidiano apunta al sector agrícola. En este caso, los organofosforados siguen siendo la base de numerosos pesticidas industriales que contaminan suelos y acuíferos.
Es por ello que contar con un material barato, estable y reutilizable que degrade estos compuestos sin requerir condiciones extremas abre la puerta a sistemas de filtración de agua mucho más eficaces que el carbón activo tradicional.

articles.title: Black Friday 2026: Diese Gadgets machen deinen Arbeitsalltag angenehmer
articles.text:
Besser arbeiten, weniger bezahlen: Die besten Homeoffice-Deals zum Black Friday
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Eigentlich ist das Arbeiten im Homeoffice ganz einfach: Notebook aufklappen und loslegen. Doch wer regelmäßig oder gar ausschließlich zu Hause arbeitet, bemerkt schnell, dass zusätzliche leistungsfähigere Hardware den täglichen Job erleichtert oder in vielen Fällen auch einfach mehr Spaß beim Arbeiten bringt. Egal ob Angestellter oder Selbständiger – es lohnt sich in vielen Fällen, in gutes Arbeitsequipment zu investieren und beispielsweise durch einen guten höhenverstellbaren Schreibtisch und die richtige Beleuchtung etwas fürs eigene Wohlbefinden und die Gesundheit zu tun.
Wir haben uns deshalb anlässlich des Black Friday umgesehen und einige Dinge ausgewählt, die ihr Geld wert sind und aktuell zu einem besonders guten Kurs erhältlich sind. An dieser Stelle wollen wir deshalb fünf Möglichkeiten für ein sinnvolles Upgrade im Homeoffice aufzeigen.
Ergonomische Tastatur und Maus: Logitech MK950
Natürlich tut’s auch die kleine, leichte Standardmaus, die für zehn oder 15 Euro im Elektronikmarkt liegt – doch schon die Tastatur des Notebooks nervt durch ihre fehlende Ergonomie. In jedem Fall angenehm und hochwertig ist dagegen die Logitech-Tastatur-Maus-Kombi MK 950, die in Weiß und Graphit erhältlich ist und für einen vernünftigen Kurs (aktuell 64,49 Euro bei Amazon) zu bekommen ist.
Die flachen, notebookähnlichen Tasten ermöglichen ein angenehmes und vergleichsweise leises Schreiben. Auch die Maus arbeitet dank Logitechs Silent-Touch-Technologie besonders geräuscharm. Ihr Smart-Wheel-Mausrad erlaubt sowohl präzises Scrollen durch Dokumente als auch schnelles Navigieren durch lange Webseiten.
Neben der sehr angenehmen Haptik überzeugt das Set durch Anbindbarkeit an bis zu drei unterschiedliche Systeme, von Windows über macOS bis hin zu Android, iOS und Linux. Die Verbindung erfolgt wahlweise über Bluetooth oder den mitgelieferten Logi-Bolt-USB-Empfänger. Mit dem zugehörigen Tool Logi Options Plus lassen sich Tasten individuell belegen und wiederkehrende Aufgaben über sogenannte Smart Actions automatisieren.
Wohlklingendes Mikrofon: Rode NT-USB Plus
Wer regelmäßig im Homeoffice arbeitet, wird naturgemäß zahlreiche Videokonferenzen führen. Die Wahrnehmung – egal ob im Team oder gegenüber dem Kunden – ist hier besonders wichtig. Wer klanglich souverän und vor allem angenehm rüberkommen will, sollte ein qualitativ hochwertiges Mikrofon für den Schreibtisch verwenden.
Das Rode NT-USB Plus (aktuell für 126 Euro bei Thomann, Amazon zieht mit) ist ein solches hochwertiges Equipment, das sich aufgrund seiner technischen Daten auch problemlos für die Teilnahme an Podcasts eignet. Die Nierencharakteristik filtert störende Umgebungsgeräusche weg, während Funktionen wie Noise Gate und ein Kompressor die Sprachqualität verbessern.
Das Mikrofon wird über USB-C direkt ans Notebook angeschlossen – zusätzliche Treiber sind fürs unkomplizierte Onboarding in der Regel nicht nötig, der Strom kommt auch per USB. Praktisch sind außerdem ein Kopfhöreranschluss zur direkten Tonkontrolle sowie das mitgelieferte Tischstativ und der Popschutz.
Unauffälliges Headset: Anker Soundcore Aeroclip 2
Wer länger am Tag telefoniert oder in Videokonferenzen arbeitet, braucht – insbesondere wenn auch andere Familienmitglieder in der Wohnung sind – außerdem ein Headset, das einerseits weitgehend störungsfreie Kommunikation ermöglicht, und andererseits auch nach mehreren Stunden nicht in oder auf den Ohren drückt. Eine gute Möglichkeit dafür sind die Aeroclip 2 von Soundcore by Anker (derzeit für 152 Euro bei Anker sowie bei Amazon).
Da die beiden Ohrhörer mit einem flexiblen Bügel ans Ohr geklemmt werden, statt im Gehörgang zu sitzen, bleiben sie auch über längere Zeit angenehm zu tragen – und die Umgebung lässt sich weiterhin wahrnehmen. In Kombination mit einem speziellen KI-Chip sorgen vier Mikrofone und zwei Knochenschallsensoren dafür, dass die eigene Stimme auch trotz möglicher Hintergrundgeräusche beim Gesprächspartner ankommt.
Praktisch fürs Homeoffice ist außerdem die Möglichkeit, zwei Geräte gleichzeitig per Bluetooth zu verbinden, etwa das Notebook und das Smartphone. Dank acht Stunden versprochener Akkulaufzeit dürfte man problemlos über den Tag kommen, zumal man ja nicht den vollen Arbeitstag über telefonieren wird.
Monitor für ermüdungsfreies Arbeiten: Dell Pro Plus P2725Q
Natürlich kann man auch mit einem einfachen 22- oder 24-Zoll-Monitor arbeiten. Produktiver wird man aber sicherlich mit einem größeren Monitor sein, der noch dazu durch eine hohe Auflösung überzeugt. Ein solches Gerät ist der Dell Pro Plus P2725Q mit 27 Zoll Bildschirmdiagonale, der aktuell im Preisvergleich ab rund 370 Euro erhältlich ist.
Der Monitor bietet eine scharfe 4K-Auflösung mit 3.840 × 2.160 Pixeln und ein hochwertiges IPS-Panel mit guten Blickwinkeln und einer vergleichsweise hohen Helligkeit von 350 Candela pro Quadratmeter. Im Vergleich zu Full-HD-Bildschirmen bietet er damit viermal so viele Pixel, was besonders bei umfangreichen Tabellen, langen Texten oder der Arbeit mit mehreren Programmfenstern von Vorteil ist. Die Bildwiederholfrequenz von 100 Hertz sorgt außerdem für eine angenehm flüssige Darstellung beim Scrollen und Verschieben von Fenstern.
Praktisch ist die integrierte Docking-Funktion, sodass sich über ein einziges USB-C-Kabel Notebooks mit dem Monitor verbinden und gleichzeitig mit bis zu 90 Watt aufladen lassen. Außerdem gibt’s USB-Anschlüsse für Tastatur, Maus und weiteres Zubehör sowie einen Ethernet-Anschluss für die kabelgebundene Netzwerkverbindung. Der Dell-Bildschirm lässt sich in der Höhe verstellen, neigen und schwenken sowie um 90 Grad ins Hochformat drehen. Die matte Bildschirmoberfläche reduziert störende Spiegelungen. Dazu bietet Dell hier einige augenschonende Einstellungen, damit auch bei längeren Arbeitstagen ein ermüdungsfreies Arbeiten möglich ist.
Höhenverstellbarer Schreibtisch: Ergotopia Desktopia Pro X
Nicht erst seit der Pandemie gibt es eine große Zahl an auch für Privatpersonen bezahlbaren höhenverstellbaren Schreibtischen, die mit einem oder zwei Motoren ausgestattet sind. Wer acht Stunden oder mehr am Schreibtisch verbringt, kann etwa mit dem Ergotopia Desktopia Pro X mehr Bewegung in den Arbeitsalltag bringen. Zwei Elektromotoren verstellen die Tischhöhe stufenlos zwischen 62,3 und 127 Zentimetern, die Motoren arbeiten mit weniger als 50 Dezibel angenehm leise. Auch in der höheren Stellung steht der Tisch deutlich fester als mancher Mitbewerber aus dem Möbelhaus – keine wackelnde Platte, die für ein regelmäßiges Zittern der Kamera sorgt.
Dank der Memory-Funktion lassen sich bis zu neun bevorzugte Tischhöhen in drei Nutzerprofilen speichern. Eher streiten kann man dagegen über den Sinn des „integrierten Bewegungserinnerers“, der auf Wunsch durch Lichtsignale oder Vibration darauf aufmerksam macht, wenn es wieder Zeit für einen Positionswechsel ist. Wichtiger ist da schon der Kollisionsschutz, der verhindern soll, dass der Tisch beim Hoch- oder Herunterfahren gegen Hindernisse stößt.
Den Desktopia Pro X gibt’s in verschiedenen Größen und mit unterschiedlichen Tischplatten-Qualitäten. Die 160 × 80 Zentimeter große Standardplatte gibt’s derzeit für 549 Euro – mit Massivholzplatte in dieser Größe werden 779 Euro und mehr aufgerufen. Wer lieber bei Amazon kauft, bekommt den Tisch zum selben Preis – allerdings nur mit grauer Platte.

articles.title: Écriture excessive sur les SSD : le correctif de NVIDIA aurait besoin d'un... nouveau correctif !
articles.text:
Il y aurait, comme pourrait le dire Hamlet, « quelque chose de pourri au royaume GeForce » et le correctif tout juste publié semble avoir des effets pour le moins limités.
Un correctif publié en urgence qui ne fait pas le travail demandé ? Ou plutôt qui améliore les choses, sans toutefois corriger l'ensemble du problème ? C'est le constat que l'on peut avoir à propos du correctif 621.35 déployé par NVIDIA pour remédier au problème d'écriture excessive sur les SSD.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Un correctif publié ce week-end…
Pas plus tard qu'hier, nous avions publié la réaction de NVIDIA face au souci rencontré par certains utilisateurs de cartes graphiques GeForce. Un souci non pas lié aux cartes en elles-mêmes, mais plutôt à leurs pilotes.
Qu'il s'agisse de la version 621.01 ou de la 621.24, des usagers ont rencontré de gros problèmes d'écriture excessive sur le SSD système de leur machine. Il serait question du composant NVDisplay.Container.exe qui occasionnerait de multiples tâches d'écriture sur le SSD et provoquerait une usure accélérée du produit. NVIDIA n'a toutefois pas commenté officiellement cette information.
En revanche, NVIDIA a bien réagi et on peut difficilement faire plus officiel que la publication d'un hotfix pour lequel il est précisé : « Cette mise à jour résout les points suivants : des écritures excessives vers le fichier nvlog.nvlgstg peuvent se produire en arrière-plan ». De notre côté, nous n'avons rencontré aucun problème d'écriture excessive et n'avons donc pu vérifier la chose.
Reste que quand NVIDIA publie un hotfix, nous invitons systématiquement les usagers à vérifier s'ils sont affectés par le problème en question et, le cas échéant, à appliquer le correctif. Nous le faisons pour NVIDIA, mais également pour les rustines déployées par le concurrent AMD qui a d'ailleurs été touché par un problème assez similaire quelques semaines auparavant.
… mais un correctif largement défaillant
Hélas, si dans le cas d'AMD, nous n'avons observé aucune suite – en tout cas pour le moment – après la publication du correctif, il en va autrement pour NVIDIA. Plusieurs voix se sont élevées pour critiquer le hotfix 621.35.
En effet, il semblerait que ladite rustine ne fasse qu'atténuer le phénomène et ne corrige donc pas le problème à sa source. Nos confrères du site VideoCardz relaient notamment les propos d'un utilisateur sur Reddit qui dispose d'un PC à base de carte graphique GeForce RTX 4090 et de SSD Samsung 990 PRO. Il précise que si le patch semblait d'abord fonctionner – seulement 90,8 Ko de données enregistrées sur la première heure –, la situation a dégénéré.
La machine a été laissée en « idle » (inactive) durant toute une nuit de neuf heures et, au matin, le processus d'écriture s'était largement emballé : 40,85 Go de données avaient été écrites, soit le chiffre extravagant de 4,54 Go par heure. C'est un cas extrême qui est ici rapporté, mais d'autres témoignages confirment que le souci n'est pas révolu, même si le patch semble améliorer la situation chez de nombreux usagers.
En l'état, nous attendons donc que NVIDIA publie une nouvelle mise à jour, un correctif plus efficace, et nous ne vous conseillons pas d'installer le hotfix 621.35. Nous vous suggérons plutôt de revenir sur une version plus ancienne des pilotes graphiques GeForce si vous êtes affectés par le problème : évitez les 621.24 et, dans une moindre mesure, les 621.01.
Il est aussi intéressant de signaler l'affirmation de NVIDIA selon laquelle les GeForce RTX 50 ne sont pas affectées par le problème. Des témoignages contredisent cette thèse, même si les cas les plus nombreux semblent survenir sur les générations précédentes de cartes graphiques.
Source : VideoCardz

articles.title: Panneaux solaires en chute de 40 % : pourquoi les Français misent sur les batteries
articles.text:
À l’échelle nationale, le marché du photovoltaïque est resté relativement stable sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026 : 4 185 mégawatts (MW) ont été raccordés au réseau entre janvier et septembre, contre 4 336 MW un an plus tôt, selon les données publiées par Enedis. Le segment des installations de moins de 36 kilowatts-crête (kWc), en revanche, a nettement décroché. Cette catégorie regroupe les équipements résidentiels et les petits projets professionnels. Suppression des primes à l’autoconsommation, baisse des tarifs de rachat du surplus ou encore évolution de la TVA : les changements réglementaires ont freiné l’intérêt des Français pour le photovoltaïque.
Les petites installations photovoltaïques accusent une chute de 31 %
De janvier à septembre 2026, la nouvelle puissance photovoltaïque raccordée au réseau d’Enedis s’est élevée à 498 MW pour les installations de moins de 36 kWc, contre 729 MW sur la même période en 2025. Le recul atteint ainsi 31 %. En nombre d’installations, la baisse est encore plus forte, autour de 40 % : 80 670 en 2026, contre 135 443 l’année précédente. En 2024, année record, le nombre d’installations sur les neuf premiers mois a presque atteint 177 000.
Le reste du marché compense ce recul. Les entreprises et les collectivités ont raccordé 2 123 MW sur les neuf premiers mois de 2026, contre 1 783 MW un an plus tôt. Elles cherchent à se protéger des variations du prix de l’électricité, et certaines doivent aussi respecter l’obligation d’équiper leurs toitures et leurs parkings en panneaux solaires.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
Le désintérêt des particuliers pour le solaire résulte de la réduction progressive des aides publiques. En mars 2025, le gouvernement avait déjà fortement diminué le tarif de rachat du surplus d’électricité solaire. Pour les installations jusqu’à 9 kWc, la rémunération du kilowattheure (kWh) injecté sur le réseau était passée de 12,69 centimes à seulement 4 centimes, et la prime à l’autoconsommation avait été divisée par deux. Une nouvelle baisse est intervenue le 5 juin 2026, ramenant ce tarif à 1,1 centime par kWh pour toutes les installations jusqu’à 100 kWc. Par la même occasion, les primes à l’autoconsommation ont été supprimées. Ces deux dispositifs constituaient pourtant des leviers importants pour accélérer l’amortissement des installations.
Pour un foyer, l’effet se chiffre facilement. Prenons un ménage qui produit 3 000 kWh par an et en consomme directement la moitié : il touchait près de 190 euros par an pour la revente de son surplus avant mars 2025, puis environ 60 euros au tarif de 4 centimes. À 1,1 centime, ces 1 500 kWh injectés ne rapportent plus qu’environ 16,50 euros par an.
En octobre 2025, une autre évolution réglementaire était venue modifier les conditions économiques du solaire résidentiel. La TVA applicable aux installations jusqu’à 9 kWc est passée à 5,5 %, contre 10 % (jusqu’à 3 kWc) et 20 % (de 3 à 9 kWc) auparavant, mais sous conditions. Ce coup de pouce fiscal a pourtant freiné l’investissement : seuls les panneaux à faible empreinte carbone (moins de 530 kg d’équivalent CO₂ par kWc) et pauvres en argent, plomb et cadmium y ouvrent droit, avec un gestionnaire d’énergie obligatoire, et peu de modèles remplissaient ces critères. Les installateurs interrogés par pv magazine disent avoir vu leurs ventes aux particuliers chuter, parfois de 30 à 50 %, depuis l’annonce de cette TVA puis la baisse des tarifs d’achat.
Un contexte qui profite au marché des batteries
Les nouvelles mesures ont en revanche favorisé un autre marché : celui du stockage. Les données d’Enedis montrent que sur les trois premiers trimestres de 2026, les installations de moins de 36 kWc équipées d’une batterie ont représenté une puissance cumulée de 88 MW. Elles comptent ainsi pour 17,5 % des nouvelles capacités raccordées sur ce segment. À la même période en 2025, seuls 33 MW de projets étaient associés à un dispositif de stockage, soit une proportion de 4,5 %.
Cette année, les consommateurs ont été davantage orientés vers l’autoconsommation. Avec un surplus racheté 1,1 centime par kWh, les particuliers ont tout intérêt à consommer eux-mêmes l’électricité qu’ils produisent, en la stockant ou en décalant certains usages, plutôt qu’à la revendre. En effet, la production photovoltaïque dépasse déjà très souvent les besoins du réseau à certaines heures, particulièrement au printemps et en été.
D’ailleurs, selon une étude publiée le 9 novembre par l’Ademe, cet essor du stockage résidentiel a même favorisé l’apparition de nouveaux modèles commerciaux. Certains fournisseurs proposent désormais de piloter à distance les cycles de charge et de décharge des équipements. Ils peuvent, en contrepartie, agréger virtuellement les capacités de stockage de centaines, voire de milliers de particuliers, afin de constituer une réserve de flexibilité suffisamment importante pour être valorisée sur les marchés de l’électricité.
Le phénomène est sans doute sous-estimé. L’Ademe relève qu’une partie des batteries échappe aux statistiques, notamment les kits « Plug & Play » posés par les particuliers eux-mêmes, sans installateur. Elle évalue le parc de batteries résidentielles à au moins 216 MWh de capacité à la mi-2026. Avec la chute du prix des batteries lithium-ion, l’agence estime que l’investissement semble désormais pouvoir être rentable pour le consommateur.

articles.title: 👨🏿‍🚀TechCabal Daily – Hello from the Absa side
articles.text:
Good morning! ☀️️️
Jensen Huang was quite possibly the happiest man in tech yesterday. The name most synonymous with NVIDIA and the graphics processing units (GPUs) powering the AI boom is back at the helm.
After a tough couple of weeks in which revelations about Huang’s personal life became public, and he resigned as chief executive officer, NVIDIA’s board reinstated him on Monday as President, CEO, and Board Director. The stock market seemed to love the decision: NVIDIA shares surged more than 30% after the announcement, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company’s market value and reversing much of the previous rout.
Good one for Huang. But he wasn’t the only one celebrating yesterday. We also did a thing: TechCabal launched TC Mzansi after months of brainstorming and refining the product. The reception has been worth every drop of sweat we put into making it happen. Key ecosystem leaders have already signed up to read the newsletter every week. I’m not sure why you’re still stalling, but if you change your mind, subscribe here.
—Emmanuel
TC Mzansi, our newsletter covering South African tech, launches today.
Features
From Phathisani: Why TC Mzansi needed to exist
Yesterday, I had the pleasure of seeing the first edition of our latest newsletter, TC Mzansi, land in readers’ inboxes for the very first time. It is an exciting milestone, not just because we are launching a new newsletter, but because we are creating space for stories I believe deserve a much bigger audience.
When we started thinking about TC Mzansi, one question kept coming up: are we telling enough stories about the innovation happening right on our doorstep?
South Africa’s tech ecosystem is often viewed through big funding rounds, established startups, and headline-grabbing deals. Those stories matter, but they are only part of the picture. Across townships, rural communities, university labs, and smaller cities, young entrepreneurs are building solutions to everyday problems, often with limited resources but plenty of ingenuity.
That is the gap TC Mzansi wants to close.
The name was deliberate. Mzansi is more than an informal name for South Africa. It speaks to our identity, diversity, and the communities that make this country the Rainbow Nation. We wanted a product rooted in our realities, giving a platform to stories that rarely make the mainstream technology conversation.
Every edition will bring you closer to the people, businesses, and ideas shaping our digital future. Expect startup stories, emerging technologies, investment developments, policy shifts, and innovation beyond the major tech hubs. We will also explore connections between South Africa and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
For me, TC Mzansi is about widening the lens. Innovation doesn’t only happen in boardrooms or venture capital meetings. Sometimes, it starts with someone in a township solving a community problem.
Those are the stories worth telling. And we’re here to tell them.

M&A
Shoprite buys 40% stake in telecoms group
Shoprite started out selling groceries. Then it began helping customers send money and pay bills. Afterward, it launched its own mobile service. Now, the retailer is making a bigger play.
What happened? Shoprite, South Africa’s largest grocery retailer, is buying a 40% stake in DN Invest (DNI) for about R3.6 billion ($206.8 million). DNI is an investment group with interests in telecoms, fibre Internet, mobile devices, and fintech, with a portfolio that includes 3G Mobile, a SIM and handset distributor; Frogfoot, a fibre network operator; Vox Telecom, an Internet service provider; and Hypa, which provides affordable fibre services.
Explain like I’m new here: Shoprite has been building a financial services business alongside its grocery operations. It launched the Money Market Account in 2022, giving customers a low-cost transactional account to pay bills and send money, and offers money transfers through Shoprite Send. The retailer also operates K’nect Mobile, a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO), launched in March 2021, that sells prepaid airtime and data. It does not own the mobile towers that carry calls and internet traffic; instead, it uses Cell C’s network.
What does Shoprite get out of this? The deal gives Shoprite access to companies that sell SIM cards and phones, provide internet services, and build digital financial products, giving it a faster route to expanding beyond its existing offering. DNI generates more than R11 billion ($631.9 million) in annual revenue and over R1.2 billion ($68.9 million) in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA). Shoprite also has the option to eventually buy the remaining shares, potentially taking its ownership to 100%, subject to agreed terms and regulatory approval.

Telecoms
Absa partners with Vodacom to combine banking and mobile services
South African banks—and even retailers (read: Shoprite)—are getting into the telecoms business, but Absa, the country’s third-largest lender by assets, has decided to take a different route. Instead of launching its own mobile network like rivals Capitec and FNB, the banking giant has partnered with Vodacom, the country’s largest mobile operator by subscribers.
Together, they plan to offer customers a mix of banking services, mobile connectivity, loyalty rewards, and smartphone financing. The partnership could give Absa a way into the mobile market without having to run its own network.
Explain like I’m new here: In South Africa, banks have discovered that mobile connectivity can be another way to keep customers using their services. Tier 1 banks, including Capitec, FNB, Standard Bank, and Nedbank, all operate bank-branded mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) services. As MVNOs, banks run mobile networks that rely on white-label services from telecom operators. FNB Connect and Capitec Connect use Cell C’s infrastructure, while Standard Bank Connect and Nedbank Connect use MTN’s network.
Banks explore this route to deepen customer loyalty, create more reasons for people to use their apps and generate revenue from services beyond traditional banking.
State of play: In October 2025, Absa told local publication TechCentral that it was preparing to launch an MVNO and had spent six months researching what would persuade customers to switch to an Absa-branded SIM card. However, by June, Absa said it was still assessing different MVNO models and wanted to ensure any offering delivered real value, according to TechCentral.
But it appears the delay will not be a denial, as Absa is now trying to kick things into full gear. Yet, Absa seems cautious; the approach feels on-brand for a bank that chose to partner with blockchain firm Ripple to expand into crypto custody in August—at least recently.
Absa has not said why it moved from preparing an MVNO launch to partnering with Vodacom. However, the partnership makes sense at a glance; Vodacom will provide the connectivity andAbsa brings its banking services and customer relationships. Each company will continue managing its own customers. Absa gets to offer mobile services without the expense and complexity of running a network itself.

Economy
Africa’s cheap phones aren’t so cheap anymore
You walk into a phone shop looking for a basic Android. Nothing fancy, just something that can run WhatsApp, your banking app, and maybe take decent pictures. The seller tells you the price, and suddenly you’re asking about fairly used phones instead.
Across Africa, even the cheapest smartphones are becoming harder to afford.
According to research firm Omdia, smartphone shipments across the continent fell 40% to 13.7 million units in Q3 2026, down from 22.8 million in the previous year.
Explain like I’m new here: Shipments are the phones manufacturers send to shops and distributors, not necessarily the number customers buy. But they offer a useful picture of demand. When phones become harder to sell, manufacturers and retailers order fewer of them.
State of play: Nigeria recorded the steepest decline among major markets, at 47%, followed by Egypt at 41% and Kenya at 35%. South Africa fared better, with a 20% drop, partly because more buyers can spread payments through mobile contracts.
Between the lines: The biggest decline was among smartphones priced below $100, where shipments plunged nearly 70%. Meanwhile, basic feature-phone shipments grew 27%.
Here’s the problem: Rising manufacturing costs are making cheap smartphones less profitable to produce. Manufacturers are raising prices or reconsidering those models, while customers who can’t afford the increase keep their old phones or buy secondhand (fairly used devices).
Africa’s average smartphone price even reached $222, a ten-year third-quarter high. But buyers aren’t necessarily upgrading to better phones. Many are simply being priced out of new ones.
Zoom out: Omdia expects shipments to fall another 25% in 2027. Companies like M-KOPA and Vodacom are offering instalment payments to help buyers, but spreading the cost doesn’t reduce it. If even a basic smartphone requires a payment plan, getting connected becomes another household expense people have to budget for carefully.

articles.title: El gran fraude de la canela: Bruselas dice que dos tercios de la que se comercializa en Europa tiene problemas
articles.text:
La canela fue la quinta especia más importada por la UE en 2023. También ha sufrido un control de laboratorio. Los laboratorios de Europa han puesto a prueba a esta especia. El Centro Común de Investigación (JRC) ha analizado 104 productos de venta. De ellos, un 66,3 % tenían algún problema.
Entre ellos se detectaron problemas de calidad o incumplimientos de seguridad alimentaria. En algunos se sospechaba de fraude y en otros había un posible riesgo asociado a su contenido en cumarina. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que dos tercios de la canela que se comercializa en Europa tenga estos problemas.
Los problemas pueden ser muy diversos. Desde los que implican un incumplimiento de los estándares internacionales de calidad hasta posibles sospechas de adulteración o dudas en cuanto a la seguridad alimentaria. Esto último no implica que haya un fraude demostrado o que sean necesariamente peligrosos para el consumidor.
Ya se habían dado casos preocupantes. En el año 2021 se publicó un informe europeo donde se detectaron indicios de adulteración en algunas especias. Así ocurrió con pimienta, comino, cúrcuma, azafrán o pimentón. En el caso de la canela, la Comisión ha hecho públicos los resultados el 24 de septiembre de 2025. Las muestras fueron adquiridas en 10 países de la UE.
Lo que decía la etiqueta y lo que había dentro
Entre los problemas destacan los casos con exceso de plomo. Otro caso es el de muestras con altos niveles de cumarina. Se trata de un componente natural de la canela cassia, algo que puede llegar a ser tóxico para el hígado. En la legislación europea se regula el máximo admisible de cumarina en ciertos productos elaborados, pero no hay un valor concreto para la que viene de forma natural en la canela. El estudio apunta a posibles riesgos asociados al consumo. En especial para niños.
Por otro lado, también se encontraron discrepancias entre las declaraciones de la etiqueta y el propio producto. Alrededor del 9 % de las muestras que se anunciaban como canela de Ceilán tenían cassia (total o parcialmente). Se trata de una variedad más barata y con un sabor más fuerte. Es decir, se puede estar comprando una cosa y en realidad tener otra diferente (sin saberlo).
Para detectar este tipo de sustituciones (y otros problemas) es necesaria más que una sola técnica analítica. El JRC avisa de que es necesario disponer de métodos estandarizados en los laboratorios de control. La Comisión hace un llamamiento a los responsables políticos y fabricantes. Es necesario asegurar que la especia es auténtica (y cumple con la legislación en materia de seguridad alimentaria) y de calidad.

articles.title: Another GTA VI Glitch Unlocks Frame Rates on Xbox
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Another GTA VI Glitch Unlocks Frame Rates on Xbox
Since the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which has so far been a commercial smash-hit, as expected, gamers have seemingly been trying their best to break the game as much as possible, despite the limitations of modern gaming consoles. The latest GTA VI hack, following the prior first-person hack and DLSS 5 implementation, is a framerate unlock on Xbox Series X|S consoles that can apparently get the game running well beyond its 30 FPS limit. 
The hack appears to take advantage of a bug in Xbox's quick resume functionality to trick GTA VI into running at up to 60 FPS instead of the typical 30 FPS limit. This hack was recently tested by Digital Foundry on YouTube, who showed that the Xbox Series X reaches 60 FPS in certain scenarios while running GTA VI. The biggest framerate jump occurs in less dense areas and when the camera is pointed at areas like the sky box, where not much is happening. In dense areas, the framerate typically hovers around 40-45 FPS, and when driving fast through a dense area, for example, the framerate will drop to as low as 30 FPS again.The framerate unlock hack can be triggered by following these steps:
- The GTA VI framerate unlock hack is triggered by doing the following:
- Change the console to 60 Hz output in settings
- Boot the game and exiting the game with the Xbox button once the loading screen with the stars appears
- Go back into settings and change the system output to 120 Hz
- Boot another game and close it again with the Xbox button once it has passed its initial splash screen
- Switch back to GTA VI
It was previously confirmed that Rockstar deemed GTA VI too demanding to run beyond that 30 FPS cap on current-gen gaming consoles, and, although there is evidence to support that the PS5 may be running into some issues—mainly caused by aging liquid metal, it seems—it looks like the Xbox Series X can fairly consistently run the open-world game somewhere between 35 and 50 FPS during most situations, although there are still instances where the frame rate will drop below 30 FPS. This inconsistent performance above 30 FPS, as described by Digital Foundry, may be part of the reason why the framerate was locked. Additionally, the testing outlet reports that the game's engine appears to be tied to that 30 FPS cap, meaning that the game actually runs faster when the framerate is unlocked.
Hilariously, as demonstrated in the video, doing the inverse of the hack—that is, switching from 120 Hz output to 60 Hz output while GTA VI is suspended—will result in the game running at a locked 15 FPS.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
articles.text:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.
The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.
The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.
“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”
Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.
The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.
Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.
Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.
Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.
Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

articles.title: AI server makers hike prices up to 45% months after contracts are signed as RAM shortage triples memory-heavy CPU node costs — financial firms still pay up as 'the compute is valuable'
articles.text:
AI server makers hike prices up to 45% months after contracts are signed as RAM shortage triples memory-heavy CPU node costs — financial firms still pay up as 'the compute is valuable'
"I am altering the deal. Pray I do not alter it further."
"Prices are really expensive for technology X" isn't truly news anymore, but it seems that even the bigshots who place orders in the magnitude of hundreds of millions of dollars are feeling the pinch. According to the Financial Times (FT), trading and financial service firms are seeing post-contract hikes of up to 45% on their data center servers.
The price upgrades are coming in well after the ink has dried on the respective agreements, often signed months in advance. One unnamed person told the FT that "it is disconcerting when you get a 25, 30, 45 percent" increase, further adding that "there is a significant disparity" between the initial figure and the one that pops up on the final invoice.
However, even this bump isn't deterring well-funded financial firms, which are reportedly buying up as much compute power as they can get their hands on, and are willing to eat the cost. Another informant said "we've never said no," noting that "at the end of the day, the compute is valuable to us and we'll pay for it." The FT asked whether the contacted companies had any clauses in their contracts preventing price volatility, but none confirmed or denied the fact.
The publication predictably points to RAM pricing as the main cause behind the out-of-nowhere hikes, noting that while GPU servers have risen in price by 20-30%, memory-heavy CPU nodes purportedly doubled or tripled in price.
This is arguably more bad news for us peons, as it illustrates the DRAM shortage is alive and well, whether natural or fabricated. Furthermore, it shows if even the big shots are more than willing to pay inflated prices, then mere mortals have little chance of a RAM price reprieve.
Not every firm is taking the price jacking lying down, though. Back in June, XTX Finland Oy took one of Dell's Irish subsidiaries to court, after Dell asked for another $62 to $70 million on top of the previously agreed-on price of $549 million for 1,680 servers. That case is still ongoing and is an interesting watch, as XTX apparently paid $5 million extra for a contract clause specifically to prevent any pricing shenanigans.
Even if XTX wins, though, the firm may find it harder to do future business with OEMs. The supply-demand balance is currently so lopsided that chip fabs and OEMs have all the ability to pretty much set any terms they wish.
