articles.title: "Nunca voté, pero veo que es necesario": las colas en los consulados españoles dejan el primer termómetro del 29N
articles.text:
Queda aún la recta final, pero el 29N puede presumir ya de ser una campaña excepcional. Y por varias razones. No todas las elecciones se convocan arrastradas por una crisis social, lidian con una huelga general y la dimisión de un ministro y permiten ver a tres de los principales candidatos a la Moncloa sentados en el estudio de un youtuber. Más allá de esas peculiaridades, el 29N es especial por otro motivo: la relevancia de los electores residentes en el extranjero, marcados por las disputas en torno a la 'ley de nietos' y los bulos que cuestionan la fiabilidad del voto por correo.
Con ese telón de fondo, este fin de semana los consulados de España en el extranjero se han encontrado con una ‘fotografía’ poco habitual: largas colas de cientos de españoles que aguardaban horas para emitir sus votos.
Y llegó el 21N. Aunque parece que la maquinaria del 29N lleva semanas a pleno rendimiento, la realidad es que su calendario avanza poco a poco y aún no ha alcanzado todos sus hitos.
Por ejemplo, los españoles que viven en el extranjero no han podido depositar su voto de forma presencial en las embajadas hasta hace un par de días. Desde el 3 de noviembre tenían la opción de hacerlo por correo, pero quienes querían entregar su papeleta en mano han tenido que esperar algo más: al período comprendido entre el sábado 21 y el jueves 26.
¿Por qué es noticia? Porque el mismo sábado algunos consulados españoles en el extranjero se encontraron con colas formadas por decenas (en algunos casos cientos) de votantes deseosos de emitir su papeleta para el 29N.
Lo contaba este fin de semana Edgar Sapiña en EFE: frente a las oficinas consulares de París se formaron largas colas con centenares de españoles residentes en Francia. Y no es un caso único. Llega con echar un vistazo a Google o X para comprobar que se han vivido escenas similares en otras sedes diplomáticas de España, como las situadas en Londres o Washington. En Panamá fue la propia embajada la que compartía en X una foto en la que mostraba cómo “numerosos ciudadanos” habían acudido a su oficina para entregar su papeleta.
La cifra: 2,7 millones. Esas imágenes se entienden mejor al conocer un dato. El registro CERA (Censo Electoral de Residentes Ausentes) para el 29N asciende a 2,78 millones de personas, si bien EFE precisa que esa cifra incluye todos los nacionalizados al amparo de la 'ley de nietos'. Por países, la mayor parte del censo exterior se concentra en Argentina (524.000), Francia (268.000), EEUU (213.700), México (192.300), Reino Unido (156.000) y Venezuela (131.000).
Fuerte: Más de 100 personas en la cola para votar en la Embajada de España en Washington. https://t.co/oPzewv0aP9
— Rafael Yuste Muñoz (@rayusmu) November 21, 2026
Cua impressionant x votar al consolat espanyol a Londres. Més de 6oo metres, i la gent segueix arribant. @diariARA @socialistes_cat @Esquerra_ERC @AdaColau https://t.co/uCv5XpmL41
— Quim Aranda (@ArandaQuim) November 21, 2026
“Es necesario”. El sábado algunos de esos votantes llegaron a esperar hasta tres horas para ejercer su derecho en el consulado de París. Juan Allende, un jubilado asturiano que emigró a Francia en 1966, reconocía que este año ha hecho una excepción: “Nunca voté, no me gusta la política, pero veo que es necesario”. Él insiste en que España ahora “está muy arriba” y quiere contribuir para que se mantenga ahí.
Otros inscritos en el CERA, como Arancha, vallisoletana residente en Reino Unido, reconocía el sábado que quería votar en persona porque no se “fía” del Gobierno y tampoco ve descabellado que pueda “manipularse” el voto por correo.
La otra cifra: 9%. En un interesante análisis sobre la evolución del voto CERA, José Á. Carpio, de DatosRTVE, recordaba hace unos días dos datos relevantes del electorado residente en el extranjero. El primero tiene que ver con su número. Los 2,8 millones registrados por el INE representan el 7,2% del censo total de electores, un peso considerable que ha ido subiendo de forma sostenida a lo largo de las últimas décadas. En 1996 el censo CERA suponía apenas el 1,6% del registro total y en 2016 representaba el 5,3%.
Que ese porcentaje crezca no implica necesariamente que el voto CERA sea cada vez más relevante. Para que sea así debe cumplirse otro requisito: una subida en los niveles de participación (una cosa es tener un derecho, otra ejercerlo). Y la realidad es que los porcentajes de 2023 muestran que su capacidad para influir en el Congreso es muy limitada.
Hasta 2008 los niveles de participación del censo CERA se movieron entre el 20 y 36%, pero cayeron a partir de 2011, cuando se aplicó el sistema de voto rogado. En poco tiempo esa horquilla se redujo hasta quedarse en un 5-7%. En 2022 la supresión del requisito hizo que la participación volviese a subir, pero aun así durante los comicios de 2023 se mantuvo un parco 9%. ¿Cuál ha sido el resultado? Que en la práctica el voto CERA solo ha alterado tres escaños desde 1986.
Consulado de España en París 🤯 https://t.co/rgVW6Ig5Qw
— Daniel P (@danpast_) November 21, 2026
Hoy, la cola para votar en el Consulado Español en Zurich. 2 horas de espera en el frio de noviembre suizo. Esperemos que haya servido la pena! #EleccionesGenerales29N https://t.co/8WoOQ5mvmt
— Mercedes 🇪🇦🇨🇭 (@spaniard_071) November 21, 2026
La lupa del 29N. Tal vez el impacto cuantitativo del voto CERA sea cuestionable, pero desde luego estas elecciones han tenido una repercusión importante a nivel cualitativo.
¿La razón? En septiembre el Tribunal Supremo suspendió los efectos electorales de la ‘ley de nietos’, lo que afectó directamente a miles de altas en el CERA. De aquello hace ya bastante, pero el alcance de esa decisión cautelar ha seguido desde entonces en el foco del debate público. De hecho el viernes, apenas nueve días antes del 29N, el Supremo exigió a la Junta Electoral que garantice que más de 160.000 españoles que han obtenido la nacionalidad a través de la Ley de Memoria Democrática se mantengan fuera del censo electoral.
El fantasma del pucherazo. Quizás parezca una cuestión técnica, pero el debate legal ha estado bien salpimentado de política desde antes incluso de la convocatoria del 29N. En junio el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, incluso llegó a calificar la 'ley de nietos' de “ingeniería electoral”. Santiago Abascal fue más allá y durante un mitin acusó a Sánchez de querer “secuestrar las elecciones generales”.
No es el único debate que probablemente ha movilizado a los votantes CERA. Desde hace semanas parte de la oposición ha agitado las dudas en torno a la fiabilidad del voto por correo y el fantasma de un pucherazo. De hecho hace poco se podían leer publicaciones que aseguraban que 16 embajadas han reducido los controles para el voto exterior, una afirmación falsa según TVE, que recuerda que la Ley Electoral exige remitir los votos por valija diplomática y el correo postal solo se usa en el envío de papeletas al consulado.

articles.title: Microsoft Teams va surveiller vos appels avec l’IA pour démasquer les arnaques
articles.text:
Après avoir annoncé une fonctionnalité permettant de surveiller la présence des employés, Microsoft Teams dévoile un nouvel outil de surveillance qui devrait, cette fois-ci, profiter directement aux utilisateurs. La firme de Redmond a ajouté le 19 novembre à sa feuille de route Microsoft 365 une fonction qui utilisera l’intelligence artificielle pour analyser certains appels passés sur Teams et détecter d’éventuelles tentatives d’arnaque, comme l’a repéré Neowin. De quoi protéger les utilisateurs contre les escroqueries, mais aussi soulever quelques questions sur la confidentialité des conversations.
Une analyse qui pose question
Intitulée « Détection de phishing vocal », cette fonctionnalité sera activée lors des appels externes individuels. Elle repérera les signes de phishing vocal, un type d’arnaque dans lequel des cybercriminels tentent de manipuler leurs victimes par téléphone, notamment en usurpant l’identité d’une personne ou d’un organisme de confiance pour leur soutirer des informations sensibles.
Si cette fonctionnalité semble particulièrement utile sur le papier, elle soulève néanmoins plusieurs questions en matière de confidentialité. Microsoft n’a pas encore précisé si l’analyse des conversations serait effectuée directement sur l’appareil de l’utilisateur ou sur les serveurs de Microsoft. On ignore également si certaines données issues des appels seront conservées et comment cette fonctionnalité pourra fonctionner avec les communications chiffrées de bout en bout, comme le soulignent nos confrères de Neowin.
Selon le calendrier prévisionnel de Microsoft, la détection du phishing vocal devrait être accessible sur PC, Mac et smartphones à partir de janvier 2027. Une préversion est attendue dès décembre 2026. D’ici là, Microsoft devrait avoir levé une partie du voile sur le fonctionnement de cet outil et les garanties apportées en matière de confidentialité.

articles.title: Weird finger-wearable gaming mouse raises $43,000 on Kickstarter, a staggering 8x its crowdfunding goal — but thumb-only controls, AI images, and timeline mismatches raise red flags
articles.text:
Weird finger-wearable gaming mouse raises $43,000 on Kickstarter, a staggering 8x its crowdfunding goal — but thumb-only controls, AI images, and timeline mismatches raise red flags
This weird "finger-worn gaming mouse" has reached $43,000 in its Kickstarter campaign.
The Borslon wearable gaming mouse takes the concept of a gaming mouse to the extreme by making your finger the aiming device. The Kickstarter has already reached over $43,000 with more than 430 backers, beating its $5,000 goal — but is it truly innovative, or just a gimmick?
The Borslon mouse, sharing a product and brand name, is a wired, “finger-worn gaming mouse,” as the brand describes it. It has all the spec numbers you’d expect from a good gaming mouse: a PAW3395 sensor, an 8,000 Hz polling rate, 0.125 ms response time, programmable buttons, and weighs 36g. However, the specs are often only the base level for performance; how it performs in the real world could be a very different story.
This product targets FPS gamers, and in the FPS gaming niche, there is an even smaller niche — aimers. These aiming communities focus purely on the mechanical skill of precisely landing shots on targets, experimenting with techniques and devices to improve their aim. The community explores various aiming devices like tiny fingertip mice and even drawing tablets, with some brands directly marketing their mice in aiming Reddit groups.
The Borslon mouse isn’t the first extreme fingertip mouse; indie mice like the Precision Gaming Gear Titan-Ø and Titan-1 with their 3D-printed titanium construction and ruby joints launched years ago and sold out extremely quickly due to their popularity in the aiming niche.
There is reason to be skeptical of the Borslon mouse, as the videos alone don’t show even remotely impressive aiming examples, only playing against bots in Counter-Strike 2 with the player showing sub-par aim, while the creator of the Titan series mice showed decent actual gameplay in Quake Champions and is active in the aiming community.
Conventionally, many Counter-Strike, Apex Legends, and Valorant players use the scroll wheel for jumping or bunny-hopping (or tap strafing in Apex Legends, a high-level movement mechanic), and most players use their index or middle finger to scroll. However, the Borslon places the mouse wheel at the thumb, including the five programmable buttons, leaving plenty of responsibility to the appendage. From the Kickstart promotional material, it doesn’t look like the index finger or the middle finger have any buttons to press — which means the thumb is responsible for your usual inputs like aiming down sights (ADS), firing, and jumping; actions that usually happen simultaneously or in quick succession.
Borslon plans to ship out by February of 2027, with mass production planned for December, leaving little to no time to drastically change the design of the product.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
There is also an unusual disconnect between the mouse and its supposedly intended market, as I have not found any discussions about the Borslon mouse in any of the top aiming circles, nor is there any mention of it in the Voltaic Discord, a popular aiming community with over 200,000 members.
Upon further research, the Borslon brand is made by Shenzhen Komodo Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., with the Borslon website fully in Chinese, but neither the website nor the Kickstarter links to the other. A machine translation of the Borslon website of the company timeline says it released its first product in November 2025, while the Kickstarter says the concept initiation was in March 2026. The misalignments, combined with the heavy use of AI lifestyle images, don’t spark confidence in the project. If this is indeed real, it could potentially be a genuinely innovative mouse if the brand talked to the intended market and made proper changes.
Our customary crowdfunder disclaimer applies. Remember that crowdfunding a project is not a guarantee of receiving a finished product. Backing a crowdfunded project is akin to an investment; you believe in the project and want it to succeed. You are not purchasing a retail product.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Also follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Jhet Borja is a serial hobbyist who was taking apart toys from childhood and sketching inventions. He now loves doing DIY projects ranging from designing custom 3D-printed parts, building PCs and keyboards, all the way to woodworking. If he's not getting his hands dirty, he's probably brainstorming his next project.
- Ralston18 Not (full disclosure) a gamer.
However, I did a simple experiment.
I am right-handed so I pressed/rested my right index finger on my desk.
Then "practiced" by sliding my right hand and index finger around abit while tapping my first finger knuckle joint with my thumb.
Emulating the device in the photograph and my understanding of how that mouse is intended to be used.
"Major design flaws" indeed.
Not at all workable for me. Others may have different results.
The "Kickstarter" / "Crowd-funding" caveats are well warranted.
Just my thoughts on the matter. Reply

articles.title: The $419 Geekom A5 2027 Edition mini PC is 'built for long shifts' at work
articles.text:
The 4-star Geekom A5 2027 Edition mini PC is 'built for long shifts' in the office — and it's got a $290 discount for Black Friday
Ideal for home office use
The Geekom A5 mini PC has long been one of our top recommendations for professionals and hobbyists who want a machine that can easily tackle general tasks, with plenty of upgrade scope too.
Now, as Black Friday kicks off, the A5 2027 Edition has dropped to $419 (was $709) at Geekom when you use code BFA5130. This model comes equipped with 16GB DDR4 RAM and 256GB SSD, both of which can be expanded.
When we tested out this machine, we found it well-specced for general office use and light content creation. It may not deliver workstation-grade performance like the Geekom A9 Max, but it's also a third of the price right now. For day-to-day work, we found it "a cooler, quieter machine built for long shifts rather than short bursts."
Designed for the office, the Geekom A5 2027 Edition comes equipped with AMD Ryzen 7 7730U processor, 16GB of memory, and 256GB SSD - although other storage capacities are also discounted for Black Friday. For the full discount, use code BFA5130.
Why we recommend it
The A5 is designed to be a practical, effective daily driver rather than a beast for tough workloads.
Inside its compact chassis you’ll find an AMD Ryzen processor, integrated Radeon graphics, and upgradeable DDR4 memory. The system also supports up to four 4K display outputs, and it’s got dual HDMI ports, USB-C connectivity, and 2.5Gb Ethernet.
When we reviewed the 2027 Edition, we awarded it four stars and found it to be "good value, well-made," with a user experience that's on-point for day-to-day office tasks. It's not a powerhouse by any measure, but for general use, it ticks all the right boxes.
It also impressed with its quiet cooling and relatively easy upgrade process. You can expand memory to 64GB and add up to 7TB SSD storage.
Price context and historical value
At this price, the A5 is a sensible choice. It’s an effective option for anyone setting up a small office or people who want to buy a smaller system that’s good for everyday computing. The upgradeable component options add versatility, and its connectivity is reasonable. I'm not convinced I've ever seen it on sale for the list price of $709, but the overall discount is a fair one.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Geekom A5 2027 Edition if… you want an affordable, compact desktop for office applications, browsing, and multitasking.
❌ Skip the Geekom A5 2027 Edition if… you need dedicated graphics, demanding creative performance, or high-speed USB4 connectivity.

articles.title: Mzansi's power moves
articles.text:
Howzit, Mzansi! 🇿🇦
Welcome to the first edition of TC Mzansi. We’re excited to bring you closer to the people, ideas, and businesses shaping South Africa’s technology ecosystem and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
South Africa’s technology story is bigger than its established tech hubs. Across the country and throughout the wider region, young people are building businesses, developing solutions, and finding new ways to tackle everyday challenges. Some are doing this in the offices and innovation hubs of Cape Town and Johannesburg; others are working in townships, rural communities, and places that rarely make the technology headlines.
This newsletter will bring those stories into focus. We will explore the people, ideas, investments, and innovations shaping the region’s digital future, while asking what it takes to turn promising ideas into businesses that create real impact.
Expect a new edition every week by 1 pm SAST (12 pm WAT).
We’re glad to have you along for the journey.
Let’s stay connected!
Phathisani Moyo
Head, South African Desk, TechCabal
Top Headlines from South Africa
Mixed reactions as Ramaphosa defends his Silicon Valley trip
Microsoft’s 18-hour outage exposed South Africa’s dependence on Big Tech
ICASA to fight Sakeliga’s court bid over 30% ownership rule
From coding at 12 to building an AI company backed by global investors
Let’s dive in, but first… check this out
Put your business in front of Africa’s decision-makers
Reach over 150,000 tech and business leaders across Africa with TC Daily and the TechCabal newsletter family. Introduce your brand, promote your product, or share your next big launch with the people building and backing businesses across the continent.
Send an email to ads@bigcabal.com
South Africa’s Cyril Ramaphosa. Image Source: NPR.
Mixed reactions as Ramaphosa defends his Silicon Valley trip
South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa’s 300-person delegation to Silicon Valley has sparked debate over public spending, diplomatic priorities, and South Africa’s ambitions in artificial intelligence (AI).
Ramaphosa defended the week-long visit, saying private companies covered much of the cost and that the mission could attract investment, build technology partnerships and position South Africa as an AI innovation hub. The delegation includes eight cabinet ministers, 24 startups, postgraduate AI students, researchers and business leaders. Its programme includes engagements with Google, Microsoft, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks.
However, the president has refused to disclose the trip’s total cost or identify its sponsors, fuelling criticism from citizens, former diplomats, and political observers. Supporters argue that the visit should be judged by its ability to deliver investment, skills development, and jobs.
Phathisani’s view: South Africa needs global technology partnerships, but taxpayers deserve transparency and clear, measurable returns, not promises wrapped in diplomatic spectacle.
Read the story
Microsoft’s 18-hour outage exposed South Africa’s dependence on Big Tech
Microsoft’s 18-hour global outage on November 13 disrupted South African businesses and public institutions, exposing the risks of relying on a handful of technology giants to keep essential operations running. Eskom, Absa, and FlySafair were among those affected, alongside the City of Cape Town and the South African Revenue Service (SARS).
The disruption hit Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint, forcing organisations to redirect customers and employees to alternative communication channels. Although Microsoft worked to restore services, the incident exposed how a failure in one global technology provider can ripple across banking, aviation, public services, and the broader economy.
As cloud platforms become central to business operations, the outage raises urgent questions about digital resilience, backup infrastructure, and business continuity. South Africa cannot build a resilient digital economy while leaving critical business and public services vulnerable to failures in infrastructure it does not control.
Read the full story
ICASA to fight Sakeliga’s court bid over 30% ownership rule
South Africa’s telecoms licencing rules are heading for a legal battle that could shape how foreign technology companies enter the market. The Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA), the country’s telecoms regulator, will oppose lobby group Sakeliga’s court application challenging the regulator’s refusal to recognise equity-equivalent investment programmes as an alternative to 30% local ownership.
The programmes would allow multinational operators to invest in areas such as skills development and enterprise support instead of selling shares in their South African businesses to historically disadvantaged groups (HDGs).
The case has implications for companies such as Starlink, the Elon Musk-owned satellite Internet company, which could face ownership requirements before securing a licence. Sakeliga wants the High Court to overturn ICASA’s decision, arguing that it failed to implement Communications Minister Solly Malatsi’s policy direction to align ownership rules with the ICT sector code.
The dispute pressures the government’s efforts to attract foreign investment while maintaining transformation requirements in the telecommunications industry.
Read the full story
From coding at 12 to building an AI company backed by global investors
Young South African tech entrepreneur Emile Ferreira is building the kind of technology that could shape how businesses use artificial intelligence. Ferreira is the co-founder and chief technology officer of Verascient, a Cape Town-founded AI infrastructure startup that recently raised R19.5 million ($1.2 million) from international investors, including Founder Collective, co-founded by South African technology entrepreneur David Frankel.
His journey is remarkable. He taught himself to code at 12, joined software development platform Replit as one of its first hires while still in high school, and developed an on-device AI assistant that reportedly reached more than 200,000 Android users. He later graduated with distinction from the University of Cambridge with a master’s degree in advanced computer science.
Verascient is tackling a practical business challenge: helping organisations turn fragmented information into useful intelligence for AI agents.
Read the full story
The former crypto sceptic building a new way to move Africa’s money
Image Source: TechCabal.
For Harry Huang’s family, paying an overseas supplier sometimes meant finding someone who knew someone. Years later, that frustration is the business opportunity behind Lumepay. The former crypto sceptic is combining stablecoins with banking infrastructure to help African businesses move money across borders. In this week’s Coffee With, TechCabal’s Phathisani Moyo speaks to Huang about building a payments company around a simple expectation: the money must arrive.
Read it now
Image Source: United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF).
In Zambia, Airtel turns mobile money into a gateway to stock-market investing: Airtel Zambia has launched Airtel Money Buy Shares, a service that lets customers buy shares in companies listed on the Lusaka Securities Exchange through the MyAirtel app using their mobile money accounts. The move pushes telecom operators further into financial services, beyond payments and transfers, and could lower barriers to stock-market participation.
The opportunity is significant. FinScope Zambia’s 2025 survey found that 76.1% of adults used mobile money, while the share using capital-market products rose from 0.6% in 2020 to 13.8% in 2025. The challenge will be turning mobile access into sustained investment participation.
Read the story
Zimbabwe’s Cabinet approves national artificial intelligence charter: Zimbabwe’s Cabinet has approved a National Artificial Intelligence Charter to establish ethical and governance principles for AI development and deployment. The framework operationalises the country’s 2026–2030 National AI Strategy and sets expectations around transparency, accountability, inclusion and human-centred technology.
It also proposes governance structures for strategic oversight, coordination and complaints handling. The development matters as African governments move from announcing AI ambitions to deciding on regulation. For businesses, the charter could provide greater regulatory clarity, but its impact will depend on how the principles are translated into enforceable rules and practical oversight.
Read the story
Paratus brings Starlink enterprise services to another SADC market: Paratus Group, a pan-African fibre and satellite operator, has launched Starlink-powered enterprise connectivity in Malawi, targeting businesses and institutions that struggle with unreliable or limited terrestrial networks. Its offering will serve sectors including banking, healthcare, agriculture, mining and education, with local installation and technical support.
The launch expands Paratus’s network presence to 16 countries across sub-Saharan Africa. The company says it has already signed several enterprise customers and can complete installations within 24 to 48 hours, depending on location. The move adds another competitor in the regional satellite connectivity market, while raising questions about affordability and how far enterprise-focused services can extend access beyond major cities.
Read the story
Four-country satellite school project targets 30 rural schools: Satellite operator SES and the International Telecommunication Union’s Partner2Connect coalition plan to connect 30 rural schools across Malawi, Burundi, Zambia and Zimbabwe by the end of 2026. The project is expected to benefit between 20,000 and 30,000 students and teachers, giving underserved communities access to online learning platforms, teacher-training resources, and digital collaboration tools.
Satellite connectivity is intended to overcome gaps where fibre and mobile infrastructure have not reached. The initiative is part of SES’s wider commitment to connect 100 schools globally, highlighting the role of satellite networks in extending digital education across rural southern Africa.
Read the story
Teraco brings wind power into SA data centre mix
Image Source: Empower Africa.
A quick look at the week’s most consequential story in Southern African tech.
Teraco, Africa’s largest interconnected data centre operator, has begun receiving wind-generated electricity through South Africa’s national and municipal grids, marking a significant step in its renewable energy strategy.
The first electricity from its contracted independent power producer (IPP) wind project reached its Cape Town data centres in September. The initiative forms part of a R3.5 billion ($200 million) renewable energy programme combining solar generation, wind power purchases and grid infrastructure investment.
A key component is Sediba, a 120MW solar plant under construction in the Free State, backed by R2.25 billion. Teraco aims to achieve 100% renewable energy by 2035, as demand for data centre capacity grows alongside cloud computing and AI.
Read the story
That’s the estimated enterprise value of Telkom as MTN revives takeover talks that could reshape South Africa’s telecommunications industry.
MTN, South Africa’s second-largest telecom group by subscribers, has revived takeover talks with Telkom, its JSE-listed rival, four years after walking away, in a deal that could reshape South Africa’s telecoms industry. The proposed acquisition would combine MTN’s mobile business with Telkom’s 25 million subscribers, fibre network and enterprise operations. But with the government owning 40.5% of Telkom and the PIC another 11.08%, the deal faces significant shareholder, competition and regulatory hurdles. If successful, it could transform the country’s connectivity market and become one of the biggest transactions in South Africa’s digital economy.
On our radar: Will X’s two-year deal deliver value to South African publishers?
South Africa’s Competition Commission. Image Source: MyBroadband.
South Africa’s Competition Commission has reached a settlement with Elon Musk’s social media platform X (formerly Twitter), requiring it to support qualifying local news publishers through a two-year monetisation programme. X must introduce the programme within six months, with twice-yearly workshops on revenue tools, audience analytics, and content strategies.
Its AI arm, xAI, will separately train publishers twice a year on managing access to their content by AI chatbot Grok. But the deal stops short of guaranteeing direct payments. The Commission’s inquiry found that four local publishers earned a combined $914.25 from X’s creator revenue programme. The test now is whether the commitments translate into meaningful income and greater control over how AI uses local journalism.
Read the story
Until next week!
That’s your weekly briefing on South Africa and Africa’s technology economy.

Jensen is back: Nvidia board reinstates Huang as CEO
articles.text:
Winners & losers: Nvidia's board has unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as the company's president, CEO, and board director. The reappointment comes 11 days after Huang resigned following revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a Singapore-based businesswoman whom US intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy.
The move marks a sharp reversal by the board. Chair Harvey C. Jones said last week that the company had no plans to reinstate Huang as CEO, a statement that came after Huang said he would be "honored" to return if the board wanted him back.
 – WallStreetBets (@wallstreetbets) November 23, 2026
In an official statement, Nvidia said the decision followed input from senior US officials, who reportedly confirmed that his return posed no national security risk. The company said the board was confident in Huang's ability to lead, and that his reinstatement "is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."
 – Trung Phan (@TrungTPhan) November 23, 2026
Nvidia said its investigation into the incident is continuing and that Huang's reappointment will not affect the process. "Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it," the company said, adding that it will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.
Nvidia's statement did not name any US official or elected politician, but the decision came a day after President Trump called for Huang's return. Trump posted on Truth Social that he hopes the Nvidia board will rehire Jensen Huang. "It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.," he added.
In a statement following the announcement, Huang said he was honored to return to Nvidia and was taking on the responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." He also thanked the board for believing in him and reinstating him as the company's president and chief executive.
Nvidia shares, which had slumped almost 50% from their October peak, surged 29% on news of Huang's reinstatement. The stock was trading up nearly 34% this morning from last Friday's 52-week low of $124.50. It's still trading about 31% below its all-time high of $243.37 from October 2026.
 – Morning Brew ☕️ (@MorningBrew) November 23, 2026
Huang resigned from Nvidia in disgrace days after The New York Times reported that he was "socializing" with Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials suspected of spying for Beijing. The relationship was subsequently confirmed as romantic by Financial Times before reports of at least two more affairs with Nvidia employees became public.

articles.title: En 'GTA VI' hay un punto de no retorno que te hace perder misiones, objetos y dinero. Antes de avanzar, asegúrate de hacer esto
articles.text:
Arreglar la casa, explorar el barrio, salir a pescar, entrenar, darle de comer a la serpiente... El principio de 'GTA VI' se presta a la calma total, pero no te confíes porque el juego tiene preparada una trampa que llega cuando menos te lo esperas. Hay un punto en el que la historia avanza de golpe al capítulo 2 y no sólo te saca de 'Leonida Keys', también te deja sin dinero y sin posibilidad de acceder a varias misiones y objetos que ya no volverán a aparecer.
La misión clave. El encargo que activa este punto crítico se llama 'Trampa para turistas' y va justo después de 'Recalibrado', la fiesta nocturna con Cal (si quieres volver a esta zona en algún momento, puedes crear un punto de guardado manual tras esta misión). Una vez aceptes la misión, se activan tres misiones consecutivas que te llevan al capítulo 2. Si quieres hacerte con objetos únicos y completar todas las tramas de esta parte de la historia, deberás hacerlo antes de llegar a este punto.
Pon tu dinero a salvo. El cambio de capítulo te deja con lo puesto. Vas a perder todo tu dinero en efectivo, incluyendo el saldo de la cuenta bancaria. Para no quedarte a cero, ingresa el máximo que te permite la cuenta de ahorros familiares de BuckMe, que son 5.000 dólares. Ese dinero acumulado en la hucha es lo único que sobrevivirá al salto de episodio, así que fúndete el resto. Puedes hacerte tatuajes, comprar ropa, armas o cualquier otra cosa que se te ocurra.
Completa las misiones de Shirley. Shirley es tu vecina y te pide dos favores. El primero es que le compres una botella de ron en una tienda local. Al llegar allí se escuchan ruidos extraños en la trastienda y, si entras, encontrarás un negocio ilegal. Después te pide que le robes el scooter a un vecino. Es una pequeña misión sin mayor importancia, pero si no la completas ahora desaparecerá para siempre.
Meditación con Lucía. Una mañana estás en casa y Lucía te propone meditar con ella. Sal al balcón con ella y acepta la oferta, es tu única oportunidad. Esto abrirá una serie de 18 meditaciones que, si completas, te dan el trofeo "Actitud mental positiva".
Objetos y coleccionables. Hay varios a lo largo del capítulo que no podrás volver a encontrar, como los libros y revistas que hay repartidos por casa de Jason o las gafas de sol que le ofrecen a Lucía en la misión 'Libertad por un día'. Casi al final del capítulo, te encargan limpiar el remolque de Donnie, donde encontrarás un revolver único.

articles.title: F1 in Las Vegas: You’ve never seen an F1 race like this before
articles.text:
Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing.
The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor.
And because it takes place at night, in the desert, in November, it’s cold—much, much colder than anywhere else the sport will visit all year. This coming weekend in the Middle East, track temperatures may well exceed 122° F (50° C ); on Saturday night in Nevada the track was a mere 59° F (15° C). Combined with the concrete streets, that spells low grip, but there is an added benefit—virtually no tire wear or overheating.
FP1 was completely rained out. A few drivers completed installation laps, but the risk of a crash was far too high.
Credit:
Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images
FP1 was completely rained out. A few drivers completed installation laps, but the risk of a crash was far too high.
Credit:
Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images
And finally, there’s the slipstream. This was far more powerful than in years past, thanks to the new aerodynamic regulations. We saw this play out in qualifying, which took place on Friday night, when Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli snatched pole position by being the last man on track and benefiting as the cars ahead cleared the air out of his way. Conversely, the Ferrari duo of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc had a torrid time by not working together—a preview for the following night, as we’ll see…
Antonelli’s pole was quickly forgotten, though, as the new World Champion would only start sixth due to a grid penalty for using an engine component outside his allowance.
These two hate each other
Because of the penalty, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was on pole, with Mercedes’ George Russell next to him. To say there is little love lost between these two drivers would be to undersell the depths of animosity in that relationship. This was evident in FP3, when the pair clashed on track in what looked like a repeat of the Verstappen/Liam Lawson incident in Mexico. This time, no penalties were handed out.
Russell and Verstappen had a robust exchange of opinions on track during FP3.
Credit:
Stephanie Tacy/NurPhoto
Russell and Verstappen had a robust exchange of opinions on track during FP3.
Credit:
Stephanie Tacy/NurPhoto
“He does this week in, week out with many drivers, and everybody accepts it, and I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to that guy,” Russell said on Friday. That set up the prospect of a lap 1, turn 1 coming together, but instead the start of the race was remarkably clean. But not boring.
Within a lap, Russell had passed Verstappen for the lead on a straight, before the Red Bull reclaimed the position going into turn 17 on the last corner. This set the tone for things to come, with the Mercedes repeatedly getting past the Red Bull at turn 14, only for Verstappen to regain the lead through sheer commitment, taking back his lead in the corners.
Don’t be tempted to call this yo-yo racing; it was nothing like the races we saw early in the season, when everyone was still trying to understand their hybrid deployment and regeneration strategies. Like an oval race, knowing when to try to move up through the pack was vital; choosing it wrong meant losing multiple positions, not just one. But like an oval, it was also possible to work one’s way up through the pack.
The second Red Bull of Isack Hadjar looked more competitive than at any other time this year, and, had the two teammates worked together, they might have been able to leapfrog each other to break free of the pack—a tactic we see used to good effect on oval races. Whether Verstappen’s temperament would allow him to let his teammate past even temporarily remains unknown (I have my doubts), but Red Bull never tried it, instead ordering Hadjar to hold position, leaving him vulnerable to attack from behind. His day was ruined when his front wing exploded on lap 25, dropping him from third to dead last.
The second Red Bull looked like it could stick with Verstappen. Hadjar was told by his team not to try to pass, but then his wing exploded.
Credit:
Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images)
The second Red Bull looked like it could stick with Verstappen. Hadjar was told by his team not to try to pass, but then his wing exploded.
Credit:
Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images)
His best yet?
So Verstappen never broke free of the chasing pack, with five or six cars covered by as little as 2.5 seconds for much of the time.
Again and again Russell took the lead briefly but lost it again to Verstappen, who worried over the radio that the Mercedes team had figured out his strategy and was going to be able to defeat it on the last lap.
“I think in the beginning we had the deployment immediately correct, but of course, people are learning and watching what you’re doing. At one point, I couldn’t get back into the lead before the start-finish line, so I just—that’s why I asked the question,” Verstappen said after the race. “But I think we had it set up well, and it was just a crazy amount of fighting. The slipstream was so big that you—it was just impossible to drive off, and it was just crazy how many people were just following you.”
But Mercedes fumbled. George Russell crashed into a barrier on lap 47—probably as he ran over a piece of Hadjar’s broken wing, preventing him from braking in time. And Antonelli blew his own chance when, instead of charging his battery for that last-lap, last-corner pass, he accidentally drained it entirely. The team that claimed the 2026 Constructors’ championship last time out in Mexico had to settle for another weekend off the podium.
George Russell went into 2026 as the clear title favorite. Instead, that went to his young teammate. He’s currently fourth in the standings, behind Verstappen and Hamilton.
Credit:
Kym Illman/Getty Images
George Russell went into 2026 as the clear title favorite. Instead, that went to his young teammate. He’s currently fourth in the standings, behind Verstappen and Hamilton.
Credit:
Kym Illman/Getty Images
Verstappen claimed his 75th win, one he said was more like Mario Kart than any of the previous 74. McLaren’s Lando Norris was just 0.64 seconds behind him, with the other McLaren of Oscar Piastri a similar gap behind his teammate. The orange pair worked well together and took home a big bounty of points in their fight with Ferrari for second place in the constructor’s championship as a result.
If you come at the King, you best not miss
Ferrari’s Friday was already being called a disaster, as the two red cars couldn’t make it into the third and final qualifying session. Had they worked together to tow each other, this might have been possible. But things are far from harmonious at Ferrari between their two very closely matched drivers, with plenty of fireworks recently in Mexico City.
During the race, things got worse. The cars stratified themselves according to performance, which meant teammates running together often. Early on, Hamilton and Leclerc kept it mostly clean, although Hamilton earned a 10-second penalty when he went off track to avoid Norris and Leclerc, dropping him to 14th at the time. With safety cars, strategy, and that strong tow, Hamilton clawed his way back up the running order and was again in front of Leclerc by lap 34.
Four laps later, Leclerc tried to pass Hamilton—despite being specifically told by his team five corners earlier to hold position. Leclerc misjudged it, like he did in Monza and Mexico, and the cars made contact, dropping Hamilton to 10th. The race stewards clearly apportioned blame to Leclerc, handing him a 10-second penalty. Hamilton eventually finished seventh, Leclerc 10th.
You just knew if any two cars were going to have a coming together, it would be the Ferrari duo.
Credit:
Tayfun CoÅkun/Anadolu via Getty Images
You just knew if any two cars were going to have a coming together, it would be the Ferrari duo.
Credit:
Tayfun CoÅkun/Anadolu via Getty Images
Leclerc appears desperate to show the team he’s better than the seven-time champion it hired to race alongside him, but time and again his efforts end badly, costing the team points instead. Team boss Fred Vasseur had evidently read Leclerc part one of the riot act before the media pen—the pallid, tear-stained face of the Monegasque driver was that of a man who looked like he knew he really screwed up this time. Having signed a massive multiyear contract, his position with the team is presumably safe. But were I Vasseur, one of Ferrari’s reserve drivers would be getting a call to get ready to replace him for the weekend in Qatar.
Like Leclerc and Hamilton, Russell has been writing checks about Verstappen that his racing hasn’t cashed, and in the post-race interview, Verstappen had simply epic levels of disrespect for the other driver.
“The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track, and honestly, you know, for me, it doesn’t really bother me because he’s so far below my level that it doesn’t really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that, you know? So it doesn’t bother me,” Verstappen said. “And today, karma is a bitch. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening, so I was like, ‘Fantastic, my day is only getting better.’ And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete.”
Did you know Red Bull served hatorade?
Credit:
Mark Sutton/Getty Images
Did you know Red Bull served hatorade?
Credit:
Mark Sutton/Getty Images
Let’s move on from Canada 2010
So many unique circumstances went into making this particular Las Vegas Grand Prix as exciting as it was, and there’s little chance the next two rounds, which both take place in the Middle East, will see similar conditions. But F1 can take something away from this race to make future seasons better, and it’s to do with the tires.
It all goes back to the 2010 Canadian Grand Prix. Like this year in Vegas, Canada 2010 was chaotic. The weather was cold, the traction zones were covered in a low-grip surface to combat the tarmac disintegration seen in the years before, and the action was unpredictable as each team tried to figure out on the fly how best to adapt.
F1’s powers that be saw this, and when they awarded Pirelli a sole supplier contract for tires the following year, they instructed the company to make race tires that would cause the same effect. Of course, it hasn’t ever worked out like that. Canada 2010 was a one-off and caught the teams off guard. But running the same Pirelli tires race after race, everyone quickly figured out the optimal strategy, leaving little room for chaos.
I don’t think every race should be like Las Vegas, but I do think it’s earned its spot on the calendar.
Credit:
Clive Mason/Getty Images
I don’t think every race should be like Las Vegas, but I do think it’s earned its spot on the calendar.
Credit:
Clive Mason/Getty Images
And the Pirelli tires, while better than they once were, are still difficult to drive on. Pirelli mandates high minimum pressures out of fear of tire failures, and next week in Qatar has told teams they cannot run a set for more than 27 laps. As we frequently see in races, tires that stay within their temperature window while running in clean air can quickly overheat when following another car. In the wake of a car ahead, the following car has less downforce and slides more in the corners, which puts more heat into the tires, and the trailing car falls behind. Pirelli makes the tires that F1 asks for, but after this weekend’s race, it’s time for the sport to ask for something different.
Jonathan is the Automotive Editor at Ars Technica. He has a BSc and PhD in Pharmacology. In 2014 he decided to indulge his lifelong passion for the car by leaving the National Human Genome Research Institute and launching Ars Technica's automotive coverage. He lives in Washington, DC.

articles.title: Jensen Huang repite la historia de Steve Jobs, Sam Altman y otros CEO: salieron y volvieron a sus empresas
articles.text:
El episodio se suma a una lista de fundadores y directivos tecnológicos que, tras ser apartados de sus empresas, volvieron a ocupar el cargo máximo, como le sucedió a Steve Jobs en Apple, Sam Altman en OpenAI y Larry Page en Google.
Cómo fue la salida y el regreso de Jensen Huang
Todo comenzó el 29 de octubre, cuando The New York Times reveló que Huang mantenía una relación cercana con Alice Huang, empresaria radicada en Singapur vinculada a Megaspeed, firma investigada en Estados Unidos por presuntamente facilitar el envío de chips a empresas chinas. Según The Information, ese vínculo habría permitido el envío de al menos USD 7.500 millones en chips en violación de los controles de exportación.
El 11 de noviembre, el mismo diario reveló un segundo vínculo, con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, lo que hizo caer las acciones 8,6% en operaciones fuera de horario. Al día siguiente, Huang renunció.
Una semana después, el empresario aseguró en X que estaba dispuesto a volver si el directorio lo consideraba conveniente. Más de 190.000 personas firmaron una petición pública por su regreso y el presidente Donald Trump señaló que no le molestaría verlo de vuelta. Hasta que este 23 de noviembre se confirmó su regreso, aunque la investigación continuará su curso.
Otros empresarios que se fueron y volvieron
- Steve Jobs
Tras el lanzamiento de la Macintosh original y la caída de las ventas, Jobs libró una disputa de poder con John Sculley, el ejecutivo de Pepsi que él mismo había reclutado.
La junta respaldó a Sculley, lo despojó de sus funciones operativas y Jobs renunció en 1985 para fundar NeXT y adquirir Pixar. A mediados de los años 90, Apple estaba al borde de la bancarrota bajo Gil Amelio y compró NeXT en 1996 por 429 millones de dólares, lo que trajo a Jobs de regreso como asesor.
En 1997, Amelio fue despedido y Jobs asumió como CEO interino, eliminó el 70% de los productos de la compañía, forjó una tregua con Microsoft y lideró la creación del iMac, el iPod, el iPhone y el iPad.
- Sam Altman
En noviembre de 2023, la junta de OpenAI lo despidió al acusarlo de no haber sido consistentemente sincero en sus comunicaciones, con Ilya Sutskever como figura clave de la decisión por desacuerdos sobre el ritmo de desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial.
Microsoft, principal inversor de la compañía, ofreció contratarlo junto a todo su equipo y más de 700 de los 770 empleados de OpenAI amenazaron con renunciar si la junta no dimitía. Cinco días después de su salida, Altman volvió como CEO con una junta renovada.
- Jack Dorsey
En los primeros años de Twitter, marcados por caídas constantes del servicio, la junta y el cofundador Evan Williams lo acusaron de ausentarse para tomar clases de diseño y yoga. Fue relegado a un rol pasivo en 2008 y Williams tomó el mando, mientras Dorsey fundaba Square.
En 2015, tras el estancamiento de usuarios y la salida de Dick Costolo, Dorsey volvió como CEO interino y luego permanente, logró la primera rentabilidad de la compañía en 2018 y renunció por voluntad propia en 2021.
- Michael Dell
No fue despedido: en 2004 cedió voluntariamente el puesto a Kevin Rollins y asumió la presidencia de la junta. Bajo Rollins, la empresa perdió el liderazgo mundial en PC frente a HP y sufrió escándalos contables. La junta lo destituyó en 2007 y Dell retomó el control, lideró en 2013 la compra de su propia compañía por 24.400 millones de dólares para sacarla de la bolsa y en 2015 orquestó la adquisición de EMC.
- Larry Page
En 2001, inversores de capital de riesgo condicionaron su financiamiento a la contratación de “supervisión adulta” y Page cedió el mando de Google a Eric Schmidt. En 2011 regresó como CEO para unificar líneas de productos y apostar por Android y Chrome, y en 2015 creó Alphabet, dejando a Sundar Pichai al frente de Google hasta su retiro en 2019.
- Sean Rad
En Tinder, tras la demanda de la cofundadora Whitney Wolfe contra Justin Mateen por acoso sexual, la junta consideró en 2014 que Rad manejó mal el escándalo y lo degradó a presidente de producto, contratando a Chris Payne como CEO. Payne duró cinco meses por choques culturales y la junta restituyó a Rad en 2015, aunque en 2016 fue movido a la junta directiva en medio de disputas con Match Group.

articles.title: Montage Technology Showcases Its Full Interconnect Portfolio at the 6th Gen AMD EPYC Processor Technology Summit
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Montage Technology Showcases Its Full Interconnect Portfolio at the 6th Gen AMD EPYC Processor Technology Summit
The 6th Gen AMD EPYC Processor Technology Summit convened on November 19 at the China World Hotel in Beijing. The event spotlighted innovations behind AMD's "Zen 6" architecture and the 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors, with a focus on the performance and application prospects of the AMD EPYC 9006 Series, alongside partner showcases of the latest server platforms and real-world deployments. Montage Technology, a leading provider of interconnect chip solutions, was among the invited partners, presenting its full interconnect portfolio, including memory interface chips and memory module supporting chips, PCIe interconnect chips, CXL Memory eXpander Controller (MXC) chips, and clock chips.
Montage's DDR5 RCD05 chips, MRCD02 and MDB02 chips for Gen 2 MRDIMMs, PCIe 6.x/CXL 3.x Retimer chips, and CXL MXC chips have all successfully completed interoperability testing and validation on the 6th Gen AMD EPYC processor platform. This milestone demonstrates the compatibility of Montage's high-speed interconnect solutions with AMD's latest generation of server processors, offering data center customers a validated portfolio that delivers high performance and reliability.As key interconnect chips for the new server platform, these products will play an important role in boosting memory bandwidth, expanding memory capacity, and enabling high-speed connectivity, helping the AMD EPYC 9006 Series unlock its computing potential for demanding AI and big data workloads.
In addition, Montage's Clock Generators, Server Clock Buffers, and Server Clock Mux Buffers can be directly deployed on the 6th Gen AMD EPYC processor platform, providing low-jitter, highly reliable clock signals for high-speed interconnect systems and further expanding Montage's portfolio for the platform.
During the summit, Montage Technology and AMD's China team held in-depth discussions on product integration, ecosystem development, and localized support. Both sides recognized that interconnect capacities are critical to advancing computing power and agreed to build on the interoperability validation as a new starting point for further collaboration. Going forward, they will continue to deepen cooperation across memory interfaces, PCIe interconnects, CXL memory expansion and pooling, and clocking solutions. Together, they aim to accelerate the adoption of next-generation AI infrastructure in the China market and help customers build a more competitive intelligent computing foundation.

				Montage Technology

articles.title: Public Mobile adds data to Black Friday plans, offers 25% off
articles.text:
Telus flanker brand Public Mobile is upping its Black Friday game after a mediocre initial offering.
The wireless provider boosted some of its plans with more data and is also offering 25 per cent off $30+ plans with a promo code, though your mileage may vary with that one.
First, the plan changes. Here’s what’s new:
- $35/50GB 5G Canada-wide (now includes 1,000 international minutes)
- $35/25GB 5G CAN/US/MEX (previously $35/20GB)
- $40/75GB 5G CAN/US/MEX (previously $40/70GB)
The changes largely make Public’s plans more competitive with Freedom Mobile. The added data makes the $35 and $40 plans slightly better than Freedom’s similarly priced plans, though Freedom’s plans get more data if you buy a phone as well.
Beyond the plan tweaks, Public is also offering a discount code. Spotted by some users over on Reddit, promo code PPTBF25FOR24 gives customers 25 per cent off for 24 months. However, there are a few caveats.
First, the promo code is only available until Nov. 30, 2026. Additionally, it’s only available for plans that cost $30/mo or more. Finally, several people note in the comments on Reddit that the offer only works for new activations, so existing customers are out of luck with this one.
Still, 25 per cent off is a welcome bonus and makes Public’s plans even more compelling. For example, the $35/25GB plan with the promo code would work out to $26.25/mo for 24 months.
You can check out all of the deals on Public’s website.
Source: Public Mobile, Reddit

articles.title: Amsterdam’s Good Heat raises €2 million to replace industrial gas-fired steam boilers with heat batteries
articles.text:
Good Heat, an Amsterdam-based startup that delivers zero-carbon heat as a service to industrial heat users, has raised €2 million to support its growing project pipeline.
The round is led by SET Ventures, Europe’s leading energy VC, with participation from Shell Ventures and existing investor Investible. In October 2025, the company announced €1.83 million ($2 million) in pre-Seed funding backed by Understorey Ventures, Investible, 2100VC, and Foobar VC.
“Industrial heat is an enormous market: a fifth of all the energy the world uses, and almost 90% of it still comes from fossil fuels. The cost of that dependence is obvious at every site we see. We have built a pipeline across two continents, and this financing lets us scale the team to deliver it. Our message to industry: take the heat, leave the project to us,” said Bauke van Gent, Founder and CEO, Good Heat.
Founded in 2025 by Bauke van Gent and Tom Geiser, Good Heat is a developer and platform for clean industrial heat. Batteries that store electricity have helped transform power grids. Good Heat expects heat batteries could play a similarly important role, charging with cheap renewable power and delivering heat when needed.
It argues this could be particularly useful for industries and factories that need significant heat for everything from frying potato chips to producing chemicals. European industry faces crippling gas bills and needs to diversify its energy supply to avoid energy disruptions
The Dutch startup replaces gas-fired steam boilers at industrial sites with heat batteries—advanced thermal energy storage systems powered by electricity. It claims to develop, finance, own, and operate each system, selling steam at a stable price with no upfront investment for the customer.
Since its launch over a year ago, Good Heat reports building a pipeline of more than 100 MWt across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Poland, supported by structured partnerships with leading energy companies that deliver leads each year, alongside Good Heat’s own origination. The same model is already driving multiple site developments.
In Australia, the company is developing Project Arcadia, a 200MWh eTES (electrified thermal energy storage) project for a food company in Victoria. The eTES system will be charged with renewable electricity, converting it to and storing it as high-temperature heat, released on-demand (24/7) as hot steam into the factory. The company says this is the largest electric thermal storage project under development in Australia and expects to reach financial close in 2027. It has an active pipeline of prospective projects totalling more than 75 MWt. It has an office in Sydney.
It also highlighted that the projects are backed by long-term offtake agreements and hedged energy supply agreements, helping provide the predictable, inflation-protected cash flows infrastructure investors seek. A growing portfolio lowers the cost of capital for each new project while supporting technology validation.
It notes that the company is technology-neutral and selects the thermal energy storage technology best suited to each site’s requirements through a competitive procurement process.
“Industrial heat isn’t held back by technology, it’s held back by the complexity of delivering and financing the projects. We’ve seen this play out in wind and solar: once independent developers took over, the market scaled. Our research into industrial process heat pointed to exactly this model, and Bauke and Tom have the track record to build it. Good Heat is our first investment in the sector, and we’re excited to lead this round,” said Anton Arts, Managing Partner at SET Ventures.

Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance with a suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the president posted an AI-generated meme of the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled the famous photo from Trump’s own assassination attempt.
Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affair with Alice Huang may have exposed the company.
Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder may face an uphill battle given the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting with a public Senate appearance scheduled for next week. He is also expected to testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.
If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.

articles.title: ¡Ya es oficial! ‘Ted Lasso’ tendrá temporada 5 en Apple TV
articles.text:
Tan solo unos pocos meses después del final de su temporada 4, Apple ha renovado oficialmente Ted Lasso para una temporada 5. Su exitosa serie regresará una vez más, curiosamente, después de que llegase a su presunto final en la tercera entrega hace unos años. la compañía y los fans pidieron que el proyecto continuase con nuevas historias y, finalmente, el equipo creativo liderado por Jason Sudeikis encontró la forma.
En la cuarta temporada, Ted regresaba a Ritchmond para entrenar al equipo femenino del club. Ahora, con la temporada 5 de Ted Lasso oficialmente en marcha en Apple TV, se espera que el proyecto continúe. En realida,d esta renovación tiene todo el sentido del mundo. Según la base de datos de Nielsen, el estreno de la cuarta temporada acumuló 296,6 millones de minutos de visionado en sus dos primeros días.
Estas cifras convirtieron a la temporada 4 de Ted Lasso en el estreno más visto de la historia de Apple TV. Por encima de cualquiera de las entregas anteriores y de otras series de éxito como Severance o For All Mankind. Ante un triunfo de esta magnitud, a la compañía no le quedaba otra opción que dar luz verde a una temporada más. Y es probable que próximamente también llegue una renovación para la sexta temporada, pues Sudeikis ya sugirió que le interesaba hacer un nuevo arco de tres entregas.
Qué pasará en la temporada de Ted Lasso
La cuarta temporada de la serie dejó algunos frentes abiertos sobre los que Ted Lasso deberá construir a partir de ahora en su temporada 5. Por ejemplo, Ted le dejaba el puesto de entrenadora del equipo femenino a Alice Chilton. A partir de los siguientes episodios, Ted solo será entrenador asistente junto a Beard.
Por otro lado, Roy Kent dejaba de ser el entrenador del equipo masculino al aceptar la oferta de entrenar al Chelsea. Además, Keeley y él esperan un hijo. Y, por su parte, Rebecca por fin se ha comprometido con Matthijs, así que es bastante probable que veamos la boda en la siguiente temporada.

articles.title: Vehicle-to-Grid: Great Idea or Unrealistic Dream?
articles.text:
You’re undoubtedly familiar with the idea of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) automobile energy transfer. It’s been a “hot” topic for the last few years, largely due to the number of pure electric vehicles (EVs) and plug-in hybrid vehicles on the road. In the U.S., these EVs/HEVs account for roughly 8% to 10% of all new cars sold (but they are a much lower fraction of cars on the road, of course); the worldwide numbers are higher depending on the region.
What is V2G? In short, V2G enables the energy stored in car battery packs to become a part of the grid, using some percent of each battery’s energy storage capacity to meet grid-level peak demand (Figure 1).
V2G appears poised for increased adoption by automakers due to the release of a new certification program for V2G technologies based on the recently issued UL 1741 Supplement SC standard. (Note that one variation of V2G is V2H, or vehicle-to-home, but we’re focusing just on V2G here.)
This adjunct standard creates a formal testing and certification pathway for bidirectional electric vehicle supply equipment (BEVSE) under UL 1741, the primary North American safety and performance standard for inverters, converters, charge controllers, and interconnection system equipment (ISE) used in distributed energy resources (DERs), such as solar panels, wind turbines, and home battery-storage systems (Figure 2).
The certification program covers AC-based V2G connections, known as V2G-AC. Under this approach, EVs equipped with certified bidirectional onboard inverters can connect to the electric grid through AC wallboxes. The wallbox oversees the connection between the vehicle, home wiring, and grid rather than relying on an external inverter.
What’s the plan?
Since energy storage is one of the bigger challenges facing efficient and environmentally friendly energy generation and distribution, using cars for transitional storage of any excess energy can minimize the need to build new generating capacity. It can also help create a more resilient grid, in principle.
The premise of V2G is that many car owners usually use only a fraction of their battery capacity, so V2G lets them offer more “use” of their cars as battery energy storage systems (BESS). Vehicle owners who send their unneeded energy back to the grid get some payment.
I’m not going to delve into the operational details of the proposed V2G operation, as that information is widely available. The idea is simple in concept: A car that is connected to a home charger when not in use can either recharge or allow its “excess” stored energy (which is temporarily unneeded) to be transferred back to the grid.
This capability would be especially useful to bolster the grid when its capacity is low compared to demand. In operation, power would flow from the grid to the car or vice versa, depending on the supply/demand balance and energy pricing at that moment.
In engineering and economic terms, everything will be optimized: supply, demand, pricing, costs—you name it. On top of that, it comes with a host of “green” virtues. So, what’s not to like?
The second part explores some issues and concerns associated with V2G.

articles.title: Le Skoda Elroq détrône le Tesla Model Y en Europe, mais le répit sera de courte durée
articles.text:
Le Tesla Model Y domine le marché européen de la voiture électrique depuis le début de l’année, avec 175 862 immatriculations entre janvier et octobre 2026. En octobre, il n’a pourtant fini que quatrième.
Le cabinet Dataforce a publié ses chiffres provisoires, repris ce lundi 23 novembre par Automotive News Europe. Ils placent en tête le Skoda Elroq, le SUV compact électrique de la marque tchèque du groupe Volkswagen, avec 9 384 ventes. Ce score est pourtant en baisse de 18 % par rapport à octobre 2025.
| Rang | Modèle | Immatriculations (octobre 2026) | Variation sur un an | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Skoda Elroq | 9 384 | -18 % | 
| 2 | Renault 5 E-Tech | 8 933 | -4,5 % | 
| 3 | BMW iX1 | 8 359 | +37 % | 
| 4 | Tesla Model Y | 8 309 | +51 % | 
Les chiffres provisoires de Dataforce couvrent 98 % des ventes de l’Union européenne, du Royaume-Uni et de l’AELE (dont la Suisse et la Norvège), et seules ces quatre places sont détaillées. Comme 50 ventes seulement séparent la BMW iX1 du Model Y, l’ordre peut encore changer une fois les chiffres du Portugal et de Chypre ajoutés.
L’Elroq connaît déjà cette première place. En octobre 2025, il avait aussi fini en tête des ventes européennes de voitures électriques. C’était son troisième mois au sommet cette année-là, avec un record mensuel de ventes.
Pourquoi le Model Y décroche en début de trimestre ?
Tesla concentre ses livraisons sur le dernier mois de chaque trimestre, juste avant de publier son bilan mondial. En septembre, 40 971 Model Y ont ainsi été immatriculés en Europe, soit près de 5 fois le score du Model Y en octobre. Le même creux avait déjà permis à l’Elroq de finir premier en juillet. Décembre, qui clôt à la fois le trimestre et l’année, devrait donc logiquement rendre la première place au Model Y.
Le marché, lui, continue de grossir. L’électrique a représenté 31 % des voitures neuves vendues en Europe en octobre, contre 21 % un an plus tôt. Dataforce compte 346 708 voitures électriques immatriculées sur le mois, 57 % de plus qu’en octobre 2025. Premier du classement, l’Elroq n’en représente qu’environ 2,7 %. Sur 10 mois, le Model Y garde 77 136 ventes d’avance sur l’Elroq (98 726). Viennent ensuite le Tesla Model 3 (92 134) et la Renault 5 E-Tech (77 927).
