articles.title: Smartphone in der Prüfung: Mit dieser Methode ließ Südkorea Schummler auffliegen
articles.text:
Smartphone in der Prüfung: Mit dieser Methode ließ Südkorea Schummler auffliegen
In Südkorea ist die landesweite Hochschulaufnahmeprüfung nicht nur im Kalender angehender Student:innen ein wichtiger Termin. Für die sogenannte Suneung, eine achtstündige Abfolge aus mehreren Examen, versetzt die Regierung das Land in den Stillstand, wie die BBC berichtet. Demnach dürfen Bauarbeiter nicht arbeiten und sogar Flugzeuge zumindest zwischenzeitlich nicht abheben. Alles, um die optimalen Voraussetzungen für die Prüflinge zu schaffen. Der Hintergrund ist durchaus ernst. Denn das Ergebnis dieser Prüfungen habe „erheblichen Einfluss auf die Verteilung von Chancen und Ressourcen“, wird Präsident Lee Jae Myung von der BBC zitiert. Sprich: Das Ergebnis kann die späteren Berufschancen beeinflussen.
Entsprechend ist es wichtig, dass es während der Prüfung nicht nur ruhig zugeht, sondern auch fair. Das heißt: keine Smartphones und keine Hilfe von KI‑Assistenzen. Weil Vertrauen gut, Kontrolle aber besser ist, hatten südkoreanische Behörden im Vorfeld Maßnahmen angekündigt, um Schummler auffliegen zu lassen.
111 Prüflinge mit unerlaubten Geräten festgestellt
Und dabei waren sie offenbar erfolgreich. Laut Bericht mit Verweis auf das Bildungsministerium habe man 111 angehende Student:innen mit unerlaubten smarten Geräten erwischt. Fünf seien demnach auf frischer Tat bei der Nutzung smarter Geräte ertappt worden. Mit einer neuen Methode wollten die Behörden Schummler auffliegen lassen. So hatten die Behörden kurzfristig angekündigt, zwischen 8:00 und 15:00 Uhr drei landesweite Notfallalarme auszulösen. Hierzulande kennt man das vielleicht vom bundesweiten Warntag. Smartphones spielen dann einen lauten Warnton ab, egal ob sie auf laut geschaltet sind, oder nicht. Ausnahmen gibt es nur, wenn sie – wie es vermutlich bei der Prüfung vorgesehen ist – abgeschaltet werden.
Zudem mussten die Schüler:innen die Knöpfe an ihren Kleidungsstücken verhüllen, um den Einsatz kleiner Kameras auszuschließen. Die Behörden führten zudem Kontrollen der Brillen durch. Smarte Brillen sind schließlich nicht immer auf den ersten Blick von einer normalen Brille zu unterscheiden.
Den Entschluss zu diesen Maßnahmen fassten die Behörden in Südkorea, nachdem der beste Absolvent der Prüfung zum Steuerberater zugab, bei dem Examen mithilfe einer kleinen Kamera, eines Smartphones und eingesetzter KI‑Tools betrogen zu haben. Solche Gadgets stellen das Bildungsministerium vermehrt vor schwierige Aufgaben. Demnach hätte man zuvor bereits vier Schüler:innen der Mittelschule und Highschool dabei erwischt, wie sie mithilfe von KI-Gadgets bei Prüfungen mogelten.
Der Einsatz von KI zum Schummeln bei Prüfungen erschüttere die Grundordnung der Gesellschaft, „indem er Fairness und Vertrauen untergräbt“, so Präsident Lee.
~~~ Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: GTA 6 : Rockstar a caché un portail secret qui plaira aux fans des vieux GTA
articles.text:
Un portail caché dans GTA 6 qui permet de replonger dans le Vice City de 2002. Et, au bout de la quête, Jason, l’un des deux héros du jeu, repart avec la chemise hawaïenne de Tommy Vercetti et sa moto.
Pour les puristes prêts à retourner chaque mètre carré de Leonida, le studio a dissimulé un véritable voyage dans le temps, pensé comme un hommage à GTA Vice City.
Un portail secret caché derrière un code de triche de 2002 sur GTA 6
On doit la découverte au youtubeur australien Memeio, qui vient de mettre en lumière un easter egg de GTA 6 de grande ampleur La quête cachée commence dans la tour radio Badger R&D, à Key Lento, où un interrupteur affiche le logo du Malibu Club sur une télévision. Il faut ensuite activer, dans l’ordre, douze sous-stations électriques réparties sur la carte, sans voyage rapide ni changement de personnage. Les lettres peintes sur leurs murs forment « LIFEISPASSINGMEBY », le code de triche de GTA Vice City qui accélérait l’horloge du jeu. Un SMS envoie alors le joueur au réacteur 2 de la centrale de Turtle Head, à visiter entre 19 h et 6 h. Oui, le voyage dans le temps se mérite.
Un portail violet y apparaît. En le traversant, Jason quitte les graphismes réalistes de GTA 6 pour les personnages anguleux et les textures d’époque de la PlayStation 2. Il se retrouve dans le célèbre Malibu Club, recréé tel qu’il apparaissait il y a vingt-quatre ans. La nostalgie est là.
Danny Dyer reprend le rôle de Kent Paul
Tommy Vercetti n’apparaît pas en personne : seules sa chemise et sa moto reviennent, en guise de récompenses. Ray Liotta, qui lui prêtait sa voix, est mort en mai 2022. Pour la voix d’époque, Rockstar Games a rappelé l’acteur Danny Dyer, qui reprend le rôle de Kent Paul, l’impresario britannique survolté de Vice City.
Pour tenter l’aventure, il faut avoir atteint le chapitre 3 de l’histoire, qui ouvre toute la carte de Leonida.

articles.title: IG Defence test-fires counter-drone micro-missile system
articles.text:
IG Defence test-fires counter-drone micro-missile system
The company's indigenously developed micro-missile system JWALA MK-I was successfully tested at Pokhran, Rajasthan.
IG Defence has successfully test-fired JWALA MK-I, an indigenously developed micro-missile system designed to counter unmanned aerial threats, at the Pokhran Test Range in Rajasthan.
The announcement was made by Bodhisattwa Sanghapriya, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of IG Defence. “India’s first indigenous Counter-UAS (CUAS) Micro-Missile System, JWALA MK-I, has been successfully test-fired by IG Defence at the Pokhran Test Range, Rajasthan,” he wrote in a LinkedIn post.
Highlighting the importance of developing domestic defence technologies, Sanghapriya said, “The future of warfare will be shaped by nations that innovate, develop and manufacture their own strategic technologies. India must not merely prepare for the future of warfare. India must build the technologies that will define it.”
The development adds a missile-based approach to India’s expanding counter-drone capabilities, an increasingly important area of defence modernisation as the use of unmanned aircraft in military operations grows.
IG Defence describes JWALA as a short-range surface-to-air missile intended for use against unmanned aerial vehicles, with a claimed engagement range of 2-5 km. It represents a hard-kill approach, in which an incoming drone is physically destroyed. Soft-kill systems, by contrast, use techniques such as electronic jamming or signal spoofing to disrupt a drone’s control or navigation signals.
India already has several counter-drone programmes employing different technologies. Bharat Electronics Limited, in collaboration with the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), has developed the D4 Counter Drone System, which combines drone detection and tracking with soft- and hard-kill capabilities, according to the Department of Defence Production.
Private-sector participation is also growing in this space. Adani Defence and DRDO unveiled a vehicle-mounted counter-drone system at Aero India 2025, integrating radar, electronic jamming and a laser-based weapon.
In July 2026, Zen Technologies announced a man-portable anti-drone system designed for high-altitude operations, using radio-frequency detection and jamming.

articles.title: Confirmado: la Justicia determina que utilizar la IA en el trabajo sin permiso de la empresa puede ser motivo de despido disciplinario y se apoya en el Estatuto de los Trabajadores
articles.text:
El uso de inteligencia artificial en el trabajo puede entrar en conflicto con las reglas de la empresa. En el caso de un programador informático, ha supuesto, junto con otros incumplimientos, un despido disciplinario (sentencia del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Castilla y León de 25 de mayo de 2026 que confirma la procedencia del despido).
Para entender la dimensión de la decisión, hay que atender al conjunto de hechos. Aunque se utiliza IA prohibida, la sentencia resalta sobre todo los proyectos para terceros y las compras personales en horario de trabajo. También destaca el incumplimiento sistemático de sus funciones. No se dice qué hubiera pasado si únicamente hubiera incurrido en el uso de IA.
En junio de 2023, la empresa informó a toda la plantilla de que estaba prohibido usar IA. Así estuvo hasta junio de 2025, en el que se permite bajo petición expresa. El trabajador utilizó IA entre enero y mayo de 2025 (en periodo de prohibición).
En España se documentan casos de restricción al uso de ChatGPT por parte de las empresas. Además de esto, en este caso se trata de la utilización del ordenador de la empresa y horas de trabajo para otras actividades.
Motivos que justifican el despido
El informático realizaba proyectos para terceros utilizando los recursos de su empleadora en horario de trabajo. Además de esto, realizaba compras personales. También incumplía las normas de seguridad informática.
En alguna ocasión hubo un retraso y la compañía decidió analizar el histórico del navegador del portátil de la empresa. El empleado alegó que se trataba de una invasión de su intimidad. Sin embargo, el tribunal no aceptó esta pretensión.
El motivo jurídico de despido es el artículo 54.2.d) del Estatuto (incumplimiento de la buena fe contractual/abuso de confianza). Desde la Sala se aprecia la gravedad y continuidad de los incumplimientos. Se desestima el recurso del trabajador y se confirma la decisión de primera instancia.

articles.title: AI Vs. High-Level Synthesis
articles.text:
AI promises to automate chip design from spec to implementation, but can it match HLS in productivity, verification, and quality of results?
Key Takeaways:
- The main advantage provided by HLS is productivity, but those gains diminish if not accompanied by a robust verification methodology.
- AI agents around current HLS tools will allow more exploration and build on existing trust but full AI potential may want to work outside those bounds.
- Producing RTL is the easy part. HLS has to generate RTL that is implementable, that meets power, performance and area constraints, within a defined context. AI struggles with this today.
High-level synthesis (HLS) initially struggled to find a market, but eventually it became a valuable tool for certain kinds of design. It is now threatened by the promise of AI, which some predict will allow engineers to go from specification to finished silicon while avoiding many EDA tools, including HLS.
Most developers of HLS solutions are not troubled by this today, though they do see many changes on the horizon.
HLS has been most valuable for algorithmic accelerators, although that could change. “When I have something that is too slow or power hungry to run on a CPU, I may want to look at custom silicon,” says Stuart Clubb, technical product management director at Siemens EDA. “I might choose to go the path of IP reuse, and that is the most likely answer for a bus interface or peripheral. HLS got shoved off to the new blocks — things that hadn’t been done before and needed some smart architectural hardware design, and solving problems that hadn’t been tackled before.”
The main advantage of HLS is productivity. “HLS handles complex control logic and data path equally well, with 10 to 20 times less code than RTL,” says Badru Agarwala, CEO and co-founder at Rise Design Automation. “Less code is easier to review, so you can trust what you’re shipping, and easier to edit when the specification changes. That is what lets a design scale from a single block to a large subsystem, whether an engineer or an AI writes it.”
Those productivity gains can be significant (see figure 1, below.) “When we talk about HLS, the goal is not to do everything using HLS, or when we attempt LLM to RTL, the goal is not to do everything on LLM to RTL,” said Diptesh Nandi, senior product marketing manager at Microchip. “There will be a certain portion that requires time to market, or faster processing that will not be optimized. If you use HLS, it’s probably going to consume more power because it’s not going to be optimized (compared to hand-crafted RTL). If you take the LLM-to-RTL route — where you focus on time to market and then apply it on the development time, the training time that you require where you’re creating the whole tools flow, or creating the whole design — then you will spend less time developing the whole solution, less time training the whole solution, thereby saving power.”
Fig. 1: An HLS flow for FPGA designs. Source: Microchip
The real challenge is that chip complexity is growing faster than engineering productivity. “Writing RTL was never the biggest bottleneck,” says Rise DA’s Agarwala. “Amdahl’s law applies here. Making one relatively small part of the development process dramatically faster doesn’t help much if the rest of the process remains unchanged. Most of the schedule is spent on verification and the iterations needed to meet performance, power, and area targets.”
This does play into one aspect of HLS, which is that verification time of C code is orders of magnitude faster than RTL. Given that HLS can synthesize designs quickly, and those can be verified at the abstract level, it enables an AI agent to evaluate a lot of alternatives in a small amount of time. This coupling may be the big winner, but we are not there yet.
“Software is leading the pack,” says Tom De Muer, fellow at Keysight EDA. “Digital design is coming next, followed by mixed analog, and then the full physics. High-level synthesis sits at that digital part. It’s lagging software. In addition, we have the problem in the semiconductor world that you cannot prompt something very vague and expect something to come out that’s production-ready.”
To see widespread adoption, it has to solve a real problem. “For 50 years, EDA progress meant climbing abstraction,” says Mehir Arora, head of engineering at ChipAgents. “We built RTL, then HLS, because the human mind cannot hold the full design space. Abstraction narrows the potential design space for an engineer, making it possible for them to reason about it. But it is a loss of potential QoR. HLS was never about better hardware, but a price of designing for human capacity.”
Still, trust must be gained for any new tool or abstraction. “When we talk about AI doing this, there is some resistance from people like us because we have been burnt by things that we didn’t understand,” says Keysight’s De Muer. “For instance, if you have a design that works, that’s great, but it works under the test conditions that you know that you tested it with. But we all had our tape outs that went into production. We had full 100% regression test, but in the field something failed, and then you need to understand how it works to fix it.”
It took a long time before HLS was trusted. “HLS is now providing significant value for a specific segment of designs,” says Dave Kelf, CEO at Breker Verification Systems. “One of the most significant barriers to entry for the technology, and indeed logic synthesis originally, was the disconnect between the abstract model, especially regarding circuit timing, and the final design output. Engineers had trouble making that connection, making them nervous about trusting the results.”
What is stopping AI from doing the synthesis itself? “The rules for the synthesizable subset of C++, and by extension SystemC, have remained relatively constant for probably the last 10 to 15 years,” says Siemens’ Clubb. “In the C+ world, modeling streaming interfaces needed some level of IP to be able to represent that in an untimed sequential language, versus trying to model the explicit concurrency. We created AC channel and bit-accurate data types. A designer, or AI, needs to write out code that understands these. There’s just not a lot of training material.”
Verification
No new abstraction is going to be successful if you don’t have both a development and a verification methodology that work together. The widespread adoption of RTL required both RTL simulation and static timing verification. ESL required C and SystemC simulation and equivalence checking.
“On the verification side for HLS, people have clamored for sequential equivalent checking,” says Clubb. “It is slowly improving, but as with any formal verification challenge, there are limitations, capacity issues, things associated with latency and throughput. There’s still a lot of RTL verification required.”
Building trust takes time. “We already trust synthesis tools to perform complicated transformations without inspecting every gate,” says Agarwala. “That trust comes from verification, not from how the implementation was generated. Coverage-driven verification is equally important. Requirements can be mapped to assertions and functional coverage points, showing which parts of the specification have been exercised and which still need attention. Formal verification adds another level of confidence by checking RTL properties exhaustively within the assumptions of the formal model. The goal is to make verification faster and more complete, not simply generate RTL faster.”
The need to perform simulation on the output slows down performance and adoption. “The issue that arises, especially with analog and RF, is that you need to verify them against a physical oracle, a high-frequency simulator,” says De Muer. “Those take a long time to simulate. An agent typically needs multiple runs, and if that run takes you two or three hours, it naturally limits how much exploration can be done. Comparing it to software, you can produce a program, compile it, test it, and it stands up. In a fraction of a second, you have a data point to learn from. That’s not the case when you’re doing a 200 or 300 gigahertz design. Many runs are required so that models can improve.”
AI’s potential
In a similar manner, the primary advantage that AI can provide is productivity. By finding better architectures through a process of trial and error, it may eventually get to better designs, but that is not the case today. “The next leap in engineering productivity won’t come from doing the same work faster,” says Agarwala. “It will come from fundamentally changing how work gets done. The biggest productivity gains will come from shortening the time between an idea, an implementation, and a verified result. The teams that succeed will be the ones that can explore, measure, and verify the best architectures fastest.”
But that is not going to happen with agents. “Somebody once said that AI is a really good cover band,” says Clubb. “It’s seen the sheet music. It knows all the lyrics, and it will give you a variation on a theme. But for something completely new, maybe not so much. AI is still a way off, and it’s still very reliant on skill files that somebody else has to put together to guide how to do it. There’s not enough volume of training material. Even with these trillions of parameters and all of this input to these frontier models, they’re still not there yet.”
In addition, agents are built around existing tools, which may not be the best idea. “An LLM is much more acceptive for lower-level abstractions,” says ChipAgents’ Arora. “Give it verification and fast feedback and it can skip abstraction layers. Taking CUDA kernel generation as an example, we’ve seen LLMs write CUDA or even lower-level PTX without traditional compiler optimizations, but generate better output. Similar trends are happening in EDA and the IC flow. While humans are well suited to microarchitecture => HLS => RTL => netlist, we already see that LLMs are better at producing RTL directly when equipped with physics surrogates to predict PPA. Indeed, in the future, we may see LLMs directly generate netlists, eliminating another layer of indirection.”
Many people point to a context issue today. “If I say, ‘Design me an inductor for some IC design,’ my agent will do this, but it probably didn’t care about how well it will perform in situ in a bigger context,” says De Muer. “Does it even select the process I’m allowed to use? All of those things are missing. AI is helping to translate those intents. But you still need to be very specific because where the engineering matters, for the semiconductor pieces, all of these things need to be specified. They are not coming out of thin air.”
This is an opportunity to bring more of the context together for some problem domains. “Engineers can develop and verify the design within a TLM-based system simulation environment, alongside processors, memories, and other components, and then synthesize that same description into RTL,” says Agarwala. “This avoids maintaining separate functional models that can gradually diverge from the hardware implementation. Software development and system-level verification can also begin before RTL is available.”
That context is the ultimate shift left as well. “HLS historically, and most RTL designers, have striven to produce RTL that closes timing because if it doesn’t close timing, it’s useless,” says Clubb. “In HLS we do a lot of algorithmic, arithmetic stuff that has cascading wavefronts. When you get to a gate-level netlist, and in order to close timing, it’s not just a nice bunch of fast adders and AND gates or multipliers. There is a benefit to making sure that you don’t put too many operators between registers, because then your glitch power starts to get unmanageable. Even though your area goes down, if you over-pipeline, you’ve got too many registers. That puts your switching power up and puts your clock tree power up. You can do design exploration to hone in on the local saddle for power, or the local saddle for area, or — and this sounds like a prompt — find me the lowest power that doesn’t exceed the smallest area by 5%.”
One of the concerns is design stability. “With AI-generated RTL, changing the pipeline, resource allocation, or memory architecture often means generating a new implementation and verifying it again,” says Agarwala. “Every rewrite creates another opportunity for subtle bugs. HLS takes a different approach. We can keep the functional description unchanged while using synthesis constraints to control pipelining, parallelism, resource sharing, and memory organization. This allows AI to explore hundreds of implementations without regenerating thousands of lines of RTL. Some architectural changes still require modification of the source, but those changes are generally easier to make and verify at a higher level.”
Reality
The big question is exactly how well can AI do this today? “It does really badly, mainly because the type of code that we are handling in HLS does not usually have an easy one-to-one mapping for RTL,” says Clubb. “Once you start the process of scheduling and laying out a data path, you need to understand the process technology and the frequency that you are aiming for. What interfacing do you want? Is this a single-ported memory as an array? Is it a dual-ported memory that has memory bandwidth limitations? Can I split that up? Can I re-architect that? There are things you can do as microarchitectural constraints in HLS because they’re programmatic, but for the interfacing things like stalling, flushing, bubble compression, AI is not good.”
Still, if you have productivity gains, is it good enough? “If you need a small widget and you don’t care too much about performance, you don’t care too much about power consumption, if all of those things are irrelevant to you, AI can produce something reasonable for digital or even analog design,” says De Muer. “But even if we reduce that time to zero, the end-to-end results or gains are pretty modest. We need to look one step further, but that’s a long journey, and it comes from changing the workflows.”
Some of the gains are consumed by additional verification demands. “There was a recent paper out of Harvard talking about how AI-generated code in general is pushing more effort into verification of that code,” says Clubb. “That means the ROI for many companies is becoming questionable.”
For now, AI appears more likely to augment HLS than replace it. While AI can accelerate RTL generation and architectural exploration, producing silicon-ready designs still requires verification, implementation awareness, and careful optimization for power, performance, and area. Whether AI ultimately replaces existing abstraction layers may depend less on its ability to generate code than on its ability to produce predictable, verifiable results.

articles.title: Que vaut le Roborock F25 Pro Turbo sur les taches séchées ?
articles.text:
| Commodité d'emploi |  | 
| Poids | 4.75 kg | 
| Sans fil | Oui | 
| Position parking | Oui | 
| Entretien |  | 
| Capacité collecteur à poussières | 0.7 l | 
| Capacité du réservoir | 740 ml | 
| Réservoir d'eau sale | Oui | 
| Autonomie |  | 
| Batterie amovible | Non | 
| Autonomie annoncée | 60 min | 
Avec ses roues motorisées et un rouleau qui accélère à la demande, le Roborock F25 Pro Turbo promet de ménager le poignet. Nous lui avons confié un bol de céréales renversé, quelques taches séchées et le dessous des meubles.
Avec le F25 Ultra, Roborock comptait sur la vapeur pour décoller les taches. Sur le F25 Pro Turbo, c'est une petite gâchette logée à l'intérieur de la poignée qui s'en charge. Tant qu'on la maintient enfoncée, le nettoyeur envoie davantage d'eau, accélère son rouleau et augmente sa puissance d'aspiration. De quoi insister sur une trace de sauce au milieu de la cuisine, puis reprendre le lavage au rythme habituel dès qu'on relâche l'index.
Pour le reste, on retrouve une bonne partie de ce qui nous avait plu sur les précédents F25. Le réservoir d'eau propre prend place sur la tête de lavage, les roues assistent les mouvements du bras dans les deux sens et l'ensemble peut se coucher à 180 ° pour passer sous un lit. Comptez sur une dépression de 25 000 Pa. Une donnée plutôt abstraite quand il s'agit de savoir ce que deviendront les miettes du petit-déjeuner, exercice auquel nous l'avons bien entendu soumis.
Le F25 Pro Turbo rejoint entre deux utilisations une station qui recharge la batterie, lave le rouleau et le sèche à l'air chaud. Une température de 95 °C est d'ailleurs mise en avant par Roborock pour l’autonettoyage.
À la sortie du carton, il suffit d'emboîter le manche dans le corps du nettoyeur et de brancher la station. Roborock fournit le nécessaire pour entretenir l'appareil, dont un goupillon, un filtre et un petit flacon de détergent.
Le F25 Pro Turbo pèse 4,75 kg à vide. Avec les 740 ml d'eau propre à bord, on dépasse donc les 5,4 kg. Heureusement, le poids ne se fait plus sentir une fois la tête posée au sol. Les deux roues motorisées accompagnent aussi bien la poussée que le mouvement de recul. On ramène le nettoyeur vers soi pour déclencher la marche arrière, sans presque avoir à tirer sur le manche.
Le réservoir d'eau propre se retire en pressant un loquet sur la tête de lavage et se remplit simplement au robinet. À côté du bouchon d'eau, une seconde ouverture accueille le détergent. L'appareil se charge ensuite du dosage. On peut tout à fait laver le sol à l'eau claire, mais si l'on souhaite ajouter du produit, Roborock préconise d'utiliser sa propre solution.
Les commandes tombent bien sous les doigts. Le pouce allume l'appareil et fait défiler les quatre modes, tandis que l'index trouve naturellement la gâchette. En mode Auto, le F25 repère les zones les plus sales et hausse le rythme de lui-même. Les modes Max et Éco permettent de privilégier la puissance ou l'autonomie, tandis que le mode Éponge sert notamment à récupérer un liquide renversé.
Au sommet du corps de l'appareil, l'afficheur rond reste dans le champ de vision pendant le lavage. Un pictogramme indique le mode actif et une jauge donne une idée de la charge restante. Pour connaître le pourcentage précis, il faut consulter l'app. Le F25 signale vocalement qu'il est temps de faire le plein d'eau propre ou de vider l'eau sale.
Entre les pieds de chaises, on peut abaisser progressivement la poignée jusqu'à coucher complètement le nettoyeur. Nous n'avons constaté aucune fuite dans cette position. Avec 12,5 cm de hauteur une fois à plat, il passe sous la plupart des meubles. Une rampe de leds aurait néanmoins été appréciable pour distinguer ce qu'il reste à ramasser dans la pénombre.
À l'inverse, redresser le manche suffit à interrompre le lavage. Le F25 tient debout tout seul, ce qui laisse les deux mains libres pour déplacer un meuble ou un objet gênant. Nous avons toutefois eu une petite surprise en le reprenant : après une pause, parfois de quelques secondes seulement, le rouleau laisse une ligne humide et sale sur le carrelage. Elle s'efface heureusement en repassant dessus.
Si le téléphone peut rester dans la poche pendant le ménage, l'app donne accès à des réglages qui méritent le détour. L'association passe par le scan d'un QR code sur l'appareil, puis une pression simultanée sur deux boutons de la poignée pour le connecter au réseau wifi.
On peut ensuite ajuster la puissance d'aspiration, le débit d'eau ou encore la force de l'assistance des roues. Le dosage du détergent se règle lui aussi avec trois niveaux disponibles et la possibilité de le couper complètement.
L'app offre même une fonctionnalité de télécommande. L'idée peut faire sourire pour un appareil que l'on tient par le manche. Pourtant, elle prend tout son sens pour nettoyer sous un grand lit, là où l'on finit généralement à genoux pour gagner les derniers centimètres. On peut alors guider le F25 à plat depuis l'écran de son smartphone.
C'est au test de l'accident de petit-déjeuner que le F25 Pro Turbo nous a le plus impressionnés. Nous avons déposé devant sa tête un tas de céréales mouillées, assez volumineux pour qu'on s'attende à en pousser au moins une partie devant le rouleau. Un seul trajet vers l'avant a suffi pourtant à tout avaler. Même pas besoin de revenir sur ses pas.
Le long des plinthes, le rouleau travaille également au plus près du bord. Nous n'avons mesuré aucune bande laissée sèche sur le côté.
Sur les taches, tout dépend du menu. Le soda disparaît en un aller-retour. Il en faut deux pour l'huile, autant pour le vin et la trace de carbone. Sur ces salissures, on avance donc assez vite avec le Pro Turbo, sans avoir à multiplier les passages.
Le ketchup séché nous a retenus nettement plus longtemps avec 12 allers-retours pour en venir à bout. Même compte pour l'œuf qui avait passé quelques heures à se déshydrater. Enfin, le rouge à lèvres nous a menés jusqu'à la limite des 20 allers-retours de notre protocole, sans pouvoir l'effacer totalement.
De retour sur sa station, le F25 peut lancer le lavage du rouleau d'une simple pression sur la poignée. On peut aussi programmer l'opération depuis l'application et demander que le séchage s'enchaîne automatiquement. C'est appréciable si l'on range le nettoyeur après chaque utilisation. Le rouleau humide ne reste pas enfermé jusqu'au prochain ménage et l'on peut privilégier le cycle silencieux si la station se trouve à proximité d'une pièce de vie.
Reste à s'occuper de ce que l'appareil a ramassé. Le collecteur d'eau sale de 720 ml se retire par l'avant du corps de l'appareil. Une fois son couvercle soulevé, on accède à la grille qui doit retenir les déchets solides pour les jeter à la poubelle avant de vider l'eau dans l'évier. Lors de notre essai, une partie des céréales est bien restée sur la grille, mêlée aux cheveux et autres débris. Nous avons toutefois retrouvé de beaux morceaux dans l'eau sale. Mieux vaut donc prévoir de filtrer cette dernière avant de la verser dans l'évier.
Le reste de l'entretien pose peu de difficultés. Retirer le réservoir d'eau propre dégage le rouleau, qui sort par le côté en tirant sur sa languette. Le goupillon fourni permet de déloger les résidus avant de rincer le rouleau à l'eau claire. Celui-ci ne passe pas au lave-linge. Le filtre, accessible depuis le couvercle du bac d'eau sale, se rince à l'eau froide. On installe le second exemplaire fourni pour laisser sécher le premier.
En mode standard, nous avons chronométré 30 min de fonctionnement sur batterie. C'est toutefois du côté de l'évier qu'il faudra faire un premier arrêt. Au cours de nos mesures, le bac d'eau sale a atteint sa limite après 25 min, tandis que la réserve d'eau propre a tenu 26 min. Autant profiter du même voyage pour vider l'un et remplir l'autre. Il restera alors quelques minutes de batterie pour terminer la pièce.
Le délai de recharge est de 3 h 30 min. Après avoir épuisé la batterie, mieux vaut donc laisser le F25 sur son socle entre deux séances.
Nous avons relevé 64 dB dans le mode de nettoyage par défaut. Le F25 Pro Turbo se fait donc bien entendre pendant qu'il aspire, davantage que d'autres modèles. Idem, le retour sur la station ne marque pas tout à fait la fin du bruit, notre sonomètre indiquant encore 60 dB pendant l'autonettoyage du rouleau. Le séchage qui suit nous a paru nettement plus discret, en particulier avec le réglage silencieux.
Il est difficile de deviner que le Roborock F25 Pro Turbo dépasse les 5 kg une fois en action. Ses roues motorisées accompagnent le bras dans les deux sens et l'on passe du ras des plinthes au-dessous d'un lit sans forcer sur le manche. La gâchette tombe bien sous l'index pour insister sur une tache. On aurait cependant aimé une grille plus fine dans le bac d'eau sale, ainsi qu'un rouleau qui ne marque pas le carrelage à la moindre pause. Pour les petits accidents du quotidien, on le sortira volontiers, mais il saura aussi rendre de fiers services pour nettoyer des surfaces moyennes.
Le Tineco Floor One S9 Scientist conviendra mieux aux grandes surfaces avec ses 62 min d'autonomie en mode Auto, d'autant qu'il se montre plus discret à l'usage. Le Roborock F25 Ultra intéressera plutôt celles et ceux qui souhaitent laver à la vapeur, tout en conservant les roues motorisées et la possibilité de passer à plat sous les meubles.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Ultra pode ganhar modo de envio seguro
articles.text:
Galaxy S27 Ultra pode ganhar modo de envio seguro
Recurso prepararia a bateria para reparos e lembra função do iPhone 18 Pro Max.
A Samsung estaria desenvolvendo um modo para preparar a bateria dos celulares antes do envio à assistência técnica. Segundo o Android Authority, o Safe Shipping (ou “envio seguro”, em tradução livre) apareceu no código da One UI 9.5 e pode estrear no Galaxy S27 Ultra.
A empresa abriu o beta do sistema em 18 de novembro para a linha S26 em mercados selecionados. O Brasil ficou fora da lista inicial, e o anúncio oficial não menciona a função encontrada.
A ligação com o S27 Ultra passa pelo possível aumento da bateria. Vazamentos indicam 5.534 mAh de capacidade nominal. O modo, quando acionado, fixaria a recarga em 80% e impediria alterações nesse limite.
Ao desativar o recurso, os ajustes anteriores de proteção da bateria seriam restaurados. Os indícios foram encontrados em um Galaxy S26 Ultra, mas a função não pôde ser ativada. A análise sugere que a própria bateria precisa suportar o recurso.
A preparação da bateria teria uma finalidade diferente do Modo de Manutenção, já oferecido pela marca. Nas orientações brasileiras para envio pelos Correios, a Samsung recomenda ativá-lo para restringir o acesso aos dados pessoais enquanto os técnicos testam o dispositivo. A fabricante já orienta fazer backup, retirar o chip e o cartão de memória e desligar o telefone antes de embalá-lo.
O equivalente mais direto é a função Preparar para Enviar, do iPhone 18 Pro Max. Segundo a Apple, a bateria do modelo supera 20 watts-hora (Wh), gerando exigências adicionais de envio em muitos países para dispositivos com bateria de uma única célula (os watts-hora representam energia armazenada, enquanto os miliamperes-hora indicam capacidade de carga).
No iPhone, em envios para reparo, troca ou devolução, o carregamento fica limitado a 80% por 14 dias. A Apple esclarece que o recurso não é necessário em viagens pessoais nem para outros modelos de iPhone.
O S27 Ultra já apareceu em outros relatos sobre mudanças no design e melhorias na Tela de Privacidade. A Samsung ainda não anunciou as especificações do aparelho nem a disponibilidade do novo modo.

articles.title: Nvidia GeForce Hotfix Driver 621.35
articles.text:
GeForce Hotfix Display Driver version 621.35 is based on our latest Game Ready Driver 621.24.
A GeForce driver is an incredibly complex piece of software, We have an army of software engineers constantly adding features and fixing bugs. These changes are checked into the main driver branches, which are eventually run through a massive QA process and released.
Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases. This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver.
The GeForce Hotfix driver is our way to trying to get some of these fixes out to you more quickly. These drivers are basically the same as the previous released version, with a small number of additional targeted fixes. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the Hotfix driver will be taken down.
To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out.
These hotfix drivers represent a lot of additional work by our engineering teams, I hope they provide value for you. We'll try it out and see if people like the idea and want us to continue.

articles.title: Tri-screen portable monitors aren’t for the faint of heart
articles.text:
Living in New York City means making the most of limited space. As a result, I’m always interested in tools that can boost my productivity at a small desk, in a cramped office, or working on the go.
I’ve experimented with dual-screen laptops in multiple form factors and numerous portable monitors, including ones with projection capabilities. I’ve had particularly good results with dual-screen portable monitors.
Naturally, a portable monitor with three full-size screens was the next logical step.
To get a four-screen (including my laptop’s screen) experience, I tested KYY’s X90G ($360 as of this writing). It’s a portable monitor with three 15.6-inch IPS screens. Each screen has 1920×1080 resolution, its own control buttons, and is specced for up to 400 nits of brightness.
The X90G isn’t the only tri-screen monitor available, but it stood out to me because of its design. Some of the X90G’s rivals place the three displays above the laptop screen, which would require you to look away from the laptop screen repeatedly.
Instead, the X90G places one screen on the left and right sides of the laptop screen and one above the laptop display for a more cohesive—but not completely unified—visual workspace.
The X90G also has better compatibility than its rivals by supporting Linux and Android in addition to Windows and macOS (on systems using an M1 processor or better).
Most laptops should fit in the X90G’s designated area, but many workstations and gaming laptops won’t, since it doesn’t support laptops larger than 17.3 inches.
A bevy of bezels
Let’s get something out of the way: If you hate bezels, a triple-portable-monitor isn’t for you.

articles.title: Google Search's AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
articles.text:
Google announced on Monday that it’s expanding Personal Intelligence in Search’s AI Mode with integrations for Google Drive, Google Wallet, and the Gemini app. Personal Intelligence is designed to offer users more personalized, context-aware answers by connecting to their Google apps and drawing on information from their digital lives. The feature can already connect to apps like Gmail, Google Calendar, and Google Photos.
By bringing Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, Google is leveraging the wealth of user data that’s already within its ecosystem. Since users rely on these services, the tech giant can deliver more personalized experiences that rivals aren’t able to match. Of course, not everyone wants AI looking at their Wallet and Drive, so connecting the apps is optional, and you can turn Personal Intelligence on or off at any time.
Google says that connecting Google Wallet to Personal Intelligence lets users track their financial goals, cut everyday spending, and make better use of credit card rewards. The tech giant notes that if users choose to connect their Wallet, AI Mode can only read information from accounts and isn’t able to move or manage their money.
As for Drive, the company says important information related to a project or major decision is often scattered across documents and spreadsheets. By connecting Google Drive to Personal Intelligence, AI can draw on those files to provide more relevant, personalized answers, such as creating a tailored plan for tax season.
Users will also be able to share context between their Gemini app and AI Mode in Search, which means that if they explore an idea in the Gemini app, they won’t have to start over with AI Mode because it will already have the information, and vice versa.
Additionally, Google says users will soon be able to view the context that AI Mode uses via a new “Personalization” icon that will appear below responses.
The company also announced on Monday that users will start to see more personally relevant responses in AI Overviews and AI Mode that will be tailored to users’ recent search context.

articles.title: GTA 6 curiosidades: Arthur Morgan de RDR2 hace una aparición especial con su icónico vestuario
articles.text:
Arthur Morgan no es un personaje dentro de GTA 6, pero Rockstar Games incluyó referencias directas al protagonista de Red Dead Redemption 2 en el mundo abierto de Leonida. La más visible permite conseguir su sombrero de vaquero, una prenda reconocible para los jugadores que siguieron la historia del integrante de la banda de Van der Linde.
El guiño importa porque GTA 6 ocurre en una época contemporánea, más de un siglo después de los sucesos de Red Dead Redemption 2, ambientados en 1899. Por eso, la presencia de Arthur no puede formar parte de la trama principal, aunque sus objetos y referencias permiten conectar ambas franquicias mediante detalles repartidos por el mapa.
El sombrero de Arthur Morgan puede comprarse en Port Gellhorn
El homenaje más directo está en una venta de garaje ubicada al sur de Port Gellhorn. Allí, Jason y Lucía pueden adquirir por 35 dólares un sombrero de cuero desgastado idéntico al que utiliza Arthur Morgan durante buena parte de Red Dead Redemption 2.
La prenda puede equiparse en ambos protagonistas. No cambia las habilidades, los atributos ni el desarrollo de la historia, pero añade una opción estética para quienes quieren recorrer Vice City, los cayos o los pantanos con un elemento procedente del western de Rockstar.
El detalle adquiere sentido por el valor simbólico del sombrero. En Red Dead Redemption 2, Arthur lo lleva durante momentos centrales de su recorrido como forajido y se convirtió en uno de los objetos más asociados con su imagen dentro de la comunidad.
Un chihuahua lleva un muñeco de Arthur en un campo de minigolf
La segunda referencia aparece en Frontier Adventure Golf, un parque temático de estética del Oeste situado en el condado de Leonard. En una de sus zonas, los jugadores pueden encontrar un perro chihuahua con un muñeco de vaquero sobre el lomo.
El diseño del muñeco reproduce el aspecto de Arthur Morgan. Es una referencia menor, pero confirma que Rockstar distribuyó homenajes en lugares alejados de las misiones principales. El parque mezcla decorados de frontera, actividades recreativas y elementos humorísticos, un contexto habitual para los secretos de la saga.
Este tipo de hallazgos invita a recorrer el mapa sin seguir únicamente los objetivos de la campaña. GTA 6 incluye ciudades, carreteras, marinas, zonas industriales, pantanos y espacios turísticos donde pueden aparecer objetos, personajes o referencias ocultas.
Leonida también incluye pistas sobre el universo Red Dead
Los guiños no terminan con el sombrero y el muñeco. En Leonida se encontraron matrículas de vehículos vinculadas con New Austin, uno de los territorios reconocibles de Red Dead Redemption 2.
También hay un libro en Brian’s Marina que relata sucesos y menciona a personajes del juego anterior, entre ellos el pistolero Flaco Hernández. Estos elementos no confirman que ambos mundos compartan una continuidad directa, pero funcionan como homenajes reconocibles para quienes conocen la franquicia western.
Rockstar suele incluir referencias cruzadas entre sus producciones. Los carteles, objetos, programas de radio y nombres de negocios permiten que los jugadores encuentren conexiones sin alterar el argumento central de cada entrega.
En este caso, las alusiones a Red Dead Redemption 2 refuerzan la sensación de que Leonida está construida para ser examinada con atención. El sombrero de Arthur se convierte así en una recompensa para quienes exploran áreas secundarias y revisan los objetos disponibles.
Arthur Morgan sigue siendo uno de los personajes más recordados de Rockstar
Arthur Morgan se ganó un lugar entre los protagonistas más valorados de los videojuegos por su arco de redención. Al inicio de Red Dead Redemption 2, aparece como un ejecutor duro, leal a Dutch van der Linde y acostumbrado a resolver conflictos mediante la violencia.
Su diagnóstico de tuberculosis modifica esa perspectiva. Arthur no elimina su pasado ni se convierte en un personaje sin contradicciones, pero utiliza el tiempo que le queda para proteger a John Marston, Abigail y Jack, además de ayudar a otras personas durante actividades secundarias.
El contraste entre su apariencia de forajido y su mundo interior también explica parte de su impacto. Su diario incluye escritos y dibujos de animales y paisajes, mientras sus interacciones revelan inseguridad, arrepentimiento y humor seco.
La interpretación de Roger Clark, reconocida en The Game Awards 2018, dio peso a esos rasgos mediante voz, captura de movimiento, silencios y cambios de tono. El sistema de Honor permitió además que cada jugador definiera cómo afrontaba la etapa final del personaje.
Aun así, el sombrero, el muñeco y las referencias a New Austin permiten que Arthur Morgan siga presente. Los guiños no cambian la historia de GTA 6, pero reconocen a un personaje que marcó una etapa narrativa para Rockstar Games.

articles.title: Adyen’s co-founder Pieter van der Does to retire as Co-CEO; Ingo Uytdehaage to become sole CEO
articles.text:
Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen, is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO
“After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling. Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades. Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition,” said van der Does, co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
Arnout Schuijff and van der Does launched Adyen in 2006, and the company was formally incorporated on 23 November 2006, when Schuijff visited a notary in Amsterdam to formally establish the company. Van der Does, who was on a sabbatical in Brazil at the time, followed the proceedings remotely over Skype.
Before starting Adyen, the co-founders had previously worked together at payments company Bibit, and their shared ambition became Adyen, which means “doing it again” in Surinamese. In his farewell letter, Van der Does says, “Adyen outgrew our wildest imagination.”
Since its early days in Amsterdam, Adyen has grown into a global FinTech processing more than €1.4 trillion annually. It serves over one billion shoppers per year across more than 29 offices worldwide and counts customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, eBay, and Microsoft.
The company listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in 2018 and has sustained double-digit annual growth since 2007. It has also expanded beyond payments into a broader enterprise financial operating system following the acquisitions of loyal technology firm Talon.One and billing platform Orb.
The leadership transition comes weeks after the company posted robust third-quarter performance results. During Q3 2026, the company reported net revenue of €738.1 million, a 23% year-on-year increase, while processed volume climbed 30% year-on-year to €451.1 billion. The platforms segment stood out during the quarter, with net revenue up 46% year-on-year. Adyen also guided net revenue growth of 21% to 23% on a constant currency basis for the full year.
In a statement, the company confirmed that the CEO transition will not impact its financial objectives and the leadership change had been in the making for over three years through a co-CEO model. “We have been planning this transition for more than three years with the Co-CEO model. It took some time for all the pieces to fall into place, but the moment is now,” Van der Does wrote in his company-wide letter.
As part of the transition, Van der Does will remain available to the company as an advisor, while the Supervisory Board chair Herna Verhagen said the company is ready for its next chapter.
Uytdehaage, who has worked alongside Van der Does for more than 15 years, acknowledged the opportunity to keep building and the responsibility to shape the next stage.
“Pieter built more than a company. He built a culture that shapes how we make decisions, how we treat each other and how we put our merchants first, and it will outlast any one of us,” he added.

articles.title: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
articles.text:
AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  York University
- Summary:
  AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?
"Artificial intelligence systems are often described as 'brain-like' because they can predict activity in parts of the brain that help us recognize objects," says York University Assistant Professor Kohitij Kar, senior author of a new study. "Until now, scientists mostly tested this in one direction. They asked whether AI models can predict brain activity."
A New Test Reveals a Hidden Problem With Brain-Like AI
The York University team decided to approach this question from the opposite direction. Rather than simply measuring how well AI could predict the activity of brain cells, they investigated whether recorded brain activity could also predict what was happening inside the AI models.
If these systems truly operate like the brain, the researchers reasoned, the relationship should work in both directions. To investigate, they developed a method called reverse predictivity testing, which allowed them to evaluate similarities that conventional tests could overlook.
"Ultimately, we need computational models to truly understand the underlying neural mechanisms of how we recognize objects. How do we see objects move? While it's a very easy task that we do every day, computationally, though, it's a very challenging problem," says Kar, the Canada Research Chair in Visual Neuroscience and a member of York's Centre for Vision Research and Centre for Integrative and Applied Neuroscience.
The research team, which included York Postdoctoral Fellow Sabine Muzellec, a trainee with the university's Connected Minds program, examined responses to a wide variety of visual images.
Their tests included 1,320 natural photographs and realistic synthetic images featuring 10 familiar subjects: a bear, an elephant, a face, an apple, a car, a dog, a chair, a plane, a bird, and a zebra. These objects appeared against a variety of natural scenes and indoor or outdoor backgrounds. The researchers also introduced 300 additional images showing the same subjects in different visual styles, including outlines, drawings, simplified representations, and artistic interpretations.
AI Can Predict Brain Activity, but the Reverse Tells a Different Story
The results revealed a significant disconnect between artificial intelligence and biological vision.
AI models were generally successful at predicting the responses of recorded neurons, which are the specialized cells that transmit information throughout the brain. However, when the researchers reversed the process, those same neuronal responses were much less effective at predicting many of the models' internal features.
This difference was particularly revealing because the researchers did not observe the same problem when comparing neuronal activity across different brains.
"The results were striking. While AI models can predict the neurons we recorded in the brain fairly well, the brain cannot equally predict many of the model's internal features. Interestingly, this is not the case when neurons from one brain is compared against ones from another brain," says Kar.
The findings suggest that an AI system can produce results that closely resemble those of the brain while relying on very different internal mechanisms. In other words, matching the brain's responses does not necessarily mean that the underlying processes are the same.
Kar warns that this distinction could become increasingly important as artificial intelligence advances. If researchers continue refining models based only on how accurately they predict neural activity, differences between those models and actual primate brains could accumulate over time.
That would undermine one of the main reasons neuroscientists use these systems in the first place: to develop realistic explanations of how the brain works.
"The findings suggest that today's AI systems solve visual tasks partly using internal strategies that the brain may not use. Importantly, the parts of AI models that align with the brain are also better at predicting real human behavior," says Kar.
Why the Discovery Matters for Neuroscience and Human Behavior
The implications extend well beyond computer vision. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to help researchers design experiments, study human behavior, and investigate neurological and psychological conditions. Many of these applications depend on the assumption that AI models process information in ways that resemble the human brain.
If that assumption is incorrect, researchers could draw misleading conclusions from models that appear accurate on the surface but operate differently underneath.
"Our findings challenge how similar current AI systems really are with the primate brain. We show that models that were previously thought to be brain-like rely on internal components that the brain does not appear to use. We provide a well-vetted diagnostic metric for the field," says Muzellec.
Developing AI systems that more faithfully reproduce brain function could eventually improve research into conditions ranging from post-traumatic stress disorder to autism. For now, however, the newly identified differences highlight the need for caution when using existing models to investigate human behavior or guide clinical research.
The concern may also apply to other areas of neuroscience. Similar artificial intelligence models are already being used to study hearing, language, and movement. If those systems also rely on internal processes that differ from biological ones, researchers may need to reconsider how much they can reveal about the nervous system.
Building AI That More Closely Matches the Human Brain
Rather than suggesting that artificial neural networks should be abandoned, the findings provide a way to make them more useful and scientifically reliable.
By identifying which features of an AI model correspond to real neural activity, researchers can focus on developing systems that more accurately reflect the biological mechanisms behind perception.
"Our approach helps identify which parts of an ANN truly match brain activity, allowing us to build more reliable models for understanding how people see and interpret the world," says Kar. "This is especially important for our autism research program, which builds on models of the neurotypical brain as a baseline."
A neurotypical brain refers to one with patterns of neurological development and functioning generally considered typical. Establishing accurate models of these patterns is important for researchers investigating how perception and information processing may differ in conditions such as autism.
To help other scientists put their findings into practice, the team has released a publicly available testing toolkit that AI developers can use to evaluate their own models and identify opportunities for improvement.
Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, the study introduces a new approach to evaluating artificial intelligence that goes beyond measuring how well a system performs a task. The researchers argue that understanding whether AI reaches its results through processes that genuinely resemble those of the brain is just as important.
The discovery could help guide the development of a new generation of AI models that not only recognize the world with impressive accuracy, but also offer a more faithful picture of how the human brain makes sense of what it sees.

articles.title: Canadian scalper places 40+ Nvidia RTX 5090s on Facebook Marketplace for over $6,600 apiece — ironically still cheaper than Memory Express's 10,000 CAD retail price, purportedly selling every unit quite quickly
articles.text:
Canadian scalper places 40+ Nvidia RTX 5090s on Facebook Marketplace for over $6,600 apiece — ironically still cheaper than Memory Express's 10,000 CAD retail price, purportedly selling every unit quite quickly
Retail pricing situation makes the entire situation quite the tragicomedy.
The lowest rungs of hell may be reserved for politicians, yes, but scalpers have a gated community somewhere in the same area code. The latest emotion-inducing story on this topic comes from Ontario, Canada, wherein a person from Oakville had an ad listing what appear to be over forty RTX 5090s for sale, priced at 9,500 CAD (over $6,600 USD) for the cheapest, and also having the gall to demand an extra 500 CAD (about $350 USD) for one with a sealed box.
The magnanimous magnate wanted to perform the transactions at his nearby police station, and claimed that "testing is available." Some Canadian police stations do open their lobbies for this purpose for added public safety. The scalper said in his ad that he had models from most every manufacturer, including Nvidia's Founders Edition and even Dell.
Should the statements by commenter "goudacheeseguy" be true, the person selling the card is their business partner. The cards purportedly came from their small neocloud outfit and are being sold as they eventually got their hands on Nvidia B300, B200, and Pro 6000 servers "with the money [they] made shorting AI funnily enough." It's possible they're telling the truth, as the presence of the Dell and Nvidia FE cards, plus the fact they're apparently mostly open-box units, would fit with that story.
Nevertheless, the response from commenters was swift and harsh. Some pointed out that the photograph depicting windows of a street-level basement, coupled with the fact that Oakville isn't that huge, could have a master geo-guesser like Rainbolt pinpointed where the scalper was.
In a similar vein, other people remarked on the danger of the seller being followed home for discussing a five-finger discount. His laissez-faire attitude infuriated some commenters, as he stated that "[he has] other models too probably missed some, too lazy to check which ones."
There's some irony in this story, however. It's safe to say that scalpers don't garner the same amount of love as puppies, and yet the 9,500 CAD he was asking for the cards is actually on par with or lower than commercial offerings. A commenter pointed out a Canadian Customs auction of an RTX 5090 that seemingly ended up selling for 8,300 CAD.
As of right now, an RTX 5090 at Memory Express will set you back around 10,000 CAD, and even the cheapest card at Newegg Canada is going for 9,300 CAD, though it's a pretty sweet combo deal (for these times), as you do get a motherboard, a case, and a power supply included in that price.

Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware. He has decades of experience with PC hardware and assorted sundries, alongside a career as a developer. He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“: Was der Job als Fluglotse für Lieferdrohnen mit sich bringt
articles.text:
„Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“: Was der Job als Fluglotse für Lieferdrohnen mit sich bringt
Als Trevor Wischnewsky hörte, dass in seiner Nachbarschaft in Texas Pizza und Sushi per Drohne ausgeliefert sollten, stand sein Entschluss fest. „Das war unglaublich faszinierend“, sagt er. „Ich wollte einfach sofort ein Teil davon sein.“ Und es klappte: Mittlerweile trägt Wischnewsky den Titel RPIC, also „Remote Pilot in Command“ und ist bei der Firma FlyTrex tätig.
Was der Job als Fluglotse für Drohnen mit sich bringt
Ein RPIC ist so etwas wie ein Fluglotse. Doch statt Flugzeuge sind diese Art von Piloten für Flotten von Hexakopter-Drohnen zuständig. Die Drohnen liefern Fracht zu Haushalten und Unternehmen in einem Umkreis von knapp fünf Kilometern. Wischnewsky sorgt nicht nur für den sicheren Transport der FlyTrex-Pakete, sondern stimmt sich auch mit den anderen Anbietern wie Zipline, Amazon und Alphabets Wing ab. Sie alle bevölkern mit wachsenden Schwärmen von Lieferdrohnen den Himmel über Dallas.
Ein kleiner Rückblick auf Wischnewskys Einstieg: Als er sich bei FlyTrex bewarb, absolvierte er gerade eine Ausbildung zum Berufspiloten und Fluglehrer. Er war bereits von der Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) als Drohnenpilot zertifiziert. Das Unternehmen verlangt diese Qualifikation. Außerdem ist ein mehrwöchiger, von der FAA anerkannter Schulungskurs erforderlich. Damit soll sichergestellt werden, dass eine Pilotin oder ein Pilot auch darauf vorbereitet ist, bei Bedarf selbst die Drohne zu steuern. Ansonsten überwacht Wischnewsky aber den Lieferprozess vom FlyTrex-Einsatzzentrum aus mithilfe von Daten aus GPS, Lasern und einer Reihe von Sensoren.
Für Drohnenpiloten gilt es, der Automatisierung zu vertrauen
Angesichts seiner Ausbildung als Berufspilot war es für Wischnewsky anfangs die größte Herausforderung, der Technologie zu vertrauen. „Im Bereich der bemannten Flugzeuge sagt man dir: ‚Vertraue der Automatisierung nicht‘“, sagt er. Der Großraum Dallas-Fort Worth ist jedoch ein Testgelände für das Verkehrsmanagement unbemannter Flugsysteme (UTM) – ein Netzwerk, das es autonomen Drohnen von FlyTrex und seinen Mitbewerbern ermöglicht, ihre Koordinaten in Echtzeit auszutauschen. So sollen Kollisionen auch außerhalb der Sichtweite des Piloten vermieden werden. Sobald Wischnewsky sich vergewissert hat, dass eine Drohne flugbereit ist, ihr Flugweg frei ist und die Wetterbedingungen gut sind, übernimmt UTM den Rest.
Digitalförster
Manager für Weltraumschrott
Hitzemanager
Wettermacher
CO₂-Buchhalter
Spezialist für Klimagerechtigkeit
Job an der weltgrößten Kamera
Wildtier-Ersthelfer
Psilocybin-Pilzzüchter
Fachpersonal für Weltraumerlebnisse
Biorisikoberater
Die Fähigkeit, unter Druck ruhig zu bleiben
Wenn viel Betrieb ist, hat Wischnewsky bis zu zehn Drohnen gleichzeitig im Blick. „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“, sagt er. Aber auch die beste Automatisierung ändert nichts daran, dass bei den Verantwortlichen ein ausgeprägtes Situationsbewusstsein vorhanden sein muss.
Vor allem das Wetter ist eine Gefahr. Wischnewsky erinnert sich an einen besonders stressigen Tag: Eine Drohne war erst seit wenigen Sekunden in der Luft, als der Wind so plötzlich auffrischte, dass er eingreifen musste. Er brachte sie sicher zurück und verhinderte so, dass die beförderte Eistorte auf den Bürgersteig prallte.

articles.title: L’alternative à la clim Midea Portasplit, qui chauffe aussi l’hiver, se trouve pour 500 € de moins pendant le Black Friday
articles.text:
Les climatiseurs se vendent surtout en juillet, quand une canicule fait grimper le thermomètre et que tout le monde cherche le même appareil au même moment. Cet été, le climatiseur le plus convoité de France ne se trouvait pas en rayon. Le Midea Portasplit a gagné l’intérêt des scalpeurs faute de stock chez les marchands — un sort qu’on réserve d’habitude aux consoles et aux cartes graphiques.
Le climatiseur mobile split Trotec PAC-S 3510 SH est à 698,39 € au lieu de 1 199,99 € sur le site de Trotec, avec le code SECRET à saisir dans le panier jusqu’au 1er décembre, sans les frais de livraison. Il est aussi proposé à 749,99 € sur Cdiscount en appliquant le code 10DES99, vendu et expédié par Trotec, avec la livraison offerte.
C’est quoi, ce climatiseur mobile split Trotec PAC-S 3510 SH ?
La plupart des climatiseurs mobiles sont des monoblocs. Le compresseur, la partie bruyante qui produit le froid, reste dans la pièce, et une gaine rejette l’air chaud par la fenêtre. Le PAC-S 3510 SH reprend plutôt le principe d’une climatisation fixe, avec deux blocs, comme le fameux Midea Portasplit, la star de cet été 2026. L’unité intérieure roule sur des roulettes. L’unité extérieure, qui abrite le compresseur, s’accroche à la fenêtre grâce à un support. Il n’y a aucun perçage à prévoir. Trotec annonce un niveau sonore de 51 dB(A) au maximum dans la pièce, soit à peu près le volume d’une conversation calme.
Sa puissance est de 12 000 BTU en mode climatiseur. D’après le fabricant, c’est suffisant pour une pièce d’environ 45 m². Avec une puissance de chauffage de 3 500 W, le Trotec PAC-S 3510 SH peut aussi faire office de chauffage d’appoint pour réchauffer une pièce pendant l’hiver. Son système réversible lui permet de fonctionner même lorsque les températures extérieures descendent jusqu’à -10 °C. Grâce à sa technologie Inverter, il adapte automatiquement sa puissance pour maintenir une température agréable, tandis que son thermostat permet de régler le confort souhaité.
Vous pouvez le piloter de trois façons : le panneau tactile de l’unité intérieure, la télécommande infrarouge fournie ou l’application gratuite Trotec Assistant, en Wi-Fi. Cette dernière permet de lancer le chauffage ou la climatisation avant de rentrer chez vous. Il y a aussi quelques contraintes. L’ensemble pèse 34,5 kg sans emballage. Il vous faut une fenêtre ou un balcon où poser l’unité extérieure, et elle doit rester dehors pendant que l’appareil tourne.
À ce prix, le Trotec PAC-S 3510 SH est-il une bonne affaire ?
Avec le froid qui s’installe, ce climatiseur réversible tombe à point nommé. Son mode chauffage permet de réchauffer une pièce dès les premières baisses de température, sans avoir à investir dans un radiateur supplémentaire ni à entreprendre de travaux. C’est notamment une solution intéressante pour profiter d’un bureau ou d’une chambre bien chauffés tout au long de l’hiver, tout en conservant la possibilité de climatiser la pièce pendant les fortes chaleurs.
Le code promo fait baisser son prix de 460 € par rapport au tarif de référence. Un tarif intéressant pour un split mobile, certes plus cher qu’un climatiseur monobloc classique, mais qui offre davantage de confort au quotidien. Si vous êtes locataire ou que vous ne pouvez pas percer vos murs pour installer une climatisation fixe, c’est une alternative à considérer. D’autant que vous pouvez en profiter dès maintenant, sans attendre le retour des fortes chaleurs et la ruée estivale sur les climatiseurs.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.

Globalement, tous les rayons profitent des remises, mais il ne faut pas pour autant se jeter sur les premiers prix bradés. N’oubliez pas que pour les enseignes, ce moment est aussi l’occasion de déstocker de vieux produits, dont les plus remisés frôlent parfois l’obsolescence.
