articles.title: Cómo instalar XUPER TV en Android o Smart TV: la búsqueda que expone contraseñas y daña dispositivos
articles.text:
Buscar cómo instalar XUPER TV, antes conocida como Magis TV, en un celular Android o un Smart TV puede parecer un atajo para acceder gratis a series, películas y transmisiones deportivas.
El problema aparece cuando la instalación exige descargar archivos desde páginas ajenas a las tiendas oficiales, una práctica que puede exponer datos personales, contraseñas y archivos almacenados en el dispositivo.
ESET analizó el archivo de instalación de Magis TV como ejemplo de los riesgos asociados a este tipo de servicios. La aplicación solicita accesos que exceden las necesidades de una plataforma convencional de streaming y que, en manos maliciosas, pueden afectar al teléfono, al televisor conectado e incluso a la red doméstica.
Por qué es peligroso instalar XUPER TV
Muchas aplicaciones de este tipo no están disponibles en Google Play Store o App Store. Por eso, quienes intentan instalarlas deben buscar archivos de instalación en sitios alternativos, enlaces compartidos en redes sociales, grupos de mensajería o páginas que prometen versiones actualizadas del servicio.
Ese recorrido elimina una de las barreras de seguridad habituales. Las tiendas oficiales aplican controles sobre las aplicaciones que publican, aunque no son infalibles. Fuera de esos entornos, es más difícil conocer quién desarrolló el archivo, si fue modificado o si contiene componentes añadidos para recopilar información.
Qué pasa al descargar una APK desde una página desconocida
El principal riesgo es instalar una APK distinta de la que el usuario cree haber descargado. Un archivo puede incluir programas espía, troyanos u otras herramientas capaces de observar la actividad del dispositivo, obtener datos privados o incorporar publicidad fraudulenta.
Los expertos advierten que estas apps pueden convertirse en una puerta de entrada para malware. En un celular, puede alcanzar fotos, documentos, grabaciones y cuentas vinculadas. En un Smart TV, el impacto puede extenderse a otros aparatos conectados al mismo router, como computadoras, consolas, cámaras o teléfonos.
Por qué los permisos solicitados por una aplicación deben generar alerta
El análisis de Magis TV identificó solicitudes de acceso que no parecen necesarias para reproducir contenidos audiovisuales. Entre ellas, hay funciones que permiten conocer qué otras aplicaciones están activas, revisar archivos guardados, modificar contenidos del almacenamiento y mostrar avisos en pantalla.
Además, puede pedir capacidad para instalar otros paquetes en el dispositivo. Esa autorización abre la posibilidad de que aparezcan supuestas actualizaciones o complementos que, en realidad, instalen software adicional sin que el usuario comprenda su origen.
Cómo puede una app maliciosa comprometer contraseñas y archivos personales
El acceso a documentos, imágenes, videos y audios puede facilitar la extracción de información sensible. Entre esos archivos pueden figurar copias de documentos, conversaciones exportadas, comprobantes bancarios, notas de voz o fotos con datos que permitan suplantar la identidad de una persona.
Asimismo, la información recolectada puede utilizarse para crear campañas de engaño más creíbles. Por ejemplo, una notificación enviada desde la propia aplicación podría imitar un aviso del banco, del servicio de correo o de una plataforma de pagos. El objetivo es inducir al usuario a entregar credenciales, códigos de verificación o datos de tarjetas.
Qué riesgos hay para el Smart TV y la red WiFi de la casa
Un televisor inteligente no es un dispositivo aislado. Comparte conexión con el resto de los aparatos del hogar y, según su configuración, puede tener acceso a cuentas de streaming, perfiles de compra, asistentes de voz o servicios de almacenamiento en la nube.
Si una aplicación maliciosa logra alterar el funcionamiento del dispositivo puede afectar la privacidad de la red. Puede consumir recursos, desplegar anuncios, modificar configuraciones o intentar comunicarse con otros dispositivos conectados.
Para evitar riesgos hay que mantener actualizado el sistema operativo del televisor y evitar archivos de páginas desconocidas.

articles.title: Sauvegardes cassées, missions bloquées... GTA 6 reçoit son premier patch depuis sa sortie sur PS5 et Xbox
articles.text:
Rockstar corrige un défaut d’autosauvegarde et plusieurs causes de plantage sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Sur la console de Sony, le téléchargement arrive par vagues.
Dans GTA 6, certains coups de fil font avancer l’histoire, d’autres donnent accès à une mission. Si le téléphone ne sonne pas, la progression peut s’arrêter là. Rockstar a corrigé ce problème avec la mise à jour du 23 novembre, la première depuis la sortie du titre, jeudi dernier.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Rockstar remet l’autosauvegarde en état
Quand l’autosauvegarde fonctionne mal sur GTA 6, un plantage peut faire perdre les progrès réalisés depuis le dernier enregistrement. Rockstar indique avoir corrigé le défaut de cette sauvegarde automatique et plusieurs causes de plantage. Le patch règle aussi un bogue qui laissait l’indice de recherche bloqué et empêchait de semer la police.
La météo pouvait, elle, rester figée pendant de longues périodes. Le studio a corrigé ce problème et rétabli deux activités qui pouvaient se retrouver bloquées. On peut de nouveau utiliser la barre de soulevé de terre à la salle de sport et récupérer auprès de ses partenaires les sacs destinés aux receleurs.
Sur PS5, le patch arrive en trois vagues
D’après les relevés de Tex2 sur X.com, la mise à jour 01.002.002 pèse 603,8 Mo sur PS5. Sur Xbox Series X|S, elle porte le numéro 1.0.2.2 et demande un téléchargement de 1,6 Go. Avant la sortie du jeu, Sony avait aussi demandé aux joueurs d’installer une mise à jour du logiciel système de la PS5.
Toujours selon Tex2, le déploiement sur PS5 commence auprès d’un tiers des joueurs, puis doit atteindre environ deux tiers après trois heures et l’ensemble des joueurs après six heures.
Rockstar ne précise pas si le patch corrige le bug qui permet de gagner de l’argent plus vite (en rechargeant une sauvegarde, le butin d’un entrepôt peut réapparaître alors que le joueur conserve ce qu’il a déjà emporté) ni celui qui peut faire sauter la limite des 30 images par seconde avec Quick Resume sur Xbox Series X|S, mais aussi accélérer anormalement le jeu. Ce soir, avant de retourner dans Vice City, jetez un œil aux mises à jour de votre console.

articles.title: Building AI in Africa is expensive. Selling it is harder
articles.text:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria and South Africa are more optimistic about artificial intelligence than the global average of 53%, according to a 2025 Google and Ipsos report. But turning that enthusiasm into a viable business is expensive.
Every diagnostic assistant, predictive model, or automated business tool comes with an infrastructure bill. Companies need computing power to train and run models, data to make those models useful in local markets, and specialised engineers to develop and maintain the technology.
Much of the infrastructure is priced in dollars, while these businesses largely operate in markets with significantly lower purchasing power.
A new report by German development agency Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) and research firm Briter Bridges, which mapped 311 AI businesses across Africa and surveyed 85 of them, found that 65% of surveyed businesses identified cloud computing, graphics processing units (GPUs), and AI infrastructure as their largest research and development spending category.
Another 61.1% identified high cloud costs as their biggest infrastructure bottleneck.
African AI companies must pay global prices to develop products for markets where customers are often unwilling or unable to pay global prices.
Between 2016 and 2025, African AI businesses raised $1.3 billion. However, the median funding ticket was just $225,000. This means that although the ecosystem has attracted investment, the typical company is operating with relatively limited capital to fund an expensive technology business.
In March 2026, OpenAI closed a funding round with $122 billion in committed capital at a post-money valuation of $852 billion.
For African founders, the challenge is building technology that can compete in an increasingly AI-driven world without the financial resources available to their global counterparts.
The AI Cost Trap
How much does it actually cost to serve your AI customers?
Model A: API Renting
Model B: In-House AI
The economics of building AI
The International Monetary Fund estimates that AI could increase sub-Saharan Africa’s economic output by as much as 4% over the next decade.
But capturing that opportunity requires more than developing a useful product. AI businesses have different cost structures depending on how they develop their products.
Some build their own models, others use open-source models or third-party application programming interfaces (APIs), while some combine these approaches. Each option comes with different financial implications.
Building an in-house model gives a company greater control over its technology but requires investment in computing infrastructure, data, and specialised engineers. Using an existing model through an API reduces the initial development burden, but introduces recurring charges whenever the business uses the service.
Open-source models can reduce licensing and API expenses, but companies still need computing resources, technical expertise, and data to adapt them to their markets. Open-source does not mean cost-free.
AI Infrastructure Cost Simulator
Should your startup pay for APIs, host open-source, or build proprietary models?
A. Third-Party API
B. Hosted Open-Source
C. Proprietary Build
Consider a hypothetical Nigerian AI startup that develops a customer service assistant for small businesses. It has 500 business customers, each paying $40 monthly for access to the product. That gives the company monthly recurring revenue of $20,000.
Now assume each customer generates 4,000 AI requests monthly. Across its customer base, the startup processes two million requests every month.
If the company relies on a third-party AI provider and pays an illustrative average of 1.5 cents per request, its monthly API bill reaches $30,000. This is already $10,000 more than its entire subscription revenue, before accounting for salaries, marketing, internet connectivity, and other operating expenses.
The company is effectively losing money every time it serves its customers at that price. AI businesses accumulate between $20,000 and $50,000 in monthly API expenses, according to the report.
The AI startup could switch to an open-source model and host it on its own infrastructure. This would change the economics. Instead of paying an API provider for every request, the company would bear the cost of running its own computing infrastructure and maintaining the model.
For illustration, assume hosting and computing cost $12,000 monthly, while specialised engineering salaries cost another $12,000. Add $8,000 in other operating expenses, and the company’s total monthly expenditure becomes $32,000.
It would still lose $12,000 monthly, but its cost structure would be different. More importantly, its computing costs would not necessarily increase at the same rate as customer usage.
At 1,500 customers paying the same $40 monthly subscription, revenue would rise to $60,000. Under the same assumptions, its API expenses could reach $90,000 if usage tripled. By contrast, its in-house infrastructure would need to expand, but its costs might rise to approximately $42,000 monthly, including additional computing capacity and operating expenses.
The company could now generate an operating surplus of $18,000. This calculation shows how difficult it can be for African AI businesses to make their products generate enough revenue to cover the cost of serving customers.
Roughly one in five surveyed African AI businesses are pre-revenue, and about 40% are not yet profitable. Only 15% have reached profitability. The report also found that 60% of profitable companies operate beyond Africa, compared with 40% that operate exclusively on the continent. This suggests that access to international markets, where customers may have greater purchasing power, could improve the economics of building AI businesses.
But finding customers willing and able to pay remains a challenge. About 56% of surveyed businesses charge less than $2,500 annually per customer, equivalent to roughly $208 a month. Meanwhile, 88% target businesses, 62% serve retail consumers, 44% target government, and 43% operate business-to-business-to-consumer models.
Pricing
Subscription pricing is the dominant monetisation model. But businesses serving price-sensitive markets also rely on freemium, grant-supported, and subsidised pricing to encourage adoption. This creates a difficult relationship between what customers can afford and what it costs to serve them.
Can Your Customers Afford AI?
The gap between what African businesses can pay and what AI companies need to charge.
1. The Customer’s Wallet (SME)
2. The AI Startup’s Costs
The problem is particularly pronounced among smaller enterprises, whose average annual turnover is often below $10,000. These businesses must already pay for internet connectivity, fuel for backup generators, and staff salaries before accounting for the infrastructure required to run AI.
For many AI startups trying to solve some of the continent’s deepest problems, the dilemma is how to make the economics work. The customers who stand to benefit most from these solutions are often the least able to pay for them, while the cost of developing, running, and maintaining the technology remains high.
Raising enough capital to sustain these businesses is another challenge. About 30% of surveyed companies are bootstrapped, while a quarter have raised less than $500,000. Just under a quarter have raised between $1 million and $10 million. Only one company has raised between $10 million and $50 million, while fewer than 10% fall within the $500,000 and $1 million funding bracket.
How Long Can Your AI Startup Survive?
Calculate how much runway remains after paying for computing, talent, and operations.
Building an AI product requires computing power, data, and specialised talent. Investment in one area often creates additional costs in another. African AI startups are therefore building with globally priced infrastructure while trying to sell to customers with locally constrained purchasing power.
Whether they build their own models or rent existing ones, they must find a way to cover these costs and remain profitable. But it is still relatively early for many of these businesses. The report puts the median age of surveyed companies at between five and nine years, suggesting that many are still working to find a sustainable business model. Their ability to do so will depend on whether they can grow revenue fast enough to cover the cost of building, running, and maintaining their products.

articles.title: Elijah Wood: el regreso al papel de Frodo tras 27 años
articles.text:
Elijah Wood ha vuelto a calzarse los pies de hobbit de Frodo Bolsón más de dos décadas después de rodar la trilogía de Peter Jackson, en este caso para ‘El Señor de los Anillos: La caza de Gollum’, la nueva película ambientada en la Tierra Media. Y, en unas declaraciones a Deadline que recoge el portal neozelandés Rova, lo ha resumido así: “Fue precioso y surrealista, y parecía que no hubiera pasado el tiempo”.
Un viaje atrás en el tiempo. Según cuenta el actor, volver al plató fue como regresar al pasado, y le bastó con mirar hacia abajo para que el cuerpo recordara lo que ya había vivido: “Ya he visto estos pies así, conozco este vestuario”. Vamos, que tiró de memoria muscular. Y es que, como explica él mismo, la sensación lo transportó de golpe: “Es como si de repente se esfumaran 27 años y estuvieras otra vez ahí dentro”.
Las ganas venían de antes. No es la primera vez que Wood habla de esta película con entusiasmo. En enero de 2026, antes de que empezara la producción, ya le decía a Screen Rant en la Fan Expo de Nueva Orleans que el proyecto era como “volver a reunir a la banda” en lo creativo, con “ese núcleo original del grupo que vuelve a juntarse para contar esta historia, que será como una exploración muy divertida de este personaje al que todos queremos tanto”.
Fin del rodaje. Pero Wood no es el único que ha dado novedades. Andy Serkis, que además de dirigir la película vuelve a interpretar a Gollum, confirmó en noviembre de 2026 en el programa ‘The Morning Mosh Pit’ que el rodaje principal había terminado, según recoge GeekTyrant en su crónica del fin de rodaje.
Caras conocidas y nuevas. La película recupera a varios personajes de la Tierra Media con sus intérpretes de siempre: Ian McKellen vuelve a ser Gandalf, Wood repite como Frodo y Lee Pace hace lo propio con Thranduil. Al reparto se suman además Anya Taylor-Joy, Kate Winslet, Jamie Dornan y Leo Woodall, según el anuncio del inicio del rodaje que recogió Hypebeast.
Una misión contrarreloj. La historia sigue la peligrosa misión de Aragorn para atrapar a Gollum antes de que este le revele a Sauron dónde está el Anillo Único. Se sitúa entre los acontecimientos de ‘El Hobbit’ y los de ‘La Comunidad del Anillo’, y se apoya en buena parte en lo que J. R. R. Tolkien dejó escrito en los apéndices de ‘El Señor de los Anillos’, tal y como explica la guía de GamesRadar sobre la película.
Eso sí, habrá que esperar para verla en pantalla, porque la película tiene previsto su estreno en cines el 17 de diciembre de 2027.

Black Friday 2026 : Le téléviseur LG 65G6 "5 étoiles" à 1 999,00 €
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le téléviseur LG 65G6 associe un contraste parfait à une forte luminosité HDR et un filtre antireflet efficace pour le salon. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : il passe à 1 999,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 6 % et 120,00 € d'économie.
LG fait évoluer sa gamme Oled haut de gamme avec le LG 65G6. Ce téléviseur de 65 pouces affine les acquis de son prédécesseur, le G5, en renforçant son filtre antireflet, sa luminosité et sa partie audio. L'appareil s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le LG 65G6 descend à 1 999,00 € chez Boulanger.com, soit environ 6 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 120,00 €.
Une dalle Oled lumineuse et taillée pour le jeu vidéo
Le LG 65G6 s'appuie sur une dalle 4K affichant un contraste parfait grâce aux pixels auto-émissifs de l'Oled. Lors des mesures réalisées pour notre test complet, notre laboratoire a relevé un pic lumineux de 2340 cd/m², garantissant des reflets spéculaires intenses lors du visionnage de contenus en HDR10 ou Dolby Vision. Le traitement antireflet contient efficacement les éclairages parasites, avec une réflectance mesurée à 17.5 %.
Ce modèle propose également une fiche technique complète pour les joueurs sur console ou PC. Il dispose de quatre entrées HDMI 2.1 capables de gérer des flux jusqu'à 165 Hz, tout en prenant en charge le taux de rafraîchissement variable G-Sync. Le retard à l'affichage mesuré à 9.3 ms évite tout décalage perceptible entre la manette et l'écran.
LG 65G6
Points forts
- Contraste parfait de l’Oled.
- Forte luminosité HDR.
- Antireflet efficace.
- Colorimétrie HDR et qualité d'image remarquable.
- Très bonnes performances en jeu vidéo.
- Quatre ports HDMI 2.1, 165 Hz, G-Sync.
- Consommation très maîtrisée.
- Bon système son.
Points faibles
- Luminosité qui stagne par rapport au G5, hormis sur les petites fenêtres.
- Spatialisation audio encore limitée.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
- Compte LG désormais obligatoire.
Quelques concessions d'ergonomie au quotidien
Malgré ses qualités, le téléviseur impose certaines contraintes d'usage. LG rend désormais obligatoire la création d'un compte utilisateur pour exploiter le système WebOS, et la télécommande fournie fait l'impasse sur le rétroéclairage des touches. La spatialisation du système audio reste perfectible, ce qui orientera les amateurs de grand spectacle sonore vers une barre de son dédiée, même si ce bémol ne gênera pas les personnes visionnant principalement des programmes classiques au quotidien.
Philips 65OLED951 : l'autre option face au LG 65G6
Le Philips 65OLED951 partage la note maximale de 5/5 avec le modèle de LG. Il se distingue par l'intégration de son système lumineux Ambilight et un pic lumineux encore supérieur mesuré à près de 2700 cd/m². En revanche, son interface connectée Titan OS se montre moins fluide et moins fournie en applications que le système WebOS du téléviseur LG.
Le Philips 65OLED951 coûte 9,00 € de moins que le LG 65G6, mais l'écran LG conserve une connectique plus avancée avec ses quatre ports HDMI 2.1 et une expérience logicielle plus complète.
Philips 65OLED951
Points forts
- Contraste quasi parfait et noirs profonds.
- Excellente colorimétrie en SDR comme en HDR.
- Pic lumineux très élevé pour de l’Oled.
- Compatibilité avec tous les formats HDR.
- Très bon TV pour les joueurs.
- Système audio convaincant.
- Ambilight toujours sympathique.
Points faibles
- Titan OS loin d’être parfait.
- Des réglages un peu obscurs.
- Pieds trop bas pour installer une barre de son sans gêne.
- Banding assez visible dans certaines scènes.
- Antireflet en retrait de Samsung et Sony.
- Consommation plus élevée que la moyenne.

articles.title: Microsoft admite: alguns e-mails não foram entregues no apagão do Outlook
articles.text:
Microsoft admite: alguns e-mails não foram entregues no apagão do Outlook
Usuários do Outlook ficaram horas sem acesso ao serviço em razão de uma falha nos sistemas da Microsoft.
Tal como prometido, a Microsoft divulgou um relatório sobre o “apagão” que afetou o Outlook e outros serviços em 12 de novembro. Além de explicar a causa do problema, o documento também revela algumas consequências, entre elas, o fato de que alguns e-mails não foram entregues quando o problema ainda se manifestava.
A razão disso é que, durante a falha, o Exchange Online (do qual o Outlook depende) estava instável a ponto de ter dificuldades tanto para processar o recebimento quanto o envio de mensagens. Isso levou a uma espécie de fila de espera de e-mails a serem entregues.
Em uma tentativa de evitar que os envios falhassem de modo massivo, a Microsoft estendeu o prazo de novas tentativas de entrega de e-mails cujo envio falha de 24 para 48 horas. Funcionou, mas parcialmente, como observa o Neowin.
Os e-mails associados a contas do Microsoft 365 para organizações foram todos entregues, mesmo que com atraso. Já algumas mensagens que tinham como destino endereços de usuários domésticos do Outlook inativos há mais de 30 dias expiraram e, com isso, retornaram ao remetente.
Uma conta de e-mail inativa não está, necessariamente, desativada. Para ser considerada como tal, presumivelmente, ela deve ficar sem acesso após determinado período de tempo (aqui, 30 dias). Isso sugere que o problema das mensagens não entregues não gerou um grande impacto, embora a Microsoft não tenha revelado o número de contas ou de mensagens afetadas.
Apesar disso, o “apagão” foi considerado grave porque também derrubou alguns mecanismos de segurança importantes, a exemplo do Zero-hour Auto Purge (ZAP), que identifica mensagens maliciosas já entregues e tenta removê-las automaticamente das caixas postais.
O Safe Links, que verifica a segurança de endereços em mensagens do Outlook, também falhou, o mesmo ocorrendo com o sistema de gerenciamento de e-mails em quarentena acessado por administradores de TI.
Mas, claro, a principal consequência foi a dificuldade de acesso aos serviços da Microsoft. O próprio Outlook só voltou à normalidade no dia seguinte ao incidente.
Tal como a Microsoft havia adiantado, a causa do problema estava em uma atualização de software nos gateways de rede do Microsoft 365, que são servidores responsáveis por receber e distribuir as conexões dos usuários entre os serviços da empresa.
Para evitar novas interrupções, a companhia revelou uma série de medidas. Por exemplo: a Microsoft planeja redistribuir, até o primeiro trimestre de 2027, as capacidades de gateway de modo que um servidor com sobrecarga não prejudique outros, causando uma reação em cadeia similar à que deu origem ao recente problema.
Os detalhes estão no relatório final da Microsoft.

articles.title: Free supprime le port antenne de son décodeur Player TV Free 4K : attention si vous utilisez la TNT
articles.text:
Depuis 2020, le Player TV Free 4K (l’ancien Player Pop) est le décodeur livré avec les Freebox Pop et Ultra. Free lui prépare un successeur, le Super Player annoncé pour début 2027, mais en attendant, l’opérateur aurait retouché le boîtier actuel. Ce lundi 23 novembre, Tiino-X83, un abonné qui repère souvent les nouveautés de Free avant leur annonce, a publié sur X les photos d’un Player TV Free 4K V2. Au dos du boîtier, la prise antenne a disparu. Ce décodeur ne pourrait donc plus recevoir la TNT, la télévision gratuite captée par l’antenne râteau.
Busyspider, un site consacré à l’actualité de Free, a ajouté à ces images le guide d’installation du nouveau Player et des photos qui comparent les deux versions. À part la prise antenne, les changements sont minces : le boîtier gagne un témoin lumineux, et la télécommande change de forme, avec deux raccourcis en plus, vers HBO Max et YouTube. Elle garde son micro pour la commande vocale avec l’Assistant Google, mais le bouton Free TV n’est plus à côté des touches des plateformes de streaming. Selon Busyspider, des abonnés auraient déjà reçu cette V2 et l’auraient signalé sur X. Pourtant, Free n’a rien annoncé, et nous n’avons pas pu vérifier ces témoignages.
🔥 Black Friday NRJ Mobile : 2 MOIS OFFERTS sur le forfait 100 Go 5G soit 0€/mois pendant 2 mois puis 9,99€/mois ! Appels/SMS/MMS illimités, +25 Go en Europe/DOM et carte SIM à 1€. Le tout 100% sans engagement, foncez en profiter 👇
Free n’a pas non plus mis à jour la fiche de la Freebox Pop, vendue 29,99 euros par mois pendant un an puis 39,99 euros. Parmi les connectiques du Player TV Free 4K, elle liste toujours une « prise antenne TNT DVB-T2 ». Au moment de s’abonner, un nouveau client ne peut donc pas savoir quelle version il recevra.
Sans tuner TNT, toute la télé passe par la box
Sur le modèle actuel, Free explique dans sa page d’assistance qu’il suffit de brancher la prise antenne murale sur le port TNT du Player, puis de lancer une recherche des chaînes depuis l’application Free TV. Ensuite, pour les chaînes trouvées, le boîtier passe par l’antenne plutôt que par la connexion Internet. Surtout, ces chaînes restent disponibles en cas de coupure Internet, puisqu’elles n’empruntent ni la fibre ni l’ADSL.
Avec la V2, toutes les chaînes arriveraient par la connexion Internet. Si la ligne tombe, le Player perd sa solution de secours intégrée. Busyspider précise que la TNT reste possible en branchant l’antenne directement sur le téléviseur. Mais il faut alors changer de source sur la télé et quitter l’interface Free TV.
Une révision du modèle de 2020 plutôt que le Super Player
Busyspider se demande si ce Player V2 est celui dont Free a parlé lors de la Journée des communautés du 2 octobre 2026, le rendez-vous annuel de l’opérateur avec ses abonnés les plus actifs.
Or, lors de cet événement, Nicolas Thomas, directeur général de Free, avait surtout confirmé l’arrivée d’un tout nouveau décodeur début 2027. Ce Super Player est attendu depuis le lancement de la Freebox Ultra, début 2024. La V2, elle, garde le nom et le format du modèle de 2020 : on dirait donc plutôt une simple révision de fabrication.
    Pour aller plus loin
Freebox Ultra, Freebox Pop ou Freebox Révolution Light ? Quelle box internet Free choisir en 2026 ? Notre comparatif
            
Ce qu’il faut vérifier si vous regardez la TNT
Free n’a pas encore communiqué sur cette V2 ni sur les abonnés qui la reçoivent. Si un nouveau Player arrive chez vous, regardez le dos du boîtier avant de ranger le câble antenne. S’il n’y a plus de port TNT, branchez ce câble directement sur le téléviseur : vous garderez ainsi les chaînes gratuites pendant une panne de box. Busyspider conseille aussi de relier le Player au Server Freebox avec un câble Ethernet plutôt qu’en Wi-Fi.

articles.title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
articles.text:
Buying a new computer in the last few years has meant wading through all manner of AI branding nonsense. Most of the AI pitches for laptops are little more than marketing hype, but the launch of Nvidia RTX Spark could bring a meaningful improvement in AI capabilities to the device you use every day. Asus has adopted Nvidia’s new chip in its latest ProArt lineup, offering a staggering amount of memory to run local AI models.
While it doesn’t have a traditional GPU, the Asus ProArt P16, with up to 128GB of memory, can also be your primary gaming and productivity machine, but this unified experience comes at a high price. If you want to run a small army of agents on your laptop, you’re looking at $7,000 for the top-end ProArt P16, and despite being more approachable on Windows, local AI still requires a lot of trial and error.
The PC stuff
Before we dive into the AI agents, let’s talk about the ProArt P16 as a laptop. Nvidia’s pitch is that the RTX Spark can be your one true machine for AI, productivity, and gaming. And it doesn’t skimp on the specs.
| Specs at a glance: Asus ProArt P16 (2026) |  |  | 
|  | Base config | As reviewed | 
| Screen | ASUS Lumina OLED, 16.0-inch, 3K (2880 x 1800) 16:10 touch screen, 120Hz, 1100 nits peak brightness | ASUS Lumina Pro OLED, 16.0-inch 4K (3840 x 2400) 16:10 touch screen, 120Hz, 1600 nits peak brightness | 
| OS | Windows 11 Home | Windows 11 Pro | 
| CPU | Nvidia RTX Spark N1X (5120-core GPU, 18-core CPU) | Nvidia RTX Spark N1X (6144-core GPU, 20-core CPU) (4.00 GHz) | 
| RAM | 64GB LPDDR5x unified memory | 128GB LPDDR5x unified memory | 
| GPU | Blackwell RTX GPU | Blackwell RTX GPU | 
| Storage | 1TB SSD | 2TB SSD | 
| Networking | Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Ports | 3x USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C with support for display / power delivery (data speed up to 40Gbps) 1x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack | 3x USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C with support for display / power delivery (data speed up to 40Gbps) 1x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1x 3.5mm Combo Audio Jack | 
| Size | 13.94 x 9.57 x 0.51 ~ 0.63 inches | 13.94 x 9.57 x 0.51 ~ 0.63 inches | 
| Weight | 3.90 lbs (1.77 kg) | 3.90 lbs (1.77 kg) | 
| MSRP | $4,399.99 | $6,999.99 | 
| Battery and charging | 99.9WHrs, 140W USB-C adapter | 99.9WHrs, 140W USB-C adapter | 
Asus has released numerous ProArt laptops, but this one is notable for including the new Nvidia Spark RTX chip in its most powerful configuration. The Spark N1X has a 20-core Grace CPU, divided between 10 high-performance Arm Cortex-X925 cores and 10 power-efficient Arm Cortex-A725 cores. The performance cluster reaches boost speeds between 4.0 and 4.1 GHz, while the efficiency cores peak at 2.8 GHz. Memory caching on the processor totals 49MB, split between 24MB of shared L3 cache and 25MB of L2 cache.
Graphics and AI are the purview of the Nvidia GB20B Blackwell GPU. It packs 6,144 cores in this configuration across 48 streaming multiprocessors, backed by its own 24MB L2 cache. These 5th-generation Tensor Cores support the full suite of Nvidia technologies, including DLSS, Reflex, ACE, G-Sync, CUDA, and NVFP4. In all, you’re looking at up to 31 TFLOPS of FP32 graphical performance and about 1,000 TOPS of FP4 AI compute.

articles.title: HighPoint Introduces PCIe Gen 5 Accelerator Expansion Solutions for NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
HighPoint Introduces PCIe Gen 5 Accelerator Expansion Solutions for NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs
HighPoint Technologies, Inc., a leader in high-performance PCIe interconnect and storage solutions, has introduced a new line of PCIe Accelerator Expansion (PAE) Solution bundles, designed to enable flexible NVIDIA Blackwell Workstation Edition (BWE) GPU deployment for challenging hardware environments.
By combining full-width PCIe Gen 5 x16 CopprLink connectivity, compact single-slot host adapters, and independent GPU power delivery with a dedicated external cooling system, HighPoint PAE solutions address five critical GPU deployment challenges: physical PCIe clearance, PCIe bandwidth integrity, host power limitations, GPU thermal management, and acoustic requirements.Designed for enterprise IT and AI infrastructure specialists, system integrators, VARs, resellers, and professional workstation users, HighPoint's PAE family offers a flexible hardware-based approach to GPU expansion for on-premises offices, enterprise facilities, and development laboratories.
Injecting High-Performance GPU Capability into Existing Infrastructure
As organizations seek expand on-premises GPU computing capabilities, IT specialists are faced with the following conundrum; existing 1U/2U servers and workstations platforms often lack the physical space, power capacity, or cooling infrastructure needed to accommodate high-performance NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
Overcoming such challenges becomes paramount in office environments and development laboratories, where GPU performance must be balanced with available electrical capacity, thermal thresholds, and operating noise.
HighPoint PAE solutions address these hurdles by enabling compatible multi-slot GPUs to operate externally while maintaining high-bandwidth PCIe connectivity to the host platform. By relocating GPU power delivery and cooling outside the chassis, organizations gain greater flexibility to expand GPU capabilities without extensive modifications to existing server or workstation infrastructure.
HighPoint provides a range of Engineering services, including host compatibility consultation and technical configuration guidance to help customers identify suitable deployment architectures.
HighPoint PAE Solutions: Five Hardware Advantages for On-Premises GPU Deployment
1. Overcomes Physical PCIe Clearance Constraints
HighPoint PAE bundles utilize compact, single-width PCIe host adapters to connect multi-slot GPUs via external accelerator enclosures, enabling deployment in compatible servers and workstations with limited internal clearance. This approach helps preserve adjacent PCIe expansion space for high-speed networking, storage, and other essential devices.
2. Maintains High-Bandwidth PCIe Gen 5 x16 Connectivity
HighPoint's PAE hardware architecture preserves the available PCIe lane width for demanding GPU data-transfer requirements across compatible AI and professional computing environments.
The dedicated PCIe Gen 5 switch adapters, combined with high-bandwidth CopprLink cable connectivity, provide full-width PCIe Gen 5 x16 external GPU connections supporting up to 64 GB/s of theoretical bandwidth, before protocol overhead.
3. Provides Independent GPU Power Delivery
HighPoint PAE external GPU enclosures feature dedicated 1300 W PSUs, enabling supported NVIDIA BWE GPUs to receive power independently of the host server or workstation infrastructure.
For customers in need of dual compute expansion, the RocketStor 8631DD is capable of supporting two independently powered GPU enclosures, reducing dependence on host PSU capacity while offering flexible power distribution for enterprise and laboratory deployments, subject to available facility electrical capacity.
4. Relocates GPU Waste Heat Outside the Host Chassis
The dedicated hardware cooling systems provided by each enclosure moves GPU-generated waste heat outside the server or workstation chassis, significantly reducing the internal host thermal load.
This external cooling architecture is designed to support sustained GPU operation while allowing organizations to manage host and accelerator thermal requirements separately.
5. Address Acoustic Requirements in Offices and Development Labs
Acoustic performance is an important consideration when deploying high-power GPUs in occupied offices, engineering facilities, and AI development laboratories.
HighPoint PAE enclosures incorporate acoustically optimized cooling fans engineered to balance high-efficiency GPU thermal management without introducing excessive noise into the working environment. Under HighPoint's specified full-load test configuration, RocketStor RS8631D enclosures measure 65.9 dBA at one meter, providing a documented acoustic reference for on-premises deployment planning.
Three PAE Solution Bundles for Flexible GPU Expansion
RocketStor RS8631DW—External Single-GPU Expansion
The RocketStor 8631DW combines a PCIe Gen 5 x16 host adapter, RocketStor RS8631D GPU enclosure, and CopprLink connectivity to enable external deployment of a single compatible multi-slot GPU; ideal for servers and workstations faced with physical clearance, host power, or cooling limitations.RocketStor RS8631DH—GPU Expansion with Internal NVMe Connectivity
The RocketStor 8631DH combines a dedicated external PCIe Gen 5 x16 GPU connection with internal NVMe connectivity through a PCIe switch-based host adapter. The architecture supports hardware-level peer-to-peer data paths between compatible GPU and NVMe devices, providing an expansion foundation for GPU-intensive workflows and internal storage resources via industry standard UBM backplanes.RocketStor RS8631DD—Dual-GPU Expansion Ready
The RocketStor 8631DD features a Broadcom 48-lane PCIe Gen 5 switch-based host adapter with two dedicated external Gen 5 x16 CopprLink connections, supporting dual-GPU expansion and switch-level peer-to-peer pathways for compatible systems.The standard RocketStor 8631DD bundle includes one RocketStor 8631D enclosure; a second enclosure is available separately for dual-GPU deployment.
Designed for Enterprise AI Infrastructure and Professional Workflows
HighPoint PAE solutions provide flexible hardware-level expansion capability for a broad range of compatible GPU-accelerated workflows, including AI development, engineering simulation, professional visualization, and data-intensive computing.
By addressing physical installation, high-bandwidth PCIe connectivity, power delivery, thermal management, and acoustic requirements, in a single unified package, PAE Bundle Solutions help organizations integrate NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs into existing on-premises server and workstation environments while avoiding costly and complicated infrastructure upgrades.
May Hwang, Marketing Director at HighPoint Technologies"As organizations bring high-performance GPU computing into enterprise offices, engineering facilities, and AI development laboratories, successful deployment requires more than GPU performance alone. HighPoint PAE solutions address the physical, power, cooling, connectivity, and acoustic challenges that can limit GPU deployment, helping customers expand their existing infrastructure with greater flexibility and confidence."
Availability and Enterprise Evaluation Programs
HighPoint RocketStor 8631DW, 8631DH, and 8631DD PAE Solution Bundles are offered through HighPoint and its authorized sales channels, subject to regional availability and product configuration.
Enterprise IT teams, AI infrastructure providers, system integrators, resellers, and professional workstation users can contact HighPoint to request a complimentary Server & GPU Compatibility Review and inquire about available technical evaluation opportunities.

articles.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Expose Trailers to Forced Braking
articles.text:
Vulnerabilities discovered in Bluetooth-enabled brake controllers made by Australian firm Elecbrakes could allow hackers to manipulate trailer brakes, potentially causing accidents, researchers warned.
The affected products include the EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000 brake controllers from Elecbrakes. According to the cybersecurity agency CISA, which last week published an advisory on the vulnerabilities, the affected brake controllers are mainly used in Australia and New Zealand.
The controllers regulate the braking force applied to trailers, with the EB2 unit mounted on the trailer and the VM1 unit on the towing vehicle. The devices can be controlled remotely via a special remote or a smartphone app.
Researchers from Australian IT and cybersecurity consultancy Element Digital — with help from AI — discovered three vulnerabilities in the braking controllers, including two critical missing authentication and insufficient replay-attack protection issues.
They demonstrated that an unauthenticated attacker who is within Bluetooth range of the targeted vehicle (up to 100 meters or 328 feet) can use a laptop or phone to engage or release a trailer’s brakes or adjust the braking force, without any interaction required from the victim.
“Your trailer’s brakes slamming to maximum while your tow vehicle keeps going is the exact recipe for a jackknife – one of the more reliably fatal things a vehicle combination can do,” the researchers warned.
The third vulnerability is a medium-severity issue related to the firmware update mechanism. Unauthorized firmware changes could enable persistent compromise of the controller, allowing an attacker to interfere with braking, brake lights, and other safety functions. However, the researchers noted that this risk is theoretical, as they did not demonstrate the full impact or attempt to install malicious firmware during their tests.
Elecbrakes was notified about the findings in mid-May and released firmware updates with patches in early July for its EB2 and VM1 products. Element Digital disclosed technical details last week.
Once the firmware patches are installed, an attacker can no longer access the brake controllers remotely without an initial pairing that requires physical access to the device and cannot be performed over Bluetooth.
The vendor is still working on a remediation plan for the older ELBC 2000 product. In a customer advisory published on Monday, Elecbrakes advised owners of the older ELBC controllers to maintain an active connection between the controller and their smartphone or wireless remote whenever the device is in use.
Elecbrakes told iTnews that nearly 40,000 app users had initially been alerted to the availability of the update, and that it had been installed on 60-70% of controllers used to connect to the system daily.
There is no evidence of malicious exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
While the researchers praised Elecbrakes for quickly developing patches, they criticized the company over the lengthy disclosure process and its failure to initially identify the older ELBC 2000 as being affected.

articles.title: Jensen Huang scheduled to testify next week in Senate following reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
articles.text:
Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website.
The development comes just hours after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, less than two weeks following his resignation after it was revealed that he engaged in at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by the U.S. government of working as a Chinese spy.
The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries.
The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.
It’s worth noting that before his reinstatement as CEO, Huang had already agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1.

articles.title: Google teme que los agentes de IA se descontrolen y planea restringirlos en Chrome
articles.text:
Google quiere limitar el poder de los agentes de IA dentro de Chrome. La compañía propone un sistema de permisos a nivel de navegador para controlar qué webs pueden visitar y qué acciones pueden realizar. La iniciativa surge tras la oleada de incidentes en donde los agentes se han saltado las barreras de seguridad y terminan hackeando páginas o accediendo a contenido para el que no estaban autorizados.
De acuerdo con Neowin, Google ha planeado un sistema que limitaría el alcance de los agentes autónomos. Ingenieros de la empresa propusieron cambios en WebDriver BiDi, el protocolo utilizado para automatización y pruebas en navegadores. En una publicación en el grupo de Chromium, los empleados anunciaron una intención para prototipar la idea y regresarle el control a los usuarios.
En la versión actual del protocolo, WebDriver BiDi asume una relación de confianza total entre el cliente y el navegador, lo que permite un control prácticamente ilimitado. Si bien esto funciona para pruebas automatizadas, resulta peligroso para agentes de IA que navegan en la web. Muchos agentes usan protocolos de bajo nivel o configuraciones que les dan acceso sin restricciones y sin supervisión del usuario.
La idea de Google es añadir extensiones para WebDriver BiDi que se aplicarán a la IA. En los casos donde un agente autónomo navegue, el sistema añadirá un nuevo tipo de sesión restringida. En esta, la IA comienza sin permisos más allá de los valores predeterminados, por lo que debe solicitar explícitamente el acceso a los recursos y capacidades.
La propuesta utiliza un sistema de permisos basado en ACL (lista de control de acceso), que define las webs que puede visitar el agente, los comandos permitidos y los eventos a recibir. Estos permisos se pueden aplicar de forma global a ciertas pestañas o navegaciones específicas.
Google Chrome limitará a los agentes de IA a través de permisos
Google señala que el uso de extensiones permite conservar el control en todo momento. Cuando se aplican, el usuario puede pausar al agente, revocar permisos o detener la sesión. Chrome puede mostrar una interfaz especial cuando el agente realice acciones activas como hacer clic, navegar, escribir texto o ejecutar scripts, de modo que el usuario sepa cuáles son las pestañas controladas por la IA en caso de que se necesite limitarlas o apagarlas.
Bajo la propuesta de Google, los usuarios de Chrome también podrían otorgar permisos muy concretos. Si necesitas que el agente acceda a una tienda en línea, pero no revise páginas de pagos externas, puedes bloquearlo.
Hasta ahora todo suena muy bien, pero existen algunas limitaciones. Por ejemplo, si le autorizas a un agente a hacer clic en botones, Chrome no puede distinguir entre un botón seguro y otro que elimine información importante. Por ello, los ingenieros tienen que seguir experimentando hasta llegar a un nivel confiable que pueda adoptarse por otros navegadores.
Por el momento, esta propuesta se encuentra en una etapa muy preliminar de desarrollo y no se sabe cuándo se implementará en Chrome.

articles.title: Anthropic researcher tunes chess software to turn a 200 MHz Pentium Pro into a behemoth that would handily defeat Kasparov and Carlsen — 1995 PC with 64 MB of RAM would crush Kasparov 9 times out of 10
articles.text:
Anthropic researcher tunes chess software to turn a 200 MHz Pentium Pro into a behemoth that would handily defeat Kasparov and Carlsen — 1995 PC with 64 MB of RAM would crush Kasparov 9 times out of 10
A mere 200 MHz chip with hyper-optimized software is enough to destroy all humans.
Readers with back pain probably recall the much-discussed 1996 chess challenge, wherein the world champion Gerry Kasparov faced off against IBM's Deep Blue chess-optimized computer. The nascent clanker lost the match with a 4-2 total, but still stunned the world by being the first piece of electric sand to win a single game against a grandmaster. Modern chess engines will utterly destroy any human, but Anthropic engineer Nicholas Carlini wondered if granting old hardware new bytes would give the machine a better chance. Spoiler: yes, indeed it would.
To understand the task, here's a quick primer on chess scoreboards. A player is rated worldwide with an Elo system (first devised for chess), wherein they lose or gain points in proportion to the difference to their opponent's rating — meaning that winning a match against Magnus Carlsen would net you a lot of points versus defeating me, who only learned about the en passant rule a handful of years ago.
At his prime, Kasparov ranked about 2800 points. Given that Deep Blue eventually barely won against him in a subsequent rematch, that is a good starting point for any. Contemporary chess engines like Stockfish have an estimated Elo of about 3,300, far higher than any human — guaranteeing it'll win most matches against a human.
Nicholas Carlini got hold of a 1995-era machine, packing a Pentium Pro CPU with all of its 200 MHz of clock speed, and 64 MB of RAM. For his first experiment, he grabbed Crafty, a 1996 chess engine, and measured how well it would do. It came in at 2,000 Elo with 1 second allotted, and 2,400 @ 10s. Running that software on a Ryzen 7 resulted in a 2,600 rating — good, but not enough.
Since Crafty's source code is available, he got Claude to mod it with modern features, and eventually reached a ceiling of 3,000 Elo @ 10s per move. That's quite an impressive feat already, especially considering that the lone Pentium Pro represented but a small fraction of the hardware that Deep Blue had. An Elo delta of +200 means this iteration would defeat Kasparov three out of every four games, while a +400 delta means a victory nine out of ten times.
Carlini then pulled out the big gun: Stockfish. He had to ask Claude to modify it to use only 32-bit arithmetic instead of 64-bit, and limit its workspace to the measly 64 MB of RAM, minus whatever the system harness took. Right off the bat, the figures were revealing: 2,500 @ 1s, and 3000 @ 10s.
The engineer performed a few optimization passes, and eventually got 2,850 @ 1s; 3,100 @ 10s; and almost 3,200 @ 30s — enough to put every human in their place, especially in a grandmaster tournament setting where there's no fixed time per move. You can play the bot using the link on the respective blog post. We'd wish you the best of luck, but there's no such concept in chess.

articles.title: Nigeria’s OnIt brings structure, trust to Africa’s informal service economy
articles.text:
Nigerian startup OnIt Innovations is building trust and access within Africa’s informal service economy, making it easier for households and businesses to access reliable everyday services while creating more structured earning opportunities for informal service professionals.
Launched in Lagos in May 2024, OnIt offers customers services including laundry, home cleaning, technical and repair services, procurement, grocery shopping and errands. Behind these services is a workforce infrastructure, with the startup recruiting, training, assessing and verifying “service associates” before deployment, then managing service delivery through defined operating standards, customer support and performance monitoring.
“OnIt started from a very practical problem I encountered while working as a practice manager in Lagos. Managing a demanding career alongside family responsibilities made reliable household support extremely important. I began to see that the problem was much bigger than simply finding someone who could perform a task. The real challenge was trust, quality, accountability and consistency,” founder and CEO Dorcas Obeahon told Disrupt Africa.
She said customers typically rely on referrals, social media or unverified workers, while capable service professionals often lack formal training, verified work records and predictable demand.
“There are several companies operating within individual parts of the service economy. Our approach is broader because we are building the underlying service and workforce infrastructure rather than simply providing a directory where customers find workers,” Obeahon said.
The startup has largely grown through founder capital, internally generated revenue and grants, and has been supported by programmes including the Women in Tech accelerator by Standard Chartered Bank and Village Capital, and Orange Corners Nigeria. Its workforce training arm, BlueVarsity, has trained more than 3,000 people, and OnIt now has a pool of more than 500 verified service associates, who have earned over N40 million (US$30,000) through the platform.
OnIt has completed more than 7,000 service orders for over 500 customers, and has generated more than NGN100 million (US$75,000) in cumulative revenue, earned primarily through margins and commissions on services. It also offers recurring household service plans, B2B contracts and workforce training, and is developing employee-benefit products for organisations.
“Customers who experience reliable service tend to use OnIt across different needs. A customer may initially come to us for laundry, and later use OnIt for cleaning, repairs, procurement or errands,” said Obeahon.
OnIt is focused on deepening its model in Lagos before expanding to other major Nigerian cities, and eventually to selected African urban markets. Standardisation has been the biggest challenge.
“We learned quite early that verification alone was not enough. We needed training, operating procedures, quality assurance, performance tracking and accountability after deployment,” Obeahon said.

articles.title: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- A drafting agent should refuse to draft when the evidence is missing. Stopping with an explicit "insufficient context" signal is safer than a fluent narrative built around gaps.
- An LLM judge is itself non-deterministic. Freeze its version and pair it with a deterministic fact-checker for names, dates, and amounts.
- Building agentic systems on probabilistic LLMs requires engineering around them: evals, context engineering, observability, regression runs, and human-in-the-loop controls contain the effects of randomness rather than removing it.
- Grounding the system in authoritative case evidence and a knowledge-augmented graph data system helps ensure that every material claim is supported by traceable data.
- Versioned models, prompts, policies, retrieval configurations, and reviewer actions make the system observable, reversible, and suitable for regulated production environments.
Investigative narrative drafting in a financial institution
Financial institutions must investigate potentially suspicious activity and prepare accurate, complete, and timely reports for Financial Intelligence Units. The process is sensitive, labor-intensive, and subject to strict deadlines. This article explains how non-deterministic Artificial Intelligence (AI) components can be incorporated into a dependable agentic system that reduces the cost of doing business, increases drafting and review speed, and maintains the quality of the final report.
What is a Suspicious Activity Report?
A Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) is a formal document submitted by regulated entities and financial institutions to law enforcement or financial intelligence units (such as the UK's National Crime Agency) to flag known or suspected instances of money laundering, fraud, or terrorist financing.
SARs should give a clear and concise explanation of the reason(s) for the suspicion, identifying:
- Who – the identity of the party, or parties involved
- What – the transaction they are involved in
- Where – a description of the criminal property
- How – a description of the prohibited act(s)
- Why – the criminal activity suspected
- When – any critical deadlines
The Inverted Pyramid Plot Model for SAR narratives organizes information from most to least important, much like a news article.
- The narrative opens with the lead, a short summary of the most noteworthy details and the main story event.
- It answers the five W questions: who, what, when, where, and why.
- Next comes the body, a series of crucial details that build up the main story event, supported by evidence, facts, and patterns.
- The narrative closes with the tail, which gives concluding remarks.
Because the structure moves from the broadest, most critical information down to the narrowest, a reader can grasp the core of the case from the opening lines alone and turn to the later sections only for supporting detail.
Risks and cost of non-compliance
- Regulators penalize institutions for systematic data deficiencies, missing narratives, or failing to report suspicious transactions adequately.
- Public enforcement actions can undermine the confidence of investors, business partners, and customers.
- Considering the sensitivity of data and investigations, typically these cases are investigated and reported by in-house employees in a very secure environment. If suspicious activity volumes increase, the cost of investigation and reporting increases as well. For example, If there are 10% of active customers who are detected, investigated, and reported, and each case takes $50 in human labour cost, there is a significant increase in the cost of doing business, which has to be eventually passed back to the customer.
Typical Deterministic System Architecture
In the following system context diagram, a human agent views the investigation notes prepared by another human agent and then drafts the suspicious activity report. Once the report is reviewed by another peer, it is submitted to a financial intelligence unit.
System Context Diagram of Suspicious Activity Reports in a Financial Institution (Source: authors)
In the following diagram, there are 4 key timelines of any investigation:
- Detection: Any suspicious activity is detected either through manual oversight or with the support of machine learning models.
- Investigation: Once suspicious activity is detected, it goes for thorough investigation and peer review to confirm the suspicion.
- Reporting: Any confirmed suspicious activity has to be reported to the national financial intelligence unit within a tight deadline. The report has to be factually correct, and the suspicion has to be clearly articulated.
- Further investigation by the Financial Intelligence Unit: All of these suspicious reported activities by all financial institutions enable the national intelligence unit to understand the complete web of illicit activities and intervene before they become a threat to national or international security.
High-level diagram of a traditional reporting system (Source: authors)
- The quality of the reports is directly proportional to the quality of investigation & editorial style of the human workforce. There is a lack of consistency.
- If there is an increase in suspicious activities, then the manual system can not keep pace with the increase in demand.
- There is a cost to the business and the customer for every suspicious activity investigation and reporting.
Non-Deterministic Agentic System Architecture
We propose improving the traditional reporting system by using AI to automate selected tasks and generate high-quality SAR drafts, followed by specialized human review and minor edits where necessary. The goal is to increase throughput, reduce cost per case, and decrease reporting failures.
In the following system context diagram, human agent effort is shifted to review/edit the AI-assisted report drafting and review.
System Context Diagram of Suspicious Activity Reports in a Financial Institution (Source: authors)
We changed the earlier design to support background automation of suspicious activity report generation. As soon as the investigation is complete, the case is sent to the queue for processing by the Agentic System. Before the human agent picks the case for drafting the report, the AI Agent has drafted the first version to speed up the report generation.
High-level diagram of an AI-powered reporting system (Source: authors)
The non-deterministic nature of AI, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), creates two central concerns:
- High-quality first-attempt drafts require strong control, evaluation, and monitoring of AI components.
- Low-quality drafts create repeated draft-and-review cycles and additional human editing, increasing the cost per report.
Multi-agent system for report generation
The proposed solution is a multi-agent system, with access to selected LLMs via a gateway, and supported by a tailored knowledge graph built from operational data.
Grounding is the foundation of trustworthy SAR generation. The system should make it easier to state only what the evidence supports, not merely make the prose more fluent.
High-level diagram of the agentic system (Source: authors)
- Preprocessed Event Plot Knowledge Graph: All the data is already tagged and collected by previous processes. There is an Event Plot Knowledge Graph already generated as part of detection and investigation.
- Data Query Planner Agent: fetches the quality data required to generate the report. If the data is not present, then we stop the agentic automation and give feedback to the user that Agents cannot generate the report as the data is not present.
- Data Reranker Agent: takes the data returned by Data Query Planner and re-ranks the data to ensure that data is relevant to the context.
- Drafter Agent: specialized agents produce a narrative from factual data, against a defined SAR schema, and cite supporting source identifiers.
- Judge Agent: deterministic checks and an independent judge assess factuality, completeness, consistency, and style.
- Coordinator Agent: Once the quality of the generated report is of decent standard, then the report is published for human review.
- Since the investigation of the network is already done, there is no need for community detection. Hence, the GraphRAG approach is not considered.
- We also need to ensure that security and privacy concerns of the cases are under consideration; hence, data is carefully labelled and collected.
- All the real-time updates are present in operational databases, which can be fetched by the agents if there are some updates for a particular user profile or transaction.
- Knowledge Graph of main and associate suspects are generated at a regular cadence through data pipeline jobs.
- If a case is investigated and reported, then data needs to be retained as per data retention policies of the jurisdiction.
Sequence diagram of Drafter agent, Judge Agent and Human (Source: authors)
High-quality report generation with Evals
Quality means more than well-written prose. It means a complete, internally consistent, reviewable narrative that meets institutional and jurisdictional requirements.
- Completeness against the required SAR narrative fields.
- Consistency across names, dates, amounts, accounts, locations, and transaction sequences.
- Clear separation of observed facts, analysis, and unresolved uncertainty.
- Appropriate tone and terminology without overstatement or unsupported conclusions.
- Traceable provenance for material statements and reviewer edits.
Unlike traditional software, LLM outputs are non-deterministic, and "quality" is subjective. In the case of report writing, "what does a good report look like?" becomes more subjective. Hence, there is a need to test the "subjective" aspects against "objective" metrics, and here the Eval shines.
Evals are like tests of regular software development practices, and they can be leveraged in the following processes:
- Initial development of the system
- Updates to the system when there is a change in the requirements
- Updates in the models
- Regular run on some percentage of production spans to assess overall drift in quality
- Any new release in any aspect of the AI system has to be gated with the Evals suite
Eval Creation
There are a few broad focus areas where the model output has to be tested on a continuous basis:
- Instruction following capability
- Generation capability
- Narrative-specific correctness
For example, Evals can be written to assess different aspects of the generated narrative like:
- Factual accuracy of the narrative
- Factual completeness of the narrative
- Name identification
- Timeframe of events
- Narrative follows the Inverted Pyramid Plot structure
- Narrative Articulation
- Narrative Coherence
- Narrative tone
- ..etc.
Sample Eval can look like this:
Sample Eval (Source: authors)
Once we have scores from all the evals, either we can use a weighted average or a simple average of all the individual scores to figure out the final grading criteria. This is how the Evals can be leveraged to grade the quality of generated output
Sequence diagram of Evals grading (Source: authors)
Regression Evals with Golden Data Set
Since the model and prompt are bound to change, this adds another dimension of non-determinism to the system. With any production system, we need to have a regression run of all evals against the golden data set before any model upgrade or prompt/config change happens.
The golden data set has to be collected initially with different edge cases with defined input and output. This will help in testing the system during development. The Golden Data Set can be augmented with human feedback in production where they love the output generated by the AI system.
Evals shall answer some of the generated report’s quality metrics like :
- Did the system provide a factually correct answer?
- Was the summary faithful to the source?
- Was the final response actually helpful to the user?
System Behavior observability
Traditional testing is a deterministic process of verification - it asks, "Did we build the product right?" against a fixed specification. This approach fails when a system’s core logic is probabilistic, because non-deterministic output may be more likely to introduce subtle degradations of quality that do not result in explicit crashes and may not be repeatable. Hence, it is important to monitor the decision-making trajectory, from initial intent to final outcome.
- LLM Model: We first check the core reasoning. Is the LLM Model itself the problem? Failures here include hallucinations, nonsensical or off-topic responses.
- RAG Performance: The response depends on the quality of its retrieved information. Failures include irrelevant document retrieval, fetching outdated or incorrect information, or the LLM ignoring the retrieved context entirely and hallucinating an answer anyway.
- System Failures: What happens when the Model is not able to find the right context or data? Does it make things up or throw the error? What happens when the underlying system is unavailable?
The system is gradually improved by generating telemetry, understanding the system, and patching the underlying issues.
Human-in-The-Loop Control
Human review remains a policy decision owned by the BSA/AML function. AI accelerates preparation; it does not replace accountable judgment.
- Risk-tiered routing: low-risk, familiar typologies may use sampling or streamlined review; novel, high-risk, multilingual, or low-confidence cases default to full review.
- Reviewer experience: show evidence beside each material claim, highlight uncertainty, and make changes explainable rather than forcing reviewers to rewrite from scratch.
- Review quality: evaluate human edits as well as AI output so reviewers correct errors without introducing unsupported statements.
- Accountability: the designated BSA/AML officer retains responsibility for filing decisions and approved risk thresholds.
Release Process
Treat models and prompts as regulated production changes. The release plane provides controlled progress rather than "ship and hope."
- Version: register the model, prompts, retrieval logic, data mappings, policies, and eval set with an owner and change rationale.
- Test: run deterministic factuality checks, rubric scoring, security and privacy checks, and jurisdiction-specific regression suites.
- Gate: require approval from engineering, Compliance/AML, Risk, and Legal according to the change type.
- Shadow and canary: compare the candidate with the incumbent before increasing traffic.
- Monitor: track factuality pass rate, judge scores, reviewer edit rate, latency, queue age, and escalation volume.
- Rollback: use configuration-based feature flags to revert to the previous model, stricter review, or full human drafting when thresholds are breached.
Engineering Trust Into AI-Drafted SARs
The bottleneck in drafting a quality Suspicious Activity Report was qualified personnel. LLM-based systems can reduce that dependency, but only if they're engineered for it, with grounding and evals as the substitute for the judgment of a qualified investigator.
The mechanism we've described treats non-determinism as an engineering problem rather than an excuse. Grounding drafts in a case-specific knowledge graph and operational data keeps the Drafter Agent grounded in evidence. A Judge Agent and deterministic fact-checker turn "does this read well?" into measurable checks against factuality, completeness, and the Inverted Pyramid structure the FIU expects. Evals and a golden dataset give these subjective judgments an objective, regression-testable backbone, the same way unit tests do for deterministic code. And a release process that versions models, prompts, and configuration, gated with shadow/canary rollout and feature-flag rollback, treats every change to the system as a production release
None of this shifts accountability away from the humans who own it. The BSA/AML officer still decides what gets filed; the agentic system's job is to make sure that when a human reviews a draft, the evidence is already assembled, the uncertain claims are flagged, and the reviewer's time goes to judgment rather than transcription. Risk-tiered routing means the system earns trust on familiar, low-risk cases before it is ever allowed near the ones that matter most.
SAR narratives can now be drafted at machine speed, by codifying what "good" looks like into evals a machine can check against. When a human reviews the output, they're not taking the narrative on faith; they can trace the reasoning and the evidence lineage behind it, and that traceability is what turns speed into trust.

articles.title: Plex and TheTVDB failed to reach a deal, and carefully sorted libraries are the collateral
articles.text:
What we know so far: Plex will stop using TheTVDB as a TV show metadata source early next month after the media server company and the database's owner failed to reach a new agreement. Plex is directing users to The Movie Database (TMDB) as the replacement source for episode titles, descriptions, and artwork. However, Plex's TMDB integration can't yet handle several episode-ordering formats that many users rely on, meaning some carefully organized libraries may soon display episodes in the wrong order.
Metadata support is a big part of what makes Plex feel like a streaming service rather than just a folder of video files. When Plex matches a show with an external database, it automatically fills in episode titles, plot summaries, posters, and other details, saving users from having to enter them manually.
TheTVDB, a community-maintained database, has become one of the most popular metadata sources among Plex users because it offers detailed show information and multiple episode-ordering options.
Plex announced the change in a post on its forums but has not explained why the negotiations fell through. The company said metadata already in users' libraries will remain intact, meaning existing collections won't be wiped or reorganized. However, libraries that continue using TheTVDB will stop receiving metadata for new episodes and seasons after the cutoff.
Plex said it will attempt to match new episodes using other metadata sources, but given the sheer number of TV shows available, those alternatives may not work equally well for every series.
The main technical sticking point is episode ordering. TheTVDB supports arrangements that Plex's TMDB integration does not, and two options are particularly important to users. DVD ordering follows the episode sequence used in physical releases, while absolute ordering numbers every episode in a continuous sequence rather than dividing them into seasons. Both are useful for shows whose original episode numbering differs from their broadcast order, a common source of confusion when media software tries to match video files with database listings.
Plex Announcement - Upcoming Change: TheTVDB Metadata Support Ending on December 3rd
by u/samwiseg0 in PleX
Anime fans may be hit hardest. Long-running anime series often use episode numbering that doesn't fit neatly into Western-style seasons, and TMDB's grouping system can differ significantly from TheTVDB's. In a Reddit thread discussing the announcement, commenters criticized both companies for failing to reach an agreement. Many also argued that TMDB alone doesn't offer the flexibility they need to keep their libraries organized.
Plex has acknowledged these limitations. The company said it plans to add support for TMDB episode groups, allowing users to select alternative episode arrangements through TMDB. However, Plex has not provided a release date, meaning the feature may not be ready before TheTVDB support ends.
Until then, Plex is advising users who rely on alternative episode ordering to continue using TheTVDB. This means keeping their existing library structure while giving up metadata updates for new episodes, at least until support for TMDB episode groups arrives.
The announcement comes at a difficult time for Plex. It follows reports of malicious cryptominers causing Plex to run slowly and generate excessive heat on some systems, as well as criticism surrounding the company's collection of user data. Both issues have fueled complaints from a user base that tends to be technically savvy and protective of its self-hosted setups.

articles.title: OpenRouter drops AI providers over leaked prompts and secrets
articles.text:
OpenRouter removed three AI providers from its platform after discovering that they had violated their stated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive data.
The company also revoked Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility for 125 endpoints as a precaution and notified all potentially affected customers.
OpenRouter is an AI model broker that lets developers access AI models from different companies using a single API key.
When an app sends a request, OpenRouter forwards it to a provider that runs the selected model and passes the answer back.
Operational technology security company Dragos alerted OpenRouter after sending two million test prompts through the platform, each containing a unique tracking link or decoy credential, and detecting "activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed."
Dragos discovered that, in some cases, those credentials were leaked to outsiders and used in the wild, indicating that the test prompts had escaped.
“We observed activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed. Our seeded test prompts were used in attempts to access our controlled test systems and canary AWS accounts,” Dragos says.
OpenRouter says there was no breach on its own systems, making the leak point at the provider level and leading to the decision to remove the three leaking inference providers: Together AI, Phala, and Novita.
Another provider, Atlas Cloud, said it would voluntarily withdraw its models from OpenRouter pending security testing, following a third-party security incident.
The other three published separate announcements responding to Dragos’ findings and explaining how the leaks occurred.
Together AI said an AI coding agent exposed a repository credential on GitHub, allowing an unauthorized party to download stored prompt samples from June and July involving MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2, and Kimi K2.6.
Phala said an attacker compromised a server processing DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 requests routed through OpenRouter between October 21 and 22, and possibly up to November 8, and obtained application credentials from affected virtual machines.
Novita said a routing misconfiguration forwarded some MiniMax requests, including those sent through OpenRouter, to MiniMax’s official API between May 28 and November 11.
All four providers are tightening security controls, strengthening their zero data retention or data deletion policies, and advising potentially impacted users to rotate any secrets that may have been exposed in the leaked requests.
OpenRouter is also adapting Dragos’ tests for ongoing use to check whether AI providers forward or leak user requests/responses to third parties, and will require validation before restoring ZDR eligibility.
