articles.title: Log out after using WhatsApp Web to prevent account hijacking: MHA advises users
articles.text:
Log out after using WhatsApp Web to prevent account hijacking: MHA advises users
According to an advisory issued by the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, active WhatsApp Web sessions could be misused to access private messages, impersonate users, and carry out cyber fraud.
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has issued a cybersecurity advisory cautioning users about the potential misuse of authenticated WhatsApp Web sessions to gain access to their accounts.
The advisory, dated November 18, was issued by the National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the MHA.
The advisory warned that leaving accounts logged in on office computers or shared devices could expose them to unauthorised access. This could allow malicious actors to read private messages, send messages while impersonating the account holder, access contacts and group conversations, and exploit trusted identities to carry out fraud, phishing and social-engineering attacks.
The advisory recommends that organisations avoid using WhatsApp Web on office computers, particularly in official and sensitive environments. Users have been advised against exchanging government, financial, confidential or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers.
The I4C has cautioned that simply closing a browser window or tab should not be treated as logging out of WhatsApp Web. Users must manually terminate their sessions after completing their work and avoid leaving accounts permanently logged in.
If access is unavoidable, the agency recommends using 'incognito' or 'private browsing' mode on a trusted computer, followed by a manual logout. Users have also been advised against accessing WhatsApp Web through cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers, or other untrusted systems.
The advisory further recommends keeping devices, operating systems, browsers and security software updated, avoiding suspicious downloads, and monitoring accounts for unexpected messages or unusual activity.
WhatsApp Web sessions targeted in 'Boss Scam'
The latest warning comes amid a rise in WhatsApp-linked account takeover fraud. In an August 7 advisory, the MHA warned corporates and finance professionals about a campaign known as the 'Boss Scam' or CEO impersonation fraud.
According to the ministry's statement published on the Press Information Bureau, fraudsters circulated malicious ZIP files disguised as account statements and regulatory communications, using names such as 'Statement of Account.zip', 'RBI.zip' and 'MCA.zip'.
The files contained malicious Windows executable (.exe) and Dynamic Link Library (.dll) files. Once extracted and executed on a Windows computer, the malware could compromise the device and hijack an active WhatsApp Web session.
Attackers subsequently used compromised accounts to circulate the same malicious files to contacts and groups. In more advanced cases, they impersonated senior executives and instructed finance employees to make urgent transfers to fraudulent bank accounts.
The MHA said it had alerted more than 58,000 potential victims through SMS messages sent under the header 'I4CMHA-G' in the preceding 30 days. More than 10,000 Indians had been protected through coordinated interventions, including the blocking of malicious infrastructure through the government's Sahyog Portal.
The ministry also said it had shared malware-related threat intelligence with the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), Microsoft Defender, and Indian cybersecurity companies, including Quick Heal, K7 Computing and Net Protector.
In its June 22 advisory, the I4C had first flagged the emerging 'Boss Scam' threat, warning that compromised WhatsApp accounts could be used to target employees with fraudulent financial instructions.
The MHA has advised users to regularly review the 'Linked Devices' section in WhatsApp and remove unfamiliar or inactive sessions. It has also urged companies to independently verify urgent payment instructions received through messaging platforms.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Jensen Huang dimitió como CEO de Nvidia y ha vuelto once días después: Donald Trump ha tenido mucho que ver
articles.text:
El pasado 12 de noviembre, Jensen Huang dimitía como CEO de Nvidia, hundido por un truculento escándalo en el que se mezclaban infidelidades, geopolítica y sospechas de espionaje para China. Once días después, el mismo consejo que aceptó su salida lo ha vuelto a readmitir como CEO por unanimidad.
Entre una fecha y otra, hubo una mano que no dejó de presionar a Nvidia para que Huang "volviera al trabajo": Donald Trump. La readmisión de Huang resuelve un gigantesco problema sucesorio para Nvidia, pero arroja una duda sobre la compañía: ¿hasta qué punto es independiente Nvidia de las decisiones que se toman en el despacho oval?
Una amistad con contraprestaciones. Según contaba NBC, el vínculo entre Huang y Donald Trump nació en una cena en Mar-a-Lago. Esa confianza fue creciendo hasta el punto de que, tal y como Huang reconoció en una entrevista con AP, el presidente "me llama en mitad de la noche y quiere hablar de alguno de estos temas". Huang ha pisado la Casa Blanca nueve veces y en septiembre se sentó en la mesa principal de una cena de Estado, junto a Trump y Xi Jinping.
También acompañó al presidente en su viaje oficial a China en mayo, donde incluso se desvió el plan de vuelo del Air Force One para recoger a Huang en Alaska. La Administración le devolvió el favor al suavizar restricciones de Biden, lo que permitió vender sus chips de la generación anterior a China. Huang defendía que era más seguro enganchar a las empresas chinas a la tecnología de EEUU que empujarlas a buscar otra.
Dinero y altavoz para la IA. Por su parte, Nvidia ha financiado con mucho dinero las iniciativas de Trump. La tecnológica aportó 25 millones de dólares al salón de baile de la Casa Blanca situándose como una de las principales donantes, solo empatada con Apple y la familia Adelson. Su gasto en lobby se ha multiplicado por ocho en este mandato y superó los 2,5 millones en el tercer trimestre, según los registros públicos que cita NBC.
En pleno evento All-In, Trump le llamó mientras todavía estaba en el escenario y Huang pidió un micro para que todos oyeran al presidente tachar de "engaño" la petición de frenar la IA. Su respuesta: "Tiene usted razón. No vamos a permitir que eso suceda, señor". Lo que calló es que si la IA se ralentiza, caen los pedidos de chips, y esos chips los fabrica Nvidia. Una mano frota a la otra.
Esa espía de la que usted me habla. Alice Huang, exdirectiva de Megaspeed, estaba siendo investigada por desviar chips a China algunos meses antes de que se hiciera público su affair con Huang. Según el NYT, Washington la vigilaba desde hacía un año. Pekín niega su implicación en el caso de espionaje.
Trump, sin embargo, restó peso al asunto. Dijo que no sabía si era espía, a pesar de los avisos de sus propios servicios, y afirmó: "Si la mujer era una espía, sí. Si no lo era, quizás sería diferente". Ante los periodistas añadió que a cualquier mujer hermosa que llega de China "dicen que es una espía". El Gobierno que la vigilaba tan de cerca como para conocer qué relación mantenía con Huang es el que ahora da por buena la vuelta de Huang.
Un consejo que da marcha atrás. El lunes 16 Trump dijo que "no le importaría" ver de vuelta a Huang al frente de Nvidia. El domingo escribió en su red social Truth que readmitirlo "sería lo mejor para la empresa y también para Estados Unidos". Una recogida de firmas con más de 206.000 participantes, entre ellos figuras como Elon Musk, también presionaba para que el consejo oyera las peticiones de readmisión de Huang.
Harvey Jones, presidente del consejo, había dicho apenas seis días antes que no había intención de restituirlo. Ya se advertía de que hacerlo parecería obedecer a la Casa Blanca. Pero ha pasado.
La llamada del presidente. En su comunicado, el consejo de administración de Nvidia asegura que recibió información de altos cargos del Gobierno de EEUU y que, con ella, la vuelta de Huang no es un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. Lo que Nvidia no cuenta en su comunicado es que también recibió la llamada de Trump presionando a su junta directiva para que Huang recuperara su puesto, tal y como desvela Semafor.
Trump celebró que la junta "ha tomado la decisión correcta y adecuada", y las acciones de la compañía se dispararon hasta subir más del 31% antes de la apertura. Nvidia no es una empresa estatal, pero el calendario sugiere quién marcó el ritmo para que Huang volviera a ser su CEO.
En Xataka | Nvidia no ha despedido a Jensen Huang: ha aceptado su dimisión, y esa diferencia abre la puerta a su vuelta

articles.title: « Pas prêt à être commercialisé » : le crackgate de l’iPhone Duo continue
articles.text:
La sortie de l’iPhone Duo a été entachée par ce que l’on appelle dorénavant le « crackgate ». Pour rappel, sur certains appareils, une ligne lumineuse apparaissait sous la pliure de l’écran interne, avant de s’étendre horizontalement vers la droite. L’entreprise à la pomme avait réagi en expliquant que le problème affectait seulement « un petit nombre d’iPhone Duo » et qu’elle s’engageait à remplacer tout appareil concerné. Nous aurions pu croire que le souci était désormais de l’histoire ancienne, mais il semble en réalité persister.
Une fissure continue d’apparaître sur l’écran interne de certains iPhone Duo
Que ce soit sur Reddit ou Facebook, de nouveaux témoignages faisant état d’une fissure sur l’écran interne de l’iPhone Duo sont apparus ces derniers jours. Un utilisateur de Reddit explique : « Le mien vient donc de se fissurer. Je suis allé dans un Apple Store. Ils m’ont expliqué qu’ils ne pouvaient pas le remplacer, mais qu’ils pouvaient le réparer gratuitement ». Un autre en arrive à une conclusion cinglante : « J’ai renvoyé le mien aujourd’hui et quel soulagement ! Ce produit n’était pas prêt à être commercialisé ».
Il faut dire qu’Apple semble vouloir proposer des solutions pour les appareils concernés, sans discussion. Seul un problème persiste : les stocks d’iPhone Duo sont actuellement très limités. Il ne suffit donc pas de se rendre dans un magasin pour bénéficier aussitôt d’un nouvel appareil. Un utilisateur de Reddit se demande ainsi : « Mon appareil de remplacement express est toujours en attente d’expédition après 3 jours ; je me demande combien ils en ont réellement en stock ». En réalité, c’est la question que pas mal d’analystes se posent : combien d’iPhone Duo l’entreprise à la pomme a-t-elle réellement été capable de produire ?
Combien d’iPhone Duo sont réellement concernés ?
Pour rappel, l’informateur chinois Kang a expliqué qu’il s’agissait d’un problème de matériaux chez l’un des fournisseurs d’Apple, et non d’un défaut de conception. Deux hypothèses sont dès lors probables : soit le problème est plus profond que prévu, soit il est ici question des derniers appareils mis sur le marché qui n’ont pas pu être corrigés à temps.
Par ailleurs, Apple assure que le problème concerne seulement « un petit nombre d’iPhone Duo », mais que cela représente-t-il pour un appareil qui a été produit probablement à plusieurs millions d’exemplaires lors de sa sortie ? Il va falloir maintenant continuer à suivre l’affaire de près afin de voir si le problème sera bel et bien définitivement réglé prochainement.

articles.title: Códigos de Free Fire para reclamar diamantes y skins gratis este 23 de noviembre de 2026
articles.text:
Garena habilitó una nueva serie de códigos de Free Fire para reclamar recompensas sin costo este lunes 23 de noviembre de 2026. Las combinaciones permiten intentar obtener diamantes, skins, atuendos, accesorios y cajas con contenido para usar dentro del videojuego.
Cada clave tiene condiciones propias de disponibilidad. El sistema puede limitar su uso por región, cantidad de canjes o plazo de activación. Por ese motivo, los jugadores deben ingresarlas cuanto antes y comprobar que su perfil esté vinculado con uno de los métodos de acceso aceptados por la plataforma.
Cuáles son los códigos de Free Fire disponibles para canjear hoy
La siguiente lista reúne las combinaciones para intentar canjear recompensas en Free Fire. Deben copiarse sin modificar mayúsculas, números ni orden de los caracteres. Tampoco deben incluir espacios antes o después del código:
- H8YCAJDUDKQ9.
- JDI3SX5NMJ64V.
- FFSGT7KSBHD82.
- B1FCCUIDN68YT.
- BR43FMAPYEZZ.
- FFSGT7KNFQ2X.
- 4ST1ZTBZBRP9.
- UPQ7X5NMJ64V.
- H8YC4TN6VKQ9.
- S9QK2L6VP3MR.
- FPSTQ7MXNPY5.
- B1RK7C5ZL8YT.
- 4N8M2XL9R1G3.
- FF6YH3BFD7VT.
Los premios pueden variar según cada clave y la disponibilidad que figure. Algunas combinaciones entregan artículos coleccionables o accesorios, mientras que otras pueden habilitar diamantes, trajes o skins de armas. La confirmación definitiva aparece una vez que el portal procesa la solicitud.
Cómo redimir los códigos en el portal oficial de Garena
El canje se realiza desde el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena. Allí, el usuario debe iniciar sesión con la misma cuenta que utiliza en el juego y luego buscar el campo destinado a introducir el código promocional.
La plataforma admite perfiles asociados con Google, Facebook, Apple o VK. Después de seleccionar el acceso correcto, corresponde pegar la clave y revisar cada carácter antes de confirmar. Una letra equivocada, un número omitido o un espacio adicional pueden hacer que el portal rechace el pedido.
Por qué sale el mensaje de código inválido o expirado?¿
El aviso de código inválido o expirado suele indicar que la combinación alcanzó el máximo de usos establecido, que su plazo de vigencia terminó o que no está disponible para el servidor desde el cual se intenta reclamar el premio. Las restricciones pueden cambiar según la región de la cuenta.
Asimismo, es posible que el problema responda a un error al copiar la secuencia. Los códigos combinan letras y números, así que resulta preferible pegarlos directamente en lugar de escribirlos de forma manual. Conviene verificar que no haya espacios al principio o al final y que se mantengan las mayúsculas originales.
Quiénes no pueden reclamar premios en Free Fire a través de códigos
Las cuentas de invitado no pueden utilizar el sistema de recompensas, incluso cuando el código aún aparece como activo. El portal necesita una cuenta registrada para identificar el perfil que recibirá los objetos y enviar el contenido correspondiente al buzón del juego.
Quienes juegan con un perfil de invitado deben vincularlo antes con alguno de los proveedores habilitados. Google, Facebook, Apple y VK figuran entre las alternativas disponibles. La vinculación de la cuenta permite que los premios queden asignados al usuario correcto y evita inconvenientes durante el proceso.
Cuánto demoran en llegar los diamantes al inventario
Los artículos obtenidos mediante los códigos suelen enviarse al correo interno de Free Fire. El plazo habitual de entrega es inferior a 24 horas, aunque algunos premios pueden tardar en reflejarse en el inventario principal del usuario.
Después de completar el canje, es clave revisar la sección de correo del juego. Los diamantes se encuentran entre las recompensas más buscadas, porque permiten acceder a contenido de pago, pero su entrega depende de la clave validada y de las condiciones que mantenga activas el sistema.
La pauta principal es utilizar únicamente el portal oficial de recompensas de Garena y descargar el juego desde tiendas verificadas. En los teléfonos con Android, la vía indicada es Google Play Store; en los dispositivos de Apple, corresponde usar App Store.

articles.title: The best wireless speakers, all tested by our experts — from JBL, Sonos, Bose, and more
articles.text:
The best wireless speakers, all tested by our experts — from JBL, Sonos, Bose, and more
The best wireless speakers you can buy for your home
Drawing on decades of combined audio expertise and hands-on testing across countless models, our team has tracked down the very best wireless speakers you can buy today. Whether you’re after a compact Bluetooth-and-Wi-Fi speaker for a single room or a flagship multi-room powerhouse, you’ll find the right fit in this guide.
Every model on our list pairs rich, room-filling sound with the freedom of a clutter-free setup. By connecting over your home Wi-Fi network, these speakers deliver high-quality streaming without messy cables. And most also include Bluetooth for effortless playback on the go. Many top picks even double as smart speakers, offering built-in voice control (Alexa, Google Assistant, or Siri), support for the best music streaming services, and companion apps for fine-tuning your EQ settings.
Before making the cut, every speaker is rigorously tested by our reviewers in real-world home environments. We judge each model on what matters most, such as audio fidelity, smart features, day-to-day ease of use, and overall value, before debating and agreeing on the final lineup as a team.
I've reviewed over 150 audio products since becoming a tech journalist, ranging from super-budget earbuds to high-end Hi-Res Audio music players. Before joining TechRadar, I spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing everything the world of audio had to offer; before that, I was a professional dancer, so obviously I have strong opinions about the quality of speakers, whether that's at home or something pro.

❌ You value simplicity: Room-filling sound and lots of features means this makes the most sense for those after an all-singing, all-dancing smart speaker.
The JBL Authentics 200 is one incredibly impressive speaker. For starters, it looks gorgeous. It’s also got all of the essential features you could need from a top wireless speaker and, most importantly, it sounds fantastic. It could have topped multiple categories in this guide, but for now, we’re naming it our best overall wireless speaker – the top choice for most people.
Expect excellent audio across the range, with full bass, rich mids and plenty of detailed treble. In our review we also commented: “Separation is impressive, and there’s a depth to its soundstage that delivers remarkable immersion for a single speaker.” The result is a lot of depth and a listening experience we described as “sublime”
All of the top features are here, including multi-room audio and connectivity to the intuitive JBL One app. There’s also Wi-Fi streaming from several services. You can integrate the app with a range of streaming platforms, as well as customize the EQ settings – but we found it most enjoyable to do that manually by turning the treble and bass knobs on the speaker itself. If you like using voice commands, there’s support for Google Assistant and Amazon Alexa to choose from.
The JBL Authentics 200 has a refreshingly different aesthetic. In our review we wrote that it delivers “a dose of vintage style in a market crowded by neutral designs”. This is down to the curved foam grille and the aluminium frame – a nod to the look of older amps. Then again, it’s not overtly retro. It doesn’t look like a regular speaker cosplaying as a cool one, is what we’re saying. All of the design choices here look subtle and the result is a stunning build and finish that also feels premium, too.
It’s not the cheapest speaker in this guide. It’s also lacking Atmos compatibility, which you can find for less. But it’s one of the most appealing right now for its combination of superb sound, a refreshing, retro look and excellent feature set. As we pointed out in our review, “there’s really nothing else like the Authentics 200.”

If your goal is to get the most sound for your money, the Sonos Era 100 SL is the budget wireless speaker we recommend. At $189 / £169 / AU$289, it brings detailed, room-filling audio to the table with fewer compromises than you might expect at this price.
On the features front, the Era 100 SL uses a mid-woofer to handle mid-range and bass, complemented by two angled tweeters for treble and a sense of stereo width. In our listening, there weren’t many sacrifices in clarity—even in the mid-range, where some similarly-priced rivals can sound relatively thin. Our reviewer noted that on Moloko’s I Want You, guitar and synth lines cut through the mix without muddying the polished vocals, which is a surprise for a speaker at this price.
Connectivity is strong, too. You get Wi-Fi 6 for fast streaming, AirPlay 2 for Apple users, and Bluetooth 5.3 for quick pairing. That versatility means it’s equally at home in a living room or paired with a phone in the kitchen. During Tidal’s hi-res streams of Wasting My Young Years by London Grammar, we heard an airy separation between vocals, piano, and drums—further proof you’re not missing out on musical nuance for the sake of saving money.
One caveat: this isn’t the pick if you need true portability or long battery life. The Sonos Play remains the better choice for taking outside or moving between rooms. Durability and water resistance are limited, too, so it’s best suited to indoor listening.
All told, the Sonos Era 100 SL delivers where it counts for budget-conscious buyers—impressive sound, modern connectivity, and a decent design without needless frills. It lacks Dolby Atmos and high-end design touches, but if you want your dollars focused on what you actually hear, it’s the best budget wireless speaker in the lineup.

The LS50 Wireless II speakers build upon the success of the LS50 Wireless, which impressed with their detailed sound and connectivity options. The result is a pair of stereo speakers that are the best you can buy today at this price.
One reason some people are put off by stereo systems like this one is that they assume they’ll be tricky. During our hands-on testing, we wrote that setting up the LS50 Wireless II speakers is “blissfully easy.” All you need to do is plug each speaker into power and connect them to your Wi-Fi network. You can then stream from the Spotify app using Spotify Connect or via Tidal, Qobuz, Amazon Music, or Deezer through the KEF Connect app.
With support for Hi-Res Audio, an expansive soundstage, and excellent detail and dexterity, audio quality is nothing short of fantastic. In our review, we wrote: “We’re happy to report that the LS50 Wireless II stereo speakers continue to provide the phenomenal audio quality offered by their predecessors – and then some.” That incredibly well-balanced, detailed, clarified sound may not appeal to bass-heads, but it will to audiophiles. It boasts great stereo separation, and a wide enough soundstage to fill any room.
Not only is the sound great and setup easy, but you can customize it easily. This is because the app is easy to use and gives you access to EQ settings that can be optimized by where you’ve positioned your speakers. You can also adjust the bass extension and treble trim and set low and high-pass frequencies. We’re happy to report that, during our testing, we found that you can pretty much tailor the sound profile exactly to your needs and environment.
There are several color options to choose from, white, black, red, and gray. The system, as a whole, looks stylish and understated. It has a sleek cabinet and a copper-colored Uni-Q driver, which fits a tweeter in the center of the bass and mid-range cone. On top of the primary speaker, you’ll find a touch-sensitive control panel that also comes with an infrared remote control.
They're a little pricey, but they’re well worth the money. These speakers sound amazing, delivering premium sound that’ll fill your room. Add to that a vastly improved app, the ability to adjust the EQ settings, and a blissfully easy setup, and you have a pair of stereo speakers that can ddo no wrong in our eyes.

The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker is our best as the best Sonos alternative if you want powerful, room-filling sound that brings a surprising sense of scale in such a small package. Audio is punchy, detailed, and dynamic, with a unique height to the soundstage that you'll certainly notice if you make use of its multi-room support.
Setup is also refreshingly straightforward, and the companion app is both clean and intuitive, making daily control (including EQ tweaks or pairing for stereo or home theater) delightfully free of friction and frustration.
What gives the Bose real ecosystem appeal is its broad connectivity: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 5.3 (with support for SBC and AAC codecs), Apple AirPlay 2, Google Cast, and Spotify Connect are all on board. There’s also a 3.5mm analog input for those who need a physical connection. If you’ve struggled with ecosystem lock-in, the flexibility here means you can join or build out a whole-home wireless system without convoluted workarounds.
Whether you’re adjusting settings in the app or calling up playlists hands-free, control is consistent and responsive. That makes the Bose just as easy to use as a true Sonos alternative for smart homes that tend to rely on app and voice controls frequently. Alexa+ is another welcome highlight, giving top quality voice assistant support for hands-free music and playlist browsing.
The main trade-offs? Bluetooth support is limited to basic codecs (SBC and AAC), so true hi-res streaming fans may want to look elsewhere, and there’s no automatic room calibration, unlike some of its rivals. If you prize robust multi-room streaming, easy setup, and a sound profile that impresses across rooms, the Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker is a top-tier Sonos alternative.

✅ You want a simple, portable speaker: It's very easy to carry this speaker around with you, good for use at home or on the move, thanks for Bluetooth connectivity.
❌ You want something really light: At 1.3kg, it's not especially weighty, but does pack on the pounds compared to its predecessor; the lighter Sonos Roam 2.
❌ You want big, audiophile sound: It's a relatively small speaker, and that limits what it can do – other options here offer way more scale and expansiveness.
The Sonos Play is for anyone who prioritizes portability without giving up quality. Its compact, durable chassis feels instantly grab-and-go, and in real-world testing, the soft-touch exterior and robust build suited outdoor use without worry.
The IP67 waterproof rating means it shrugs off splashes, and even after hours at the beach, the speaker’s enclosure wiped clean with no fuss. This is a speaker you’ll actually want to take everywhere, unlike many rivals that claim portability but feel awkward on the go and perhaps don't clean up as well.
The Sonos Play supports both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, so it transitions seamlessly from home streaming to outdoor playlists. There’s a USB-C line-in for wired listening, and you can even top up the battery via USB-C on the fly. Compared to bulkier, less adaptable alternatives like the Bose Mini, the Play’s dual charging and connection options make it a no-brainer for travel, outdoor gatherings, or simply moving from room to room.
Sonically, the Play delivers weighty audio that betrays its size. Mids are crisp, bass is surprisingly full, and the highs ring with clarity, resulting in a rounded, energetic sound that fills a patio or living room better than most compact speakers we’ve tested. While it doesn’t quite match the dynamic punch or stereo depth of high-end, stationary speakers, it outclasses nearly every other portable in its weight class and price range.
There are a few trade-offs to keep in mind. The Play can be a bit overzealous about conserving battery: it sometimes powers down quickly if left idle, which might catch you off-guard. The touch controls on top are also hard to distinguish by feel, especially in low light or while multitasking. These quirks don’t overshadow the overall experience, but they are worth knowing if you're going hands-on with it frequently.

Sonus Faber is well-known for its high-priced, luxury hi-fi equipment, and the Omnia is no exception. This is a sleek, sophisticated, and fairly big all-in-one system that we found incredibly easy to use thanks to comprehensive wireless connectivity, with built-in support for the major streaming services, AirPlay, Chromecast, and Roon.
The Sonus Faber Omnia is an all-in-one system that brings simplicity and ease of use thanks to its wireless connectivity features and built-in support for major streaming services, AirPlay, Chromecast, Spotify, Tidal and Roon. There’s wired connectivity, too. You’ll find a switchable phone/line input to connect it to a turntable or other analog device, HDMI ARC, and an Ethernet port. Otherwise, you can control the speaker via your smartphone. If you’re on an iOS device, you’ll need the Home app to connect the Omnia to your Wi-Fi, while Android users can do this with the Google Home app. During our review, we found that setting up the Omnia was easy – follow the instructions in the app of your choice or use a wired Ethernet connection.
The Sonus Faber Omnia has a four-way closed-box system. This has seven drivers that are powered by 490W of amplification. Sonically speaking, it’s exemplary, with a wide soundstage, excellent clarity, and a deep bass response. During our testing, we were impressed by its stellar performance: “This is a powerful speaker that can soundtrack a party just as well as it can act as your TV’s main speaker in place of a soundbar.”
The Omnia may not sound as supremely detailed as Sonus Faber’s larger speakers, but it will still convey the minutiae of your favorite tracks with aplomb. In our review, we wrote: “It really shines in its presentation of close-mic vocals. In Eva Cassidy’s rendition of What A Wonderful World, the raspiness of her voice comes across with exquisite detail.”
The system has a tactile lacquered wooden surface that lights up when you interact with it. As we wrote in our review, we’ve seen for ourselves how these speakers are made and can confirm that plenty of care goes into picking the right wood, sanding it down, and preparing it by hand. Consider that this is a larger speaker, so although it looks sleek and sophisticated enough to elevate any home, you’ll need space.
This is a luxury speaker with a price tag to match. This means it’s only the right choice for people willing to invest in their sound system. But if you’re an audiophile with a big budget and want an option that works with your favorite streaming services at the touch of a button, the Sonus Faber Omnia is a top choice.

✅ You want to create a Sonos surround system: Pair two Sonos Era 300 units with a Sonos Arc Ultra for glorious surround sound.

Sonos was generous enough to launch two new wireless speakers into its range in 2023. The Era 100 and this Era 300, which is the more premium version, and we went as far as to say in our review that it is on a whole new level when it comes to dispersing sound.
It's a very flexible speaker, and by far the best if you want to set up a Sonos surround system. You can also access the Sonos app to support AirPlay 2, Bluetooth 5.0, line-in, Hi-Res Audio and (of course) Dolby Atmos. Unlike previous Sonos products, the Era 300 supports a new type of room tuning tech called TruePlay Quick Tuning that works with both iOS and Android devices. You play a sound on your phone and the speaker listens and adjusts to your room.
The Sonos Era 300 sounds amazing in every conceivable way. First of all, we were blown away by the levels of detail on offer here. In our Sonos Era 300 review we wrote: “It elevates voices in the mix better than anything else I've heard at this size or price.” At times, we were slightly disappointed by the bass, which didn’t hit quite as deep as we expected, but we did note that it improved at higher volumes.
The speaker sounds so good for all sorts of reasons, but most notably, it’s the first speaker from Sonos with Dolby Atmos support. Thanks to up- and side-firing speakers, its spatial audio is also next-generation, which is the biggest differential factor of the two Era offerings and the main reason we would choose the 300 over the 100. This was really obvious during our sound tests, where we noted: “The Sonos Era 300 may be the most well-dispersed soundstage I've heard from a single speaker.”
The Sonos Era 300 has an unusual squashed cylinder shape, but that’s because it needs to have multiple angled speakers and horn shapes for its compression drivers. Still, Sonos has done a good job at making it look sleek and stylish, like the rest of its devices. One thing to note, however, that we picked up on during testing is that you can’t put it on a set of shelves where it’s covered at the top or on its sides. It must be in the open to blast soundwaves up and to the sides.
The Sonos Era 300 is great as a high-quality, super-flexible speaker. It’s not cheap, but it's not the most expensive wireless speaker either. Instead, it delivers exceptional audio prowess that most affordable speakers can’t touch, but you can opt for even more premium models if you want more bass extension. We also think that hi-fi fans may prefer the more traditional sound and style of the Sonos Five, although that device feels a little old compared to Sonos' newer models.

Other wireless speakers to consider
B&W Zeppelin (2021): Take a look at our Bowers & Wilkins Zeppelin (2021) review and you'll see we gave it a rare 5 out of 5 rating. Why? It sounds amazing, looks stunning and works well. The only reason it's not longer in this guide is the company released the latest model, which is currently in the guide above as our 'best under $1000' pick.
Bluesound Pulse M: We recently tested this wireless speaker and although we rated the detailed hi-res audio and simple design, as you'll see from our Bluesound Pulse M review, the whole package just didn't live up to expectations, especially for the price.
Denon Home 400: This spatial audio-leaning wireless speaker is absolutely superb, boasting immersive, room-filling sound and a seriously premium build quality. Our only major gripe is the lack of voice assistant support, which feels like a glaring omission by today's standards. Still, it's well worth reading about in our Denon Home 400 review.
Edifier D32: If you enjoy a vintage vibe, this speaker should look the part in your home. You won't find booming bass and power for big parties here, but if that's not a priority for you, then this is a lovely-looking choice that delivers high-res sound and style for a decent price. Read our full Edifier D32 review for more.
Kanto Ren: Now, these aren't wi-fi enabled, so why are we mentioning them? Well, read our Kanto Ren review and you'll learn that these 5 star rated stereo speakers are powered (so no need for separate amps) and also boast Bluetooth connectivity. Which means if you want something to plug into your TV, laptop or other setup that also has Bluetooth baked in, the sound is truly sensational.
KEF LSX II LT: We rated this excellent, simple streaming hi-fi system highly in our KEF LSX II LT review and it's an ideal smaller and cheaper alternative to the LS50 II Wireless in the guide above.
KEF LS Luxe: There's so much to love and enjoy about these wireless speakers. They put forward clear, authoritative sound and look fantastic in any living space. The downside? They're monumentally expensive and don't ship with stands. Those are sold separately and also command a princely sum. Check out our KEF LS Luxe review to learn more.
Meridian Ellipse: Glance quickly at our Meridian Ellipse review and you might think you were looking at the B&W Zeppelin (above) but it's actually quite a different beast – and not always in a good way. It's crammed with smarts and looks the part, but we think it's missing the low end clout it needs for this kind of money.
PSB iQ2: These spenny speakers deliver energetic and punchy audio, but overall sound isn't particularly roomy and the phono stage leaves much to be desired. Do give our PSB iQ2 review a read to learn more.
Sonos Era 100: For a long time, the Era 100 was our top overall pick, and while we now think there are better options, it’s still a fantastic speaker. With excellent detail, clarity, and bass, it remains a solid choice. Read our full Sonos Era 100 review to see why we love it. However, as time has passed, newer models have surpassed it in value and audio performance, making it a little less competitive than it once was.
Sonos Five: Once our top pick for the best connectivity, the Sonos Five has now been overtaken by the newer Cambridge Audio Evo One. That said, it’s still worth considering for its room-filling sound and Sonos and AirPlay integration. However, the lack of Bluetooth and hi-res support means it’s no longer our top choice. Read our Sonos Five review to learn more.
WiiM Sound: Once a sitter in our 'best Sonos alternative' category, it's still an incredible wireless speaker worth checking out if you're after superb sound quality and a handy touchscreen on-device. Check out our WiiM Sound review for more info.
Other AirPlay speakers: If you're on the hunt for other wireless speakers, do also take a look at our best AirPlay speakers guide. This is packed full of wireless options that work particularly well with Apple's wireless streaming tech – although they're not all from Apple. You'll find speaker options from KEF, Naim and Sonos, too.
How to choose the best wireless speaker
It's not easy when the market is awash with wireless, cubes, oblongs, teardrops cylinders and cushions all claiming to be the best, is it? If casting music from your phone or any other Bluetooth device is important to you, a Wi-Fi only connection (even if it uses Apple AirPlay 2) may not be sufficient.
But when it comes to picking a new wireless speaker for your home, room-filling sound is key, so look for models that feature 360-degree grilles and disperse audio at all angles. If it's true audio fidelity you're after, opt for trusted brands such as Sonos, Bowers & Wilkins and KEF – speakers from these companies are always likely to sound brilliant.
If you have an iPhone or an iPad, it might also be worth checking out the best AirPlay speakers, which allow you to stream music, podcasts or audiobooks directly from your devices to your speaker. That means room-filling sound from your phone without the need for a more complex entertainment set-up. With so many fantastic home wireless speakers on the market right now, we’ve selected and ranked only the best ones to include in this buying guide.
Will wireless speakers work with Spotify Lossless?
Spotify Lossless is now finally rolling out to Premium users of the streaming service. It should work with all wireless speakers that already support Spotify Connect, which is Spotify's own way of letting you play music over Wi-Fi, assuming they have a hi-res-capable decoding chip (which basically all will have).
Apps for wireless speakers that have Spotify library support built-in will also be able to access and play Spotify Lossless, but not all offered this at launch – a wait for an update may be necessary in some cases, such as on Sonos.
As you'd expect, a high-end Wi-Fi speaker or multi-room system will get more from the improved sound than a cheaper one with more basic speakers.
Can I turn regular speakers into wireless speakers?
Yes, you can. You don’t necessarily need to replace your old wired speakers to go wireless, but you will need a wireless adapter. These devices can connect to your existing speaker system via an aux or optical input and will then connect to your Wi-Fi or Bluetooth source.
These adapters are essentially a way to upgrade your system, allowing you to stream music from your phone, laptop or smart home devices without having to plug anything in. It’s a good way to make your beloved hi-fi setup more modern, but without spending big on brand new wireless speakers.
How do I control wireless speakers?
Wireless speakers are most really simple to use. Which means you usually have a few options about how you control them.
Some have on-device controls. These are physical buttons that allow you to change volume, play/pause or switch inputs.
You can also control many with apps. Most brands now have a companion app for advanced controls, including EQ, grouping speakers together and streaming.
Many wireless speakers have voice assistants, like Alexa, Google Assistant or Siri built-in, which lets you control them hands-free.
Finally, some speakers support systems like Spotify Connect, Apple AirPlay and Google Cast (AKA Chromecast). These allow you to control playback directly from your streaming app.
The best option will depend on your speaker. You'll tend to find that entry-level Bluetooth models might only offer basic buttons and phone control. But high-end Wi-Fi speakers often become part of a whole home smart system that you can run entirely from your phone or with your voice.
Do wireless speakers offer Hi-Res Audio?
Yes, these days the vast majority of Wi-Fi and multi-room speakers now support Hi-Res Audio.
Hi-Res Audio means the music is streamed at a higher quality than standard CD audio, which captures more detail in the track you're listening to. Some wireless speakers are now certified for this kind of Hi-Res playback, especially models from higher-end brands, such as Bowers & Wilkins and KEF.
Also bear in mind that all of the other devices you're using matter here. For example, the source (like your streaming service or files) must also be Hi-Res, and the connection method has to support it, too.
With Wi-Fi speakers, that's no problem – it's got the bandwidth for Hi-Res Audio and then some, and works across all devices.
Are Sonos wireless speakers still worth buying?
Sonos speakers are still a good choice. However, you should know that Sonos rolled out big changes to its app in 2024. These changes caused frustration among Sonos fans because key features were missing or harder to access, and the rollout felt rushed. Backlash to the changes was loud, which is why Sonos has steadily been issuing updates to restore missing functionality and improve the overall experience.
With all that in mind, we do think the core appeal of Sonos remains intact and the app has been restored to working very well, in our experience. Sonos products deliver strong audio quality, seamless multi-room support, and lots of compatibility with streaming services and smart home systems.
So if you're already in the Sonos ecosystem or considering a Sonos speaker, we still think Sonos devices are absolutely worth buying. However, do keep an eye out for news about ongoing updates – especially if the app experience is a top priority for you.
What are the best wireless speaker brands to look out for?
It really depends on what kind of speaker you're after. If you want multi-room connectivity and excellent sound, look for home speakers from Sonos.
Need a smart speaker? Check out models in the Google Nest and Amazon Echo ranges (and if you're a Siri user, Apple). Bear in mind though, you're not stuck with these brands if you need a voice assistant, as many third-party speakers come with Alexa and Google Assistant compatibility.
If it's pure audio fidelity you're after, brands like KEF, Naim, and Devialet are worth looking into. And, for portability, check out the likes of JBL, Ultimate Ears, Bose, and Urbanista.
What is the difference between these wireless speakers and a Bluetooth speaker?
The key difference about what's in this guide compared to our list of the best Bluetooth speakers lies in Wi-Fi support. Wireless speakers often connect via Wi-Fi, which provides a more stable and high-quality audio stream. That’s because the Wi-Fi connection allows larger data transmissions, which results in better sound quality, especially with high-resolution audio files. Wi-Fi speakers can also connect to multiple devices simultaneously, making them ideal for multi-room setups controlled via apps.
In contrast, Bluetooth speakers connect directly to devices like smartphones, tablets, or laptops using Bluetooth. While convenient and portable, Bluetooth has a shorter range and can be more prone to signal interference and compression, which can affect audio quality.
However, when considering the difference between wireless speakers and Bluetooth speakers, it’s also worth considering that most of the best wireless speakers also have Bluetooth built-in, bringing you both options.
Wi-Fi is relatively uncommon in portable speakers, because it uses a lot more power than Bluetooth, and usually requires a network to connect to. However, there are some portable options in this guide.
What are the disadvantages of wireless speakers?
There’s a lot to love about wireless speakers, but they do have some disadvantages compared to wired speakers. One of the main drawbacks is that they’re dependent on a stable Wi-Fi network. This means that if your Wi-Fi signal is weak or inconsistent, you might experience interruptions or poor sound quality. Setting up wireless speakers can also sometimes be more complex, requiring apps and network configurations.
Another potential downside is latency. Wireless connections can sometimes introduce a slight delay in audio transmission. This could be noticeable when you’re watching videos or playing games. Battery life can also be a concern for portable wireless speakers, as they’d need regular charging.
Can I use a turntable with wireless speakers?
Yes, you can likely use one of the best turntables with wireless speakers, but exactly how will depend on the speakers or the turntable. The simplest option is, of course, if your turntable has wireless capabilities. There are products like the Cambridge Audio Alva TT V2 that can broadcast Bluetooth to headphones or wireless speakers, while some support Wi-Fi to play to certain wireless system, such as the Sonos-friendly Victrola Stream Carbon.
However, a lot of wireless speakers have wired inputs, and they always have their own built-in amplification, so these can be connected to a turntable use RCA wired cabling… as long as either the turntable or wireless speaker has a phono stage pre-amp built in. This is common in turntables, but much less common in speakers, so make sure you've got this somewhere in there.
Finally, there are adapters that you can plug a turntable into to add wireless transmission to them, such as a WiiM Pro Plus or a Sonos Port.
What streaming services do wireless speakers work with?
Most of the best wireless speakers support several different streaming services. Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect, Apple AirPlay and Qobuz Connect are some of the most commonly supported streaming services. Roon is less common, but is often supported by higher-end models.
However, it does depend on the brand of speaker. So, for example, at the time of writing Sonos supports Spotify Connect, Tidal Connect and Apple AirPlay but not Qobuz Connect.
Which is why we always suggest that you check your product's software support before you buy, depending on your music streaming platform of choice. We've listed everything you need to know about support in our reviews, of course, so do click through to those in the guide above.
It's also worth mentioning that if you’re a big podcast or audiobook listener, you'll need to make sure your speaker supports the apps you use most – or that it has Bluetooth as a backup. If you have Bluetooth (or Apple AirPlay and Google Cast, to a degree), you can play basically anything from your phone or other device.
Are wireless speakers' connections reliable?
Generally, yes. However, it does depend on your home Wi-Fi. Wireless speakers rely on a strong, stable signal to deliver quality sound. In most homes with a decent router, you’ll get a smooth experience with little to no dropouts.
But if your Wi-Fi is patchy or overloaded, you might experience some lag or interruptions. Multi-room setups are especially sensitive to network strength, so it might be worth considering a Wi-Fi mesh system or positioning your router centrally for the best possible results; or even using an Ethernet cable to connect directly to your router.
Bluetooth tends to be very stable if you're in the same room, but will drop of quickly when walls get in the way.
What's the best multi-room wireless speaker system?
Sonos is still one of the best choices. Its multi-room setup is intuitive, reliable and it works across a range of speaker types and budgets, which means that you can start with one speaker and expand room by room.
But there are other strong options too. In the guide above, several of the picks have some multi-room functionality, including brands such as JBL, Bowers & Wilkins and Cambridge Audio.
Google Cast and Apple AirPlay can offer multi-room support using speakers from different brands, which is useful for mixing and matching what you need. Google and Amazon also support multi-room setups for their smart speakers.
Will a wireless speaker work if my internet goes down?
This would depend on how your speaker is set up. If you’re streaming directly from the cloud, such as using Spotify Connect or playing music from Apple Music via the Sonos app, then yes. No internet would mean no music.
However, if your speaker also supports Bluetooth, AirPlay/Google Cast, or has an aux input, then you’ve got a backup plan. You would be able to switch to local playback from your phone or laptop until the connection’s back.
Bluetooth and an aux input don't require your network at all. AirPlay and Google Cast both use your home's Wi-Fi network – but this may still be working even if you're internet is down. If it's just the internet that's not working and you have saved music on your phone, you're fine; if your Wi-Fi went down along with the internet, then Bluetooth or aux-in are the only options.
How we test the best wireless speakers
At TechRadar, we get our hands (and ears, of course,) on dozens of wireless speakers every year, so we know exactly which features matter. And we know that the very best models can rival a traditional stereo system when set up properly.
Because manufacturer specs don't always tell the full story, we put every claim to the test in real-world conditions. We pit each speaker directly against its closest rivals to compare audio quality and key features like multi-room compatibility and app support, ensuring that when we call a speaker the best, it has genuinely earned the title.
Our reviewers live with these speakers in their own homes to test day-to-day reliability and consistency, never signing off on a verdict until we're completely confident in the sound. We stream across multiple sources and play a wide mix of genres, from bass-heavy dance tracks to subtle, spoken-word podcasts, to see how well each model adapts.
Backed by years of audio testing and complete editorial independence, our star-rated reviews are strictly earned: if a speaker falls short on sound, design, or usability, it simply won't make this list.

Becky became Audio Editor at TechRadar in 2024, but joined the team in 2022 as Senior Staff Writer, focusing on all things hi-fi. Before this, she spent three years at What Hi-Fi? testing and reviewing everything from wallet-friendly wireless earbuds to huge high-end sound systems. Prior to gaining her MA in Journalism in 2018, Becky freelanced as an arts critic alongside a 22-year career as a professional dancer and aerialist – any love of dance starts with a love of music. articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.text:
Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
  November 16, 2026
- Source:
  University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:
As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.
The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.
Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.
A New Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy
The breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.
Quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can quickly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.
But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties."
Rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the new approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify important interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.
"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy."
Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator
To evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.
After this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, showed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.
This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.
Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems
The next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.
"This is particularly important because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important."
The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.
Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.
"After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," says Peter Zoller.
This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how quickly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.
The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

articles.title: GTA 6 est déjà jouable sur PlayStation Portal sans PS5
articles.text:
Avant le lancement de GTA 6 le 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X, Rockstar Games avait mis en avant la possibilité de jouer en streaming au sein de l’écosystème Xbox — y compris sur une vieille console comme la Xbox One. Le jeu était jouable sur Xbox Cloud Gaming dès le 19 novembre, et on pensait à une belle exclusivité pour Microsoft. Elle n’aura duré que quatre jours, puisque la technologie est disponible sur PlayStation depuis ce lundi 23 novembre, comme l’a repéré Power Up Gaming.
Concrètement, il est désormais possible de jouer en streaming à GTA 6 sur une PlayStation 5 ou un PlayStation Portal, à deux conditions : être propriétaire de la version numérique du jeu et être abonné au PlayStation Plus Premium, la formule la plus chère du service (18,99 € par mois, 54,99 € pour trois mois ou 151,99 € pour un an).
Vous n’avez plus besoin d’une PS5 pour jouer à GTA 6
L’arrivée de cette fonctionnalité signifie qu’il n’est plus nécessaire d’être propriétaire d’une PS5 pour jouer. Un PlayStation Portal peut suffire, aux deux conditions citées et, bien entendu, de faire quelques concessions graphiques sur l’expérience, le streaming ne pouvant atteindre une qualité comparable à un jeu installé sur la PS5.
Jusqu’ici, le PlayStation Portal ne pouvait lancer GTA 6 qu’en Remote Play : il affichait l’image d’une PS5 restée allumée à la maison. Avec le cloud, le jeu tourne sur les serveurs de Sony, et la console de salon n’a plus besoin d’être allumée, ni même d’exister. Les sauvegardes se synchronisent entre la version installée et la version streamée, ce qui permet de reprendre sur le Portal une partie commencée sur PS5.
Il faut aussi une bonne connexion internet pour jouer confortablement. Sur la page officielle du streaming sur PlayStation, Sony exige au moins 5 Mb/s, en téléchargement comme en téléversement. Sur PS5, Sony recommande 13 Mb/s pour du 720p (HD), 23 Mb/s pour du 1080p (Full HD), 38 Mb/s pour du 1440p et 52 Mb/s pour du 2160p (4K). Le PlayStation Portal, lui, plafonne à 1080p en cloud, avec 13 Mb/s minimum (7 Mb/s pour du 720p).
Notons quand même que le cloud gaming PlayStation se limite à deux appareils seulement, quand celui Xbox permet de jouer sur un nombre bien plus important d’appareils — des anciennes consoles aux smartphones, en passant par les téléviseurs connectés. Depuis ce mois de novembre, Microsoft plafonne aussi le cloud gaming : 15 heures par mois avec le Game Pass Ultimate, 10 heures en Premium et 5 heures en Essential. Au-delà, il faut acheter des heures supplémentaires. Pour un monde ouvert comme GTA 6, 15 heures passent vite. Dans les deux écosystèmes, il faut acheter le jeu, vendu 79,99 € en édition Standard.

articles.title: Notée 4,5/5, cette tablette Samsung passe sous les 700 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La tablette Tactile Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+ à 699,99 € (-14%)
Actuellement notée 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, la Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+ combine un écran lumineux et bien calibré à de solides performances pour le travail comme pour le divertissement. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 699,99 € chez Fnac.com et Darty.com, soit une baisse d'environ 14 % et 117,86 € d'économie.
Samsung a conçu la Galaxy Tab S10+ pour répondre aux besoins de productivité et de divertissement sur grand écran, en s'appuyant sur une dalle Amoled de 12,4 pouces et le processeur Dimensity 9300+. Cette tablette tactile haut de gamme s'est distinguée lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à son équilibre général et ses outils dédiés au travail.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+ descend à 699,99 € chez Fnac.com et Darty.com, soit environ 14 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (817,85 €). Cela représente une économie de 117,86 €.
Un grand écran Amoled très lumineux taillé pour le multitâche
Avec sa diagonale de 12,4 pouces, la dalle Amoled affiche une belle précision pour travailler sur deux applications en simultané ou visionner des vidéos. Le laboratoire a mesuré une luminosité maximale de 521 cd/m², une valeur confortable pour conserver une excellente lisibilité même sous un éclairage direct en intérieur. La justesse d'affichage est aussi de la partie, avec une température des couleurs relevée à 6605 Kelvins, très proche de la norme idéale pour éviter les dérives bleutées, comme le confirme notre test complet.
Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+
Points forts
- Écran lumineux et bien calibré.
- Performances solides.
- Productivité optimisée.
- Sept ans de suivi logiciel.
Points faibles
- Qualité photo limitée.
- Charge assez lente.
- Pas de touchpad sur le clavier.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une autonomie solide mais une charge qui demande de la patience
Propulsée par sa puce Dimensity 9300+, l'ardoise offre une réactivité sans faille sous Android et bénéficie d'une autonomie mesurée à 14,6 heures par notre labo, ce qui assure une grosse journée d'usage sans passer par la prise. En revanche, le temps de recharge atteint 109 minutes, un délai assez long si vous devez récupérer rapidement de la batterie avant de partir. Le volet photo reste également en retrait, mais cette faiblesse ne gênera guère les utilisateurs qui réservent la tablette à la bureautique ou aux appels vidéo.
Apple iPad Mini (A20 Pro) : l'autre option face au Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+
L'Apple iPad Mini (A20 Pro) adopte une philosophie opposée : alors que le modèle de Samsung privilégie le confort d'un espace de travail de 12,4 pouces avec son stylet S Pen, la petite ardoise d'Apple mise sur une compacité maximale pour un usage ultra-nomade, désormais renforcée par une dalle Oled.
Les deux appareils s'affichent aujourd'hui au même tarif de 699,99 €, soit un écart de 0,00 €. L'iPad Mini (A20 Pro) décroche la note maximale de 5/5 pour sa portabilité absolue, mais la Samsung Galaxy Tab S10+, actuellement notée 4,5/5, offre une surface d'affichage bien plus généreuse pour travailler.
Apple iPad Mini (A20 Pro)
Points forts
- Écran lumineux et peu sujet aux reflets.
- Puce A20 Pro très puissante.
- Très bonne autonomie.
- Poids ultra-léger.
Points faibles
- Charge lente.
- Stockage de 128 Go en 2026.
- Taux de rafraîchissement limité à 60 Hz.

articles.title: “Si arranca y se mueve, no pasa nada”: la lógica que más llena los talleres, según un mecánico con 18 años de oficio
articles.text:
Aunque el coche parezca que ha empezado a dar tirones o pierde potencia, puede seguir siendo capaz de arrancar y circular. Además, si esto ocurre de forma recurrente, es fácil que se vuelva habitual. Por eso se puede asumir que es por los kilómetros. Posponer los mantenimientos tiene sus consecuencias, advierte Juande Rodríguez (mecánico con 18 años de experiencia).
“El error más caro es acostumbrarse a que el coche ya no va como antes”. Empezó en los talleres con 16 años. A los 20 abrió su propio negocio. En su currículum destacan ocho años de mecánica de competición. Deja claro que, aunque el coche siga siendo operativo, es importante actuar ante los primeros síntomas.
Por ejemplo, el color del humo que sale por el escape puede ser indicativo. Si tenemos pérdida de potencia y sale humo blanco o azulado, es posible que sea el turbo. También puede ir asociado a consumo de aceite. Es fundamental saber cuál es el origen.
El humo negro puede hacer referencia a problemas en la admisión. Por ejemplo, si el filtro de aire está tapado, no llega suficiente aire al motor. También puede haber pérdida de potencia sin humo. En este caso, la causa puede ser un sensor de admisión sucio o carbonilla.
Embrague y batería también tienen sus señales
Si al acelerar el motor gira más rápido, pero no aumenta la velocidad en la misma proporción, es posible que esté patinando el embrague. Es importante que, antes de que deje de transmitir fuerza a las ruedas, se revise. También es relevante revisarlo si el pedal está duro o cuesta enganchar marchas (por razones diferentes).
Otro elemento a revisar es el Start-Stop. Si no apaga el motor en las paradas, es posible que tenga que ver con el estado de la batería. También puede ser desactivado por la electrónica (cuando no se cumplan las condiciones necesarias para su funcionamiento). Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que haya una avería.
Además de los síntomas visuales, existen otros que podemos percibir auditivamente o por sensación. Por ejemplo, si aparecen vibraciones o los zumbidos aumentan con la velocidad, pueden deberse a problemas de suspensión, rodamientos o neumáticos. La vibración también puede deberse a los discos (si aparece al frenar). Es importante saber cuál es la causa. No siempre es por desgaste.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI earns $US3.8bn on its first day to make it the biggest entertainment release of all time
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI is officially the biggest entertainment release of all time after racking up $US3.8bn at the end of its first full day.
That’s $5.74bn in Australian dollars.
The game is projected to earn more than $US5bn
Rockstar Games pre-sold 32.5 million copies of the game ahead of its official launch last week which easily eclipsed the previous chapter, Grand Theft Auto V which earned $US1.5bn in its first 5 days of release.
The Grand Theft Auto VI haul in a single day is almost $US1bn more than the most successful movies of all time including Avengers: Endgame which has made $US2.943bn since it was released in 2019.
James Cameron’s Avatar released in 2009 has made $US2.924bn.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day, released earlier in 2026, has racked up $US2.524bn.
International sales data shows 75 per cent of GTA VI sales were for the PlayStation 5 with 25 per cent for Xbox.
Rockstar Games is reportedly developing a multiplayer expansion for Grand Theft Auto VI one with a PC version of the smash-hit game.

articles.title: GTA 6 : deux adolescents volent un bus pour faire comme dans leur jeu favori... et finissent dans le fossé
articles.text:
GTA 6 est vraiment l'événement du moment, avec une folie mondiale à la clé. Mais il ne donne pas que des bonnes idées à certains publics !
C'est déjà l'un des plus grands phénomènes de notre époque. Depuis sa sortie le 19 novembre dernier, GTA 6 a explosé les records de vente, avec 24 premières heures déjà historiques. On compte aussi à la fin du week-end près de 45 millions de ventes, pour des revenus générés d'environ 4 milliards de dollars. Autant dire que partout dans le monde on y joue, et que certains se sont peut-être laissés un peu trop influencer !
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Deux adolescents dégradent une dizaine de bus en dépôt avant d'en voler un autre
Des adolescents qui jouent à GTA 6, et qui souhaitent reproduire certains actions illégales dans la réalité ? C'est ce qui est arrivé dans la commune italienne de Rovigo, selon le quotidien La Stampa.
Deux mineurs se sont en effet introduits dans un dépôt de bus, dans la soirée, vers 23h. À l'intérieur, ils ont dégradé une dizaine de bus en y brisant les fenêtres, et en en faisant foncer plusieurs les uns sur les autres. Ils ont fini par voler l'un d'eux, et ont entamé une petite course qui a fini dans un fossé !
Les adolescents facilement retrouvés… puisqu'ils se filmaient !
Et pour ceux qui douteraient de l'influence de GTA 6 dans cette action insolite, il faut noter que les adolescents ont eu la grande intelligence de filmer leur forfait. Une intelligence telle qu'ils ont ensuite posté la vidéo directement sur les réseaux sociaux.
Et dans cette vidéo, ils ont fait référence à GTA 6, jeu bien connu pour ses détournements sauvages de véhicules roulants. Les deux jeunes sont dorénavant poursuivis pour vols, dégradation, entrave à un service public et conduite sans permis. Et dans la vraie vie, il n'y a pas la possibilité de relancer une nouvelle partie en liberté quand on est arrêté par la police !
Source : La Stampa

articles.title: Kein Kabelfrust zu Weihnachten: So machst du den Weihnachtsbaum smart
articles.text:
Kein Kabelfrust zu Weihnachten: So machst du den Weihnachtsbaum smart
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Den Tannenbaum zum Leuchten zu bringen, ist manchmal gar nicht so einfach. Zwar gibt es längst Lichterketten in allen möglichen Farben, das heißt aber nicht, dass die passende Steckdose immer gut erreichbar ist. Dann kann es auf Dauer nerven, den Stecker ein- und auszustöpseln. Es gibt aber auch Hersteller, die sich des Problems angenommen haben – etwa in Form smarter Lichterketten. Aber auch mit anderen Gadgets könnt ihr nicht nur Weihnachtsbaumbeleuchtung bequem mit dem Smartphone oder via Sprachbefehl an Siri, Alexa oder Gemini steuern.
Smarte Lichterketten von teuer bis günstig
Dabei kommt es natürlich darauf an, wie viel ihr für diesen Komfort ausgeben wollt. Am oberen Ende des Spektrums befindet sich etwa die Lichterkette Festavia von Philips Hue*. Die lässt sich über die App des Anbieters steuern. So ist etwa möglich, die Beleuchtung in drei Zonen einzuteilen, eigene Effekte zu erstellen oder die Lämpchen passend zur Musik auf Spotify leuchten zu lassen.
Grundsätzlich könnt ihr die Lichterkette per Bluetooth bedienen. Das volle Potenzial entfaltet sie aber erst in Verbindung mit der Hue-Bridge. Dann ist es möglich, sie mit anderen Lampen des Herstellers zu synchronisieren, in Szenen einzubinden und über Smarthome-Lautsprecher und -Displays zu steuern. Günstig ist die Festivia nicht. Online zahlt ihr derzeit rund 170 Euro für die 20 Meter lange Lichterkette. Die 40 Meter lange Ausgabe kostet 273 Euro.
Erschwinglicher sind die Govee Christmas String Lights 2* für rund 75 Euro. Diese Lichterkette lässt sich ebenfalls per Bluetooth steuern. Über die Govee-App habt ihr Zugriff auf 130 Szenen und einen KI-Assistenten, der die Beleuchtung nach euren Wünschen anpassen soll. Über das sogenannte Shape Mapping kann das System außerdem erkennen, wo sich welche LED am Baum befindet. Damit sollt ihr die Effekte optimieren können. Eine Musikerkennung ist ebenfalls integriert. Einziger Wermutstropfen: Um die Lichterkette ins Smarthome einzubinden und per Sprache steuern zu können, benötigt ihr einen Matter-fähigen Hub. Der ist allerdings schon vielen smarten Lautsprechern von Amazon, Apple oder Google eingebaut.
Eine dritte Alternative ist die smarte Lichterkette von Nanoleaf*, die ebenfalls diverse Szenen und animierte Farbverläufe bietet und auf Wunsch passend zur Musik leuchtet. Wie die anderen beiden Modelle könnt ihr das Exemplar von Nanoleaf per Bluetooth steuern. Alternativ ist die Einbindung ins Smarthome per Matter möglich. Auch hier braucht ihr dafür einen kompatiblen Hub. Zusätzlich könnt ihr die Lichterkette über ein integriertes Steuerelement am Kabel bedienen. Darüber lässt sie sich ein- und ausschalten. Einige vorprogrammierte Szenen könnt ihr auf diese Weise auch aktivieren. Die Nanoleaf-Lichterkette ist etwa bei Amazon für rund 66 Euro zu haben.
Smarte Steckdosen als günstige Alternative
Wollt ihr nicht gleich 100 Euro oder mehr in eine Lichterkette investieren, ist eine smarte Steckdose eine günstige Alternative. Die dient als Zwischenstück zwischen der normalen Steckdose und der Lichterkette. Der Vorteil: Ihr müsst eure bestehende normale Lichterkette nur einmal einstöpseln und könnt die Steckdose danach via Smartphone steuern. Bei Integration ins Hue- oder Samsung-Smarthings-System klappt es sogar über smarte Lautsprecher. Auf besondere Effekte müsst ihr dann zwar verzichten. Ihr erkauft euch über die Lösung aber etwas Komfort.
Und: Eine solche Steckdose muss im Vergleich zu den smarten Lichterketten gar nicht so teuer sein. Die Modelle aus der Tapo-Reihe von TP-Link starten etwa bei rund acht Euro* für die einzelne und 27 für die Mehrfachsteckdose*. Beide sind mit Alexa und Google kompatibel, unterstützen allerdings nur WLAN, aber kein Zigbee.
Habt ihr schon ein Smarthome-System, etwa von Philips Hue, solltet ihr darauf achten, dass die Steckdosen den Standard Zigbee unterstützen. Dann lassen sie sich einfach einbinden. Solche gibt es etwa von Hue selbst* für rund 27 Euro. Etwas günstiger (20 Euro) ist das Modell von Innr*, das aber auch mit dem Hue-System kompatibel ist.
Speziell für Apple-Nutzer:innen hat Eve mit dem Energy Strip* eine Mehrfachsteckdose im Angebot. Diese könnt ihr entweder über die App des Herstellers steuern oder sie in Homekit integrieren. Neben einem iPhone oder iPad braucht ihr dazu allerdings einen Homepod (Mini 2) oder ein Apple TV. Dazu kommt, dass die Steckleiste in der Regel um die 100 Euro kostet. Derzeit ist sie allerdings auf rund 70 Euro reduziert. Zusätzlich verzichtet Eve auf eine Cloud und die Registrierung in der App. Eure Daten bleiben also bei euch.

Capital Markets
Dangote considers selling his personal shares as refinery IPO demand surpasses supply
Aliko Dangote, the Nigerian billionaire and founder of the Dangote Group, is in talks with Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the country’s capital market regulator, about selling part of his personal stake in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, Bloomberg reported on November 19.
Explain like I’m new here: Dangote opened the refinery’s initial public offering (IPO) on September 14, offering investors a chance to own a piece of the business. The refinery initially offered about 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 ($0.40) per share, targeting ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion). However, applications reached ₦5.85 trillion ($4.3 billion), with nearly 4 million investors.
In the original IPO, investors were buying shares offered by the refinery. In a secondary sale, an existing shareholder sells some of the shares they already own.
The IPO also included an option to sell up to 30% more shares if demand justified it. Dangote currently owns about 87.3% of the refinery. After the original offer, his stake would fall to roughly 84.4%. If the full additional share option is used, it would drop further to about 83.6%. A separate sale of his personal shares could provide another way to accommodate demand without requiring the refinery to issue more shares.
What does this mean for investors? The proposed sale could give investors who applied for shares but received fewer than they requested another chance to buy into the refinery. However, the discussions do not mean the sale has been approved or that every investor who applied will receive the shares they requested. The SEC still has to review the proposal and approve the final allotment.

Funding
Baobab raises $50 million in bonds to expand small business lending in West Africa
Baobab, the microfinance group owned by Egypt’s Beltone Holding, has raised CFA 30 billion ($50.2 million) through two sustainability-linked bond issues in Côte d’Ivoire and Senegal. The group raised CFA20 billion ($33.5 million) in Côte d’Ivoire and CFA10 billion ($16.8 million) in Senegal. Both bonds mature in five years, with a one-year grace period before principal repayments begin.
Explain like I’m new here: Baobab is in the business of lending money to people and businesses that traditional banks may overlook. In 2025, Baobab had a €957 million loan portfolio and €555 million in customer deposits. It disbursed €1.2 billion in loans during the year and reported a net profit of €1.47 million. By raising CFA francs in the markets where it operates, Baobab would not have to rely on foreign-currency borrowing, which can cause a mismatch between the currency it borrows and the currency in which it lends.
A new chapter: The fundraising comes about ten months after Beltone completed its $197.6 million acquisition of Baobab in January 2026. The deal gave the Egyptian financial services group an established microfinance network across seven African countries, including Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Mali, Burkina Faso, Madagascar, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Nigeria.
What it means: African small businesses face an estimated $331 billion shortfall in financing. Baobab bets its microfinance model can serve some of these businesses. The new money could help it extend more loans, particularly to women-led enterprises, while supporting private education providers and green projects.
