articles.title: AI agents design new CPU architecture that's 4x more efficient than a conventional core, startup claims
articles.text:
Forward-looking: Brand-new CPU architectures are rare, since even designing a regular CPU core can take a large team of engineers years. However, a Palo Alto startup called Architect Labs now says its AI agents came up with one largely on their own, right down to the final chip layout. The company also claims its Frostbite design is over four times as efficient as a conventional core.
Humans did pick what the chip should be good at, selecting 25 test programs, ten of which the agents could use to tune their designs. Beyond that, the AIs had no starting design to build on, according to a research post the company published last week, so they started out by combing through research papers and benchmarks, then prototyped candidate designs as simple Python models.
They eventually landed on interaction nets, an idea introduced in 1990 that treats a program as a web of connected nodes. The program then runs by rewriting pairs of those nodes over and over. Those rewrites never get in each other's way, so lots of them can happen at once. That means the chip doesn't need complex hardware to hunt for work it can run in parallel.
The agents' first spec ran to 141 pages, but the team ended up deleting it. Once the first circuit design came in, many of its numbers turned out to be physically impossible. After that, swarms of agents pitched changes in parallel and tested each one against a fast software model of the whole chip.
Oddly enough, one feature nobody had asked for showed up along the way. The chip is split into small processing tiles, and idle ones pull work from busy neighbors. When no neighbor has any to spare, the idle tiles simply power down.
As for the payoff, a cluster of four Frostbite tiles was 4.59 times as efficient as a regular CPU core on average. But that average leans on the ten programs the agents tuned the design with. Those scored 6.02x on their own. On the 15 programs the agents never saw until the final test, the lead shrank to 3.83x.
The rival core is a modest one, too. Architect Labs won't name it for legal reasons. Still, it's a simple in-order design, much like the small cores phone chips use for light background tasks.
Nothing has been fabricated yet either, so every power figure comes from models rather than real silicon. Existing x86 or Arm software won't run on Frostbite at all. Instead, programs are written in Vine, a Rust-like language built by a Cambridge startup called Tendrils Compute.
By contrast, an AI agent from chip startup Verkor.io designed a RISC-V CPU in 12 hours earlier this year, but it used an existing instruction set that already had software. Next up, Architect Labs plans an FPGA-hosted playground where anyone can run programs on Frostbite.

articles.title: Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious
articles.text:
Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The company is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline.
“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the company’s 2026 sustainability report.
That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.
Such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line.
“We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch.
A few years ago, Meta was arguably one of the better corporate stewards of the climate. The company has been one of the largest purchasers of clean power, and it set ambitious goals for water conservation.
More recently, though, its multibillion-dollar bet on natural gas at its Hyperion data center in Louisiana has undone much of that progress. Natural gas may burn cleaner and more efficiently than coal, but its impact on global warming can be just as bad when the leaky infrastructure needed to burn it is factored in.
Despite years of clean power procurement, Meta’s greenhouse gas emissions have more than doubled in the last four years. Between 2024 and 2025, its data center emissions increased more than 12 times, and Hyperion isn’t online yet.
That commitment to natural gas led to the company’s departure from RE100, a corporate renewable energy initiative, in July. The company had been part of the group for a decade, though the two split after RE100 started requiring more rigorous reporting toward renewable energy targets.
“When we set our net zero emissions goal, we anticipated steady growth, falling clean energy costs, and changes in the broader system that would enable progress at the pace we envisioned,” they added. “The reality has been far more complex. Demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected, arriving on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades, and meeting it has meant building at a pace and scale the industry has never attempted.”
That’s all true, but when put that way, it sounds like Meta has little agency in the matter. But the company’s decision to chase AI was a conscious one.
You could argue that Meta has a fiduciary duty to chase after its peers, which have also dived headfirst into AI. But there’s precious little data to support the idea that AI will be a profit driver for a company like Meta, which is almost entirely consumer-focused.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg is optimistic that improving Muse’s energy efficiency will turn that around, but how much will everyday people be willing to pay for software that translates your offhand thoughts into surreal memes? Or monitors your emails so you won’t forget to reply to your mom? Meta is betting that it’ll be enough to support a $200 billion-plus data center, and probably more.
The choice of the fuel to power those AI ambitions was also a conscious one. Natural gas power plants, besides being able to run 24/7, are actually not a great fit for AI data centers. Turbines like to run at constant speeds, while AI data centers’ energy requirements surge and sag depending on the load. They need batteries as a buffer, which begs the question: Why not just connect to the grid and use batteries to bridge any gaps during times of peak demand? That’s what one expert recommends.
Meta’s bet on natural gas appears mistimed. Long-duration energy storage is coming into its own — and geothermal energy appears poised to become the next major power source on the grid in the U.S. Companies like Fervo, Mazama, and Quaise have been logging milestones at a rapid clip, potentially unlocking tens of gigawatts of capacity. The technology isn’t competitive with natural gas today, but it very well could be in the mid-2030s, just a few years after Meta completes Hyperion. Geothermal is also not vulnerable to supply chain shocks, like what happened with natural gas and the Iran War.
Beyond that, the company’s decision to abandon its 2030 net-zero goal risks fomenting the sort of backlash that leads to regulations with real teeth. Such regulations won’t just apply to Meta, and the broader industry would be justified in their frustration.
In that light, Meta’s timing couldn’t be worse. Surveys show the general public doesn’t hold AI or data centers in high esteem, rightly sensing that the infrastructure development is driving a rapid and often-unchecked expansion of polluting infrastructure.
The tech industry has spent over a decade trying to prove that it would be different from previous industrial juggernauts like oil and gas or automobile manufacturing. In a single PDF, Meta might have undone much of that goodwill. After this, who will trust another tech company’s voluntary net-zero goals?

articles.title: Lua hoje: confira a fase da Lua desta terça-feira 24/11/2026
articles.text:
Hoje, 24 de novembro de 2026, a Lua está no primeiro dia da fase cheia e 100% visível. Confira o calendário completo de fases da Lua deste mês, de acordo com o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet).
Confira as próximas fases
As fases da Lua no mês de novembro começam no dia 1º com a chegada da Lua Minguante, às 17h30 (horário de Brasília). Depois disso, dia 9, foi a vez da Lua Nova, que chegou às 4h02. A Lua Crescente surgiu às 8h48 do dia 17. Por fim, chegou a Lua Cheia, dia 24, às 11h55.
Leia mais:
- Entenda o que é a Lua, como e quando ela se formou
- Saiba como tirar a melhor foto possível com uma câmera de celular
- 7 dicas para fotografar a lua com seu celular
Calendário fases da Lua em novembro de 2026
- Lua Minguante: dia 1, às 17h30
- Lua Nova: dia 9, às 4h02
- Lua Crescente: dia 17, às 8h48
- Lua Cheia: dia 24, às 11h55
O que é o ciclo lunar?
Uma lunação ou ciclo lunar, como é chamado o intervalo de tempo entre luas novas, é sutilmente variável, com média de duração de 29,5 dias. Durante esse período, ela passa pelas quatro fases principais (nova, crescente, cheia e minguante), e cada uma se prolonga por aproximadamente sete dias.
Também existem as “interfases”: quarto crescente e crescente gibosa (entre as fases nova e cheia) e minguante gibosa e quarto minguante (entre a cheia e a minguante).
Entenda cada fase da Lua
Lua Nova
Na Lua Nova, o satélite se posiciona entre a Terra e o Sol. Isso faz com que o lado iluminado da Lua fique voltado para o Sol, enquanto o lado escuro fica voltado para nós. Por esse motivo, a Lua não é visível no céu noturno. Essa fase marca o início de um novo ciclo lunar e está relacionada ao recomeço e a novas possibilidades.
Lua Crescente
Depois da Lua Nova, surge a fase Crescente. Aos poucos, uma pequena faixa iluminada começa a aparecer no céu, aumentando noite após noite. No início, vemos apenas um fino arco de luz, mas com o passar dos dias a parte iluminada cresce até que metade da Lua esteja visível, momento chamado de Quarto Crescente. Essa fase simboliza crescimento, desenvolvimento e a construção de novos caminhos.
Lua Cheia
Na Lua Cheia, a Terra se encontra entre o Sol e a Lua. Isso permite que o lado lunar voltado para nós receba luz por completo, tornando-se totalmente visível e brilhante no céu. É o período de maior intensidade luminosa, quando a Lua nasce no horizonte exatamente no momento em que o Sol se põe. A Lua Cheia é associada à plenitude, ao auge de processos e à energia em seu ponto máximo.
Lua Minguante
Após a Lua Cheia, a luz da Lua começa a diminuir gradualmente. A cada noite, vemos menos da sua superfície iluminada. Quando apenas metade dela está visível, ocorre o Quarto Minguante, fase oposta ao Quarto Crescente. A Lua continua a perder luminosidade até chegar novamente à Lua Nova, reiniciando o ciclo. A fase Minguante simboliza reflexão, encerramento e preparação para novos começos.
Qual a fase da Lua hoje?
Hoje a Lua está na fase Cheia.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: GTA 6 para PC podría llegar antes de lo esperado por culpa de una filtración
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI tendrá una versión para PC hasta la primavera de 2027, pero eso no significa que habrá ports no oficiales. Una filtración de la versión de Xbox ha abierto la puerta para desarrollar recompilaciones del juego de Rockstar Games, las cuales se podrían ejecutar en PC. Un grupo de hackers compartió la pieza que hacía falta, por lo que ahora la pelota está en la cancha de los desarrolladores independientes.
De acuerdo con Videocardz, Cyberleek publicó el ejecutable de GTA 6 para Xbox, el único componente que hacía falta para completar la filtración de todo el juego. Este archivo permitiría a los desarrolladores descifrar cómo es el proceso de arranque o cómo interactúan los distintos sistemas que componen el juego. Sin el ejecutable, los proyectos solo podían analizar los recursos extraídos, como los gráficos, shaders o archivos de datos, pero trabajaban a ciegas.
Uno de los primeros proyectos que intenta llevar GTA 6 al PC es Leonida. Según el repositorio de GitHub, esta recompilación tiene como objetivo ejecutar el código del juego de forma nativa en Windows. Aunque la Xbox Series X|S y el PC comparten la arquitectura del CPU, el juego depende del hardware específico de la consola, por lo que estos juegos necesitan resolver estas dependencias.
Leonida se encuentra en una fase muy temprana de desarrollo y el juego todavía no arranca. Los desarrolladores han conseguido implementar muchas de las herramientas que se necesitan para analizar archivos, exportar recursos y preparar la infraestructura. El repositorio menciona que han conseguido exportar los modelos 3D, texturas, audio y shaders, pero todavía faltan las piezas más importantes, como la capa que traduce Direct3D 12 de Xbox a Vulkan, el soporte de ray tracing y más.
La IA ayudará a que GTA 6 llegue a PC antes de tiempo
Una de las características de estas recompilaciones es el uso de la inteligencia artificial para ayudar en el desarrollo. A diferencia de los proyectos de recompilaciones que veíamos hace tres o cuatro años, la IA ha avanzado tanto que ya permite acelerar la traducción de shaders, depuración de errores o asistir en las tareas de ingeniería inversa. El lanzamiento de GPT-6 Astra y Claude Opus 5.5 hace unos meses dio pie a una oleada de recompilaciones de juegos que hasta ahora se mantenían exclusivos de consola.
El siguiente reto será llevar GTA 6 a PC antes de que salga la versión oficial durante el primer trimestre de 2027. Con el acceso al ejecutable filtrado, los desarrolladores podrán acelerar el desarrollo apoyándose en la IA, aunque tendrán que resolver todos los inconvenientes que conlleva una recompilación, como reimplementar partes del sistema de la consola y asegurarse de que el rendimiento es estable.
Antes de emocionarse, hay que entender que una recompilación de GTA 6 no llegará de inmediato y, de hacerlo, no ofrecería todas las ventajas de la versión oficial. A diferencia de la recompilación, que intenta adaptar el código original de consola, la versión nativa de PC llegaría con soporte completo para el hardware, incluida una configuración avanzada para las tarjetas gráficas o el soporte para mods.
Otro detalle es que Take-Two no se va a quedar de brazos cruzados y es probable que los abogados de la compañía se encarguen de matar cualquier intento de llevar GTA 6 al PC antes que ellos.

articles.title: Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
articles.text:
Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.”
Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
Kagi Mail is launching in public beta with a 60-day free trial.
With Kagi Mail, you get an @kagimail.com address, but the service also supports unlimited aliases and domains. It also offers 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. On the roadmap, you can expect contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, but native mobile apps aren’t expected to arrive until Q3 2027.
“Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once,” Kagi says. “There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way.”
Kagi Mail is available now with a 60-day free trial before you have to pay $99 per year. The service is available as part of a $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription.

articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.text:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.
When the complete link was simulated, the outcomes diverged after transmission over 150 meters: the 850 nm channel exhibited better performance compared to the 910 nm channel. By examining the performance of both channels in back-to-back, it is concluded that the difference in performance results from the impairments of the multimode fiber.
System-level simulation of the 850 nm and 910 nm channels after 150 m reveals different transmission performance despite comparable VCSEL modulation bandwidths.
The study found that fiber bandwidth metrics alone did not fully predict system performance. Instead, link quality depended on interactions among:
- VCSEL mode structure
- modal dispersion
- chromatic dispersion
- fiber differential modal delay (DMD)
- wavelength-dependent behavior
That’s an important distinction.
A component-level metric describes an important part of the design, but not necessarily what happens when that component interacts with other components in a link.
For a short-reach optical link, the transmitter, launch conditions, fiber, modal behavior, and receiver all contribute to the final result.
Studying system-level performance reveals the limitations of the system and helps determine the maximum transmission distance, the optimum launch power, and the appropriate driving conditions. Moreover, it enables the prediction of system performance at higher data rates using the same components. These findings may feed back into component design, for example by motivating efforts to extend the bandwidth limitations of the VCSEL. As a result, the design process becomes iterative, progressing from component design to system design and then back to component optimization. This interdependence highlights the need for integrated design tools.
The VCSEL example illustrates a broader challenge in photonic engineering.
At the device level, engineers need an accurate representation of optical and physical behavior.
At the component level, they need to understand how devices work together.
At the system level, the question changes again:
Does the completed design deliver the required performance in its target application?
In the VPIphotonics framework described in the study, an optical link is constructed from parameterized building blocks including lasers, couplers, fibers, photodetectors, filters, receiver blocks, and analysis tools.
That allows the engineer to move beyond “Does this component meet specification?” to “How does this component affect the performance of the complete system?”
Consider the VCSEL-to-fiber interface.
Launch conditions influence which fiber modes are excited. In the VPIphotonics model, coupling between the VCSEL and fiber can account for factors including lateral offset, angular tilt, longitudinal spacing, coupling losses, and the modal fields of the two devices.
The fiber introduces additional considerations, including modal field distributions, effective indices, DMD, chromatic dispersion, attenuation, group delay, and mode coupling.
None of those effects exist independently in the operating link. The engineering value comes from understanding how they combine to influence system-level outcomes.
For the multimode-link application, the VPIphotonics framework includes virtual test benches for measurements such as:
- Differential Modal Delay (DMD)
- Effective Modal Bandwidth Calculated (EMBc)
- Encircled Flux (EF)
The study also evaluates complete-system outputs including eye diagrams and symbol error rate.
This creates a useful connection between simulated component behavior and the measurements engineers use to evaluate the finished link.
For the 850/910 nm example, that system context exposed performance differences that VCSEL bandwidth metrics by themselves did not predict.
At what level do I need to simulate my design to answer the question I am trying to solve?
Detailed device simulation remains important when the problem is the physical behavior of the photonic component.
Component- or circuit-level simulation becomes important when individual devices interact together to perform some function within a single component.
System-level simulation adds the application context needed to investigate how components and circuits affect the performance of the complete optical system.
These are different views of the same engineering problem.
With VPIphotonics now part of Keysight, the broader opportunity is to look at photonic design across multiple levels of abstraction.
The goal is not simply to apply more simulation. It is to use the appropriate level of abstraction for each engineering question and understand how decisions made at one level influence performance at another.
The 850/910 nm example illustrates why that matters. Comparable component metrics did not result in identical link behavior. The difference became clear when interactions among the VCSELs, launch conditions, fiber characteristics, and receiver were evaluated at the system level.
As photonic systems grow more complex, that system context can become increasingly important for making informed design decisions before committing to hardware.
By linking component design directly to system performance, engineers can work from application requirements rather than isolated device metrics. This closes the loop between system architects and component designers, leading to faster development cycles, more efficient trade-offs, and solutions that are optimized for real-world deployment.

articles.title: Phishing, Ransomware, Zero-Day – 23 Begriffe einfach erklärt
articles.text:
Cybersicherheit: 23 Begriffe von Phishing bis Zero-Day erklärt
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Das Bundeskriminalamt hat 2024 insgesamt 131.391 Fälle von Cyber-Kriminalität erfasst. Hinzu kommen aber noch einmal mehr als 200.000 Fälle, die vom Ausland oder von einem unbekannten Ort ausgeführt wurden. Die Zahlen zeigen, wie groß das Problem mittlerweile ist.
Weil Cyber-Sicherheit sowohl unser Privatleben, als auch unsere Arbeit betrifft, wollen wir euch im Folgenden die wichtigsten Begriffe erklären. So könnt ihr Warnungen und Meldungen in Zukunft hoffentlich besser verstehen und im Notfall auch eure eigenen Daten besser vor Angriffen schützen.
Advanced Persistent Threat (APT)
Als Advanced Persistent Threat – also: fortgeschrittene, andauernde Bedrohung – werden Gruppen bezeichnet, die sich durch teils komplexe und zeitaufwendige Methoden Zugriff auf Computernetzwerke verschaffen, um dort möglichst lange unentdeckt agieren zu können.
Aufgrund des hohen Aufwands sind ATP mittlerweile häufig staatlich unterstützte Gruppen, die etwa Wirtschaftsspionage betrieben. So hat etwa die Gruppe Salt Typhon 2024 die Netzwerke mehrerer US-amerikanischer Internet-Anbieter infiltriert und Nutzer:innen-Daten erbeutet. Expert:innen vermuten, dass die Gruppe vom chinesischen Ministerium für Staatssicherheit betrieben wird.
Ein anderes bekanntes Beispiel ist die Lazarus Gruppe. Die soll Teil des nordkoreanischen Geheimdienstes sein. Im Gegensatz zu vergleichbaren Gruppen aus anderen Ländern hat sich Lazarus allerdings weniger auf Spionage und mehr auf konkrete Geldbeschaffung für das Regime spezialisiert. So werden ihr etwa Krypto-Diebstähle und Ransomware-Kampagnen zugeschrieben.
Air Gap
Air Gap ist Englisch für Luftspalt. Im Cyber-Security-Kontext sind damit Computer gemeint, die nicht mit dem Internet oder anderen Netzwerken verbunden sind. Daten oder Systemupdates können bei einem solchen System nur durch physische Datenträger eingespielt werden. Damit sollen ein Abfluss besonders sensibler Daten sowie Angriffe von außen verhindert werden.
Ganz ausgeschlossen werden kann ein Angriff aber auch hier nicht, wie das Beispiel Stuxnet zeigt. Dabei handelte es sich um einen Computerwurm, der im Juni 2010 entdeckt wurde. Über bis dato unbekannte Sicherheitslücken verbreitete er sich über Wechseldatenträger. Expert:innen vermuten, dass der Wurm speziell dazu konzipiert wurde, von der Außenwelt abgeschirmte Systeme in iranischen Atomanlagen zu sabotieren.
Botnet
Als Botnet wird eine Ansammlung von Rechnern bezeichnet, auf denen eine Schadsoftware läuft. Die sogenannten Bots, die das Netzwerk ausmachen, werden meist von außen kontrolliert und dann etwa genutzt, um gemeinsam DDoS-Angriffe aufzuführen oder große Mengen Spam– oder Phishing-Mails zu versenden.
Eines der größten bekannten Botnets war das im November 2010 von niederländischen Strafverfolgungsbehörden abgeschaltete Bredolab-Botnet. Das soll aus mindestens 30 Millionen infizierten Geräten weltweit bestanden haben. Der Betreiber hatte sein Botnet an Cyber-Kriminelle vermietet. 2012 wurde der damals 27-jährige Russe in Armenien zu vier Jahren Haft verurteilt.
Brute-Force-Methode
Bei einem Brute-Force-Angriff werden automatisiert alle erdenklichen Passwortkombinationen ausprobiert, um sich so Zugriff auf einen Account zu verschaffen. Die Methode ist allerdings nur bei sehr kurzen und einfachen Passwörtern effektiv. Je länger und komplexer euer Passwort ist, desto geringer die Aussichten, dass sich mit dieser Methode wirklich die richtige Kombination finden lässt.
Datenleck
Als Datenleck wird das versehentliche Offenlegen oder auch der Diebstahl von sensiblen Daten bezeichnet. Gemeint sind damit vor allem personenbezogene Informationen wie Namen, Adressen, E-Mail-Adressen oder Telefonnummern.
Eines der größten Datenlecks der Geschichte fand zwischen 2013 und 2014 statt. Damals erbeuteten kriminelle Hacker rund drei Milliarden Nutzer:innen-Daten von Yahoo.
Wer wissen möchte, ob eigene Daten im Rahmen eines Datenlecks öffentlich geworden sind, der kann dazu die Website Have I been pwned von dem australischen Security-Experten Troy Hunt benutzen.
Distributed-Denial-of-Service-Angriff (DDoS-Angriff)
Bei einer Denial-of-Service-Attacke wird das Ziel mit so vielen Anfragen überlastet, dass es irgendwann zusammenbricht. Auf die Art können Angreifer:innen etwa Websites unerreichbar machen. Der Zusatz Distributed – also verteilt – meint in dem Kontext, dass der Angriff nicht von einem Computer, sondern von einer Vielzahl von Rechnern ausgeführt wird. Auf die Art wird es für das Opfer schwieriger, den eingehenden Traffic zu blockieren. Heute werden DDoS-Angriffe meist von Botnets ausgeführt.
Exploit
Als Exploit wird eine Methode oder Software-Code bezeichnet, mit dem sich eine bestehende Sicherheitslücke konkret ausnutzen lässt. Während also eine Sicherheitslücke erst mal nur eine theoretische Möglichkeit darstellt, ein System anzugreifen, ist der Exploit der praktische Beleg dafür, dass das auch funktioniert.
Exploits werden zum einen von Kriminellen entwickelt. Zum anderen aber auch von Sicherheitsexpert:innen, die damit auf die Gefahr der Lücke hinweisen oder dem betroffenen Hersteller:in die Möglichkeit geben wollen, schneller einen Patch zu entwickeln.
Firewall
Eine Firewall – zu Deutsch: Brandmauer – ist ein System, mit dem Zugriff auf ein Netzwerk oder einen einzelnen Computer eingeschränkt werden kann. Damit wird etwa der Zugriff auf Dienste begrenzt oder ganz abgestellt, die von den Nutzer:innen nicht verwendet werden, um so etwaige Angriffe auf diesem Weg auszuschließen.
Sowohl macOS als auch Windows kommen heutzutage mit eigener Firewall-Software. Allerdings ist die Firewall bei Apple standardmäßig deaktiviert, bei Microsoft hingegen angeschaltet. Auch Internet-Router wie die Fritzbox verfügen über eine integrierte Firewall, mit der das Heimnetz vor Angriffen aus dem Internet geschützt wird.
Keylogger
Als Keylogger wird eine Lösung verstanden, mit der die Tastatureingaben von Nutzer:innen aufgezeichnet werden. Das kann in Form einer Software passieren oder auch mithilfe von Hardware, die zwischen Computer und Tastatur angeschlossen wird. Mit einem Keylogger können etwa Login-Daten abgefangen werden.
Malware
Malware steht für Malicious Software – also bösartige Software. Gemeint ist jede Art von Software, die für die eigentlichen Besitzer:innen des Systems einen Nachteil darstellen würde. Dementsprechend fallen sowohl Viren als auch Würmer oder Trojaner unter den Sammelbegriff Malware.
Patch
Als Patch werden Ausbesserungen an Software bezeichnet, mit denen bestehende Fehler behoben werden. Wenn es sich bei dem Fehler um eine Sicherheitslücke handelt, wird bisweilen auch konkret von einem Sicherheits-Patch gesprochen.
Wenn eine von euch genutzte Software eine bekannte Sicherheitslücke aufweist und der Hersteller einen Patch dafür anbietet, solltet ihr den schnellstmöglich installieren.
Phishing
Beim Phishing handelt es sich um eine Betrugsmasche, mit der Angreifer:innen versuchen, an Login-Daten und andere sensible Informationen zu gelangen. Das Ganze funktioniert meist über gefälschte E-Mails oder Websites. Die Angreifer:innen geben sich dann etwa als eure Bank oder einen Onlineshop aus, um eure Anmeldedaten für genau diese Dienste zu erhalten.
Ransomware
Ransomware ist ein Kofferwort, das aus den Bestandteilen Ransom (englisch für Lösegeld) und Software besteht. Gemeint ist damit eine Schadsoftware, die den Inhalt von Festplatten verschlüsselt. Wer seine eigenen Daten wieder entschlüsseln will, der muss den Angreifer:innen ein Lösegeld bezahlen.
Ransomware-Angriffe haben in den vergangenen Jahren immer weiter zugenommen. Ransomware-Gruppen nehmen neben Einzelpersonen auch immer wieder ganze Unternehmen ins Visier, um so Millionenbeträge zu erpressen.
Laut einer Prognose von Cybersecurity Ventures könnten Ransomware-Gruppen 2025 weltweite Schäden in Höhe von 57 Milliarden US-Dollar verursachen. Auf das Jahr umgelegt wären das 156 Millionen Dollar pro Tag oder 1,1 Milliarde Dollar wöchentlich.
Sicherheitslücke
Als Sicherheitslücke wird eine Schwachstelle in Software oder Hardware bezeichnet, die Angreifer:innen ermöglicht, unbefugt auf ein System zuzugreifen. Dazu bedienen sich die Angreifer:innen eines sogenannten Exploits.
Social Engineering
Egal wie gut es aus technischer Perspektive um die Sicherheit eines Systems bestellt ist, am Ende arbeiten damit immer Menschen – und die können manipuliert werden. Genau darum geht es beim Social Engineering. Hier werden Mitarbeiter:innen von Unternehmen gezielt ausgetrickst, um sich etwa Zugriff auf eigentlich sichere Systeme zu verschaffen.
Angreifer:innen geben sich beim Social Engineering etwa am Telefon als Kolleg:innen aus, die dringend Hilfe benötigen. So nutzen die Angreifer:innen die Hilfsbereitschaft der meisten Menschen aus.
Lesetipp: Wer sich dafür interessiert, findet in dem Buch Die Kunst der Täuschung* des Hackers und Cyber-Security-Beraters Kevin Mitnick eine ganze Reihe von faszinierenden Beispielen dafür, wie Social Engineering in der Praxis aussehen kann.
Spam
Unter dem Begriff Spam verstehen wir den massenhaften Versand von ungewollten Nachrichten – meist per E-Mail. Während ein Großteil des Spams vermutlich „nur“ ungewollte Werbung ist, wird der massenhafte Versand von Nachrichten auch zur Verbreitung von Malware genutzt. Auch werden häufig Botnets für den Versand von Spam genutzt. Die Mail-Adressen der Opfer stammen wiederum häufig aus verschiedenen Datenlecks.
Spoofing
Spoofing bezeichnet eine Reihe von Methoden, mit denen Angreifer:innen ihre wahre Identität verschleiern können. Also beispielsweise ihre IP, Mail-Adresse oder Telefonnummer. Auf die Art wirken sie unter Umständen vertrauenswürdiger und werden nicht sofort von etwaig bestehenden Schutzmechanismen erkannt.
Spyware
Der Begriff Spyware setzt sich aus den englischen Wörtern Spy (Spion) und Software zusammen. Entsprechend versteht man darunter Malware, mit der einzelne Systeme ausspioniert werden können. Im Gegensatz zu einem simplen Keylogger können mit einer Spyware die gesamte Arbeit einer Person und deren Daten aus der Ferne ausspioniert werden. Auch Änderungen an dem System sind denkbar.
Trojaner
Als Trojaner werden in Anspielung auf das Trojanische Pferd aus der griechischen Mythologie Malware-Programme bezeichnet, die zunächst harmlos erscheinen und als sinnvolle Programme getarnt sind.
Virus
Als Virus wird eine Malware bezeichnet, die sich dauerhaft in einem System oder bestimmten Dateien einnistet – genau wie das biologische Vorbild. Im Gegensatz zu Würmern verbreiten sich Viren zwar aktiv auf einem einmal infizierten System, sie suchen sich aber selbst keine neuen Opfer.
Wurm
Wie der Virus dient auch der Wurm dazu, sich möglichst weit zu verbreiten. Er nistet sich dazu aber nicht in fremden Dateien ein, sondern verbreitet sich selbst aktiv, etwa in einem lokalen Netzwerk oder per E-Mail.
Zero-Click
Da moderne Betriebssysteme mit einer Vielzahl an Sicherheitsmechanismen ausgestattet sind, ist Malware in den meisten Fällen darauf angewiesen, dass Nutzer:innen selbst aktiv werden und etwa ein Programm öffnen oder einen Warnhinweis wegklicken. Bei sogenannten Zero-Click-Exploits ist das nicht notwendig. Schon der Besuch einer Website oder der Abruf einer E-Mail könnte in dem Fall ausreichen, um einen Angriff zu starten.
Sollte ein von euch genutztes Programm eine Zero-Click-Sicherheitslücke aufweisen, solltet ihr daher sofort prüfen, ob es einen Patch dafür gibt. Falls das noch nicht der Fall ist, solltet ihr sicherheitshalber davon absehen, das Programm zu verwenden.
Zero-Day
Als Zero-Day-Sicherheitslücken werden Schwachstellen in Soft- oder Hardware bezeichnet, die dem Hersteller noch nicht bekannt sind. Entsprechend kann es für diese Sicherheitslücke auch noch keinen Patch geben.
Weil es gegen die noch nicht bekannten Lücken auch keinen Schutz geben kann, hat sich ein lukrativer Schwarzmarkt für Zero-Day-Lücken entwickelt. Neben Kriminellen sollen auch Geheimdienste Zero-Day-Lücken ankaufen, um sie für gezielte Angriffe zu nutzen.
Hersteller von betroffener Software wiederum bieten sogenannte Bug-Bounty-Programme an, bei denen Hacker eine finanzielle Entschädigung erhalten, wenn sie die Zero-Day-Lücken gegenüber dem Unternehmen offenlegen, statt sie auf dem Schwarzmarkt zu verkaufen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 21.09.2025 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
)) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Le Scuba X1 perd 550 € chez Aiper : quatre robots de piscine en promo
articles.text:
Le Black Friday 2026 est l’occasion de s’équiper pour l’été prochain sans se ruiner ! Jusqu’au 30 novembre, Aiper propose des réductions sur plusieurs de ses robots de piscine. Mais lequel choisir selon son bassin et ses besoins ? Voici les offres à ne pas manquer.
C’est souvent hors saison que l’on fait les meilleures affaires sur les équipements de piscine ! Et ce Black Friday 2026 en est la preuve : Aiper propose de jolies remises sur plusieurs de ses robots nettoyeurs. Reste à choisir le bon modèle, car tous ne répondent pas aux mêmes besoins.
Black Friday Aiper : jusqu’au 30 novembre
Un point commun à tous ces robots ? Ils sont là pour vous simplifier la vie ! Fini les longues séances de nettoyage manuel… ils prennent en charge une bonne partie de l’entretien de votre piscine :
- Aiper Scuba S1 (2026) : 499,99 € au lieu de 549 €, soit 9 % de réduction ;
- Aiper Scuba V3 : 849 € au lieu de 899 €, soit 6 % de réduction ;
- Aiper EcoSurfer S2 : 379 € au lieu de 399 €, soit 5 % de réduction ;
- Aiper Scuba X1 : 749 € au lieu de 1 299€, soit 42 % de réduction.
Aiper Scuba S1 (2026) : nettoyer sa piscine sans se ruiner
Pas besoin de dépenser une fortune pour s’offrir un robot de piscine efficace… Surtout pendant le Black Friday !
Le Scuba S1 (2026) gère non seulement les saletés au fond du bassin, mais aussi les parois et la ligne d’eau. Ses chenilles lui assurent une bonne adhérence pour se déplacer, y compris à la verticale. Quant à la technologie WavePath 2.0, elle adapte les trajectoires et limite les passages inutiles pour couvrir un maximum de surface.
Côté autonomie, le robot peut fonctionner jusqu’à 180 minutes en utilisation standard et atteindre 240 minutes en mode Éco, de quoi s’occuper des piscines allant jusqu'à 150 m².
Son débit d’aspiration de 15 900 L/h s’accompagne d’un panier filtrant de 180 microns et d’un filtre ultrafin MicroMesh de 3 microns, pour retenir aussi bien les gros débris que les particules les plus fines.
Le Scuba S1 (2026) propose cinq modes de nettoyage : Auto, Fond, Parois, Éco et Programmation. L’application Aiper permet de sélectionner les programmes et de personnaliser les cycles selon les besoins de la piscine.
Les points forts du Scuba S1 (2026) :
- WavePath 2.0 : navigation optimisée ;
- Aspiration de 15 900 L/h ;
- Double système de filtration ;
- Nettoyage des piscines jusqu'à 150 m² ;
- Cinq modes de nettoyage.
Aiper Scuba V3 (2026) : un robot IA pour les piscines complexes
Le Scuba V3 (2026) mise sur l’intelligence artificielle pour détecter les saletés, optimiser ses déplacements et automatiser le nettoyage du fond, des parois et de la ligne d’eau.
Grâce à sa caméra frontale associée à des capteurs ToF, le robot reconnaît plus de 20 types de débris et repère les zones les plus sales, puis adapte ses trajectoires pour éviter les passages inutiles. La technologie JetAssist améliore quant à elle le nettoyage horizontal de la ligne d’eau.
Le mode AI Navium planifie les cycles de nettoyage en fonction des caractéristiques du bassin et de l’historique d’entretien. Le Scuba V3 dispose en outre d’un éclairage LED, qui lui permet de travailler lorsque la luminosité est faible, ainsi que d’une station de recharge sans fil.
Les points forts du Scuba V3 (2026) :
- AI VisionPath : reconnaissance de plus de 20 types de débris ;
- JetAssist : nettoyage de la ligne d’eau ;
- AI Navium : planification intelligente des cycles ;
- Éclairage LED et station de recharge sans fil.
Aiper EcoSurfer S2 : un skimmer solaire qui ne laisse rien flotter
Contrairement aux autres modèles de cette sélection, l'EcoSurfer S2 ne descend jamais au fond du bassin. Ce robot skimmer reste à la surface pour intercepter les feuilles, les insectes et le pollen avant qu'ils ne coulent et ne finissent par encrasser la piscine. Son système DebrisGuard empêche les débris récupérés de ressortir de son panier de 4 litres, tandis que son filtre de 150 microns retient aussi les plus petites impuretés flottantes.
Recouvert d'un large panneau solaire, il s'appuie sur la technologie SolarSeeker, qui l'oriente vers les zones ensoleillées du bassin pour optimiser sa recharge et lui permet de fonctionner en continu tant que le soleil brille. Quand le ciel se couvre, sa batterie prend le relais et offre jusqu'à 35 heures d'autonomie après une recharge sur secteur.
Ses capteurs optiques l'aident à contourner les obstacles, et l'application Aiper permet de le lancer, de l'arrêter ou de vérifier son niveau de batterie sans avoir à le sortir de l'eau. Il intègre également un compartiment à pastilles de chlore, qui diffuse le produit dans le bassin au fil de ses déplacements.
Les points forts de l'Aiper EcoSurfer S2 :
- Nettoyage de la surface en continu grâce à la recharge solaire ;
- SolarSeeker : recherche automatique des zones ensoleillées ;
- DebrisGuard et panier de 4 litres ;
- Jusqu'à 35 heures d'autonomie sur batterie ;
- Compartiment à pastilles de chlore intégré.
Aiper Scuba X1 : un robot de piscine puissant avec filtration ultrafine
Le Scuba X1 mise sur la puissance de son aspiration et la précision de son nettoyage pour se démarquer.
Avec un débit d’aspiration pouvant atteindre 25 200 litres par heure, le Scuba X1 récupère aussi bien les feuilles que le sable et les poussières. Son système de filtration MicroMesh de 3 microns retient les particules les plus fines, tandis que son panier de 5 litres limite les allers-retours pour le vider. La technologie WaveLine 2.0 se révèle quant à elle précieuse pour nettoyer la ligne d’eau et éliminer les dépôts qui s’y accumulent.
Le Scuba X1 s’appuie sur WavePath 3.0 et sur les capteurs ultrasoniques OmniSense pour optimiser ses déplacements et contourner les obstacles. Il offre jusqu’à 180 minutes d’autonomie et propose cinq modes de nettoyage, à choisir selon les besoins du bassin.
Les points forts du Scuba X1 :
- Aspiration de 25 200 L/h ;
- Filtration MicroMesh de 3 µm ;
- Nettoyage de la ligne d’eau avec WaveLine 2.0 ;
- Navigation optimisée et détection des obstacles.
Quel robot de piscine Aiper choisir pour le Black Friday 2026 ?
Petit budget, piscine aux formes complexes ou bassin entouré d’arbres : à chaque besoin son robot de piscine.
Aiper Scuba S1 (2026) : le meilleur choix à moins de 500 €
Il nettoie le fond, les parois et la ligne d’eau. Ajoutez à cela une filtration efficace et une autonomie généreuse permettant de couvrir jusqu’à 150 m².
Aiper Scuba V3 : le robot pour les piscines complexes
Sa caméra et son intelligence artificielle lui permettent de repérer les débris et d’adapter son parcours pour insister sur les zones les plus sales. Le mode Cognitive AI Navium se charge d’organiser les cycles de nettoyage en tenant compte des caractéristiques de la piscine et des nettoyages précédents.
Aiper EcoSurfer S2 : lorsque la piscine est entourée d'arbres
Ce robot de surface alimenté par l'énergie solaire collecte les feuilles, les insectes et les autres débris flottants avant qu'ils ne tombent au fond du bassin. Il travaille en continu dès que le soleil est au rendez-vous et complète très bien l'un des robots Scuba de cette sélection.
Aiper Scuba X1 : quand on veut ce qui se fait de mieux
Avec son débit d’aspiration de 25 200 L/h et son filtre ultrafin MicroMesh de 3 microns, le Scuba X1 s’attaque aussi bien aux gros débris qu’aux poussières les plus fines. Sa technologie WaveLine 2.0 assure quant à elle un nettoyage horizontal de la ligne d’eau, tandis que WavePath 3.0 optimise ses déplacements dans le bassin.

articles.title: Her Startup selects 12 women-led startups for 2nd accelerator cohort
articles.text:
Women-focused accelerator Her Startup has selected 12 tech startups from seven African countries for its second cohort.
Her Startup is backed by KSH Foundation, Tomorrow Foundation and EHA Impact Ventures, and is this year running the programme with Founder Institute Morocco.
After receiving 468 applications from 33 countries, more than double the number for its first edition, 20 founders were shortlisted, and the accelerator increased its intake from 10 to 12. The selected startups get Founder Institute training, startup capital through convertible revenue-based financing, and six months of mentorship.
Half the cohort comes from Nigeria, namely Kadosh Mechatronics, which makes solar-powered greenhouse sensors; FriendnPal, an AI-powered mental health platform; Glorious Farmgate, a poultry automation startup; Fuse Varsity, an ed-tech company; Odnaworld, an agrifood firm; and TESA Global Solutions, a media-tech company.
The other six startups are SAB Biomanufactures (Tanzania), which turns brown seaweed into products for agriculture and food preservation; Uptech Africa (Malawi), an agri-tech marketplace; AEN Holdings (Uganda), which repurposes used batteries; EON (Ethiopia), a plastics recycler; Dosy (Egypt), a micromobility platform for women; and UNTUM Recycling (South Africa).
“The selected founders can look forward to an intensive and transformative journey combining mentorship, practical insights, expert guidance and access to a valuable entrepreneurial network,” said Youssef Koun and Hicham Sentissi, who lead the Founder Institute Morocco chapter.

articles.title: Spanish LaLiga confirms hackers stole soccer fans’ personal data
articles.text:
LaLiga, Spain's top men's professional football league, disclosed a data breach that exposed personal information belonging to users of its services and those of some affiliated clubs.
According to the organization, the incident occurred between November 14 and 16, and the attacker extracted data from compromised systems.
LaLiga organizes Spain’s top two men’s professional football divisions.
The top league is one of the world’s most prominent football leagues, where clubs with a global audience, such as Real Madrid, FC Barcelona, and Atlético Madrid, play.
On November 16, the organization’s security team identified the source of the unauthorized access and implemented measures to block the attack and stop the data extraction.
“LALIGA was the target of a cyberattack on one of its technology platforms for fan services,” reads the announcement.
“Between November 14 and 16, a cybercriminal gained unauthorized access to the platform and extracted personal data belonging to users registered for digital services offered by LALIGA and some clubs.”
LaLiga underlined that the incident was confined to a specific platform and did not extend to other systems that support the running of the competitions.
After implementing containment measures, LaLiga launched an investigation to determine the scope of the incident and introduced more thorough monitoring to detect future attempts to breach its systems.
The football organizer also reported the incident to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) and filed a complaint with the National Police’s Central Cybercrime Unit.
Impacted clubs were also directly notified, and actions to inform impacted fans are being coordinated.
At the time of writing, no ransomware group has claimed responsibility for the attack on LaLiga.
BleepingComputer has contacted the organization to learn more about the attack and which clubs were impacted, but we have not received a response as of publication.

articles.title: Le MacBook Neo 2 arriverait en mars, avec la mise à jour qu’on attend tous
articles.text:
Dès son premier modèle, le MacBook Neo d’Apple a réussi à se positionner comme un des PC portables avec le meilleur rapport qualité-prix du marché. Selon le toujours bien informé Mark Gurman de Bloomberg, le constructeur américain souhaiterait désormais renouveler son ordinateur d’entrée de gamme tous les ans. Ciblant la fenêtre de mise à jour iOS 27.4 entre février et mars, cette seconde version n’arriverait pas seule. Apple travaillerait en effet dans le même temps sur un iPad d’entrée de gamme équipé à la puce A19, ainsi que sur les iPhone 18 et 18e.
Une nouvelle puce et plus de RAM pour le MacBook Neo 2
Cette deuxième version du MacBook Neo passerait ainsi à la puce A19 Pro, contre l’A18 Pro pour le modèle actuel. Cela reste malgré tout une puce de retard par rapport à l’iPhone 18 Pro ou l’iPad mini 2026. Mais la principale évolution se situerait au niveau de la mémoire vive, qui grimperait de 8 Go à 12 Go de mémoire unifiée. Pour ceux qui font pas mal de multitâche ou qui utilisent des logiciels gourmands, ce gain de RAM serait loin d’être négligeable.
La marque envisagerait aussi de renouveler fréquemment les coloris du MacBook Neo. On ne sait pas encore sur quelle fréquence, mais le fait de retrouver des couleurs qui ne sont tout simplement pas présentes sur les MacBook Air et MacBook Pro est un argument à ne pas sous-estimer. Côté calendrier, d’autres appareils comme l’iPhone Air 2 et un nouvel iPad Pro seraient également prévus durant la première moitié de l’année, mais arriveraient un peu plus tard dans la saison.
Une hausse de prix inévitable ?
Après une augmentation de 699 euros à 799 euros en juin dernier, le MacBook Neo a pris du plomb dans l’aile. Avec l’intégration de 12 Go de mémoire vive de base, une nouvelle hausse tarifaire semble très probable pour le futur modèle. Reste maintenant à savoir de combien.

Une hausse de 50 euros qui amènerait le MacBook Pro Neo 2 à 849 €, ce qui resterait intéressant compte tenu de ce que propose la concurrence et de la hausse générale des prix ces derniers mois. articles.title: El regreso de Jensen Huang es una victoria para los accionistas, aunque también abre un precedente peligroso
articles.text:
Lo vaticinamos esta misma mañana, apenas unas horas antes de que se conociese el regreso de Jensen Huang al liderazgo de Nvidia: iba a ser casi imposible llenar el vacío que este ejecutivo había dejado en la compañía. Huang estaba involucrado en la mayor parte de los procesos de Nvidia. En las grandes decisiones, y también en los proyectos de corto alcance que a menudo pasan desapercibidos para los directores generales de las grandes compañías de tecnología.
Con toda probabilidad todo va a volver a ser como antes. Los 11 días que ha estado fuera de la dirección ejecutiva de la compañía que cofundó no bastan para cambiar nada. De hecho, si el consejo de administración ha decidido volver a apostar por él es debido a que ha recuperado la confianza tanto en él como en su capacidad de gestión. Durante los últimos años unos 60 altos cargos de Nvidia rendían cuentas directamente ante él, y no hay ningún indicio que nos invite a pensar que esto va a cambiar.
Sea como sea, su regreso no se entiende sin observar la presión que ha tenido que soportar Nvidia desde su salida de la compañía, el pasado 12 de noviembre. Su cotización llegó a caer un 27,7% entre el cierre del 11 de noviembre y el del 20 de noviembre, pasando de 173,73 a 125,53 dólares por acción. No obstante, esto no es todo. Pocos días después de su dimisión nació una campaña pública que exigía su reincorporación. Más de 200.000 personas la firmaron, y entre ellas se encontraban miles de empleados y accionistas de Nvidia.
La presión externa ha movilizado al consejo de administración
Elon Musk y Donald Trump expresaron públicamente su apoyo a Jensen Huang y la necesidad de que regresase a Nvidia. No obstante, según Reuters, los inversores han ejercido un papel determinante en su vuelta debido a que consideran que esta compañía no puede permitirse prescindir de su cofundador y líder en un momento tan delicado para la industria de la inteligencia artificial (IA). Y el mercado ha reaccionado inmediatamente al que sin duda es el acontecimiento del día. Y, posiblemente, de la semana.
Las acciones de Nvidia han subido hasta un 30% en la sesión de hoy, recuperando así buena parte del terreno perdido durante los días de incertidumbre. Este comportamiento expresa hasta qué punto es crucial para los inversores el rol del fundador como un activo fundamental, y también como eje del liderazgo de Nvidia en la carrera de la IA. Sin embargo, este giro también nos invita a hacer otra lectura en el ámbito del liderazgo empresarial que va mucho más allá de Nvidia.
Lo que acaba de suceder con Jensen Huang demuestra que la presión de los accionistas y el miedo a perder valor pueden degradar la supervisión del consejo de administración
Los consejos de administración de las empresas son los responsables de supervisar a sus directivos, defender los intereses de las compañías e investigar posibles incumplimientos de la regulación. Sus decisiones no deben estar ligadas solo a la cotización a corto plazo de la organización cuyos intereses defienden. Lo que acaba de suceder con Jensen Huang demuestra que la presión de los accionistas y el miedo a perder valor pueden degradar la supervisión del consejo de administración.
En este escenario tiene todo el sentido del mundo que nos preguntemos hasta qué punto las grandes empresas tecnológicas son capaces de mantener sus mecanismos de control cuando el directivo cuestionado es, al mismo tiempo, su principal activo. En cualquier caso, la "crisis de Huang" no ha terminado. El consejo de administración de Nvidia ha confirmado que la investigación independiente que iniciaron cuando Jensen Huang salió de la compañía seguirá adelante.

articles.title: En 1724 cayó un meteorito en Alemania: acabamos de descubrir que contenía un material 'imposible' para la física
articles.text:
El meteorito de Steinbach fue hallado en Alemania en 1724. Alguno de sus fragmentos está en el Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de París. De él han estudiado una peculiaridad de su conducta térmica. Concretamente, han medido la conductividad térmica de uno de sus minerales en función de la temperatura. Se trata de un mineral que presenta un comportamiento poco habitual. Este estudio nos ayuda a conocer mejor los materiales que presentan comportamientos híbridos entre cristales y vidrios.
El mineral en cuestión es la tridimita. Es un tipo de dióxido de silicio similar al cuarzo, aunque estructuralmente diferente. En la muestra del meteorito que han estudiado, observan que la conductividad térmica de este mineral es casi constante en el rango de temperatura de 80 a 380 kelvin (que se corresponden aproximadamente con -193 y 107 grados centígrados). Este estudio se publica en PNAS el 11 de julio de 2025.
Dos mecanismos que se compensan
En materiales cristalinos sencillos, suele observarse que la conductividad térmica disminuye con el aumento de temperatura. Esto es debido a que el mecanismo de transporte de calor es el de propagación de vibraciones de la red. A medida que aumentamos la temperatura, estas vibraciones tienen más dificultades para propagarse. En materiales vítreos (con estructura atómica desordenada) puede verse que la conductividad térmica aumenta con el aumento de temperatura (hasta un punto de saturación).
En el caso de la tridimita del meteorito, observamos que hay una mezcla de orden en la red de enlaces y de geometría distorsionada (similar en algunos aspectos a un vidrio). Por ello podemos encontrar dos tipos de mecanismos de transporte de calor. Por un lado, tenemos el de propagación de vibraciones (como en los cristales simples) y, por otro, el de acoplamiento de modos vibracionales (un efecto de tunelización de tipo ondulatorio).
A medida que varía la temperatura, vamos a encontrar que cada una de estas contribuciones va cambiando en sentidos opuestos, compensándose entre sí. Los expertos llaman a este comportamiento PTI (siglas en inglés de “propagation-tunneling-invariant”). De esta manera conseguimos que, en el rango de temperaturas estudiado, la conductividad total sea casi constante. En el archivo de datos del equipo pueden ver cómo existe una mezcla de orden en enlaces y desorden geométrico.
Esto es consistente con una explicación física que se había dado antes. En 2019, Michele Simoncelli, Nicola Marzari y Francesco Mauri publicaron una teoría unificada del transporte térmico. Utilizaban el formalismo de Wigner. La ecuación que ellos desarrollaron es capaz de describir tanto el comportamiento de los cristales como el de los vidrios e incluso casos intermedios. En este estudio de la tridimita ponen en contraste las predicciones de esta teoría con un material real. No es que haya una violación de las leyes físicas.
Para determinar la conductividad han utilizado la técnica de termorreflectancia modulada. Consiste en utilizar un láser para calentar una región de la muestra. Además, se utiliza un segundo láser para medir los cambios en la reflectividad (que están relacionados con los cambios de temperatura). Estas señales se analizan utilizando un modelo de difusión del calor que permite determinar la conductividad. Han realizado medidas experimentales que han contrastado con los cálculos teóricos.
Lo que resulta estable es la conductividad (la capacidad de transmitir calor). También podemos calentar o enfriar la muestra.
¿Qué nos permite decir este hallazgo?
Desde la Universidad de Columbia explican que esto tiene que ver con el diseño de materiales para controlar el calor. Sin embargo, no quiere decir que con este material se puedan diseñar dispositivos electrónicos que nunca se sobrecalienten. Tampoco implica que mejoren la eficiencia de escudos térmicos en aplicaciones aeroespaciales.
La tridimita no es única de este tipo de roca. La NASA ha documentado la presencia de tridimita en Marte (en el cráter Gale). También explican cómo se forma en entornos volcánicos terrestres. No quiere decir que en Marte tenga el mismo comportamiento térmico que en Steinbach. Tampoco implica que pueda ser extraída por minería espacial.
Asimismo, han estudiado una fase de tridimita que se encuentra en ladrillos refractarios (utilizados en hornos industriales desde hace años). Relacionan las propiedades de estos materiales con la mejora en el control de calor en los hornos.

Actuellement noté 4/5 par notre rédaction, le casque Bluetooth Nothing Headphone (a) délivre une restitution sonore équilibrée et atteint 84 heures d'autonomie avec sa réduction de bruit active. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 99,99 € chez Fnac.com, Son-Video.com et Darty.com, soit une baisse d'environ 22 % et 28,57 € d'économie.
Nothing décline sa gamme audio avec le Nothing Headphone (a), un casque Bluetooth pensé pour offrir les fonctions essentielles de la marque tout en soignant l'autonomie et les commandes. L'appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire en conservant un équilibre sonore agréable et des fonctionnalités complètes.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le casque descend à 99,99 € chez Fnac.com, Son-Video.com et Darty.com, soit environ 22 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (128,56 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 28,57 €.
Une autonomie de premier ordre et des commandes complètes
Ce casque circum-auriculaire s'illustre particulièrement lors des longues sessions d'écoute sans prise secteur. Selon les mesures de notre test complet, l'autonomie atteint 84 heures avec la réduction de bruit active enclenchée, ce qui dispense de recharges fréquentes pendant plusieurs semaines d'utilisation quotidienne. La marque intègre également des commandes physiques intuitives et une compatibilité avec les codecs SBC, AAC et LDAC pour la diffusion sans fil.
Nothing Headphone (a)
Points forts
- Restitution équilibrée et engageante.
- Basses profondes et punchy.
- Contrôle intuitif, expérience complète.
- Audio via USB-C, égaliseur paramétrique.
- Autonomie record en réduction du bruit.
Points faibles
- Précision globale perfectible.
- Bas-médium creusé.
- ANC peu efficace dans le grave.
- Bandeau en caoutchouc agrippant.
- Coques non pliables.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une restitution équilibrée malgré une réduction de bruit perfectible
Le rendu audio propose des basses profondes et un équilibre tonal maîtrisé, même si la précision globale montre quelques limites et que le bas-médium reste creusé. L'isolation active (ANC) peine à atténuer les bruits les plus graves, ce qui conviendra pour des espaces calmes ou des bureaux, mais montrera ses limites dans les transports bruyants comme le train. Le bandeau en caoutchouc agrippant et les coques non pliables demandent aussi un peu d'attention lors du transport dans un sac.
CMF Headphone Pro : l'autre option face au Nothing Headphone (a)
La marque propose également le CMF Headphone Pro, un modèle encore plus abordable qui mise lui aussi sur une autonomie solide et une ergonomie soignée. En contrepartie, ce modèle d'entrée de gamme montre des limites plus marquées sur la captation vocale des micros en milieu bruyant et présente une construction plus basique.
Le CMF Headphone Pro est vendu 50,00 € moins cher que le Nothing Headphone (a), mais ce dernier justifie son tarif par sa note actuelle de 4/5 et un kit mains-libres plus efficace au quotidien.

Points forts
- Sonorité douce et équilibrée.
- Confort appréciable.
- Contrôle étendu, multiples fonctions.
- Réduction de bruit correcte.
- Autonomie très généreuse.
Points faibles

articles.title: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
articles.text:
A security issue discovered in Microsoft’s Azure API Management (APIM) service appears to have been responsible for the security incidents reported last week by two Norwegian energy firms, with impact extending beyond Norway.
Microsoft is notifying customers about the issue in Azure APIM, which is designed for publishing, securing and managing APIs. The vulnerability may have allowed threat actors to gain access to secrets stored in some APIM instances.
According to a private notification shared on Reddit by one customer, the tech giant discovered the issue on November 18 and closed the access path the next day.
“Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue,” Microsoft said.
Exposed data can include secrets stored as named values, client secrets for identity providers, subscription keys, and tokens for APIM’s direct management APIs.
Microsoft noted that APIM Classic tiers that don’t follow its documented security guidance are affected. Instances on v2 tiers are not impacted.
Norway’s National Security Authority (NSM) said on November 20 that the vulnerability had affected several organizations in the country, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi, which independently disclosed cybersecurity incidents last week.
Equinor reported the attack on November 17, one day before Microsoft identified the APIM flaw. The company said it found no evidence that data was stolen or altered. Skagerak Energi disclosed the incident on November 18, saying it did not impact operations or production, and it found no evidence of information compromise.
NSM said an unknown threat actor targeted tokens, secrets and named values stored in APIM. It’s unclear how widely the weakness has been exploited, but the organization noted that several sectors in Norway and abroad are impacted.
APIM users have been advised by NSM to treat their secrets and named values as compromised and replace them. They should also verify that their instances have been updated and identify the data accessible through the service.
Security expert Anders Kristiansen warned that credentials lifted from APIM could be used against outside services. The extent of the exposure depends on each credential’s permissions.

articles.title: Tech-packed cars are driving up repair bills and insurance costs, wasting $12 billion a year
articles.text:
Winners & losers: The more technology that gets packed into something, the more things can go wrong. That old adage is especially true with vehicles. According to a new investigation, the time US mechanics lose trying to access and use automakers' repair software is worth an estimated $12 billion a year. Drivers can feel it in their wallets, too, as higher repair bills can push up insurance premiums.
The report, titled Closing Shop, highlights the reality of repairs on today's heavily computerized vehicles. Its authors, from the US PIRG Education Fund, iFixit, and FULU, note that finding a failed sensor, releasing an electronic parking brake, or getting a car to recognize a replacement part can require plugging a laptop or tablet into the vehicle.
This modern problem illustrates the irony of the service light on a dash showing a hand tool. As the authors put it, "it should be a laptop." On some jobs, the mechanic has to pay the manufacturer for software access before the wrench work can start.
As for where that $12 billion figure comes from, the researchers estimate that about one in five repairs at independent shops requires manufacturer software. On those jobs, the median estimate from mechanics was 75 minutes spent buying access, downloading software, logging in, and waiting.
Across the US, that works out to 83 million hours a year, roughly the annual workload of 42,000 full-time technicians. The authors valued those hours at a typical shop rate of $140. The subscription fees themselves are a separate expense.
Buying the software doesn't always get you very far, either. One Ford Ranger Raptor owner cited in the report replaced a faulty anti-lock brake module, bought Ford's diagnostic software, and picked up a new adapter. Then the software asked for professional security credentials to reset the anti-theft system. With the replacement part already fitted, the owner said the truck would either refuse to start or cut out when shifted into drive.
There's also the question of how many subscriptions independent shops can justify. A Nissan dealer can spread the cost of one brand's software across the cars coming through its doors, but a neighborhood mechanic might see five different makes before lunch.
Of the mechanics surveyed, 88% had turned away at least one repair in the past year because they couldn't get or afford the software. For more than a million Americans who live over 100 miles from the nearest Nissan dealer, that could mean quite a tow.
That trip to the dealership can mean a bigger repair bill, too. A 2020 study cited in the report found that Massachusetts dealerships charged 36% more than independent shops for the same work. So if your usual mechanic has to turn you away because they can't access the software your car needs, you could end up paying more for exactly the same fix.
Even drivers whose cars never see the inside of a repair shop can feel it when their insurance comes up for renewal. When a car costs more to fix after a crash, the insurer faces a bigger claim, and those costs can feed into premiums for everyone. The report points to federal figures showing that US auto insurance prices rose 122% since 2012, compared with a 40% rise in consumer prices overall.
Carmakers have backed down over unpopular tech before. BMW dropped its heated-seat subscription after owners objected to paying extra to use hardware already in their cars, while Volkswagen pledged to bring back physical controls for essentials such as volume and heating. The report's authors want lawmakers to go further by making basic diagnostic software and service information free and capping what manufacturers can charge for their other repair tools.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
articles.text:
Securing AI agents is a variation of the insider-risk problem, requiring distinct identities, narrowly scoped credentials and fine-grained policy controls, according to Amanda Walker, senior director of engineering for privacy, safety and security at Google. In a QCon San Francisco session, she outlined patterns for teams whose agents have been adopted organically and are running ahead of their security and observability frameworks.
With agents now executing multi-step plans in live production environments, Walker argued that "a rogue AI agent is the same problem as a rogue human insider," one that acts with superhuman speed and persistence. Controls therefore need to work at machine speed, rather than relying on someone reviewing logs the next morning. She covered identity and credentials, boundary defence, subagent orchestration and policy-based containment.
Walker described giving an agent raw human credentials as the fastest path to production failure. The agent inherits the user's authority, so a prompt injection in a document can turn that access to an attacker's purposes. She recommended explicit principals for agents, the AI equivalent of service accounts, so each agent can be provisioned and logged separately without impersonating anyone.
Scoped OAuth tokens limit an agent's access in time and scope, but are immutable once issued. With credential attenuation, an orchestrator instead mints narrower tokens for its subagents, such as read-only access to logs, or read-only access to a repository between two commits when bisecting a broken build.
She pointed to Eclipse Biscuit, a token format whose holders can append restrictions, but cannot remove existing ones without invalidating its signature. It takes more work than reusing human authentication infrastructure, but suits services where teams control both ends.
For API keys, a proxy can give the agent a short-lived synthetic key and substitute the real one as traffic leaves, protecting it from prompt injection and exfiltration.
Walker cautioned that a virtual machine protects the host, not the resources an agent can reach: an agent with network access can still delete a database. Container sandboxes, ephemeral runtimes and sidecar proxies such as Envoy give finer control over file system and network access. But "a perfectly isolated compute sandbox is not useful," she said, so teams need policies that constrain what agents do with the services they call.
She also highlighted poisoned skills on public marketplaces that steal API keys and cryptocurrency wallets, citing Snyk research that found more than a third of publicly available skills had at least one security flaw.
Agents also cause harm by being wrong rather than malicious. Walker described an agent that read internal SRE documentation and invoked a break-glass process intended for emergencies, having decided it was the most expedient route. Monitoring caught it, but the lesson was that organisations must distinguish agents from the people they work for, because some processes depend on a human accepting risk. For the same reason, she described computer-use agents, which drive a mouse and keyboard, as in essence impersonation, while acknowledging they solve problems that machine protocols such as MCP cannot.
Asked in the question-and-answer session about tagging identities as agents, Walker said: "The biggest thing it gave us was auditability about some of these risk decisions." The distinction supports human-only rules, such as emergency access, and can help with agent-only rules, such as signed releases in regulated environments, although she noted that an agent flag alone is not enough for those.
In the Q&A, she also advised security teams not to simply say no, which pushes colleagues to work around controls, but to allow experimentation where mistakes are reversible and keep human review for irreversible actions such as wire transfers.

articles.title: Samsung Launches the Odyssey G6: The World's First 1,100Hz Gaming Monitor
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Samsung Launches the Odyssey G6: The World's First 1,100Hz Gaming Monitor
Samsung Electronics America today announced the launch of the 27-inch class Odyssey G6 (G60H), the world's first gaming monitor to support a refresh rate of up to 1,100 Hz in HD. The monitor also features Dual Mode, which allows players to choose between HD at up to 1,100 Hz and QHD at up to 600 Hz to suit their game and preferred play style.
The Odyssey G6 is designed for fast-paced gaming, where players need to track movement and respond quickly. Its IPS panel combines high refresh rates with a 1 ms gray-to-gray (GtG) response time, helping reduce motion blur and deliver smoother on-screen action. This newest model in the Odyssey gaming monitor portfolio will roll out at U.S. retailers nationwide beginning in December, priced at $899.99.
Hun Lee, Executive Vice President of Visual Display (VD) Business at Samsung Electronics"With the Odyssey G6, we are bringing together an ultra-high refresh rate and enhanced motion clarity, while enabling gamers to toggle between display modes depending on their gaming preferences," "We will continue to advance display technology to make the gaming experience more immersive."
Speed and Clarity for Competitive Play
Dual Mode lets players select the refresh rate that suits the game by simply switching resolutions for a more flexible and optimized gaming experience. Whether a gamer needs high resolution for an immersive open world game, or a faster refresh rate for quick action, Dual Mode offers easy switching based on preference. In HD mode, the monitor reaches up to 1,100 Hz for fast-moving scenes, while in QHD mode, it offers a sharper 2,560 x 1,440 resolution with up to 600 Hz.
The Odyssey G6 also introduces Odyssey Clear Motion, a feature that reduces motion blur to help players see fast-moving action more clearly during critical moments in gameplay. Through the optimized blur reduction algorithm, the Odyssey G6 keeps fast-changing scenes clear and crisp. Following its introduction on the Odyssey G6, Samsung plans to bring Odyssey Clear Motion to more gaming monitor models.
Smooth Gameplay and Detailed HDR Visuals
The Odyssey G6 supports HDR10+ Gaming, which optimizes brightness and contrast in real time, revealing
details hiding in dark shadows and bright highlights. Black Equalizer also makes details in darker scenes easier to see by adjusting lower luminance levels, while automatically adapting to the game genre for an optimal gaming experience.
Support for NVIDIA G-SYNC compatibility and AMD FreeSync Premium helps reduce choppiness, screen tearing, and stuttering for smoother gameplay when used with compatible graphics cards.Connectivity Designed for Convenience
Crystal clear picture quality is supported by advanced connectivity options. With one DisplayPort 2.1 port and two HDMI 2.1 ports, the Odyssey G6 offers connections for multiple devices. Auto Source Switch+ detects a newly connected source so players can switch inputs without manually cycling through them. The convenient experience is enhanced by the premium, ergonomic design of the Odyssey G6. Players can adjust swivel, tilt, and pivot angles, as well as height, to suit their own gaming setups.
The Odyssey G6 builds on Samsung's leadership in the global gaming monitor market, which it has held for seven consecutive years, from 2019 through 2025.
