articles.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
articles.text:
Frontier AI labs are very clear about their responsibilities: making the model more robust, better guarded, and harder to hijack. They are also clear about what they can’t do, which is understand the business context of an action. An agent deleting files from Google Drive could be malicious or perfectly normal. They can't tell.
That raises questions about the shared responsibility model for Agentic AI. In cloud security, there is a clear separation of responsibilities between cloud vendors and their customers. If you copy data from AWS into SFDC, each vendor is responsible for the data's infrastructure security while they have it, but the customer is responsible for the action.
The AWS Shared Responsibility Model is a classic example.
The separation isn’t nearly as clean for AI agents. Agents act as intermediaries between you and the request, and that intermediary isn't deterministic by nature. It sends authenticated, authorized requests that can be compromised or rogue.
The first scenario is somewhat clear and goes back to what the AI labs try to prevent: a rogue agent has either misunderstood something or acted in a way it shouldn’t. A human mistake, only not human and not necessarily a mistake.
Five organizations have published guidance on responsibility for AI agents: shared responsibility models from Microsoft, CSA and CoSAI, AWS's security guidance for AgentCore, and Anthropic's “Trustworthy agents in practice.” Only two assign ownership of an agent’s identity, and they split it differently. No one agrees on who is responsible for the agent's behavior.
A look at the existing approaches
The available guidance approaches responsibility from different angles. Some publications assign specific tasks to providers and customers; others describe security layers or broader stakeholder roles.
Together, they show why organizations need to determine who owns each agent, what permissions it has, and how it operates across the systems it uses.
| Company | Description | Focus | 
| Microsoft | Publishes an AI agent shared responsibility model with a matrix for IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS deployments. | The customer remains accountable for agent actions across all three models. Agent identity and delegated token management, along with per-action authorization checks, are customer responsibilities in IaaS and shared responsibilities in PaaS and SaaS. | 
| AWS | No agent-specific model, but AgentCore's security guidance applies AWS's general shared responsibility model. Closest match: the Agentic AI Security Scoping Matrix and its NIST comment. | Builders bear final responsibility for the behavior and permissions of the systems they assemble. AWS recommends enforcing security through infrastructure-level controls outside the agent and discusses agent identity, credentials, and delegation. | 
| Anthropic | “Trustworthy agents in practice” describes four layers of an agent system: model, harness, tools, and environment. It does not provide a formal responsibility matrix. | Calls for defenses across all four layers and asks customers to consider which tools, permissions, and environments they give agents. In a separate NIST response, Anthropic identifies authentication and permissions across agent boundaries as an unresolved challenge. | 
| CSA | Agent Shared Security and Safety Responsibility Model (Agent 3SRM) maps the CSA AI Controls Matrix to a ten-layer agent architecture. | Its public summary introduces an Agent Owner with ultimate, non-delegable accountability for agent actions and addresses accountability for sub-agent delegation. The summary does not detail its identity and authorization assignments. | 
| CoSAI | The AI Shared Responsibility Framework V1.0 uses five layers, responsibility matrices, and autonomy levels L0 to L5. | Its general principle calls for one accountable party per component, and its identity and access management matrix assigns accountability to the end user or organization. Its autonomy guidance also describes shared accountability between the agentic provider and application developer at L4 to L5, creating an apparent tension with that principle. | 
Let's say it goes wrong
Consider a coding agent that reads a support ticket through an MCP server. That ticket contains malicious instructions that cause the agent to push a change to GitHub using the developer's token.
It isn't a contrived case. In the organizations Token monitors, 60% of Claude Code and Desktop agents called two or more outside vendors, and 47% called three or more, in the span of one month.
Now to the million-dollar question: who's responsible for catching the malicious push and stopping it?
The Agentic Universe from Token Security
Nobody has ever secured AI agents.
Learn how security teams at Roblox, Amex, and more give each agent an owner, narrow its access, and cut it off fast, then see how Token Security does it in a live demo.
Explore the playbooks now
Could it be the harness?
The software that runs the agent has the most visibility: it knows where the instructions were (albeit not why they were there) and the command about to run.
Claude Code, for example, checks both. A server-side probe "scans incoming tool results and flags suspicious content before Claude reads it." In auto mode, now the starting mode for interactive sessions, a separate classifier blocks actions that appear "driven by hostile content Claude read."
OpenAI, Cursor, and GitHub each have their own versions of approval prompts, automated reviewers, network limits, and sandboxes.
This capability doesn't come with responsibility, though. Harnesses put that squarely on the user's shoulders, both within the interface and in their terms.
Will the MCP catch it?
The poisoned ticket came in over MCP, a protocol built for model clients. You might expect it to carry some of the load, because it's a door purpose-made for agents. At least conceptually, it could denote expanded responsibility for the people who built this door.
The MCP spec hands the load back to the client. Clients SHOULD validate tool results before passing them to the model, and "there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations," it says.
The server's duties involve tokens, inputs, access controls, and rate limits.
And so, a typical MCP server will check who sent a request, not whether it should have been sent.
It all goes back to the MCP spec, which neither uses the term "prompt injection" nor provides the server with any verified information about its caller; client information is "self-reported." It says outright that "MCP itself cannot enforce these security principles at the protocol level."
Atlassian, for its part, calls the use of MCP clients with its products "a customer-elected action."
Could GitHub be the solution?
The push reaches GitHub with a valid token. Unless an admin has set up a branch protection rule for main, nothing stops it, and by default, those rules "don't apply to people with admin permissions to the repository."
GitHub's audit log includes an agent marker, actor_is_agent, for agents that run on GitHub. Nothing in the docs says it marks a local agent's push, though. And the terms are the same as everyone's: "You are responsible for all content posted and activity that occurs under your Account."
Do agent identities close the gap?
In an ideal scenario, every agent has its own identity, which should carry narrower, shorter-lived access.
Microsoft, for example, gives agents identities of their own: a Microsoft Entra agent identity is a service principal in your Entra tenant. Microsoft's framework also marks per-action authorization as shared.
But when an agent acts on behalf of a user, Microsoft's documentation says "risky activity is attributed to the user." A Conditional Access policy aimed at an agent identity "doesn't cover agent requests made on behalf of the user."
And that's the story in a nutshell, within one vendor. Even if the framework points to shared responsibility, the product attributes the risk to the user when it's actually time to act.
You share the responsibility
That leaves you. And it's probably going to remain the norm. While platforms could, in theory, do more, agents are considered extensions of our will, even though they often have a “will” of their own.
It's a novel scenario, and the only choice is to look at the risk honestly and decide how much of it we're willing to accept. And even that is easier said than done because you can't see the agent as a single thing.
The harness has its telemetry, Atlassian has its MCP log, and GitHub has the developer's push. Coding agents like this one run under the developer's credentials by default, so their actions appear to be the developer's.
No vendor in this chain sees the whole agent:
- The harness sees the instruction
- The MCP server sees a token
- GitHub sees a developer pushing code
Only the identity the agent uses crosses all three. That makes it the one place where a single owner can set scope, expiry, and revocation. Branch protection and allowlists help, but identity ties them together.
What to do about it
Ideally, you treat the agent as one identity, whatever number of vendors it touches:
- Inventory per agent, across vendors. For each agent, list credentials.
- Give agents identities of their own, scoped to the task and short-lived.
- Decide where your log trail for agentic decision-making and action lives.
- Turn on branch protection, read-only modes, tool allowlists, and everything else that can help.
- Build a revocation path and practice killing an agent's access across all vendors.
- Ask your vendors what they can show you about an agent that also acts elsewhere.
An organization cannot delegate accountability for an agent’s actions to a model provider or infer intent from an authenticated request. It can assign an owner, limit the agent’s access, connect its activity across systems, and test how to stop it.
Those decisions make agent adoption governable without assuming any single vendor can see the whole workflow.
If the responsibility is yours, it pays to be responsible.

articles.title: NVIDIA : Alice Huang aurait été en contact avec un espion chinois
articles.text:
L'affaire politico-romantique de Jensen Huang est encore loin d'être réglée. On le voit avec ces nouvelles informations assez compromettantes qui viennent d'être dévoilées !
Aujourd'hui doit être un grand jour pour Jensen Huang. Le fondateur de NVIDIA, évincé de son poste après la révélation d'une liaison, est finalement réintégré, à peine onze jours après sa démission. Mais ce retour en grâce ne va pas nécessairement s'accompagner d'une ardoise totalement effacée. Car certains problèmes demeurent.
Alice Huang en contact constant avec un espion chinois pendant une partie de sa liaison avec Jensen Huang
Quand la liaison de Jensen Huang avec Alice Huang a été révélée, elle a d'abord fait scandale car celle-ci a été présentée comme une espionne chinoise. Une information qui avait ensuite été relativisée, voire quasi-niée, plusieurs jours plus tard. Mais si elle n'est pas une espionne à proprement parler, elle est loin d'être étrangère à ce monde.
En effet, une nouvelle information du New York Times, obtenue auprès de sources dans le renseignement américain, nous apprend qu'Alice Huang a été en contact avec un officiel du Ministère de la Sécurité de l'État (principal agence de renseignement chinoise). Ce contact a été constant entre le printemps 2025 jusqu'à l'automne 2026, soit en partie pendant l'époque de sa liaison avec Jensen Huang.
L'époux d'Alice Huang lui aussi en lien avec les renseignements chinois
La période durant laquelle a duré le contact correspond aussi au moment où la société d'Alice Huang, Megaspeed, acquérait de très larges volumes de puces avancées produites par NVIDIA. Certaines étaient intégrées à des data centers en Asie du sud-est pour offrir de la puissance de calcul à des géants chinois, comme Alibaba, quand d'autres - suspectent les renseignements américains - pourraient avoir tout simplement passé la frontière en contrebande en direction de la Chine.
Autre information, l'homme que l'on présente comme l'époux d'Alice Huang, Kang Wei, serait lui aussi en contact avec le Ministère de la Sécurité de l'État. et pour rappel, Washington mène actuellement une enquête approfondi pour connaître le rôle exacte d'Alice Huang et de Kang Wei dans un réseau d'entreprises d'Asie du Sud-Est permettant de contourner les restrictions américaines sur l'exportation des puces NVIDIA vers la Chine. De quoi maintenir une épée de Damoclès au dessus de la tête de Jensen Huang ?
Source : New York Times

articles.title: Free Mobile lance un service de traduction des appels avec des résumés IA par SMS
articles.text:
Free Mobile ajoute de l’intelligence artificielle à son forfait haut de gamme. Certains abonnés peuvent désormais activer « Traduction Live », un traducteur qui s’invite directement dans les appels. Il suffit de taper ## pendant une conversation, puis de dire « OK Free, traduis en anglais » pour que chaque phrase soit traduite à voix haute dans l’autre langue.
La particularité de Traduction Live, annoncé ce 24 novembre 2026, tient à son architecture : la traduction se fait dans le réseau de Free, pas depuis une application sur le téléphone (Samsung ou Apple intègrent des services de traduction à leurs OS). Seuls les abonnés Free Max sont éligibles au lancement.
Des résumés d’appels par SMS et des appels traduits en temps réel
Free Mobile prend en charge 10 langues : français, anglais, allemand, espagnol, italien, portugais (brésilien), russe, chinois (mandarin), coréen et japonais. La traduction fonctionne à tour de rôle, dans les deux sens. Il faut donc attendre la fin de chaque traduction avant de répondre et Free recommande sur son site de s’isoler dans un endroit calme pour éviter qu’un brouhaha gâche la traduction. Interrogée par Numerama, la marque ne dit pas quels sont les modèles utilisés par son service. Est-il exclusivement français (Mistral et Kyutai) ? Ou repose-t-il sur de la technologie américaine ou chinoise ?
À la fin des appels, Free envoie par SMS un résumé généré par IA qui reprend les informations essentielles, comme la date et le lieu d’un rendez-vous. Le correspondant en est informé et peut refuser en tapant 0.
L’approche tranche avec celle de Samsung ou d’Apple, dont les traductions d’appels en direct reposent sur le smartphone et ne fonctionnent qu’avec des modèles récents. Free mise sur son réseau, ce qui ouvre la fonction à tous ses abonnés Free Max, quel que soit leur téléphone (on peut néanmoins se demander si les abonnés Free Max n’ont pas déjà un smartphone haut de gamme). Le service colle aussi au positionnement voyageur du forfait, facturé 29,99 euros par mois (19,99 euros pour les abonnés Freebox) avec de la data illimitée dans 142 destinations.
Du clonage de la voix : l’autre prouesse de Free
En plus de la traduction, Free permettra depuis son application de cloner sa voix. Un modèle apprend le timbre de l’utilisateur et peut le remplacer par une voix de synthèse qui l’imite. Rien de nouveau pour qui suit activement le monde de la tech, mais une première fois pour de nombreuses personnes qui ne savent pas que le clonage est devenu simple. L’opérateur promet que les conversations ne sont ni enregistrées ni utilisées pour entraîner son IA, que les traitements sont hébergés en France et que les transcriptions servant aux résumés sont supprimées après l’envoi du SMS.
Le service s’active depuis l’Espace Abonné ou l’application Free, dans Abonnement > Mes options.

articles.title: Diesel -26 %, électrique +57 % : le marché auto européen bascule enfin
articles.text:
Les détracteurs de la voiture électrique sont encore très nombreux. Mais dans les faits, cette motorisation continue de s’imposer sur les routes. Une tendance d’ailleurs confirmée par les chiffres, et notamment ceux qui viennent d’être dévoilés par le cabinet Dataforce pour Automotive News Europe. Ces données, encore préliminaires, couvrent l’Union européenne, le Royaume-Uni et les pays de l’AELE (Norvège, Suisse, Islande et Liechtenstein). Au mois d’octobre, ce ne sont pas moins de 346 708 unités qui ont été immatriculées. C’est 56,6 % de plus qu’en octobre 2025, quand 221 336 exemplaires avaient été immatriculés.
La progression de l’électrique tranche avec celle du marché dans son ensemble : toutes motorisations confondues, les immatriculations n’augmentent que de 3,3 % en octobre, tandis que les ventes de voitures à essence reculent de 18 % et celles des diesels de 26 %, d’après les chiffres Dataforce relayés par Bevolt.
Désormais, les autos zéro émission (à l’échappement) affichent une part de marché particulièrement conséquente de 31 % en octobre 2026. Elle était de 21 % en octobre 2025. Une belle progression, portée par plusieurs facteurs que relevait déjà Automobile Propre en septembre : la hausse des prix des carburants liée au conflit au Moyen-Orient, les aides à l’achat en France, en Allemagne et en Italie, et l’arrivée de nouveaux modèles plus abordables chez les constructeurs. Le classement des modèles va d’ailleurs dans ce sens. En effet, au mois d’octobre, c’est le Skoda Elroq qui s’est imposé sur le Vieux Continent, avec 9 384 immatriculations, malgré un recul de 17,6 % par rapport à octobre 2025. Le SUV électrique démarre actuellement à partir de 36 020 euros hors aides.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
Mais il pourrait à terme être détrôné par son petit frère, l’Epiq, affiché à partir de 27 670 euros hors aides, avant déduction de la prime CEE. Quoi qu’il en soit, la star du constructeur tchèque est talonnée de très près par une voiture électrique tricolore. Il s’agit sans grande surprise de la Renault 5 E-Tech, qui continue à séduire massivement. Située sur la 2e marche du podium, la citadine a été écoulée à 8 933 exemplaires en octobre 2026. Soit une petite baisse de 4,5 % par rapport à octobre 2025.
Côté prix, la Renault 5 E-Tech démarre à 28 490 euros hors aides en finition evolution (120 ch), soit 24 870 euros une fois la prime Coup de pouce de 3 620 euros déduite. Elle coûte ainsi environ 7 500 euros de moins que le Skoda Elroq en prix catalogue. Renault place d’ailleurs une seconde citadine dans le top 10 d’octobre : la Twingo E-Tech, 10e avec 6 870 immatriculations, alors qu’elle n’apparaissait pas du tout dans les chiffres un an plus tôt.
Les marques européennes dominent
Nous retrouvons ensuite le BMW iX1, avec 8 359 immatriculations, soit une hausse de 36,8 % par rapport à octobre 2025. La Tesla Model Y se retrouve quant à elle au pied du podium, avec ses 8 309 exemplaires vendus. Il progresse pourtantde 51,2 % en un an. En revanche, le SUV électrique s’en sort bien mieux lorsque l’on regarde les chiffres depuis le début de l’année 2026. Sur les dix premiers mois, c’est lui qui domine le classement, avec 175 862 unités, soit une augmentation de 51,6 % (près de 60 000 de plus qu’en 2025 à la même période).
Le Skoda Elroq est sur la 2e marche, avec 98 726 exemplaires, et il est suivi par la Tesla Model 3 (92 134 exemplaires). La R5 E-Tech est en 4e place avec ses 77 927 unités. On notera par ailleurs que les marques chinoises sont absentes du classement. Pour en trouver une, il faut regarder le classement des modèles grand public, qui exclut le premium. Le Leapmotor B10 y arrive 10e en octobre, avec 6 007 immatriculations. Sur les dix premiers mois de 2026, la 10e place revient à sa petite sœur, la citadine Leapmotor T03, vendue à 43 435 exemplaires, soit une envolée de 237,3 %.
À part ça, aucune BYD, Xpeng ou encore Jaecoo dans le classement pour le moment. Les marques européennes restent très dominantes, notamment sur le segment des modèles premium. Depuis janvier 2026, celui-ci est dominé par le BMW iX1 (63 588 unités), suivi par la Mercedes CLA (58 889 unités). La berline électrique affiche d’ailleurs des immatriculations en hausse de 593 % en un an, un bond à relativiser : elle n’en comptait que 8 498 sur la même période de 2025.
Les marques chinoises se rattrapent en revanche sur l’hybride rechargeable. Selon les mêmes données Dataforce, le BYD Seal U est l’hybride rechargeable le plus vendu en Europe en octobre, avec 8 716 immatriculations, devant le BYD Atto 2 (7 533). Le Jaecoo 7 se classe 4e (5 221) et le Geely Starray 5e (4 501).

articles.title: Black Friday: Diese 5 Tools helfen dir, echte Schnäppchen zu finden
articles.text:
Bereit für den Black Friday? Diese 5 Tools machen dich zum Schnäppchenprofi
Die Black-Friday-Woche zählt zu den umsatzstärksten Tagen im Onlinehandel und viele Verbraucher:innen sparen sich bewusst Kaufentscheidungen auf, weil sie an den Tagen besonders attraktive Angebote erwarten. Umgekehrt werden die Händler:innen mit ihren Sonderangeboten immer lauter. Für Kund:innen wird es dennoch immer schwerer, die wirklichen Sonderangebote von Lockangeboten zu unterscheiden.Mit den folgenden fünf Tools und Services lässt sich die Vorbereitung für den Black Friday vereinfachen.
Histozon vergleicht Amazon-Preise weltweit
Histozon kennt die Preise einer Vielzahl von Produkten auf mehr als einem Dutzend nationaler Amazon-Seiten. Dazu vergleicht der Gratis-Dienst alle aktuellen Angebote und rechnet unterschiedliche Währungen automatisiert um. Interessant ist auch die Preisentwicklung der vergangenen 90 Tage – das ermöglicht es, besser zu erkennen, ob der Preis für ein bestimmtes Produkt kürzlich künstlich erhöht wurde. Außerdem kann ein Wunschpreis festgelegt werden, sodass der Nutzer per Mail informiert wird, sobald dieser erreicht ist. Praktisch ist die Browser-Erweiterung, die es für alle gängigen Browser gibt. Einen Nachteil bei dem internationalen Ansatz gibt es allerdings: Die mit der Bestellung verbundenen Versandkosten, Zoll- und Einfuhrgebühren sind ja individuell und müssen daher durch den Nutzer berücksichtigt werden.
Got Cashback: Erstattungen von Händlern
Rückvergütungen von bestimmten Händlern sind inzwischen zu einer durchaus interessanten Sparmöglichkeit geworden, auch wenn es sich dabei jeweils nur um kleinere Beträge handelt. Doch angesichts der zahlreichen Cashback-Portale wird es schwierig, schnell zu ermitteln, worüber man den jeweiligen Kauf sinnvollerweise abrechnet. Got Cashback ist ein Dienst, der nach eigenen Angaben derzeit 17 Portale mit ihren Angeboten für insgesamt rund 9.300 Onlineshops im deutschsprachigen Raum berücksichtigt. Die Kund:innen sehen so, über welchen Dienst wie iGraal oder Shop Back sie die höchste Erstattung erhalten. Hierfür ist zwar keine Registrierung bei Got Cashback nötig, wohl aber beim jeweiligen Cashback-Service, über den dann auch die jeweilige Auszahlung abgewickelt wird. Wichtig ist es, in dem Zusammenhang auf die Bedingungen der Vergütungsnetzwerke zu achten – denn oftmals gibt es Einschränkungen beim Anerkennen von Käufen.
Fake Shop Detector: Sicherer vor Betrug
Neben der deutschen Verbraucherzentrale, die regelmäßig über Fakeshops und verdächtige Sites in diesem Kontext informiert, hat eine österreichische Initiative eine spannende Lösung entwickelt, die es auch als Browsererweiterung für Chrome, Firefox und Edge gibt. Der Fake Shop Detector gleicht die besuchte Website mit einer Datenbank bekannter seriöser und betrügerischer Anbieter ab, also matched sie mit einer Whitelist und Blacklist. Zusätzlich kommt bei unbekannten Shops eine KI zum Einsatz, die auf verdächtige Merkmale achtet und direkt ein Ergebnis nach dem Ampelprinzip ausgibt: Grün bedeutet Entwarnung, während Gelb eine genauere Prüfung empfiehlt und Rot vor einem möglichen Fake-Shop warnt. Eine hundertprozentige Sicherheit bietet die Analyse allerdings ebenfalls nicht, sorgt aber für deutlich mehr Misstrauen bei den Nutzer:innen.
Distill Web Monitor: Sonderpreise überwachen
Gerade im Vorfeld des Black Friday ist es sinnvoll, Preise kontinuierlich zu tracken. Mit Hilfe von Distill Web Monitor lässt sich nahezu jede Produktseite in einen persönlichen Preiswecker umwandeln. Dabei überwacht die Browser-Extension für Chrom, Firefox und Edge beliebige Teile einer Seite auf Veränderungen, sodass man etwa den angezeigten Preis eines Produkts markieren kann. Benachrichtigt wird man dann etwa, sobald der Preis sinkt oder einen bestimmten Betrag unterschreitet. Gerade für kleinere spezialisierte Shops, für die es keinen entsprechenden Feed gibt, ist das die einzig sinnvolle Lösung, einen Preis zu überwachen. Übrigens kann man so auch Lagerbestände und diesbezügliche Veränderungen überwachen. In der Gratisvariante sind maximal 25 Überwachungen möglich.
Aliprice: Preisvergleich für Aliexpress
Gerade wenn es darum geht, Preise im Chinahandel im Blick zu behalten, tun sich viele Nutzer:innen schwer, weil es oftmals nicht einfach ist, ähnliche oder gleiche Produkte als solche zu erkennen und somit valide zu vergleichen. Aliprice kann als kostenlose Browser-Erweiterung die Preisentwicklung von Produkten bei Aliexpress aufzeigen – und das über die vergangenen drei oder sechs Monate. Nutzer:innen können dabei die üblichen Preisalarme einrichten und sich bei sinkenden Preisen benachrichtigen lassen. Hilfreich ist gerade in diesem Kontext die integrierte Bildersuche, mit der sich identische oder ähnliche Produkte bei anderen Händlern aufspüren und vergleichen lassen. Darüber hinaus fahndet Aliprice nach verfügbaren Gutscheinen und liefert Informationen zu Verkäufern.
Einkaufstour mit der KI? Noch nicht uneingeschränkt zu empfehlen
Abgesehen davon kannst du schon in dieser Black-Friday-Saison gut auf die Power der KI setzen. Sowohl ChatGPT als auch Gemini oder Claude könnten bei der Schnäppchensuche helfen, indem sie Produktbeschreibungen vergleichen, auf Alternativen hinweisen und vermeintlich günstige Angebote aufspüren. Noch nicht perfekt sind die KI-Assistenten allerdings, wenn es um aktuelle Preise und echte Rabatte geht? Unser Praxistest zeigt auf, wo die Fallstricke liegen und warum auch die KI manchmal irrt. Wer sich beim Black-Friday-Shopping auf KI verlässt, sollte die Ergebnisse deshalb unbedingt überprüfen und insbesondere Preisangaben mit unabhängigen Quellen abgleichen. Sicher ist: Bis zum wirklichen Agentic Commerce ist es noch ein weiter Weg.
Tipp: Pflichtprogramm für alle, die bei Amazon Preise vergleichen wollen, ist Keepa, das auch in der für private Nutzung kostenlosen Version schon extrem leistungsstark ist. Es erlaubt gute Einblicke in die historischen Preise auf der deutschen und einigen europäischen Amazon-Plattformen. Wir haben die wichtigsten Features und Tricks zusammengefasst.
)))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Beyond tickets: How LightSprint.ai is building a multiplayer software factory where PMs and designers ship with engineers
articles.text:
NetApp Excellerator
View Brand Publisher
Beyond tickets: How LightSprint.ai is building a multiplayer software factory where PMs and designers ship with engineers
AI made writing code faster. It did not make it easier for the people closest to customers to change the product. LightSprint.ai, part of NetApp Excellerator's Cohort 15, is changing that.
It is Monday morning. A product manager has a customer escalation, a designer has spotted exactly where users drop off, and both know what should change. They write a ticket. It joins a backlog waiting on an engineering team that is already stretched. Weeks later, the change ships, often not quite as intended.
AI coding agents have made individual engineers dramatically faster, yet the way most companies build software has barely changed.
Enter LightSprint.ai, which is building a multiplayer software factory, one shared place where engineers, product managers and designers plan, build and ship together on the codebase they already have, with engineering approving every merge.
The problem: AI made coding single-player
Today's coding agents live in one developer's editor or terminal. One person drives, and everyone else falls out of sync. Planning stays buried in documents, context lives in someone's head, and reviewers approve large batches of AI-written code with little shared understanding of why it was written.
Prototyping tools showed non-engineers they could create software, but on a blank canvas. Real companies depend on complex codebases with years of conventions and review rules. A prototype can ignore all of that; a production change cannot, so the prototype gets rebuilt and the speed is lost.
The bottleneck has moved. Writing code is no longer the slowest step. Coordination is.
Why enterprises feel it most
For large organizations, every change needs to be traceable: which requirement it came from, which acceptance criteria it meets, and which tests prove it works. Teams must follow approved packages and design systems, and security teams want to know where code and
data live and who approved what. Opening AI coding to more people without that structure creates risk; withholding it leaves the backlog where it is.
LightSprint.ai's approach
LightSprint.ai sits on top of the coding agents teams already use and turns them into a shared workspace for the whole product team. It rests on three pillars.
- Spec first, with traceability built in. Anyone can describe a change in plain language. LightSprint.ai asks clarifying questions, drafts a spec with acceptance criteria, and the team agrees on the plan before any code is written, while it is still cheap to change. Each change stays traceable from requirement to spec to tests and the final pull request.
- Multiplayer by default. Product managers, designers and engineers work in the same live session. Anyone can join an agent, steer it, and review a live preview of the change. Shared skills and memory capture the team's conventions, so every teammate and agent builds the way the organization already works.
- Engineering in control. Engineers set up the environment once, and nobody else needs a local development setup. Agents work in isolated cloud sandboxes, credentials stay out of AI-written code, automated verification checks each change, and engineers approve every merge through the GitHub workflow they already use. Teams can bring their own models and LLM gateway.
The result is not fewer engineers. It is engineers spending their time on the decisions that need their judgment, while the people closest to customers ship the changes they understand best.
Building with NetApp
Through NetApp Excellerator, LightSprint.ai is working with NetApp teams on evaluating how a multiplayer software factory fits an enterprise environment: spec-driven development, traceability from requirement to test, adherence to approved packages and UI standards, and a security model that meets enterprise review.
"Coding agents made engineers faster, but most software teams are still single-player. The people closest to customers write tickets and wait," said Ben Ong, Co-founder and CEO of LightSprint.ai. "Working with NetApp through the Excellerator program has sharpened what enterprises need for a multiplayer model to work at scale: clear specs, end-to-end traceability and security built in from day one."
Early signs of a shift
Since starting with early users in April 2026, LightSprint.ai now works with over 100 companies, and non-engineers have shipped thousands of pull requests on the platform, with an aggregate merge rate averaging above 80%. Companies are adopting a "coding for all" strategy, where product, design and operations build alongside engineering.
And that Monday morning? The product manager and designer open a shared session, agree on the plan with an engineer, click through a live preview together, and the engineer approves the merge the same week. No ticket left waiting.

articles.title: Una hoja de papel tiene 0,1 mm de grosor, pero al doblarla 27 veces se forma una pila más alta que el Everest. 15 pliegues más la elevan más allá de la Luna
articles.text:
El doblez de una hoja de papel es una acción muy común. Sin embargo, si tratamos de hacerlo muchas veces seguidas, nos encontraremos con algunos problemas. Por ejemplo, cuantos más dobleces hacemos, menos superficie queda. También se va engrosando el paquete. Hasta aquí son problemas físicos. Pero, si dejamos de lado esto último, podemos seguir calculando. Es decir, podemos pensar en cómo sería el tamaño de una hoja de papel doblada muchas veces.
Con 27 pliegues por la mitad, tenemos un grosor teórico de unos 13,42 km. Esto quiere decir que el Everest está por debajo (su altura sobre el nivel del mar es de 8.848,86 metros). Además, bastaría con 15 pliegues más (42 en total) para tener un tamaño de unos 439.805 km, que es superior a la distancia media de la Tierra a la Luna. Estos cálculos están hechos en el caso ideal (sin limitaciones de una hoja real).
Simplemente vamos doblando por la mitad. Es decir, en cada paso multiplicamos el grosor por dos. Empezando con 0,1 mm, tenemos: 0,1 mm × 2 = 0,2 mm (primer doblez); 0,2 mm × 2 = 0,4 mm (segundo); 0,4 mm × 2 = 0,8 mm (tercer doblez)… En general, el grosor tras N dobleces es 0,1 mm × 2^N.
Estos primeros números los podemos manejar en nuestro entorno. Por ejemplo, 10 pliegues nos darían 1.024 capas (grosor de 10,24 cm). Con 10 pliegues más tendríamos 1.048.576 capas (unos 105 metros). En cada paso multiplicamos por dos.
De esta forma podemos entender por qué saltamos el Everest. Con 24 pliegues tenemos unos 1,68 km. Con 25, unos 3,36 km y con 26, unos 6,71 km. La siguiente doblez nos añade 6,71 kilómetros de golpe. De esta forma superamos la cumbre.
De igual forma llegamos a la Luna. Con 40 dobleces tenemos cerca de 110.000 km. Con 41 dobleces tenemos cerca de 220.000 km. Con 42 dobleces llegamos a casi 440.000. Hemos hecho solo 15 dobleces desde que superamos el Everest. La distancia media a la Luna es de 384.400 km (NASA).
Esta es una de las dificultades que tenemos a la hora de manejar cantidades que se van multiplicando. Se trata de un sesgo del crecimiento exponencial. Como describen los investigadores Martin Schonger y Daniela Sele, hay una tendencia a subestimar el crecimiento exponencial. No es fácil imaginar cómo son los incrementos exponenciales.
La estudiante que consiguió doblar el papel 12 veces
Además de estos problemas de tipo geométrico, también tenemos que pensar en que, conforme vamos engrosando el paquete, necesitamos cada vez más material para poder hacer el siguiente pliegue (hay que envolver el conjunto). Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que era imposible pasar de 7-8 pliegues.
Sin embargo, en 2002 Britney Gallivan (que entonces era estudiante de secundaria en California) rompió este techo. El reto era doblar algo 12 veces por la mitad. Se trataba de un reto académico. Ella probó con hojas y periódicos. Y otros materiales. Pero fue acumulando fracasos. Al final llegó a plantear las ecuaciones correspondientes. Dependiendo de la dirección de los pliegues, la longitud necesaria varía según el grosor.
Guinness documenta que consiguió doblar 12 veces una misma pieza. Para ello utilizó una tira de papel tisú continua (de unos 1.219 m). Trabajó durante unas 8 horas. Las ecuaciones que desarrolló relacionaban las dimensiones del material con el número de pliegues posibles (tanto en una dirección como alternando). Para superar este techo es necesario utilizar una tira mucho más larga que una hoja normal.
A partir de ahí podemos seguir con la progresión matemática. Por ejemplo, con 69 pliegues llegamos a la escala de años luz. Con poco más de un centenar tenemos un tamaño parecido al del universo observable. Todos estos casos siguen siendo extensiones de este modelo ideal (fuera de las posibilidades físicas del papel).
Antes tenemos otro umbral. Con 51 pliegues tenemos unos 225,2 millones de km. Es decir, superamos los 150 millones de km que de media separan a la Tierra del Sol.
Foto | Xataka

articles.title: Resumo do OD: a volta de Huang; Tesla + SpaceX; hoje tem Superlua!
articles.text:
Jensen Huang passou 11 dias fora da cadeira de CEO da Nvidia. A empresa anunciou, nesta segunda-feira (23), o retorno do executivo ao comando.
Huang havia renunciado em 12 de novembro, após a revelação do seu relacionamento extraconjugal com Alice Huang (apesar do sobrenome, eles não são parentes).
Autoridades americanas investigam a empresária por suspeita de envolvimento em atividades de espionagem para a China.
O episódio reforça como, no Vale do Silício, alguns CEOs exercem muito poder sobre as empresas onde trabalham. É o que acontece, por exemplo, na SpaceX (Elon Musk) e Meta (Mark Zuckerberg).
Além disso, as guinadas erráticas envolvendo Huang lembram a “novela” da demissão e readmissão de Sam Altman do comando da OpenAI em 2023.
A renúncia e retorno do executivo ao comando da Nvidia também levantam a questão: como suceder (ou substituir) um CEO que “é” a empresa onde atua?
“O “não” de um conselho só se sustenta quando existe um sucessor pronto. E a Nvidia não tem. (…) O poder desses homens é enorme, mas tem dono do outro lado da mesa. É Washington que autoriza ou proíbe a venda dos chips da Nvidia para a China, e foi no palanque da posse de Trump, em 2025, que Musk e Zuckerberg fizeram questão de aparecer. Um CEO que volta pela mão do presidente volta devendo” – diz Kenneth Corrêa, especialista em IA e professor da FGV, em entrevista ao Olhar Digital.
E por que Jensen Huang é quase insubstituível? Para Wharrysson Lacerda, publisher do Olhar Digital, o executivo é um visionário e responsável por quase tudo o que a Nvidia se tornou. Mas existe um outro lado também.
“Tem um outro aspecto não tão nobre ou pragmático. Temos que lembrar que Donald Trump tem interesse pessoal na Nvidia. Nos últimos anos, especialmente de um ano para cá, ele multiplicou em várias vezes seu investimento pessoal na Nvidia. Então quando Jensen Huang sai da empresa e suas ações derretem, jogando uma enorme dúvida sobre o médio prazo no mercado de IA americano, temos dois aspectos. O primeiro é social. Boa parte da economia dos EUA depende dos investimentos em IA. É uma coisa inédita, nunca aconteceu de o crescimento do PIB dos EUA depender tanto de apenas um setor. O outro lado, não tão institucional, é que Donald Trump e muitos outros perderam muito dinheiro”.
EUA colocam empresa ligada a escândalo da Nvidia em lista comercial restrita
O governo dos Estados Unidos colocou a empresa Megaspeed em sua lista de restrições comerciais nesta segunda-feira (23). A medida impede que companhias estadunidenses forneçam chips avançados, softwares e outras tecnologias à organização sem licença do governo. A decisão ocorre em meio à investigação sobre o suposto envio ilegal de semicondutores da Nvidia para a China.
Saiba mais.
Corrida pela IA começa a sufocar outros setores da economia
A expansão acelerada da infraestrutura de inteligência artificial está impulsionando a economia dos Estados Unidos, mas também começa a pressionar empresas de diferentes setores. A disputa por trabalhadores, equipamentos, energia e investimentos tem encarecido recursos essenciais e dificultado as atividades de outros segmentos.
Saiba mais.
Tesla + SpaceX
A Tesla e a SpaceX estão avançando nas negociações para uma fusão de US$ 3,5 trilhões (R$ 20,8 trilhões), que seria a maior da história. Segundo o jornal Financial Times, o acordo entre as companhias de Elon Musk pode sair até o fim do ano.
WhatsApp amplia grupos para até 1.500 pessoas e libera mensagens que desaparecem
O WhatsApp está introduzindo duas novidades em seu aplicativo: o aumento do limite de participantes em grupos, que poderá chegar a 1.500 pessoas, e mensagens de texto que desaparecem depois de serem lidas. As mudanças estão em fase de distribuição gradual para usuários de iPhone e Android, segundo informações do site especializado WABetaInfo.
Saiba mais.
Olhe para o céu: hoje tem Superlua!
Esta semana traz um “show” no céu: a penúltima Superlua de 2026! Na noite de terça-feira (24), o satélite poderá parecer até 14% maior e cerca de 30% mais brilhante do que em uma Lua cheia comum, devido à sua maior proximidade com a Terra.
Isso acontece porque a órbita lunar não tem formato de círculo perfeito, mas de elipse. Por isso, a distância entre os dois corpos celestes muda constantemente. Em determinados momentos, a Lua fica mais próxima da Terra, posição conhecida como perigeu. Em outros, alcança o ponto mais distante, chamado apogeu.
O que é uma Superlua?
O termo Superlua é usado para descrever uma Lua cheia que ocorre quando o satélite está no perigeu ou próximo desse ponto. Segundo a plataforma de observação astronômica InTheSky.org, a Lua chegará à fase cheia às 11h53 de terça-feira (24), pelo horário de Brasília. Já o perigeu será atingido às 17h58 de quarta-feira (25).
Em média, a distância entre a Terra e a Lua chega a aproximadamente 356 mil km no perigeu. Já no apogeu, pode ultrapassar 406 mil km. São cerca de 50 mil km de diferença, o que altera o tamanho aparente do disco lunar no céu.
Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
  November 12, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

Materials provided by University of California - Santa Barbara. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Pehuén Moure, Jacob Granley, Fabrizio Grani, Leili Soo, Antonio Lozano, Rocío López-Peco, Adrián Villamarín-Ortiz, Cristina Soto-Sánchez, Shih-Chii Liu, Michael Beyeler, Eduardo Fernández. Deep learning-based control of electrically evoked activity in human visual cortex. Neuron, 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2026.07.006

articles.title: N-able Patches Critical Flaw Discovered After Mail Assure Cyberattack
articles.text:
N-able has patched a critical server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability discovered during its investigation into a cyberattack targeting its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services last week.
On November 16, the company disabled access to the portal and API and suspended related services, including logging, mailbox synchronization, the management portal, and quarantine, noting that email delivery was not affected.
Two days later, it confirmed that the services were targeted in a cyberattack and that the hackers hit a web server and likely accessed certain credentials stored there.
The company immediately initiated response and remediation actions, contained the incident, changed credentials, and revoked API tokens and OAuth tokens.
On November 21, N-able restored access to the Mail Assure and SpamExperts dashboard and APIs, while continuing to monitor the environments. The company says it has found no evidence of exploitation beyond the previously identified N-able-hosted server.
On Sunday, N-able revealed that it has patched an SSRF vulnerability identified during its investigation. Tracked as CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS score of 9.3), the flaw exists because the vulnerable service “did not restrict the destination of the LDAP synchronization connection check performed when a relay is configured”.
The flaw could allow an API user with sufficient privileges to make the vulnerable server connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, identify those that are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.
“N-able has remediated the recent security incident affecting our Mail Assure and SpamExperts environments and restored the impacted functionality. Our investigation to date indicates that exploitation was confined to a single N-able hosted server and continued monitoring since remediation has found no further malicious activity,” the company told SecurityWeek.
N-able also noted that its investigation into the incident continues, adding that it would provide further details on the incident in a formal root cause analysis within the next two weeks.
Mail Assure/SpamExperts version 20261121.1943 contains patches for the security defect.

articles.title: Google’s AI agents cut quantum computing costs 290-fold — now you can check their work
articles.text:
Google’s AI agents cut quantum computing costs 290-fold — now you can check their work
Google DeepMind has open-sourced the Lean 4 framework used to verify quantum algorithms developed by its Gemini 4 agents, including one that reduced estimated computational costs by 290 times.
The GitHub repository contains the mathematical definitions, specifications, and verified solutions, but Google has kept the system that coordinated the agents’ work internal.
Monday’s release follows “Discovering Formally Verified Quantum Programs with AI,” a paper Google posted to arXiv on November 6 that describes how it combined multi-agent algorithm discovery with machine-checked proofs.
The agents used a theorem prover to check whether their quantum programs met predefined requirements for correctness and computational cost.
The agents used a theorem prover to check whether their quantum programs met predefined requirements for correctness and computational cost. Google recently took a similar approach when it used Gemini 4 Carbon to prove properties of Signal’s encryption in Lean.
Inside the Lean 4 framework
Google built the framework on Lean 4, extending the Mathlib and Physlib libraries to support quantum programming and verify its computational costs; the same theorem prover underpins code-focused projects such as Mistral’s Leanstral.
QuantumComputation contains the core quantum programming tools and mathematical definitions, while QuantumComputationSpecs defines the problems the agents were tasked with solving and the requirements their solutions had to meet.
The framework supports both classical control flow and quantum operations, using quantum Hoare logic to prove that programs behave as expected. It also calculates the resources each algorithm requires, with Google measuring computational cost by multiplying the number of logical qubits by the number of T gates.
Developers can build the repository using Lean’s Lake build system.
lake exe cache getlake build
The company keeps the verified algorithms in a separate discoveries branch and has released the software under Apache 2.0. Google also plans to expand its cost models to account for classical computation and control flow.
How the agent teams coordinated
Independent teams of Gemini 4 Carbon agents worked on optimization problems with fixed mathematical specifications. The agents refined their algorithms in response to Lean’s verification results.
The most collaborative effort involved a non-Born-Oppenheimer photochemistry simulation, with as many as seven teams working in parallel.
The teams maintained a shared wiki of verified results and met virtually every four hours to compare their progress and build on one another’s discoveries.
Stopping agents from gaming proofs
Because the agents could modify files in their own environments, there was a risk they might weaken specifications or introduce assumptions simply to make their proofs pass. Submissions were therefore checked in clean sandboxes against fixed specifications, with Lean Comparator flagging changes to definitions and theorems and rejecting proofs containing placeholders or unauthorized axioms.
The separation resembles the approach Anthropic’s Claude Code team uses, relying on automated checks rather than human review to evaluate AI-written code. Google has published the formal verification libraries and solutions, but not the infrastructure that coordinates the Gemini agents.
What the algorithms save
The largest gain came from a fixed-point arcsin algorithm, where estimated resource costs fell by a factor of 290. The revised circuit requires 100 logical qubits and 3,698 T gates, compared with 245 qubits and at least 440,576 T gates in the original implementation. Classical testing produced the initial improvements, with formal verification enabling more complex circuit designs that cut costs by another 11%.
Photochemical simulation costs fell roughly eightfold, while a simulation involving cytochrome P450 saw a 2.5-fold improvement.
For an inertial confinement fusion simulation, the agents reduced estimated costs by a factor of 11.8 and lowered the logical qubit requirement from 5,650 to 4,338. Photochemical simulation costs fell roughly eightfold, while a simulation involving cytochrome P450 saw a 2.5-fold improvement.
These are formally verified resource estimates, not performance measurements from quantum hardware; scientific simulations remain beyond the capabilities of current quantum computers.
Developers can independently check the published proofs using the repository’s pinned Lean, Mathlib and Physlib dependencies, with the verified algorithms available in a separate branch. Reproducing the discovery process is another matter, since Google’s agent orchestration system remains proprietary.
The framework’s resource model also has limitations. As noted in Google’s research announcement, it does not yet fully account for classical computation and control flow, which the team plans to address in future updates.

articles.title: GrapheneOS accuses Google of anti-competitive pressure as it expands to Motorola hardware
articles.text:
The takeaway: One of the better known security-focused versions of Android says Google is trying to steer phone makers away from it. GrapheneOS developers claim Google has been asking Android manufacturers whether they work with the project, citing its Google Mobile Services licensing terms in the process. The accusation comes as GrapheneOS moves onto Motorola hardware, its first step beyond Google's own Pixel phones.
The team made the claims on X and described Google's outreach as a threat to the brands involved. It also said Google might eventually take a range of steps meant to block GrapheneOS and other Android forks. Its leaders said they want to speak with US Attorney General Todd Blanche and others to stop what they called "Google's escalating anti-competitive behavior."
GrapheneOS is built on Android's open-source code and hardens the operating system to improve security and privacy. For most of its existence, Pixel phones were its only officially supported hardware. That made it dependent on the same company it now accuses of working against it.
That dependence is starting to loosen. GrapheneOS partnered with Motorola last year, and the Motorola Signature 27 is being offered in a GrapheneOS variant. People who want the operating system will no longer have to buy a Pixel. A second hardware source protects the project if its relationship with Google gets worse. It also creates the kind of manufacturer relationship that licensing pressure could affect.
The project has also kept adding features. Recent work includes a secure paste feature merged into the operating system, part of a steady stream of changes aimed at limiting what apps can see and access.
The GrapheneOS team did not portray everyone at Google as an opponent. It credited Google's engineers and said many have helped the project at a technical level.
"There are a lot of engineers at Google who support what we're building and have directly worked with us," the team said. "People there have repeatedly helped us and even explicitly added support for GrapheneOS to Google software including supporting Vanadium for Play services FIDO2 and passkeys."
 – GrapheneOS (@GrapheneOS) November 20, 2026
That last detail shows how closely GrapheneOS and Google's software remain connected. Vanadium is the GrapheneOS browser. FIDO2 and passkeys are the authentication standards that let users sign in without passwords, using cryptographic keys stored on the device. When Google's Play services support those standards in Vanadium, GrapheneOS users can use passwordless sign-in through the project's own hardened browser. That kind of compatibility work happens at the engineering level, and the project says it has received that help.
According to GrapheneOS, the problem is Google's business division, not its engineers. The project's argument depends on that split. Technical teams at Google have made room for the fork, while the commercial side is now pushing manufacturers on licensing.
The licensing question has a legal history. Google has already lost court battles over its agreements with Android manufacturers, including terms that limited their ability to ship devices running Android forks. If Google is now using Google Mobile Services licensing to discourage manufacturers from working with GrapheneOS, it would be returning to a kind of restriction that courts have already examined.
For now, the claims come from one side. GrapheneOS has not publicly named the manufacturers it says Google contacted or shared the wording of any communications. Google and Motorola have not publicly responded to the allegations.
The outcome could affect more than one project. GrapheneOS's move onto Motorola hardware tests whether a hardened Android fork can survive outside the Pixel line. If manufacturers decide that working with the project puts their Google licensing at risk, other Android forks could find it harder to get onto new hardware.

articles.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
articles.text:
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving the work of acquiring and preparing heap memory off the startup path and onto dedicated concurrent worker threads. On Linux 6.1 and later it also upgrades 4 KB pages to 2 MB pages while the application runs. The 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's headline numbers comes from elsewhere: adaptive heap sizing, in the companion JEP 546, which still defaults to off.
Deploying ZGC has until now meant choosing which half of a trade-off to pay for. The collector's pause times do not grow with the heap, but its collection frequency does, so a small heap brings on early and frequent cycles. The JEP describes the older ergonomic behavior of committing one sixty-fourth of physical memory for the initial heap.
A team chasing fast startup set a tiny -Xms and accepted a long warmup, because the collector then had to acquire and prepare memory in increments while the application was already allocating. A team chasing fast warmup set a large -Xms, usually with -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch, and paid the whole bill before the first request landed. The JEP puts the spread at roughly a tenth of a second to start with a 2 MB heap against more than ten seconds with a 32 GB one on current hardware.
That work now happens in a new thread, ZMemoryWorker, one per heap partition. It commits and uncommits memory concurrently as capacity changes. It also heats memory before application threads reach it, which means pre-touching page by page and collapsing small pages into large ones.
The budget is fixed rather than adaptive. ZConcurrentWorkersCPUShare in zGlobals.hpp is 0.25, so preparation takes at most a quarter of the available CPU. ZGC's director caps young-generation worker counts when adaptive sizing is on, which keeps collection inside its CPU target while expansion continues and the collector deliberately runs above its heuristic heap size target.
Large pages on Linux no longer require an administrator to reserve them up front. ZGC probes for MADV_COLLAPSE, the madvise mode added in Linux 6.1, by mapping a 4 MB region, pre-touching a single page and collapsing an aligned 2 MB range. When the probe succeeds and memory heating is enabled, the collector enters a new Collapse state and upgrades pages in the background. The call races the kernel's khugepaged, so the implementation retries on EAGAIN.
The change shows up in what a deployer no longer has to decide. Where JDK 25 forced a choice between two tunings, JDK 28 offers a third option:
JDK 25, tuned for startup
$ java -XX:+UseZGC -Xms2m -Xmx32g -jar app.jar
JDK 25, tuned for warmup
$ java -XX:+UseZGC -Xms32g -Xmx32g -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch -jar app.jar
JDK 28, neither trade-off
$ java -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZAdaptiveHeapSizing -jar app.jar
The third command produces the JEP's case study figures, a 38% drop in startup time and a fall in warmup from 80 seconds to 10 for Spring PetClinic on a 32 GB machine. -XX:+ZAdaptiveHeapSizing takes the minimum and initial heap down to 2 MB and raises the MaxHeapSize ceiling to 100% of physical memory. Without it, ZGC falls back to the shared heap sizing path and a 25% ceiling. Concurrent preparation still runs, but not the aggressive expansion the measurements depend on.
Using identical memory techniques on every operating system is an explicit non-goal, so large pages may be the default on Linux and not on Windows. The JEP also cautions that applications tuned around a larger initial heap may warm up more slowly and need re-tuning.
Two further edges live in the implementation rather than the text. Pairing -XX:+UseLargePages with adaptive sizing and no -Xmx logs a warning and disables explicit large pages for the heap. The retry loop around MADV_COLLAPSE can also spin indefinitely when EAGAIN persists, a case the code attributes to pinning through mlock or long-term DMA and treats as user error.
Teams can see the heap sizing difference for themselves on the JDK 28 early-access builds by comparing the resolved flags:
$ java -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version | grep -E "MinHeapSize|InitialHeapSize|MaxHeapSize"
$ java -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZAdaptiveHeapSizing -XX:+PrintFlagsFinal -version | grep -E "MinHeapSize|InitialHeapSize|MaxHeapSize"
The second run drops the minimum and initial sizes to the 2 MB floor and lifts the maximum from a quarter of physical memory to all of it. Adding -Xlog:gc+init reports Memory Heating: Enabled and, once the collapse path is active, Large Page Support: Enabled (Transparent, JVM enforced).
Services already running a modest heap on Linux 6.1 or later pick up concurrent pre-touch and background large pages without touching a flag, because memory heating is on by default. Services carrying a large pre-touched heap purely to buy warmup have something to delete, though only after enabling adaptive sizing. That 100% ceiling reads worse than it behaves. The policy tracks machine-wide memory and holds a reserve, preferring to leave a fifth of the machine free, fighting for a tenth and enforcing a twentieth, with those margins widening when usage is unstable or compressed.
JDK 28 reaches Rampdown Phase One on December 3, 2026, with general availability scheduled for March 9, 2027. The JEP's own future work points at better CPU sharing between concurrent collection and concurrent commit, and at ahead-of-time compilation from JEP 544, already Completed for JDK 28, which frees JIT cycles the memory workers could spend instead.
