articles.title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
articles.text:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam, senior software engineer at Netflix, described how the company's Commerce team retrofitted its software development lifecycle so that AI coding agents and engineers could ship together safely.
Khuzam argued that most of the work was not about agents at all, but about documentation, consistency and review.
Much of Commerce runs as server-driven UI, an approach Netflix has discussed at QCon before. A single screen-composition service behind the API gateway builds screens for iOS, Android, web and TV.
Khuzam opened with a mock company email announcing that every engineer now had Claude Code and asking how much faster everyone was shipping. The problem the team ran into next was summed up in one line.
Agents promised speed. But we spent 20 years building for humans.
The team's first attempt was having an agent migrate tests, and it took four tries. The team started with "migrate this file," then added instructions, then the APIs to use, then how to mock data.
The docs were also hard to find, since the agent's context window ran out before it found the right page. And they were inconsistent, because tests were not written the same way across the codebase.
Developers rated the internal framework at a Net Promoter Score of -3. Moving from one test to a whole feature, from screen to data to route to test, meant teaching the agent how the team builds.
Khuzam described the fix as context engineering, "getting what engineers know into what agents see." The team wrote 45 architecture decision records, each "written for people and for agents."
Each record covers the context, the decision, a pattern and an anti-pattern, and AI usage notes on what an agent should do. It also links to related docs and code, and the records now ship inside almost every repository.
To keep those records and more than 300 other documents findable, the team borrowed from how search engines read a site. An AGENTS.md file, the project instructions file that coding agents read before anything else, plays the part of robots.txt.
The second half of the talk followed code after an agent writes it. Khuzam noted that the CI pipeline is still deterministic, running builds, tests, screenshot diffing, merge queues and canaries.
What changed is how agents plug into each phase. A review agent pre-reviews each pull request against the docs and ADRs, flags anti-patterns and looks at what depends on the change.
Its first version left 23 comments on a single PR, starting with "Overall this PR looks great!" It now posts only verified blockers, each with evidence, a fix and the ADR rule it breaks. Engineers can add a revise label to have an agent read the review and push a fix to the same PR. Changes aren't yet auto-merged, and engineers own the code.
Khuzam reported no Sev 1 incidents in 2026 on a core service and 32% more pull requests year over year. Developer NPS rose from -3 to +25 over three quarters.
Ahead of the session, Khuzam framed the stakes on LinkedIn: "Agents can write code, but what gives us the confidence to ship Tier 0 services to 300M+ members without everything falling apart?"
Work that crosses services raised a harder question. A product engineer building one feature touches the payment API, billing, the gateway and every client, so the team had to decide who owns the context and how it follows the work.
Khuzam listed approaches that did not hold up. Loading every repository did not fit, Git submodules were brittle, a Git MCP server "sees one file, not the system," and shared copies went stale.
The team needed context that was accurate, portable across agents, owned per domain and kept fresh. It settled on GraphRAG per domain, taking structure from the code and meaning from the docs and ADRs.
Each graph is pinned to specific commits and served through a single Model Context Protocol tool. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, a Slack bot and CI review all query the same graph, and every answer cites a file and a line.
Khuzam closed with three rules: decide what agents should do and tell them, make it easy to find how to do it, and remember that human judgement still matters. "None of this is new. It's good engineering, built for a new reader."
Developers interested in learning more can watch InfoQ in the coming weeks for video of the session and can view the session details here.

articles.title: Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
Intel's "Bartlett Lake-S" CPU series are reportedly booting natively without modifications on select MSI motherboards. Initially, Uniko's Hardware shared tests of the Intel Core 9 273PE with 12 P-cores and the Core 7 253PE with 10 P-cores on an MSI Z790 MPOWER motherboard, using a modified BIOS to boot and utilize the P-Core only SKUs. However, X user LovK2X successfully booted and operated a Core 9 273PE qualification sample without any modifications on the MSI MEG Z690I motherboard, demonstrating that these CPUs can run without modifications and with minimal restrictions. Reportedly, all MSI motherboards from the Z690 and Z790 series support "Bartlett Lake-S" with the latest BIOS version, with the only limitation being a DRAM frequency lock. Every other aspect can be tuned and customized.
Built on the Intel 7 node and designed for Socket LGA1700, "Bartlett Lake" is a non-hybrid chip featuring up to 12 "Raptor Cove" P-cores without any E-core clusters. It was not intended to be compatible with consumer Intel Z790 chipset motherboards. However, the main issue was never the socket itself. "Bartlett Lake" shares the same physical LGA 1700 layout as Intel's "Raptor Lake" chips, but that doesn't automatically make it compatible with consumer boards. Typically, there was no official BIOS and microcode support to allow proper CPU initialization. However, MSI's latest BIOS update makes it possible to run these CPUs natively, and the second-hand market will likely value them for their potential gaming performance.The flagship "Bartlett Lake" Core 9 273PQE is also notable for its P-core-only design, featuring 12 performance cores and 24 threads. This sets it apart from Intel's more common hybrid desktop CPUs that combine performance and efficiency cores. It requires no intervention from Thread Director or the Windows 11 kernel to manage the threads, which could significantly enhance gaming performance. This uniqueness makes it appealing to enthusiasts, especially those curious about its performance compared to chips like the Core i9-13900K or Core i9-14900K. However, this setup is experimental, as these CPUs are circulating as qualification samples instead of regular consumer SKUs.
Sources:
				LovK2X on X, 				via VideoCardz			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on Intel "Bartlett Lake-S" CPUs Reportedly Boot Natively on MSI Z690/Z790 Motherboards
I do, but unfortunately it doesn't seem to be working anymore. I've disassembled and cleaned it, there was a bug under the heatsink - but it doesn't POST and the code reader says "--"No, production units are available. What is called "Bartlett Lake-S" is in fact referring to the Raptor Lake-S A0-type silicon, which replaces the 16 E-cores by four additional P-cores (12P0E configuration).
These were only released for the embedded segment and no microcode update was issued to support them on consumer motherboards, rendering them unbootable unless added manually somehow. Normally this would not be a problem, but since no A0-type Core i9 exists (only B0-type configs), you normally cannot use them on an unmodified say, Z690 or Z790 motherboard.
The 10P+0E should perform pretty close to a 8P+6E setup. I would like that instead of the 8P+8E if possible.

articles.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy 'pervert glasses'
articles.text:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.
The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, said that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”
Critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when users are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.
The Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.
The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

articles.title: ApplyBoard co-founder’s startup Passage deepens its admissions push with Kira acquisition
articles.text:
The talent recruitment startup from the co-founder of ApplyBoard is bolstering its university admissions automation platform.
The news: Passage calls itself an “applied AI lab” that’s building tech to connect international students to schools and talent to job opportunities. The company announced on Thursday that it has acquired Toronto-based Kira Talent, an admissions assessment platform that’s majority-owned by the private equity arm of US non-profit Educational Testing Service (ETS).
Kira Talent’s AI-powered product will be combined with Lectoris, Passage’s admissions operating system, to help institutions assess prospective students and manage acceptances more efficiently, the companies said in a news release. A Passage spokesperson told BetaKit that Kira Talent’s entire team is joining Passage, bringing its headcount to around 60 employees.
From the source: Passage founder and CEO Martin Basiri told international education news site The PIE News that its product will help admissions officers dealing with AI-assisted applications and inflated grades. “Getting to know the students, and seeing how they react and who the real person behind the resume is, is very important—and I think that’s only becoming more important,” Basiri said.
The context: Basiri founded Passage in 2023 after leaving ApplyBoard, the edtech startup and former unicorn he co-founded with his younger brothers. While ApplyBoard helps international students apply to Western schools, Passage was meant to financially support foreign workers looking to move to Canada to fill skilled labour gaps.
Passage raised $40 million CAD to fuel these plans, but a federal clampdown on international students and immigration starting in 2024 forced the company to pivot, Basiri told The Globe and Mail. It landed an exclusive partnership this August to provide technology to ETS, the main US developer of standardized admissions tests like the Graduate Record Examinations. Now, Passage has acquired Kira Talent from ETS; according to its website, Kira has been used by more than 1,100 academic programs.
Final thought: Passage’s partnership with ETS saw it lean into the educational admissions tech space, which ApplyBoard CEO Meti Basiri told the Globe now puts the two startups in competition. With its new acquisition of Kira Talent, Passage appears to have further boosted its AI offering in educational admissions.
Feature image courtesy Passage.

articles.title: “El error fue corregido”: Elon Musk apoya regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia
articles.text:
Elon Musk afirmó en X que “el error ha sido corregido” después de que NVIDIA restituyera a Jensen Huang como presidente ejecutivo y miembro de su consejo de administración. La decisión, efectiva de inmediato, devuelve al cofundador al mando de la empresa tras una crisis que abrió interrogantes sobre seguridad nacional y gobierno corporativo.
La restitución fue aprobada por unanimidad por el consejo de NVIDIA. La junta explicó que adoptó la determinación después de varias reuniones con Huang y de recibir información de altos funcionarios del Gobierno de Estados Unidos. Con esos elementos, afirmó que su regreso no implica un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
La publicación de Musk llegó después del anuncio corporativo y se sumó a las expresiones previas de respaldo que había manifestado para el regreso del directivo. El propietario de Tesla y SpaceX había apoyado públicamente la vuelta de Huang en medio del debate por su salida y la posterior conducción interina de la compañía.
El consejo dijo que la restitución beneficia a accionistas y empleados de Nvidia
Harvey C. Jones, presidente del consejo, sostuvo que los directores consideraron que Huang es la persona adecuada para encabezar nuevamente a la empresa. “El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar NVIDIA y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”, señaló Jones en el comunicado de la compañía.
La decisión devuelve a Huang tres funciones de forma simultánea: presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo. Jones continuará al frente de la presidencia del órgano de administración, mientras que Colette Kress dejará la dirección ejecutiva interina y seguirá como directora financiera.
Kress había asumido el liderazgo temporal durante el período de ausencia de Huang. El consejo agradeció su trabajo en esa función, en un momento sensible para una compañía que ocupa un lugar central en el mercado de procesadores avanzados destinados a sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
La empresa no precisó qué funcionarios del Gobierno estadounidense aportaron información al proceso ni detalló el contenido de esas conversaciones. Sin embargo, subrayó que la conclusión sobre la ausencia de riesgo para la seguridad nacional fue determinante para el voto unánime de sus directores.
Huang prometió colaborar con la investigación independiente
En su declaración, Jensen Huang calificó su regreso como un honor y dijo que retomaba la responsabilidad con “la mayor humildad y un compromiso renovado”. También agradeció al consejo, a Kress, al equipo ejecutivo, a los empleados, a los accionistas y a los socios de la empresa.
“Estoy deseando volver al trabajo”, afirmó Huang. El ejecutivo vuelve a encabezar una firma cuya evolución se convirtió en un indicador seguido de cerca por inversores, fabricantes de equipos tecnológicos, centros de datos y desarrolladores de modelos de inteligencia artificial.
La restitución, no obstante, no pone fin a las pesquisas abiertas alrededor del caso. NVIDIA recordó que había creado previamente un comité formado solo por directores independientes para investigar reportes según los cuales Huang habría sido blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera.
Ese comité contrató asesoramiento jurídico independiente y continuará con su labor, de acuerdo con el comunicado. Huang se comprometió a cooperar plenamente con la investigación, una condición que la empresa incluyó expresamente al informar su retorno al puesto.
La continuidad del proceso marca una separación entre la evaluación que permitió la vuelta inmediata del ejecutivo y la revisión interna de los hechos que motivaron la apertura del expediente. El consejo indicó que había quedado conforme con la franqueza de Huang y con su capacidad para dirigir la compañía, aunque no dio detalles adicionales sobre las conversaciones.
NVIDIA creó un comité para controlar riesgos de seguridad nacional
El consejo señaló la creación reciente de un Comité de Seguridad Nacional y Control de Exportaciones. El nuevo grupo está integrado exclusivamente por consejeros independientes y tendrá la tarea de supervisar el cumplimiento de las reglas comerciales y los riesgos vinculados a la seguridad nacional.
Según la empresa, el comité consulta con abogados especializados en esa materia. Esos asesores, a su vez, podrán contratar a otros expertos para apoyar el trabajo de revisión. La estructura refuerza el control sobre un sector sujeto a restricciones comerciales y geopolíticas por la relevancia estratégica de los chips de alto rendimiento.
Asimismo, NVIDIA inició la búsqueda de un director de Cumplimiento Normativo. La persona elegida deberá supervisar las obligaciones regulatorias en toda la empresa e informar al Comité de Nominaciones y Gobierno Corporativo.
La compañía afirmó que seguirá colaborando con las investigaciones y consultas gubernamentales en curso. La vuelta de Huang, por lo tanto, se produce mientras permanecen activos los mecanismos internos de control y las gestiones con autoridades estadounidenses.

articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ destrona a ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ como la película más taquillera de 2026 en España: sus cifras son históricas
articles.text:
La taquilla de España tiene un nuevo rey en este 2026. Y es que, después del último fin de semana (20-22 de noviembre), La Bola Negra ha destronado a Spider-Man: Brand New Day y se ha convertido en la película más taquillera del año en nuestro país. Un hito que parecía imposible para la película de los Javis pero que, a pesar de llevar ya dos meses en cartelera, no deja de sumar alegrías.
Con su recaudación más reciente, La Bola Negra acumula ya 40,5 millones de euros en la taquilla de España. Son unas cifras con las que ha superado los números de Spider-Man: Brand New Day y de La Odisea, los dos mayores blockbusters del año a nivel mundial. De hecho, la película del arácnido es la tercera más taquillera de todos los tiempos, por lo que el triunfo de los Javis tiene todavía más mérito.
Además, los datos domésticos de La Bola Negra son especialmente increíbles porque se encuentra a apenas dos millones de euros más de superar a Lo imposible (42,4 millones). Si lo consigue, se encumbraría como la segunda película más taquillera de la historia de España, solo por detrás de los 56 millones de euros de Ocho apellidos vascos. Ya no cabe duda de que el filme ha hecho historia para siempre.
Por otro lado, a nivel internacional La Bola Negra acumula otros 50 millones de dólares más. unos datos muy sólidos teniendo en cuenta que su distribuidora en Estados Unidos es Netflix, por lo que allí los espectadores están esperando a verla en streaming. Con una recepción tan positiva y con la temporada de premios a la vuelta de la esquina, solo queda soñar con todo.
Los Juegos del Hambre dominan la taquilla mundial
Al margen de La Bola Negra, la película que ha dominado claramente la taquilla de los cines estos últimos días es Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha. La cinta ha conseguido 3,7 millones de euros en nuestro país, lo que supone más de la mitad de la recaudación de este fin de semana. Y a nivel mundial sus números son todavía más impresionantes.
Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la cosecha ha alcanzado, en total, los 225 millones de dólares en solo tres días. En Estados Unidos ha tenido un mejor estreno que Sinsajo - Parte 2 y, por supuesto, que Balada de pájaros cantores y serpientes, el lanzamiento más flojo de la franquicia a nivel de taquilla. En las próximas semanas se demostrará si esta nueva entrega tiene piernas para aguantar sus buenas cifras.

articles.title: A Link Is Not Architecture: Why Multi-Die Systems Need More Than Die-to-Die Connectivity
articles.text:
Maintaining consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
The system-on-chip (SoC) transformed semiconductor design by bringing the major functions of an electronic system onto one die, an integration that shaped chip architecture for years. Multi-die design is now changing the model again, distributing system functionality across multiple dies within a single package.
While this approach gives engineers greater flexibility to align semiconductor design with system requirements, bringing these designs to life takes more than a die-to-die link to transport transactions across the package. It requires a system architecture that manages how data moves between dies.
In AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems, multi-die architectures enable teams to scale compute and select an appropriate process technology for each part of the design. These partitioning choices determine which transactions remain within a die and which must cross die boundaries. Treating each boundary independently increases integration and verification effort, complicates performance management, and reduces the practical value of chiplet reuse.
Still, managing communication across these die boundaries requires a clear separation between the physical interface that transports transactions and the system architecture that manages them. Extending the system’s data-movement architecture across die boundaries allows engineers to repartition or scale designs without rebuilding the entire communication architecture.
The die-to-die controller and PHY provide transport between dies: the controller handles protocol functions, while the PHY provides the electrical interface. The link does not automatically preserve the traffic management, quality of service (QoS), routing, address handling, and observability established by the network-on-chip (NoC). These functions remain part of the system architecture above the physical interface.
Getting transactions across a die boundary is only part of the challenge. Those transactions must also compete for shared bandwidth, often with different performance and latency requirements. QoS manages how bandwidth is allocated across die boundaries, preserving traffic priorities as the system architecture evolves.
In architectures that implement end-to-end QoS, service can be coordinated for each transaction along its route, from initiator to target. Arbitration and packet-level priorities determine which traffic advances when demand changes, while bandwidth controls regulate how much capacity each source can consume. Coordinating these mechanisms across the NoC ensures that each traffic class receives its configured service level, while the physical link is responsible for transport.
A multi-die package can carry coherent shared-memory traffic alongside non-coherent data and control flows. Coherent interconnects support data sharing across dies, while non-coherent interconnects serve paths that do not require shared-memory coherency. These different traffic requirements call for different interconnect capabilities, with Arteris addressing both coherent and non-coherent communication through its multi-die IP portfolio.
FlexGen Multi-Die smart interconnect IP provides non-coherent NoC connectivity for AI and HPC architectures. It extends NoC connectivity and QoS across chiplet boundaries, enabling traffic management across the multi-die system. FlexGen Multi-Die supports bidirectional transactions over a single UCIe PHY, reducing PHY area, power, and I/O requirements by up to 50 percent.
Ncore Multi-Die interconnect IP addresses cache-coherent compute architectures. It extends cache coherency and data sharing across dies, enabling software to see the multi-die assembly as a single piece of silicon.
Magillem integration automation supports IP, chiplet, and hardware-software integration as the number of components and interfaces increases. This reduces the engineering effort and complexity associated with assembling a growing set of reusable components.
As a multi-die system adds interfaces between dies, the number of trust boundaries increases. Security assurance must therefore extend beyond individual dies to cover the interfaces and trust boundaries.
Cycuity hardware security assurance helps teams uncover vulnerabilities, identify weaknesses, and verify security requirements.
Bringing these capabilities together requires coordination across the multi-die system. As chiplet configurations evolve, engineers must manage a changing combination of components and interfaces while maintaining the system’s communication, integration, and security requirements.
These products operate within a broader ecosystem because no single layer defines the complete multi-die stack. Arteris focuses on interconnect, data movement, integration, and assurance while engineering teams select the controller, PHY, package, and surrounding tools for their design. Standards-aligned integration helps preserve those technology choices, while co-optimization balances system performance and power. As controller, PHY, packaging, and tool roadmaps change, engineers must evaluate how those changes affect the complete design.
The next phase of multi-die design will depend on preserving system intent across all physical partitions. As chiplet combinations and interface technologies evolve, engineers must maintain consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations. The goal is to give designers the freedom to partition systems according to their requirements without having to rethink the entire architecture each time the physical implementation changes.

articles.title: GTA 6: Warum Leonida jede andere Open World alt aussehen lässt
articles.text:
GTA 6: Diese 4 Details machen Leonida lebendiger als jede Open World zuvor
Wenn ihr nach all dem langen Warten endlich in Grand Theft Auto 6 den fiktiven Bundesstaat Leonida erkunden könnt, richtet sich euer Blick wahrscheinlich erstmal auf die schiere Opulenz der Bilder: die feinen Lichteffekte in den Nächten von Vice City, die flirrende Hitze über den Sümpfen oder die realistisch modellierten Charaktere. Doch der eigentliche Generationssprung von GTA 6 steckt nicht in höheren Texturauflösungen oder noch besseren Partikeleffekten – so imposant das alles auch sein mag.
Die wirklich interessanten Neuerungen sind hinter der glänzenden Oberfläche zu finden. Im unsichtbaren Räderwerk von Rockstars hauseigener Rage-Engine. Wer das Spiel nicht nur als reine Action-Kulisse durchrast, sondern zwischendurch stehen bleibt und genau beobachtet, entdeckt ein eng verzahntes Zusammenspiel aus verschiedenen Systemen, die das Spiel besonders lebendig erscheinen lassen. Auf diese vier technischen Aspekte lohnt es sich beim ersten Streifzug besonders zu achten.
GTA 6: KI-Systeme ersetzen starre Skripte
In der Debatte um Games und Künstliche Intelligenz wird die KI oft mit generativen Werkzeugen gleichgesetzt, die Entwickler nutzen, um etwa Artwork zu erstellen oder Level zu designen. Rockstar Games aber sagt, dass sie KI nicht auf diese Weise eingesetzt haben, jede Straße, jedes Kleidungsstück und jedes Artwork sei handgefertigt.
Der technologische Sprung ist stattdessen in der System- und Verhaltens-KI zu finden, die die Kulissen des Spiels zum Leben erweckt. Aus veröffentlichten Patenten des Publishers geht hervor, wie Rockstar klassische, starre Skript-Schleifen und Entscheidungsbäume durch mehrstufige Modelle und dynamische Gewichtungen ablöst.
Das werdet ihr etwa im überarbeiteten Fahndungssystem erleben können. Während die Polizei in früheren Serienteilen oft wie telepathisch vernetzte Verfolger agierten, die immer genau wussten, wo ihr gerade seid, setzt GTA 6 stärker auf zeugenbasierte Meldungen und taktische Einkreisung. Beim Spielen könnt ihr beobachten, wie Informationen durch die Spielwelt wandern: Wer hat eine Tat tatsächlich gesehen? Wann greift ein Passant zum Telefon? Und genügt es, ungesehen um die Ecke zu biegen und das Fahrzeug zu wechseln, damit Suchtrupps zunächst nur das alte Kennzeichen verfolgen?
Ebenso interessant ist das Gedächtnis der Open World. Das Spiel bewertet, ob Überfälle sauber und professionell ablaufen oder in unsinnigem Blutvergießen enden. Diese Einstufung wirkt sich darauf aus, wie nervös Ladenbesitzer, Passanten und Sicherheitskräfte auf die von euch gesteuerten Protagonisten Jason Duval und Lucia Caminos reagieren. Statt eines binären Gut-Böse-Schemas entsteht ein kleinteiliges Netz aus Konsequenzen, das bestimmte Stadtteile nach wiederholten Eskalationen spürbar angespannter wirken lässt.
NPCs als eigenständige Akteure in GTA 6
An belebten Knotenpunkten wie Vice Beach oder den Einkaufsmeilen von Downtown drängen sich deutlich mehr NPCs, also Non-Player-Characters, gleichzeitig als es in früheren Teilen von GTA noch der Fall war. Diese größeren Menschenmengen wären jedoch kaum der Rede wert, wenn alle Passanten nach demselben Muster agieren und reagieren würden. Denn gerade in Videospielen ist Mehr nur selten auch Besser. 
Die bemerkbare Neuerung in GTA 6 erkennt ihr daran, wie diese NPCs situativ und individuell reagieren. Fällt ein Schuss oder kracht ein Wagen in eine Absperrung, flüchten Umstehende nicht mehr wie eine synchronisierte Herde in dieselbe Richtung. Je nach Entfernung, Blickfeld und Charaktereigenschaften, suchen manche hinter Mauern Deckung, andere erstarren kurz oder zücken ihr Smartphone, um das Geschehen für die spielinterne Social-Media-Plattform live zu streamen.
Ein genauer Blick auf die Bewegungsabläufe verrät zudem, wie eng Animation und Physik mittlerweile verschmolzen sind. Durch modernes Motion Matching und eine weiterentwickelte Version der Euphoria-Physik-Engine reagieren NPCs nicht mehr mit vorgefertigten Standard-Animationen auf Rempler, Stürze oder Treffer. Im Spiel lohnt es sich daher, auf kleine Alltagsmomente zu achten: Stolpert ein abgelenkter Passant über eine Bordsteinkante, stützt er sich instinktiv an der nächsten Hauswand ab. Auf Treppenstufen passen sich Fußstellung und Körperschwerpunkt fließend an die Neigung an.
Auch sind die Dialoge und Monologe der NPCs inzwischen deutlich komplexer. Die Charaktere sprechen kontextabhängige Dialogzeilen, passend zur Tageszeit, dem Wetter, der Umgebung oder dem Zustand eurer Spielfigur. Ein verschwitztes Shirt nach einem Sprint, Schmutz an der Kleidung oder ein plötzlicher Platzregen schlagen sich unmittelbar in Kommentaren und Handlungen nieder. So wirken die Bewohner Leonidas weniger wie austauschbare Statisten und mehr wie Nachbarn mit eigenem Tagesrhythmus.
Wird GTA 6 das Gaming verändern? Wahrscheinlich kaum – aber andere Branchen dafür schon
Dynamische Verkehrsströme mit individuellen Fahrprofilen
Jahrelang war der Straßenverkehr in Open-World-Spielen kaum mehr als eine bewegliche Hindernisbahn auf unsichtbaren Schienen. In GTA 6 steuert eine hierarchische Wegfindungs-KI die Verkehrsströme auf Basis von Tageszeit, Straßenzustand und aktuellen Störungen. Gleichzeitig weisen die zugrunde liegenden Systeme den einzelnen Fahrern unterschiedliche Persönlichkeitsmerkmale wie Geduld, Risikobereitschaft oder Aggressivität zu.
Wer sich auf eine vielbefahrene Kreuzung stellt oder einen kleineren Blechschaden provoziert, kann diese Profile unmittelbar studieren: Vorsichtige Fahrer vergrößern bei Störungen den Sicherheitsabstand und scheren behutsam aus, während ungeduldige Hitzköpfe riskant die Spur wechseln, hupen oder sich lautstarke Wortgefechte liefern. Hinzu kommen spürbare Rushhour-Wellen am Morgen und am späten Nachmittag, in denen Hauptverkehrsadern tatsächlich verstopfen und sich Einsatzfahrzeuge mit Blaulicht erst eine Gasse bahnen müssen.
Ergänzt wird das Verkehrsbild durch bodenständige Logistik- und Fahrzeugmechaniken. Lieferwagen folgen nachvollziehbaren Routen, Fahrzeuge verfügen über Diebstahlsicherungen, die das spontane Knacken teurer Sportwagen erschweren, und Tank- sowie Ladestationen binden Autos stärker in den Alltag der Spielwelt ein. Der Verkehr ist damit kein bloßer Hintergrund mehr, sondern ein unberechenbarer taktischer Faktor bei jeder Flucht.
Wetter beeinflusst Spielwelt und Physik
Das fiktive Gegenstück zu Florida bietet sich für drastische Wetterumschwünge freilich sehr gut an. In GTA 6 dient das Klima nicht nur dazu, die Atmosphäre des Spiels zu verändern, sondern hat schon nahezu Simulations-Charakter. Volumetrische Wolkentürme, die nicht nur Textur-Tapete sind, ziehen über den Himmel und erzeugen lokale Mikroklimata – es kann also an der Küste stürmen, während wenige Kilometer landeinwärts noch die Sonne scheint.
Besonders aufmerksam solltet ihr dabei auf das Zusammenspiel zwischen Wind, Wasser und Fahrzeugphysik achten. Starke Böen rütteln nicht nur Palmen und Leuchtreklamen durch, sondern türmen Wellen auf, erschweren den Landeanflug mit leichten Flugzeugen und beeinflussen sogar das Fahrverhalten von schnellen Sportwagen. Setzt tropischer Platzregen ein, sammeln sich Pfützen auf dem Asphalt, der Bremsweg verlängert sich und die Sichtweite sinkt stark.
Und natürlich wirkt sich das Wettersystem auch auf die Charaktere in der Spielwelt aus: Fußgänger spannen Regenschirme auf oder flüchten unter Vordächer, Autofahrer drosseln bei Nässe ihr Tempo und selbst die Tierwelt in den Feuchtgebieten passt ihr Verhalten an die Witterung an. All das lohnt es sich zu beobachten.
Die spannendsten Momente von GTA 6 erlebt ihr also nicht unbedingt bei wilden Verfolgungsjagden und lauten Schusswechseln. Auch nicht in den Missionen, die mitunter sogar etwas monoton werden können. Sondern in den scheinbar nebensächlichen Momenten dazwischen. Wenn ein plötzlich aufziehender Küstensturm den Feierabendverkehr ausbremst, ein ungeduldiger Fahrer ein riskantes Überholmanöver wagt, Passanten einen Unfall direkt mit dem Smartphone festhalten und eine Streife aufgrund von Zeugenaussagen die Fahndung beginnt. Genau in diesen ungeskripteten Kettenreaktionen könnt ihr eine Welt erleben, die dank ihrer vielen Systeme so lebendig wirkt wie kaum eine andere zuvor.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 19.11.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Black Friday : Amazon baisse le prix du robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro et le propose à -45 %
articles.text:
La belle saison est terminée : place au Black Friday ! Amazon propose le robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro à 599 € au lieu de 1 099 €, ce qui vous donne l’opportunité de préparer le retour du printemps en profitant de 45 % de réduction.
Acheter un robot tondeuse hors saison est une bonne solution pour alléger la facture. À ce titre, la période du Black Friday s’avère idéale pour investir dans ce genre d’appareil connecté coûteux. Pour preuve, le Dreame A1 Pro est actuellement proposé à 599 € chez Amazon, au lieu de 1 099 €. Ce modèle est destiné aux propriétaires de terrain dont la pelouse occupe, au maximum, 2000 m² d’espace. L’un de ses avantages tient à sa capacité à naviguer sans avoir besoin de câble périphérique, ce qui facilite sa mise en place.
Le robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro est disponible à 599 € chez Amazon, avec 45 % d’économies à la clé.
Pourquoi choisir le Dreame A1 Pro ?
- Pour son installation sans fil périphérique : son système OmniSense utilise un LiDAR 3D pour se repérer, sans antenne RTK à installer.
- Pour ses réglages par application : vous pouvez définir les zones de tonte, les espaces interdits et les horaires de passage.
- Pour sa hauteur de coupe ajustable : le réglage de 3 à 7 cm permet d’adapter la tonte à vos préférences.
Une tonte automatisée qui respecte votre planning
Le robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro est adapté à un espace de tonte maximal de 2 000 m², qui peut être séparé en plusieurs zones. Le robot suit des trajectoires en U pour organiser ses passages, puis rejoint automatiquement sa station lorsqu’il doit se recharger. S’il n’a pas fini de tondre, il reprend le travail une fois qu’il a regagné suffisamment d’autonomie. Ses roues tout-terrain lui permettent de franchir des pentes allant jusqu’à 45 % et il est capable d’éviter efficacement les obstacles. Enfin, sa hauteur de coupe est réglable depuis l’application.
Peu de contraintes d’installation, mais plus de finitions
Si le Dreame A1 Pro a l’avantage de ne pas nécessiter la mise en place de câbles périphériques, il faut tout de même prendre le temps de paramétrer les limites du terrain. De plus, ses utilisateurs soulignent que des finitions manuelles peuvent être requises le long des murs et des bordures, bien que ce ne soit pas toujours le cas.
✅ Les points forts
- Navigation sans câble périphérique ni borne RTK.
- Zones et horaires personnalisables dans l’application.
- Hauteur de coupe réglable de 3 à 7 cm.
❌ Les limites
- Bordures pouvant nécessiter un passage au coupe-bordure.
- Paramétrages indispensables dans l’application.
Profitez de la promotion d’Amazon pour vous équiper du Dreame A1 Pro à 599 € durant le Black Friday.
Si vous avez envie d’anticiper l’entretien printanier de votre pelouse pour un prix intéressant, alors le robot tondeuse Dreame A1 Pro tombe à pic, surtout à moins de 600 €. L’absence de câble périphérique constitue un avantage appréciable pour vous lancer dans cette démarche.
Mais attention, si vous avez un jardin très pentu et beaucoup de bordures, mieux vaut vous assurer que ce modèle est adapté en consultant les recommandations de la marque. Pensez aussi à prévoir un endroit stratégique pour installer sa station de chargement.

articles.title: GTA 6 sur PC : le principal projet est abandonné, mais le jeu commence à démarrer
articles.text:
En moins de 24 heures, le portage pirate de GTA 6 sur PC a pris deux directions opposées. D’un côté, le jeu de Rockstar commence à démarrer sur des ordinateurs, à partir de la version Xbox qui a fuité. De l’autre, le projet principal, Leonida, s’est effondré en une heure dans la nuit du lundi 23 au mardi 24 novembre 2026.
Leonida s’était pourtant préparé à l’arrivée de l’exécutable en adaptant le jeu en avance, mais son développeur semble avoir eu peur des risques juridiques. Pour rappel, l’émulation de GTA 6 sur PC est totalement interdite et l’impossibilité d’extraire légalement sa propre copie empêche toute tolérance de Rockstar.
Cyberleek a tenu parole et a publié l’exécutable de GTA 6
Lundi 23 novembre, vers 15h, le hacker Cyberleek a publié l’exécutable principal de la build Xbox 1.0.2.1 de GTA 6. L’archive pèse 57 Mo et permet, théoriquement, de lancer les 200 Go du jeu qu’il avait proposé au torrent précédemment. Dans son message, il affirme que Take-Two n’a toujours pas réussi à l’identifier et dit laisser les projets de recompilation s’occuper de la suite : il ne compte pas publier son propre émulateur.
Un écran noir, du son, et un jeu qui « démarre presque »
L’exécutable n’est pas chiffré et les contributeurs de Leonida l’ont chargé dans leurs outils en moins d’une heure. Dans la soirée, un message publié sur le Discord du projet, repéré par GamesRadar, résumait la situation : le jeu « démarre presque », avec un écran noir et un son qui se coupe.
L’écran noir signifie que la couche graphique, qui doit convertir les appels DirectX de la Xbox en appels Vulkan, ne fonctionne pas encore. Sur la machine d’un contributeur, la documentation du projet décrivait une douzaine de blocages franchis l’un après l’autre, avant un arrêt sur la gestion de la mémoire graphique, l’une des grandes différences entre la console et le PC.
À force de s’obstiner, des contributeurs ont réussi à démarrer l’écran de chargement du jeu. GTA 6 reste très loin d’être jouable, mais le temps devrait réussir à rendre la build Xbox compatible avec les PC.
Surprise : le projet Leonida jette l’éponge
Lundi soir, Leonida a d’abord déménagé vers une nouvelle organisation GitHub, puis tout s’est arrêté. Vers minuit, le serveur Discord du projet, qui comptait près de 179 000 membres, ne répondait plus. Vers 1 heure du matin, le dépôt GitHub, suivi par plus de 33 000 personnes, a disparu.
Au même moment, son créateur, NotRexed, a annoncé son départ sur X. « J’arrête, je suis désolé », a-t-il écrit, en expliquant se heurter sans cesse à des problèmes qu’il ne maîtrisait pas, sans préciser lesquels. Il est aussi l’un des développeurs de Hookshot, qui avait porté le remake de Zelda: Ocarina of Time sur PC un jour après sa sortie sur Switch 2.
Rien ne permet d’affirmer que Rockstar ou Take-Two sont derrière cette disparition, mais il est probable que les risques encourus aient joué dans la décision de NotRexed. L’équipe semble avoir supprimé le projet elle-même, très certainement pour se protéger.
La fin de Leonida ne marque pas la fin du portage. Le projet était publié sous licence libre GPL et il a été copié des milliers de fois sur GitHub avant sa suppression. Plusieurs copies reprennent déjà le travail avec tout l’historique du code, dont l’une qui réunit les correctifs de démarrage des contributeurs. Des archives complètes circulent aussi hors de GitHub. Certains affirment qu’il sera rapidement possible de lancer le jeu, même s’il faudra sans doute un peu de patience pour corriger toutes les incompatibilités.
Take-Two peut-il encore arrêter GTA 6 sur PC ?
Take-Two a l’habitude de ces combats. En 2021, l’éditeur avait fait supprimer de GitHub re3 et reVC, deux projets qui reconstruisaient le code de GTA III et Vice City, avant d’attaquer leurs auteurs en justice. Plus récemment, il a visé des centaines de portages mobiles de GTA V sur la même plateforme. Et cet été, il a obtenu des citations à comparaître contre Discord et Microsoft pour tenter d’identifier Cyberleek.
Face à un code libre déjà dupliqué partout, Take-Two peut ralentir les projets et disperser leurs contributeurs, mais ne pourra pas empêcher le lancement de GTA 6 sur PC. La seule vraie réponse possible est une annonce prématurée d’une version PC officielle, mais le faire maintenant reviendrait à un aveu d’échec. Le piratage reste heureusement dérisoire : la plupart des joueurs PC attendront une version officielle.
Depuis la publication de l’exécutable, les faux sites « Leonida » et les faux téléchargements « GTA 6 PC » se multiplient. Aucun de ces projets ne propose de version prête à installer : tout fichier présenté comme tel est à éviter.

articles.title: Microsoft testing fix for Windows 11 Bluetooth audio quality drops
articles.text:
Microsoft is working to fix a long-standing Windows issue that has been causing significant audio quality drops for Bluetooth headphone users.
This is triggered when Windows automatically switches from the headphone (A2DP stereo) profile to the headset (hands-free, phone-call-like) profile when an app or game activates and uses the headset's microphone, because bandwidth is limited in two-way mode.
After installing the preview builds released for the Beta and Experimental channels on Friday, Windows 11 Insiders with newer Bluetooth headsets can keep playing high-quality audio even after the OS switches between profiles.
"Bluetooth LE Audio devices can now play at full-range stereo fidelity while also using the device's microphone, ensuring you continue to hear great audio quality when in game chat, in a voice call, using voice typing, or using voice chat in Copilot Chat," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines.
"When using an LE Audio device with a PC that supports Super Wideband Stereo, choose the new 2 channels, 16 bit, 48000Hz option from Settings > System > Sound > Output > {Bluetooth device} > Output settings > Format when microphone is active."
This new feature is available for all Bluetooth LE Audio devices that support 48kHz playback, such as headphones, earbuds, and speakers.
Earlier this month, Microsoft also fixed USB audio issues that have plagued Windows users who installed security updates released since September.
As it explained when it acknowledged this known issue days after the September 2026 Patch Tuesday, USB Audio Class 1.0 devices failed to start or produce audio on some systems after installing recent updates.
Two years ago, Microsoft also blocked Windows 24H2 upgrades on systems with incompatible Intel Smart Sound Technology (SST) audio drivers due to blue screen of death (BSOD) issues and confirmed an issue that was causing game audio to go full volume when using USB DAC sound systems.
In January 2025, Microsoft addressed a bug causing audio playback problems and Code 10 errors on Windows 11 24H2 systems with USB audio device drivers after installing the KB5050094 preview update.
More recently, on Tuesday, Microsoft announced that it's testing a new feature that lets IT admins remotely lock stolen or lost enterprise Windows devices without wiping them.

articles.title: Après une cyberattaque, Nissan coupe un outil vital pour ses concessionnaires
articles.text:
Nissan est à nouveau dans le viseur des cybercriminels. Le constructeur automobile révèle avoir « identifié un accès non autorisé à une partie d’un système de diagnostic de véhicules utilisé par nos concessionnaires dans le monde ». Par précaution, le groupe japonais a coupé une partie de cet outil il y a dix jours, le 13 novembre. Celui-ci est toujours hors service au moment où cet article est écrit.
À lire aussi : C’est l’une des Nissan les plus populaires, mais vous ne verrez sans doute jamais sa version électrique
Des clés impossibles à reprogrammer
Le système Nissan compromis s’intitule CONSULT-III plus. Il est utilisé par les garages Nissan pour intervenir sur l’électronique des voitures et réaliser des réparations. Plusieurs fonctions en ligne ont été désactivées dans le sillage de la cyberattaque, à savoir la programmation des calculateurs de la voiture, le déverrouillage de certains modules et la gestion de l’antidémarrage, le système antivol électronique présent dans toutes les voitures récentes, qui empêche le moteur de démarrer si la clé n’est pas reconnue.
Concrètement, un client qui a perdu ou abîmé sa clé ne peut pas en faire programmer une nouvelle chez son concessionnaire. Selon les informations du New York Times, certaines réparations électroniques peuvent aussi être retardées.
En dépit de l’attaque informatique, les concessions Nissan restent ouvertes et peuvent effectuer la plupart des autres interventions, rassure le groupe nippon. L’entreprise précise que la nouvelle version de l’outil, baptisée CONSULT-IV, n’a pas été touchée par la cyberattaque. Sur son site destiné aux professionnels, Nissan indique que la coupure a été prolongée le temps de terminer l’enquête, sans donner de date de retour à la normale. Pour le moment, on ignore encore qui est derrière l’attaque, depuis quand les pirates avaient accès au système et si des données de clients ont été volées durant l’opération.
À lire aussi : Nissan va avoir un système de conduite autonome similaire à Tesla
Nissan, une cible récurrente pour les pirates
Ce n’est pas la première fois que Nissan se retrouve dans le viseur des hackers. En 2017, le fabricant automobile s’est déjà retrouvé dans le viseur du ransomware WannaCry. Plus récemment, c’est le gang Red Hat qui a piraté l’un des prestataires de Nissan, compromettant les données de plus de 20 000 clients.

articles.title: Enterprise data security startup Matters.AI raises pre-Series A round of about Rs 115 cr
articles.text:
Enterprise data security startup Matters.AI raises Rs 115 Cr in pre-Series A round
Matters.AI gives security teams one source of truth for sensitive data, showing where it is, where it has travelled, who or what has touched it, and whether that use was intended.
Bengaluru-based enterprise data security startup Matters.AI has raised about Rs 115 crore ($12 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners.
IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures, and Tetration Ventures joined the round, along with existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners.
The round brings the startup's total funding to about Rs 175 crore ($18.25 million), Matters.AI said in a statement.
The company will use the fresh capital for research and development in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence, and prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents. It will also build its North American sales team, starting with senior leadership hires.
According to the statement, AI agents now read, copy and move enterprise data with the permission of the employees who run them. Most data security tools show where sensitive data sits. They do not show who or what is using it, or why. So security teams connect alerts from separate tools before they can respond.
Matters.AI says it gives security teams one source of truth for sensitive data, showing where it is, where it has travelled, who or what has touched it, and whether that use was intended. It builds a picture using AI to understand the context of the data and the intent behind each use.
The startup brings together elements that enterprises buy as separate products for data security posture management, insider risk, activity monitoring and data loss prevention.
Matters.AI is deployed in more than 50 organisations, including major financial institutions, stockbroking and asset management firms, large retailers, and digital media and entertainment platforms.
“Security teams don’t need another tool telling them something might be wrong. They need a system that understands the problem, investigates it, and takes action," said Keshava Murthy, Co-founder and CEO of Matters.AI.
He added, "We built Matters.AI with a simple conviction. Enterprise data security should evolve from fragmented tools and manual investigations into an AI security engineer capable of doing the work.
"As AI agents increasingly access and move sensitive information alongside humans, we believe every enterprise will need an AI security engineer protecting its most valuable asset, its data.”
Sankalp Gupta, Managing Partner at Tanglin Venture Partners, believes enterprise data security is at an inflection point.
He said, ”As AI agents increasingly operate alongside humans, the challenge is no longer just knowing where sensitive data resides, but understanding how its being used and acting before it becomes a risk.
"Matters.AI stood out to us for its fundamentally different approach, building an AI security engineer that combines deep data intelligence, identity behaviour, and autonomous investigation and remediation. Rather than adding another layer of alerts, the team is rethinking how enterprise data security operates."

articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, l'antivol Kryptonite Keeper 785 passe à 29,89 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'antivol vélo Kryptonite Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm Gris à 29,89 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la chaîne Kryptonite Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm passe à 29,89 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 8 % et 2,69 € d'économie. Résistant aux pinces et facile à positionner sans abîmer le cadre, cet antivol affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 dans nos tests.
Kryptonite propose avec le Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm un antivol vélo pensé pour sécuriser un deux-roues au quotidien en misant avant tout sur la solidité. Ce modèle de milieu de gamme vise une protection efficace contre le vol sans compliquer l'attache lors des arrêts fréquents. Cette chaîne avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur les bancs de test.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Kryptonite Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm descend à 29,89 € chez Amazon, soit environ 8 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 2,69 € sur un équipement actuellement noté 4,5/5 par notre rédaction.
Une chaîne solide et protectrice pour le cadre du vélo
Le Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm mise sur sa fabrication associant acier et manganèse pour décourager les tentatives de vol rapides. Lors des essais détaillés dans notre test complet, cet antivol vélo a prouvé sa robustesse face aux outils d'attaque courants comme les pinces et les coupe-boulons. Sa conception souple de 85 cm facilite également son positionnement autour d'un point fixe par rapport à un modèle rigide.
En pratique, l'enveloppe textile qui entoure les maillons métalliques protège directement la peinture et les tubes du vélo lors des manipulations. Livré avec un jeu de 2 clés, il sécurise le cadre sans imposer de manipulation fastidieuse une fois descendu de selle.
Kryptonite Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm
Points forts
- Costaud.
- Résiste aux pinces et coupe-boulon.
- N'abime pas le cadre.
- Facile à positionner.
Points faibles
- Assez lourd et encombrant.
- Pas de cache-serrure.
- Quelques accrocs à l'insertion de la clé.
Quelques concessions sur le transport et la serrure
L'épaisseur de ses maillons entraîne logiquement un encombrement non négligeable lors des trajets, d'autant qu'aucun support d'attache sur cadre n'est fourni pour le transporter. Notre test a aussi relevé l'absence de cache de protection sur le cylindre et quelques accrocs occasionnels à l'insertion de la clé, ce qui demandera un peu d'attention par temps de pluie ou lors d'un verrouillage à la hâte. Ces défauts n'empêcheront pas les cyclistes urbains de profiter d'une sécurité sérieuse lors de leurs stationnements réguliers.
Decathlon B'Twin Elops U 900 : l'autre option face au Kryptonite Keeper 785 Chaîne 85 cm
Pour sécuriser un vélo, Decathlon oppose son B'Twin Elops U 900, un antivol au format rigide en U qui affiche la note maximale de 5/5 dans nos tests. articles.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
articles.text:
PHP last week patched a critical-severity vulnerability residing in the same dangerous state as the PHP2Shell flaws, cybersecurity firm Depthfirst says.
Dubbed phpAfterShell, the security flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS score of 9.2), and was resolved on November 19 alongside six other critical issues.
According to Depthfirst, the bug could allow an attacker who can control data written to a session file and interrupt the session write operation to trigger an object deserialization and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
It exists because PHP overwrites the session file from the start without emptying it first. If the operation is interrupted mid-write, or before the subsequent truncation operation removes old trailing data, the file is left with mixed content: fresh session data followed by remnants of the old session.
“We discovered reliable methods to interrupt the file operation during session upload-progress updates, allowing us to splice the prefix of one valid session with the suffix of another. A subsequent session operation treats the corrupted data as legitimate server-side state, giving attackers control over session values and the ability to trigger object deserialization,” Depthfirst notes in its technical write-up.
An attacker could arrange the new and old data so that the combined file would be interpreted differently from the original sessions, and parts of ordinary strings would become serialized object data. A future session would create the objects and invoke their deserialization.
“Session upload progress provides one way for a remote client to influence stored session data through multipart uploads. The same underlying problem can arise when an application stores large user-controlled strings in a session. In threaded PHP builds, a hard memory-limit failure in another thread can terminate the process while the session write is in progress,” PHP notes in its advisory.
phpAfterShell, Depthfirst explains, is related to PHP2Shell, which occurred because, during the parsing of an unauthenticated multipart request, PHP’s upload-progress callback could open and decode a file-backed session before the target script would begin.
Because objects would become active during the callback, PHP added restrictions to which objects could be created in memory, but did not modify the underlying file update behavior.
“Even with the new restrictions in place, the callback still reads the existing Session, adds upload-progress state, serializes the whole thing, and writes it back to the same file,” Depthfirst explains.
Successful exploitation of phpAfterShell requires certain conditions to be met: default session storage to be active, an exploitation route (the easiest is upload progress tracking), the PHP process to stop mid-write, a request to call session_start() on the corrupted file, and a deserialization-to-code-execution path.
Patches for the vulnerability were included in PHP versions 8.6.0, 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36. There appear to be no reports of phpAfterShell’s in-the-wild exploitation.

articles.title: Hace 12 años, la exmujer de Elon Musk dijo que una de las mejores técnicas del multimillonario es saber usar sabiamente la psicología de la oposición
articles.text:
Los dos grandes hábitos que observó Justine Musk en su exmarido durante su explosión profesional fueron el de trabajar mucho y el de decir “no”. “Me di cuenta de que detrás de cada no hay un sí más profundo a lo que realmente quieres”, explica en la charla que ella misma transcribió.
Es decir, que cada vez que decía no, estaba diciendo que sí a algo más profundo. Porque en realidad lo que estaba haciendo era bloquear el tiempo y la energía para poder dedicarlos a lo que había decidido que iba a hacer. Se trata de un sí que tiene que ver con lo que uno tiene derecho a querer para sí mismo.
Lo que cuesta decir “no”
Por ejemplo, en el caso de sus hijos. Cuando querían afirmar su independencia, decían que no. A ella le costaba más. ¿Y esto? Justine se preguntó si le costaba porque no se sentía con derecho a defender lo que quería. Lo relacionó con lo que había aprendido de pequeña. De hecho, terminó minimizando sus ambiciones en un mundo que esperaba de las mujeres que fueran modestas.
Esta escena coincide con lo que se ha visto en un estudio sobre autonomía infantil. Los investigadores han seguido a 51 niños con sus madres en dos momentos diferentes. Primero, cuando tenían entre 16 y 51 meses, y luego a los 5 años. En esta última fase aumentan las respuestas negativas verbales sin enfado y las que buscan llegar a algún tipo de acuerdo. Disminuyen los desafíos abiertos.
Temer que nos encontremos con enfados puede llevarnos a aceptar por compromiso. La psicóloga Ahona Guha describe ese miedo entre sus pacientes. También señala que tenemos en cuenta qué piensan los amigos y familiares y que nos preocupa que se nos considere egoístas. Hay que pensar a qué nos vamos a comprometer. Es decir, si tenemos tiempo o no para ello.
La agenda de Buffett y las prioridades de Jobs
Bill Gates también observó en Warren Buffett un modo similar de proteger su tiempo. En una entrevista con Charlie Rose, habló de cómo había aprendido viendo la agenda de Buffett. Gates dijo que era de los que llenaban cada minuto. Creía que era la única manera de hacer las cosas. Pero, viendo cómo organizaba su tiempo Warren, entendió que sentarse a pensar podía ser más importante que muchas de las cosas que ponemos en nuestro calendario.
Steve Jobs también asociaba los “no” con el enfoque. En una conversación con desarrolladores en una conferencia de Apple en 1997, comentaba cómo, para poder concentrarse en determinados proyectos, había que renunciar a otros. Recordó que en Apple había equipos trabajando en ideas interesantes de manera independiente. Sin embargo, juntas no ofrecían una dirección clara para la empresa. También había planteado este principio de priorización en relación a las reuniones de trabajo. En una nota interna de 1986 para el equipo de NeXT, planteaba que todos los jueves se dedicarían a trabajar sin reuniones.

articles.title: Nanoleaf's Smart Cordless Circulator Fan cools your entire home and offers cordless freedom to use anywhere
articles.text:
The hot weather is here on the eve of another summer but thankfully we’ve been reviewing the Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator Fan have easily managed to keep our cool.
As I write this, I am in my home office, which because of all the TVs, monitors, computers, devices and 3D printers, easily runs around 5-degrees Celsius warmer than the rest of the house.
I have the Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator trained on me at the highest fan speed (which is 9) and staying as cool as a cucumber.
What’s impressive about this relatively small fan is its reach, with a powerful airflow that can reach more than 30m.
It is 11 inches wide and has three 8-inch blades.
The Nanoleaf Smart Air Circulator Fan also has vertical and horizontal oscillation. We like to get it moving horizontally to spread the cool air around in our office.
If you want to go the whole hog, you can have both horizontal and vertical working at the same time so it’s literally covering the entire room.
There are four modes of operation – normal natural, sleep, and turbo.
For us it’s go big or go home so Turbo has been our favourite.
But it’s good to know that there is a sleep mode that operates at just 21 dB so you’re able to easily fall asleep on a hot summer night.
It even has a night light which offers a soft 3000K glow
But one of the best features is the fact that it has a rechargeable battery so you can move it room to room. Forget about looking for a power point to plug it in – you don’t need it.
And when it is plugged in, it is recharging the internal battery. Users can also charge it quickly through the built-in USB-C port.
And you can use it outside, or in a tent, or on your travels. But it’s not waterproof it just needs to be kept out of the rain.
What’s even more impressive is the fact the battery can run for up to 70 hours (with the night light and oscillation off) before it needs to be plugged back into the wall to recharge.
It also has a sleep timer which can be easily set up within the app so you’re able to delay its shutdown by up to 9 hours.
Part of this efficiency comes down to the 24W motor which really punches above its weight and yet it provides so much runtime when it’s unplugged operating from the battery.
Being a Nanoleaf product, it naturally works efficiently through the Nanoleaf app.
It also has Matter connectivity so it could also work with Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home for easier control.
Nanoleaf Smart Cordless Circulator Fan is usually priced at $199.99 but is available at the special price if you act now for $159.99.

articles.title: Nvidia confirms it is investigating possible third-party data breach, says it will 'continue to monitor the situation'
articles.text:
Nvidia confirms it is investigating possible third-party data breach, says it will 'continue to monitor the situation'
The Gentlemen adds Nvidia to its data leak site
- Ransomware group The Gentlemen claims to have breached Nvidia, and is threatening to leak stolen data unless paid
- Nvidia says it has found no evidence that its systems or networks were compromised and continues investigating
- The incident highlights growing extortion tactics where threat actors publicize alleged breaches before providing proof of data theft
Nvidia has confirmed it is investigating claims of a data breach after a prolific ransomware operator added the company’s name to its data leak website.
On November 18, 2026, threat actors going under “The Gentlemen” added Nvidia to their website, as per International Cyber Digest. They didn’t share any details - we don’t know the nature of the stolen files, or the size of the allegedly exfiltrated archive.
The group only said “DATA INFO - SOON” on the website entry and shared a clock that counts down to November 28 2026 - most likely the date when they plan on leaking everything (unless Nvidia decides to pay the ransom demand in the meantime).
"No indication of a breach"
Cybersecurity professionals and law enforcement generally advise companies not to pay the ransom. There is no guarantee the criminals won’t leak the data anyway, and there is even less guarantee they won’t attack the company again in a few weeks’ or months’ time. Also, in case the data is encrypted, there is no telling if the decryptor works properly, so the company could end up paying and still losing everything.
Instead, they advise organizations to keep an updated backup archive of all crucial information, and to tighten up on security to make sure they don’t get breached. That includes educating the employees on the dangers of phishing, as well as keeping all hardware and software updated with the latest patches and upgrades.
When asked about the claims made by the threat actors, the AI giant told The Register it was looking into it: “We have found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected,” a spokesperson said. “We continue to monitor the situation."
Since the group did not post a sample on its leak site, it is impossible to determine whether the claims are real or not. However, The Gentlemen is a rather prolific threat actor with a history of successful breaches. It first emerged during 2025 and has, since then, made a name for itself by targeting organizations across multiple sectors including healthcare, manufacturing, education, and finance. Notable victims include Puerto Rico’s Caribbean Medical Center, which reported a data breach affecting some 92,000 people. In April this year, the group struck US manufacturer Gator Cases, in which it exposed sensitive data on 1,171 individuals.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The Gentlemen run a ransom-as-a-service (RaaS) operation and offer its affiliates 90% of ransom payments, some sources said. According to Microsoft, its encryptor is built in Go and, besides the traditional encryption features, also allows the actors to move laterally and quickly spread throughout the target network. In its writeup, The Register says its affiliates claimed more than 320 victims as of April, with the majority of these alleged infections (240) taking place in the first half of 2026.
Nvidia's been hacked before
Pointing to a Check Point research, the publication argues that the actual count is likely much higher, since the researchers found an affiliate’s live C2 server while responding to an incident earlier this year. On the server they found telemetry for more than 1,570 victims, most of which were US-based organizations.
Nvidia, best known for manufacturing graphics cards, became insanely popular with the emergence of AI and AI data centers (all of which need Nvidia’s hardware to run). These days it is one of the most valuable companies on the planet but even before the proliferation of AI it was a popular target for cybercriminals. Back in 2022, for example, it suffered an attack in which threat actors made away with a terabyte of sensitive data.
The company was struck by LAPSUS$ which, at the time, was one of the largest and most dangerous hacking collectives in existence.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.text:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
  November 11, 2026
- Source:
  ETH Zurich
- Summary:
  Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.
The breakthrough, described in the journal Science, introduces a different approach to quantum computer design. Instead of closely integrating information processing and storage, as many existing systems do, Chu's team has developed an architecture that gives these functions more distinct roles.
Quantum Memory Inspired by Conventional Computers
The researchers drew inspiration from the basic design of everyday digital computers. In a conventional machine, the central processing unit (CPU) carries out calculations while information is held separately in working memory, commonly called random access memory (RAM). The arrangement of these components plays an important role in determining how efficiently a computer operates.
Chu's quantum system follows a similar principle. A superconducting qubit acts as the processing and control unit, performing a role comparable to that of the central processing unit (CPU). Meanwhile, a separate quantum memory temporarily holds the information needed during calculations, allowing the processor to retrieve and modify it as necessary.
The major difference lies in how that information is stored.
"In our quantum working memory, however, information is not stored electromagnetically -- as is usually the case today -- but rather in the form of mechanical vibrations," explains Chu.
Quantum computers take advantage of unusual properties of quantum physics, including superposition, which allows quantum systems to exist in combinations of different states, and entanglement, which creates powerful connections between quantum states. These effects could eventually enable quantum machines to tackle certain extremely complicated calculations much faster than conventional computers, including some problems that are currently beyond their practical capabilities.
Why Vibrating Quantum Memory Could Be Better
One of the greatest challenges in quantum computing is maintaining precise control over quantum information. The states used for calculations are delicate, and even small disturbances can cause information to be lost. To perform calculations reliably, the processor and memory must interact closely enough to transfer and manipulate quantum states with high precision.
In the new system, microscopic structures called mechanical resonators hold information in particular patterns of vibration. When the superconducting qubit needs that information, it accesses the stored vibrational state, performs the required operation, and returns the modified information to memory.
Many existing quantum computers instead use electromagnetic memory alongside superconducting qubits. Researchers understand these technologies well, and they can be combined to provide extremely accurate control over quantum states, including reading, changing, and manipulating stored information.
However, electromagnetic memory systems have a significant disadvantage. They can occupy considerable space, making it difficult to expand experimental quantum devices into the larger, more capable computers that researchers and industries ultimately need.
Mechanical resonators offer several potential advantages. They are substantially smaller, allowing more compact designs. They can also support numerous different patterns of vibration, providing opportunities to store more information simultaneously than conventional electromagnetic memory.
Another important benefit is that mechanical vibrations can preserve quantum states for longer periods before the stored information begins to fade. Longer storage times could make it easier to carry out complicated calculations that require information to remain available throughout multiple processing steps.
New Quantum Computer Passes Major Tests
The research published in Science provides the first experimental demonstration that mechanical resonators can work together with superconducting qubits to carry out quantum computations. The results establish that vibration-based memory is a feasible alternative to electromagnetic storage.
The achievement goes beyond simply storing information. Chu's team demonstrated that its architecture can handle both relatively straightforward calculations and more demanding quantum operations.
To evaluate the system, the researchers tested two important computational techniques: the quantum Fourier transform and period finding. Both are fundamental tools in quantum computing and require a computer to coordinate multiple quantum states with considerable precision.
"The Quantum Fourier Transform is a fundamental computational procedure required for many quantum algorithms. The period-finding algorithm we implemented served as a demonstration of how this procedure can be used," explains Igor Kladaric, doctoral student in Chu's team and co-author of the publication.
Successfully completing these tasks requires the system to store, control, and maintain coherent relationships among multiple quantum states at the same time. The experiments showed that the new architecture can meet these requirements, providing strong evidence that it can support genuine quantum computation rather than simply function as a memory device.
A Promising Step Toward Powerful Quantum Computers
One of the most significant findings is that the new system can, in principle, carry out all the fundamental operations needed for arbitrary quantum computations. This means the architecture has the essential capabilities required for a programmable, general-purpose quantum computer.
However, demonstrating those capabilities in an experimental chip is only the beginning. The next major challenge is scaling the technology to larger systems with greater processing power while preserving the precision and reliability demonstrated in the laboratory.
Chu and her colleagues are continuing to investigate how their approach can be developed further. Its long-term success will depend on whether mechanical quantum memory can remain effective as more components and increasingly complex computations are added.
Practical quantum computers powerful enough for widespread scientific and industrial applications are still some distance away. Nevertheless, by showing that tiny mechanical vibrations can serve as compact, capable quantum memory, the ETH Zurich team has demonstrated a promising new route toward making those machines a reality.

Materials provided by ETH Zurich. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yu Yang, Igor Kladarić, Martynas Skrabulis, Michael Eichenberger, Stefano Marti, Simon Storz, Jonathan Esche, Raquel García Bellés, Max-Emanuel Kern, Andraz Omahen, Arianne Brooks, Marius Bild, Matteo Fadel, Yiwen Chu. Mechanical resonator–based quantum computing. Science, 2026; 392 (6801): 972 DOI: 10.1126/science.aef4139
