articles.title: GTA VI player gets 30-day PSN suspension for sharing screenshot of in-game nudity with friend
articles.text:
WTF?! Here's an important reminder for anyone who uses messages over the PlayStation Network: don't send any nude images, even if they come from a video game. One GTA VI player discovered the consequences of breaking this rule when they sent a picture of the game's nudist colony, taken with the in-game camera. His punishment was a 30-day suspension from the PSN's social features.
X user DerrickGott007 posted the notification he received from PlayStation, along with a warning not to send images that contain nudity. He sent a friend an image of GTA VI's nudist beach, which the company says breached its code of conduct set out in its terms of service. It classifies the offending content as pornographic or obscene, earning him a month-long ban.
There's also a warning that any offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just the PSN social features.
 – DerrickGott007💎 (@derrickgott007) November 20, 2026
PlayStation's code of conduct lists several types of prohibited content, which apply to text, images, videos, and links sent in private chats or group messages. The explicit or graphic media section notes that sharing sexually explicit, nude, or excessively violent images/videos can trigger bans, even if captured from an age-restricted game and sent to a friend, which is what happened in this case.
It does seem strange to apply these rules to content found in a game, especially one that is now driving up sales of the PlayStation 5 and PS5 Pro, but the company says this sort of action is necessary to protect PlayStation and its players, apparently.
GTA VI, of course, has lived up to the pre-release hype. Take-Two confirmed that day-one retail sales of Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI reached an estimated $3.79 billion, making it the biggest launch in entertainment history.
The latest entry in the long-running franchise has a Metascore of 99, putting it level with Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game ever. That's quite a contrast to the user score, which stands at just 5.6. A lot of the complaints are over claims that the story and game itself have become too "woke," though there are several mentions of bugs and the 30fps max framerate that can dip even lower at times.
However, with more than 32.5 million pre-orders, the 43.9K negative reviews represent a minuscule fraction of buyers, and Metacritic does not require users to prove they own or have played a game to submit a rating or review.

articles.title: Z.ai ran the same 28 layers twice — and claims its 750B model can rival a 3-trillion-parameter one
articles.text:
Z.ai ran the same 28 layers twice — and claims its 750B model can rival a 3-trillion-parameter one
Z.ai released GLM-5.4 on Monday, introducing a Loop Transformer architecture that executes the same layers multiple times to increase computational depth without adding parameters.
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters…
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters, although it has not published full-scale benchmarks to support that comparison.
Built by continuing to train GLM-5, the model runs a shared block of 28 layers twice during inference. Z.ai developed the architecture for demanding coding and agentic workloads.
Depth without more parameters
Z.ai chose to modify a pretrained model after earlier experiments showed that looped Transformers trained from scratch performed worse than conventional models given the same pretraining compute.
Repeating layers at this scale created problems with activation stability and attention caching. Z.ai introduced per-token gates to regulate updates to the residual stream and prevent activation norms from growing across iterations.
GLM-5.4 shares the first iteration’s KV cache and maintains a separate sliding window for the second pass, avoiding the memory cost of duplicating the entire attention history at context lengths of up to one million tokens. The model also reuses sparse attention indices between iterations, which Z.ai says had negligible impact on performance in its testing.
Z.ai developed fused inference kernels to reduce intermediate memory reads and writes during repeated layer execution.
What the 30B benchmarks show
Z.ai tested the architecture at 1 billion, 4 billion, 30 billion, and 750 billion parameters, but the detailed benchmark results come from the 30-billion-parameter model.
In those tests, the looped model outperformed a conventional Transformer of the same size on math, scientific reasoning, and long-context tasks, despite requiring about 10% more training compute.
The model also generated 10% to 14% fewer output tokens on benchmarks including MMLU-Pro and GPQA-Diamond. Z.ai attributes the shorter responses to reasoning handled within the repeated layers rather than through additional generated tokens.
From code to robot arms
Z.ai calls its approach Generalized Coding. Its GLM-5.4 demonstrations include building games with physics and combat systems, creating 3D environments with GLSL shaders, and designing a six-axis robotic arm in FreeCAD.
In a post on X, Z.ai head Zixuan Li reported improvements over GLM-5.3 in test writing, code QA, feature development, bug fixes, and terminal-based tasks, although the company has not published the underlying evaluations.
Performance has varied since launch. Z.ai claims throughput of up to 200 tokens per second during off-peak hours, dropping to 70 to 80 during peak traffic.
One developer reported speeds of 150 to 170 tokens per second initially, followed by reports of 40 to 50 tokens per second and traffic errors later in the day. Controlled comparisons of inference latency and cost remain unavailable.
Z.ai also acknowledges that GLM-5.4 can spend excessive time reasoning through tasks.
Z.ai also acknowledges that GLM-5.4 can spend excessive time reasoning through tasks. The company is exploring adaptive computation to limit additional iterations to tokens that need them.
GLM-5.4 is available through the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode, and Z.ai Chat, with vision support and a one-million-token context window.

articles.title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
articles.text:
Agoda has introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce code coupling and enforce domain boundaries without rewriting the existing service. The approach combines component-based code organization, automated architecture checks, and incremental migration. The team reported 64% shorter median code review time and 34% shorter time to initial substantive feedback for framework-backed changes compared with legacy code.
The change addresses growing maintenance challenges in BAPI, which coordinates cancellations, booking amendments, refunds, and customer communications. Agoda extracted the API from its aging core monolith in 2019 through a largely line-by-line migration. As development increased, merge requests more than quadrupled between 2022 and 2025, while some files exceeded 4,000 lines.
The team characterized the migration as a tactical design trade-off, drawing on John K. Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design,
We had deliberately traded a strategic design approach for a tactical one to prioritize speed to market. This tactical mindset was exactly what the business needed at the time.
Rather than undertake a complete rewrite, the team introduced architectural boundaries incrementally.
The framework, called Platform, organizes code around business domains such as cancellations, rebooking, and payments rather than technical layers. Each component encapsulates its business logic and data access behind defined interfaces, with application, service, repository, and model layers contained within the component. This package-by-component approach aims to localize changes and reduce dependencies between business domains.
Platform framework boundaries inside a domain module (Source: Agoda Blog Post)
Agoda uses the Data Mapper pattern to keep repository-specific models, including database entities and API payloads, out of business logic. Typed builders centralize object creation and transformations, making it easier for developers to find where domain objects and service inputs are constructed.
The team also uses ArchUnit to encode architectural constraints as automated tests in continuous integration. For example, repository-specific models can only be accessed by their respective repositories. Violations fail the build rather than relying on code reviewers to identify unauthorized dependencies manually.
The team described these constraints as architectural fitness functions, a concept discussed by Neal Ford and Mark Richards in Software Architecture: The Hard Parts. One engineer explained:
By codifying our layer boundaries into an ArchUnit test suite, our CI pipeline serves as an automated guardrail, catching structural drift on every pull request before a human reviewer ever sees it.
Platform is now the default for new modules, while existing functionality is migrated incrementally when feature development provides an opportunity.
Agoda compared framework-backed and legacy merge requests in Q2 2026. Median review completion time was 1.08 hours for framework-backed changes, compared with 3.02 hours for legacy changes. Time to first substantive feedback was 10.34 hours versus 15.77 hours. Between June and August, framework-backed changes also used 29% fewer AI prompts per 100 changed lines, although median prompts per merge request were similar (20 vs. 22). Agoda cautioned that the AI findings were directional due to the short observation period. A related approach is Spring Modulith, which provides module verification and dependency-cycle checks for Spring Boot applications.

articles.title: Is Silicon Valley turning its back on Europe? Plug and Play's Thomas Bigagli weighs in
articles.text:
Sequoia Capital’s decision to close its London office has reignited debate about the future of European innovation and the commitment of US investors to the continent – especially amid other departures including Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. However, not all US investors in Europe share this gloomy outlook.
Thomas Bigagli, Partner and Managing Director at Plug and Play, believes the move says more about Sequoia’s investment strategy than Europe’s ability to produce successful startups.
On 4 November 2026, Silicon Valley-based Sequoia Capital announced it would close its London office, established in 2020, as part of a broader restructuring. The changes also include merging its early-stage and growth investment teams, simplifying its partnership structure, and discontinuing its Arc accelerator and Scouts programme.
The announcement follows similar decisions by Andreessen Horowitz, which closed its London office in 2025, and Coatue, which withdrew in 2024, raising questions about whether international investors are reconsidering their physical presence in Europe.
Speaking to EU-Startups, Thomas offered a different interpretation.
“I wouldn’t necessarily interpret Sequoia’s decision as a lack of confidence in European entrepreneurship, but rather as a reflection of an evolving investment strategy and operating model. […] That is fundamentally different from saying that Europe no longer presents attractive investment opportunities.”
Investing in Europe, or investing in its future?
According to Thomas, Sequoia is moving towards a leaner, more centralised organisation capable of investing internationally without maintaining offices in every market. For established startups seeking growth capital and access to US networks, this approach can be effective.
“However, it raises an interesting question about how international venture capital firms approach foreign markets: are you investing in an ecosystem, or are you genuinely invested in that ecosystem? There is a fundamental difference.”
For Plug and Play, a Silicon Valley-based investment and innovation platform founded in 2006 by Saeed Amidi, maintaining local relationships remains central to its strategy. The firm operates across more than 70 locations worldwide, including over 25 in Europe, and works with more than 600 corporate partners.
Its European journey began in Berlin in 2013, when it became the first investor in German fintech N26. Since then, its portfolio has expanded to include companies such as Owkin, Zama, Einride and FINN.
Thomas explained that local teams enable investors to identify founders before fundraising begins, establish connections with universities and understand the needs of corporations and institutions. These relationships can also translate into commercial opportunities for portfolio companies.
“Technology travels fast, but trust takes time.”
Plug and Play doubles down
This long-term approach appears to be paying off. According to a PitchBook ranking cited by Thomas, Plug and Play is the most active US investor in European venture capital by deal count.
“What I find particularly interesting about this ranking is that it is not the result of a recent strategic decision to invest in Europe. It reflects more than a decade of continuous investment in European ecosystems.”
In 2022, the firm accelerated its regional investment activity by establishing a dedicated European investment committee and strengthening local decision-making. Thomas says its European portfolio has more than doubled since then.
Looking ahead, Plug and Play plans to develop additional investment vehicles alongside European institutional investors, family offices and corporate limited partners. It is also strengthening its university partnerships and developing industry-focused AI Centres of Excellence to connect research, startups and established businesses.
“We believe that some of the most valuable investment opportunities and competitive advantages are built through years of developing relationships, earning trust, and actively contributing to local ecosystems, rather than simply accessing them when attractive investment opportunities emerge.”
Despite Sequoia’s departure, there are indications that American capital remains interested in European startups. According to PitchBook’s Q3 2026 European Venture Report, US investors participated in 22.2% of European venture rounds during the first nine months of 2026, the highest proportion recorded this decade.
Recent EU-Startips coverage from 2026 provides further evidence that US investors remain active in Europe. On 17 November 2026, less than two weeks after announcing the closure of its London office, Sequoia Capital co-led a €4.5 billion Series C round for British AI drug-discovery company Isomorphic Labs, alongside Greenoaks, with Andreessen Horowitz also participating. Earlier in the year, Sequoia led ElevenLabs’ €424 million Series D, while Andreessen Horowitz backed Stockholm-based Pit’s €13.6 million funding round.
Plug and Play, meanwhile, participated in Barcelona-based NeuralTrust’s €17.2 million Seed round, Lithuania’s Axiology (€5 million), France’s Orakl Oncology (€30 million), Swiss Aylight Zurich (€4.5 million), and French Davis AI (€4.6 million).
Thomas expects this participation to continue, although investors may become more selective.
“You cannot fully understand what is happening in Paris, London, Stockholm, Munich, Vienna, Warsaw, Lisbon, Milan or Barcelona simply by sitting in Silicon Valley. […] Ultimately, the importance of having a local presence depends on where and how you intend to create value as an investor.”
Europe’s next big test: Scaling up
Thomas sees particularly strong opportunities where AI intersects with Europe’s established industrial and scientific capabilities, including robotics, advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, energy, healthcare, space technology and cybersecurity.
“I believe Europe represents one of the most compelling and, in certain sectors, underestimated technology investment opportunities globally. [..] From an investment perspective, the best-performing European venture capital funds can generate returns comparable to their US counterparts.”
However, he acknowledges that the continent still faces substantial obstacles to building global technology companies, particularly fragmented markets, limited growth-stage financing, slower technology adoption and weaker exit opportunities compared with the US.
“Compared with the US, Europe suffers from market fragmentation, slower decision-making and technology adoption, limited access to growth capital, and insufficient institutional investment in venture capital. […] Europe does not have a talent or technology creation problem. It has a commercialisation, financing, scaling, and liquidity problem.”
For Thomas, addressing these structural weaknesses will require stronger European growth funds, greater institutional investment and more opportunities for successful companies to remain and scale within the continent.
“We need more success stories like Spotify, Revolut, and ElevenLabs. […] Europe should not aspire to become the next Silicon Valley. It should build its own model of technological leadership, inspired by its unique competitive advantages.”
Where does this leave Plug and Play and the like?
Ultimately, Sequoia’s restructuring illustrates how different investment philosophies are shaping international venture capital. While some investors are prioritising centralised operations, others see local presence as a competitive advantage.
“We want to be more than an American investor investing in Europe. We want to be a long-term partner in building Europe’s next generation of global technology leaders.”
And although Thomas would not be surprised if additional US firms followed Sequoia’s example, Plug and Play has no intention of joining them.
“We don’t see this as a reason to reconsider our European presence. Quite the opposite.”

articles.title: GL.iNet Routers, KVMs Compromised via Remote Management Service Flaw
articles.text:
GL.iNet has warned customers that a threat actor exploited a vulnerability in its cloud-based remote management service to deliver malware to some routers and KVM devices.
China-based networking hardware maker GL.iNet is well known for its pocket-sized travel routers and Comet KVM devices. The devices can be managed remotely through its GoodCloud platform.
The vendor discovered the remote management service vulnerability leveraged by the attacker on November 20 and has since patched it.
However, it noted that the fix doesn’t remove the malware from infected devices — customers need to install a separate “security firmware” for that. GL.iNet recommends installing the security firmware on all devices, even those with no signs of infection.
It remains unclear who is behind the attack and how many devices were compromised.
It’s also unclear whether the attackers reached the computers connected to compromised KVM devices.
“As a precaution, check for unfamiliar programs, browser extensions or user accounts; unexpected startup items or scheduled tasks; and unusual settings changes or network activity. Run a full scan with up-to-date security software,” the company recommends for KVM devices.
Security and networking firm RemoteToHome Consulting, which manages a large number of GL.iNet routers, has been investigating the incident. Based on its code analysis, the attack worked because the GoodCloud software on the routers ran commands from cloud messages without checking them. GL.iNet has not confirmed this information.
RemoteToHome reported that most of the nearly 200 routers it checked appeared to be impacted, either by this new attack or an older backdoor that appears to date back to September 2025. RemoteToHome says it doesn’t know how that older backdoor was installed.
SecurityWeek has reached out to GL.iNet for additional information and will update this article if it responds.

articles.title: COLORFUL Launches iGame B850I MINI W OC Motherboard for Compact PC Enthusiasts
articles.text:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
COLORFUL Launches iGame B850I MINI W OC Motherboard for Compact PC Enthusiasts
Colorful Technology Company Limited, a leading brand in gaming PC components, gaming laptops, and Hi-fi audio products, announces the launch of the iGame B850I MINI W OC, a white edition of its previously released iGame B850I MINI OC motherboard. Designed for enthusiasts building high-performance small form factor (SFF) systems, the new white model retains the same powerful hardware, overclocking capabilities, and compact Mini-ITX design as its black counterpart, making it an ideal choice for white-themed PC builds.
The original iGame B850I MINI OC has earned recognition among enthusiasts for its industrial-inspired design and impressive overclocking capabilities. Responding to demand for an alternative color scheme, COLORFUL now introduces the iGame B850I MINI W OC, bringing the same performance-focused platform to builders who prefer a clean, all-white aesthetic.9+2+1 Phase Power Design and Advanced Overclocking
The iGame B850I MINI W OC features a robust 9+2+1 phase power delivery design, providing sufficient power to support high-end AMD Ryzen/AMD Ryzen X3D processors, including the AMD Ryzen 9 9950X. It also integrates an external clock generator for asynchronous overclocking, giving enthusiasts greater flexibility when fine-tuning CPU frequencies and system performance.
The motherboard's BIOS also includes COLORFUL's proprietary X3D AI Turbo Mode, which uses one-click optimization to unlock additional gaming performance from AMD Ryzen 9000 Series X3D processors.
Dual PCIe 5.0 M.2 Storage and Extensive Connectivity
Despite its compact Mini-ITX form factor, the iGame B850I MINI W OC offers extensive expansion and connectivity options. It features two onboard PCIe 5.0 M.2 slots for high-speed NVMe storage, alongside eight high-speed USB ports on the rear I/O panel, including a USB-C 20 Gbps connection.
This combination provides connectivity and storage expansion that rivals larger microATX motherboards, making it well-suited to compact gaming systems without compromising essential features.
White Edition for SFF Enthusiasts
The iGame B850I MINI W OC completes COLORFUL's iGame MINI OC lineup with a white alternative to the original black model. Both motherboards share the same hardware specifications and overclocking capabilities, allowing builders to choose their preferred aesthetic without sacrificing performance.
Whether paired with white graphics cards, cooling components, and chassis, or incorporated into a contrasting build, the iGame B850I MINI W OC offers enthusiasts another option for creating powerful and visually coordinated small form factor PCs.
SpecificationsPricing and Availability
The COLORFUL iGame B850I MINI W OC motherboard is set to launch in China on November 23rd, 2026, with global availability expected to follow shortly after. It will retail for 1,599 RMB (approximately US$239). Contact your local COLORFUL representative for regional pricing and availability.

articles.title: Los 11 días que conmovieron al mundo: la caída y el regreso de Jensen Huang a Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang cofundó Nvidia hace más de tres décadas, la convirtió en la empresa más valiosa del sector tecnológico y se transformó en una figura central de la carrera global por la inteligencia artificial.
El 29 de octubre de 2026, un artículo de The New York Times desencadenó una crisis que en menos de dos semanas lo sacó del cargo que había ocupado desde la fundación de la compañía —y que, once días después de su salida, lo devolvió a él.
El origen de la crisis
The New York Times publicó el 29 de octubre que Huang mantenía una relación cercana con Alice Huang —sin vínculo familiar con él—, empresaria radicada en Singapur que dirige una firma llamada Megaspeed, bajo investigación en Estados Unidos por la presunta facilitación de envíos de chips Nvidia avanzados a empresas chinas en violación de los controles de exportación vigentes.
Las autoridades de inteligencia estadounidenses sospechaban que Alice Huang actuaba en representación de los servicios de inteligencia de China, acusación que Beijing rechazó. Según The Information, la relación entre ambos habría facilitado el envío de al menos USD 7.500 millones en chips a empresas chinas.
La publicación fue suficiente para que legisladores republicanos reclamaran una sesión cerrada con Huang y para que el directorio de Nvidia quedara bajo presión pública desde el primer día.
La semana que lo hundió
El 8 de noviembre, Huang reconoció ante los empleados de Nvidia que había sido infiel a su esposa, sin identificar a la persona involucrada. Ese mismo día, el directorio abrió una investigación independiente.
El 9 de noviembre, Nvidia y Huang fueron demandados en una acción colectiva de accionistas que los acusaba de fraude por ocultar los vínculos del CEO con Alice Huang y su impacto sobre la compañía.
Dos días después, el senador republicano Kevin Cramer pidió públicamente su renuncia, al sostener que la relación con una sospechosa de espionaje dejaba a la compañía expuesta a presiones externas.
El 11 de noviembre, The New York Times reveló una segunda relación: Huang también había mantenido un vínculo con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, cargo que la ponía en la línea de reporte directa con el CEO.
Las acciones de la compañía perdieron 8,6% en operaciones fuera de horario esa misma noche.
Ese mismo día, Taiwan revocó el permiso de ingreso de Alice Huang al país, en una señal de que el caso había adquirido dimensión diplomática regional. El directorio se reunió de urgencia. Al día siguiente, el 12 de noviembre, se anunció la renuncia con efecto inmediato.
Colette Kress, directora financiera de la empresa, fue designada CEO interina mientras el directorio iniciaba la búsqueda de un reemplazo permanente.
El costo en los mercados
La incertidumbre que siguió a la salida de Huang se reflejó en la cotización de Nvidia. Entre el anuncio de la renuncia y el punto más bajo registrado durante los once días siguientes, el título llegó a cotizar a USD 125,53, un 35,5% por debajo del cierre récord anterior.
La pérdida de valor acumulada desde el máximo histórico superaba un tercio del precio de la acción en su mejor momento.
La primera señal pública de Huang
El 17 de noviembre, cinco días después de su salida, Huang rompió el silencio con un mensaje en la red social X.
“Desde mi partida, he visto un torrente de llamados de empleados, inversores, socios comerciales y clientes de Nvidia para que regrese como CEO. Si el directorio decide que mi regreso es en el mejor interés de nuestros accionistas, nuestros empleados, la empresa y de Estados Unidos, sería un honor responder a esos llamados y volver como CEO”, escribió según publicó The Wall Street Journal.
La respuesta fue amplia: más de 190.000 personas —entre accionistas, exempleados, socios y referentes del sector tecnológico— firmaron una petición en línea por su restitución.
El presidente Donald Trump también se pronunció a favor: “Ciertamente no me molestaría verlo de vuelta”, respondió ante periodistas.
El mismo día, el presidente del directorio, Harvey C. Jones, descartó el regreso en declaraciones a CNBC: “El directorio no tiene intención de restituirlo”.
El giro del 23 de noviembre
Seis días después de ese “no” público, el directorio votó en forma unánime la restitución de Huang como presidente ejecutivo y miembro del directorio, con efecto inmediato, según informó la agencia AP.
En el comunicado oficial difundido desde Santa Clara, California, Nvidia explicó que la decisión se tomó “luego de una serie de conversaciones y reuniones con Huang, tras las cuales el directorio quedó conforme respecto a su franqueza y su capacidad de liderazgo”.
El directorio también recibió aportes de altos funcionarios del gobierno estadounidense y concluyó que el regreso “no implica ningún riesgo para la seguridad nacional”.
“El directorio cree que Jensen es la persona adecuada para liderar Nvidia y que su restitución es en el mejor interés de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”, afirmó Jones, quien permanece como presidente del directorio. Kress retoma sus funciones como directora financiera.
Lo que queda abierto
La restitución de Huang no cierra todas las cuestiones pendientes. Nvidia aclaró en el comunicado que el comité de directores independientes constituido para investigar los hechos relacionados con la presunta operación de inteligencia extranjera continuará su trabajo “hasta su conclusión”.
La empresa señaló que Huang “apoya plenamente la investigación y está comprometido a cooperar con ella”.
El 1 de diciembre, Huang está citado a comparecer ante tres comités de la Cámara de Representantes de Estados Unidos —Relaciones Exteriores, Inteligencia y el Comité Selecto sobre China— para ser interrogado sobre las denuncias vinculadas al acceso de Beijing a chips avanzados de la compañía, según informó Nvidia en su comunicado oficial.

articles.title: Google dá prazo para apps de Android ganharem versões dobráveis
articles.text:
Google dá prazo para apps de Android ganharem versões dobráveis
Apps que não se adequarem às regras de telas dobráveis perderão o direito de publicar novas versões e terão menos alcance na Google Play Store.
O Google determinou que, a partir de abril de 2027, desenvolvedores atendam ao Nível 3 (Tier 3) das diretrizes de qualidade adaptável do Android para dispositivos dobráveis. Na prática, isso significa que um app não poderá funcionar de modo improvisado quando expandido para uma tela maior.
Talvez você já tenha passado pela experiência de usar um app em celular convencional e, ao abri-lo em um smartphone dobrável ou até em um tablet, notar que ele ficou com elementos desalinhados ou com grandes áreas não aproveitadas, por exemplo. É justamente esse tipo de situação que o Google quer evitar com as novas diretrizes.
Para tanto, há uma série de exigências a serem seguidas. Uma delas determina que a interface do aplicativo continue funcional quando houver mudança de orientação ou de dimensões, o que ocorre quando o usuário abre ou fecha a tela dobrável.
Outra exigência determina que o app ocupe de modo adequado o espaço oferecido por uma tela expandida, não podendo exibir seu conteúdo como se estivesse em um celular convencional (com visor estreito). Vai além: o aplicativo também deve suportar modos de múltiplas janelas.
Também a partir de abril de 2027, os desenvolvedores deverão fornecer pelo menos três capturas de tela de seus aplicativos registradas em celulares dobráveis, de modo que os usuários possam verificar, já na Google Play Store, como eles funcionam com diferentes configurações de tela.
O Google comenta as novas exigências:
Ao investir nesses dispositivos de última geração, os usuários esperam que os apps e jogos favoritos ofereçam uma transição perfeita e suave entre os estados dobrado e desdobrado, além de novas experiências que só são possíveis em telas dobráveis.
Mekka Okereke, gerente geral de apps na Google Play Store
Os aplicativos que não seguirem as condições do chamado Nível 3 não poderão ter novas versões disponibilizadas na Google Play Store, muito menos publicarem atualizações.
Note que os aplicativos já disponíveis na loja serão mantidos por lá, mas poderão ter sua visibilidade reduzida se não atenderem às novas regras.
Observe que o Nível 3 consiste em um conjunto básico de novas regras. Com o passar do tempo, os desenvolvedores deverão adequar os seus aplicativos ao Nível 2 e ao Nível 1:
- Nível 2: o aplicativo deve suportar layouts responsivos com múltiplos painéis, evitando elementos esticados desproporcionalmente, bem como oferecer suporte básico a acessórios como teclado, mouse e trackpad;
- Nível 1: deve permitir usos em modos livro e mesa (com o aparelho parcialmente dobrado), continuidade da câmera, picture-in-picture interativo, entre outros.
Os Níveis 2 e 1 não são obrigatórios, razão pela qual ainda não têm prazo de adoção. Porém, eles deverão fazer parte do programa de qualidade da Google Play Store em algum momento, quando então serão exigidos.

articles.title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
articles.text:
President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”
The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk.
In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.
There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”
Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.
Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”
Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below.
The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

articles.title: Could you be Canada’s next top student entrepreneur?
articles.text:
Connor Kapahi was still completing his PhD when he set out to commercialize a medical device that could detect one of the leading causes of irreversible vision loss.
His company, Mandel Diagnostics, was developing a tool that could screen patients for early signs of macular degeneration in just two minutes. Between his academic research and the demands of building a company, Kapahi had plenty on his plate.
“Ultimately, we need to help young people experience that failure isn’t the opposite of success, it is often part of the process of getting to success.”
Catherine Fowler,
Enactus Canada
“I found out early on that working on a startup while finishing school didn’t mean I was splitting my time 50/50,” said Kapahi, who is CEO and Founder of Mandel Diagnostics. “It was more like one-third of my time on my PhD research, one-third on the startup, and one-third worrying that I wasn’t balancing the other two goals correctly.”
Kapahi said much of his anxiety stemmed from not knowing whether customers would actually pay for the device. According to research from RBC, nearly 60 percent of young Canadians say a fear of failure would stop them from starting a business.
For the last three decades, Enactus Canada has worked to make entrepreneurship more accessible to postsecondary students, and through its Student Entrepreneur National Competition the organization is encouraging more young founders to take a chance on themselves.
Making room for failure
Catherine Fowler, President and CEO of Enactus Canada, understands why young people might hesitate to pursue entrepreneurship. Even those with promising ideas or skills can find themselves overwhelmed by everything it takes to run a business.
“Suddenly you are navigating accounting, technology, human resources, sales, and long-term strategic planning,” Fowler said. “Each new challenge can feel like another opportunity to fail.”
Still, she believes that students should have opportunities to experiment with entrepreneurship while they still have access to resources and a community of support.
“The postsecondary years are a pivotal time in a young person’s life,” Fowler said. “Students are exploring their interests, considering their futures, and discovering what they are capable of achieving.”
Enactus Canada is a registered charity that supports postsecondary students through entrepreneurial education and experiential learning. Its Student Entrepreneur National Competition, now celebrating its 30th anniversary, gives full-time postsecondary students running their own businesses a chance to get advice from established entrepreneurs, make connections, and compete for funding.
According to Fowler, the competition also gives students a chance to confront their fear of failure and learn from it, rather than avoid it altogether.
“Ultimately, we need to help young people experience that failure isn’t the opposite of success, it is often part of the process of getting to success,” she added.
The competition follows a multi-stage process. An initial group of 30 entrepreneurs receives feedback on their applications, with 12 advancing to a video pitch round and three ultimately selected to share a live presentation at the national final.
Judges assess participants’ business models, market knowledge, traction, and growth potential, and provide feedback at each stage. Those who do not advance can return in subsequent years if they remain eligible.
The value of a good introduction
Kapahi’s involvement with the competition began when an Enactus representative saw him pitch at another event and encouraged him to apply. By then, Kapahi had already participated in several startup competitions, but he saw this as an opportunity to share the story of how he turned his research into a business while completing his studies.
He ultimately won the 2026 national title and its $10,000 prize, which has helped the company commit two of its eye-screening tools to medical missions serving patients both abroad and in remote Canadian communities. The devices will be used by optometrists providing eye care in underserved communities, allowing Mandel Diagnostics to see how its technology performs in challenging clinical environments.
Kapahi valued the connections he made through the competition. “You never know who you’ll meet or what doors they can open for you,” he said.
Having started Mandel Diagnostics in the Waterloo Region, where there is an established startup community, Kapahi knew the value of advice from other founders. He found a similar network through Enactus Canada.
“Their experience, advice, and their ability to make key introductions is an extremely valuable resource that will continue to guide Mandel Diagnostics forward,” he added.
Thirty years of student entrepreneurship
When the Student Entrepreneur National Competition launched in 1997, entrepreneurship was rarely taught in postsecondary institutions, according to Fowler, and students had few avenues to secure funding or get exposure.
The first national champion operated a retail soccer business. Last year, Diana Virgovicova won with Xatoms, which is developing advanced water purification technology with AI and quantum chemistry. Kapahi followed in 2026 with Mandel Diagnostics.
According to Fowler, the range of businesses represented over the years shows how new technologies have expanded the possibilities for student entrepreneurs, although she still sees familiar qualities in the founders who participate.
“At their core, they are still the same ambitious, resourceful, self-starting individuals who see opportunities where others see obstacles and are willing to take meaningful risks to turn their ideas into reality,” Fowler said.
Enactus Canada is accepting nominations for its next Student Entrepreneur National Competition until December 4. Eligible entrepreneurs must be full-time postsecondary students who own at least 25 percent of their businesses. Students can either nominate themselves or be nominated by someone else in as little as ten minutes.
Eligible nominees will be invited to submit full applications by January 10, 2027, with the top 30 announced on January 13. Three national finalists will receive an all-expenses-paid trip to Toronto to present their ventures to a live audience on April 28.
Fowler believes the most important step is getting young entrepreneurs to put themselves forward in the first place.
“Don’t let the application be the barrier,” she said. “You don’t need a perfect business plan or to have everything figured out. The experience itself, regardless of how far you advance, can help you become a stronger entrepreneur.”
Kapahi, for his part, encouraged aspiring founders to start by speaking with potential customers, understanding their problems, and determining whether there is demand for their solution.
“If you can find customers desperate for what you’re building and willing to pay for it, then do it,” Kapahi said. “Whether you win Enactus Student Entrepreneur of the Year or not, you’ll have a far stronger foundation for your business.”

articles.title: The Enigma of SoftBank’s $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Attempt
articles.text:
SK Hynix, the world’s second-largest memory chipmaker, is in the news again, this time for being the target of a trillion-dollar buyout attempt by the Japanese tech conglomerate SoftBank. According to a report published in The Information on Friday (Nov. 20), SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son recently explored a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix.
A SoftBank spokesperson responded in a short statement: “SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration.” SK Hynix said the company had no knowledge of the matter and that any outreach happened entirely on the SoftBank side.
Apparently, Son sounded out a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix and then shelved it. The most likely hurdles could be financing, chaebol governance, and the Korean Government’s view of the memory industry as a strategic asset. The latter makes it a deal that could never close anyway. And there were no negotiations or a term sheet.
But that’s only half the story. Especially when the report didn’t establish Son’s specific rationale for choosing SK Hynix. For starters, the trillion-dollar figure is far higher than SK’s $577 billion market valuation recorded on Friday, Nov. 20. So, the floated trillion-dollar price is 1.7× SK Hynix’s current market value.
The largest tech industry acquisition on record is SpaceX’s $250 billion takeover of xAI in 2026, combining aerospace, satellite, and AI operations. Moreover, SoftBank’s balance sheet is already stretched by its AI bets on OpenAI and Stargate; it recently sold its entire Nvidia stake to raise cash. It’s also mobilizing its stake in Arm to secure funding for investments in OpenAI and Stargate.
So, the question is how SoftBank would arrange the sheer scale of this trillion-dollar funding. In retrospect, it looks more like a financing inquiry. There were no price negotiations and no indications of commitments from Wall Street banks. In other words, it wasn’t a takeover attempt, but an early-stage exploration.
More importantly, there is literally no chance that the Korean Government would approve such a deal. Furthermore, while Korean Government approval is almost unimaginable, SK Hynix has no reason to sell either. That makes this whole episode a non-starter. So, what’s this fuss all about? If Masayoshi Son didn’t actually want to buy SK Hynix, what would he gain from this buyout story, for which he paid nothing?
What Son wants
Industry observers believe this buyout attempt signals Son’s grand plan to build an AI empire, which requires owning every layer of the value chain. Start with Arm, which sits at the semiconductor design IP layer. It controls chip designs that underpin a range of AI processors; furthermore, Arm’s neutral licensing platform effectively serves the entire chip design industry.
Next, SoftBank snapped Graphcore in 2024 and Ampere Computing in 2025, the two upstarts developing AI processors. The Japanese conglomerate has also acquired a significant stake in Intel. At the model layer, powered by AI processors, SoftBank has committed a massive investment in OpenAI.
At the AI infrastructure level, SoftBank has poured nearly $500 billion into the Stargate joint venture and the acquisition of data center investor DigitalBridge. The Japanese giant is also the largest shareholder in SB Energy, which runs data center and power businesses.
What’s missing here is memory, which has become a chokepoint in the AI buildout. In fact, memory suppliers have become more important to the companies designing AI accelerators and building data centers to run them. And on SoftBank’s AI buildup map, one layer is empty: memory.
It’s worth mentioning that SK Hynix is a pioneer in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which enables processors to handle the vast volumes of data required for AI computing. In 2025, SK Hynix’s HBM revenue more than doubled year on year. Nvidia is SK Hynix’s largest customer, accounting for 14.8% of its revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and according to TrendForce, Nvidia is expected to place about two-thirds of its HBM4 orders with SK Hynix.
Apparently, by owning a major memory chipmaker, SoftBank could extend its reach across the AI supply chain. So, it’s probably a precursor to SoftBank buying a partial stake in a memory chipmaker or buying the whole company outright.
SK Hynix isn’t up for sale, and Son doesn’t need to buy it because even a hostile takeover bid isn’t realistic. But Son tested the financial appetite for bankrolling an acquisition of a memory chipmaker and then walked away. After this free due diligence, if he buys a partial stake in a memory company or buys the whole company for much less, it will look like a concession.

articles.title: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans
articles.text:
A Peruvian call center operator was sentenced to eight years in prison for helping steal millions of dollars from over 30,000 Spanish-speaking US residents in a years-long government-impersonation fraud scheme.
45-year-old Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza of Lima, Peru, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud after being charged in an 18-count indictment following her March 2023 arrest and April 2025 extradition to the United States.
According to court documents, Alcedo managed and operated Peruvian call centers linked to multiple large-scale fraud and extortion schemes between January 2013 and December 2018.
The scammers first contacted Spanish-speaking Americans, claiming they qualified for free services or products. However, they later impersonated US government officials and lawyers and told the victims they were contractually obligated to pay large sums of money to receive them.
Together with her accomplices, she defrauded and extorted thousands of Americans by falsely threatening them with court action, arrest, and immigration consequences in unsolicited phone calls targeting Spanish-speaking Americans.
"The scheme spanned several years and thousands of victims made payments to Alcedo. Collectively, the scheme was responsible for defrauding more than 30,000 Spanish-speaking residents of the United States out of $15 million," the Department of Justice said.
"These criminals preyed on hardworking Americans, using fear and intimidation to steal millions of dollars. They deliberately targeted Spanish-speaking communities, impersonating government officials and threatening innocent people with arrest and legal consequences," added Acting US Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas.
Alcedo was the tenth defendant extradited from Peru and sentenced in this scheme, with ten other Peruvian call center owner-operators and four distribution center owner-operators involved in the scheme convicted so far.
This follows a June 2026 warning from the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) that Americans have lost $3.5 billion to impersonation scams in 2025, with reported losses nearly tripling since 2020 and approximately $920 million stolen by government impersonators.
In April, the FBI also warned in its 2025 Internet Crime Report that US victims lost nearly $21 billion to cyber-enabled crimes throughout last year.

articles.title: MOVA Rover X10 robot pool cleaner review - impressive unit that can take over the pool care and cleaning duties
articles.text:
- RATING
MOVA Rover X10 (love its rhyming name) it's a seriously impressive unit that can completely take over your pool cleaning duties produce stunning results. It's an investment in giving you back your time and pool.
Anyone who owns a pool knows looking after it is a year-round job. The new MOVA Rover X10 robot pool cleaner help you make light work of it. In fact it will take over completely.
This premium seven-in-one robot pool cleaner and surface skimmer can completely take over your pool maintenance.
It has quadruple motors that generate 38,000 LPH suction and FloatDrive propulsion so it can clean not only the floors and walls but also the steps and other shallow areas and skim the surface.
The EdgeDrive brush can get into edges and corners provide a thorough clean while the 360-degree AquaScan LDS (laser distance sensor) that maps your pool.
PoolNavi also does the heavy lifting in terms of dynamic route planning to get around and clean your pool thoroughly.
It can handle seven zones in your pool: the surface, floor, walls, corners, waterline, steps and shallow zones.
Under the hood are 15 motors that are coordinated to navigate your pool with 4 motors dedicated to smooth vertical hovering.
Tech Guide tested the MOVA Rover X10 robot pool cleaner and setup was easy.
It was just a matter of unpacking it and connecting it to the MOVAhome app.
Also included is a remote-controlled float that connects to your Wi-Fi and uses an ultrasound signal communicate to the robot while it’s underwater to give you real-time monitoring and control.
The unit itself is quite large (it’s 54cm long, 46cm wide and 32cm thick) and heavy (it’s 15.8kg) and requires a bit of strength to manage.
When it’s connected you can choose, either on the unit itself or within the app, whether you want to do the complete clean or choose just the floors or the walls.
We chose everything and threw it in the deep end of our pool.
Took a few minutes to fill up with water and sink to the bottom but once it did, we were off to the races.
The pool we used it in was about 8m long and about 3m wide so it was nothing the MOVA Rover X10 couldn’t handle.
We know for a fact could effortlessly clean and maintain a much bigger swimming pool.
A single charge, you can cover 500 square metres.
It’s suited to all types of pool surfaces whether it’s marble, PVC, ceramic, stainless steel, fibreglass, mosaic tiling or concrete.
Thanks to the intelligent mapping it can also handle all types of pool shapes as well.
The Rover X10 has a 5 L filter basket and has replaceable ultrafine filters to capture everything from leaves to fine particles.
Once it has finished it’s clean. It’s easy to pop open the top panel, remove the basket, and empty it to get it ready for the next clean.
Is a 15,000mAh lithium-ion battery which adds up to about 6 hours of continuous cleaning.
What we liked about the MOVA Rover X10 was the fact that it was a set-and-forget system.
Once it’s in the pool you can leave it and trust it to do its thing.
There are two signs to see that the clean is finished.
First your pool is sparkling clean with no leaves or any surface mess to be seen.
Second, the robot empties itself of water and floats to the surface.
Other robot pool cleaners require the user to drag it from the bottom of the pool with a special hook.
This takes a bit of effort and the added water inside the robot makes it much heavier.
With the X10 at least the water has been released so it can float to the surface to make easier retrieval before you place it back on the charging stand, ready for next time.
Still 15.8kg is not ideal for some customers who may not be able to handle the size and weight of the robot.
One other thing we learned was not to have the filter on while the robot is in the pool.
The robot itself is okay. It can go about its merry way.
But the remote control float would wind up in the filter box.
The other thing to discuss is the price.
Now to be clear, this is a thoroughly efficient pool cleaning robot that can do everything.
But it is priced at $3,699.
What you need to consider is the amount of time this would give back to a pool owner.
Anyone who owns a pool knows it takes a lot of work to maintain all year round.
Some even employ dedicated pool cleaners to come and do the work for them.
The MOVA Rover X10 can be your new dedicated pool cleaner, which, if you had employed someone to do the work for you, will pay itself off in no time.
VERDICT
MOVA Rover X10 (love its rhyming name) it’s a seriously impressive unit that can completely take over your pool cleaning duties produce stunning results. It’s an investment in giving you back your time and pool.

articles.title: Réseau 4G : dans ces villes, le signal s’effondre dès que vous entrez chez vous
articles.text:
Ookla, une entreprise américaine spécialisée dans l’analyse et la mesure des performances des réseaux Internet et mobiles (à l’origine notamment de la plateforme Speedtest), a publié une étude sur la qualité de réception du signal 4G à l’intérieur des bâtiments à travers le monde. Pendant un an, l’entreprise a effectué des mesures dans plus de 100 villes et 60 pays. Mauvaise nouvelle : l’Europe figure parmi les mauvais élèves.
L’Europe à la traîne face à l’Asie de l’Est et au Moyen-Orient
Tout d’abord, commençons par les régions qui sortent en tête de cette étude : l’Asie de l’Est et le Moyen-Orient. À Séoul (Corée du Sud), Bangkok (Thaïlande) ou encore Dubaï, le signal 4G médian mesuré dans les bâtiments de ces villes atteint environ -88 dBm, contre -105 dBm à Naples (plus la valeur est proche de zéro, meilleure est la réception). À Séoul, seuls 2 % des bâtiments mesurés présentent un signal 4G faible, contre 50 % des bâtiments de Naples.
En effet, toujours selon l’étude d’Ookla, Naples serait la ville européenne où la réception du signal 4G à l’intérieur des bâtiments est la plus mauvaise. Environ 50 % des bâtiments de la ville afficheraient un signal inférieur à -105 dBm. Plus généralement, l’Europe semble particulièrement mal lotie : Genève (47 % de bâtiments concernés par une faible réception du signal 4G), Birmingham (45 %), Zurich (45 %), Rome (39 %) ou encore Lyon (32 %). Les grandes capitales européennes ne s’en sortent pas vraiment mieux : 34 % des bâtiments sont concernés à Londres, 33 % à Madrid et 31 % à Paris. Parmi les bons élèves européens, nous retrouvons : Helsinki (12 %), Oslo (11 %) et Budapest (10 %).
À noter que les grandes villes nord-américaines affichent également de mauvais résultats : Miami (40 % de bâtiments concernés par une faible réception du signal 4G), Vancouver (39 %), Seattle (39 %). En revanche, New York s’en sort relativement bien avec 25 % des bâtiments de la ville concernés.
Comment expliquer une telle disparité de réception à l’intérieur des bâtiments ?
Tout d’abord, les matériaux qui composent un bâtiment peuvent avoir un impact direct sur la qualité de la réception du signal 4G à l’intérieur de celui-ci. Le béton, la pierre, le métal ou encore les vitrages confectionnés pour l’isolation thermique peuvent par exemple sensiblement amoindrir le signal. À ce titre, les modèles de l’Union internationale des télécommunications, cités par Ookla, estiment que la traversée des murs extérieurs d’une construction fortement isolée peut entraîner une perte de signal allant jusqu’à 31 dB, contre 14 à 16 dB pour un bâtiment traditionnel.
Mais les matériaux qui composent un bâtiment n’expliquent pas à eux seuls un faible signal 4G. La fréquence utilisée par le réseau mobile joue également un rôle important. Les basses fréquences traversent plus facilement les murs, tandis que les hautes fréquences sont davantage freinées (mais offrent de meilleurs débits). Mais surtout, c’est la qualité du réseau extérieur qui explique une mauvaise réception du signal 4G. Selon Ookla, elle serait à l’origine de 85 % des écarts de réception observés à l’intérieur des bâtiments entre les différentes villes étudiées.
Dès lors, un bâtiment constitué de matériaux qui bloquent les ondes et situé dans une zone où la couverture mobile est médiocre recevra mal le signal 4G. Ookla rappelle tout de même qu’il existe des solutions pour améliorer la réception mobile à l’intérieur des bâtiments, comme l’installation de petites antennes-relais ou de systèmes d’antennes distribuées (DAS).

articles.title: Noté 5/5, ce clavier Razer passe sous les 170 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le clavier Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% "5 étoiles" à 169,89 € (-33%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% passe à 169,89 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 33 % et 84,05 € d'économie. Ce modèle sans fil associe une frappe tactile agréable, un écran Oled pratique et une construction robuste, ce qui lui vaut une note actuelle de 5/5 par notre rédaction.
Razer décline son clavier pour le jeu dans un format compact sans pavé numérique avec le Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%. Ce modèle mécanique mise sur des commutateurs tactiles pour répondre aux exigences des joueurs. L'appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur notre banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% descend à 169,89 € chez Amazon, soit environ 33 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (253,94 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 84,05 €.
Une frappe tactile précise et un écran Oled utile
Ce clavier mécanique sans fil adopte une disposition resserrée à 75 % qui libère de l'espace sur le bureau pour les mouvements de la souris. Les commutateurs tactiles assurent un retour précis sous les doigts, garantissant une excellente sensation de frappe pour le jeu comme pour la saisie quotidienne. Comme le détaille notre test complet, sa construction robuste encaisse les sessions intenses sans faiblir.
L'intégration d'un petit écran Oled apporte un vrai confort d'utilisation au quotidien. Loin du simple accessoire décoratif, cet affichage permet de vérifier les réglages actifs ou l'état de l'appareil directement sous les yeux, sans devoir basculer sur une fenêtre logicielle en pleine partie. Le clavier affiche la note maximale à ce jour dans nos tests.
Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%
Points forts
- Très bonne sensation de frappe.
- Construction robuste.
- Moniteur Oled pratique.
Points faibles
- Peut s'avérer trop bruyant.
- Sérigraphie inégale.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une frappe sonore qui demande quelques concessions
La conception mécanique et tactile génère un niveau sonore qui peut déranger dans une pièce partagée ou lors d'un appel sans micro directionnel. On relève également une sérigraphie inégale sur certaines touches, ce qui n'altère en rien la réactivité des commandes mais détonne sur un modèle de cette catégorie. Ces points restent secondaires pour qui joue au casque dans un espace dédié.
Logitech G915 X Lightspeed : l'autre option face au Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%
Le Logitech G915 X Lightspeed mise sur un format mécanique ultra-plat (low profile) et une personnalisation logicielle très poussée des commandes, là où le Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% préfère une architecture compacte traditionnelle avec un retour tactile plus marqué et un écran Oled intégré. Les deux références affichent la note maximale de 5/5 dans nos tests.
Le Logitech G915 X Lightspeed offre une ergonomie plus plate pour la frappe prolongée, mais son prix est supérieur de 21,10 € par rapport au Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% à son tarif du jour.
Logitech G915 X Lightspeed
Points forts
- Frappe de qualité.
- Construction robuste et légère.
- Larges options de personnalisation.
- Rétroéclairage RGB efficace.

articles.title: Taking a personal loan with variable income? Here's how to plan your EMI smartly
articles.text:
Taking a personal loan with variable income? Here's how to plan your EMI smartly
From assessing affordability to choosing the right tenure, freelancers and self-employed borrowers can use an EMI calculator to navigate loan repayments with greater confidence.
For freelancers and self-employed professionals, monthly income can fluctuate significantly. One month may bring several projects, while the next may be quieter. This makes fixed loan repayments harder to plan. An EMI calculator can help estimate monthly instalments, but borrowers with variable income should also build a repayment strategy that accounts for slower months.
Why variable income requires careful EMI planning
Unlike salaried employees, freelancers may not receive the same amount every month. Business owners can also experience seasonal changes in revenue, delayed client payments, or unexpected expenses.
Before taking a Rs 1 lakh loan, consider your average monthly income rather than basing affordability on your strongest earning month. Reviewing income over several months can provide a more realistic picture of what you can comfortably repay.
How an EMI calculator helps
An EMI calculator uses the loan amount, interest rate, and repayment tenure to estimate the monthly instalment. This allows borrowers to test different combinations before committing to a loan.
- Loan amount: A higher borrowing amount generally increases the EMI.
- Interest rate: Higher interest rates increase the EMI and total interest payable.
- Tenure: A longer tenure generally lowers the EMI but increases the overall interest cost.
- Repayment period: Affects the total interest payable.
For example, when planning a Rs 1 lakh loan, you can adjust the tenure and interest rate in the calculator to see how the estimated EMI changes. With FIRSTmoney personal loan by IDFC FIRST Bank, your EMI starts at Rs 2,124 per lakh for a five-year tenure.
How much EMI can you comfortably afford?
The calculated EMI should be assessed against your average disposable income, not simply your gross monthly receipts.
Consider:
- Average monthly income over the past several months
- Essential household expenses
- Business operating costs
- Existing EMIs
- Taxes and other financial obligations
- Emergency savings
A freelancer earning Rs 70,000 in one month and Rs 35,000 the next should not plan repayments solely around the higher figure. Building the EMI around a more conservative income estimate can provide greater flexibility.
Should you choose a longer tenure?
A longer tenure can reduce the monthly EMI, which may be useful when income varies. However, extending the repayment period can increase the total interest paid.
Using an EMI calculator to compare different tenures can show this trade-off clearly. The lowest monthly instalment is not automatically the lowest overall borrowing cost.
For a Rs 1 lakh loan, compare at least two or three tenure scenarios and consider which EMI remains manageable during a lower-income month.
For example, at an interest rate of 9.99% per annum, here’s what the EMI and interest would look like:
- 12 months: Approximate EMI of Rs 8,791; total interest of approximately Rs 5,492.
- 24 months: Approximate EMI of Rs 4,614; total interest of approximately Rs 10,736.
- 36 months: Approximate EMI of Rs 3,226; total interest of approximately Rs 16,136.
*Illustrative calculations for a Rs 1 lakh loan at 9.99% p.a. on a reducing-balance basis. Actual EMI and total interest may vary based on the lender's terms and applicable charges.
Build a buffer before borrowing
Variable-income borrowers should ideally maintain an emergency reserve before taking on another repayment obligation. This can provide a cushion when client payments are delayed or business income temporarily falls.
It is also useful to keep loan repayments separate from money required for essential business expenses. Missing an EMI because expected income arrived late can create additional financial pressure.
What should self-employed borrowers check?
Before applying, review:
- Applicable interest rate
- Processing and other charges
- Loan tenure options
- Total repayment amount
- Prepayment conditions
- Documentation requirements and convenience of application
- EMI affordability during low-income periods
The RBI's key facts statement framework requires key loan information and charges to be disclosed to prospective borrowers for applicable retail term loans. This can help borrowers understand the cost before accepting the loan.
Why choose IDFC FIRST Bank for your personal loan needs
When planning a personal loan, flexibility in borrowing and repayment can make managing finances easier. IDFC FIRST Bank’s FIRSTmoney offers eligible customers personal loans up to Rs 15 lakh, with a fully digital process, 10-minute disbursal and flexible tenures from nine to 60 months. It also comes with zero foreclosure charges and zero processing fees, which can help borrowers manage early repayment more flexibly.
Using an EMI calculator before submitting an application can help borrowers understand the expected monthly commitment and compare repayment scenarios.
Conclusion
An EMI calculator is particularly useful for freelancers and self-employed borrowers because it makes different repayment scenarios easier to compare. Before taking a Rs 1 lakh loan, assess your average income, essential expenses, and emergency reserves rather than relying on your highest-earning month. Choosing an EMI that remains manageable during slower periods can make borrowing easier to accommodate within a variable income pattern.

articles.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
articles.text:
Anthropic has added Code Mode to Claude Code, an experimental feature in which the model writes JavaScript to drive its tools instead of requesting each Bash, Read, or Edit call separately. Code Mode is off by default, requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later, and is enabled with the CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 environment variable. Anthropic warns it may change or be removed in any release.
In a normal session, Claude asks for one tool call, reads the full result, and decides the next step. In Code Mode, one script can run commands in parallel, pass one result into the next call, and return only the output the model needs. The documentation's example finds a file with rg, raises a retry limit, runs the tests, and returns just the path and test output. The conversation still shows each tool call and diff, while the generated code sits in the transcript viewer. Anthropic recommends it for edits repeated across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands. Code that Claude waits on stops after ten minutes; sessions started in auto or bypassPermissions mode can push it to the background for up to two hours while the conversation continues.
The permission model is the part architects should read first. Each call inside a script still goes through deny and ask rules and PreToolUse hooks, but in auto mode the classifier reviews the script before it runs, not each call, and cannot see values computed at run time. A git push can now reach a hook as cd 'app' && git push, so hooks must check every part of a command; a hook matching the REPL tool can read the JavaScript from tool_input.code. Project settings cannot enable Code Mode, so a cloned repository cannot switch it on, and administrators can block it through managed settings.
Code Mode runs only in interactive terminal sessions of the native build, on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, or Fable 5.2, through a Claude subscription or Console account. It does not work with -p, the Agent SDK, the VS Code panel, the Desktop app, Amazon Bedrock, gateways, or zero-data-retention organizations. Agent teams need v2.1.326. Anthropic has published no token or latency figures for it.
George (@bolyki) compared Code Mode with normal mode across eight interactive Sonnet 5.5 runs and posted:
Same results every time. Context 20-25% smaller. On the bigger task: 37% fewer tokens, 19% lower cost. But it is not faster, and on a tiny task it cost more.
Ravi Madabhushi, who builds agent auth infrastructure, pushed back on claims that the feature makes MCP obsolete:
It doesn't materially change anything wrt authentication, authorization and audit policy layers; Your agent still makes those same MCP calls, with the same auth tokens and context and what materially changes is how much context gets into the model window and how much can be discarded.
The idea, and the name, predate Anthropic's release. Cloudflare introduced Code Mode for MCP converting MCP tools into a TypeScript API that models code against inside sandboxed Workers, where bindings keep API keys away from generated code. Anthropic's own post on code execution with MCP described one workflow dropping from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens, and the Claude API offers programmatic tool calling in a remote code execution container. Code Mode instead runs the script in the developer's local session, against Claude Code's built-in tools and permission system.
Code Mode remains opt-in and experimental, and Anthropic collects feedback through /feedback. Setup steps and troubleshooting are in the Claude Code documentation

articles.title: Los jóvenes están cada vez más ansiosos y este factor psicológico es una de las principales causas
articles.text:
Que los jóvenes tienen más problemas de ansiedad que las personas de más edad es algo que tenemos más que comprobado. Si los millennials ya veníamos pisando fuerte en ese sentido, los más jóvenes (porque los millennials también somos jóvenes, ¿vale?) lo tienen aún más crudo. En España los trastornos de ansiedad son el problema de salud mental más registrado en la adolescencia, con 34,6 casos por cada 1.000 habitantes. Pero no es solo una cuestión española.
En Estados Unidos, por ejemplo, también se está dando cada vez más esta tendencia. Por eso es tan importante el estudio realizado recientemente por un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Columbia. Y es que, tras analizar cómo ha evolucionado un importante factor psicológico a lo largo de los años, han comprobado que puede ser el quid de la cuestión. Se trata de la intolerancia a la incertidumbre y conocerla es muy importante.
El término. La intolerancia a la incertidumbre (IU por sus siglas en inglés) hace referencia a la tendencia a angustiarse, preocuparse o evitar situaciones cuando no se sabe qué va a pasar. Aunque no se sabe con seguridad quién lo acuñó, se le atribuye ampliamente a un grupo de investigadores canadienses de la Universidad Laval, por el artículo “Why do people worry?”, publicado en 1994 en la revista Personality and Individual Differences. Textualmente, ellos lo describieron como una serie de “reacciones cognitivas, emocionales y conductuales ante la incertidumbre en situaciones cotidianas”.
Todo esto está muy vinculado a la ansiedad y los trastornos asociados a la misma y desde entonces se ha considerado como uno de sus principales factores de riesgo.
Cada vez peor. Los autores del estudio de la Universidad de Columbia realizaron un metaanálisis de 138 artículos con más de 35.000 estudiantes universitarios de Estados Unidos y Canadá, realizados entre 1992 y 2023. Con ello, no solo querían saber cuál es la incidencia de los trastornos de ansiedad en este grupo poblacional. También esperaban comprobar si la situación ha mejorado o empeorado con el tiempo. Y lo cierto es que, al menos en lo que a IU respecta, parece que ha empeorado.
Cada año los niveles de IU en los estudiantes eran mayores, pero ese aumento era más rápido cuanto más cerca de la época actual. Concretamente, entre 2012 y 2023 el aumento fue unas tres veces más rápido que entre 1992 y 2011.
Los motivos. Los autores de este estudio y otros estudios sobre el tema consideran que las causas de este hecho son multifactoriales. En primer lugar, influye la constante exposición en redes sociales, ya que los jóvenes se ven en la obligación de documentar todo y quedan a la expectativa de lo que el resto pueda comentar. Dependen mucho de esa valoración externa. Por otro lado, la pandemia de COVID-19 paralizó de golpe buena parte de la educación y vida social de muchos de estos jóvenes, generándoles esa sensación de incertidumbre por el futuro. Y por si eso no fuese suficiente, los conflictos políticos y la crisis climática generan una gran desconfianza sobre el futuro del planeta en el que vivimos.
Algunos de estos factores, como la pandemia en pleno desarrollo social, están mucho más vinculados a las generaciones más jóvenes. Otros, como la crisis climática o los conflictos políticos nos influyen a todos, aunque hay motivos por los que ellos los sufren más. Uno de ellos es el horizonte temporal. Una persona de 18 años sabe que va a pasar prácticamente toda su vida sumida en la crisis climática. Alguien de 65 años ha tenido una proporción muy grande de su vida sin el peso del cambio climático. Además, al ser tan jóvenes sienten que tienen menos poder para cambiar las cosas, por lo que experimentan más desasosiego.
Cambian las tornas. Tradicionalmente, la felicidad humana se había descrito con una gráfica temporal en forma de U, donde los mayores niveles de la misma se presentan al principio y al final de la vida y los más bajos en la mediana edad. Ahora, en cambio, la gráfica ha cambiado, pues este tipo de estudios demuestran que los niveles de felicidad están bajando en adolescentes, a la vez que aumentan los de ansiedad.
Hay solución. Por suerte, cada vez hay más enfoques terapéuticos centrados en la IU, por lo que los jóvenes pueden recibir atención psicológica dirigida a este parámetro que tanto influye en su malestar. Lógicamente, cada caso es único y debe estudiarse de forma individual, pero plantarle cara a la IU puede ser una buena manera de empezar.
