articles.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
articles.text:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.
The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.
Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.
That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.
Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.
Startups operating in the CX space have seen multimillion-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.
During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

articles.title: Telecom giant Bell says “agentic threat actor” accessed customer information
articles.text:
Canadian telecommunications giant Bell and its subsidiaries have been breached by an “agentic threat actor.”
The news: On Nov. 17, an unknown party gained unauthorized access to an internal Bell system that included customers’ personal information, the company told customers in an email on Monday morning. The breach was carried out by an “agentic threat actor” and affected Bell and subsidiaries, including Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus, and Lucky Mobile, the company told BetaKit in an email.
Bell told customers that impacted personal information may have included names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and account details such as account numbers, product information, business names, as well as the date and amount of their last payments. Bell added that highly sensitive personal information, such as credit card numbers or bank account information, was not affected.
From the source: “Upon discovering the incident, Bell immediately removed the threat actor and initiated emergency protocols,” Bell told customers in the email. “We continue to monitor all systems closely. We take our obligation to safeguard your information very seriously and we have engaged the RCMP’s cybercrime unit to investigate.”
The context: High-profile cybersecurity incidents have been common this year, beginning with an OpenAI model hacking Hugging Face over the summer. This past month, in particular, has seen numerous cybersecurity failures, including at Canadian accounting firm KPMG, a British Columbia school district, and Staples Canada. Other recent high-profile incidents include the hacking of grocery store refrigerators in Europe, the US Department of Agriculture, and an identified vulnerability in the PHP programming language that brought down websites around the world as site owners rushed to patch their systems.
Final thought: While the use of AI hasn’t been confirmed in all of those breaches, cybersecurity agencies in the Five Eyes intelligence alliance, including the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, urged organizations to boost their cyber defences earlier this year, as they said AI is lowering the barrier for malicious actors and increasing the speed and complexity of attacks.
Following its own breach, Bell is reminding customers to remain wary of any unsolicited requests for personal information by someone posing as Bell, to avoid clicking on links or downloading attachments from suspicious emails or text messages, and to regularly review their accounts for suspicious activity.
Feature image courtesy Bell.

articles.title: ¡Confirmado! Hailee Steinfeld vuelve en ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ como Kate Bishop: ¿llegan los Jóvenes Vengadores al UCM?
articles.text:
Después de muchos meses suplicando por esta noticia, Marvel por fin ha correspondido a sus fans. La actriz Hailee Steinfeld, que interpretó a Kate Bishop en la serie de Ojo de Halcón, volverá en Avengers: Doomsday. Se trataba de uno de los personajes más queridos de esta Saga del Multiverso, pero hasta ahora no había noticias sobre su regreso al UCM en ningún proyecto a la vista.
Por fortuna, todo ha cambiado hace solo unas horas. Y es que, durante la campaña promocional de su próxima película de animación para Disney, Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, ha sido la propia actriz quien ha anunciado la buena nueva. En un vídeo publicado en redes sociales, Hailee Steinfeld ha desvelado que vuelve en Avengers: Doomsday.
"Hola, pues estoy aquí con mi película Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, pero parece que me han traído una silla de otra película", sugiere, enfocando una de las sillas con las que Marvel anunció el reparto completo de la próxima película de los Vengadores. "No te pierdas a Hailee Steinfeld en Hechizo: Bienvenidos a Hexe, de Disney, antes de que vuelva a la gran pantalla en Avengers: Doomsday, reza también la descripción del post.
Hailee Steinfeld debutó en Marvel como Kate Bishop en Ojo de Halcón allá por 2021. Un par de años más tarde, en 2023, también tuvo un cameo en The Marvels al unirse a Kamala Khan para un nuevo equipo. Pero desde aquella aparición, nunca más habíamos vuelto a verla. Ahora, volverá en Avengers: Doomsday y las teorías sobre su papel en el filme no ha tardado en aparecer.
¿Aparecerán los Jóvenes Vengadores en Avengers: Doomsday?
Con la presencia confirmada de Hailee Steinfeld como Kate Bishop en Avengers: Doomsday, los fans de la saga ya solo piensan en una cosa: los Jóvenes Vengadores. Este equipo de los cómics reúne a varios de los héroes más novatos y de menor edad para luchar contra diversos villanos. Durante años se ha rumoreado con su llegada al Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel, e incluso se habló de una película propia. Entre ellos podrían estar la propia Kate Bishop junto a Ms. Marvel, Yelena Belova, Spider-Man, Billy y Tommy Maximoff, Ironheart o Cassie Lang.
Pero la compañía jamás confirmó esa producción y, cuando en el anuncio del reparto de Avengers: Doomsday la mayoría de esos nombres no estaban entre los elegidos, las esperanzas de verles formando una alianza se desvanecieron. Sin embargo, el regreso de Kate Bishop ha vuelto a encender la chispa. Porque lo más probable es que vuelva con la propia Ms. Marvel. Y con Yelena Belova y Cassie Lang también confirmadas en el filme, cada vez son más los que confían en que Marvel finalmente sí reúna a sus Jóvenes Vengadores para la batalla contra el Doctor Doom.
Avengers: Doomsday se estrena en cines el 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
articles.text:
In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks.You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases. You can simulate how conversations shift based on moods, preferences, accents, or environmental conditions such as factory background noise. Rather than relying on simply binary pass or fail, the rule based task verifiers can measure whether the task was completed as well as threshold metrics for cost, efficiency, safety, and compliance.
Simulations can be used during the entire software lifecycle. Product managers can use them for prototyping and design. Engineers can use them for testing in CI/CD pipelines. They can also be used to test production for model drift or failure of third party tools. They can also be used to test compliance with the laws in different regions. Simulations can also be used with synthetic data to fine-tune models.
Key Takeaways
- To evaluate AI agents you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks because the systems are not deterministic, and often the results depend on prior responses. Testing requires using dynamic simulations that can incorporate personas, goals, and corner cases.
- Using simulations for testing applies to the entire software lifecycle. Product managers can use it for designing. Engineers can use it for unit and regression tests. Before deployment you can do stress testing. You can use it to test production for model drift or failure of third party tools.
- Reliability Engineering for AI systems requires the combination of skills from machine learning, systems reliability, and traditional software engineering. Human subject matter experts refine simulation scenarios based on production data, design documents, or even social media.
- Simulation of conversational agents can evaluate multiple parts of the human - software interaction. For example, it can consider the varying interaction possibilities stemming from prior responses, and the way they might change based on human moods, as well as varying goals and preferences. Another example is simulation of corner cases. It can also take into consideration environmental considerations such as factory noise. It can verify whether a task was completed alongside metrics for cost, efficiency, safety, and compliance. Legal compliance in different regions can also be verified.
- Detailed logging of agent statements and tool calls also provides an audit trail for regulatory compliance and failure analysis.
Subscribe on:
Transcript
Michael Stiefel: Welcome to the Architects Podcast where we discuss what it means to be an architect and how architects actually do their job. Today's guest is Zhou Yu, who is a computer science professor at Columbia University and co-founder of Arklex.ai. She obtained her PhD from Carnegie Mellon University. Dr. Yu was named one of the Forbes 30 Under 30 and has extensive research and product experience in conversational agents, computer user agents and LLM model training. Her company enables automated quality assurance testing for AI agents.
It's great to have you here on the podcast. And I'd like to start out by asking you, how did you get interested in conversational agents and simulation? I mean, it's not something you decided one morning when you woke up and decided to do it.
Zhou Yu: I have been working on AI for quite a long time. So I started my PhD in 2011 at Carnegie Mellon. So back then I was in the language technology institute. There are many professors working on natural language processing, speech-related questions. So I was always very interested about interaction. It's not just speech recognition or processing text, but how people interact with machines. To me, that was the ultimate AI, the moment a human can talk to a system or entity the same way that this person is talking to another human being in order to collaborate on various tasks or even negotiate, persuade each other. So to me, that was the ultimate goal of artificial intelligence.
So I was really interested in working on this interactive AI. So my PhD is focused on that. We worked a lot on multimodal conversational agents. How can we do better time taking? How can we, in real time, have agents to think and speak at the same time and various things like that?
The Importance of Simulation [02:33]
Michael Stiefel: So I guess the best way to start out talking about this is what's the importance of this simulation? I mean, to me, one of the important things is this simulation, in addition to testing, helps architects and designers actually to understand what their system is really doing because that's almost impossible to know otherwise.
Zhou Yu: Yes. To me, coming from a research background, the ultimate goal of building a new technology or a new research project is on how you evaluate it. Is there a standard way that you can repeatedly get the same answer? For example, the robustness matters and the standardized testing or evaluation matters. It's more, to me, the very fundamental base of a technology development is about evaluation.
And then if you think about what I have been doing on conversational agents, evaluation has always been one piece of my major research direction. If you think about traditional software testing or website testing, a lot of times there are people are using a manual way to test it or there are automated tooling to support this, like how do you roll out different pages or websites and stuff like that. But the hard part is actually how do you make sure there is a good coverage of various behaviors?
Multi-Turn Agents and Moving Targets [04:03]
And then most importantly, if you think about agents, they're not single turn agents. They're multi-turn, multi-hub, multi-tool calling, long horizon traces kind of programs. Let's just take a simple application of chat bots. Chatbots, in some sense, why do we call them multi-turn, is if you say something, the agent says something back. Based on what the agent says, your next user's input is going to be different. So making the evaluation really difficult, it's like a moving target. If you change your system, you have to redo the evaluation. You can't rely on a static benchmark of what we call reference-based evaluation. This is the question, this is a gold data standard answer that you always can reference towards it because that reference will change based on how your agent changes because a user might ask a different question next time or maybe a user would ask for a clarification at this point.
Simulating User Personas [05:09]
And then the hard part is also that different users might interact with the agent slightly differently because currently natural language is an input, which is exponential in terms of complexity and diversity. If you think about traditional software as this is a button, you press it and there are two actions, they can do swipe left or swipe right. So that makes the testing infinitely hard in various ways.
So that's why we started looking into it a long time ago, is how can we actually use agents to simulate user behaviors? So now you're not relying on standard static benchmarks, you're relying on standard personas or scenarios that you're testing and then you standardize these scenarios and then you build the app based on the standard golden CI/CD pipeline we built, which is these virtual scenarios with human profiles, different goals. And then you're tested consistently on these scenarios that have all the corner cases, has the diversity of the user dimensions that you want to simulate real user study testing where you have to recruit all these people, have them manually tested, now using AI to automate this.
Testing Non-Deterministic Systems [06:29]
Michael Stiefel: From your response, multiple questions come to mind, so take them one by one. One of the first things that you said that struck me was there is a dependency on what came before. One of the most difficult things I think for architects, engineers, SREs, everybody, to wrap their head around is that these are non-deterministic systems, which we've never encountered anything like this before. Because in the past, even if there were more than one or two answers, there were some number of answers and you could check the input to know if this is right, is this wrong. But here, just forget about dialects and accents and all the differences that you can. The system itself is non-deterministic. So how do you build a test? What does a test look like and how does that fit into the CI/CD pipeline?
Goal Completion and Task Verifiers [07:33]
Zhou Yu: That's a really good question because if you think about these current agents, what makes it amazing is they're going to come up with plans in real time. And every time the plan is different, so you can't just look at it turn by turn, what is it doing? Give them all these kinds of shackles or guidelines. It's really about you have to do integrated tests, which means that did this agent ultimately complete the goal that the user wanted to complete? So that's why we use a general term called a goal completion. Once the interaction is finished, has the user actually completed this goal while we give them as sort of an original goal.
So if you think about the testing, we give different users with different profiles, different goals. And we test it to see, sometimes we call it a task. We give it a task and then we look to see if the agent was able to complete the task. Sometimes we also call it verifications, verifiers, task verifiers. And the task verifier has to be correlated with the task. And then for an individual task, the verifier might slightly be different. Some of them can be rule-based. Some of them could be LLM judges. So some of them maybe have various different verifications we need to run in terms of safety, in terms of alignments. So that is the important part.
Verifying Information and Corner Cases [08:57]
Michael Stiefel: When you say completion, I can think of two broad scenarios. One is completion of, "I want to buy a ticket to a concert. I either get the ticket or I don't get the ticket". So it seems easy to define, but if I come and ask for information, how in that scenario do you verify that they got this information? Because if the chat abruptly stops, it may be because the user got frustrated, not because they got the answer they wanted.
Zhou Yu: Yes, that's a really valid thing that people have been doing. So that's why even more important is to be able to simulate different scenarios. So for example, when we are setting up these kinds of simulated users, we give it a specific goal and then we try to verify that goal while the interaction is completed. This user's goal might just be, I wanted to get this information. Once you get the information, you can leave, right? And then some of them are just you're going to be a difficult user, you're going to abandon them in the middle and then come back with a different goal. So then you kind of know what you're dealing with at the end of the day that you can evaluate based on the goal of the user. So that's the great part about simulator users.
If you look at production data, you don't know the real intent behind the user, then it's much more difficult. Of course, when we are doing these simulated users, we are also extracting scenarios based on production data so that we have a diversity of that that could cover better ranges of real user behavior.
So your agent in some way pressure tests for various different things. We have seen various corner cases that real users do. People ask repeated questions, not paying attention. There was some glitch on their keyboard. They keep typing these wrong words a couple of times. So all this is our pressure test or variations we need to capture. And then as you said it before, a different accent or different ways of speaking, experienced users and inexperienced users may use different acronyms describing things in various ways. So I think the diversity really matters when it comes to these natural language input based systems.
Designing, Running, Maintaining Simulation Tests [11:18]
Michael Stiefel: It sounds like there's a lot of work for humans still to do because you have to define these personas. You have to understand what the system is trying to accomplish. We haven't got to the point yet where we can have agents design these tests yet. And so it's still certainly human in the loop situation.
So if that's the case, I know this is probably going to run in our listeners' minds is this question, let's say I am an architect, a developer, SRE, a QA person, whatever, how do I design this test? What do I go through? Do I define a persona first? I define a goal? And how do I express that? And once I evaluate the test, how do I feed that back into the system to know how to change the system appropriately?
Zhou Yu: Yes, that's basically exactly what we're doing, how to make other people's life easier. So if you think about how you design the testing cases, that's basically the most important thing or the holy grail. So there are different ways we can use machine learning algorithms to help in terms of permutations of different aspects, trying to figure out based on the systems, what kind of tool calls you already have that we can base on the trajectories to actually design certain goals and scenarios automatically.
And then the other thing is that if you have existing data, of how humans are approaching the task. For example, in customer service, there are usually certain things you already have data for. Or there are some existing data in terms of your product design doc that talks about what your customers would usually do. And then how diverse, let's say e-commerce. Usually people have some user studies they have already done, like, "What kind of people come to our store? What are they usually wanting to do with us when they're calling in for customer service or when they're calling in for suggestions or things?"
And then there's also domain knowledge for various domains that you really sort of can leverage on. Sometimes we can even mine social media to say, "Well, what are the things that people are going to do when it comes to these scenarios?" So that's sort of the way that we can gather information in order as an input to generate these kinds of happy paths or corner cases.
Michael Stiefel: Or unhappy paths.
Humans in the Loop and the Ever Changing Real World [13:40]
Zhou Yu: Yes, corner cases, unhappy paths. And then the most important thing is, like you said, humans in the loop. You show these scenarios in natural language so that the product manager or subject expert, SMEs, can come in to look at them to see, "Ah, are there other things we haven't thought about?" And then they can edit them, add new cases.
And then the most important part is also once you have these simulated scenarios, you can run the interaction with the agent and generate these data. And then it might be easier for a subject expert to look at the data to really think about, "Is it similar to what I have been seeing in the real world? What are some things I'm lacking and I'm giving some diversity attributes?" Or I say, "Oh, I actually think we want more code switching". Code switching means switching between different languages. "I wanted to add a little bit of noise in the background. Because I work in a factory, I wanted to add a specific kind of noise to the background so it's closer to my real world".
And the important part is if you think about the CI/CD pipeline, CI/CD pipeline for these iterative developments the customer-facing agents should be ever-changing because your users may change or what we usually say user distribution may change. Let's say you're an e-commerce, right? Suddenly you have a new product coming in and everyone's asking about the new product. I think it's really about being aware of this technology, knowing how to adopt them, how do you efficiently integrate them into your workflows. It takes time. It takes certain domains or certain applications would adopt it faster because it's more critical to them. Eventually this is just a good practice that all agent builders should adopt.
Michael Stiefel: Well, thank you very much again and talk to you soon.
Zhou Yu: Thanks.

articles.title: Theseus Robotics secures €455k to put robots to work in supermarkets across Europe and US
articles.text:
Theseus Robotics, a Swiss startup developing AI-powered robots to automate shelf restocking and online grocery order picking, has secured €455k ($500k) from Y Combinator and will be launching in a grocery store in Silicon Valley.
The investment follows earlier backing from Founderful Campus, S2S Ventures, Earthling VC and Berlin-based Caesar Ventures, as the company prepares to introduce its robot, Theo, into its first grocery stores in the EU and US in November 2026.
“Robot hardware is turning into a commodity, so we build the brain,” said Samarth Malhotra, co-founder and CEO of Theseus Robotics.
Theseus’ software-led approach has parallels with other European robotics financings announced in 2026.
Paris-based Bleu Robotics secured €5 million to develop humanoid learning software, while Inbolt raised €11 million for robot vision and intelligence. In warehouse automation, Poland’s Nomagic raised €8.3 million and Germany’s Sereact secured €93 million. Closer to home, Swiss Physical AI companies Enact Intelligence and Exclaim Robotics secured €26.68 million and €4.29 million respectively, with mutual investor Founderful co-leading Exclaim’s round.
Together with Belgium’s Motion (€1.7 million) and Theseus’ €455k investment, these 2026 financings total approximately €150.4 million.
Founded in 2026, Theseus Robotics is the first spinoff from the ETH Robotics Club and focuses on automating one of the remaining manual processes in grocery retail: moving individual products from storage areas onto supermarket shelves.
The startup is targeting a sizeable operational challenge. According to figures provided by Theseus, Europe and the US together have more than 100k large grocery stores, with supermarkets spending over €54 billion ($60 billion) annually on manual shelf replenishment. While warehouses have adopted automation extensively, shelf replenishment and in-store order picking continue to rely heavily on human workers.
The startup’s robot, Theo, is designed to address both tasks, with a reported capacity to restock up to 400 units per hour and pick up to 40 units per hour for online orders. Its operating schedule allows it to switch between functions, picking customer orders until 9 p.m. before moving to overnight shelf replenishment until stores reopen at 9 a.m.
Rather than developing its own robotic hardware, Theseus Robotics purchases existing wheeled, two-armed robots and focuses on building the software and AI models that enable them to operate in retail environments.
Theo operates using a proprietary operating system and AI models trained by the company to recognise, grasp and place products across different shelf configurations. The technology is designed to handle thousands of product types, ranging from fragile yoghurt cups to heavier items such as cases of water.
Force sensors help Theo adjust its grip to avoid damaging delicate packaging, while its software can compare shelf conditions against planograms, the layouts retailers use to determine where individual products should be placed.
This functionality provides retailers with information about stock availability and shelf organisation, potentially helping them identify missing products and improve replenishment decisions. When Theo encounters a situation it cannot resolve autonomously, a human operator can intervene remotely.
The company reports that its technology has already been deployed in two stores, with pilots involving supermarket and pharmacy retailers in Europe and the US, alongside two major American online delivery platforms.
The recent Y Combinator investment is expected to support Theseus Robotics’ first US grocery store deployment in Silicon Valley. The startup is also preparing a broader programme of pilots across Switzerland, Germany and the US during the first quarter of 2027.

articles.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
articles.text:
Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume.
Dubbed BadBox 3.0, it is the third iteration of a large operation targeting low-cost Android devices. The first BadBox botnet ensnared more than 190,000 devices, while BadBox 2.0 was initially found on over 1 million devices, but eventually ensnared more than 10 million.
“At its height, BadBox 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform,” Human Security says, noting the bid request volume was three times the volume recorded for the VastFlux ad fraud scheme.
Portions of BadBox 3.0, the cybersecurity firm says, were operated via command-and-control (C&C) domains that were disrupted when Google took down XCPE, a botnet of over 1.3 million Android set-top boxes.
The botnet consists of low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules designed to render hidden video ads and to enroll the devices into residential proxy networks.
Human Security says its Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team has uncovered an actively maintained catalog of fraud modules hosted on public repositories, as well as links to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ. Some of the modules were previously seen in BadBox and BadBox 2.0.
“Most modules in the catalog are residential proxy modules and the droppers that install them, but the collection also carries new ad fraud modules, and researchers traced both payloads to the same infrastructure and code,” Human Security notes.
Mimicking video ad software development kits (SDKs), the botnet’s ad fraud modules render ads in a hidden window, making the bid requests appear as coming from known, legitimate apps that the threat actors impersonated.
While the device owner does not see the ads, the supply chain sees a premium CTV inventory consisting of well-known applications that likely aren’t even installed on the infected devices, along with residential IP addresses and full video ads. In some cases, the threat actors relied on server-side ad insertion (SSAI) to monetize application spoofing.
“The volume reached roughly 40 billion bid requests a day, and much of it arrived from IP addresses associated with residential proxy networks, which helped it pass as ordinary household viewing,” Human Security notes.
Proxyjacking modules deployed on the same devices enrolled them in eleven residential proxy networks, including a rebranded version of IpMoYu, now named PXYEDGE, the network operated by the threat actors behind BadBox and BadBox 2.0.
Human Security has found several links between BadBox 3.0 and the Chinese company TXCZ: the modules check for TXCZ build properties, a TXCZ domain serves payload download routes and configurations for the hidden ads, and Human linked TXCZ to repositories distributing ad fraud launchers.
In addition to public repositories, the threat actor uses a second code platform and a file server to host payloads. For some payloads, it also uses a free open-source CDN that mirrors public repositories. The operators also use a self-hosted GitHub proxy.
Human Security has not provided an estimated size of BadBox 3.0, but noted that the mirror for one repository served over 367,000 requests over a month, which does not reflect the number of infections.
“These are requests rather than unique devices, and some come from researchers and scanners. It should be made very clear: these numbers are only for one repository, and only of the third backup delivery mechanism. The actual number of BADBOX 3.0 infections can be presumed to be significantly higher,” the cybersecurity firm notes.

articles.text: Luciano Floridi, en una fotografía cedida por su editorial. Luciano Floridi lleva años pidiendo que dejemos de llamar inteligencia a la inteligencia artificial (IA). Este filósofo especializado en tecnologías de la información, y director del Centro de Ética Digital de la Universidad de Yale , lo deja claro en su nuevo libro desde el título: Esto no es inteligencia (Shackleton) . Floridi (Roma, 62 años) sostiene que las máquinas actuales son asombrosas, pero no inteligentes; por eso, prefiere hablar de “agentes”, como los atmosféricos, que no deciden ni intentan hacer nada: simplemente actúan. articles.title: Jensen Huang vuelve como CEO de Nvidia y la accion sube 31,8%
articles.text:
Jensen Huang volvió a la dirección de Nvidia como presidente y consejero delegado, tras la decisión unánime del consejo de administración de restituirlo con efecto inmediato.
El anuncio impulsó las acciones de la compañía un 31,8% en las operaciones previas a la apertura de Wall Street. El fabricante de chips informó que la reincorporación se produjo después de varias conversaciones con el ejecutivo de origen taiwanés, en las que los directores evaluaron su continuidad al frente del grupo y descartaron que su regreso suponga riesgos para la seguridad nacional de Estados Unidos, según Nvidia.
“El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar NVIDIA y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes … Tenemos plena confianza en Jensen y esperamos colaborar con él en su regreso al frente de la compañía. Agradecemos a Colette Kress su excelente labor como Directora Ejecutiva interina, además de seguir desempeñando sus funciones como Directora Financiera de NVIDIA”, afirmó Harvey C. Jones, Presidente del Consejo.
El regreso llega después de una salida marcada por un escándalo. Huang había renunciado a sus cargos luego de admitir una relación extramatrimonial con una exejecutiva de una empresa de centros de datos en Singapur, cliente de NVIDIA, señalada por autoridades estadounidenses por presuntos vínculos con espionaje chino y desvío de chips restringidos.
El caso se agravó cuando The New York Times reportó una segunda relación extramatrimonial del ejecutivo, esta vez con una empleada de NVIDIA bajo su supervisión directa.
La controversia derivó en investigaciones del FBI, una indagación independiente dentro de la compañía y caídas en las acciones de NVIDIA, mientras Pekín negó las acusaciones de espionaje y no se estableció públicamente que Huang hubiera entregado información confidencial de forma deliberada.
Cómo se mueven las acciones del sector tecnológico
La subida de NVIDIA se dio en medio de un rebote generalizado del sector tecnológico y de inteligencia artificial este 23 de noviembre, tras las fuertes caídas de la semana pasada.
Anthropic también se recuperó después del desplome registrado tras su salida a bolsa, presentando un aumento de más de 4% durante la jornada. Zscaler lideró las subas de la jornada, con un avance cercano al 13%, impulsado por el acuerdo de CrowdStrike para adquirirla por 43.900 millones de dólares en acciones.
AMD subió alrededor de un 5%, beneficiada por el optimismo hacia el hardware y los semiconductores de inteligencia artificial. Oracle avanzó cerca de un 5% después de reafirmar su objetivo de superar los 30.000 millones de dólares en flujo de caja libre para el año fiscal 2029.
Micron Technology y CoreWeave, ligadas a la cadena de suministro de centros de datos, también avanzaron de forma notable.
Cómo queda Nvidia con el regreso de Huang y su investigación
El regreso de Huang se produjo once días después de que renunciara a sus tres cargos y no cierra los procesos internos que la compañía sigue tramitando.
El consejo recordó que, tras conocerse que Huang había sido blanco de una presunta operación de inteligencia extranjera, había formado un comité integrado exclusivamente por consejeros independientes, asistido por asesoría legal externa, cuya investigación continuará hasta su conclusión.
NVIDIA informó además la creación de un Comité de Seguridad Nacional y Control de Exportaciones, también compuesto solo por directores independientes, encargado de supervisar el cumplimiento comercial y los riesgos de seguridad nacional con apoyo de abogados y asesores especializados en la materia.
La compañía anunció que inició la búsqueda de un director de cumplimiento (Chief Compliance Officer), un cargo nuevo que reportará ante el comité de nominaciones y gobierno corporativo, y reiteró que continuará cooperando con las investigaciones y consultas de las autoridades estadounidenses.
Harvey C. Jones, nombrado presidente del consejo el 12 de noviembre, el primero de ese tipo en la historia de la empresa, conserva el cargo. Mientras que Colette Kress, que ejerció como directora ejecutiva interina, vuelve a concentrarse en su rol como directora financiera de NVIDIA.

articles.title: Misfit Ventures aims to tap into charitable giving with new donor-advised fund
articles.text:
Misfit Ventures is launching its own donor-advised fund (DAF) with the help of fellow Vancouver organization Charitable Impact Foundation as it looks to convince more high-net-worth individuals to put their capital behind LGBTQ+ technology entrepreneurs.
The venture capital (VC) firm revealed Misfits Foundation on stage last Thursday during QueerTech’s latest annual conference. The two-day event, the largest in Canada for members of the LGBTQ+ community working in tech, brought over 700 people to Toronto’s Evergreen Brick Works to discuss inclusive AI and other topics from a variety of perspectives.
“I’m willing to be that guinea pig of trying something new to try and get more capital into the ecosystem.”
Misfit, which is currently raising its inaugural fund, claims to be Canada’s first and North America’s largest VC firm focused on LGBTQ+ founders building in tech, while Charitable Impact is a registered charity and public foundation that offers an online platform for individuals, families, and organizations to manage their charitable giving from a single account.
“There [are] a lot of [HNW] individuals that we’ve approached … or we’ve been introduced to, for potential investment, [who] really just don’t understand the [VC] world, so they want to stay away from it,” Misfit co-founder and managing partner Mandy Potter told BetaKit in an interview. “But what they do understand is donating.”
That realization was a driving factor behind Misfit’s decision to launch the Misfits Foundation DAF under Charitable Impact. Another was the state of the VC fundraising market, which has been particularly challenging for emerging managers and impact funds like Misfit, which has set out to finance LGBTQ+ and other historically underrepresented entrepreneurs at the earliest stages.
Potter described trying to raise a first fund in this environment as “fucking impossible” during her remarks on stage. “It’s the hardest thing I’ve ever done,” she added.
While Misfit’s new DAF was built “in a selfish way in the sense that we needed to find different avenues for capital,” Potter said her intentions are pure. “I want to see more impact funds and new fund managers be successful, so I’m willing to be that guinea pig of trying something new to try and get more capital into the ecosystem.”
RELATED: “A perfect storm”: 2025 was the worst year for Canadian VC fundraising since 2016
In Canada, a DAF is a fund established by a charity to which others donate and help guide. This structure permits donors to collectively give to multiple causes from the same account. Potter and fellow Misfit co-founder and managing partner Douglas Lui are leading the initiative.
Dollars donated to Misfit’s DAF will be held by Charitable Impact, while the fund’s strategy and giving will be guided by Potter. Those donations will be invested into Misfit’s core fund and deployed into startups with LGBTQ+ leadership. Potter said the firm’s DAF has already secured commitments, but declined to share how much exactly to date.
Unlike limited partners (LPs) investing in Misfit’s fund, individuals who donate to this DAF will receive an immediate charitable tax receipt from Charitable Impact. Any returns generated on the capital that Misfit invests from this DAF will remain committed to charity and be redistributed to other causes at the discretion of Misfit’s leadership team.
QueerTech board chair Bradley Breton, who previously served as chief of staff at Toronto FinTech firm Zafin, is a Misfit LP. For donors, he said this DAF offers a means for folks interested in maximizing their impact on LGBTQ+ communities while also reaping the associated tax benefits, whereas becoming a Misfit LP provides a pathway that balances that impact with financial returns.
RELATED: Queer tech founders explore move to Canada as US abandons DEI
Breton is also one of the champions of another DAF focused on LGBTQ+ communities through Charitable Impact called Q Impact. Launched by Breton, founding donor Barry Inouye, a former leader at Amazon and Coca-Cola, and Trevor Loke, a community ambassador at Charitable Impact.
Q Impact is a cause fund, a structure that Kirsten Hurlbut, account manager at Charitable Impact, said allows people “to come together and support the cause instead of the organization.”
“The goal is to create a sustainable cause fund that can support the queer community across different policy issues, both nationally and internationally,” Breton told BetaKit in an interview.
Dollars donated to Q Impact are held by Charitable Impact. According to Q Impact’s website, the cause fund has secured more than $1.3 million to date.
Charitable Impact also helps power another such fund dedicated to promoting therapies for those living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or ALS.
Potter is hoping that Misfit’s DAF can serve as a model for other emerging managers and impact funds. Breton said QueerTech is also exploring how to use DAF-based giving to support some of its own programming.
Feature image courtesy QueerTech. Photo by Naomi Silver-Vézina.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
articles.text:
In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.
The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.
Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.
In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.
Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.
A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.
The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”
Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.
Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.
“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”
In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
This story is developing...

articles.text:
Arsenal e Borussia Dortmund se enfrentam nesta terça-feira (24), às 17h (de Brasília), pela quinta rodada da Fase de Liga da Champions League 2026/27. A partida será disputada no Emirates Stadium, em Londres, na Inglaterra. Como chegam Arsenal e Borussia Dortmund para o jogo?
O Arsenal chega ao confronto na liderança da Premier League, com seis pontos de vantagem sobre Brighton e Manchester City, seus perseguidores mais próximos. O time inglês, porém, tem desfalques importantes. Zubimendi e Bukayo Saka seguem lesionados, enquanto o goleiro David Raya machucou o ombro esquerdo durante o empate por 2 a 2 com o Newcastle, no último sábado (21). Kepa deve ocupar a posição, como aconteceu no confronto contra os Magpies.

articles.title: Verifying UCIe.mem: Flexible Verification For Compute And Memory Chiplets
articles.text:
Validate UCIe.mem implementations across development stages while reusing a common verification environment.
By Ujjwal Negi and Prashant Dixit
As chiplet-based designs become increasingly common, connecting compute and memory dies efficiently is an important part of building scalable systems. The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard provides a common die-to-die interconnect, while UCIe.mem defines a standardized protocol for memory transactions between compute and memory chiplets.
Modern systems can combine compute chiplets with different memory technologies, including HBM, DDR, and LPDDR. Traditionally, integrating these components can involve technology-specific interfaces and custom mechanisms. UCIe.mem addresses the growing need for scalable and flexible memory architectures in modern computing systems by providing a common, memory-technology-agnostic way to communicate memory requests and responses across chiplets.
This standardization provides a foundation for more modular and scalable chiplet-based architectures. It allows compute and memory chiplets to be developed independently and integrated across implementations from different vendors, reducing reliance on custom, technology-specific interfaces. By decoupling memory communication from the underlying memory technology, UCIe.mem gives system designers greater flexibility to combine, reuse, and scale compute and memory resources to meet different application requirements.
Fig. 1: Memory and compute chiplet over UCIe.
While a common protocol helps streamline integration, verifying UCIe.mem introduces challenges at multiple levels. The protocol must be validated across initialization, credit management, transaction handling, packing, and data integrity. Verification must also account for concurrent requests, different channel configurations, and the correct association of responses with their originating requests.
A further challenge is accommodating different DUT interfaces and levels of integration. Early-stage designs may not yet implement UCIe.mem and may expose only a conventional memory interface, such as AXI. Other designs may implement UCIe.mem and expose FDI, allowing the DUT to generate and receive control and memory payload flits directly. At the system level, verification must extend beyond protocol compliance to include realistic interactions with the memory subsystem.
A flexible verification environment must support these different scenarios while maintaining consistent protocol validation and end-to-end checking.
Questa One Avery UCIe VIP provides a versatile verification platform that adapts to different DUT interfaces and system configurations. Rather than limiting verification to a single integration model, it enables teams to validate UCIe.mem implementations across development stages while reusing a common verification environment.
For early-stage DUTs that do not implement UCIe.mem, the VIP can bridge conventional memory interfaces (such as AXI to UCIe.mem transactions) enabling memory-access functionality to be verified before the DUT incorporates the protocol. For UCIe.mem-compatible DUTs that expose FDI, the VIP acts as the link partner, allowing the DUT’s own protocol implementation and generated traffic to be directly validated.
Beyond protocol-level testing, the solution enables realistic system-level verification by modeling the compute and memory sides of a chiplet-based system. A CXL.mem root host VIP can model the compute-side host while the DUT acts as the memory chiplet. Alternatively, a memory subsystem VIP, comprising a memory controller and memory model, can represent the memory side while the DUT acts as the compute chiplet. These configurations allow verification to go beyond basic request-response exchanges, exercising the DUT under realistic system conditions. Configurable latency, timing, and memory operating parameters help model different system behaviors and evaluate how the DUT handles them.
Complementing this integration flexibility, the VIP offers an exhaustive UCIe.mem compliance test suite, comprehensive protocol checking, and end-to-end data and transaction score-boarding. Together with transaction tracking for easier debug, these capabilities help ensure protocol compliance and identify design issues.
Teams can begin with early-stage memory-access validation, progress to direct UCIe.mem protocol testing, and extend verification to realistic system-level scenarios—all within a flexible verification environment.
Fig. 2: Questa One Avery UCIe.mem solution.
As chiplet architectures continue to develop, verification environments need to accommodate different implementation choices and levels of design maturity. With support for varied DUT interfaces and memory subsystem integration, Questa One Avery UCIe VIP makes UCIe.mem verification more adaptable across development stages and system configurations.
The result is a flexible approach to validating memory communication between chiplets, helping design teams begin verification early and extend it as their implementations mature.
For a detailed look at the UCIe.mem verification architecture, capabilities, and supported integration topologies, refer to the whitepaper, Verifying UCIe.mem: A Scalable Framework for Chiplet-Based Compute and Memory Systems.
Prashant Dixit develops verification solutions for UCIe-based designs and manages the Storage Verification IP team at Siemens EDA. Prior work included the design and verification of IP and SoCs in the networking and storage domains at Samsung. Dixit earned a Bachelor of Technology in Electronics and Communication from Uttar Pradesh Technical University in 2004 and a Master of Engineering degree in Microelectronics from BITS Pilani in 2006.

articles.title: „Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
articles.text:
„Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
Schwarze Löcher faszinieren die Wissenschaft schon lange. Dabei handelt es sich um Bereiche im Weltall mit so starker Gravitation, dass nichts mehr aus ihnen entkommen kann – nicht einmal Licht. Schwarze Löcher entstehen, wenn sehr viel Masse auf kleinstem Raum konzentriert ist und die Raumzeit dadurch stark gekrümmt wird.
Nach Albert Einsteins allgemeiner Relativitätstheorie wird die Raumzeit von Masse gekrümmt. Bei einem Schwarzen Loch ist diese Krümmung so stark, dass selbst Lichtstrahlen nicht mehr nach außen gelangen können.
Die Aufnahme mit der Bezeichnung M87* erlangte weltweite Bekanntheit
Im April 2019 wurde das erste von der Menschheit aufgenommene Bild eines supermassereichen Schwarzen Lochs der Öffentlichkeit präsentiert. Es entstand mithilfe des Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), einem weltweiten Verbund von Radioteleskopen. Das Bild zeigt das supermassereiche Schwarze Loch im Zentrum der Galaxie Messier 87 (M87), die 55 Millionen Lichtjahre von uns entfernt ist. Die Aufnahme, die weltweite Bekanntheit erlangte, bekam die Bezeichnung M87*.
Siebeneinhalb Jahre später hat ein unabhängiges Forschungsteam dieses Bild jetzt verifiziert. Dies bestätigt Einsteins allgemeine Relativitätstheorie, die bereits die Existenz Schwarzer Löcher sowie das Aussehen ihrer unmittelbaren Umgebung vorhersagte. Die Forschungsergebnisse des Teams sind in der Fachzeitschrift Nature veröffentlicht worden.
KI als Basis des zur Bildverifizierung angewandten Verfahrens
Samuel Lai, Forscher bei der australischen Wissenschaftsbehörde CSIRO (Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation), entwickelte mit seinem Team fortschrittliche Methoden des maschinellen Lernens und der künstlichen Intelligenz, um Informationen über die Struktur des Schwarzen Lochs zu gewinnen. Dabei filterten sie Störungen heraus, die dadurch entstanden, dass das EHT das Objekt M87* durch die Atmosphäre unseres Planeten hindurch beobachtet hatte. Das angewandte Verfahren – „GenDIReCT“ genannt – berücksichtigte zudem Verzerrungen, die durch die Zusammenschaltung mehrerer Teleskope entstanden waren.
„Als wir die Methode auf den ursprünglichen EHT-Datensatz anwandten, erhielten wir ein Schwarzes Loch, das in Größe und Form nahezu identisch mit dem historischen EHT-Bild war“, sagte Lai in einer Pressemitteilung und ergänzte: „Wichtig ist: Unser Modell hatte keinerlei Vorkenntnisse darüber, wie ein Schwarzes Loch aussieht, als wir es auf die M87-Daten anwandten.“ Laut ihm ist die „erste wirklich unabhängige Validierung“ des EHT-Bilds ein „wichtiger Schritt im wissenschaftlichen Prozess“.
Bestätigung für Albert Einsteins allgemeine Relativitätstheorie
Auch Lai teilt die Faszination für die besondere M87*-Abbildung und unterstreicht die Schwierigkeit, überhaupt zu dieser gelangt zu sein: „Es ist, als würde man im eigenen Garten stehen und versuchen, einen Donut auf dem Mond zu fotografieren“, erklärte er gegenüber space.com.
Die Verifizierung des Bildes ist auch ein erneuter Ritterschlag für Albert Einsteins allgemeine Relativitätstheorie, die er 1915 veröffentlicht hatte. Sie lieferte auch Vorhersagen darüber, wie die Umgebung eines Schwarzen Lochs aussehen müsste: ein Ring aus extrem heißem, leuchtendem Plasma, auf den der Schatten des Schwarzen Lochs fällt.
Als Wissenschaftler:innen das erste Bild von M87* sahen, waren sie erstaunt, wie genau es die Vorhersagen von Einsteins allgemeiner Relativitätstheorie widerspiegelte – ein erneuter Beleg für die Richtigkeit der Theorie. Die nun erfolgte Verifizierung festigt diese Erkenntnis weiter.
))))))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Visa prépare plus que jamais les boutiques européennes à des clients qui ne sont pas humains
articles.text:
Visa annonce étendre son programme Agentic Ready aux commerçants et aux prestataires de paiement européens. Plus de 85 acteurs, dont Adyen, Stripe et Worldline, vont tester les achats réalisés par des agents IA, avant un prochain déploiement.
Le géant Visa a annoncé, ce lundi 23 novembre, l'extension de son programme Agentic Ready aux commerçants, aux prestataires de services de paiement et aux acquéreurs européens. Lancé en mars auprès des banques, ce dispositif doit préparer le réseau aux paiements initiés par des agents IA, ces assistants capables d'acheter pour le compte de leur utilisateur. Avec l'identification des agents, la sécurisation des transactions mais aussi les premiers retours de terrain, les participants disposent désormais d'un cadre commun pour passer aux tests réels.
Visa veut que les commerçants européens puissent vendre à des agents IA
La liste des premiers inscrits au programme a des airs de Gotha du paiement en ligne, avec des noms comme Stripe, Klarna, Barclaycard, Adyen, Checkout.com, Nexi… Côté français, on repère notamment Worldline, BPCE Merchant Services et HiPay. Tous reçoivent un cadre commun pour tester en conditions réelles l'identification des agents IA, leur authentification et le traitement des transactions qu'ils lancent. L'objectif, selon Mathieu Altwegg, responsable produits et solutions Europe de Visa est à l'origine de « tester des solutions concrètes ».
Visa détaille l'achat en quatre parties. D'abord, à l'entrée, le site doit reconnaître les agents de confiance pour les laisser passer, et s'inscrire dans l'Agentic Directory de Visa pour que ces agents puissent le trouver. Il doit ensuite rendre son catalogue lisible par les intelligences artificielles et les laisser composer un panier. Vient l'étape du paiement, avec des cartes « tokenisées ». Dans le détail, le vrai numéro de carte reste caché derrière un jeton, selon le principe de tokenisation, et le marchand doit accepter les achats sans création de compte client. La dernière marche, c'est l'après-vente. Chaque transaction doit pouvoir être rattachée à la carte d'origine, pour qu'un remboursement ou une contestation puisse aboutir.
Certains ont déjà pris de l'avance. Worldline assure avoir démontré l'été dernier que les paiements agentiques pouvaient « passer du concept à la réalité », avec des transactions de bout en bout sur plusieurs marchés européens. Chez Stripe, Kenny Wolf estime que les entreprises devraient pouvoir « vendre à des agents IA aussi facilement qu'elles vendent à des consommateurs ». La fintech va tester plusieurs façons d'identifier ces paiements, de renforcer le contrôle des commerçants et d'améliorer le taux d'autorisation, c'est-à-dire la part des transactions acceptées.
Commerce agentique : des tests, mais pas encore de date
Visa assure avoir conçu ce volet sur mesure pour l'Europe, un marché au tissu commercial très divers, où la sécurité, l'authentification et le contrôle des paiements par le consommateur font l'objet d'exigences fortes. Le cadre couvre les cartes grand public comme professionnelles, et prépare de futurs paiements entre entreprises initiés par des intelligences artificielles. La Visa Acceptance Platform complète le dispositif (lutte antifraude, gestion des litiges) pour traiter ces achats sans remplacer les infrastructures existantes.
Pour Adyen, le commerce agentique « ne pourra réussir qu'à travers une collaboration ouverte » entre tous les acteurs. Karan Katyal, responsable mondial du sujet chez le néerlandais, juge essentiel de « définir des standards clairs et opérationnels pour les transactions agentiques ». Ce volet prolonge le travail mené avec plus de 40 émetteurs de cartes européens. Visa, qui revendique plus de 140 participants dans le monde pour cette nouvelle phase, attend d'autres recrues tout au long de 2027.
Certains d'entre vous se demandent peut-être quand il sera possible de confier leur carte à un agent IA ? Aucune date n'est avancée, et ChatGPT Wallet, auquel Visa est associé, reste réservé aux États-Unis pour le moment. Visa a bien testé en France avec Revolut un paiement agentique validé par biométrie, mais ne dit pas qui paiera en cas d'achat contesté. Or, prévient Mathieu Altwegg, les consommateurs, commerçants et acteurs du paiement doivent « avoir confiance dans la sécurité et la fiabilité de ces nouvelles transactions ». Pour l'instant donc, l'agent IA fait ses classes chez les commerçants européens, avant, peut-être, de remplir un jour notre panier.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users
articles.text:
Microsoft confirmed that some Forcepoint users may experience printing issues after installing the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch.
In a Friday service alert seen by BleepingComputer, Microsoft said this known issue affects only systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later.
According to Microsoft, the printing problems stem from a compatibility issue between the KB5132043 Windows hotpatch update and the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent endpoint data loss prevention solution.
"After installing the November 2026 Windows hotpatch update (the Originating KBs listed above), devices running Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent might experience printing issues," Microsoft said. "Affected users might find that the print option is greyed out or encounter errors when selecting a printer. This issue occurs because the Print Spooler service fails to start."
While a fix is not yet available, Forcepoint has shared a temporary workaround for its customers in this support document, which can be accessed after signing in to the Forcepoint support portal.
Last week, Microsoft also warned that the KB5132043 hotpatch is causing installation and launch issues affecting Office and third-party applications on Windows 11 systems.
These two known issues should not affect systems with the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, only those that have installed the hotpatch updates pushed through Microsoft's Windows Autopatch, a cloud-based enterprise service designed to automate Windows and Microsoft 365 updates.
However, as the company confirmed two weeks ago, the November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates may also break printing for users trying to print documents with complex formatting on server (Windows Server 2016 or later) and client (Windows 10 or later) devices.
Microsoft unveiled Windows Autopatch in April 2022, saying it would be available for free to customers with a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater starting in July 2022. Windows Autopatch was made available in public preview in early June 2022 and reached general availability in July 2022.
In March, it announced that it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through Microsoft Intune and the Graph API on systems with the May 2026 Windows security updates installed.
One month later, Microsoft fixed a Windows Autopatch bug that deployed driver updates restricted by administrative policies on some Autopatch-managed Windows devices belonging to customers across the European Union.

articles.title: 367 ch et une carrosserie bodybuildée : Volkswagen signe une bombe électrique, mais il y a un gros hic
articles.text:
Trop sages, les voitures électriques ? Volkswagen a déjà tenté de démontrer l’inverse avec sa défunte gamme GTX, sans grand succès. Résultat, c’est au tour du blason GTI de faire son apparition sur les véhicules à batterie, histoire de dresser un parallèle subtil avec les modèles thermiques. Au cas où la mayonnaise ne prenait toujours pas, le constructeur allemand déballe une version encore plus radicale de ses GTI électriques, la Clubsport.
Ce label bien connu déjà appliqué aux sportives à essence prend donc place sur les modèles électriques. Voici l’ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, qui fête au passage les 50 ans de la première Golf GTI. Et quelle manière de le faire ! La citadine est littéralement transformée avec une carrosserie élargie de 100 mm grâce à des passages de roues gonflés de 50 mm de chaque côté. Les conséquences de ce changement sont immédiates.
Ailes élargies de 10 cm et deux portes en moins : le retour d’un détail oublié sur la Polo
Il a fallu supprimer les portières arrière de l’auto, ce qui la transforme en deux portes, une configuration qui n’a pas été vue depuis la Polo de cinquième génération. Les jantes ont naturellement été revues, avec un kit BBS de 19 pouces noir aux bordures rouges. La face avant gagne pour sa part une lèvre plus proéminente optimisant l’appui aérodynamique. Le capot accueille de son côté deux grandes ouïes posées aux extrémités.
La poupe suit cette tendance radicale, avec un immense aileron en fibre de carbone flottant bien au-delà de la lunette arrière avec deux bras prenant prise au centre du toit. De par sa taille XXL, le diffuseur est immanquable. À bord, c’est un déluge d’Alcantara qui attend les occupants. Ces derniers prendront place dans deux sièges baquets Recaro équipés de harnais rouges à cinq points avec des surpiqûres assorties.
Arceau rouge à la place de la banquette et baquets Recaro : ambiance pistarde assumée
Mauvaise nouvelle pour la praticité, la banquette arrière a été remplacée par un arceau de sécurité couleur Rouge Tornado. Plus sympa pour la course, mais moins commode au quotidien. Volant et écrans sont en revanche identiques à ceux de l’ID. Polo GTI. Le châssis a été revu avec une hauteur de caisse abaissée de 15 mm alors que les suspensions pilotées ont été recalibrées.
Côté mécanique, l’ID. Polo GTI Clubsport reprend le moteur APP550 de l’ID.7 avec ce coup-ci 367 ch et 550 Nm de couple. L’auto demeure une stricte traction, ce qui a nécessité l’installation d’un différentiel autobloquant pour limiter le patinage des roues. Le 0 à 100 km/h est en effet abattu en 4,7 s, contre 6,8 s pour l’ID. Polo GTI. Excitant, sauf que le véhicule n’est encore qu’un concept dont la commercialisation demeure incertaine.

articles.title: Sarvam's new AI model promises better performance at lower cost
articles.text:
Sarvam's new AI model promises better performance at lower cost
Sarvam’s latest model promises better reasoning, tool use and Indian-language capabilities at lower costs, as competition to build India’s AI ecosystem gathers pace.
Sarvam AI has released Sarvam-105B-1711, an updated model designed for businesses handling large volumes of customer queries, phone calls and software-based tasks. The company said it follows instructions more reliably, uses digital tools better and handles Indian languages more effectively, at a lower cost.
Released on November 22, it updates Sarvam’s 105B model, first released in March. The 105 billion parameters refers to the internal values the model adjusts during training to recognise patterns and produce answers.
Sarvam said it trained the new version using Nvidia’s Blackwell B200 chips, powerful processors built for AI calculations.
Co-founder Pratyush Kumar said, “Over the last few months, alongside putting together the token factory and scaling up our enterprise offerings, we optimised our training stack for Blackwell GPUs and achieved significantly higher performance.”
The training stack refers to the hardware, software and processes used to train the model.
Sarvam described it as a “Flash-Lite” model, meaning it is designed to handle many requests at relatively low cost. Its architecture activates only selected parts of the model to generate each response, helping reduce computing requirements. Potential uses include customer-service chatbots, AI voice assistants that speak with callers, and digital assistants that use other software to complete tasks.
Sarvam is making the model’s learned settings, known as weights, available for download. This is called an open-weight release. It allows businesses with suitable computers to run the model themselves rather than relying entirely on Sarvam’s online service. The company has also published instructions for running and training it, although the data used to train the model are not necessarily public.
Sarvam said the new version scored 73.9 on average across eight tests, compared with 42.6 for its March model. The tests assess how well it follows instructions, writes responses, uses software tools and handles Indian languages. These are average scores, not percentages of questions answered correctly. Sarvam’s comparison places it close to Google’s Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, at 74.0, and Gemma 4 31B, at 73.0.
Cost is central to the release. Sarvam noted the combined cost of processing text sent to and generated by the model has fallen from $0.44 to $0.15 per million tokens. Tokens are small pieces of text, sometimes whole words and sometimes parts of words, that an AI model reads or produces. Its Indian rates are Rs 10 per million input tokens and Rs 25 per million output tokens.
The latest release is part of a broader push by Sarvam to build models for different AI applications. Earlier in November, the company introduced Sarvam Prism, a model built on its 105B system for making quick, straightforward decisions. It also released Bulbul V4 Flash in October, which converts written text into natural-sounding speech, and Saaras V4 in September, which converts spoken language into text across 22 Indian languages.
Other Indian companies are pursuing similar ambitions, although their models target different needs. In August, Bengaluru-based Gnani AI introduced Evon v3.3, a 30-billion-parameter model designed to work across 11 Indian languages, alongside Plexus, a platform for building AI assistants that can perform tasks.
More recently, under the IndiaAI Mission, Soket Labs introduced EKA-1, a 26.3-billion-parameter model designed for all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English, with applications in mathematics, coding and reasoning.

articles.title: Tres barcos, dos mares y 24 horas: Ucrania acaba de convertir el mapa naval de Rusia en un tablero de Hundir la Flota
articles.text:
Durante buena parte de la guerra, Rusia ha tenido que reorganizar su flota en el mar Negro para protegerla de los ataques ucranianos. Como contamos, Moscú llegó incluso a trasladar numerosas embarcaciones a bases alejadas de Crimea, buscando refugio frente a los drones navales de Kiev. Los acontecimientos del último fin de semana sugieren que el problema ruso ha adquirido una dimensión geográfica completamente distinta.
Tres barcos, dos mares y un fin de semana. En cuestión de horas, tres embarcaciones rusas han sido objeto de ataques atribuidos a Ucrania en dos escenarios marítimos muy alejados entre sí. En el Mediterráneo, la moderna corbeta Merkury ha terminado hundida en el puerto libio de Bengasi, mientras que el carguero Ascalon fue alcanzado frente a sus costas.
Paralelamente, en el mar Báltico, el carguero ruso Sparta II quedó a la deriva tras otro presunto ataque ucraniano. La sucesión de incidentes dibuja una nueva fase de la guerra en la que Kiev parece haber convertido el mapa naval ruso en un gigantesco tablero de Hundir la Flota.
Hundido en África. Las imágenes satelitales obtenidas por The War Zone muestran al Merkury completamente escorado y hundido junto al muelle de Bengasi, con apenas la parte delantera de la proa visible sobre el agua. Según Associated Press, al menos seis drones navales participaron en la operación: cuatro fueron interceptados y dos consiguieron alcanzar el buque.
La agencia sostiene que los aparatos fueron lanzados desde una base operada por fuerzas ucranianas en el oeste de Libia, aunque TWZ no ha podido confirmar ese extremo. Una fuente ucraniana atribuyó la operación al Servicio de Seguridad de Ucrania (SBU), que no se ha pronunciado oficialmente.
Una pieza especialmente valiosa. El Merkury no era precisamente un barco prescindible. Incorporado a la Armada rusa en 2023, pertenecía a la clase Steregushchiy, una de las generaciones más modernas de corbetas de Moscú. Con 104 metros de eslora, 1.800 toneladas de desplazamiento estándar y una tripulación de aproximadamente 90 personas, disponía de ocho misiles antibuque Uran, doce celdas de lanzamiento vertical para misiles antiaéreos y sistemas de armamento antisubmarino.
Aunque estaba asignado a la Flota del Mar Negro, había estado operando desde bases de la Flota del Norte, en el Ártico, durante la guerra.
Tocado en el Mediterráneo. El segundo objetivo frente a Bengasi fue el Ascalon, un carguero ruso que, según la inteligencia militar ucraniana, había sido utilizado para transportar armamento. El buque estaba vinculado al denominado Expreso Sirio, la ruta logística empleada por Moscú para abastecer militarmente a Siria desde puertos rusos a través del Bósforo.
Tanto la embarcación como su propietaria, M Leasing LLC, estaban sometidas a sanciones estadounidenses. Su ataque se suma así a una creciente lista de incidentes y explosiones de origen diverso que han afectado a barcos vinculados a Rusia en aguas mediterráneas.
Tocado en el Báltico. A miles de kilómetros de Libia, las autoridades finlandesas participaban en las labores de rescate del Sparta II. Según la Guardia Fronteriza de Finlandia, el carguero había sido alcanzado por drones ucranianos en aguas territoriales rusas, perdió su capacidad de gobierno y terminó desplazándose a aguas finlandesas.
Tras dos días de trabajos para extinguir el incendio, una embarcación de rescate rusa comenzó a remolcarlo el domingo. El episodio resulta especialmente significativo porque sitúa la amenaza ucraniana en uno de los espacios marítimos más próximos al corazón territorial de Rusia.
El mapa se está llenando de cruces. Porque los ataques no son acontecimientos aislados. En diciembre, Ucrania reivindicó una operación contra el petrolero Qendil, vinculado a la flota fantasma rusa, a más de 2.000 kilómetros de su territorio. En el Báltico, Kiev también ha reivindicado acciones contra las corbetas Serpukhov y Naro-Fominsk, además del ataque del pasado 3 de junio contra el Boikiy, un buque gemelo del Merkury.
La sucesión de operaciones apunta a una campaña que ya no distingue únicamente entre barcos de guerra y cargueros, sino que también amenaza las redes logísticas que sostienen las operaciones militares rusas.
Rusia se queda sin casillas seguras. Hasta ahora, uno de los grandes éxitos de los drones navales ucranianos había sido obligar a Moscú a retirar buena parte de sus activos navales de la Crimea ocupada. La aparición de ataques en el Mediterráneo y el Báltico plantea un problema mucho mayor: alejar los barcos del frente ya no garantiza su seguridad.
Rusia debe proteger ahora instalaciones portuarias, rutas comerciales y embarcaciones militares en escenarios separados por miles de kilómetros. Así, Ucrania, un país sin una gran flota convencional, está consiguiendo que una de las mayores potencias navales del planeta tenga que replantearse dónde puede dejar sus barcos.
