articles.title: Accelerating Direct Sparse Solvers for Computational Engineering with NVIDIA cuDSS 1.0
articles.text:
Sparse linear systems are at the core of nearly every engineering and scientific simulation, from structural mechanics and computational fluid dynamics to circuit simulation and power grid analysis. As problem sizes and complexity grow, and accuracy needs tighten, developers need a direct solver that scales on GPUs without giving up the robustness that production simulations depend on.
The NVIDIA GPU-accelerated cuDSS library is designed to solve large sparse linear systems for engineering and scientific simulations. The general availability of cuDSS marked a major milestone, making it a production-ready library that developers and software vendors can confidently deploy in commercial applications.
This post walks you through how the cuDSS 1.0 release can help you with your applications. Specifically, it explains where industry-leading performance gains can be realized on real-world workloads, how the new pivoting and matching defaults improve accuracy on difficult symmetric indefinite systems, and how system-level optimization with intelligent use of GPU and CPU resources together enable solving problems at scale.
Enabling best performance for key computational engineering applications
Benchmark matrices for cuDSS were selected from key semiconductor design, manufacturing, and computer-aided engineering workflows, including circuit simulation, TCAD, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, and fluid dynamics. They span a wide range of sparsity patterns, conditioning, and scaling behavior.
Figures 1-3 show cuDSS 1.0 geometric-mean speedups on these real-world problems of 2.5x for analysis (reordering and symbolic factorization) (Figure 1), 5.9x for numerical factorization (Figure 2), and 151x for triangular solve (Figure 3). In practice, applications typically combine all three phases, so overall speedup depends on each phase’s relative contribution.
Benchmark configuration: cuDSS 1.0 speedup against Intel MKL version 2026.1.0; GPU: NVIDIA B200 (192 GB HBM3e); CPU: INTEL XEON PLATINUM 8570. The benchmark result reflects cuDSS performance relative to Intel MKL on a given matrix. The benchmark is not a comparison across the vendor matrices themselves.
cuDSS performance has steadily improved over releases for a variety of workloads, including superpanels in factorization (v0.4.0), multithreaded analysis (v0.5.0), tuned solve-phase kernels (v0.8.0), and targeted performance optimizations (v1.0). Figures 4 and 5 show speedups relative to v0.3.0 through v1.0 for two matrices of significantly different sizes and structures. Developers building on cuDSS get these gains just by upgrading, with no changes to their application code. These improvements spanning across the different solve phases enable applications to be run faster from end to end and take on larger, more complex sparse problems.
Enhancing accuracy for symmetric matrices
Many of the numerically challenging sparse systems are symmetric indefinite. They arise in optimal power flow, mixed finite element discretizations of fluid flow and porous media, PDE-constrained optimization, and interior mode computation for structural problems.
cuDSS now offers symmetry-preserving matching and scaling and Bunch-Kaufman pivoting, both enabled by default for symmetric systems. Matching and scaling use HSL MC64, from the HSL collection of Fortran codes for large-scale scientific computation. For more information, refer to The HSL Mathematical Software Library.
Prior to cuDSS 1.0, matching was off by default because it did not preserve symmetry, which hurt memory and performance. Matching now preserves symmetry and is on by default, improving accuracy in many cases. It can add overhead during analysis and later stages if it causes additional fill-in. To restore the previous nonsymmetric behavior, set CUDSS_CONFIG_FORCE_NONSYMMETRIC_MATCHING.
For symmetric indefinite matrices, diagonal-only pivoting preserves symmetry but can cause unrecoverable accuracy loss when diagonal elements are small. Saddle-point and KKT matrices are the canonical examples. Previously, cuDSS used diagonal pivoting with perturbation of small pivots, which led to accuracy loss for many saddle-point matrices.
Bunch-Kaufman pivoting fixes this by allowing 2×2 pivots, which keep the factorization stable while preserving symmetry. With CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN, cuDSS applies the local Bunch-Kaufman test to each column and chooses a 1×1 pivot, an interchanged 1×1 pivot, or a 2×2 block. The threshold can be overridden through CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD. Smaller values favor 1×1 pivots, which can give sparser factors at the cost of accuracy.
Bunch-Kaufman pairs effectively with symmetry-preserving matching: matching cycles are split into candidate 1×1/2×2 groups that reordering keeps adjacent, so the pivot search finds the 2×2 blocks it needs without breaking the fill-reducing ordering. CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO now selects Bunch-Kaufman for symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices wherever it is supported, and otherwise falls back to diagonal pivoting.
Table 1 shows results of solving linear systems \(Ax = b\) with cuDSS 1.0 under two configurations:
- No matching (CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE) and diagonal pivoting (CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL)
- With matching and scaling (CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT), and Bunch-Kaufman pivoting (CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN)
The latter configuration is now the default configuration. In each case, the matrix \(A\) is from the SuiteSparse matrix collection, and the right hand side vector \(b\) is a corresponding vector of all ones. For each system considered, common measures of accuracy for linear system solvers are reported. With \(x\) representing the solution computed by cuDSS, Relative Residual is the typical 2-norm measurement:
\(\frac{\left\|b-Ax\right\|_2}{\left\|b\right\|_2}\)
while NRBE is the normwise relative backward error, again measured with respect to the 2-norm:
\(\frac{\left\|b-Ax\right\|_2}{\left\|A\right\|_F\left\|x\right\|_2+\left\|b\right\|_2}\)
Note that the NRBE computation uses the Frobenius norm of \(A\) because it is easy to compute for large, sparse \(A\). Each configuration also reports the number of perturbed 1×1 pivots, meaning pivots replaced by an appropriately signed pivot epsilon because they were too small to proceed. Perturbed pivots indicate accuracy loss in the factorization, caused by an insufficient pivoting strategy or poor matrix conditioning. To get their count, request CUDSS_DATA_NPIVOTS after the factorization phase. Learn more about configuring treatment of perturbed pivots in cuDSS. The results in Table 1 show significant improvement in factorization due to reduced perturbed pivots.
|  |  |  | No matching, diagonal |  |  | Matching, Bunch-Kaufman |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix | n | nnz | Relative residual | NRBE | Perturbed pivots | Relative residual | NRBE | Perturbed pivots | 
| kkt_power | 2063494 | 12771361 | 3.6e+08 | 1.1e-13 | 48106 | 4.9e-05 | 1.4e-23 | 0 | 
| cont-300 | 180895 | 988195 | 9.3e+02 | 1.1e-08 | 42065 | 2.6e-08 | 3.2e-19 | 0 | 
| TSOPF_FS_b39_c30 | 120216 | 3121160 | 2.1e+03 | 3.4e-08 | 36941 | 1.6e-08 | 6.4e-18 | 0 | 
| c-big | 345241 | 2340859 | 1.8e-07 | 4.2e-11 | 0 | 4.3e-14 | 1.0e-17 | 0 | 
| c73-b | 169422 | 1279274 | 1.3e-04 | 1.5e-09 | 0 | 3.6e-13 | 4.0e-18 | 0 | 
Test configuration: cuDSS 1.0, CTK13, RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS)
For these matrices, cuDSS is now up to 10 orders of magnitude more accurate in NRBE, and a stark reduction in perturbed pivots shows improved factorization quality.
cuDSS 1.0 also enables matching and scaling by default for nonsymmetric matrices, not just symmetric and Hermitian ones, with improvements here too. Table 2 shows SuiteSparse matrices that improve with matching enabled.
|  |  |  | No matching, diagonal |  |  | Matching, Bunch-Kaufman |  |  | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matrix | n | nnz | Relative residual | NRBE | Perturbed pivots | Relative residual | NRBE | Perturbed pivots | 
| largebasis | 440020 | 5240084 | 5.4e+01 | 1.8e-06 | 139886 | 2.6e-12 | 3.3e-19 | 0 | 
| hvdc2 | 189860 | 1339638 | 1.2e+00 | 3.4e-09 | 13 | 1.0e-10 | 2.9e-19 | 0 | 
| TSOPF_RS_b39_c30 | 60098 | 1079986 | 3.7e+42 | 3.1e-04 | 11 | 2.4e-12 | 7.1e-20 | 0 | 
| conf6_0-8×8-20 | 49152 | 1916928 | 2.4e+101 | 4.6e-03 | 22958 | 1.5e-14 | 3.5e-17 | 0 | 
Test configuration: cuDSS 1.0, CTK13, RTX PRO 1000 Blackwell, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS)
While generally helpful, matching with scaling does not always help with improving accuracy specifically. In a few cases, it can result in a loss of accuracy. Matching in cuDSS can be disabled by setting the matching algorithm to CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE.
Hybrid execution paradigm: A solution for small and large problems
Hybrid memory mode reflects a core design philosophy of cuDSS: the GPU and CPU together are the compute platform. Factorization is particularly data hungry, generating a dense fill structure in the L and U factors that can have more non-zeros than the original sparse matrix. Modern server nodes pair an NVIDIA GPU with substantial CPU memory (often 512 GB to 2 TB of DRAM), and hybrid memory mode treats that memory as an extension of the device’s effective capacity.
cuDSS intelligently orchestrates data placement across GPU HBM and CPU DRAM, keeping the most compute-intensive portions of the factorization and solving kernels on the GPU while offloading data not immediately needed to CPU memory. As a result, engineers do not need to partition a simulation into smaller subdomains that fit on the GPU or use multiple GPUs. The full problem can be solved as a single system.
Reduced memory footprint
Figure 2 shows minimum memory requirements reduced by an average of 30% across a representative suite of large VLSI examples. Problems that previously required multiple GPUs can now be solved on a single NVIDIA H100, NVIDIA B200, or a single NVIDIA Vera Rubin, simplifying deployment and reducing compute cost.
In cuDSS, you can query the minimum required device memory for hybrid memory mode using cudssDataGet() with the CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN parameter:
cudssDataGet(cudssHandle, solverData, CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN, &minMemory, sizeof(size_t), NULL);
This should be called after the analysis phase. More broadly, you can also use CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES with cudssDataGet() to get a full breakdown in a single call. The returned array includes:
- [0] – permanent device memory
- [1] – peak device memory
- [4] – minimum device memory for hybrid mode
- [5] – maximum host (CPU) memory for hybrid mode
Note that CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN reflects the total device memory cuDSS needs (not just the matrix factors). You can then pass a custom limit anywhere between that minimum and available free memory (queryable via cudaMemGetInfo) using CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT.
Pinned memory handler: Optimized data transfers
Hybrid memory mode in cuDSS keeps full buffers holding factor values on the host. Prior to cuDSS 1.0, these host buffers by default were pinned (registered) after allocation by calling standard cudaHostRegister() / cudaHostUnregister() CUDA APIs. This behavior is controlled through the following script:
cudssConfigSet(config, CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_CUDA_REGISTER_MEMORY, &value, sizeof(int));
The default behavior is equivalent to setting value = 1(if the device supports it). Note that value = 0 (disabling registration) can actually be faster in some cases, since cudaHostRegister has an overhead. For large systems, the overhead can be quite noticeable. Now there is a way to reduce this overhead.
cuDSS 1.0 introduces an opt-in user-configurable pinned memory handler, reducing latency and bandwidth overhead for host-to-device transfers in hybrid CPU-GPU execution.
cudssSetPinnedMemHandler() allows users to implement a custom allocator for pinned memory, similar to the existing cudssSetDeviceMemHandler() for device memory allocations, but the new pinned memory handler is for the pinned host memory. A minimal implementation requires alloc and dealloc functions:
class ExamplePinnedMemPool {
  public:
    int alloc(void **ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t) {
        if (size == 0) {
            *ptr = NULL;
            return 0;
        }
 int status = cudaMallocHost(ptr, size);
 return status;
    }
    int dealloc(void *ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t) {
        if (ptr == NULL) {
            return 0;
        }
        return static_cast<int>(cudaFreeHost(ptr));
    }
This simple implementation would not change the performance compared to the default, which is using cudaHostRegister(). To achieve better performance for the hybrid memory mode for large systems, users can now implement special handling such as pinned memory pools and parallel prefaulting.
Symbolic factorization improvements
Symbolic factorization determines the nonzero structure of the factors and prepares internal data structures for numerical factorization. Recent releases added GPU speedups and optional CPU offloading.
In cuDSS 1.0, GPU symbolic factorization is 2.21x faster (geometric mean) than in cuDSS 0.8.0 on both NVIDIA B200 and H100. The comparison covers ~400 matrix/configuration cases with 80 to 130.3 million rows on B200, and ~250 cases with 120 to 22.9 million rows on H100. Replacing only the symbolic factorization timings, with reordering, numerical factorization, and solve held at 0.8.0 values, gives estimated geometric-mean end-to-end speedups of 1.18x on B200 and 1.14x on H100.
Optional execution of symbolic factorization on the host introduced through hybrid execute mode in cuDSS 0.8.0 to improve two cases:
- Small matrices: Hybrid execute mode was designed for smaller matrices, running numerical factorization and solving on the host (reordering always runs on the host). Prior to cuDSS 0.8, GPU symbolic factorization could add device execution and data-transfer overhead to this otherwise host-based computation. Running it on the host can reduce this overhead.
- Large matrices: Host symbolic factorization can reduce peak device memory during analysis, making analysis possible for systems that would otherwise exceed device memory.
Starting with cuDSS 0.8, users can control where symbolic factorization is executed by enabling/disabling the hybrid execute mode. To run symbolic factorization on the host, enable the hybrid execute mode before analysis:
int value = 1; cudssConfigSet(config, CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE, &value, sizeof(int));
With hybrid execute mode disabled, symbolic factorization runs on the GPU. With it enabled, symbolic factorization runs on the host, even when numerical factorization and solve remain on the GPU.
For better host performance, enable the threading layer to and allow cuDSS to use more than one CPU thread. The CUDSS_CONFIG_HOST_NTHREADS setting controls the thread limit for cuDSS.
Hybrid execute mode and hybrid memory mode can now be enabled together in supported configurations. They serve different purposes: hybrid execute mode controls where computation runs, while hybrid memory mode allows factor data to be stored in host memory. The remaining mode restrictions still apply.
| Phase | Default | With hybrid execute mode enabled | 
|---|---|---|
| Reordering (including matching) | Host | Host | 
| Symbolic factorization | Device | Host | 
| Numerical factorization | Device | Host, device, or host/device* | 
| Solve | Device | Host, device, or host/device* | 
*With hybrid memory mode disabled, an internal heuristic selects placement for numerical factorization and solve-based on matrix structure. Enabling hybrid execute mode does not force these phases onto the host. When hybrid memory mode is also enabled, numerical factorization and solve use the GPU, while symbolic factorization runs on the host.
Get started with cuDSS
cuDSS 1.0 is the production-ready standard for performance-critical simulation, extending GPU computing to problem scales previously impractical or impossible to solve. The release rests on three mutually reinforcing technical pillars:
- Advanced accuracy techniques improve robustness
- Best-in-class performance delivers consistent, substantial speedups over CPU-based solvers
- A system-level optimization strategy, anchored by host-assisted symbolic factorization, hybrid memory mode, and a significantly reduced GPU memory footprint
As each new GPU architecture brings greater memory capacity, higher memory bandwidth, and faster interconnects, cuDSS algorithmic innovations will compound these advances, enabling ever larger and more efficient solutions to the sparse linear systems at the core of the world’s most demanding engineering applications.
Download cuDSS to get started.

articles.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.text:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue.
While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.
The cybersecurity agency also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within three days, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, CISA urged all network defenders, including private-sector security teams, to prioritize patching this flaw to block ongoing attacks that may target their networks.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise," it warned.
Internet intelligence company Censys now observes nearly 14,900 Cisco Expressway hosts exposed online, but there is no information on how many have already secured against attacks targeting the CVE-2026-76466 vulnerability.
Exploited to gain root on Internet-exposed devices
While CISA has yet to share details on these ongoing attacks, Russian cybersecurity company F6 said on Thursday that it spotted attackers using an unnamed AI assistant to successfully exploit CVE-2026-7646 and gain remote command execution with full root privileges on Internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices.
"The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices. Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network," F6 security researchers noted.
"After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure. They used custom Python scripts designed to scan the network, discover accessible SMB resources, interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and explore GitLab repositories in order to exfiltrate credentials and other sensitive information."
Two weeks ago, CISA also flagged a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability (CVE-2026-20320) as actively exploited in attacks and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by November 24.
According to threat intelligence firm Malbear Labs, a Chinese-speaking threat actor abused CVE-2026-20320 in autonomous AI attacks targeting a European telecommunications provider and 13 organizations that used its data centers and cloud infrastructure.
CISA has added 103 Cisco vulnerabilities to its list of actively exploited flaws since November 2021, seven of which ransomware gangs have also used in the wild.

articles.title: Bitcoin: cuál es el precio de esta criptomoneda este día
articles.text:
El bitcoin fue la primera criptomoneda que salió al mercado. Ideada por Satoshi Nakamoto en 2008, esta divisa digital promovía un ideal libertario y buscaba poner en jaque a las instituciones monetarias y financieras tradicionales luego de la crisis financiera mundial que se vivió ese año.
La victoria electoral de Donald Trump significó un movimiento positivo para las principales criptomonedas del mercado. A finales de 2024, bitcoin registró un nuevo máximo histórico que logró superar los 107.000 dólares por unidad, después de que el presidente estadounidense reiteró su idea de crear una reserva estratégica de la criptodivisa en Estados Unidos.
Las divisas digitales serán un foco de atención durante este año, las iniciativas del presidente de Estados Unidos y el desarrollo de nuevos modelos de inteligencia artificial fungirán un papel importante en la cotización de estos activos. Después del lanzamiento del nuevo modelo de IA chino DeepSeek, BTC y otras criptos cayeron en la mayoría de los mercados de valores.
Cotización de la criptomoneda Bitcoin
El precio de la criptomoneda bitcoin para este día a las 14:00 horas (UTC) es de 61027.57 dólares. Esto quiere decir que el activo digital registró un cambio de 0.63% en el último día, así como un movimiento de 0.0% en la última hora.
Por su nivel de capitalización, esta moneda digital ocupa la posición #1 entre las más populares.
El flujo histórico de inversiones impulsa a bitcoin a máximos nunca antes vistos
En marzo del año pasado el bitcoin ha logrado un nuevo máximo histórico, superando los valores anteriores y reafirmándose como la criptomoneda más importante en el mercado, acercándose a los 73 mil dólares. Este récord se obtuvo en medio de un flujo sin precedentes de inversiones hacia las criptomonedas, un acontecimiento notable para el sector financiero digital.
El aumento en el valor de bitcoin ocurre en un contexto donde hay un entrante masivo de capital hacia las criptomonedas, lo que indica un creciente interés y confianza de los inversores en estos activos. La subida del precio beneficia no solo a bitcoin sino que también tiene un impacto positivo en el mercado de las criptomonedas en general, favoreciendo una mayor estabilidad y visibilidad, de acuerdo a un análisis de Bloomberg.
Expertos financiaron este aumento a diferentes factores, como la adopción institucional de las criptomonedas, la búsqueda de alternativas de inversión debido a la incertidumbre económica mundial y la innovación continua en la tecnología blockchain que respalda a bitcoin y otras divisas digitales. Esta combinación de factores ha creado un entorno propicio para el crecimiento continuo en el valor de Bitcoin.
Cómo adquirir criptomonedas
Para comprarlas e intercambiarlas se utilizan portales especializados. Su valor varía en función de la oferta, de la demanda y del compromiso de los usuarios, por lo que puede cambiar más rápido que el dinero tradicional, pero mientras más gente esté interesada y quiera comprar determinada divisa, mayor será su valor.
No obstante, quien invierte en este tipo de monedas digitales debe tener muy claro que esta forma trae consigo un elevado riesgo al capital, pues, así como puede haber un incremento, también puede tener inesperadamente un desplome y acabar con los ahorros de sus usuarios.
Para almacenarlas, los usuarios deben contar con un monedero digital o wallet, que en realidad es un software a través del cual es posible guardar, enviar y hacer transacciones de las criptomonedas. En realidad, este tipo de monederos sólo guarda las claves que marcan la propiedad y el derecho de una persona sobre cierta criptomoneda, por lo que estos códigos son los que en realidad se deben proteger.

articles.title: Tesla annonce enfin un nouveau modèle grand public, mais attendez vous à une douche froide
articles.text:
Le Tesla Roadster est une révolution ! Non parce qu’il est capable des pirouettes les plus improbables. Juste parce qu’il s’agit d’un véhicule remplaçant un modèle existant. C’est peu, mais chez Tesla, c’est tout simplement historique ! Sauf que dans les faits, une telle folie sur roues a peu de chances de débarquer chez nous telle quelle. Tesla explique même qu’il est possible que le véhicule ne soit pas du tout livré !
Avouez que ça jette un froid… C’est peut-être la raison pour laquelle le constructeur vient d’annoncer un autre modèle plus raisonnable. Sauf qu’encore une fois, il y a un hic qui pourrait gâcher la surprise… Lors du sommet Dealbook du New York Times consacré à l’économie et à la politique, Elon Musk a confirmé l’arrivée d’un Model Y sans volant ni pédales « adapté pour transporter 6 ou 7 personnes ».
Un Model Y avec 7 places… mais sans volant ni pédales
Le soufflé retombe aussi sec, nous qui attendions avec impatience un nouveau modèle d’entrée de gamme. Inutile de dire qu’un Model Y sans aucune commande ne fait pas sauter au plafond… Pourtant, l’engin est censé combler l’attente avant l’arrivée du Roadster. Un peu maigre comme lot de consolation, vous l’accorderez. Pourtant, il s’agit bien d’un véhicule complémentaire au Cybercab, qui ne peut trimbaler que 2 occupants.
Musk l’a bien confirmé en expliquant que Tesla a « toujours besoin de véhicules autonomes si ses clients voyagent en famille ». C’est la raison pour laquelle la marque prévoit « une version autonome du Model Y qui n’aura pas de volant ou de pédales ». En y réfléchissant plus profondément, on se dit que le constructeur avait possiblement prévu le coup depuis 2016 avec la Model 3. Le tableau de bord ultra dépouillé n’était peut-être pas là par hasard.
Vers l’arrivée d’un Model Y L autonome en Europe ?
En retirant volant et pédales, vous vous retrouvez avec un intérieur parfaitement symétrique, comme sur le Cybercab ! Aucune information supplémentaire n’a cependant été livrée. Cela dit, le fait d’évoquer le transport de 7 personnes est un indice révélateur convergeant les hypothèses vers le Model Y L. Cette version rallongée du SUV offrant une meilleure praticité est néanmoins indisponible chez nous.
Elle pourrait bientôt l’être si ce futur véhicule est confirmé en Europe. On bénéficierait alors d’une version améliorée des Robotaxis circulant outre-Atlantique. Pour rappel, ces engins autonomes ne sont ni plus ni moins des Model Y pouvant être utilisés à la demande. Mais ils conservent leurs volants et pédales, par sécurité. Et ils ne sont pas à vendre, contrairement au Cybercab. Le futur Model Y L autonome devrait donc suivre la même recette.

articles.title: What it takes for Indian startups to win when building is no longer the hard part
articles.text:
What it takes for Indian startups to win when building is no longer the hard part
At TechSparks 2026, Lukas Jablonskas of Hostinger and Amar Dixit of WOI India discussed how founders can turn ideas into sustainable businesses in the age of AI.
Building a product is no longer the biggest hurdle for many aspiring entrepreneurs. AI tools have made it easier to develop applications, test ideas, and bring solutions to market, but getting customers to use those products and building a sustainable business remain difficult. As more founders gain access to similar technology, understanding the market, finding the right distribution channels, and securing suitable funding become increasingly important.
At TechSparks 2026, Lukas Jablonskas, Head of WebPro at Hostinger, and Amar Dixit, CEO of WOI India, joined Madanmohan Rao, Research Director at YourStory, for a panel discussion titled ‘The New Startup Infrastructure: Expanding India’s Builder Economy’, exploring what it takes to build a globally relevant company from anywhere in India and how access to technology can be turned into sustainable entrepreneurship.
Understanding customers is still a competitive advantage
For Jablonskas, access to technology alone does not give an entrepreneur an advantage. AI can help founders build faster, but it cannot replace their understanding of the people they are building for. He used the example of two entrepreneurs developing a solution for the dentistry sector. Even if one has a better grasp of the technology, the other could build a more relevant product by understanding dentists, their customers, and the challenges they face in a particular market.
“The differentiator that you have now as a builder, as an entrepreneur, is talking to users, understanding your users the best, and being able to get the first user faster than others,” Jablonskas said. The ability to identify a genuine customer need, therefore, remains central to building a business, regardless of how advanced the available tools become.
Understanding the customer is only part of the challenge. Founders must also work out how to reach potential buyers and persuade them to choose their products over competing alternatives.
Dixit pointed out that developing an application or coming up with a solution is becoming easier, but validating it with the market and identifying potential buyers require a different set of capabilities.
“Anyone can build an app, anyone can come up with a solution,” he said, adding that having a distribution base in place can make the journey considerably easier. In a market where technology is increasingly accessible, the ability to find and retain customers can determine whether a product becomes a viable business.
Building a startup ecosystem beyond Bengaluru
Dixit believes entrepreneurs need more than funding to turn their ideas into businesses. At WOI India, the focus is on creating an integrated ecosystem that brings together capital, education, and services that help founders navigate the practical demands of running a company, from legal and financial requirements to fundraising, marketing and sales.
The organization operates a startup park in Koramangala, Bengaluru, and plans to build an environment where founders can access resources and support in one place.
Dixit said India needs more such ecosystems across Tier II and Tier III cities, rather than concentrating entrepreneurial opportunities in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Gurugram. The aim is to enable people to build companies from different parts of the country without having to move to an established startup hub to access the necessary networks and services.
This broader approach also calls for a rethink of how startups are funded. While venture capital has helped companies pursue rapid growth, Dixit pointed out that the model is not suitable for every business. India has diverse markets and businesses with different growth trajectories, and not all founders are looking to build unicorns or eventually list their companies on the stock market. Some businesses can generate revenue, create employment, and contribute to the economy without following that path.
Dixit called for more funding options, including family offices, high-net-worth individuals, and investors who can offer strategic support alongside capital. He also discussed the potential for funds that seek more modest returns over shorter periods than traditional venture capital investments. Such models could help entrepreneurs whose businesses do not fit conventional venture capital expectations find the backing they need to grow.
The technologies shaping the next wave
Jablonskas spoke about the potential of agentic AI, where systems use tools, assess the results and adapt based on feedback. Dixit pointed to physical AI as another area attracting global investment. He also called for more startups in agritech, a sector WOI India is keen to invest in, given agriculture’s importance to India.
For aspiring founders, Jablonskas had a simple message: test the ideas you are most afraid might fail. Early feedback can help founders understand what works and what needs to change. “So be very open and allow yourself to fail. This is the biggest thing I could recommend to all of you,” he said.
Dixit’s advice was to play the long game. Building a company takes persistence, and founders need to be prepared for a journey that may not deliver immediate results.

articles.title: India ranks sixth globally in GTA VI search volume, says study
articles.text:
India ranks sixth globally in GTA VI search volume, says study
India recorded nearly 9.44 lakh average monthly searches for GTA VI-related terms, ranking sixth globally by search volume. However, it ranked 106th on a per-capita basis, according to a study by The Action Network.
India ranks sixth globally in total search volume for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), recording approximately 943,900 average monthly searches for the game-related terms, according to a study by The Action Network.
However, when adjusted for population, India ranks 106th globally, with around 66 searches per 100,000 people. This highlights the difference between the scale of interest in a large market such as India and the intensity of interest among smaller populations.
The Netherlands topped the rankings with 2,045 average monthly searches per 100,000 people, followed by France (1,594), Finland (1,514), Switzerland (1,490) and Belgium (1,483). The Netherlands recorded 369,900 monthly searches despite having a population of approximately 18.1 million, compared with France's 1.09 million searches and population of 68.7 million.
Meanwhile, the United States recorded the highest overall search volume, with 3.06 million average monthly searches, followed by other major markets such as Brazil, Germany, France and the United Kingdom. However, the US ranked 22nd on a per-capita basis.
An Action Network spokesperson said: “An analysis of Google search data found the Netherlands to be the world's most GTA VI-obsessed country, with 2,045 average monthly searches per 100,000 people, ahead of France and Finland.”
The study examined average monthly searches over the preceding 12 months for four keywords—GTA VI, GTA 6, Grand Theft Auto VI and Grand Theft Auto 6—across 150 countries and all 50 US states. Search volumes were adjusted for population to determine interest per 100,000 people.
India's growing appetite for GTA VI
The search interest is reflected in GTA VI's launch-day response in India, where gaming cafes, livestreams and social media saw heightened activity.
India has an estimated 550 million gamers, according to Reuters, although most play on mobile devices. This has created an opportunity for gaming cafes to offer access to premium console titles to consumers who may not own expensive gaming hardware.
Gaming cafes charged around Rs 250 per hour to play GTA VI. A Delhi-based cafe received 40-50 enquiries on launch day and was fully booked through the weekend. Reuters also reported crowds at gaming cafes in Delhi, Bengaluru and Srinagar.
The game's popularity has also spilled over into India's creator economy. Popular YouTubers CarryMinati and Mythpat streamed GTA VI for around 10 hours each, with both streams crossing 13 million views by the afternoon of November 19.
A separate analysis by data research platform seodata.dev found that searches for 'GTA 6 price' averaged 49,500 a month in India. It also found that searches for GTA VI's female protagonist, Lucia, were more than nine times those for Jason, at 4,400 and 480 average monthly searches, respectively.
The economics behind the hype
While search rankings indicate growing anticipation for GTA VI, they do not necessarily translate into game sales, pre-orders or active players. This distinction is important in India, where gaming is predominantly mobile-first and premium console gaming remains a smaller market.
Beyond game sales, major releases create opportunities for gaming cafes, content creators, livestreaming platforms, hardware manufacturers and advertisers. The success of GTA V also highlights the commercial potential of long-running gaming franchises that generate revenue through initial sales and recurring online engagement.
Image source: Rockstar Games

articles.title: Ladybird, un véritable concurrent à Chrome et Firefox, arrive en alpha
articles.text:
Lancer un nouveau navigateur est à la portée de presque tout le monde. Entre Orion, Arc, Dia, Atlas et tous les autres, ces dernières années n’ont pas été avares en nouvelles manières de surfer sur le web. Créer un moteur de rendu de zéro demande un tout autre travail, et c’est précisément ce qu’a annoncé la Ladybird Browser Initiative ce lundi 23 novembre.
En développement depuis longtemps, le navigateur Ladybird vient officiellement de sortir en version alpha avec son moteur maison. De quoi enfin concurrencer réellement Chrome et Firefox.
Sécurisez vos achats durant Black Friday avec la meilleure offre de l’année. Dénichez les bonnes affaires, Bitdefender s’occupe des arnaques.
Pourquoi c’est important d’avoir un nouveau moteur de rendu ?
Les plus vieilles et les plus vieux se souviendront sans doute d’une époque lointaine où le marché des navigateurs web était dominé par Internet Explorer 6 et où la plupart des sites web étaient « optimisés » pour le navigateur de Microsoft. Quiconque avait l’outrecuidance d’utiliser Firefox à l’époque était régulièrement confronté à des pages web qui ne fonctionnaient pas proprement, alors même que le logiciel respectait bien mieux les standards du web que son concurrent.
C’est cette différence et cette compétition dans le milieu des moteurs de rendu qui a forcé Microsoft à améliorer son navigateur et a permis à un web plus sain de se développer. Or, l’histoire semble aujourd’hui se répéter avec Blink, le moteur de rendu développé par Google. Ce dernier propulse Chrome, navigateur ultra-dominant, mais aussi la plupart de ses concurrents. Résultat : quand Google prend la décision de réduire l’efficacité des bloqueurs de pub, c’est quasiment tout l’écosystème du web qui est contraint de se mettre au pas.
Rompre avec Google !
Voir un nouveau moteur émerger est donc une excellente nouvelle pour la diversité et la résilience du web. Pour le moment, seul Ladybird l’utilise, mais son code est open source et rien n’empêche qui que ce soit de s’en emparer pour proposer une expérience vraiment différente de celles de Google (Blink), d’Apple (WebKit, le moteur de Safari) ou de Mozilla (Gecko, celui de Firefox).
La Ladybird Browser Initiative promet que son navigateur et son moteur de rendu sont complètement indépendants et que la structure n’acceptera jamais d’accord de monétisation avec des moteurs de recherche ou d’accord de monétisation tout court d’ailleurs. Une manière de se démarquer de Mozilla qui reste malgré tout terriblement dépendant de Google de ce point de vue–là.
    Pour aller plus loin
Vous voulez quitter Google, mais ne savez pas par où commencer ? Ce site a tout ce qu’il vous faut
            
Si vous voulez voir à quoi ressemble un web qui se bat pour son indépendance, vous pouvez donc essayer le navigateur Ladybird. À noter tout de même, ce dernier n’est pour le moment disponible qu’en version alpha et uniquement sur macOS (Apple Silicon) et Linux. Une version Windows arrivera ultérieurement. Il est fort probable que vous ne voyez pas immédiatement la différence avec Chrome ou Firefox et que des plantages interviennent (le bonheur des versions alpha) mais au moins vous ne serez pas dépendant des décisions d’une énorme multinationale.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, ce casque Sony noté 5/5 passe à 314,98 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le casque Bluetooth Sony WH-1000XM6 "5 étoiles" à 314,98 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Sony WH-1000XM6 passe à 314,98 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 8 % et 28,22 € d'économie. Référence du silence grâce à sa réduction de bruit active et doté d'une restitution sonore très précise, ce casque Bluetooth affiche la note maximale de 5/5 dans nos tests à ce jour.
Avec le Sony WH-1000XM6, le constructeur japonais perfectionne sa recette pour proposer un casque Bluetooth circum-auriculaire axé sur l'isolation phonique et la fidélité acoustique. Ce modèle améliore la formule de ses aînés et s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le casque descend à 314,98 € chez Amazon, soit environ 8 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 343,20 €. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 28,22 €.
Isolation de premier ordre et endurance solide au banc d'essai
Le casque sans fil bénéficie d'une conception pliable pratique pour les déplacements et assure un maintien confortable sur les oreilles. Notre banc d'essai a mesuré 36 heures d'autonomie continue avec la réduction de bruit active enclenchée, ce qui permet d'enchaîner plusieurs jours d'écoute sans recharger la batterie. Comme l'indique notre test complet, l'atténuation des bruits extérieurs isole très efficacement dans les transports bruyants.
Sony WH-1000XM6
Points forts
- Restitution précise des médiums.
- Aigus naturels, superbe dynamique.
- Réduction du bruit la plus polyvalente du marché.
- Parfait compromis entre confort et maintien.
- Conception pliable.
- Utilisation intuitive et fonctionnalités nombreuses.
Points faibles
- Basses un peu trop généreuses.
- Finition légère pour du haut de gamme.
- Absence d'audio via USB-C.
- Microphones perfectibles.
Une restitution sonore dynamique malgré quelques limites matérielles
Ce modèle délivre des médiums précis et des aigus naturels, même si les basses s'avèrent un peu trop généreuses par défaut. La transmission sans fil s'appuie sur le codec LDAC pour préserver les détails du flux audio, mais notre laboratoire a relevé une latence Bluetooth de 210 ms, perceptible si l'on regarde une vidéo sans synchronisation automatique.
Les finitions semblent un peu légères pour un produit haut de gamme, les microphones peinent par vent fort et le port USB-C ne véhicule pas le flux audio direct. Ces concessions n'affecteront pas les mélomanes nomades qui recherchent d'abord une écoute musicale immersive.
Sony WH-1000XM4C : l'autre option face au Sony WH-1000XM6
Le Sony WH-1000XM4C adopte une structure très proche des générations antérieures avec des coussinets non amovibles, tout en conservant une réduction de bruit performante et une sonorité bien équilibrée dans les médiums et les aigus.
Le Sony WH-1000XM4C coûte 64,99 € de moins que le Sony WH-1000XM6 à son tarif remisé, mais le XM6 justifie cet écart par ses coussinets détachables et sa réduction de bruit plus efficace.

Points faibles

- Connectivité limitée (pas de LE Audio ni d'audio en USB-C).
- Mode Transparence peu efficace.
- Micros en difficulté en milieu bruyant.
- Quelques caractéristiques datées.

articles.title: Which iPad Model Should You Get? Full 2026 Update
articles.text:
Apple's iPad lineup has an unusual pecking order in 2026. The newest iPad mini packs an OLED display and the A20 Pro chip, while the larger iPad Air still uses an LCD. With current discounts, the Air can even cost less. Meanwhile, a round of price hikes has pushed the entry-level iPad to $449 and the Pro into territory where a MacBook starts to look tempting.
The result is that there's no obvious best iPad for everyone. We still believe Apple leads the way in tablets, thanks to hardware and software that work remarkably well together. But which model is best for you? That's what this guide is for.
We've updated our guide to reflect the latest models, prices, and accessories. Below is a side-by-side look at the current lineup, followed by the trade-offs that matter most when deciding which iPad is worth your money.
| Model | iPad | iPad Mini | iPad Air M4 | iPad Pro M5 | 
| Generation | 11th-gen | 8th-gen | 8th-gen | 8th-gen | 
| Release Date | Mar 2025 | Nov 2026 | Mar 2026 | Oct 2025 | 
| MSRP / Amazon | $449 / $399 | $699 / $699 | $749 / $649 | $1,199 / $1,099 | 
| Processor | A16 | A20 Pro | M4 | M5 | 
| Display Size | 10.9" | 8.5" | 10.9" or 12.9" | 11" or 13" | 
| Display Technology | 60Hz LCD | 60Hz OLED | 60Hz LCD | 120Hz OLED | 
| Min / Max Storage | 128GB / 512GB | 128GB / 512GB | 128GB / 1TB | 256GB / 2TB | 
| Keyboard | Magic Keyboard Folio | n/a | Magic Keyboard for iPad Air | Magic Keyboard for iPad Pro | 
| Pencil | 1st-gen & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | Pencil Pro & USB-C | 
Is the base iPad all you need?
If you're looking for a great tablet for watching videos and browsing the web, the basic and most affordable iPad will cover your needs well. The base iPad has the same display resolution (2360 x 1640) and maximum brightness (500 nits) as the 11-inch iPad Air. Additionally, it features an ultra-wide 12MP front camera, like the other models.
If you want a tablet that can double as a basic laptop, the iPad supports the Magic Keyboard Folio, which includes function keys and a trackpad. While you could get the MacBook Neo for the combined price of the iPad and the keyboard, the iPad can provide a more portable solution if you want a tablet first and foremost, plus it offers a better camera. Although the kickstand design requires more desk space, it allows you to detach the keyboard when needed.
For the price, the base iPad offers impressive features, but it's not the best choice for everyone. The display lacks an anti-reflective coating, making it less ideal for outdoor use. If you use your iPad for drawing, you'll appreciate the fully laminated display and broader color gamut available on other models, too.
Most notably, the A16 SoC and 6GB of RAM pale in comparison to the Apple M4 and 12GB offered by the iPad Air. That also makes it the only current model that can't run Apple Intelligence, which utilizes on-device processing.
Although the iPad includes a USB-C connector, it still supports the 1st-gen Pencil. If you already own the 1st-gen Pencil, you'll need a $9 adapter to connect it. Alternatively, it supports the more affordable USB-C Pencil, which forgoes pressure sensitivity but attaches magnetically to the iPad's bezel.
The iPad's MSRP has been raised to $449 from $349, but can still be had for $399 with the 128GB Wi-Fi model. For an additional $100, you can upgrade to 256GB, and upgrading from 256GB to 512GB costs another $200. Color options include silver, blue, pink, and yellow, offering some vibrant choices even without a case.
The iPad mini goes premium
The iPad Mini has been updated in 2026 with the same A20 Pro chip found in the iPhone 18 Pro series, and 12GB of RAM. It outperforms the M4 chip found in the iPad Air in single-core and graphic tasks, although it still trails in multi-core performance.
You'll struggle to find anything faster in such a small package and at this price, making it a great choice for mobile gaming or 3D modeling on the go.
However, only the 512GB model comes with a fully enabled chip, including two performance cores, four efficiency cores and a dual neural engine. The other versions have one efficiency core and one neural engine disabled.
The Mini is among the largest tablets that most adults can comfortably hold in one hand, measuring 7.7 x 5.2 inches (19.5 x 13.3 cm). Thickness has been significantly reduced to 0.21 inch (5.4mm) from 0.25 inch (6.3mm) in the previous, A17-based model. If you need a tablet you can use while standing, the Mini may be your best choice. Strangely, the front camera has been moved to the longer edge, like the other models, making it less ideal for one-handed use.
With a resolution of 2316x1512, the new 8.5-inch display has slimmer bezels than its predecessor and the highest pixel density of any iPad. It uses an OLED panel with 1,200 nits of peak brightness (600 nits for the entire screen) while still being able to display true black at the pixel level.
It's also the first iPad with an "acoustic display," which uses vibrations from the screen to help produce sound. By eliminating traditional speaker grilles, Apple has also made the mini IP67-rated for water and dust resistance.
It only supports Bluetooth keyboards, but it does support the wireless Pencil Pro, which adds features like rotation, squeeze, haptic feedback and Find My compatibility. Even with the USB-C version, the Mini supports the mouse-like Pencil hover feature. It supports 35W fast charging, although the included adapter only provides 20W.
Unlike previous Mini models (and like the iPad Pro), the new Mini only comes in two colors: "midnight" and "starlight." The Mini starts at $699 with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi. The storage upgrade options are the same as the basic iPad's. An optional nano-texture display reduces glare for another $100, but is only available on the 256GB and 512GB models.
If you're interested in the Mini for its size rather than its performance, you can still get the previous model for just $499.
The iPad Air remains the sweet spot
The iPad Air is powered by a cut-down version of Apple's M4 chip, with three performance cores and five efficiency cores, and 12GB of RAM. It excels in multitasking, video editing, and other demanding tasks, although its LCD display isn't ideal for HDR work. It's a good choice if you want something larger than the iPad mini without the limitations of the basic iPad. The Air is compatible with the space-efficient Magic Keyboard as well as the Pencil Pro.
The 11-inch iPad Air currently starts at $649 with 128GB of storage, and for an additional $200, you can upgrade to the 13-inch model. The larger version offers higher maximum brightness (600 nits), enhanced bass, and a 4:3 aspect ratio, which reduces scrolling when held horizontally. A comparable upgrade to the iPad Pro would cost $300.
The Air's color options include starlight, space gray, and subtle shades of blue and purple.
Like the Mini, the Air allows upgrades to 256GB and 512GB of storage. For an additional $300 (up from $200), you can expand from 512GB to 1TB – still a more affordable option than the $400 cost on the iPad Pro.
If you're looking for an iPad with a 13-inch display and 1TB of storage, the Air can save you hundreds compared to the Pro.
When is the iPad Pro worth the premium?
The iPad Pro is designed for professionals who demand top performance. Graphic artists will appreciate the smooth experience of drawing on a 120Hz display. For interior designers who need to show clients room layouts in real time, the built-in LiDAR can be genuinely useful.
Video editors who work on the go may find the Pro to be the device of their dreams. Its tandem OLED display uses two stacked panels to achieve up to 1,600 nits of peak HDR brightness, with 1,000 nits sustained across the entire screen.
It's also a great backup camera, with ProRes recording (the 256GB versions can only shoot ProRes at 1080p, though), audio zoom and stereo recording.
The Apple M5 chip easily outperforms the cut-down M4 in the Air, with a USB-C port that supports USB4/Thunderbolt speeds. Only the 1TB and 2TB versions feature a fully enabled M5 with four performance cores, six efficiency cores, and 16GB of RAM, ideal for heavy multitasking.
Other versions of the iPad Pro have one disabled performance core and 12GB of RAM, but they still outperform the Air's M4.
The iPad Pro is compatible with the Pencil Pro, and the Magic Keyboard for iPad Pro, which includes function keys and haptic feedback on the trackpad. The device also boasts four speakers and a TrueDepth front camera with Animoji and Memoji support. It supports 60W fast charging, but not with the included 20W adapter.
The 11" iPad Pro Wi-Fi model currently starts at $1,099 with 256GB of storage (Amazon discounts it $100 vs. Apple's MSRP). The larger 13" iPad Pro is currently an extra $300 (that's a cool and hefty $1,399). Increasing storage to 512GB will be $200. Going from that to 1TB will be $400, ane upgrading from 1TB to 2TB will add $500 to the price. The iPad Pro only comes in black and silver.
Should you add 5G to your iPad?
Adding sub-6GHz 5G to your basic iPad, iPad Mini or iPad Air will make it $150 more expensive. Adding the exact same capability to your iPad Pro will add $200 to the price. Sure, you can turn your smartphone into a hotspot, but doing so will drain the battery of both devices.
The more expensive the iPad, the more practical it may be to invest in cellular connectivity. For a Pro model with 1TB or more of storage, the extra $200 is likely a worthwhile expense.

articles.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls
Today we are announcing the general availability of the trusted access program API on Amazon Bedrock. The API gives you one place to discover, request, and enroll in model provider trusted access programs. We are also announcing the public preview of the first two offerings, Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC). Both are available on Amazon Bedrock, including Claude Fable, Claude Mythos, and Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 used through the Cyber Verification Program (CVP).
Frontier AI labs require stricter safety monitoring policies to their most capable models, and those policies still apply on Amazon Bedrock. For eligible customers, model providers also offer customers more control on how those policies are met, such as where retained data is stored and how it is reviewed. Each offering has its own terms, approvals, and settings.
The Amazon Bedrock trusted access program API gives every provider offering one consistent Amazon Bedrock experience. Your teams discover offerings, check eligibility, and enroll in the same way for every provider. Your administrators decide who can enroll, using existing IAM policies and service control policies. As more model providers add offerings, those appear in the same place.
EFS and EDC were built in partnership between AWS and Anthropic. They let you access Anthropic’s most capable models safely, from both a model use and a customer data perspective. With both EFS and EDC, when automated safety monitoring finds a risk, it creates a Safety Case for your team to review. With EFS, customers store their data in their own AWS account, and prompts and completions are not retained by Anthropic or Amazon Bedrock. With EDC, retained data is stored in Amazon-managed storage instead of your account and prompts and completions are not retained by Anthropic. One application gives access to both programs.
In this post, we explain how the trusted access program API works, then walk through EFS and EDC storage options and setup.
How trusted access programs work
A trusted access program is a named provider program that gives customers more control of safety reviews and access to model capabilities in exchange for accepting the program’s terms. Amazon Bedrock trusted access program API now gives you one place to find the model and use case programs available to your account. EFS and EDC are the first offerings available today. Offerings that providers add later appear in the same place and follow the same steps.
Anyone with access to the trusted access program API can list the offerings and check their status for an account, an organization in AWS Organizations, or an Amazon Bedrock project. The status tells you what to do next. eligible means you’re eligible for the offering and can enroll, requestable means you need approval for eligibility first, and the statusReason field in the response explains how to request it. The model provider (or AWS, as authorized by the model provider) approves your eligibility.
Enrolling is a separate step where you accept the offering’s terms imposed by the provider. You enroll at the scope where you were approved: an account, every account in an organization from the management account, or a single project. You can opt out at any time. Each step is a call to the trusted access program API, so you control who can enroll with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies and service control policies (SCPs). More information is available in the trusted access programs documentation.
Enterprise Frontier Safeguards
With Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), you can retain your data in your own AWS environment with full control. It is designed with over 100 customers, including a quarter of the Fortune 100 and many companies in industries with strict rules on data visibility, like healthcare, financial services, and law.
Automated safety monitoring looks for patterns that only show up across many requests. These include intentional misuse that could lead to serious harm, such as offensive cyber operations. They also include agents that go beyond what a user asked for, such as using a software exploit to reach an internal system.
On Amazon Bedrock, AWS operates EFS and the customer inputs and outputs stay within the customer’s AWS account. Only automated safety monitoring within AWS reads the retained inputs and outputs. AWS human reviewers don’t review content for EFS. Your review stays with you. Neither AWS nor Anthropic humans access your retained inputs or outputs. Your inputs and outputs are never used for training.
How it works
Amazon Bedrock reaches your AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket as a single AWS service principal and only through the key policy and bucket policy that you write. You can remove that access at any time, but Amazon Bedrock stops serving the covered models 24 hours after it loses access to your key or bucket.
When you call a covered model including Claude Fable, Claude Mythos, and Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 used through the Cyber Verification Program (CVP):
- Your application calls the model. Inference works as it does for any Amazon Bedrock model.
- Amazon Bedrock writes the prompt and response to its retention and key services.
- These services encrypt the data with your AWS KMS key.
- Bedrock writes the prompt and response to your bucket, encrypted with your key, or to Amazon-managed storage. When writing to your bucket, Amazon writes the content within minutes. On some failures with your key or bucket, we can retry for up to 72 hours.
- Automated safety monitoring, which runs in AWS owned and operated accounts, scans the data and looks for misuse across requests.
- If automated safety monitoring finds a potential risk, a case is created in your bucket for your review.
How your team handles cases
A Case summarizes what automated safety monitoring found and references the related transcripts. Retained records arrive under the transcripts/ prefix in your bucket, and case files arrive under review-cases/. Your team reviews each Case and writes a response file to review-responses/, stating whether it found a violation (violation or no_violation) and, for a violation, the applicable policy category.
Enterprise Data Controls
EDC offers the same automated safety monitoring as EFS and human review of flagged activity stays with your team. Unlike EFS, EDC stores retained data in Amazon managed storage, encrypted with AWS managed keys, so there’s no bucket or key to set up. Eligible customers can access both EFS and EDC through a single enrollment application. If your policy allows retained data to stay in Amazon-managed storage and encrypted with AWS-managed keys, enroll in EDC. If your policy instead requires retained data to be encrypted with your AWS KMS key and stay in your S3 bucket, enroll in EFS. Either way, your team will be able to review flagged activity.
Outside EFS and EDC, you can use Claude Fable models on Amazon Bedrock in two ways today:
- With the aws_review data retention mode, Amazon Bedrock retains inputs and outputs for up to 30 days, where they are available for review within the AWS boundary.
- Eligible customers can use current Fable models for internal use with zero data retention (ZDR) through at least June 30, 2027. EFS is the long-term path after ZDR ends.
Choose where retained data is stored
With EFS, retained data is stored only in your own S3 bucket, encrypted with your KMS key. Neither Anthropic nor AWS keeps it in their own storage. The following table compares EFS with the other routes.
|  | Not Eligible for ZDR, EFS, or EDC | ZDR exception (interim) | EFS, your own Amazon S3 bucket (public preview) | EDC, Amazon-managed storage (public preview) | 
| Data retention | Up to 30 days | None, through at least June 30, 2027, for current Fable models and existing Cyber Verification Program models for internal use | Amazon Bedrock keeps no copy. Your lifecycle rules apply, 30 days minimum. | Up to 30 days, then Amazon Bedrock deletes it | 
| Where the retained data is stored | AWS managed storage | Not retained | Your Amazon S3 bucket | Amazon-managed storage | 
| Encryption key | AWS managed | Not applicable | Your AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key | AWS managed | 
| Safety monitoring | Available for review within the AWS boundary | None | Automated. Cases arrive in your bucket for your team to review. | Automated. Your team reviews flagged Cases. Cases aren’t delivered during the public preview. | 
| What your AWS CloudTrail shows | Your Amazon Bedrock API calls | Your Amazon Bedrock API calls | Your Amazon Bedrock API calls, plus Amazon Bedrock’s use of your key and bucket | Your Amazon Bedrock API calls | 
| Storage cost | Not applicable | Not applicable | Usual Amazon S3 and AWS KMS charges | Not applicable | 
Table 1: Routes for Claude Fable models on Amazon Bedrock.
Storage configurations apply to one Region at a time, and a Region without a configuration uses Amazon-managed storage. Save a configuration in every Region where you call covered models.
Getting started
Start by checking your EFS status with the trusted access program API:
If the status is eligible, your account is approved. If it’s requestable, follow the steps in the statusReason field to request access. Joining the preview turns off zero data retention for the accounts you add.
After you’re approved, set up EFS in each Region where you call covered models:
- Create an AWS KMS key and an Amazon S3 bucket in the same Region. The key and bucket policies give Amazon Bedrock access only through its service principal and only for your account’s data.
- Give your role permission to save the storage configuration.
- Save your storage configuration. Amazon Bedrock checks your key and bucket settings before it saves, and the error names any check that fails.
- Set your data retention mode to aws_review.
- Call a Claude Fable model, then confirm that AWS CloudTrail shows Amazon Bedrock using your key. Retained records usually appear in your bucket within minutes but can take up to 72 hours if Amazon Bedrock has to retry.
The EFS documentation has the complete key policy, bucket policy, IAM policy, and API calls for each step. It also covers organization and project configurations, and troubleshooting. To use enterprise data controls instead, skip steps 1 and 2 and choose Amazon-managed storage in step 3.
Conclusion
The trusted access program API, now generally available, gives you one way to find model provider offerings on Amazon Bedrock, check your status, and enroll, with IAM policies and SCPs controlling who can opt in. EFS and EDC are the first offerings in public preview. They give you control over your data when you use Claude Fable and Cyber Verification Program models. With your own Amazon S3 bucket, Amazon Bedrock keeps no copy of the retained data, your AWS KMS key encrypts it, and every access appears in your own AWS CloudTrail logs.
To get started, check your EFS status with aws bedrock list-trusted-access-programs and enroll in the EFS preview. To learn more, see the trusted access programs documentation and the EFS/EDC documentation.
To enroll in the EFS and EDC public preview, work with your AWS account team to submit a request. Have the AWS account IDs ready (or Amazon Bedrock runtime project ARNs for projects) and note that the preview is for customers already enrolled in EFS ZDR.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $43.9 Billion Deal
articles.text:
CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) on Monday said it has agreed to acquire Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion.
The deal would combine one of the largest endpoint security providers with a pioneer in cloud-delivered zero-trust access and give CrowdStrike a much larger presence in network security.
The two companies already share more than 2,000 customers and have 16 product integrations. In September, they announced plans to expand their partnership so Falcon could continuously assess user risk and share that information with Zscaler’s access controls. CrowdStrike said it plans to bring the products together on a single platform with a common data layer and a single customer contract after closing.
Zscaler’s own acquisition spree
Zscaler has used acquisitions to expand beyond its core network security business. In February 2026, it acquired SquareX, whose browser extension helps enterprises enforce security policies on unmanaged devices. In November 2025, it bought SPLX, adding tools to discover, test and protect AI models, applications and agents.
Zscaler also completed its acquisition of managed detection and response provider Red Canary in August 2025, expanding its presence in security operations. The deal followed Zscaler’s 2024 purchases of Avalor, a $350 million acquisition that added technology for combining security data and prioritizing risk, and Airgap Networks, which brought network segmentation capabilities.
CrowdStrike expects the combined company to have more than $10 billion in annual recurring revenue at closing and projects about $1 billion in additional annualized revenue within 30 months, in part from selling more products to existing customers.
The deal would put CrowdStrike in more direct competition with broad cybersecurity platform providers such as Palo Alto Networks.
Both boards unanimously approved the deal, which is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike’s fiscal 2028.
Unter the terms of the agreement, Zscaler shareholders would receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each Zscaler share. Based on Friday’s closing prices, the exchange ratio values Zscaler at $260.41 per share, a premium of roughly 34%. CrowdStrike shareholders would own approximately 84.1% of the combined company, with Zscaler shareholders holding the remaining 15.9%.
Zscaler founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue to lead the Zscaler business and join CrowdStrike’s board after the deal closes.

Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta segunda-feira (23/11).
Como não cair em golpes e economizar na Black Friday
Aproveitar os descontos da Black Friday exige planejamento financeiro, acompanhamento antecipado de preços e atenção redobrada à segurança digital. Para evitar compras por impulso ou fraudes virtuais, consumidores podem estabelecer um teto de gastos, checar a reputação das lojas e utilizar ferramentas de inteligência artificial para comparar ofertas e condições de pagamento.
BepiColombo entra na órbita de Mercúrio após manobra decisiva
A missão BepiColombo, da Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA), entrou com sucesso na órbita de Mercúrio nesta sexta-feira (21) após uma operação de 37 minutos com o acionamento de quatro propulsores. Após a captura orbital ao redor do planeta mais interno do Sistema Solar, a sonda restabeleceu contato com a Terra e equipes já analisam os dados de telemetria dos sistemas.
Ações da Anthropic continuam caindo
A Anthropic protagonizou o maior IPO da história ao levantar mais de US$ 100 bilhões na Nasdaq e atingir valor de mercado estimado em US$ 1,1 trilhão. Apesar de dispararem na estreia (de US$ 83 para até US$ 111), as ações perderam força e fecharam a semana abaixo de US$ 89, refletindo o pessimismo do mercado diante dos altíssimos custos para desenvolver e operar inteligência artificial.
Bancos dos EUA endurecem controle sobre agentes de IA por segurança
Bancos de grande e médio porte dos Estados Unidos estão endurecendo os protocolos de segurança sobre seus agentes de inteligência artificial para impedir que os sistemas executem ações não autorizadas. A medida ganhou força após incidentes com modelos experimentais da OpenAI exporem falhas de proteção, levando instituições financeiras a criarem equipes internas para mapear vulnerabilidades.

articles.title: The catch in IBM’s offer to relocate its U.S.-based immigrant workers
articles.text:
For some IBM employees, keeping their jobs could mean moving to another country — and taking a steep pay cut in the process.
Earlier this month, IBM said it would no longer support the U.S. immigration status of workers in its consulting division, offering them the option to take a role with the company in another country or exit, according to a Bloomberg report citing a company document.
“IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages,” an IBM spokesperson told Rest of World. “That participation has been declining for a number of years, and as skill availability and client need have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting.”
IBM Consulting employs more than 150,000 people globally. The company does not disclose the geographical split for its workforce, making it hard to ascertain the exact number of workers impacted by this decision. On November 19, the company’s career portal listed 1,278 open roles for the consulting division outside the U.S., including 1,125 in India, 23 in Singapore, and 18 in the U.K. In the U.S., it listed 89 roles.
For employees, relocation does not automatically ensure continued engagement, effective collaboration, or equal access to professional opportunities, Zakaria Laaraj, founder of consultancy Global New Ventures, told Rest of World. It may affect their access to decision-makers, established networks, and career opportunities. “The credibility of such an offer depends on employee tenure, available positions, immigration requirements, and compensation,” Laaraj said.
Discussions on Blind, an anonymous employee forum used by 14 million professionals, suggest relocating may not be realistic for many.
Moving to India, for instance, could mean an approximately 80% pay cut, one IBM employee wrote on Blind.
“Employees get three weeks to decide,” Blind’s CEO Sunguk Moon told Rest of World. “The alternative is three months of severance and a last day of December 31. And the news came in a surprise one-on-one ‘career sync’ with a manager.”
For any relocation option to be viable, companies must go beyond just assigning a new job to their employee, George Carrillo, CEO of career development and staffing company HireMe, told Rest of World.
“Moving a position can mean uprooting a family. It affects a spouse’s employment, children’s schooling, healthcare, and years of planning. HR should provide clear options, deadlines, and coordinated support. Leaders must own the follow-through,” Carrillo said.
Most U.S. tech giants are navigating the challenges arising from changing visa norms under Donald Trump’s leadership.
“IBM has an advantage because it already operates international offices with the infrastructure and staff to absorb those workers,” Lacey Kaelani, CEO of job search engine Metaintro, told Rest of World. “Rather than abandoning the talent, companies like IBM can move the work to where the talent is.”
Earlier this year, Amazon allowed stranded H-1B workers to work from India amid consular delays but only temporarily. Microsoft defended its international talent hiring strategy in an October blog post pushing back against the U.S. administration’s allegations that it replaces American workers with foreign visa holders. The statement followed its suspension from the Department of Labor’s PERM green card program alongside Adobe and six other IT outsourcing firms, including TCS and Infosys.
“Companies are looking for solutions, but they’re also making business decisions,” Cassandra Fultz, co-founder of Doherty Fultz Immigration, told Rest of World. “Sponsoring an employee indefinitely, particularly when the outcome is uncertain, can be expensive and disruptive. Moving that employee to an existing operation abroad may be an option with more stability for the business. That doesn’t mean every employee will be offered the opportunity for placement abroad. Each country has its own eligibility requirements and work authorization rules. Companies will inevitably prioritize the people and positions they consider most valuable or difficult to replace.”
Even employees are reevaluating the lure of the American Dream as the uncertainty tax of constant visa changes weighs heavily on them. The wait for green cards for Indian nationals — who typically receive three-quarters of the H-1B visas and comprise the majority of the green card queue — can take several decades, according to the National Foundation for American Policy. Even with Democrats winning control of both the House and the Senate, immigration issues will stay with the White House and executive agencies.
“Mid-career professionals in the queue for green cards are most impacted,” Abhijit Bhaduri, former general manager for global learning and development at Microsoft and author of the upcoming book AIdentity: How to Become Irreplaceable in the New World of Work, told Rest of World. “They built a life in a country that still lists them as temporary. A visa is a document. But the vanishing green card queue feels like a broken promise. They followed every rule for years, and the finish line moved. You can relocate a job overnight. Rebuilding and redesigning a new identity takes years. That is the invisible price that gets missed.”

articles.title: Anthropic tested the market. Will Cohere follow?
articles.text:
Anthropic just answered a question that, until Friday, investors have mostly had to guess the answer to. Until now, markets have priced the value of AI features or integrations, but not a frontier lab itself. So what is a pure-play AI company worth?
It turns out: a lot. Anthropic closed its first day on the Nasdaq on Thursday with a market cap of nearly $1.3 trillion USD, the largest IPO in history.
Now, that solid debut isn’t a guarantee of continued momentum or overall faith in the AI trade, as anyone staring into a sea of red in their portfolios would have told you on Friday. Analysts have noted that it’s likely many traders dumped other tech stocks to give Anthropic a heavier weight in their portfolios. Meanwhile, lingering anxiety over inflation and massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure contributed to a nasty end to the week as stock markets entered correction territory.
But as the first frontier company to test the waters, Anthropic appears to have found them decently warm.
Canada’s entrant in the frontier model race was watching closely, even though it doesn’t seem ready to jump in just yet. “A rising tide lifts all boats, and a very successful IPO is good for everyone,” Cohere co-founder Aidan Gomez wrote on X, congratulating Anthropic, followed by a small dig: “I hope Anthropic adjusts its strategy to support a healthy community of competitors and a diversity of different ideologies and opinions.”
Gomez said last year he thought Cohere could IPO “soon,” but told the Wall Street Journal earlier this month that timing is still uncertain. Instead, Cohere appears to be focusing on M&A—it’s made four this year, all in Europe. Given the broader tech selloff and its new pile of government money, Cohere is likely in no rush to join Anthropic all that “soon.”
